title: Failed to start container: unable to sethostname when calling

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
The e2e tests started failing sometime this afternoon because docker was not able to set the hostname.

Sample e2e run: go/k8healthz/job/kubernetes-e2e-gce/3797/consoleFull
The log is full of sethostname errors:

```
Error syncing pod, skipping: API error (500): Cannot start container 48c57647f75fba98c3ed7d82574e3fdad936d87c4f352773bf7c5a1b7fe6d5c1: unable to sethostname "fluentd-to-elasticsearch-e2e-test-jenkins-minion-4gnu.c.kubernetes-jenkins.internal": invalid argument
```

kubelet uses `pod.name` as the container hostname (I am not sure why). In the example above, the hostname is 83 characters, which has exceeded the max length of 64 on the system.

The cause of this is that static pods (i.e., pods from file/http sources) use `podName-hostname` as the actual pod name so that we can distinguish pods from different nodes. #5775 replaced os.Hostname() with kubelet.Hostname. This led to the change of hostname from
`e2e-test-jenkins-minion-4gnu` to `e2e-test-jenkins-minion-4gnu.c.kubernetes-jenkins.internal`, thus exceeding the limit.

body:
I tried to spin up GCE kube environment using kube-up and got the following error:

``` shell
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "cluster/../cluster/gce/../../cluster/gce/kube-env.py", line 19, in <module>
    import yaml
ImportError: No module named yaml
```

The script would then hang on a subsequent command.

The verify-prereqs for kube-up should require yaml support for python and fail early.

To rectify, I had to do the following:

``` shell
sudo yum install python-yaml
```

title: Many flaky tests caused by blocking on large image pulls

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

milestone.title: v1.0
milestone.description: Issues that need to be resolved for v1.0 of Kubernetes.

body:
Docker v1 daemon serializes pull requests per https://github.com/docker/docker/issues/150
"v1 (which is what is used when you pull coderpad/coderpad) doesn't [support parallel pulls], and is unlikely to feature parallelism (the way it is designed prevents it)"

That causes many of our tests that include timeouts to fail when a test with a small timeout and a small image is blocked on a pull by a large image.  E.g., on cluster setup, we run a pod for elasticsearch-logging.  If a small image, e.g. serve_hostname gets scheduled 2nd, it won't pull until the elasticsearch-logging image finishes, which can take minutes on GCE.  Of course, once the big image finishes the pull, the 2nd smaller image runs quite quickly.

% kubectl get pods
POD                                                IP                  CONTAINER(S)            IMAGE(S)                           HOST                                                                        LABELS                       STATUS
elasticsearch-logging-controller-gziey             10.245.1.6          elasticsearch-logging   dockerfile/elasticsearch           e2e-test-mohr-minion-1tmg.c.mohr-instance-manager.internal/130.211.163.89   name=elasticsearch-logging   Pending
send-events-00814060-b7c1-11e4-b03c-10604b6be770   10.245.1.10         p                       kubernetes/serve_hostname          e2e-test-mohr-minion-1tmg.c.mohr-instance-manager.internal/130.211.163.89   name=foo,time=299941735      Pending

We should consider one or more of the following:
- to test actual functionality and exclude the variability of pull times, pre-pull all images as part of test infrastructure creation
- before starting a test, list pods and don't start until any pods are in Pending.
- use Really Big Timeouts on all tests.
- figure out why pulls of large images are slow.

Brendan had a CL with a list of images and an idea of how to pre-pull them, so passing to him for now.

The apiserver proxy rewrites links to the form "/proxy/ns/default/...":

https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/apiserver/proxy.go#L162

But this form stopped working recently, seemingly around https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/commit/18609e17062ad4a56c3533f80014299815bfee76. The "/proxy/ns/default/..." form always returns "404: Page Not Found", similar to the problem seen in https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/pull/4283. If you remove "/ns/default" from the URL, it works.

title: Erroneous service port conflicts for external services

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

body:
From a user:

I'm trying to expose multiple services on the same port in a GKE Kubernetes 0.8.1 cluster. My question is similar to this SO post but it is not solved by 0.5.x+

I've deployed a service (hellogo) with an external load balancer which works correctly. Deploying another service (pynote) which is extremely similar fails

{
    "apiVersion": "v1beta1",
    "kind": "Service",
    "id": "pynote-service",
    "selector": {
        "name": "pynote"
    },
    "containerPort": 8080,
    "protocol": "TCP",
    "port": 80,
    "createExternalLoadBalancer": true
}

gcloud preview container services --cluster athena --zone $ZONE create --config-file pynote-service.json
ERROR: F0124 19:42:27.683068   55331 create.go:61] service "pynote-service" is invalid: service "pynote-service" cannot be updated: port: 80 is already in use

If I delete the other service and start pynote first, the service and load balancer are setup correctly, but the other service cannot be deployed with the same error.

I believe the current proxying design is that service routing occurs via proxies on every node which are part of the target pool. Every service gets its own IP. Putting up two external services on port 80 on GKE should allocate two load balancers, each with a fixed IP address. This design does not preclude exposing services on the same port as each service is accessed through a separate external IP. Furthermore, Kubernetes itself runs a service (kubernetes-ro) on port 80 which coexists with my first service nicely.

At the very least, the message is misleading. There is no requirement that the services deployed on a cluster use unique ports. In the source, it becomes apparent that its the external load balancer creation that causes the command to fail. Indeed, I can deploy pynote with createExternalLoadBalancer to false. Happily coexisting:

hellogo-service     <none>                                    name=hellogo        10.143.249.126      80
pynote-service      <none>                                    name=pynote         10.143.254.255      80

I've tried to define my own target pool called pynote-service, selecting all the cluster node instances and created a network load balancer with a forwarding rule on port 80 to the target pool. Despite the fact that it corresponds to the one created automatically for hellogo-service, it does not seem to resolve to the running pynote pod. 

This feels like I'm missing something small, but I've been blocked on this. Perhaps I'll only ever run one lonely web service...

title: Unregister v1beta3

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
We need to stop supporting v1beta3 before 1.0.

We can stop exposing v1beta3 by default in the master (https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/server.go#L290), which is a small change.
To totally disallow users to use v1beta3, we can stop registering the API and its conversion funcs (https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/api/registered/registered.go#L38)

We can work on deleting all v1beta3 code post v1.

title: DNS searches across namespaces is BROKEN on some OSes

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

milestone.title: v1.0
milestone.description: Issues that need to be resolved for v1.0 of Kubernetes.

body:
Debian wheezy:

```
root@d7c52f99509a:/# dig +search +noall +answer kubernetes.default
kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local. 30 IN A   10.0.0.1
root@d7c52f99509a:/# dig +search +noall +answer +ndots=3 kubernetes.default
kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local. 30 IN A   10.0.0.1
```

Debian jessie (and ubuntu 14.04):

```
root@8f7524ea72c0:/# dig +search +noall +answer kubernetes.default
root@8f7524ea72c0:/# dig +search +noall +answer +ndots=3 kubernetes.default
kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local. 30 IN A   10.0.0.1
```

Our DNS tester just happens to be based on wheezy, as does our container VM image.  Apparently this does not (and has never?) worked for other OSes.  There is a resolv.conf param called "ndots" that governs this and it is documented as defaulting to 1 while we need it to be at least 3.  I found a thread where someone else also saw this on Debian late 2014, but no root cause.

As far as I can tell, there is no way to get docker to write this resolv.conf option.  I will open a bug with them.

@smarterclayton @bgrant0607 @brendandburns @ArtfulCoder 

I am marking this as P0 for discussion so we can decide what, if anything, to do.

title: kube-apiserver unable to write to etcd

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/cluster-lifecycle
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Cluster Lifecycle.

milestone.title: v1.0
milestone.description: Issues that need to be resolved for v1.0 of Kubernetes.

body:
In about 100 test runs overnight, 5 clusters failed with the same problem:
Nodes try to register with the apiserver, apiserver sends back a 500.
Looking at the kube-apiserver logs, I see:

```
E0619 20:37:50.685032       5 errors.go:62] apiserver received an error that is not an api.Status: 501: All the given peers are not reachable (failed to propose on members [http://127.0.0.1:4001] twice [last error: Unexp
ected HTTP status code]) [0]
I0619 20:37:50.685229       5 handlers.go:135] POST /api/v1/namespaces: (12.228060557s) 500
...
E0619 20:37:50.643558       5 errors.go:62] apiserver received an error that is not an api.Status: 501: All the given peers are not reachable (failed to propose on members [http://127.0.0.1:4001] twice [last error: Unexp
ected HTTP status code]) [0]
I0619 20:37:50.643762       5 handlers.go:135] POST /api/v1/nodes: (12.228247163s) 500
```

To me, that looks like writes to etcd are failing. Looking into the etcd container logs, I see a lot of:

```
2015/06/19 20:40:38 etcdhttp: unexpected error: etcdserver: request timed out

2015/06/19 20:40:47 etcdhttp: unexpected error: etcdserver: request timed out

Trying to hit etcd directly:

```
# curl -L http://127.0.0.1:4001/v2/keys/message -XPUT -d value="Hello world"

```

Etcd's data directory is pretty empty, other than one entry in members/wal, so I tried listing members:

```
# curl http://127.0.0.1:4001/v2/members
{"members":[]}
```

In a working cluster, that looks more like:

```
# curl http://127.0.0.1:4001/v2/members
{"members":[{"id":"ce2a822cea30bfca","name":"default","peerURLs":["http://localhost:2380","http://localhost:7001"],"clientURLs":["http://127.0.0.1:4001"]}]}
```

I'm about at the extent of my etcd knowledge, so if anybody has any idea what else to poke at, I'd love to hear it.

title: Cluster addons make large clusters unstable (user container's oom_score_adj is misconfigured)

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent

milestone.title: v1.0

body:
1. Setup a 100 node cluster with 0 extra pods
2. Periodically run `kubectl get pods | sort -k 5 -u` till you notice a youger cluster addon, eg:

```
monitoring-heapster-v2-jnxgm                       1/1       Running   0          10m

fluentd-elasticsearch-e2e-test-beeps-minion-i8ke   1/1       Running   1          7m
NAME                                               READY     REASON    RESTARTS   AGE
```

At this point you'll probably have some dead nodes, or at least a kubelet restart (related:  https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/issues/7815).

kubectl exec -p nginx date

title: Kubelet should store the config of a static pod as an annotation in the mirror pod

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

milestone.title: v1.1
milestone.description:
Release 1.1.

P1 features:
* 250+ nodes, at our published SLO
* kube-proxy perf. improvements (via IPTables)
* Docker 1.8.x
* Horizontal pod auto-scaling
* Job
* Ingress
* Schema validation in kubectl
* Experimental API and API groups
* Graceful pod termination

body:
See #8642 for more context.

Currently, kubelet compares the spec of a mirror pod (created via apiserver) with that of a static pod (config stored as a file) to decide whether the two are considered identical. If they differ, kubelet would delete the mirror pod and re-create it with the correct spec. Due to the fact that apiserver may set default values for some fields in the spec of the mirror pod, the specs could deviate undesirably. To avoid problems like this, we can store the config of a static pod as an annotation in the mirror pod, and compare the static pod with the annotation.

During some 'chaos' testing I noticed that if all Nodes are taken offline (NotReady status) then Pods freeze in the "Running" state indefinitely (well, at least over an hour at the time of writing) as you can see below.

The controller logs spam out "Evicting pods2" (see below) but no action is taken. Pod fail-over was working while taking one node down at a time, so it would suggest the issue occurs only when no nodes are available.

title: cpu.share is not properly set for containers in kubernetes

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
I were trying to use limitRange to set default cpu request for each container to prevent overcommit a node badly before we have more intelligent scheduler, and identified the issue. 

Through kubernetes I scheduled a container asking for 400m, (409 cpu.share) but kubernetes always assigns 1024 cpu.share to that cgroup. 

```
# cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/docker/63b0724fdfa08d44401bf7965689bd4105f099beb751b31d1bf26e2aeb71fadc/cpu.shares 
1024
```

Initially I thought kubelet doesn't pass cpu limit properly to docker, but docker inspect proves I were wrong:

```
# docker inspect 63b0724fdfa08d44401bf7965689bd4105f099beb751b31d1bf26e2aeb71fadc
[{
    "AppArmorProfile": "",
    "Args": [
        "-g",
        "daemon off;"
    ],
    "Config": {
        "AttachStderr": false,
        "AttachStdin": false,
        "AttachStdout": false,
        "Cmd": [
            "nginx",
            "-g",
            "daemon off;"
        ],
        "CpuShares": 409,
        "Cpuset": "",
        "Domainname": "",
        "Entrypoint": null,
        "Env": [
...
```

Then I thought it might be capped at docker level, but I tested it through docker cli, and proves I were wrong again:

```
# docker run -c 200 busybox sh
[{
    "AppArmorProfile": "",
    "Args": [],
    "Config": {
        "AttachStderr": true,
        "AttachStdin": true,
        "AttachStdout": true,
        "Cmd": [
            "sh"
        ],
        "CpuShares": 200,
...

# cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/docker/efc87fa9a7c0087c60e116d0832e11d7f74a3c3c4ad51bd0348d7ec28a871037/cpu.shares 
200
```

It might be docker/libcontainer issue and triggered by the way how we are using docker itself. Filed the issue here for investigation. @vmarmol  is going to look into it.

title: Make template Deletion/Creation more robust

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/cluster-lifecycle
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Cluster Lifecycle.

milestone.title: v1.0
milestone.description: Issues that need to be resolved for v1.0 of Kubernetes.

body:
'kubernetes-soak-weekly-deploy' sometimes fails to deploy because the clean-up cluster `down` step fails to delete the template:

```
go run ./hack/e2e.go -v --down
...
Bringing down cluster
Managed instance group e2e-soak-minion-group is being deleted. Operation: operation-1431129917493-5159ae65c0f09-cd441be6-481553bf
ERROR: (gcloud.compute.instance-templates.delete) Some requests did not succeed:
 - The instance_template resource 'e2e-soak-minion-template' is already being used by 'e2e-soak-minion-group'

```

Then the subsequent cluster `up` step fails to create the template, because it already exists:

```
go run ./hack/e2e.go -v --up
...
Created [...e2e-soak-master-https].
Created [...e2e-soak-master-pd].
Created [...e2e-soak-master-ip].
Created [...e2e-soak-minion-all].
Created [...e2e-soak-master].
...
Creating minions.
...
ERROR: (gcloud.compute.instance-templates.create) Some requests did not succeed:
 - The resource 'projects/kubernetes-jenkins/global/instanceTemplates/e2e-soak-minion-template' already exists
...
[0;33mAttempt 1 failed to create instance template e2e-soak-minion-template. Retrying.
...
ERROR: (gcloud.compute.instance-templates.create) Some requests did not succeed:
 - The resource 'projects/kubernetes-jenkins/global/instanceTemplates/e2e-soak-minion-template' already exists
```

It keeps retrying and failing, because the template already exists, until it times out and the deployment fails.

Suggested fixes:
- Cluster down should try harder to delete the template (maybe wait/retry).
- Cluster up should recognize that the template exists, and try to delete/recreate, or just re-use the existing.

title: Secrets not surviving server reboot...

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: kind/support
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as a support question.

labels.name: sig/cluster-lifecycle
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Cluster Lifecycle.

milestone.title: v1.0
milestone.description: Issues that need to be resolved for v1.0 of Kubernetes.

body:
I believe I'm seeing an issue where secrets are not available after server reboot. 

The steps to reproduce are below.  Note that the following steps have been run on v.0.16.2:

Create the following simple secret:

```
# From kubernetes/examples/secrets/secret.yaml
apiVersion: v1beta3
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: test-secret
data:
  data-1: dmFsdWUtMQ0K
  data-2: dmFsdWUtMg0KDQo=
```

Then create the following pod:

```
apiVersion: v1beta3
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: test
    image: centos:centos7.0.1406
    command: [ "bash", "-c", "while [ true ]; do cat /etc/test-secret/data-1; sleep 5; done" ]
    volumeMounts:
    - mountPath: /etc/test-secret
      name: test-secret
      readOnly: true
  volumes:
  - name: test-secret
    secret:
      secretName: test-secret

```

After starting the pod you can see that it is correctly slowing the data-1 value from the secret

```
kubectl log test
2015-05-08T16:06:37.433196624Z value-1
```

Now reboot the server running the pod.  After reboot I see the following in the log output:

```
kubectl log test
2015-05-08T16:08:53.172253741Z cat: /etc/test-secret/data-1: No such file or directory
```

That seems to indicate to me that the pod is re-starting after the reboot but that it is unable to get the secret.  Note that after the reboot manually stopping ( kubectl stop pod test ) and re-starting the pod shows the expected results.

My expectation of the behavior is that if the server a pod is running on reboots that the pod will re-start with the same secret it had when it started previously.  If the secret had been updated since the pod had been originally started I would expect the original secret to be available.

body:
After #14156 was merged, updating of scale sub-resource for (experimental) replication controller stopped working. In affect, the whole horizontal pod autoscaler is not working now. The problem seems to be that experimental scale sub-resource is trying to update experimental replication controller (while it should update the stable one).

(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/registry/experimental/controller/etcd/etcd.go#L97):
no kind "ReplicationController" is registered for version "experimental/v1alpha1"

This also cause failure of horizontal pod autoscaler e2e tests.

title: Confusing status for successful pod

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

milestone.title: v1.1
milestone.description:
Release 1.1.

P1 features:
* 250+ nodes, at our published SLO
* kube-proxy perf. improvements (via IPTables)
* Docker 1.8.x
* Horizontal pod auto-scaling
* Job
* Ingress
* Schema validation in kubectl
* Experimental API and API groups
* Graceful pod termination

body:
``` console
$ cat > succeeder.yaml <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: succeeder
  labels:
spec:
  containers:
  - command:
    - bash
    - -c
    - echo ok
    image: centos:centos7
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    name: c
  restartPolicy: OnFailure
EOF
$ kubectl create -f succeeder.yaml
pods/succeeder
$ sleep 10
$ kubectl describe pods/succeeder.yaml
...
Status:             Succeeded
...
Containers:
  c:
    State:      Terminated
      Reason:       Error
      Exit Code:    0
      Started:      Mon, 21 Sep 2015 13:55:06 -0700
      Finished:     Mon, 21 Sep 2015 13:55:06 -0700
```

It is confusing to call the container "Terminated with Reason Error" when Exit Code was 0, and when the Pod status is "Succeeded".

It is also confusing that there are so many events for the Pod, but not one saying that a successful Container exited 0 and was cleaned up.

title: Setting resources.requests in pod template breaks updates of resources.limits

milestone.description:
Release 1.1.

P1 features:
* 250+ nodes, at our published SLO
* kube-proxy perf. improvements (via IPTables)
* Docker 1.8.x
* Horizontal pod auto-scaling
* Job
* Ingress
* Schema validation in kubectl
* Experimental API and API groups
* Graceful pod termination

body:
Thought of this while hashing out #12823.

Luckily, pod resources are not yet updatable #5774.

However, they are in pod templates.

Scenario: User sets limits in ReplicationController template. Later, user does a get, modifies limits, and then put. They changed limit but not request. Boom.

My proposal is that we don't default request from limit in pod templates and that we just do it in pods. LimitRange also just applies to pods. The fields are not updatable in pods, so not a problem there.

I'm sure what the best way is to handle this in the defaulting pass. We might need to copy the Go struct type for ResourceRequirements.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/api/v1/defaults.go#L168

cc @davidopp @derekwaynecarr @vishh

Test is failing pretty regularly at the same [point](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/service.go#L608); after updating service nodeport, it expects the loadbalancer ingress to be the same as before, but this is not the case:

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent

body:
In this Jenkins run:

there are 10 failed tests. 
From the logs, it seems that at some point node e2e-gce-minion-gkwy became unreachable. After that, a bunch of tests failed.

I started looking into it and at least some of them may fail if a node is unreachable.
For example all PD tests will fail if first node returned from the LIST nodes operation will be unreachable:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/pd.go#L61
(we don't check whether that node is healthy).

We should also check the other tests is that run.

title: Scheduler algorithm rename breaks backwards compatibility

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

body:
1.0.0 shipped with `ServiceSpreadingPriority` (https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/blob/release-1.0/plugin/pkg/scheduler/algorithmprovider/defaults/defaults.go#L70). The rename at https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/pull/10667/files#r36776577 breaks backwards compatibility with serialized scheduler config files.

We should:
1. Add a test for backwards compatibility with the serialized version of the priorities/algorithms
2. Alias or revert the rename to that priority algorithm

Forked from #11355.

GKE went to beta with 0.19 rather than 0.20, so now we need to support backward compatibility with 0.19.

title: GCE UpdateTCPLoadBalancer removes all VMs from load balancer

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

milestone.title: v1.0
milestone.description: Issues that need to be resolved for v1.0 of Kubernetes.

body:
UpdateTCPLoadBalancer works by getting the list of the current nodes in the load balancer's target pool and then comparing them to the list of nodes in the cluster. In the process, though, it compares the project ID returned by the target pool API with the string ID known to the controller manager, but one of them is the numeric project ID and the other is the string project ID. We then add the ones that we know about before removing the ones that look wrong to us. This causes all cluster resizes and upgrades to remove all nodes from existing target pools.

We should avoid comparing the project IDs, since we already know the project ID should be correct given that we used it to get the target pool in the first place.

title: Versioned API descriptions breaks existing release flow

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

body:
#10690 doesn't work with our existing release flow. I thought it did, but, from https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/pull/10812#issuecomment-119078638:

> The process we use right now is to create the release branch locally, tag it, propose a PR (like this one), then push the branch. Most of those instructions are actually sitting right in mark-new-version.sh, and some are here: https://github.com/zmerlynn/kubernetes/blob/i1883/docs/devel/releasing.md#branching-tagging-and-merging.
> 
> The problem, and I didn't really think about it long enough when it went in, is that the new sandwich commit you're creating, is always going to get backmerged back like this - git will always try to mutate head from the release version. We take that as good from the release version because we've been trying to keep the head version in sync with the patch version (long story), but not for these cases.
> 
> We do have a weird cost for merging back and forth between release N-1 and master (we try to keep the release tags merged back to master). Not sure how to crack this particular nut.

cc @eparis @thockin 

closing out #10812.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

body:
This came up in late GKE testing. (As a reminder, GKE GA'd on 0.19.x, and we still have a number of customers with 0.19.x and 0.21.4 nodes.)

After upgrading the master, the old, upgraded system pods come up and stayed stuck in `Terminating` state. @mikedanese already identified the culprit on our internal bug: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/node/nodecontroller.go#L332

(As a meta-point, I'm really dubious of that code doing version string checking at all, rather than some sort of capability/API level check. :/)

title: Remove Autoscaling tests from GCE skip list

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/autoscaling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Autoscaling.

body:
Per our email discussion while getting 1.1 out the door.  It looks like this never happened, though, which means we're not running autoscaling tests against GCE on the 1.1 branch, (we were running it on GKE with the 1.1-features job, but I'm removing that job in #17539).

I'd once again like to (strongly) suggest that we mirror test suites running against release branch to jobs running against master, so that we avoid this problem of accidentally not running tests when we think we are.  I'd much rather have a perhaps-unnecessary slow/HPA/whatever suite than continually try to figure out where slow/HPA/whatever tests are running, depending on if I'm looking at release jobs versus jobs running against master.

cc @jlowdermilk @ixdy

title: NFS recycler does not work in containerized kube-controller-manager

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

body:
When controller manager looks for a recycler for a NFS volume, it calls `nfsPlugin.CanSupport()`, which checks for presence of `/sbin/mount.nfs` or `/sbin/mount.nfs4`. Since controller manager is containerized, it does not see any such executables and returns `false`.

This is related to issue #14244, volume plugins are used both by kubelet, where checking for `mount.nfs` makes sense, and by controller manager, which does not need `mount.nfs` at all.

body:
An HPA request is submitted against namespaceA, but contains a reference to namespaceB (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/apis/extensions/types.go#L75).  The request is accepted because I have rights to create on in namespaceA, but no checking is done to see if I can scale what I'm asking.

The HPA request has a namespace, but it also duplicated a namespace field instead of using a `LocalObjectReference` extended with `kind` and `subresource` field.  The HPA controller then blindly uses the second namespace field: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/podautoscaler/horizontal.go#L99.

This allowed someone in the dev namespace to accidentally (or intentionally) scale down resources in the production namespace.

...
```

I could certainly assume that downtimes at AWS may never last more than `t` minutes and increase the `node-monitor-grace-period` and `pod-eviction-timeout` in my kube-controller-manager accordingly, but there is something dangerous in making such assumptions and relying _only_ on the cloud provider to define nodes' health, since a not responding cloud provider doesn't mean a completely unhealthy platform.

We paid that price today and saw our whole prod cluster going down while everything was fine on the instances themselves :see_no_evil:

body:
User reports:

I am running my web service behind an SSL proxy on my Kubernetes cluster as described in this tutorial. It works 90% of the time, but from time to time my browsers (Chrome/Firefox) get SSL errors when accessing my web service. Firefox says this:

api.[mydomain.com] uses an invalid security certificate.

The certificate is not trusted because the issuer certificate is unknown.
The server might not be sending the appropriate intermediate certificates.
An additional root certificate may need to be imported.
The certificate is only valid for the following names:
  [MY-CLUSTER-IP], 10.0.0.1, kubernetes, kubernetes.default, kubernetes.default.svc, kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local, kubernetes-master  

(Error code: sec_error_unknown_issuer)
After a reload, all requests work fine - until the error pops up again after a while. Is this a problem with Kubernetes or am I doing something wrong here?

Since a while ago we added the master to the list of nodes.  I think that we must be adding the master to the GCE target pool resource.  This is clearly the wrong thing to do.  We shouldn't add nodes that aren't schedulable.

body:
With #16071 we're finally setting proper memory limit for Heapster, but it can be as big as 3G on 250-node cluster (which is the scaling limit we're advertising for 1.2).

Currently we use t2.micro default VM size for AWS, which only has 1G of memory. I think our choices (from easiest to hardest for us) are
- add a release note (and update docs/getting-started-guides/aws.md and ./cluster/aws/options.md) telling people what VM size to use depending on what cluster size they use
- increase default VM size to t2.medium in ./cluster/aws/{config-default,config-test}.sh(and update the aforementioned docs)
- change cluster/aws/config-default.sh to dynamically pick VM size depending on cluster size

t2.medium is 4G and t2.small is 2G, which means the sizes we'd want to use based on @gmarek's data and the values @brendandburns used in #16071 are something like
t2.micro: 1-50 nodes
t2.small: 51-150 nodes
t2.medium: 151+ nodes

ref/ #15747

title: Regression: identical writes to storage interface are not ignored

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/scalability
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scalability.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

milestone.title: v1.2
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/wiki/Release-1.2

body:
Historically, a write to etcd that did not change content (existing content == new content on CAS) would not result in a watch event.  At some point between last year and now, that changed, and identical object writes via the etcd storage result in multiple watch events.  This is bad for several reasons - bad controller loops can flood the event logs trying to write the same data, clients are unnecessarily taxed, etc.

Opening this to ensure it gets tracked down - we saw this in openshift/origin#5275.  This could be a 1.1 blocker.

UPDATE: Caused because we started serializing the resource version of the persisted object to the store, which we used to not do.  The version in the store was 1 off from the version we would write (because we return the resource version that someone should watch from), which meant that the objects were different as serialized.

title: UpdateApplyAnnotation stores large annotation on every kubectl operation

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

milestone.title: v1.1
milestone.description:
Release 1.1.

P1 features:
* 250+ nodes, at our published SLO
* kube-proxy perf. improvements (via IPTables)
* Docker 1.8.x
* Horizontal pod auto-scaling
* Job
* Ingress
* Schema validation in kubectl
* Experimental API and API groups
* Graceful pod termination

body: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/14626 is adding the full object serialization as an annotation on almost every mutating kubectl operation. This is doubling serialization size unnecessarily, and breaking any objects that were close to the annotation size limit. What benefit is this providing? The `apply` command should be able to do a 3-way merge between the current state of the API object and the desired state client-side. Not doing so means that `kubectl apply` isn't useful against objects created by older clients, or objects created or modified by non-kubectl clients.

title: Incorrect state for pods with crashlooping containers

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

milestone.title: v1.1
milestone.description:
Release 1.1.

P1 features:
* 250+ nodes, at our published SLO
* kube-proxy perf. improvements (via IPTables)
* Docker 1.8.x
* Horizontal pod auto-scaling
* Job
* Ingress
* Schema validation in kubectl
* Experimental API and API groups
* Graceful pod termination

body:
With the enhancement of container restart backoff, pod phase may not progress monotonically.

A pod is considered running if at least one container in the pod has been started. If the container happens to be crashlooping, the restart backoff would eventually kick in. From that point on, the container status becomes waiting, and [kubelet determines the phase](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2497) as **pending**.

Once the pod transitions from `Running` to `Pending`, it's impossible to retrieve logs from the crashlooping container using kubectl. This prevents the users from debugging the cause of container failures.

``` console
$ kubectl logs -p heapster-v10-3ayyj --namespace=kube-system
Error from server: Internal error occurred: Pod "heapster-v10-3ayyj" in namespace "kube-system" : pod is not in 'Running', 'Succeeded' or 'Failed' state - State: "Pending"
```

An easy fix is to check `LastTerminationState` of a container before determining the pod phase.

/cc @samsabed

title: Liveness checks against a pod that supports keep-alive are broken

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

milestone.title: v1.1
milestone.description:
Release 1.1.

P1 features:
* 250+ nodes, at our published SLO
* kube-proxy perf. improvements (via IPTables)
* Docker 1.8.x
* Horizontal pod auto-scaling
* Job
* Ingress
* Schema validation in kubectl
* Experimental API and API groups
* Graceful pod termination

body:
Scenario:
1. User running a liveness probe against HTTP 8080
2. Default delay 30s, timeout 3s, no interval set
3. Pod is a unicorn server which supports keep-alive, but has a 30s timeout

Symptom: pod is restarted continuously with:

```
Liveness probe failed: Get http://10.1.1.46:8080/: read tcp 10.1.1.46:8080: use of closed network connection (4 times in the last 2 minutes, 31 seconds)
```

We allow keep-alive, which means the TCP connection stays in the golang transport.  After 30s, unicorn closes the connection but we don't see it.  The next liveness check tries to connect to the pod, but because of the golang client library, can't open the connection (because the connection in the pool is closed and stale).  It returns an error which results in the kubelet killing the pod.

2 changes:
1. We probably shouldn't use client-keepalive from the health checker, or, if we do
2. We should check for use of closed network connection errors explicitly and retry (the Go http library clears the connection from the pool so a new connection will be opened on the next request).

This is fairly high severity because liveness checks are broken in real world use cases.

title: Rename "experimental" group

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

milestone.title: v1.1
milestone.description:
Release 1.1.

P1 features:
* 250+ nodes, at our published SLO
* kube-proxy perf. improvements (via IPTables)
* Docker 1.8.x
* Horizontal pod auto-scaling
* Job
* Ingress
* Schema validation in kubectl
* Experimental API and API groups
* Graceful pod termination

body:
Currently, features in the `experimental` api group are at version `v1alpha1`.
As I describe in #15339, I think that the `alpha` version should be the thing that signals to users that a feature is unstable, not the name of the api group, which, for historical reasons, is `experimental`.   

Also, I don't think anyone expects these Kinds to stay in "experimental" indefinitely.  But I haven't heard a plan about what api group they eventually go into.

So, I think we should rename `experimental` api group to something else which doesn't imply unstable.

Three reasons why I think we need to make this change/distinction.
1. when features in the `experimental` api  group graduate to version `v1beta1`, they will have additional stability ... more than the word _experimental_ might imply.
2. we may introduce new `alpha` quality interfaces in a subsequent version (v1.2 or v1.2).  For example, we miay introduce OpenShift authorization objects.  Because there are so many, they should go into their own API group, e.g. `policy` at first.  The meaning of `experimental` is confusing when there are other api groups that are also unstable at first.
3.  Once current features in experimental graduate to `v1beta1`, we don't want to add new things into that group (e.g. we don't want `apiVersion: experimental/v1beta1 kind:job` at the same time as `apiVersion: experimental/v1alpha1 kind: newThing`.)  It is just confusing to have different things at different versions in one api group.

So, I see a couple of options at this point:
1. do not rename "experimental" in v1.1, but plan to move each Kind that is currently in experimental into a new, more appropriate group, in the next minor version.
2. rename "experimental" to something less scary, like "demo" right now.  Plan to move each Kind that is in "demo" into a new, more appropriate group, prior to graduating them to "v1".
3. add multiple API groups now (prior to v1.1) and try to sort Kinds into them now.  

The last option is the most coding to do before v1.1 to support even more api groups, and could stall on bike shedding on deciding what the final group names are.

milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
(cc @quinton-hoole @roberthbailey)

Right now, our [upgrade tests](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/cluster_upgrade.go) only test that the cluster continues to function in between the steps it takes to do the upgrade, (i.e. before the master upgrade, after the master upgrade, before the node upgrade, after the node upgrade).

We should instead parallelize the test somehow, and make sure that the expected things stay up _during_ the steps:
- during master upgrade, resources should still be reachable
- during node upgrade, resources should still be reachable and scheduling should still work.

title: kubelet on the master node in a GCE cluster does not perform housekeeping tasks

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

milestone.title: v1.1
milestone.description:
Release 1.1.

P1 features:
* 250+ nodes, at our published SLO
* kube-proxy perf. improvements (via IPTables)
* Docker 1.8.x
* Horizontal pod auto-scaling
* Job
* Ingress
* Schema validation in kubectl
* Experimental API and API groups
* Graceful pod termination

body:
We configure salt the populate the http manifest source for the master node [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cluster/saltbase/salt/kubelet/default#L54). 

```
{% set manifest_url = "" -%}
{% if grains['roles'][0] == 'kubernetes-master' and grains.cloud in ['gce'] -%}
  {% set manifest_url = "--manifest-url=http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/attributes/google-container-manifest --manifest-url-header=Metadata-Flavor:Google" -%}
{% endif -%}
```

If user doesn't supply such a file, kubelet would think not all sources are ready and would refuse to delete pods and/or performing housekeeping tasks.

A cluster created by kube-up.sh doesn't have `google-container-manifest` attribute set.

``` console
$ curl "http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/attributes/" -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google"
kube-env
startup-script
```

What periodically appears in kubelet.log if you increase the logging level to 6.

```
I1005 22:28:17.276930    4035 config.go:99] Looking for [file http], have seen map[file:{}]
```

This issue is not urgent because we don't schedule any user pods on the master node, however, it might be important for the longevity of the master node. It will need to be resolve to handle mirror pod deletions, etc #13102. One solution is to supply an empty manifest file upon cluster creation.

title: Extremely high CPU usage in Kubelet on systemd nodes

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

milestone.title: v1.2
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/wiki/Release-1.2

body:
For each cgroup in the cgroupfs tree, cAdvisor is collecting network stats using the pid of the launching process.  On a systemd node where everything is managed in a cgroup by default, there are very large numbers of nodes in the cgroup tree!  This logic error in cAdvisor causes network stats to be read over and over again for the same pid for each cgroup in the tree.  The fix is to only read network stats for the root cgroup.

This causes extremely large CPU usage on a node and can peg the CPU entirely taking over the node.

The fix in cadvisor is here:
https://github.com/google/cadvisor/pull/1158

We need it merged and a cadvisor bump.

/cc @bgrant0607 @dchen1107 @kubernetes/rh-cluster-infra @eparis

labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

body:
Commit 53d4b15 moved columns into wide option to make result more readable. However, the patch did not consider more than one container in the rc, e.g.:

```
NAME              DESIRED          CURRENT                                                               AGE
kube-dns-v10      1                1                                                                     5d
                  kube2sky         gcr.io/google_containers/kube2sky:1.12                                          
                  skydns           gcr.io/google_containers/skydns:2015-10-13-8c72f8c                              
                  healthz          gcr.io/google_containers/exechealthz:1.0
```

The desired output shall be probably something like that:

```
NAME              DESIRED          CURRENT                                                               AGE
kube-dns-v10      1                1                                                                     5d
```

and the remaining information in `-owide`.

```
quinton: The ubernetes-lite e2e clusters stopped coming up 2 days ago, 
and I suspect your or zml's PR's around that time, but unfortunately I don't 
understand the scripts well enough any more to debug effectively.

spxtr: Might've been me.

quinton: In summary, most of the projects that e2e tests run in have a 
network configured in them, named similarly to the project they're in.  
Mine no longer has one, and as a result the VM's are all isolated 
from the network.  In the old days those networks were created by 
he e2e scripts, but these days they are perhaps manually created?  
It's possible that I deleted mine while cleaning up leaked resources, 
and perhaps it's no longer being automatically created?
https://pantheon.corp.google.com/compute/instances?project=k8s-jkns-e2e-gce-ubelite 
is a good place to start.  All of the instances are network-isolated 
as far as I can see (can't ssh to them, and they fail to come up 
because they fail to connect outbound either).  All of the "working" 
e2e projects seem to have 3 networks configured (e.g.
"default", ""jenkins-e2e", "jenkins-gke-e2e-serial", but 
mine (project=k8s-jkns-e2e-gce-ubelite) only has the first
 two for some reason.

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

milestone.title: v1.2
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/wiki/Release-1.2

body:
From https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/22454#issuecomment-192034464

`kubectl get hpa -o yaml` prints the output in `autoscaling/v1` but `kubectl.sh convert -f docs/user-guide/horizontal-pod-autoscaling/hpa-php-apache.yaml` prints the output in `extensions/v1beta1`

We should have one default group version for all kubectl commands for hpa.

@kubernetes/kubectl @piosz @kubernetes/autoscaling @kubernetes/sig-api-machinery

title: Kubelet failed to delete pods which has container(s) stucking at waiting state (failed to docker creation)

body:
This is a regression for sure. 

I tried to reproduce docker hung issue (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/22259) the all morning by scale up one replicaset from 0 to 300 and scale down another one from 300 to 0 in my 3-nodes cluster. After several rounds to scale up and scale down testing, I have a pod staying on terminating state forever.

title: Updating pod-template-hash race

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: kind/flake
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a flaky test.

milestone.title: v1.2
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/wiki/Release-1.2

body:
I'm just documenting a half debug that i did because it's weird, but don't have time to go down a rabbit hole. 
http://kubekins.dls.corp.google.com:8081/job/kubernetes-pull-build-test-e2e-gce/31298/consoleFull
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/22203#issuecomment-191162549
Failed because 2 pods weren't deleted. I think I see the following:   
1. update pod with pod-tempate-hash
2. update rc with pod-template-hash
3. rc manager sees 2 before 1 and create a pod with pod-template-hash (so now we have 2 pods)
4. Rc manager is prematurely deleted
5. Test fails because 2 pods are leaked

How does deployment wait on some signal about 1/2? Why did it think it was safe to delete the RS?

Generation number is updated when the rc manager _sees_ the update. 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/replication/replication_controller_utils.go#L40
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d0ce85a6d1dfd45cf30fda02980aba6a48409008/pkg/registry/controller/strategy.go#L64

Maybe this is what's confusing us? Does this need to change to "only update generation if rc manager has fulfilled spec"?

Then we can do:    
1. Update pod label
2. Update rc label
3. Wait till rc manager updates generation (this means it has fulfilled the rc label update, which means it must have seen the pod label update OR it created a new pod AND sees the pod label update -- so this could still backfire?).

Maybe I'm totally off about this? 

@janetkuo @nikhiljindal

title: Services no longer support "export"

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

milestone.title: v1.2
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/wiki/Release-1.2

body:
It appears that ability to export services no longer works in recent builds of Kubernetes. This problem surfaced in redspread/spread#67.

The error is produced in [/pkg/apiserver/resthandler.go:137](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a608cc9/pkg/apiserver/resthandler.go#L137) 
### kubectl

```
$ kubectl get --export=true services/example-service

Error from server: export of "services" is not supported
```
### API

`curl -v "localhost:9000/api/v1/namespaces/default/services/example-service?export=1"`
##### Request

```
GET /api/v1/namespaces/default/services/example-service?export=1 HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:9000
User-Agent: curl/7.43.0
Accept: */*
```
##### Response

```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json
Date: Tue, 01 Mar 2016 02:56:18 GMT
Content-Length: 182

{
  "kind": "Status",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "metadata": {},
  "status": "Failure",
  "message": "export of \"services\" is not supported",
  "reason": "BadRequest",
  "code": 400
}
```

title: docker 1.9.1: No available IPv4 addresses on this network's address pools: bridge

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: kind/flake
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a flaky test.

milestone.title: v1.2
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/wiki/Release-1.2

body:
I ran into this issue twice today by running pod creation/deletion tests (100 pods per node).

After reading @aboch's comments in the issues (e.g., https://github.com/docker/docker/issues/18535#issuecomment-164494430), all three issues below have the same root cause.
- No available IPv4 addresses: https://github.com/docker/docker/issues/18527
- Same IP address for different containers: https://github.com/docker/docker/issues/18535
- Docker 1.9.1 breaks for custom bridges: https://github.com/docker/docker/issues/18145

After screening the fixes in libnetwork during that time, it seems like https://github.com/docker/libnetwork/pull/771 might be the fix (though I could be totally wrong given my limited knowledge on networking).

Since we may go with docker 1.9.1 for v1.2, any thoughts on how to proceed with this problem? 

(BTW, I couldn't find any existing issue on this. Feel free to close this one if there is already one)

/cc @dchen1107

title: Docker 1.9 doesn't restart cleanly

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

milestone.title: v1.2
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/wiki/Release-1.2

body:
I have a node stuck in NotReady with the symptoms described in: https://github.com/docker/docker/issues/17083. Essentially supervisord keeps restarting docker. 

docker logs: https://storage.googleapis.com/devnul/active_endpoints_docker.log
kubelet: https://storage.googleapis.com/devnul/active_endpoints_kubelet.log
kern (though this doens't looke like a kernel issue): https://storage.googleapis.com/devnul/active_endpoints_kern.log

A couple of weird things:

First it gets shutdown for some reason:

```
time="2016-02-10T04:50:09.765992265Z" level=info msg="GET /version" 
time="2016-02-10T04:50:14.773215450Z" level=info msg="GET /version" 
time="2016-02-10T04:50:19.866889346Z" level=info msg="GET /version" 
/usr/bin/docker already running.
time="2016-02-10T04:50:21.214073277Z" level=info msg="Processing signal 'terminated'" 
```

Then it complains about cbr0, which is probably ok (though still weird):

```
time="2016-02-10T04:50:29.765361165Z" level=fatal msg="Error starting daemon: Error initializing network controller: Error creating default \"bridge\" network: bridge device with non default name cbr0 must be created manually" 
time="2016-02-10T04:50:37.233355561Z" level=fatal msg="Error starting daemon: Error initializing network controller: Error creating default \"bridge\" network: bridge device with non default name cbr0 must be created manually" 
time="2016-02-10T04:50:52.337432352Z" level=fatal msg="Error starting daemon: Error initializing network controller: Error creating default \"bridge\" network: bridge device with non default name cbr0 must be created manually" 
```

then it goes lookin in the store:

```
time="2016-02-10T18:19:25.597635188Z" level=warning msg="Failed deleting endpoint 09230581f955753c5e4af795e3eaff527d1a43ce630c1d8c742d6e015443065c: failed to get endpoint from store during Delete: could not find endpoint 09230581f955753c5e4af795e3eaff527d1a43ce630c1d8c742d6e015443065c: Key not found in store\n" 
time="2016-02-10T18:19:30.665621023Z" level=error msg="getEndpointFromStore for eid d4f9cbeee5f2b6f2e6931462445ca39f2b7efc37431549cd962e1c587723e62a failed while trying to build sandbox for cleanup: could not find endpoint d4f9cbeee5f2b6f2e6931462445ca39f2b7efc37431549cd962e1c587723e62a: Key not found in store" 
time="2016-02-10T18:19:30.665749581Z" level=warning msg="Failed detaching sandbox d16eed32af089019fe2ab199e5fbe34db834c7cf0ad1a08cc420c17c15ed7872 from endpoint d4f9cbeee5f2b6f2e6931462445ca39f2b7efc37431549cd962e1c587723e62a: failed to get endpoint from store during leave: could not find endpoint d4f9cbeee5f2b6f2e6931462445ca39f2b7efc37431549cd962e1c587723e62a: Key not found in store\n" 
```

it's wedged:

```
time="2016-02-10T19:08:42.686296946Z" level=error msg="Error during graph storage driver.Cleanup(): device or resource busy" 
time="2016-02-10T19:08:42.686453183Z" level=fatal msg="Error starting daemon: Error initializing network controller: could not delete the default bridge network: network bridge has active endpoin
```

But a rm -rf /var/lib/docker/network/files/ fixes it, though I suspect it was just some corrupt state in `/var/lib/docker/network/files/local-kv.db`.

@kubernetes/goog-node have we tested restarts with 1.9?

title: Be more conservative with the `[Flaky]` label

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: kind/flake
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a flaky test.

body:
The `[Flaky]` label is just causing us to leave tests unattended:
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/17873#issuecomment-177035197
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/6541#issuecomment-177035310
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/18952#issuecomment-177035567
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/17829#issuecomment-177035881
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/19023#issuecomment-177035897
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/17518#issuecomment-177035960
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/20362

I propose we stop using the `[Flaky]` label, and instead deal with flaky tests by either fixing asap them or moving them into `[Feature:.+]` suites as necessary.  (This has the added benefit that we don't have to worry about the `-flaky` jobs which are currently just dumping grounds for tests people don't want to care about.)

cc @kubernetes/sig-testing @kubernetes/goog-testing

body:
As part of #10548 I'm trying to run only `[Serial]` tests in serial and run the rest in parallel to speed up recovery time of the submit queue.  However, when doing so, the following arise:
- [ ] Etcd failure [Disruptive] should recover from SIGKILL (Failed 2 times in the last 30 runs. Stability: 93 %) No flake or failure
- [ ] Etcd failure [Disruptive] should recover from network partition with master (Failed 2 times in the last 30 runs. Stability: 93 %) No flake or failure
- [x] Kubelet [Serial] [Slow] regular resource usage tracking for 35 pods per node over 20m0s (Failed 2 times in the last 30 runs. Stability: 93 %)Failed with 0 retries (#20231)
- [ ] Nodes [Disruptive] Network when a node becomes unreachable [replication controller] recreates pods scheduled on the unreachable node AND allows scheduling of pods on a node after it rejoins the cluster (Failed 2 times in the last 30 runs. Stability: 93 %) No flake or failure
- [ ] Restart [Feature:Restart] should restart all nodes and ensure all nodes and pods recover (Failed 2 times in the last 30 runs. Stability: 93 %) No flake or failure
- [x] Kubelet [Serial] [Slow] regular resource usage tracking for 0 pods per node over 20m0s (Failed 3 times in the last 30 runs. Stability: 90 %)Failed with 0 retries (#20231)
- [ ] SchedulerPredicates [Serial] validates resource limits of pods that are allowed to run [Conformance](Failed 3 times in the last 30 runs. Stability: 90 %) No flake or failure
- [ ] Nodes [Disruptive] Resize [Slow] should be able to add nodes (Failed 4 times in the last 30 runs. Stability: 86 %) No flake or failure
- [ ] Nodes [Disruptive] Resize [Slow] should be able to delete nodes (Failed 5 times in the last 30 runs. Stability: 83 %) No flake or failure
- [ ] SchedulerPredicates [Serial] validates MaxPods limit number of pods that are allowed to run [Slow](Failed 5 times in the last 30 runs. Stability: 83 %) No flake or failure

The job is http://kubekins.dls.corp.google.com/job/kubernetes-e2e-gce-serial/

These tests seem way flakier in this job than when we run them in http://kubekins.dls.corp.google.com/job/kubernetes-e2e-gce/, but I have no idea why.  I'll continue working on triaging, but I thought I'd file an issue so @dchen1107 could start digging too.

title: e2e unit tests failing due to 60 minute timeout?

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: kind/flake
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a flaky test.

body:
It appears that the unit tests in e2e are sometimes failing due to a 60 minute timeout, but it does not appear to be being correctly applied.

Logs here:
https://console.developers.google.com/storage/browser/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/0586d866de1b0ca888ad3de53ad41cdb2077dd0e/kubernetes-pull-test-unit-integration/10243/

The weird thing is that the logs show that the unit tests themselves only took the normal amount of time - ten minutes or so (14:38 - 14:50 in the logs).  But I'm guessing there is an invisible delay before the first timestamp or after the last timestamp (or the 60 minute limit is not being correctly applied).

The wall clock time in between my request to retest and the failure result being posted was a little more than an hour (I think), so I think there is a silent delay somewhere.

title: kube::util::wait-for-jobs fails to set fail on fail

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: kind/flake
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a flaky test.

milestone.title: v1.2
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/wiki/Release-1.2

body:
kube::util::wait-for-jobs has a fail count which is declared `local`.  cluster/gce/util.sh does this:

```
  # Wait for last batch of jobs
  kube::util::wait-for-jobs || {
    echo -e "${color_red}${fail} commands failed.${color_norm}" >&2
  }
```

But if wait-for-jobs fails, fail is not set.  This gives an error like `cluster/gce/util.sh: line 699: fail: unbound variable`  e.g. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/17919#issuecomment-173378103

cc @quinton-hoole

milestone.title: v1.2

body:
The PR #19061 added functionality to push docker images during the release, but the new workflow requires a special valentine-locked gcloud authorization to proceed.  The new workflow simply assumes the user is logged into gcloud with the k8s.production.user@gmail.com user.

We need to figure out a way to seamlessly auth and allow this new functionality to run without interrupting the release workflow.

Rolling back is an option, but preferably we could just fix this somehow.

title: Secrets broken on Docker 1.9.1 on non-containerized kubelet

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
I am running Docker 1.9.1 on Kubernetes 1.1.3 on SL6 with a 3.10.0-229.14.1.el7.x86_64 kernel with a NON-containerized kubelet. Secrets mounting works fine on the same host when I am running on Docker 1.7.1.

```
kind: Secret
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name:
    mysecret
data:
  abc: ZGVm # "def"
```

```
kind: Pod
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: mypod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: nginx
      image: docker-registry-vip.dev.box.net/jenkins/nginx
      volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: "/secret"
          name: "secret"
          readOnly: true
  volumes:
    - name: secret
      secret:
        secretName: mysecret
```

```
$ kubectl create -f secret.yaml
secret "mysecret" created
$ kubectl create -f pod.yaml
pod "mypod" created
```

All those setup steps are same on Docker 1.7.1 and Docker 1.9.1. This is what happens on Docker 1.7.1 (working):

```
$ # docker exec into the pod's container
$ sudo docker exec -t -i 683 /bin/bash
root@mypod:/# ls -al /secret/
total 8
drwxrwxrwt  2 root root   60 Jan 13 23:18 .
drwxr-xr-x 22 root root 4096 Jan 13 23:26 ..
-r--r--r--  1 root root    3 Jan 13 23:18 abc
root@mypod:/# ls -al /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/
drwxrwxrwt 2 root root   80 Jan 13 23:18 .
drwxr-xr-x 3 root root 4096 Jan 13 23:26 ..
-r--r--r-- 1 root root 7845 Jan 13 23:18 ca.crt
-r--r--r-- 1 root root  846 Jan 13 23:18 token
root@mypod:/#
```

This is what happens when I upgrade the machine to Docker 1.9.1 (not working):

```
$ # docker exec into the pod's container
$ sudo docker exec -t -i 2fc /bin/bash
root@mypod:/# ls -al /secret/
root@mypod:/# ls -al /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/
root@mypod:/#
```

With Docker 1.9.1, the files DO exist on the host:

```
$ sudo ls -al /var/lib/kubelet/pods/ea4ad4dd-ba4b-11e5-bc0f-005056894f70/volumes/kubernetes.io~secret/secret
total 8
drwxrwxrwt 2 root root   60 Jan 13 15:18 .
drwxr-xr-x 4 root root 4096 Jan 13 15:18 ..
-r--r--r-- 1 root root    3 Jan 13 15:18 abc
$ sudo ls -al /var/lib/kubelet/pods/ea4ad4dd-ba4b-11e5-bc0f-005056894f70/volumes/kubernetes.io~secret/default-token-7pgja
total 16
drwxrwxrwt 2 root root   80 Jan 13 15:18 .
drwxr-xr-x 4 root root 4096 Jan 13 15:18 ..
-r--r--r-- 1 root root 7845 Jan 13 15:18 ca.crt
-r--r--r-- 1 root root  846 Jan 13 15:18 token
```

So it seems that for both the kubernetes service account secret and user-specified secrets, the files get pulled down to the host but are not viewable from the container.

labels.name: kind/bug

milestone.title: v1.4
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.4/Release-1.4.md

body:
Description of problem:
kubernetes/deployment: Proportional scaling while rolling out have unexpected result in unpause. 

Version-Release number of selected component (if applicable):

```
# kubectl version
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"4+", GitVersion:"v1.4.0-alpha.0.890+ecfd4aa131035a", GitCommit:"ecfd4aa131035a4747cfdf90d89a2fe823341657", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2016-06-27T08:34:32Z", GoVersion:"go1.6.2", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"4+", GitVersion:"v1.4.0-alpha.0.890+ecfd4aa131035a", GitCommit:"ecfd4aa131035a4747cfdf90d89a2fe823341657", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2016-06-27T08:34:32Z", GoVersion:"go1.6.2", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
```

How reproducible:
Always

[Problem]: Proportional scaling and rollout have unexpected result in unpause. 
Steps to Reproduce:
Step 1. Generate a deployment with two RSs, as below:
Deployment.replicas=10
maxSurge=3
maxUnavailabl=2

```
# kubectl get rs
NAME                         DESIRED   CURRENT   AGE
nginx-deployment-508933516   8         8         33s
nginx-deployment-520009149   5         5         9s
```

How to generate above two RSs:
Step 1.1 Create deployment with below yaml file:

```
apiVersion: extensions/v1beta1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nginx-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 10
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:1.7.1
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
  strategy:
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 3
      maxUnavailable: 2
    type: RollingUpdate
```

Step 1.2 Edit deployment, and change image from `nginx:1.7.1` to `nginx:abc`

Step 2. Edit deployment, change replicas from 10 to 20 and image from `nginx:abc` to `nginx:123` together

```
# kubectl edit deployment/nginx-deployment
deployment "nginx-deployment" edited
```

Step 3. Check scaled result via: `# kubectl get rs`

Actual results: Only the the new rs scale up 10 replicas in unpause.
Step 3. Check scaled result

```
# kubectl get rs
NAME                          DESIRED   CURRENT   AGE
nginx-deployment-1690416429   10        10        12s
nginx-deployment-508933516    8         8         5m
nginx-deployment-520009149    5         5         2m
```

Expected results: Proportional scaling should work while rolling out in unpause, result should be same with in pause and then resume.
Step 3. Check scaled result

```
# kubectl get rs
NAME                          DESIRED   CURRENT   AGE
nginx-deployment-1690416429   5         5         5s
nginx-deployment-508933516    14        14        2m
nginx-deployment-520009149    4         4         1m
```

Additional info: 
I also did some comparing test in pause, the result looks well.
Steps from comparing test:
Step 1. Generate a deployment with two RSs, as below:
Deployment.replicas=10
maxSurge=3
maxUnavailabl=2

```
# kubectl get rs
NAME                         DESIRED   CURRENT   AGE
nginx-deployment-508933516   8         8         33s
nginx-deployment-520009149   5         5         9s
```

Step 2. Pause deployment

```
# kubectl rollout pause deployment nginx-deployment
deployment "nginx-deployment" paused
```

Step 3. Edit deployment, change replicas from 10 to 20 and image from `nginx:abc` to `nginx:123`

```
# kubectl edit deployment/nginx-deployment
deployment "nginx-deployment" edited
```

Step 4. Check scaled result

```
# kubectl get rs
NAME                         DESIRED   CURRENT   AGE
nginx-deployment-508933516   14        14        1m
nginx-deployment-520009149   9         9         1m
```

Step 5. Resume deployment

```
# kc rollout resume deployment nginx-deployment
deployment "nginx-deployment" resumed
```

Step 6. Check rs again

```
# kubectl get rs
NAME                          DESIRED   CURRENT   AGE
nginx-deployment-1690416429   5         5         18s
nginx-deployment-508933516    14        14        2m
nginx-deployment-520009149    4         4         1m
```

title: restclient only retries if Retry-After header is set.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
We want the client to retry on 500s and 429s, but it currently only does so if the Retry-After header is set.

This appears to be the underlying cause of #27839, #27537, and #27506.

The [retryAfterSeconds function](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/client/restclient/request.go#L1022) tries to parse the Retry-After header to determine a server-indicated minimum backoff. If it doesn't find one (or can't parse it), it returns `0, false`, which means "no retry." It should return `0, true`.

body:
This is at least partially responsible for #27320 - some tests can't run when dns is down. 
Logs from just before the crash:

```
I0622 14:14:13.889398       1 logs.go:41] skydns: failure to forward request "read udp 10.180.1.8:43875->169.254.169.254:53: i/o timeout"
I0622 14:14:14.894338       1 dns.go:421] Received DNS Request:kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local., exact:false
I0622 14:14:14.894365       1 dns.go:453] records:[], retval:[], path:[local cluster svc default kubernetes]
I0622 14:14:15.826099       1 dns.go:156] Ignoring error while waiting for service default/kubernetes: Get https://10.0.0.1:443/api/v1/namespaces/default/services/kubernetes: dial tcp 10.0.0.1:443: getsockopt: no route to host. Sleeping 1s before retrying.
E0622 14:14:15.826174       1 reflector.go:216] pkg/dns/dns.go:139: Failed to list *api.Service: Get https://10.0.0.1:443/api/v1/services?resourceVersion=0: dial tcp 10.0.0.1:443: getsockopt: no route to host
E0622 14:14:15.826216       1 reflector.go:216] pkg/dns/dns.go:138: Failed to list *api.Endpoints: Get https://10.0.0.1:443/api/v1/endpoints?resourceVersion=0: dial tcp 10.0.0.1:443: getsockopt: no route to host
F0622 14:14:18.682159       1 server.go:124] Received signal: terminated
```

It got killed because Kubelet decided to kill it (readiness probe failed):

```
I0622 14:14:18.379547    8526 prober.go:106] Readiness probe for "kube-dns-v15-scynu_kube-system(c4a78332-3881-11e6-a37e-42010af00002):kubedns" failed (failure): Get http://10.180.1.8:8081/readiness: net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
I0622 14:14:18.380077    8526 server.go:651] Event(api.ObjectReference{Kind:"Pod", Namespace:"kube-system", Name:"kube-dns-v15-scynu", UID:"c4a78332-3881-11e6-a37e-42010af00002", APIVersion:"v1", ResourceVersion:"277", FieldPath:"spec.containers{kubedns}"}): type: 'Warning' reason: 'Unhealthy' Readiness probe failed: Get http://10.180.1.8:8081/readiness: net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
I0622 14:14:18.380134    8526 prober.go:106] Liveness probe for "kube-dns-v15-scynu_kube-system(c4a78332-3881-11e6-a37e-42010af00002):kubedns" failed (failure): Get http://10.180.1.8:8080/healthz: net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
I0622 14:14:18.380162    8526 kubelet.go:2577] SyncLoop (container unhealthy): "kube-dns-v15-scynu_kube-system(c4a78332-3881-11e6-a37e-42010af00002)"
```

It started happening quite recently - I'm trying to locate a build which caused this. Repro:
run "Kubelet should not restart containers across restart" test - it caused this behavior for me multiple times today.

cc @wojtek-t @piosz @davidopp @kubernetes/goog-cluster - I applied the P0/v1.3 label/milestone, as I think it should be a blocker. Feel free to decrease the priority if you disagree @goltermann

body:
We have been solving the support for kubenet, but however there's a little left for cni plugin support: The cniNetworkPlugin bails out if the runtime [is not docker](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.3.0-beta.1/pkg/kubelet/network/cni/cni.go#L141), ehh..

Will work out a PR ASAP.

title: Can't create LoadBalancer on medium->large GCE clusters

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

milestone.title: v1.2
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/wiki/Release-1.2

body:
Customer impact: Attempts to create services with type `LoadBalancer` will never get an external IP or any GCE object created on all clusters >=124 nodes (with variably cutoffs starting even at 72 nodes, depending on the cluster name). I believe, but haven't tested, that L7LB will fail to create firewalls on these size clusters as well (based on code inspection).

Analysis: There's an issue in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/090e6ff660d82120c17f10fe63d9f8a1c1aa23b3/pkg/cloudprovider/providers/gce/gce.go#L2430 where, depending on the name of the cluster, if you attempt to call the function with x > ~100 nodes (roughly, it depends on the cluster name), the GCE API will reject you because the `Filter()` parameter is too large.

At some larger cluster sizes, the API endpoint just outright rejects the `GET` request completely, versus clearly indicating the `Filter()` is wrong.

This is a problem in all 1.2.x and forward.

I have a PR incoming for base k8s, then we'll probably need to rev L7LB as well.

title: Make volume manager more robust across restarts

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: kind/documentation
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to documentation.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
When kubelet is restarted, volume manager loses its internal state. It rebuilds this state and calls attach/mount on volumes that may already be attached/mounted.

This issue is to track two items:
1. Verify that if mount is called on a volume that is already mounted that it does not fail.
2. If a pod was deleted while kubelet was unavailable, the associated volume will not be unmounted (since Kubelet would not know about it after restart). So volume_manager should find a way to recover the pre-attached volumes and populate actual state of the world on startup so that they get cleaned up appropriately.
