title: Test Flake Exit Criteria: flake issue SLO

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/testing
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Testing.

labels.name: lifecycle/rotten
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

body:
An automated system for getting humans to fix flakes. From the [doc shared with kubernetes-dev mailing list](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jnGRrZymgnXoVUNnZVER_TOKH_Z11VvsKxlLxU1gg0A/edit#heading=h.4zycjcwy0c59).

The goal here is to have a redundancy in the system: if a flake has been assigned to someone without activity for long enough, we need something to cause either a reassignment or cause the human to actually work on the thing.

Daily, generate the following reports:
- Average age of open flakes, bucketed by priority.
  - Start counting from when the flake was filed or its most recent priority change.
- All flake issues violating the SLO defined below.
  - Maybe send this list as an email to kubernetes-dev if it’s not empty?
- All flake issues half as old as the SLO defined below.
  - Automatically make a comment on each of these issues asking the owner to update their status. Do this on {P0, P1, P2} issues no more than once per {12, 24, 48} hours

Idea to get the ball rolling. Define the below:
- Flake fix/activity SLOs:
  - flakes labeled P0:
  - We expect a fix in 2 days.
  - flakes labeled P1:
  - We expect a fix in 1 week.
  - flakes labeled P2:
  - We expect a fix in 2 weeks.

Generate reports of all issues violating the SLO. Send these reports to the contact for the org that the assignees are a part of. TODO: identify teeth. We could block PRs from orgs out of compliance, but that’s very drastic. Hopefully we can think of something friendlier.

title: Test Flake Exit Criteria: Presubmit test requirements

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/testing
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Testing.

labels.name: lifecycle/rotten
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

body:
From the [doc shared with kubernetes-dev mailing list](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jnGRrZymgnXoVUNnZVER_TOKH_Z11VvsKxlLxU1gg0A/)

All presubmit test jobs:
- Must finish in less than 30 minutes.
- Because it's frustrating to have a hard timeout, to keep this rule,
  - Our actual time goal is 20 minutes.
  - Human(s) need to be alerted or paged if the test run goes above 30 minutes.
  - That should be treated as a P0 issue until the time is below 30 minutes again.

If we're over 30 minutes per retest, we can't possibly hope to keep up with demand.

body:

The problem is this [line](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/replication/replication_controller.go#L357). It should enqueue the old rc if old rc exists.

title: Supplemental groups on PVs mutate pod spec in kubelet

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

body:
#20490 added a beta feature which allows PVs to be annotated with a GID that owns them.  This is to facilitate volumes like NFS that cannot be safely chowned/chmoded from the client and thus do not work with FSGroup.  There are a couple issues with this PR that need to be sorted out:
1.  The pod spec should not be mutated.  We should formalize in the contract for volume plugins that the `api.Pod` they are passed is a read-only view and should not be mutated.  We should probably do a copy of the pod when creating Mounters.
2.  Currently there is no security policy check to see whether the Pod can use the supplemental group the volume is annotated with.  We must be able to validate this.

@kubernetes/sig-storage

title: cAdvisor /stats/summary endpoint in kubelet returns incorrect cpu usage numbers

labels.name: kind/bug

body: ### Environment Kubernetes version: 1.2.3 Docker version: 1.10.3 3 node(c4.xLarge) cluster on AWS running CoreOS 1010.4.0. ### Issue After facing an issue with incorrect metrics being reported by heapster kubernetes/heapster#1177 I tried querying the cadvisor /stats/summary endpoint directly to see if that would give me consistent values for node cpu usage. title: The multizone setting in gce.conf is ignored

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
I tried spinning up a multizone cluster with 1.3.0-alpha.5, and the multizone option isn't passed through, so nodes in other zones register and are immediately deleted by node controller.

Sample output from kube-controller-manager.log

```
I0609 20:58:18.386281       9 nodecontroller.go:643] Deleting node (no longer present in cloud provider): multi-zone-minion-group-f73f
I0609 20:58:18.386318       9 nodecontroller.go:720] Recording Deleting Node multi-zone-minion-group-f73f because it's not present according to cloud provider event message for node multi-zone-minion-group-f73f
W0609 20:58:18.386359       9 nodecontroller.go:787] Missing timestamp for Node multi-zone-minion-group-sds7. Assuming now as a timestamp.
I0609 20:58:18.386538       9 event.go:216] Event(api.ObjectReference{Kind:"Node", Namespace:"", Name:"multi-zone-minion-group-f73f", UID:"multi-zone-minion-group-f73f", APIVersion:"", ResourceVersion:"", FieldPath:""}): type: 'Normal' reason: 'DeletingNode' Node multi-zone-minion-group-f73f event: Deleting Node multi-zone-minion-group-f73f because it's not present according to cloud provider
E0609 20:58:18.462865       9 gce.go:2467] getInstanceByName/single-zone: failed to get instance multi-zone-minion-group-sds7; err: googleapi: Error 404: The resource 'projects/jeffmltest/zones/us-central1-b/instances/multi-zone-minion-group-sds7' was not found, notFound

```

It appears that we have an e2e test for this, http://kubekins.dls.corp.google.com/job/kubernetes-e2e-gce-ubernetes-lite/. However, the test has the exact same failure, and is not catching that the master is running in single-zone mode. From the latest passing run (https://console.cloud.google.com/storage/browser/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/kubernetes-e2e-gce-ubernetes-lite/4643)

```
I0609 21:02:00.157122       6 nodecontroller.go:720] Recording Registered Node jenkins-e2e-minion-group-z3jn in NodeController event message for node jenkins-e2e-minion-group-z3jn

I0609 21:02:00.157168       6 nodecontroller.go:822] Node jenkins-e2e-minion-group-kixe ReadyCondition updated. Updating timestamp.

I0609 21:02:00.157537       6 event.go:216] Event(api.ObjectReference{Kind:"Node", Namespace:"", Name:"jenkins-e2e-minion-group-s3qs", UID:"jenkins-e2e-minion-group-s3qs", APIVersion:"", ResourceVersion:"", FieldPath:""}): type: 'Normal' reason: 'RegisteredNode' Node jenkins-e2e-minion-group-s3qs event: Registered Node jenkins-e2e-minion-group-s3qs in NodeController
I0609 21:02:00.157583       6 event.go:216] Event(api.ObjectReference{Kind:"Node", Namespace:"", Name:"jenkins-e2e-minion-group-u3fe", UID:"jenkins-e2e-minion-group-u3fe", APIVersion:"", ResourceVersion:"", FieldPath:""}): type: 'Normal' reason: 'RegisteredNode' Node jenkins-e2e-minion-group-u3fe event: Registered Node jenkins-e2e-minion-group-u3fe in NodeController
I0609 21:02:00.157597       6 event.go:216] Event(api.ObjectReference{Kind:"Node", Namespace:"", Name:"jenkins-e2e-minion-group-z3jn", UID:"jenkins-e2e-minion-group-z3jn", APIVersion:"", ResourceVersion:"", FieldPath:""}): type: 'Normal' reason: 'RegisteredNode' Node jenkins-e2e-minion-group-z3jn event: Registered Node jenkins-e2e-minion-group-z3jn in NodeController
E0609 21:02:00.258501       6 gce.go:2492] getInstanceByName/single-zone: failed to get instance jenkins-e2e-minion-group-s3qs; err: googleapi: Error 404: The resource 'projects/k8s-jkns-e2e-gce-ubelite/zones/us-central1-a/instances/jenkins-e2e-minion-group-s3qs' was not found, notFound
I0609 21:02:00.258559       6 nodecontroller.go:643] Deleting node (no longer present in cloud provider): jenkins-e2e-minion-group-s3qs
I0609 21:02:00.258570       6 nodecontroller.go:720] Recording Deleting Node jenkins-e2e-minion-group-s3qs because it's not present according to cloud provider event message for node jenkins-e2e-minion-group-s3qs
```

Note the the gce.conf file does exist on the master, but is apparently not being plumbed through, as kube-controller-manager.log is missing the expected ["Using GCE provider config %+v"](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/cloudprovider/providers/gce/gce.go#L269)

This needs to be fixed asap for 1.3. cc @quinton-hoole @andyzheng0831. kubernetes-e2e-gce-ubernetes-lite should also be failing right now, since it's supposed to test this functionality.

milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
This appears to be a regression. Create an nginx pod and service such as:

``` yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: echoheaders
  labels:
    app: echoheaders
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 8080
    protocol: TCP
    name: http
  selector:
    app: echoheaders

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ReplicationController
metadata:
  name: echoheaders
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: echoheaders
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: echoheaders
        image: gcr.io/google_containers/echoserver:1.3
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
```

And a test pod like:

``` yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: busybox
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - image: radial/busyboxplus:curl
    command:
      - sleep
      - "3600"
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    name: busybox
    volumeMounts:
    - mountPath: /tmp/foo
      name: test
  volumes:
  - name: test
    emptyDir: {}
  restartPolicy: Always
```

Try and get them to land on different nodes. 

``` console
19:52:02-beeps~/logs]$ k get svc
NAME          CLUSTER-IP     EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)   AGE
echoheaders   10.0.204.199   <none>        80/TCP    3h
kubernetes    10.0.0.1       <none>        443/TCP   4h

$ k exec -it busybox /bin/sh
[ root@busybox:/ ]$ ip addr
1: lo: <LOOPBACK,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 65536 qdisc noqueue 
    link/loopback 00:00:00:00:00:00 brd 00:00:00:00:00:00
    inet 127.0.0.1/8 scope host lo
       valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever
    inet6 ::1/128 scope host 
       valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever
3: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1460 qdisc noqueue 
    link/ether 0a:58:0a:b4:01:08 brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
    inet 10.180.1.8/24 scope global eth0
       valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever
    inet6 fe80::20db:d6ff:febd:ed7b/64 scope link 
       valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever
```

curl the service vip

``` console
[ root@busybox:/ ]$ wget -qO- 10.0.204.199
CLIENT VALUES:
client_address=10.240.0.5
command=GET
real path=/
query=nil
request_version=1.1
request_uri=http://10.0.204.199:8080/

SERVER VALUES:
server_version=nginx: 1.9.11 - lua: 10001

HEADERS RECEIVED:
connection=close
host=10.0.204.199
user-agent=Wget
BODY:
-no body in request-
```

And in another window:

``` console
19:52:42-beeps~/logs]$ k logs echoheaders-k5fs5 --follow
10.240.0.5 - - [09/Jun/2016:02:53:21 +0000] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 386 "-" "Wget"
```

I expected a source ip of `10.180.1.8`. We should just be DNATing to the pod ip.
I see rules like:

```
:CNI-252089a662c3409f212af1da - [0:0]
-A POSTROUTING -s 10.180.1.0/24 -m comment --comment "name: \"kubenet\" id: \"dc71fad93e755458b75b6cc3379b4f0052941ce4612a06d7c421ec5c1e522168\"" -j CNI-252089a662c3409f212af1da
-A CNI-252089a662c3409f212af1da -d 10.180.1.0/24 -m comment --comment "name: \"kubenet\" id: \"dc71fad93e755458b75b6cc3379b4f0052941ce4612a06d7c421ec5c1e522168\"" -j ACCEPT
-A CNI-252089a662c3409f212af1da ! -d 224.0.0.0/4 -m comment --comment "name: \"kubenet\" id: \"dc71fad93e755458b75b6cc3379b4f0052941ce4612a06d7c421ec5c1e522168\"" -j MASQUERADE
```

@kubernetes/sig-network @dcbw

title: Validating GCI image as the default image for GCE & GKE

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

milestone.title: v1.4
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.4/Release-1.4.md

body:
We want to deprecate today's debian-based container-vm image, and switch to GCI image by default. Before we do that, we need to validate the image using Kubernetes testing infrastructure. GCI image has three different release channels: dev, beta, and stable. Besides that they also build ci release nightly. Today we already run the the following jenkins jobs against each image release: 
- kubernetes-gce-e2e, 
- kubernetes-gce-e2e-slow,
- kubernetes-gce-e2e-serial

But we are missing kubernetes-gce-e2e-soak, kubernetes-gce-e2e-scalability, probably also kubernetes-gce-e2e-upgrade (? not sure how to handle this since it is the first release), and kubernetes-gce-e2e-features.

We also need to include gci image to node-e2e test suite too. 

Next step we should to identify the critical builds for gci to block merge-bot. 

Eventually, we can switch GCI image as the default image on GCE, but keep debian-based container-vm image testing until we can deprecate it.

@andyzheng0831 and @wonderfly are going to write detail plan on this. 

cc/ @roberthbailey from GKE side. 
cc/ @mansoorj from PM side

title: Unit test flake: TestCheckVersionCompatibility() Expected value not to be nil

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: kind/flake
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a flaky test.

body:
The recently merged PR #21741 added a version cache in dockertools, which makes the test [`TestCheckVersionCompatibility`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/dockertools/manager_test.go#L1856-L1895) flaky.

```
--- FAIL: TestCheckVersionCompatibility (0.01s)
         <autogenerated>:31:                                 Error Trace:    manager_test.go:1892
                 Error:          Expected value not to be nil.
                 Messages:       test case #0 test version "1.20" version error check

FAIL
```

The reason is that `TestCheckVersionCompatibility` injected error into fake_docker_client and then expected to see the error from `fake_docker_client.Version()` right after that (See [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/dockertools/manager_test.go#L1890-L1892)). However, the error was consumed by the goroutine which periodically updates the version cache (See [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/dockertools/manager.go#L262)).

The docker daemon version is rarely updated, and we only need version once for each container creating, during which we also do container create, start, inspect  #etc.
1) Do we care about the cost of the `Version` call so much that we have to introduce the complexity?
2) Kubelet periodically calls `runtime.Status()`, can we rely on that to update the cache? 

Anyhow, at least, we should disable the cache or have a fake one in the unit test. :)

@yujuhong @vishh @resouer 
/cc @kubernetes/sig-node

title: Volume attached/detached info out of sync at master when node is terminated.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

body:
## User reported issue:

When AWS nodes are terminated and then later replaced by AWS cluster, some pods are found mounted to the wrong volumes.
## Problem analysis:

The cause of this issue is that when nodes are terminated, volumes are detached without noticed by the volume manager.
In current design, master is responsible for attaching/detaching volumes. After the operation attach/detach finishes, volume controller will cache this information (which volume is attached to a node) into actual state of world. The reconciler then periodically compares actual state and desired state to trigger attach/detach if needed. However, the cached actual state might be out of sync in case

- Node is terminated so that the volume is also detached.
- User explicitly detach the volume from the node

When the above events happen, the controller is not aware that volume is already detached and of course the device path is no longer valid. So the actual state will not change and reconciler continue to think the volume is still attached to the node with the old device path. On node side, if kubelet happens to mount the volume, it will use the wrong device path which might belong to other volumes. The following describes the sequence of events that could cause AWS mounting to wrong volume issue
1. An AWS volume is attached to node on device path (/dev/path1) by master and kubelet mount the volume on the path.
2. Node is terminated (volume will be also detached by AWS) or user explicitly detach the volume to node, master will try evicts the pods from the node after detecting node is not responding.
3. At master, reconciler tries to detach the volume since pods are deleted. However, it won’t trigger detach for a while because the node status shows that the volume is still mounted by kubelet (Note: kubelet periodically updates which volumes are mounted to node status. When kubelet dies, the status will not be changed for a while). So at this moment, master thinks the volume is still attached to the node on a /dev/path1, but it is no longer true.
4. Node is rebooted, the master create some pods on the same node. At the node, kubelet tries to check whether the volume still attached to the node before trigger mounting operation. Because of step 3, since master still thinks volume is attached to /dev/path1, kubelet will use /dev/path1 to mount this volume. However /dev/path1 could be used by other AWS volumes after it is freed up by step 3. After mounting, the pod will get wrong volume.
### Why this issue only happens on AWS cluster, not GCE?

AWS dynamically assign devices to attached volumes. Once detached, the device is become available and might be assigned to other attached volumes immediately. Since the attached volume information is cached in master, if volume is detached without proper triggering detach volume operation through master, the cached information will be stale and cause kubelet mount to the wrong device. 
For GCE cluster, GCE only uses a fixed device path for each volume using their pd names and the device path will not be assigned to other volumes. Since a device path is statically mapped to the volume so it won’t cause the above mounting to wrong volume problem. But stale information might still problems. For example, a volume is attached to a node. After the node is terminated and restarted, master still thinks the volume is attached in actual state, and will not try to attach it ever again. 
## Proposal:

To solve this problem, I proposed the following two fixes on volume controller and AWS attacher respectively. 
On Master, a sync state process will be added to periodically check whether the cached attached volume in actual state is actually still attached. Cloud providers such gce, aws have the functions to check whether the volume is attached to the node (instance). To avoid putting high number of requests to cloud provider, batch operation to check a list of volumes will be issued per node instead of one request per volume. Currently I proposal to check which disks are attached on a node every 1-3 second. The checking will be asynchronous (with a go routine per node).  
On AWS attacher, when assigning devices to volumes, propose to use random selection instead of using alphabet order. In this way, the chance the same device will be reused immediately will be highly reduced. 
### Verify the proposal

Potential race condition between periodic state sync up and other volume operations?
Volume operations (attach/detach) and state sync up (check volume still attached or not) are all asynchronous (each operation uses a go routine). With operation executor, Attach/Detach operations on the same volume is serialized to avoid race condition during attach/detach operations and updating actual states. State sync up operation is checking a list of volumes through cloud provider to see whether they are still attached. It has three steps
1. Retrieve a list of volumes for each node
2. Make a request to cloud provider to get the attached volumes of each node
3. Update states if any volumes to check is no longer attached according to b

During this checking, attach or detach operations might be going on and interleave with the above steps. Considering the following scenarios
- After check the volume is not attached, an attach operation finishes and mark volume is attached in actual state, but the check will mark back the volume as detached. The result is that volume is already attached, but actual state records it is not. The reconciler will correct this situation by issuing another attach operation and update the state. (Interleaving detach operation should not affect anything)
- After check the volume is attached, an detach operation finishes and update the state. The sync process will not change anything which cause no problem. (Interleaving attach operation has no effect)
### Will the proposed approach solve the problem completely?

No. Detach/attach might happen at any moment. On AWS, if user manually detach and attach volumes very quickly, the mounted path will be changed and master will not catch this change right now. But with above fixes 1 and 2, the chances of mounting to the wrong volume should be much lower. Node termination and reboot will take normally much longer time and periodic updates every few second should be sufficient to catch the change.
## Performance overhead

The added overhead for this change is to periodically send requests to cloud provider to get the instance information. It would be one request for node. So the overhead would be proportional to the number of the nodes in the cluster. Will work on some scalability tests to cover this issue.

title: etcd3 watcher doesn't scale

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/scalability
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scalability.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
I did some scalability tests with etcd3 enabled and it seems that watcher.go pretty much doesn't scale.

I think the problem we have is with `tranform` function:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/storage/etcd3/watcher.go#L234

So to give you some numbers, in 2000-node kubemark, I started cluster at:

```
I0928 09:48:36.043709    3547 config.go:404] Will report 10.240.0.24 as public IP address.
I0928 09:48:36.045790    3547 server.go:328] Initalizing cache sizes based on 120000MB limit
```

and 12 second later I started getting:

```
W0928 09:48:48.398584    3547 watcher.go:319] Fast watcher, slow processing. Number of buffered events: 100.Probably caused by slow decoding, user not receiving fast, or other processing logic
```

I have **millions** of such lines in my logs.

Note that this was empty cluster - there weren't any pods at that time in the system - so it was mostly traffic from nodes.

**This is pretty much a blocker for launching etcd3 - we can't launch with worse performance than etcd2**

@kubernetes/sig-scalability @xiang90 @hongchaodeng @timothysc

title: NFS PV tests are failing on GCI

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

body:
Relevant test failures: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/33401

I ran the e2e that "create a PV and a pre-bound PVC: test write access" and it fails on GCI. 
I debugged a bit and figured that the mount command is failing - 

``` shell
Sep 24 21:17:31.083: INFO: At 2016-09-24 21:11:05 -0700 PDT - event for write-pod-1mzyy: {kubelet e2e-test-vishnuk-minion-group-jo
4u} FailedMount: MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "kubernetes.io/nfs/13fd01f0-82d6-11e6-959f-42010af00002-nfs-1nmbf" (spec.Name
: "nfs-1nmbf") pod "13fd01f0-82d6-11e6-959f-42010af00002" (UID: "13fd01f0-82d6-11e6-959f-42010af00002") with: mount failed: exit s
tatus 32
Mounting arguments: 10.180.0.10:/exports /var/lib/kubelet/pods/13fd01f0-82d6-11e6-959f-42010af00002/volumes/kubernetes.io~nfs/nfs-
1nmbf nfs []
Output: mount: wrong fs type, bad option, bad superblock on 10.180.0.10:/exports,
       missing codepage or helper program, or other error
       (for several filesystems (e.g. nfs, cifs) you might
       need a /sbin/mount.<type> helper program)

       In some cases useful info is found in syslog - try
       dmesg | tail or so.
```

Looking at the kernel logs, I got the following information:

``` text
Sep 25 04:10:26 e2e-test-vishnuk-minion-group-jo4u kernel: RPC: Registered named UNIX socket transport module.
Sep 25 04:10:26 e2e-test-vishnuk-minion-group-jo4u kernel: RPC: Registered udp transport module.
Sep 25 04:10:26 e2e-test-vishnuk-minion-group-jo4u kernel: RPC: Registered tcp transport module.
Sep 25 04:10:26 e2e-test-vishnuk-minion-group-jo4u kernel: RPC: Registered tcp NFSv4.1 backchannel transport module.
Sep 25 04:10:26 e2e-test-vishnuk-minion-group-jo4u kernel: Installing knfsd (copyright (C) 1996 okir@monad.swb.de).
Sep 25 04:10:26 e2e-test-vishnuk-minion-group-jo4u kernel: NFSD: attempt to initialize umh client tracking in a container ignored.
Sep 25 04:10:26 e2e-test-vishnuk-minion-group-jo4u kernel: NFSD: attempt to initialize legacy client tracking in a container ignored.
Sep 25 04:10:26 e2e-test-vishnuk-minion-group-jo4u kernel: NFSD: Unable to initialize client recovery tracking! (-22)
Sep 25 04:10:26 e2e-test-vishnuk-minion-group-jo4u kernel: NFSD: starting 10-second grace period (net ffff8801e8941840)
```

I looked at the NFS server logs and found the following:

```
Serving /exports
rpcinfo: can't contact rpcbind: : RPC: Unable to receive; errno = Connection refused
Starting rpcbind
exportfs: /exports does not support NFS export
NFS started
```

I'd like to know if this is a test setup issue or a base image issue? NFS has been confirmed to be working on GCI by other users of GCI. Even then, I'd like to understand the reason for the NFS PV test failure in GCI.

cc @matchstick @saad-ali @kubernetes/sig-storage @thockin @Amey-D

title: Kube-dns should not be setting CPU limits

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

milestone.title: v1.4
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.4/Release-1.4.md

body:
CPU limits are enforced on most distros excepting Google's debian based containerVM. The current CPU limits for kube-dns are not based on empirical data ( quoting @bprashanth ). 
The kube-dns pod is already in the `Burstable` class. I propose removing CPU limits altogether until we profile kube-dns in more detail.
This issue will impact users.

title: Dialing different nodes breaks TLS-verified master<->kubelet connections

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

milestone.title: v1.4
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.4/Release-1.4.md

body:
When the master dials nodes, it is mutating the tlsConfig held by the master kubelet client, to add a server name.

That means if two different nodes are dialed from a master started with `--kubelet-certificate-authority`, x509 verification will fail for the second one.

Introduced in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/7e9d82129e58196b2d3f0b22e6b139c1c6b04dd1#diff-e00658bdc0ba8e28b32f709e4e41558eR72

**Kubernetes version** (use `kubectl version`): v1.4.0-beta.8
`Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"4+", GitVersion:"v1.4.0-beta.8", GitCommit:"3040f87c570a772ce94349b379f41f329494a4f7", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2016-09-19T07:54:34Z", GoVersion:"go1.7", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"4+", GitVersion:"v1.4.0-beta.8", GitCommit:"3040f87c570a772ce94349b379f41f329494a4f7", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2016-09-19T07:54:34Z", GoVersion:"go1.7", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}`

**Environment**:
- **Cloud provider or hardware configuration**: virsh
- **OS** (e.g. from /etc/os-release): Debian GNU/Linux 8 (jessie)
- **Kernel** (e.g. `uname -a`): Linux 299e561bce9845aeb537a4a1a50a4562.dev.local-planet 3.10.0-327.el7.x86_64 #1 SMP Thu Oct 29 17:29:29 EDT 2015 x86_64 GNU/Linux
- **Install tools**:
- **Others**:

**What happened**:
kubectl w/o cluster configuration does not connect to apiserver with the following error: `The connection to the server localhost:8080 was refused - did you specify the right host or port?`

**What you expected to happen**:
kubectl w/o parameters used to connect using in-cluster approach, using a token and `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST` / `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT` pair

**How to reproduce it** (as minimally and precisely as possible):
Install a cluster with `k8s 1.4-beta.8`, run a pod with `kubectl` and issue any command

**Anything else do we need to know**:
I think the problem is in this line:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/32613/files#diff-47197a425491d7fcfa69115333533db9R116

``` go
if IsConfigurationInvalid(defErr) && !IsEmptyConfig(err) {
```

where `err` (apparently) is always `nil`, and (I guess) should be the following instead:

``` go
if IsConfigurationInvalid(defErr) && !IsEmptyConfig(defErr) {
```

title: Manual upgrade: No CA_CERT in metadata after upgrade on GCE

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

milestone.title: v1.4
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.4/Release-1.4.md

body:
During a manual upgrade test, described in [this doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1yv9tm5qeCqbyw5SWysHaXxSLDRZ-RmK8QRBrkbnh6Tg/edit#), a kubelet failed to communicate via SSL to its master.  
This is currently blocking the 1.4 release.

There is not a repro for this yet.

The cluster was running 1.3, and was upgraded to 1.4 successfully, but upon downgrading to 1.3, the kubelets one one or more machines are not able to talk to the master.

Current kubelet version is `v1.4.0-beta.5`. (EDITED)

The error when talking to the master is (lots like this):

```
# journalctl -u kubelet | grep x509 | tail -1
Sep 15 19:04:35 kubernetes-minion-group-20m5 kubelet[1239]: E0915 19:04:35.106381    1239 reflector.go:203] pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go:406: Failed to list *api.Node: Get https://kubernetes-master/api/v1/nodes?fieldSelector=metadata.name%3Dkubernetes-minion-group-20m5&resourceVersion=0: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```

I think this means that the kubelet cannot verify the master's cert.  I can't find the master's cert.

Since there is not flag to kubelet to tell it where to find its config, I assume it is using the default location, which is `/var/lib/kubelet/kubeconfig`.

```
# cat /var/lib/kubelet/kubeconfig
apiVersion: v1
kind: Config
users:
- name: kubelet
  user:
    client-certificate-data: 
    client-key-data: 
clusters:
- name: local
  cluster:
    certificate-authority-data: 
contexts:
- context:
    cluster: local
    user: kubelet
  name: service-account-context
current-context: service-account-context
```

It seems wrong that clusters[0].cluster.certificate-authority-data is empty.  That should have the cert for the master, right?

I see this thing:

```
# cat /mnt/stateful_partition/home/kubernetes/kube-manifests/kubernetes/kubelet-config.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Config
users:
- name: kubelet
  user:
    client-certificate-data: ${KUBELET_CERT}
    client-key-data: ${KUBELET_KEY}
clusters:
- name: local
  cluster:
    certificate-authority-data: ${CA_CERT}
contexts:
- context:
    cluster: local
    user: kubelet
  name: service-account-context
current-context: service-account-context
```

but I don't understand what process generates `/var/lib/kubelet/kubeconfig`, and if, presumably, from that template, why it isn't setting the env var CA_CERT.

title: If GarbageCollection is on, NamespaceController gets confused

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

milestone.title: v1.4
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.4/Release-1.4.md

body:
The logic flow of namespace controller is as follows:

1) estimate graceful termination for groupVersionResource
2) delete collection for groupVersionResource
3) list collection for groupVersionResource and expect 0 items unless graceful estimate != 0

This works great unless garbage collection is on.  When GC is on, the list call is not returning 0 items as expected and the namespace controller says WTF! and it sees unexpected items.  This is because the GC orphan finalizer has not yet run to completion.

If GC is on in our E2E runs, there is good reason to believe this is the source of all our namespace deletion flakes.

/cc @kubernetes/sig-api-machinery @smarterclayton @ncdc @lavalamp @caesarxuchao

title: `kubectl edit` cannot delete an element from a list of simple type

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

body:
To reproduce, create an object with multiple [finalizers](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/api/types.go#L151), and `kubectl edit` cannot remove a single finalizer from the list. This is part of the problem reported in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/32339. `kubectl update` can remove a finalizer.

I think the root cause is `kubectl edit` uses strategicmerge PATCH, but its syntax does not support deleting an element from a list of simple type, because we cannot specify a merge key.

We probably cannot fix it for 1.4, but we should at least document it somewhere.

cc @bgrant0607 @janetkuo

milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.4/Release-1.4.md

body:
Encountered some issue when exercising upgrade and downgrade master node. The following lists the steps 
1. Bring up a 1.3.6 cluster in GCE
2.  Upgrade the master to 1.4.0-alpha (cluster/gce/upgrade.sh -M v1.4.0-beta.0), verify master is running fine and the version is 1.4.0
3. Downgrade the master back to 1.3.6. Now master is no longer running correctly. Still be able to login the master with gcloud, but all related logs (etcd.log, cloud-init.log) are empty. Kubelet is not running.

title: Pods are deleted across node upgrade

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

milestone.title: v1.4
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.4/Release-1.4.md

body:
During node upgrade it looks like sometimes the node can leave the cloudprovider, leading the nodecontroller to think it should delete pods on the node. This is obviously disruptive, but if the pod is not managed by an RC, it can just disappear, which is worse. 

Create a job

``` yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: echo-success
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      name: echo-success
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: c
        image: busybox
        command: ["/bin/sh",  "-c", "echo success"]
      restartPolicy: Never
  parallelism: 3
  completions: 3
```

Wait for it to succeed and check job:

```
$ k get job 
NAME           DESIRED   SUCCESSFUL   AGE
echo-success   3         3            31m

$ k get po --show-all 
NAME                        READY     STATUS      RESTARTS   AGE       IP            NODE
echo-success-70guk   0/1       Completed   0          13m
echo-success-83k2b   0/1       Completed   0          13m
echo-success-csjo9   0/1       Completed   0          13m
```

Check nodes

```
NAME                           STATUS                     AGE
kubernetes-master              Ready,SchedulingDisabled   30s
kubernetes-minion-group-a9np   Ready                      34s
kubernetes-minion-group-bj5r   Ready                      35s
kubernetes-minion-group-c26b   Ready                      34s
```

Upgrade nodes

```
$ cluster/gce/upgrade.sh -N v1.4.0-beta.0
```

Check nodes

```
NAME                           STATUS                     AGE
kubernetes-master              Ready,SchedulingDisabled   33m
kubernetes-minion-group-a9np   Ready                      11m
kubernetes-minion-group-bj5r   Ready                      9m
kubernetes-minion-group-c26b   Ready                      7m
```

Check jobs

```
$ k get job
NAME           DESIRED   SUCCESSFUL   AGE
echo-success   3         3            29m

$ k get po --show-all -o wide
NAME                 READY     STATUS      RESTARTS   AGE       IP           NODE
echo-success-83k2b   0/1       Completed   0          29m       10.244.1.4   kubernetes-minion-group-a9np
```

This is confusing because the job says 3 but I can only see 1 when I know I saw 3 before upgrade. 
What's worse, I can't see its logs

```
$ k logs echo-success-83k2b
Error response from daemon: No such container: 35935b7065a03f7ac60edf203c1cdc19aaec6696ddbb1036aebf74509457a30d
```

Node controller has

```
I0908 22:08:28.687091       5 deletion_utils.go:273] Recording Deleting Node kubernetes-minion-group-bj5r because it's not present according to cloud provider event message for node kubernetes-minion-group-bj5r
I0908 22:08:33.689852       5 deletion_utils.go:273] Recording Removing Node kubernetes-minion-group-bj5r from NodeController event message for node kubernetes-minion-group-bj5r
I0908 22:08:33.744494       5 deletion_utils.go:273] Recording Deleting all Pods from Node kubernetes-minion-group-bj5r. event message for node kubernetes-minion-group-bj5r
W0908 22:08:55.886551       5 deletion_utils.go:168] Unable to find Node: kubernetes-minion-group-bj5r, deleting all assigned Pods.
```

@kubernetes/goog-cluster @kubernetes/goog-gke fyi for slo around node upgrade
I don't know if we want to do anything about this, marking p0 1.4 for triage.

title: ThirdParty E2E framework tests should be [Flaky] in kube 1.4

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
ThirdPartyResources (TPR) E2E test creates a custom resource type, and creates an instance of that type in a namespace.  The namespace is purged, but the namespace controller DOES NOT observe the dynamic mutation of the type hierarchy.  As a result, the instances of that type are never purged, and we could potentially leak resources.

In prior discussions of @kubernetes/sig-api-machinery we agreed that users of TPR would have to kick the namespace controller in the interim in order for it to observe the creation of the new TPR type and have it take part in namespace lifecycle.

If TPR is a priority, we should address the namespace controller issue in kube 1.5, and eliminate the [Flaky] flag from the TPR E2E.  The updates in the e2e framework that intropsect the server dynamically to verify all resources are deleted are getting tripped up by the presence of this test and impacting all others.

Here is an example:
https://k8s-gubernator.appspot.com/build/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/32278/kubernetes-pull-build-test-e2e-gce/57833/

/cc @kubernetes/sig-api-machinery @smarterclayton @lavalamp @brendandburns @ncdc @pwittrock

title: Regression in OOM score configuration starting from v1.3+

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

milestone.title: v1.4
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.4/Release-1.4.md

body:
Kubelet and docker daemon were expected to run with an `oom-score-adj` of `-999` as mentioned [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/qos/policy.go#L25) and [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/docs/design/resource-qos.md#oom-score-configuration-at-the-nodes).

This behavior has been broken since v1.3+. I consider this a serious regression because system OOMs will result in kubelet and/or docker daemon getting evicted instead of pod. QoS will essentially be broken at the node level. 

I'm working on a patch to fix this in v1.4 for now. I will then attempt to cherry-pick the patch into v1.3 release branch. 

I will also be adding a test for these settings.

cc @kubernetes/sig-node

title: HPA tests are failing in gke-large cluster

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

milestone.title: v1.4
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.4/Release-1.4.md

body:
HPA tests are currently failing in gke-large cluster suite:
http://kubekins.dls.corp.google.com:8080/view/Scalability/job/kubernetes-e2e-gke-large-cluster/

I did some debugging and the problem seems to be related to pod-nanny.

Looking into logs from the last run:
1. Heapster was first scheduled on the large node dedicated to it
2. Then pod-nany updated heapster deployment
3. And then heapster was scheduled on the normal node (when it actually shouldn't fit)
4. From that point it was never updated by the pod nanny.
5. From that point, heapster started crashlooping (OOMing) [which in fact was expected in too small machine]

So it's pretty clear that that pod-nanny changed the amount of resources to something smaller, which in fact it shouldn't.

body:
I have a container that got the broadcast address of podCIDR subnet. 
My CNI conf is:

```
{
  "cniVersion": "0.1.0",
  "name": "kubenet",
  "type": "bridge",
  "bridge": "cbr0",
  "mtu": 1460,
  "addIf": "eth0",
  "isGateway": true,
  "ipMasq": false,
  "hairpin": "false",
  "ipam": {
    "type": "host-local",
    "subnet": "10.180.2.0/24",
    "gateway": "10.180.2.1",
    "routes": [
      { "dst": "0.0.0.0/0" }
    ]
  }
}
```

And the container in question has `10.180.2.255/24` which is the broadcast address for the subnet. So it can't figure out the MAC of cbr0 because all frames are getting sent to `ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff` (or at least, that's what `arp -n` seems to indicate). 

Eg: tcpdump alonside a wget on google.com

```
beeps@e2e-test-beeps-minion-group-4737:~$ sudo tcpdump -e -i cbr0 -n host 10.180.2.255
tcpdump: verbose output suppressed, use -v or -vv for full protocol decode
listening on cbr0, link-type EN10MB (Ethernet), capture size 65535 bytes
19:09:25.644425 a2:c7:88:bc:5c:e0 > ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff, ethertype ARP (0x0806), length 42: Request who-has 10.180.2.1 tell 10.180.2.255, length 28
19:09:26.640693 a2:c7:88:bc:5c:e0 > ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff, ethertype ARP (0x0806), length 42: Request who-has 10.180.2.1 tell 10.180.2.255, length 28
19:09:27.640721 a2:c7:88:bc:5c:e0 > ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff, ethertype ARP (0x0806), length 42: Request who-has 10.180.2.1 tell 10.180.2.255, length 28
```

vs a similar normal container

```
beeps@e2e-test-beeps-minion-group-4737:~$ sudo tcpdump -e -i cbr0 -n host 10.180.2.171
tcpdump: verbose output suppressed, use -v or -vv for full protocol decode
listening on cbr0, link-type EN10MB (Ethernet), capture size 65535 bytes
19:09:44.965805 c2:9d:c9:0d:e5:bc > 22:cf:99:33:19:ff, ethertype IPv4 (0x0800), length 83: 10.180.2.171.36148 > 169.254.169.254.53: 3769+ PTR? 1.2.180.10.in-addr.arpa. (41)
19:09:44.969367 22:cf:99:33:19:ff > c2:9d:c9:0d:e5:bc, ethertype IPv4 (0x0800), length 171: 169.254.169.254.53 > 10.180.2.171.36148: 3769 NXDomain 0/1/0 (129)

title: Lots of upgrade tests have been broken for 2 months

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

body:
A couple dozen upgrade and skew e2e test suites have been broken for exactly the same amount of time (1 month, 23 days). I looked at 2, and they were both broken due to:

```
/workspace/sh2ju.sh: line 125: bc: command not found
```

This problem was introduced by #27825 in June, and apparently wasn't entirely fixed by #30556.

We lost 2 months of upgrade test coverage due to this. What can we do to notice such failures earlier? 

Visible here, if you scroll all the way to the right:
https://k8s-testgrid.appspot.com/google-upgrade#gke-1.3-1.4-kubectl-skew&width=3

Also, we have repeated problems with the lack of portability of shell scripts. If we're not going to ban them, can we make them more hermetic?

cc @ixdy @kubernetes/sig-testing @freehan @spxtr @lavalamp

title: Upgrades from 1.2 => 1.3.4 are broken

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/auth
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Auth.

body:
The issue is that KUBE_USER env variable is not set on cluster upgrades.
If KUBE_USER is not defined we do not copy the "abac-authz-policy.jsonl" file.
The assumption in the [startup scripts](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cluster/gce/gci/configure-helper.sh#L675) is that we are upgrading from 1.3.X to 1.3.4, in which case we would not want to overwrite the file.
However, in this scenario we are upgrading from 1.2.5 to 1.3.4 where the file was never created so we end up with a crashlooping kube-apiserver.

```
F0809 01:49:45.646163       5 server.go:238] Invalid Authorization Config: open /etc/srv/kubernetes/abac-authz-policy.jsonl: no such file or directory
Flag --address has been deprecated, see --insecure-bind-address instead
```

Manually creating this file brought the cluster into a healthy state.

title: update Google Cloud API client import paths and more

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

milestone.title: v1.4
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.4/Release-1.4.md

body:
The Google Cloud API client libraries for Go are making some breaking changes:
- The import paths are changing from `google.golang.org/cloud/...` to
  `cloud.google.com/go/...`. For example, if your code imports the BigQuery client
  it currently reads
  `import "google.golang.org/cloud/bigquery"`
  It should be changed to
  `import "cloud.google.com/go/bigquery"`
- Client options are also moving, from `google.golang.org/cloud` to
  `google.golang.org/api/option`. Two have also been renamed:
  - `WithBaseGRPC` is now `WithGRPCConn`
  - `WithBaseHTTP` is now `WithHTTPClient`
- The `cloud.WithContext` and `cloud.NewContext` methods are gone, as are the
  deprecated pubsub and container functions that required them. Use the `Client`
  methods of these packages instead.

You should make these changes before September 12, 2016, when the packages at
`google.golang.org/cloud` will go away.

title: Wrong AWS volume can be mounted

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: lifecycle/stale
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR has remained open with no activity and has become stale.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
Background: K8s often has problems attaching/detaching AWS volumes: If I do a `kubectl replace` on a deployment, I frequently observe K8s not correctly detaching the volume, and the new deployment will be forever stuck in a crash loop because it times out getting the new volume. Seems like a race condition. The steps I always do when this happens is to delete the deployment, manually force-detach via EC2 API, and manually `umount` the mounts, otherwise they never seem to be cleaned up.

So today I experienced this again, and I did the following:
1. Delete deployment.
2. Manually detach volume via EC2 API, since it was not being released.
3. **Manually `umount` wrong volume**. I accidentally unmounted the volume of a different pod because I didn't read the `mount` output correctly. Oops.
4. Created deployment.
5. Noticed my mistake.

What happened was that the new deployment was mounted with the wrong device:

``` shell
$ mount | grep xvdb
/dev/xvdba on /var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/aws-ebs/mounts/vol-0e3bf8343563ee5aa type ext4 (rw,relatime,data=ordered)
/dev/xvdba on /var/lib/kubelet/pods/a8f54bf6-4ebd-11e6-89fc-065b459e106f/volumes/kubernetes.io~aws-ebs/data type ext4 (rw,relatime,data=ordered)
```

This is the right volume _ID_, but it has mounted the wrong device. According to EC2, the (right) volume is attached to `/dev/xvdbb`.

``` shell
$ aws ec2 describe-volumes --volume-ids vol-0e3bf8343563ee5aa
{
    "Volumes": [
        {
            "AvailabilityZone": "us-east-1e", 
            "Attachments": [
                {
                    "AttachTime": "2016-07-20T21:05:17.000Z", 
                    "InstanceId": "i-06d03923e9e5a6329", 
                    "VolumeId": "vol-0e3bf8343563ee5aa", 
                    "State": "attached", 
                    "DeleteOnTermination": false, 
                    "Device": "/dev/xvdbb"
                }
            ], 
            "Tags": [],
            "Encrypted": false, 
            "VolumeType": "gp2", 
            "VolumeId": "vol-0e3bf8343563ee5aa", 
            "State": "in-use", 
            "Iops": 100, 
            "SnapshotId": "", 
            "CreateTime": "2016-07-19T00:25:00.168Z", 
            "Size": 30
        }
    ]
}
```

`/dev/xvdba` is the volume I accidentally unmounted by mistake:

``` javascript
            // ...
            "Attachments": [
                {
                    "AttachTime": "2016-07-19T17:56:27.000Z", 
                    "InstanceId": "i-06d03923e9e5a6329", 
                    "VolumeId": "vol-0e0a13f1b3a4a6dbc", 
                    "State": "attached", 
                    "DeleteOnTermination": false, 
                    "Device": "/dev/xvdba"
                }
            ], 
```

So it's mounting the wrong volume into the pod.

Of course I was being naughty, but it seems to me that this should never happen, since EC2 has already allocated `xvdbb`?

[Here's](https://gist.github.com/atombender/a1c8199ed202c2ea0d6b4566db65c60b) the entire KCM output from this fiasco.

title: Don't recreate forwarding rule/target pool on master restart

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
Restarting master causes a recreation of fwrule and target pool for type=loadbalancer services. We are saved in the non restart case because we compare a cached verson of the service to decided if we should even call into the cloudprovider and update resources. 

This is happening because our reconciliation routines are confused about session affintiy and lbip, leading them to recreate, since inplace update isn't allowed. 

The impact is at best a few seconds of radio silence, at worst who knows? 

Repro: 
Create a loadbalanced service, eg: 

``` yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nginx
  labels:
    app: nginx
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 80
    protocol: TCP
    name: http
  selector:
    app: nginx

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ReplicationController
metadata:
  name: nginx
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: gcr.io/google_containers/nginx-slim:0.8
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
        volumeMounts:
        - name: host-proc
          mountPath: /host-proc
        command:
        - sh
        - -c
        - |
          echo 1024 > /host-proc/sys/net/core/somaxconn && nginx -g "daemon off;"
      volumes:
      - name: host-proc
        hostPath:
          path: /proc
```

Wait for it to acquire a vip. 

``` console
$ k get svc
NAME         CLUSTER-IP   EXTERNAL-IP       PORT(S)   AGE
kubernetes   10.0.0.1     <none>            443/TCP   5m
nginx        10.0.68.45   104.197.169.231   80/TCP    48s

```

Try it out

``` console
$ while true; do wget -q -O - --retry-connrefused --waitretry=1 --read-timeout=1 --timeout=1 -t 0 104.197.169.231; sleep
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
<title>Welcome to nginx!</title>

```

Ssh into master and restart kube-controller-manager:

``` console
$ docker kill $(docker ps | grep kube-controller | awk '{print $1}')
```

Watch the wgets, you'll notice radio silence after a bit.
This is because the targetpool and forwarding rule get recreted, for 2 reasons: 
- affinity mismatch

```
$ k get svc nginx -o yaml | grep -i affinity
    sessionAffinity: None
$ gcloud compute target-pools describe abd65fb3837ec11e69d3642010af0000 --format=json --region=us-central1
{
  "creationTimestamp": "2016-06-21T13:14:54.713-07:00",
  "description": "{\"kubernetes.io/service-name\":\"default/echoheaders\"}",
  "id": "5596799261850476241",
  "kind": "compute#targetPool",
  "name": "abd65fb3837ec11e69d3642010af0000",
  "region": "https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/kubernetesdev/regions/us-central1",
  "selfLink": "https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/kubernetesdev/regions/us-central1/targetPools/abd65fb3837ec11e69d3642010af0000"
}
```

So this check fails: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/cloudprovider/providers/gce/gce.go#L816
- Lbip mismatch: 

```
$ k get svc nginx --template='{{.spec.clusterIP}}'
10.0.68.45
$ k get svc nginx --template='{{.spec.loadBalancerIP}}'
<no value>
$ $ gcloud compute forwarding-rules list abd65fb3837ec11e69d3642010af0000 --format=json
[
  {
    "IPAddress": "162.222.178.160",
    "IPProtocol": "TCP",
    "creationTimestamp": "2016-06-21T13:14:58.244-07:00",
    "description": "{\"kubernetes.io/service-name\":\"default/echoheaders\"}",
    "id": "1689396002026692269",
    "kind": "compute#forwardingRule",
    "name": "abd65fb3837ec11e69d3642010af0000",
    "portRange": "80-80",
    "region": "us-central1",
    "selfLink": "https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/kubernetesdev/regions/us-central1/forwardingRules/abd65fb3837ec11e69d3642010af0000",
    "target": "us-central1/targetPools/abd65fb3837ec11e69d3642010af0000"
  }
]
```

So this check fails: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/cloudprovider/providers/gce/gce.go#L765 (lbip is retrieved here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/cloudprovider/providers/gce/gce.go#L535)

title: NodeController doesn't evict Pods en masse in case of master network problems

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

milestone.title: v1.4
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.4/Release-1.4.md

body:
We need to mitigate master networking problems that cause massive pod evictions. Originally master evicts all Pods that it doesn't hear in ~5 minutes. It's a perfectly OK behavior as long as it's not the master machine which as networking problems. In such case NodeController will think that all Nodes are unhealthy and evict all Pods within the cluster (they'll get instantly rescheduled). We implemented a stopgap which prevents NC from evicting anything if no Nodes are reporting to master, but we don't handle partial segmentations yet.

We need to behave sanely in case of partial segmentation, especially in multi-zone clusters.

cc @wojtek-t @davidopp @mml @lavalamp @smarterclayton

title: Eviction manager's observed memory.available is vastly different from /proc/meminfo MemAvailable

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
I'm working on a node e2e memory eviction test, and even though I set the aggressive hard eviction threshold of `--eviction-hard memory.available<2.5Gi`, I noticed that my pods were chewing up memory without getting evicted, so I started digging.

I logged the `observations` made from the `synchronize` function in `kubernetes/pkg/kubelet/eviction/eviction_manager.go`, with `glog.Infof("eviction manager: observations: %s", strings.Replace(spew.Sdump(observations), "\n", " ", -1))`, and I saw the following:

`eviction manager: observations: (eviction.signalObservations) (len=1) {  (eviction.Signal) (len=16) "memory.available": (*resource.Quantity)(0xc820d61940)(3377236Ki) }`

sampling `/proc/meminfo` about two seconds later reveals:

```
MemTotal:        3801016 kB
MemFree:          826748 kB
MemAvailable:    1213620 kB
```

Assuming kB and Ki are equivalent units (they seem to both be kibibytes), that's a 2163616Ki difference in reporting between `memory.available` and `MemAvailable`.

My test collectively chews up memory in steps of about 40MB every 10 seconds, so they could show up as different, but shouldn't be THAT different.

Tagging @vishh @derekwaynecarr

title: Scheduler is ignoring some pods in large clusters and they hang in "pending" state for hours

body:
There seeem to be a regression in apiserver/scheduler which leads to the situation that scheduler in not scheduling some pods in large clusters.
So what is happening is that in 5000-node kubemark, pretty much every run of Density test in the last few days is ending with the following error:
```
/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/density.go:721
Expected error:
    <*errors.errorString | 0xc49b9b2640>: {
        s: "Only 2994 pods started out of 3000",
    }
    Only 2994 pods started out of 3000
not to have occurred
```

The first such failure is this one:
https://k8s-gubernator.appspot.com/build/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-kubemark-gce-scale/114

However, we have broken kubemark just before that, so the last run without such failure before this one is:
https://k8s-gubernator.appspot.com/build/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-kubemark-gce-scale/108

So the regression was somewhere between those two runs.

It's not even in which part of code the regression is - e.g. it may potentially be in watch.

However, what is suspicious is that it is always about the scheduler that doesn't schedule pods. If the pod is scheduled, then it is also successfully picked by kubelet.

We're seeing an abnormal number of soft lockups, pegged cpus and unusable nodes recently. The last repros were from @bowei and @freehan. 

**Symptoms**
Kernel logs showed ebtables related traces, CPU was pegged at 100% and remained there, no ssh, basically no clarity till the node was reset. Looking back through older test logs, there are several failures that had NotReady nodes that MIGHT be the same bug. 

**Actions**
Minhan's working on a repro and @dchen1107 is trying to figure out when this spike happened by spelunking test logs. 

We've been syncing iptables rules from kube-proxy more often than we need to for a couple of releases (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/26637), this is the only thing that springs to mind that might cause cpu spikes. 

We should probably try to mitigate for 1.5, marking as release-blocker till we have a better handle.

title: pod disruption budgets cannot handle concurrent requests

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

body:
**What happened**:
When I try to test `kubectl drain` after implementing the 1st approach according to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/37460#issuecomment-263437516, I found pod disruption budgets cannot handle concurrent requests.

The error message is:
```
Error from server (Conflict): Operation cannot be fulfilled on poddisruptionbudgets.policy "my-db": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again
```
```
server response object: [{
  "metadata": {},
  "status": "Failure",
  "message": "Operation cannot be fulfilled on poddisruptionbudgets.policy \"my-db\": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again",
  "reason": "Conflict",
  "details": {
    "name": "my-db",
    "group": "policy",
    "kind": "poddisruptionbudgets"
  },
  "code": 409
}]
```
It is an Optimistic Lock error message. It means PDB can't handle concurrent requests.


**How to reproduce it** (as minimally and precisely as possible):
1) Create a deployment with 6 replicas and schedule them to the same node, say node A. You can leave only one node scheduling enabled, and then create the deployment.
2) Create the PDB that match the deployment's label
3) Uncordon another node, say node B
4) Drain node A using concurrent POST eviction requests. Ref: #37604

@davidopp I'm not sure if this behavior is OK for PDB.
I think I can make `drain` work by waiting for a while if current pod label(s) match previous pod label(s).

**What you expected to happen**:

Upon Node upgrade, Pods should either be terminated (so a controller can recreate them) or they should come back to Running on their own.

**How to reproduce it** (as minimally and precisely as possible):

1.  Start a v1.4 cluster on GCE.

    ```shell
    git checkout release-1.4
    git pull upstream release-1.4
    make clean quick-release
    cluster/kube-up.sh
    ```

1.  Create the following example PetSet and wait for all Pods to be Running.

    ```shell
    kubectl create -f petset.yaml
    ```

    ```yaml
    # A headless service to create DNS records
    apiVersion: v1
    kind: Service
    metadata:
      name: nginx
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      ports:
      - port: 80
        name: web
      # *.nginx.default.svc.cluster.local
      clusterIP: None
      selector:
        app: nginx
    ---
    apiVersion: apps/v1alpha1
    kind: PetSet
    metadata:
      name: web
    spec:
      serviceName: "nginx"
      replicas: 5
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app: nginx
          annotations:
            pod.alpha.kubernetes.io/initialized: "true"
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: nginx
            image: gcr.io/google_containers/nginx-slim:0.8
            ports:
            - containerPort: 80
              name: web
            volumeMounts:
            - name: www
              mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
      volumeClaimTemplates:
      - metadata:
          name: www
          annotations:
            volume.alpha.kubernetes.io/storage-class: anything
        spec:
          accessModes: [ "ReadWriteOnce" ]
          resources:
            requests:
              storage: 1Gi
    ```

1.  Delete PetSet without cascading (keep the Pods).

    ```shell
    kubectl delete petset web --cascade=false
    ```

1.  Upgrade master and nodes to `v1.5.0-beta.2` with `cluster/gce/upgrade.sh`.

    ```shell
    git checkout release-1.5
    git pull upstream release-1.5
    cluster/gce/upgrade.sh v1.5.0-beta.2
    ```

1.  Check for Pods stuck in ContainerCreating.

    ```
    NAME      READY     STATUS              RESTARTS   AGE
    web-0     0/1       ContainerCreating   0          42m
    web-4     0/1       ContainerCreating   0          42m
    ```

**Anything else do we need to know**:

After the above steps, some Pods may end up terminating. It seems to be random which ones terminate and which ones get stuck in ContainerCreating.

Manually deleting and recreating all the stuck Pods after the Nodes are upgraded allows them to correctly attach to the preexisting PVCs and become Running.

title: Etcd2 -> etcd3 migration is broken

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
It seems that after etcd2->etcd3 migration all objects are in their initial state (i.e. in the state in which they were created, as if there were no updates at all in the system).

How to repro:
- start a cluster from head
- create some data (e.g. kubectl run pod1 --image=gcr.io/google_containers/pause-amd64:3.0)
- login to master of the cluster
- kill apiserver sudo mv /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.manifest .
- wait until apiserver is down (so that noone will be writing to etcd)
- open /etc/kubernetes/manifest/etcd.sh and change:
  a) image: to 3.0.13-experimental.2 (from 2.2.1)
  b) TARGET_STORAGE to etcd3
  c) TARGET_VERSION to 3.0.13
- save the manifest and wait until etcd will be restarted and running again (underneath it will perform the migration using
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cluster/images/etcd/migrate-if-needed.sh

@xiang90 @hongchaodeng @mml @lavalamp

title: HPA uses wrong count to calculate target replcias

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/autoscaling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Autoscaling.

body:
The current formula looks like: 

``` go
currentReplicas := scale.Status.Replicas
[...] 
usageRatio := float64(utilization) / float64(targetUtilization)
    if math.Abs(1.0-usageRatio) > tolerance {
        return int32(math.Ceil(usageRatio * float64(currentReplicas))), &utilization, timestamp, nil
    }
```

If currentReplicas doesn't match to the number of replicas used to calculate utilization then the result can be way bigger than necessary. For example if there are 10 pods created in apiserver (= current replicas) but only 1 is scheduled and it is running at its last legs (300% of the target utilization) then the target will grow to 30 pods.
20 (30-10) pods get created and are not scheduled and will increase the replicas even further.

Solly you did some fixes in this area: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/33593. 
Will this PR fix the above scenario?

cc: @DirectXMan12  @jszczepkowski @fgrzadkowski @davidopp

title: Move submit queue blocking tests to GCI by default.

labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
We are planning to switch the following submit-queue blocking test jobs to use GCI as the default image on nodes before the code freeze (but ideally as soon as possible):
- `kubernetes-e2e-gce`
- `kubernetes-e2e-gce-slow`
- `kubernetes-e2e-gke`
- `kubernetes-e2e-gke-slow`

The status of these jobs (container-vm vs GCI pass rates) and issues under investigation are being tracked here (you must be a member of the kubernetes-dev@googlegroups.com mailing list to access): https://docs.google.com/a/google.com/spreadsheets/d/1HY8b1EUCPPDj8ZJvprVIJRevlyUA1_ZpyIJN-8c0Xss/edit?usp=sharing

Once we are confident in the stability of the GCI equivalents for the above jobs, the PR to make the change is: https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/723

I will be continually checking in with anyone assigned to P0 issues in the list in that spreadsheet.

labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/network
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Network.

milestone.title: v1.4
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.4/Release-1.4.md

body:
Restart docker and you'll see the number of allocatd ips jumping:

``` console
# ls /var/lib/cni/networks/kubenet/ | wc -l
51

# sudo systemctl restart docker.service

# ls /var/lib/cni/networks/kubenet/ | wc -l
69
```

Do it enough times (or with enough pods, do it once) and the node is effectively unschedulable, but reports ready: 

``` console
# ls /var/lib/cni/networks/kubenet/ | wc -l
254

# docker ps
CONTAINER ID        IMAGE                                                                  COMMAND                  CREATED             STATUS              PORTS               NAMES
1e60c680bb0f        gcr.io/google_containers/kube-proxy:fa5094377f97111eda3c700c05b313b2   "/bin/sh -c 'kube-pro"   2 minutes ago       Up 2 minutes                            k8s_kube-proxy.84f0299f_kube-proxy-e2e-test-beeps-minion-group-1uut_kube-system_90fd8ba4ce791b234b5cbbba324659b6_a32991a1
68d21830a8d4        gcr.io/google_containers/pause-amd64:3.0                               "/pause"                 2 minutes ago       Up 2 minutes                            k8s_POD.d8dbe16c_kube-proxy-e2e-test-beeps-minion-group-1uut_kube-system_90fd8ba4ce791b234b5cbbba324659b6_a8345dfb
47c4073a177f        bprashanth/kube-dnsmasq-amd64:0.1                                      "/usr/sbin/dnsmasq --"   2 minutes ago       Up 2 minutes                            k8s_dnsmasq.b185c2d1_dnsmasq-e2e-test-beeps-minion-group-1uut_kube-system_66b11a42154e4cd1f207bf98be04a70a_f2725cc2
d92c0f6f80b3        gcr.io/google_containers/pause-amd64:3.0                               "/pause"                 2 minutes ago       Up 2 minutes                            k8s_POD.d8dbe16c_dnsmasq-e2e-test-beeps-minion-group-1uut_kube-system_66b11a42154e4cd1f207bf98be04a70a_858b398a

```

Scheduling pods on it show

``` console
Tolerations:    <none>
Events:
  FirstSeen LastSeen    Count   From                        SubObjectPath   Type        Reason      Message
  --------- --------    -----   ----                        -------------   --------    ------      -------
  5s        1s      4   {kubelet e2e-test-beeps-minion-group-1uut}          Warning     FailedSync  Error syncing pod, skipping: failed to "SetupNetwork" for "echoheaders-3ty5d_default" with SetupNetworkError: "Failed to setup network for pod \"echoheaders-3ty5d_default(997a82ce-8c15-11e6-bbb0-42010af00002)\" using network plugins \"kubenet\": Error adding container to network: no IP addresses available in network: kubenet; Skipping pod"
```

I'm guessing this is because we don't release unused ips, but allocate new ones.
@kubernetes/sig-network @kubernetes/sig-node 

Maybe we can fix this by invoking kubenet everytime kubelet notices a container restart?

title: kubeadm 1.6.0 (only 1.6.0!!) is broken due to unconfigured CNI making kubelet NotReady

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/network
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Network.

body:
Initial report in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubeadm/issues/212.

I suspect that this was introduced in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/43474.

What is going on (all on single master):
1. kubeadm starts configures a kubelet and uses static pods to configure a control plane
1. kubeadm creates node object and waits for kubelet to join and be ready
1. kubelet is never ready and so kubeadm waits forever

In the conditions list for the node:
```
  Ready 		False 	Wed, 29 Mar 2017 15:54:04 +0000 	Wed, 29 Mar 2017 15:32:33 +0000 	KubeletNotReady 		runtime network not ready: NetworkReady=false reason:NetworkPluginNotReady message:docker: network plugin is not ready: cni config uninitialized
```

Previous behavior was for the kubelet to join the cluster even with unconfigured CNI.  The user will then typically run a DaemonSet with host networking to bootstrap CNI on all nodes.  The fact that the node never joins means that, fundamentally, DaemonSets cannot be used to bootstrap CNI.

### Edit by @mikedanese: please test patched debian amd64 kubeadm https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/43815#issuecomment-290616036 with fix

title: kubelet can panic when trying to determine the pids for a cgroup

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body: When the kubelet is checking for the pids in a cgroup, it checks to ensure a path exists, and then calls `filepath.Walk`. If the path was deleted in between the existence check and the walk, the kubelet can panic because the walk func isn't checking the passed in `err`.

title: Kubelet starts pods before CNI is configured

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/network
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Network.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
This appears to be a regression since v1.5.x, and should be a blocker for releasing v1.6.

**Kubernetes version** (use `kubectl version`):
Built from master

**Install tools**:

- Seen by @luxas on a cluster created via kubeadm.  
- I've seen this on GCE using cluster/kube-up.sh and NETWORK_PROVIDER=cni.

**What happened**:

The kubelet is starting pods before a CNI config file is present on the node, and thus pods are started without networking.

Specifically, the DNS pod starts up and fails to watch the API, causing its health checks to fail.

**What you expected to happen**:

The kubelet should wait for a CNI network config to be present in the configured `cni-conf-dir`.

**How to reproduce it** (as minimally and precisely as possible):

Launch a cluster built from master using `--network-plugin=cni` on the kubelet and do not install a CNI plugin / config.

title: Pod volume/cgroup cleanup logic is faulty

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
Both cleanup rely on the periodic `syncBatch` in the status manger to trigger the final pod deletion. This is specifically checked in [`if m.needsUpdate(syncedUID, status) || m.couldBeDeleted(uid, status.status) `](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.7.0-alpha.0/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L396
). 

However, `syncBatch` calls `syncPod`, which checks [`if !m.needsUpdate(uid, status)`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.7.0-alpha.0/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L417), and skip if it's true at the beginning of the function. This means that it will never trigger the final deletion request (unless something else triggers it).

This causes pod deletion to take > 1 minute in many cases, hence a bunch of test flake. 

Ideally, kubelet should not rely on the periodic `syncBatch` to send out deletion request, but at the least, this buggy logic should be fixed.


/cc @kubernetes/sig-node-bugs @dchen1107 @Random-Liu
