body:
Default toleration should be applied to newly created Pods. But:
```bash
$ kubectl run test --image=kubernetes/pause
$ kubectl get pod -o json
```
Gives result:
```json
            "spec": {
                "containers": [
                    {
                        "image": "kubernetes/pause",
                        "imagePullPolicy": "Always",
                        "name": "test",
                        "resources": {
                            "requests": {
                                "cpu": "100m"
                            }
                        },
                        "terminationMessagePath": "/dev/termination-log",
                        "terminationMessagePolicy": "File",
                        "volumeMounts": [
                            {
                                "mountPath": "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount",
                                "name": "default-token-x4vbw",
                                "readOnly": true
                            }
                        ]
                    }
                ],
                "dnsPolicy": "ClusterFirst",
                "nodeName": "e2e-test-gmarek-minion-group-9vzb",
                "restartPolicy": "Always",
                "schedulerName": "default-scheduler",
                "securityContext": {},
                "serviceAccount": "default",
                "serviceAccountName": "default",
                "terminationGracePeriodSeconds": 30,
                "volumes": [
                    {
                        "name": "default-token-x4vbw",
                        "secret": {
                            "defaultMode": 420,
                            "secretName": "default-token-x4vbw"
                        }
                    }
                ]
            },
```

Log from the apiserver says:
```
E0308 07:16:37.959599       5 admission.go:71] expected pod but got Pod
```
Which indicates some problems with casting:
```
 69   pod, ok := attributes.GetObject().(*v1.Pod)
 70   if !ok {
 71     glog.Errorf("expected pod but got %s", attributes.GetKind().Kind)
 72     return nil
 73   }
```

This admission controller is using:
```
"k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/api/v1"
```

Which is probably wrong, as I guess it should be `api/v1/` from client-go. Another example when apimachinery refactoring bites us. cc @deads2k @lavalamp @caesarxuchao @brendandburns 

@kevin-wangzefeng please fix, and verify that it's working.

cc @davidopp

I only checked the one failure shown up in my PR https://k8s-gubernator.appspot.com/build/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/42264/pull-kubernetes-e2e-kops-aws/15658/
While the cluster was still starting up (kubelet registering itself, creating mirror pods, etc), the replicaset created >70 kube-dns pods in less than 40s because all pods were rejected.
 1. The mirror pods on the master were not fully created yet, and the dns pods got assigned to the master node and rejected by kubelet due to insufficient resources on the node.
 2. After the mirror pods were created correctly, there was still one node that hadn't registered yet. All new dns pods failed at scheduling because the pod could not fit on any node.

For (2), After the node registered itself, it waited for ~50 to be assigned the pod CIDR. Seems a little bit high to me.
Also, on GCE, master nodes are unschedulable (taint?), but that doesn't seem like the case on AWS. Not sure if this is a feature or bug.

labels.name: sig/cli
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG CLI.

body:
kubectl caches API discovery results without being aware of its changes. Registering/Removing a new API service with api aggregator results in a change in API discovery but kubectl has no way to know the result is changed.

Possible solutions:

short term - implement e-tag for API discovery
long term - move to OpenAPI for api discovery

This is possibly a release blocker.

cc @lavalamp @pwittrock @dchen1107

@kubernetes/sig-cli-misc @kubernetes/sig-api-machinery-misc

title: Network becomes unavailable on terminating pods

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
**What keywords did you search in Kubernetes issues before filing this one?**: terminationGracePeriodSeconds, termination, network.

---

**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**: Bug report

**Kubernetes version**: 1.6.0

**Environment**:
- **Cloud provider or hardware configuration**: GCP and minikube
- **OS**: `Alpine Linux v3.4`
- **Kernel**: Linux 4.7.2


**What happened**:

Pod in "Terminating" state loses network connection two minutes after it was scheduled for termination, while still performing the work in the container. The bug prevents a pod from gracefully finishing the work.

**What you expected to happen**:

Terminating pod should gracefully finish the work with network being available according to `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`.


**How to reproduce it** (as minimally and precisely as possible):

Run a pod that does something like:

```ruby
require 'net/http'
loop do
  Net::HTTP.get_response('google.com', '/')
  sleep 1
end
```

For convenience I pushed the script to the docker hub (`kirshatrov/sleep-with-signals:v2`).

Create the pod with longer terminationGracePeriodSeconds policy:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: gracefully-terminating-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: kirshatrov/sleep-with-signals:v2
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 1500
```

Delete the pod (`kubectl delete pod gracefully-terminating-pod`) and watch the logs.

After two minutes the network will go down and the app will crash with:

```
Failed to open TCP connection to google.com:80 (getaddrinfo: Try again) (SocketError)
```

**Anything else we need to know**:

This happens both in GCP and Minikube on Kubernetes 1.6.0.
The kind of work we're performing in the containers is not safely interruptible and we'd like to use longer termination timeout (`terminationGracePeriodSeconds`) to allow the pod to finish the work before it's killed. This networking issue prevents us from relying on `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`.

cc @ibawt @Sirupsen @dwradcliffe @dturn

title: TLS-bootstrapped kubelet loses client certs after reboot, node stays on NotReady status

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/auth
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Auth.

body:
Updated description:

## Problem
The default `--cert-dir` path points to a transient location (`/var/run/kubernetes`) that is removed on reboot. The default `--kubeconfig` location points to a persistent location. This means that after a reboot, a kubelet can be stuck with configuration that is missing credentials needed to reach the API server.

## Solution
* `kubeadm` users:
  * Updated kubeadm packages (deb `1.8.0-01`, rpm `1.8.0-1`) have been released with a config change that prevents this issue from occurring. 
  * If you have a node that is already in this state:
      1. Verify this is the issue you are experiencing:
          * the `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf` file references `/var/run/kubernetes/kubelet-client.crt`
          * the `/var/run/kubernetes/kubelet-client.crt` file does not exist
      2. update the kubeadm package
      3. remove the `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf` file
      4. restart the kubelet to allow it to bootstrap
* Custom deployments should set the `kubelet` `--cert-dir` flag to a non-transient location, like `--cert-dir=/var/lib/kubelet/pki`

## Details

In 1.8.0, TLS bootstrapping (using `--bootstrap-kubeconfig`) writes certs to the `--cert-dir` path and a kubeconfig referencing those certs to the `--kubeconfig` path. That means that on reboot:
* the client certs are removed
* `--bootstrap-kubeconfig` is ignored, because `--kubeconfig` exists
* `--kubeconfig` cannot be loaded, which causes the kubelet to log an error (but not exit)

In 1.7, TLS bootstrapping inlined the certificates in the written `--kubeconfig`, which sidestepped the issue with the `--cert-dir` getting removed.

body:
As discussed in the release burndown meeting yesterday, here's a briefing of the issue:

Most of the folks (@smarterclayton, @liggitt, @jdumars, @gmarek and many from the release team) almost unanimously agreed with the requirement of post-submit blockers. Their absence is affecting us in multiple ways:

1.Release quality: We are shipping the release with a known performance regression violating our SLO (#51899) documented as a [known issue](https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/58315cc33c51f8f4d05364d80f0b66f5d980bad7/release-1.8/release-notes-draft.md#known-issues) - which would potentially leave some users unwilling to upgrade to 1.8. A proper fix to it was infeasible that close to the release, which wouldn't have been the case if we early-blocked on it. OTOH reverting the concerned PR would've also compromised us on release signal and kicked out a correctness fix from the release.

2.Eng productivity: We've spent multiple weeks of eng time to debug/fix the issues involved, complicated further by the fact that multiple of them got piled up due to lack of post blockers:
  - 2w of my time for running 2 rounds of bisection, debugging/fixing/studying code/logs (3 regressions - #52107 (node OOMs), #51899 (audit-log performance), #51899(kubelet-gc thundering herd))
  - 3-4d of @liggitt (senior member from RedHat) examining the issue, going through a PR diff storm, plotting some graphs, etc
  - 2w of folks from concerned SIGs combined (scalability, api-machinery, node, instrumentation) - involves debugging / PR fixes & reviews / issue reporting
  - 1w of release team's time combined (long burndown meeting(s) with multiple folks, slack discussions, triaging/understanding/documenting the regressions)

3.Release schedule: The release had to be pushed off by a day to resolve the issue and led to some chaos and discussion few hours before the release ETA.

Note that the proposal is not to block until the post-submit is fixed, but to block until we have a clear enough idea about the cause. We should then be able to unblock the queue (possibly manually) and work on the fix independently without needing to block further. This release is a clear example of how a little investment early on can reap huge benefits later.

cc @kubernetes/sig-release-members @kubernetes/sig-testing-feature-requests @dims @spiffxp

<!-- This form is for bug reports and feature requests ONLY! 

If you're looking for help check [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/kubernetes) and the [troubleshooting guide](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/debug-application-cluster/troubleshooting/).
-->

**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:
BUG REPORT

> Uncomment only one, leave it on its own line: 
>
/kind bug
> /kind feature


**What happened**:
Occasionally our nodes stop reporting their status to apiserver, and get marked as NotReady. However, they remain connected to the apiserver and receive the update to delete all their pods - which they do.

```
  OutOfDisk 		Unknown 	Thu, 28 Sep 2017 07:55:44 +0000 	Thu, 28 Sep 2017 07:57:04 +0000 	NodeStatusUnknown 	Kubelet stopped posting node status.
  MemoryPressure 	Unknown 	Thu, 28 Sep 2017 07:55:44 +0000 	Thu, 28 Sep 2017 07:57:04 +0000 	NodeStatusUnknown 	Kubelet stopped posting node status.
  DiskPressure 		Unknown 	Thu, 28 Sep 2017 07:55:44 +0000 	Thu, 28 Sep 2017 07:57:04 +0000 	NodeStatusUnknown 	Kubelet stopped posting node status.
  Ready 		Unknown 	Thu, 28 Sep 2017 07:55:44 +0000 	Thu, 28 Sep 2017 07:57:04 +0000 	NodeStatusUnknown 	Kubelet stopped posting node status.
  KernelDeadlock 	False 		Thu, 28 Sep 2017 07:58:38 +0000 	Wed, 27 Sep 2017 08:44:28 +0000 	KernelHasNoDeadlock 	kernel has no deadlock
```

In this example, the node last reported at 7:55:44.

This always seems to happen after I see these sort of log messages:
```
Sep 28 07:57:54 ip-10-50-97-190 start-kubelet.sh[1748]: E0928 07:57:54.064121    1748 remote_runtime.go:163] ListPodSandbox with filter "nil" from runtime service failed: rpc error: code = 4 desc = context deadline exceeded
Sep 28 07:57:54 ip-10-50-97-190 start-kubelet.sh[1748]: E0928 07:57:54.064194    1748 kuberuntime_sandbox.go:185] ListPodSandbox failed: rpc error: code = 4 desc = context deadline exceeded
Sep 28 07:57:54 ip-10-50-97-190 start-kubelet.sh[1748]: E0928 07:57:54.064209    1748 generic.go:198] GenericPLEG: Unable to retrieve pods: rpc error: code = 4 desc = context deadline exceeded
Sep 28 07:57:54 ip-10-50-97-190 start-kubelet.sh[1748]: E0928 07:57:54.081115    1748 remote_runtime.go:163] ListPodSandbox with filter "&PodSandboxFilter{Id:,State:&PodSandboxStateValue{State:SANDBOX_READY,},LabelSelector:map[string]string{},}" from runtime service failed: rpc error: code = 4 desc = context deadline exceeded
Sep 28 07:57:54 ip-10-50-97-190 start-kubelet.sh[1748]: E0928 07:57:54.081169    1748 kuberuntime_sandbox.go:185] ListPodSandbox failed: rpc error: code = 4 desc = context deadline exceeded
Sep 28 07:57:54 ip-10-50-97-190 start-kubelet.sh[1748]: E0928 07:57:54.081187    1748 kubelet_pods.go:842] Error listing containers: &grpc.rpcError{code:0x4, desc:"context deadline exceeded"}
Sep 28 07:57:54 ip-10-50-97-190 start-kubelet.sh[1748]: E0928 07:57:54.081210    1748 kubelet.go:1886] Failed cleaning pods: rpc error: code = 4 desc = context deadline exceeded
```

Which looks like the dockershim is timing out, maybe blocked on something.

Oddly, I never see these errors again in the kubelet logs - which indicates to me the PLEG loop continues to run successfully.

However after this time, all heartbeats to the apiserver stop. This even happened on an apiserver node, where kubelet connects to the localhost. So it doesn't seem like a network issue to me.

Next time this happens I'll try to capture a goroutine dump.

**What you expected to happen**:

Even if there is a temporary blip in the PLEG loop, kubelet should continue to send heartbeats, and then eventually go ready again.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
I've been unable to reproduce it yet - it happens quite infrequently.

body:
The 1.8 release team would like to identify the list of tests we are using for go / no-go signal.  This umbrella issue is to gain consensus on (and link to PR's that help with):

- our decision to continue the trend of expecting tests to pass 3 times in a row for go / no-go signal, except for...
- tests we will be willing to relax this expectation (eg: upgrade tests, flaky tests, and long tests)
- tests we believe should be removed from the release-1.8-blocking dashboard
- upgrade tests we are willing to explain away as known failures

body:
So kubernetes is running CNI version 0799f5732f2a11b329d9e3d51b9c8f2e3759f2ff and there were issues where people seemed to assume we were running CNI 0.6.0.  But we chose (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/49480) not to upgrade to 0.6.0 in 1.8

However, this is now a 1.8 release concern, in that presumably some of the commits in between 0799f5732f and 0.6.0 are important.

Can we please get a list, suitable for populating the known-issues for the 1.8 release notes, but also (more critically) to verify that none of the known issues might be considered release-blocking.

e.g. no hostPort support with CNI providers
e.g. promisc mode https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/49480#issuecomment-326581571

cc @kubernetes/sig-network-misc

body:
Separating this out from the umbrella issue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/52189 to just focus on the e2e_node test coverage for verifying device plugin functionality with kubelet restarts. This is important to verify that device plugin checkpointing works as intended.

We would like to get this test into 1.8 to verify the device plugin feature we introduced in 1.8 works as intended.

Note: This test is benign and it only exposes additional signals. It will not de-stabilize the release or affect other release blocking tests.

title: Need downgrade tests for 1.8 release

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/release
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Release.

body:
From what I learned on slack we're testing upgrades only - we check if we upgrade 1.7 cluster to 1.8 cluster things keep working. On the other hand we're NOT testing if downgrading 1.8 cluster to 1.7 works at all. Downgrades are extremely important for everyone running kubernetes in production - if it turns out that 1.8 has a bug that breaks some of user's workloads.

Standard mitigation policy in such case is to downgrade cluster to 1.7 and start working on a fix. In the absence of downgrade possibility, he/she will need to wait, possibly days, for hot-fix which is risky by itself.

We should consider making downgrades work a prerequisite for releasing 1.8. I'm aware that we haven't done downgrade testing since around 1.5, but the fact that we somehow managed that until now doesn't mean we should continue to ignore this problem.

@kubernetes/sig-release-bugs @thockin @bgrant0607 @smarterclayton @spiffxp

title: AllowPrivilegeEscalation missing API validation

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/auth
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Auth.

body:
**What happened**:
The new `AllowPrivilegeEscalation` feature has silent defaulting logic performed in the kubelet, related to whether the container requests privileged mode or the CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability. Instead, the kubelet should just use the value of the field if specified, and validation should be added to prevent setting the field to true for privileged or CAP_SYS_ADMIN containers.

/cc @jessfraz

title: Supporting docker log splitting in Kubernetes logging integrations

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/instrumentation
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Instrumentation.

body:
Follow-up of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/52433

Docker 1.13 introduced a change into the logging mechanism (https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/22982), that split the log lines longer than 16K into chunks of no more than that. Current default logging integrations (fluentd-gcp and fluentd-es addons) do not support that and this might result in broken ingestion, i.e. when JSON parsing is broken for entries longer than 16K.

One possible solution is introducing a fluentd plugin to the configuration to concat such entries in the similar way https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/fluent-plugin-detect-exceptions does it (assuming there is one out there, cc @tagomoris @repeatedly @edsiper for that)

/cc @igorpeshansky @fgrzadkowski @piosz

title: 1.8 regression: Can't pull images from docker.io without explicit path on centos/fedora/rhel

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/51751 bumped the vendored docker library and introduced a regression where pods with images that don't contain an explicit "docker.io/" repo path result in `ErrImagePull` failures.

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: busybox
spec:
  containers:
  - name: busybox
    image: busybox
    command:
    - sleep
    - "100"
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 0
  restartPolicy: Never
```

Results in the following error:
```
Failed to pull image "busybox": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = no such image: "docker.io/library/busybox:latest"
```

Pod gets `ErrImagePull`

`docker images` shows that the image has been pulled, though not by that name
```
$ docker images | grep busybox
docker.io/busybox                                      latest              d20ae45477cb        2 weeks ago         1.13 MB
```

Changing the image to `docker.io/busybox` in the pod spec corrects the issue.

I think the new code that is changing the behavior is somewhere in here
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/vendor/github.com/docker/distribution/reference/normalize.go#L78-L98

`familiarizeName()` is a new function brought in by the bump.

If I checkout the commit before the bump, the problem does not occur.

@derekwaynecarr @DirectXMan12 @dashpole 

related: https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1496630

title: APIServices auto-register controller duels on HA apiserver upgrades

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
Working through HA upgrade scenarios from 1.7 -> 1.8, I found several situations the current APIService auto-register controller does not handle well:

Health vs liveness:
* Problem: The apiserver health check that waits until local APIServices are registered and available should not go unhealthy if those APIServices are later removed.
* Solution: Make the health check a no-op once it has completed successfully once

CRD flutter:
* Problem: The auto-register controller should not start managing APIService objects until it has completed its initial listing of registered CRD objects and determined the APIService objects it expects to exist.
* Solution: Wait to start the autoregister controller until the CRD controller has completed an initial sync of the initial list of CRD objects.

Controller dueling:
* Problems:
    * If an API server registers APIServices for additional API groups on start, an already-running API server's controller will delete those APIServices.
    * If an API server removes APIServices for API groups no longer served, an already-running API server's controller will re-add those APIServices.
* Solution: expand the controller's automanaged/not-automanaged options to add an "auto-managed on start" option - the controller would sync services with this option exactly once. That allows it to establish services at start, but not duel with API servers started later. In an HA API server setup, that would mean the last API server to start would determine the configured local API services.

The current behavior of the controller:

|                                | Desired: not found          |  Desired: sync always       |
|--------------------------------------|--------------------|--------------------|
|  **Current: error**                               | error              | error              |
|  **Current: not found**                           | noop                | create             |
|  **Current: no sync**                             | noop                | noop                |
|  **Current: sync always**                         | delete             | update             |


The behavior of the controller, adding a "sync on start" option (with the differences in behavior bolded):

|                               | Desired: not found          |  Desired: sync on start     |  Desired: sync always       |
|--------------------------------------|--------------------|--------------------|--------------------|
|  **Current: error**                               | error              | error              | error              |
|  **Current: not found**                           | noop                | **create once** | create             |
|  **Current: no sync**                             | noop                | noop                | noop                |
|  **Current: sync on start, present at start**     | **delete once** | **update once** | **update once** |
|  **Current: sync on start, not present at start** | **noop**                | **noop**                | **noop**                |
|  **Current: sync always**                         | delete             | **update once** | update             |

cc @deads2k @kubernetes/sig-api-machinery-bugs

title: `delete pods` API call latencies shot up on large cluster tests

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
Updated issue description with latest findings:

#50350 introduced a change to kubelet pod deletion that results in `delete pod` API calls from kubelets being concentrated immediately after container garbage collection.

When performing a deletion of large numbers (thousands) of pods across large numbers (hundreds) of nodes, the resulting concentrated delete calls from the kubelets cause increased latency of `delete pods` API calls above the target threshold:
```
Sep 27 14:34:14.484: INFO: WARNING Top latency metric: {Resource:pods Subresource: Verb:DELETE Latency:{Perc50:4.551ms Perc90:10.216ms Perc99:1.403002s Perc100:0s} Count:122966}
```

Seen on https://k8s-gubernator.appspot.com/builds/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-scale-performance/

Not seen on https://k8s-gubernator.appspot.com/builds/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-kubemark-gce-scale/

hoisted details from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/51899#issuecomment-332868313 into description:
Graphs over a three minute window (both latency in ms and distribution of delete calls per second):

the delete calls from the gc controller merely set deletionTimestamp on the pod (which the kubelets observe and start shutting down the pods). the delete calls from the kubelet actually delete from etcd.

![screen shot 2017-09-28 at 11 47 18 am](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/980082/30976458-d3f6ab28-a442-11e7-96d3-79511f8a6455.png)

![screen shot 2017-09-28 at 12 05 18 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/980082/30977371-58d87824-a445-11e7-9dac-a78063701a82.png)

there were multiple spikes throughout the run (corresponding to deletions of 3000-pod replication controllers). here's a graph of delete calls that took more than one second throughout the whole run:
![screen shot 2017-09-28 at 11 24 22 am](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/980082/30975188-a1bbd8fc-a43f-11e7-9922-484eef42be97.png)

Seems like a kubelet-induced thundering herd, when deleting massive numbers of pods across massive numbers of nodes. kubemark's gc is stubbed since there are no real containers, so this isn't observed there


Original issue description follows:

From 5k-node density test run (no. 26) on last friday:

```
I0901 10:11:29.395] Sep  1 10:11:29.395: INFO: WARNING Top latency metric: {Resource:pods Subresource: Verb:LIST Latency:{Perc50:66.805ms Perc90:375.804ms Perc99:8.111217s Perc100:0s} Count:11911}
I0901 10:11:29.396] Sep  1 10:11:29.395: INFO: Top latency metric: {Resource:nodes Subresource: Verb:LIST Latency:{Perc50:417.103ms Perc90:1.090847s Perc99:2.336106s Perc100:0s} Count:1261}
I0901 10:11:29.396] Sep  1 10:11:29.395: INFO: WARNING Top latency metric: {Resource:nodes Subresource:status Verb:PATCH Latency:{Perc50:5.633ms Perc90:279.15ms Perc99:1.04109s Perc100:0s} Count:5543730}
I0901 10:11:29.396] Sep  1 10:11:29.395: INFO: Top latency metric: {Resource:pods Subresource:binding Verb:POST Latency:{Perc50:1.442ms Perc90:15.171ms Perc99:921.523ms Perc100:0s} Count:155096}
I0901 10:11:29.396] Sep  1 10:11:29.395: INFO: Top latency metric: {Resource:replicationcontrollers Subresource: Verb:POST Latency:{Perc50:3.13ms Perc90:218.472ms Perc99:886.065ms Perc100:0s} Count:5049}
```

And from the last healthy run (no. 23) of the test:

```
I0826 03:49:44.301] Aug 26 03:49:44.301: INFO: Top latency metric: {Resource:pods Subresource: Verb:LIST Latency:{Perc50:830.411ms Perc90:1.468316s Perc99:2.627309s Perc100:0s} Count:10615}
I0826 03:49:44.302] Aug 26 03:49:44.301: INFO: Top latency metric: {Resource:nodes Subresource: Verb:LIST Latency:{Perc50:337.423ms Perc90:427.443ms Perc99:998.426ms Perc100:0s} Count:1800}
I0826 03:49:44.302] Aug 26 03:49:44.301: INFO: Top latency metric: {Resource:apiservices Subresource: Verb:PUT Latency:{Perc50:954Âµs Perc90:5.726ms Perc99:138.528ms Perc100:0s} Count:840}
I0826 03:49:44.302] Aug 26 03:49:44.301: INFO: Top latency metric: {Resource:namespaces Subresource: Verb:GET Latency:{Perc50:445Âµs Perc90:2.641ms Perc99:83.57ms Perc100:0s} Count:1608}
I0826 03:49:44.302] Aug 26 03:49:44.301: INFO: Top latency metric: {Resource:nodes Subresource:status Verb:PATCH Latency:{Perc50:3.22ms Perc90:9.449ms Perc99:55.588ms Perc100:0s} Count:7033941}
```

This is a huge increase we're seeing:
LIST pods : 2.6s -> 8.1s
LIST nodes: 1s -> 2.3s
PATCH node-status: 56ms -> 1s
...

title: Publish updates of staging repos

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
The staging repo publishing bot https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/tree/master/mungegithub/publisher is broken since beginning of August. Meanwhile, I have worked on https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/4134 to update our publishing algorithm for a number of reasons, the most important:

- handling of merges on our branches
- automatic tagging of repos
- preparation for golang/dep

Compare https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Y0mWank9s6XZy83wz689O6Q1v-KHxS2J0WIJPBB0sSo/edit?usp=sharing for a longer write-up of the rational.

While the PR needs proper review and probably a rewrite of parts using go-git, @caesarxuchao and I decided to go forward with a manual push of the output of that PR in order to unblock people who rely on our published repos. Intentionally, this should be push (not single PRs) because PRs drop (empty) merge commits which are essential for our ability to automatically tag.

Throughout the day, I have tested the branches as far as I can do that manually:
- by vendoring k8s.io/kuber-aggregator and its dependencies apimachinery, api, client-go and apiserver 
- and compiling kube-aggregator.

This should have smoke tested a big number of packages. All looks fine so far.

Hence, **I propose to do a push of my forks to the corresponding `github.com/kubernetes/*` repos**.

**All branches are clean fast-forward branches** (with the exception of k8s.io/metrics), i.e. no force-push is necessary. So just in case, we can easily revert to the old state. The repo `k8s.io/metrics` was not under control of our publisher bot before. To keep the old history, I propose to rename the `master` branch to `legacy`. Then projects vendoring it using a sha1 (e.g. in Godeps) will continue to work.

These are forked repos and branches:

- https://github.com/sttts/sample-apiserver: master, release-1.6, release-1.7 |
- https://github.com/sttts/kube-aggregator: master, release-1.6, release-1.7
- https://github.com/sttts/apiserver: master, release-1.6, release-1.7
- https://github.com/sttts/client-go: master, release-3.0, release-4.0
- https://github.com/sttts/api: master
- https://github.com/sttts/apimachinery: master, release-1.6, release-1.7
- https://github.com/sttts/metrics: master, release-1.7
- https://github.com/sttts/apiextensions-apiserver: master, release-1.7

**Here is a script to do the push effectively**: https://gist.github.com/anonymous/0db2c5b10dce604acb712964aef37eea

Closes https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/issues/4080

title: apiserver should export global timeout as a flag

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

body:
#51353 explains a problem with kubectl, where it reacts poorly when the apiserver closes the connection due to [timeout](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/filters/timeout.go#L34).

That timeout is hard-coded to 60s.  That's probably a fine default, but we have found cases where ordinary requests won't complete in that time.  We should export this as a flag so that cluster admins can crank it up if they find this happening to them.

title: gRPC update causing failure of API calls with large responses

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

body:
For e.g the density test started failing on all our kubemark jobs that are big (i.e on >= 100 nodes):
- https://k8s-testgrid.appspot.com/sig-scalability#kubemark-100
- https://k8s-testgrid.appspot.com/sig-scalability#kubemark-500

And it clearly seems to be a regression caused by this PR (from the diff) - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/50531 - which updated gRPC vendor code. The error we're seeing is the following:

```
Expected error:
    <*errors.StatusError | 0xc42d8c0900>: {
        ErrStatus: {
            TypeMeta: {Kind: "", APIVersion: ""},
            ListMeta: {SelfLink: "", ResourceVersion: ""},
            Status: "Failure",
            Message: "rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = grpc: received message larger than max (26710706 vs. 4194304)",
            Reason: "",
            Details: nil,
            Code: 500,
        },
    }
    rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = grpc: received message larger than max (26710706 vs. 4194304)
not to have occurred
```

It's coming from this line of the test - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/scalability/density.go#L232 - where we list all pods across all namespaces. Seems like the MTU for gRPC calls changed as a result of the update.

cc @kubernetes/sig-scalability-bugs @RenaudWasTaken @wojtek-t

title: Incorrect Status: 'deployment "testapp" exceeded its progress deadline'

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

body:
<!-- This form is for bug reports and feature requests ONLY! 

If you're looking for help check [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/kubernetes) and the [troubleshooting guide](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/debug-application-cluster/troubleshooting/).
-->

**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

> Uncomment only one, leave it on its own line: 
>
/kind bug
> /kind feature


**What happened**:
When setting an image using the example command and following it up with a status check, the command incorrectly indicated that the deployment exceeded it's progress deadline.

I'm using a shell script for deploys, those commands look similar to this:

```bash
kubectl set image deployments/${deployment_name} ${container_name}=${image_name}:${tag} --record
kubectl rollout status deployments/${deployment_name} --namespace ${environment}
if [[ $? != 0 ]]
then
  echo "The deploy has failed"
fi
```

During a deploy, sometimes the output looks like this:
```
deployment "testapp" image updated
error: deployment "testapp" exceeded its progress deadline
The deploy has failed
```

When in fact the deployment continued to work just fine.  We never hit the limit of our `progressDeadlineSeconds` at all.

The problem comes in that my deploy script is larger then the above.  I rely on the exit code of the `status` command to determine if if should perform a rollback.  When the `status` command runs it sometimes receives the wrong information and exits with status `1`.

**What you expected to happen**:
I expected the status to report to me the legit status of the on-going deployment.  Example successful output:

```
deployment "testapp" image updated
Waiting for rollout to finish: 1 old replicas are pending termination...
Waiting for rollout to finish: 1 old replicas are pending termination...
deployment "testapp" successfully rolled out
```

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. Create a deployment with `.spec.progressDeadlineSeconds` set to something reasonable, in my case it's set to `100`.  [I'm using this gist for testing.](https://gist.github.com/jtslear/aecb16e73254a6e864cde274c6b0332b)
1. In one terminal execute: `while true; do kubectl rollout status deploy/testapp; done`
1. In another terminal update the deployment, example in my case: `kubectl set image deploy/testapp testapp=jtslear/testapp:0.0.15`


**Anything else we need to know?**:
This is flakey.  I've seen this in our production clusters only a few times, and even recreating it is rather tricky.  I've had to repeat the steps above a couple of times before I ran into it.

To work around this, I've added a 3 second sleep between the `set` and `status` commands.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): seen on versions 1.7.0 and 1.7.1
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration**: minikube/GKE
- OS (e.g. from /etc/os-release):

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Cluster Lifecycle.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

body:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

/kind feature

It's time to decide which CNI version to use for v1.8.
We should do early in the cycle to catch regressions in the CNI <-> k8s integration.
We don't want the thing that happened in v1.6 to occur again, so we need to be very careful.

Currently, we're using v0.5.1 and consuming tarballs via a sha pushed by this `Makefile`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/build/cni/Makefile

We did this earlier because CNI didn't provide binary artifacts for all platform that kubernetes supports.
Since v0.5.2, they do, so we can get rid of `build/cni/Makefile` :tada:

Also, we don't want to consume a strange SHA as the version indicator, instead we want to use a version number _and_ possibly a SHA for verification.

I guess it would make sense to bump CNI to v0.5.2 for the v1.8 cycle.
Agree/disagree? It's not clear to me when v0.6.0 will be released, but the rc has been out for some time already...

cc @kubernetes/sig-network-feature-requests @ixdy @freehan @kubernetes/sig-cluster-lifecycle-feature-requests @dcbw

body:
/kind bug

We're having trouble retrieving images from a private registry on DockerCloud. For nearly a year the following has worked flawlessly. Last Friday I pulled down the 1.9.0 CLI (via brew) and since then have not been able to access any image in a private registry on DockerCloud. I've tried this on 10+ brand new clusters created with kops v1.8.0. The Kubernetes cluster version have been 1.8.0, 1.8.4, 1.8.5 and 1.9.0 (which is not supported by kops yet) and all exhibit the same problem.

We create the secret as such:
```
kubectl create secret docker-registry dockerclouduser \
    --docker-server=https://index.docker.io/v1/ \
    --docker-username={my-username} \
    --docker-password={my-password} \
    --docker-email={my-email}
```

And verify it using:
```
kubectl get secret dockerclouduser --output=json | jq --raw-output '.data | .".dockercfg"' | base64 -D | python -m json.tool
```

Which yields:
```
{
    "auths": {
        "https://index.docker.io/v1/": {
            "auth": "{what-appears-to-be-a-token}",
            "email": "{my-email}",
            "password": "{my-password}",
            "username": "{my-username}"
        }
    }
}
```

And create a test service with `kubectl create -f` with these contents:
```
apiVersion: apps/v1beta1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test-service
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: test-service
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: test-service
        image: {my-org}/{my-repo-name}:{my-tag}
        imagePullPolicy: Always
      imagePullSecrets:
        - name: dockerclouduser
```

The pod fails immediatly with: 
```
Failed to pull image "{my-org}/{mmy-repo-name}:{my-tag}": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Error response from daemon: repository {my-org}/{mmy-repo-name} not found: does not exist or no pull access
```

I've reviewed the 1.9.0 release notes and nothing jumps out as the root cause.

For reference I've tried putting quotes around the `{my-password}` value when creating the secret to no avail.

I've also tried prefixing the `spec.template.spec.containers.[0].image` value with `index.docker.io`, so the full value would read: `image: index.docker.io/{my-org}/{my-repo-name}:{my-tag}` also to no avail.

**Environment**:
Kubernetes version:
```
$ kubectl version
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"9", GitVersion:"v1.9.0", GitCommit:"925c127ec6b946659ad0fd596fa959be43f0cc05", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2017-12-16T03:16:50Z", GoVersion:"go1.9.2", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"darwin/amd64"}

```

title: Kubelet often fails on AWS spot instances

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
/kind bug

In a kops created cluster running Kubernetes 1.8.4 nodes sometimes start but fail to connect to the masters. I have tracked the issue down to this difference:

Failed:
I1216 07:28:57.369519 1900 aws.go:847] Building AWS cloudprovider
I1216 07:28:57.369555 1900 aws.go:810] Zone not specified in configuration file; querying AWS metadata service
E1216 07:28:57.586712 1900 tags.go:94] Tag "KubernetesCluster" nor "kubernetes.io/cluster/..." not found; Kubernetes may behave unexpectedly.
W1216 07:28:57.586744 1900 tags.go:78] AWS cloud - no clusterID filtering applied for shared resources; do not run multiple clusters in this AZ.
I1216 07:28:57.586807 1900 server.go:301] Successfully initialized cloud provider: "aws" from the config file: ""

Successful:
I1218 08:32:38.492573 28476 aws.go:847] Building AWS cloudprovider
I1218 08:32:38.492596 28476 aws.go:810] Zone not specified in configuration file; querying AWS metadata service
I1218 08:32:38.669713 28476 tags.go:76] AWS cloud filtering on ClusterID: kube.test.int
I1218 08:32:38.669788 28476 server.go:301] Successfully initialized cloud provider: "aws" from the config file: ""

So in the failing case the AWS metadata either doesn't respond or the response is missing critical information (I'm not sure how to find out which). This query isn't retried during kubelets general "retry connecting to the api" loop, so the kubelet will keep running but it will never retrieve the information it needs to install and configure calico and join the network.

title: CSI Teardown Path does not contain `volume_id`

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

body:
<!-- This form is for bug reports and feature requests ONLY! 

If you're looking for help check [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/kubernetes) and the [troubleshooting guide](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/debug-application-cluster/troubleshooting/).
-->

**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

> Uncomment only one, leave it on its own line: 
>
/kind bug
> /kind feature


**What happened**:
Teardown path does not contain `volume_id` or `driver_name`

* During mount, the CSI Mounter (i.e. `NewMounter(...)`), sets `volumeID` and `driverName` to `pvSource.VolumeHandle` and `pvSource.Driver` (see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/volume/csi/csi_plugin.go#L143).
* `volumeID`  and `driverName` are then used to generate the target mount path: e.g. `/var/lib/kubelet/pods/e6a8b147-d74d-11e7-a08f-42010a800002/volumes/kubernetes.io~csi/com.google.csi~gcepd/mypd` (see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/volume/csi/csi_mounter.go#L54).
* On unmount, the CSI unmounter leaves `volumeID`  and `driverName` empty (see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/volume/csi/csi_plugin.go#L151), because it does not have the volume spec on unmount (Kubernetes wants to maintain the ability to unmount even if a spec is not available).
* Therefore when the path to unmount is generated, it is missing the `volumeID`  and `driverName` and the unmount function will either be unable to establish a connection to the CSI client (because `volumeID`  and `driverName` is missing) or the CSI `NodeUnpublishVolumeRequest` receives an incomplete path (because : e.g. `/var/lib/kubelet/pods/e6a8b147-d74d-11e7-a08f-42010a800002/volumes/kubernetes.io~csi`.

**What you expected to happen**:
On unmount function should be able to call CSI `NodeUnpublishVolumeRequest` without issue.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
See above.

**Anything else we need to know?**:
Possible solutions:

1. Attempt to parse the target path to recover these fields
    * Cons:
      * If multiple CSI volumes exist for 1 pod, this may get tricky.
      * If csi volume_id is very long or contains invalid characters recovery via path may not be possible.
2. Store required information (`volumeID`  and `driverName`) in a file along with mount.
   * Cons: managing a file can get tricky for backwards compatibility.

title: apiserver uses wrong CommonName to verify service certificates for aggregated API Server when External admission controller is enabled

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

/kind bug

**What happened**:
After you configured webhook admission controller (ExternalAdmissionHookConfiguration) inside your cluster pointing to a service, apiserver will try to verify your new APIService certs against that admission controller service's Common Name. 
For example, a webhook admission controller is registered inside the cluster pointing to a service called "webhook" inside kube-system namespace (Common Name is webhook.kube-system.svc in this case). When you try to register a new APIService called `v1beta1.testapiservice.k8s.io` pointing to a service `testapiservice` inside `testns` namespace after that webhook admission controller was registered, you will see error inside apiserver log like this:
`E1127 01:22:06.230506       1 controller.go:111] loading OpenAPI spec for "v1beta1.testapiservice.k8s.io" failed with: failed to retrieve openAPI spec, http error: ResponseCode: 503, Body: Error: 'x509: certificate is valid for testapiservice, testapiservice.testns, testapiservice.testns.svc, testapiservice.testns.svc.cluster.local, not webhook.kube-system.svc'`
And aggregation layer cannot talk to the custom apiserver due to invalid certs.

**What you expected to happen**:
apiserver should only verify the new aggregated API Server certs against its own service's Common Name and shouldn't verify it against webhook admission controller service's Common Name.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. register a webhook admission controller inside your cluster like the example [here](https://github.com/caesarxuchao/example-webhook-admission-controller) using service webhook.kube-system.svc
2. register a new aggregated API Server using service testapiservice.testns.svc
3. aggregation layer cannot talk to the custom apiserver  and kube-apiserver generates error logs because it couldn't find valid Common Name `webhook.kube-system.svc` for your aggregated API Server service. 

**Anything else we need to know?**:
On the other hand admission controller works fine without any problem in this case described above.
We also tried deploying them in a different order. So deploy the aggregated API Server first and then register the admission controller webhook. In that case, the aggregated API server works fine but admission controller webhook won't work. From kube-apiserver log, you can see it's trying to verify the webhook admission controller service certs against aggregated API Server service's Common Name.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.8.3
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: Aws
- OS (e.g. from /etc/os-release): Container Linux by CoreOS 1576.2.0 (Ladybug)
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 4.13.11-coreos
- Install tools:
- Others:


/sig api-machinery

title: StatefulSet creates multiple controllerrevisions on controller restart

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/apps
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Apps.

body:
version: v1.10.0-alpha.0-469-g6b1b6d504a

When you create StatefulSet and restart statefulset controller, while it's starting it will create multiple controllerrevisions. See https://github.com/openshift/origin/issues/17435#issuecomment-346499744

I've traced this to a [recent change adding collision avoidance](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/50490) which made newRevision not re-entrant anymore and uncovered bug where statefulset controller doesn't wait on syncing revision informer.

/sig apps
/cc @smarterclayton @kow3ns @enisoc @liyinan926

--
I need to verify the rest next week but I suspect collision avoidance will be problematic in cases of picking up objects from queue multiple times before changes propagate to the informer - that probably needs expectations or revert. Also for cases of rollback (I am not sure if we support it yet or not) it wouldn't work probably either because if the collisionCount would be different, the hash for controllerRevision being rollbacked to would differ too.

**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

**What happened**:

I have a CRD which is backed by a controller which creates and deletes other CRDs. The dependent CRDs have a controller owner reference set. If I delete the controller object with --cascade=true, everything works as expected and the resources are cleaned up. If I use --cascade=false, I see that an "orpan" finalizer is added. No owner references on one of the dependents is removed and the main object gets never deleted.

**What you expected to happen**:

I would have expected that the garbage collector removes the owner reference and then removes the "orphan" finalizer afterwards from the object, before finally deleting it.

The metadata of the controller object then looks like this:

title: AWS: cannot mount volumes on C5 instances

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

body:
C5 instances don't mount volumes on the device path, instead they mount them on "random" nvme devices:  http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/nvme-ebs-volumes.html

We need to identify the device using the nvme ioctls (directly or indirectly via the nvme command).

body:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:
BUG REPORT
/kind bug

**What happened**:
AWS NVMe device path starts with `/dev/nvme` according to [doc](http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/device_naming.html), it fails aws device probe [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/cloudprovider/providers/aws/aws.go#L1429)
```go
	for _, blockDevice := range info.BlockDeviceMappings {
		name := aws.StringValue(blockDevice.DeviceName)
		if strings.HasPrefix(name, "/dev/sd") {
			name = name[7:]
		}
		if strings.HasPrefix(name, "/dev/xvd") {
			name = name[8:]
		}
		if len(name) < 1 || len(name) > 2 {
			glog.Warningf("Unexpected EBS DeviceName: %q", aws.StringValue(blockDevice.DeviceName))
		}
		deviceMappings[mountDevice(name)] = awsVolumeID(aws.StringValue(blockDevice.Ebs.VolumeId))
	}
```


**What you expected to happen**:
NVMe device should be supported.

Code reading

body:
I'm seeing the jobs go through fine, but failing during AfterSuite action. E.g:

- https://k8s-gubernator.appspot.com/build/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-large-correctness/15
- https://k8s-gubernator.appspot.com/build/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-scale-correctness/32

From the [build-log](https://storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-large-correctness/15/build-log.txt) of the first one, I'm seeing the following:

```
I1118 06:40:42.351] [91m[1m[AfterSuite] AfterSuite [0m
I1118 06:40:42.351] [37m/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/e2e.go:254[0m
I1118 06:40:42.351] 
I1118 06:40:42.351]   [91m[1mTest Panicked[0m
I1118 06:40:42.351]   [91mclose of closed channel[0m
I1118 06:40:42.351]   /usr/local/go/src/runtime/panic.go:491
I1118 06:40:42.352] 
I1118 06:40:42.352]   [91mFull Stack Trace[0m
I1118 06:40:42.352]   	/usr/local/go/src/runtime/panic.go:491 +0x283
I1118 06:40:42.352]   k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/framework.(*containerResourceGatherer).StopAndSummarize(0xc420d06690, 0xc426e97290, 0x3, 0x3, 0xc4210c0930, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0)
I1118 06:40:42.352]   	/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/framework/resource_usage_gatherer.go:292 +0x47
I1118 06:40:42.352]   k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/framework.(*Framework).AfterEach(0xc42118a7e0)
I1118 06:40:42.352]   	/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/framework/framework.go:324 +0xbc1
...
```

The panic suggests that it was attempted to close a closed channel, more specifically it seems to be the `stopCh` of the resource-gatherer from the stack-trace:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2aaab817de5c90340cf94913df166f389d8d6aca/test/e2e/framework/resource_usage_gatherer.go#L291-L293

cc @kubernetes/sig-scalability-misc @porridge

I1115 11:31:02.863] error dialing jenkins@35.193.52.163:22: 'ssh: handshake failed: read tcp 172.17.0.4:51754->35.193.52.163:22: read: connection reset by peer', retrying

title: HPA not scaling due to evicted pods

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/autoscaling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Autoscaling.

body:
/kind bug
**What happened**:
HPA fails to launch additional pods due to pods in evicted state, even with utilization significantly over target.

**What you expected to happen**:
When HPA pods reach the target utilization, new pods should be allocated and provisioned.
 
**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Launch a HPA, let the pods fill the disk on the host which will trigger evictions due to "Pod The node was low on resource: [DiskPressure]", HPA will exceed target and not allocate additional pods.

**Anything else we need to know?**:
Seems related to #55051 and #54525 though those are not specific to HPA.

title: Pod startup latency regression

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/scalability
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scalability.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
/kind bug

**What happened**:

In 5k node cluster tests pod startup latency has roughly doubled at all (50th, 90th, 99th, 100th) percentiles, apparently due to some change merged between Oct 16th and 20th. The following graph (for the ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-scale-performance job) makes it obvious (note values are capped at 10s for readability):

![0jjh2pnsh7p](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/489420/32377396-c4c39f36-c0a7-11e7-9f3f-19184b923c28.png)

The last run with good latency (3.2s@99%) was 49, on October 16th.
Since then it's been between 4.7s and ~5s at 99th %ile.
The [56th run](https://k8s-gubernator.appspot.com/build/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-scale-performance/56/) actually failed because the latency exceeded the threshold (5s). Since we're so close to the threshold, the test is now more flaky.

/cc @kubernetes/sig-scalability-bugs

As discussed earlier, in 1.9 release API stays in Beta for stabilization. Here's the list of tasks for this K8s release:

## API-related changes

- [x] Add a policy-wide `OmitStages` field (more context in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/49280#issuecomment-319711384)
  - @CaoShuFeng is working on this in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/54634
- [x] Fix the timestamps in the API (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/52160)
  - @CaoShuFeng is working on this in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/52981

## Pipeline bugfixes

- [x] Make webhook parameters configurable
  - @crassirostris is working on this in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/56638 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/56890
- [x] ~Introduce buffering for the log backend to fix file writing bottleneck (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/53006)~
  - Deferred until the next release
- [x] ~Restore audit logging in the scalability tests (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/53020)~
  - Deferred until the next release
- [x] Shutdown http handlers before shutting down audit backend (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/50781)
  - @hzxuzhonghu is working on this in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/54849
- [x] Policy without kind/apiVersion is still valid (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/54254)
  - @ericchiang is working on this in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/54267
- [x] Rate-limit batching webhook backend (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/52907)
  - @crassirostris is working on this in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/53417, with the help of @hzxuzhonghu
- [x] Network errors are not retried (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/52909)
  - @crassirostris is working on this in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/53947

## Policy changes

- [x] ~GCE audit policy should be made re-usable by other setups (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/53321)~

- [x] ~Audit policy should be tested (e.g. that it includes all core resources, more context in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/52265#issuecomment-329243972)~

## Misc

title: NFS PV recycler unverified

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

body:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:
/kind bug

**What happened**:

If a pod is already running in the default namespace with the expected name (i.e. `recycler-for-VOL`), the PV recycle method just assumes it's a recycler pod. However, if it is not a recycler, it could result in the volume being reused without the data being cleared.

**What you expected to happen**:

The recycled volume should not be reused until the data has been verifiably deleted. The easiest approach would be to make it an error to not run the recycler pod successfully, i.e. delete these lines:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/volume/util.go#L83-L85
I think that should be safe, since the recycler will retry.

Other errors in that method should also be considered fatal, e.g.:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/volume/util.go#L92

title: Opaque integer resources will get deleted by kubelet in v1.8

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
The introduction of device plugin support in kubelet ended up deleting Opaque Integer Resources that are not exposed via device plugins. 
Relevant code [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_node_status.go#L616).

Two things need to happen now in v1.8:
1. Add a test to catch this regression
2. Have kubelet not delete extended resources.

Cluster admins will have to manually remove extended resources exposed via device plugins when they remove plugins.

title: pvc volumes used with subPath volume mounts don't support reconstruction

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

body:
**Fix status:**
- [x] fixed in master in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/61373
- [x] fixed in release-1.10 branch in #61518, will be in 1.10.0
- [x] fixed in release-1.9 branch in #61519, will be in 1.9.7
- [x] fixed in release-1.8 branch in #61520, will be in 1.8.11
- [x] fixed in release-1.7 branch in #61521, will be in 1.7.16


In SubPath fixes, PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/61044 adds bind mount for subpaths. It uses `/var/lib/kubelet/pods/<uid>/volume-subpaths/<volumename>` as the path name. The volumename in this path is the container's mount volume name which is also called OuterVolumeSpecName in [operation_executor.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_executor.go#L476).

This becomes an issue for volume reconstruction when kubelet restarts. Volume [reconstruction](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler.go#L556) scans the volume directories and recover the InnerVolumeSpecName (which is used to construct pod volume paths). Volume reconstruction has not enough information to recover the OuterVolumeSpecName and figure out which volume it maps to. In case kubelet needs to clean up mounts (it happens when volume spec cannot be reconstructed), it will fail to clean up the subpaths because of lacking the OuterVolumeSpecName.

We think it is better to use InnerVolumeSpecName for volume subPath instead of OuterVolumeSpecName so that volume clean up can work. The issue we might have is that some users might already deploy a cluster with subpath might already [SubPath fix](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/61044). If the users perform an in-place upgrade, since new version will use InnerVolumeSpecName which might have conflicts with some other older version's OuterVolumeSpecName among different volumes. This change requires clear documentation and communication with the users.

title: Subpath volumes don't receive set-GID flag

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

body:
**Fix status:**
- [x] fixed in master in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/61284, will be in 1.10.0
- [x] fixed in release-1.9 branch in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/61308, will be in 1.9.7
- [x] fixed in release-1.8 branch in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/61309, will be in 1.8.11
- [x] fixed in release-1.7 branch in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/61310, will be in 1.7.16

Subpaths of volumes with fsGroup may be mounted into a container without SGID bit on themselves:

```sh
$ kubectl create -f - <<EOF                                                                                                                kind: Pod
apiVersion: v1
metadata: { name: "subpath" }
spec:
  volumes:
    - { name: "direct",  emptyDir: {}}
    - { name: "subpath", emptyDir: {}}
  securityContext:
    fsGroup: 100
    runAsUser: 35
  containers:
    - image: aosqe/hello-openshift
      name: show
      volumeMounts:
        - name: "direct"
          mountPath: "/mnt/direct"
        - name: "subpath"
          mountPath: "/mnt/subpath"
          subPath: "a"
EOF

$ kubectl exec -ti subpath -- ls /mnt -la
drwxrwsrwx    2 root     users            6 Mar 16 15:13 direct
drwxrwxrwx    2 root     users            6 Mar 16 15:13 subpath
```

The mode of `subpath` should be `drwxrwsrwx` instead of `drwxrwxrwx`.

Reason for this is `fchmod` at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5110db5087513801fc5946abcbd73c44e692b2c8/pkg/util/mount/mount_linux.go#L1035:

```go
	if err = syscall.Fchmod(parentFD, uint32(perm)&uint32(os.ModePerm)); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("chmod %q failed: %s", currentPath, err)
	}
```

1. it should not filter out sgid/suid/sticky flags with `&os.ModePerm`
2. `Fchmod()` int32 argument expects suid/sgid/sticky flags on different bits than `os.FileMode`.


/kind bug
/sig storage

title: CSI NodePublishVolume readonly is never set

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

body:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:
/kind bug


**What happened**:
The `readonly` field passed to `NodePublishVolume` is never set. 

In https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/volume/csi/csi_mounter.go#L198:

```GO
	err = csi.NodePublishVolume(
		ctx,
		c.volumeID,
		c.readOnly,
		deviceMountPath,
		dir,
		accessMode,
		c.volumeInfo,
		attribs,
		nodePublishSecrets,
		fsType,
	)
```

where `c` is a `csiMountMgr` object that is initialized in the `NewMounter(...)` method in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/volume/csi/csi_plugin.go#L113:

```GO
	mounter := &csiMountMgr{
		plugin:       p,
		k8s:          k8s,
		spec:         spec,
		pod:          pod,
		podUID:       pod.UID,
		driverName:   pvSource.Driver,
		volumeID:     pvSource.VolumeHandle,
		specVolumeID: spec.Name(),
		csiClient:    client,
	}
```

Notice the `readonly` field is never set.

**What you expected to happen**:

The `readonly` field should be set to `Pod.PodSpec.Containers[x].VolumeMounts[x].readonly`

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Create a CSI volume and set `Pod.PodSpec.Containers[x].VolumeMounts[x].readonly` to true.
Check the value of `readonly` in the CSI `NodePublishVolume(...)` call.
It should be true, but is false.

title: Scheduler logs exploding in large clusters - Can crash master!

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: kind/failing-test
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a consistently or frequently failing test.

body:
Today while running our 2k-node scalability presubmit against PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/60891, I noticed that scheduler throughput has fallen by ~4-5 times from the normal, i.e 100 pods/s -> 25 pods/s. Simultaneously, another 2k-node run I was manually running (against ~same code) showed normal throughput. I compared the scheduler manifests and only difference found was `--v=1` vs `--v=4`.

When I looked at size of scheduler logs, they were huuuugely differing (116KB vs 21GB):

```
shyamjvs@e2e-test-shyamjvs-master /var/log $ ls -al kube-scheduler.log 
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 116826 Mar  8 14:47 kube-scheduler.log
```

vs

```
shyamjvs@e2e-3-master /var/log $ ls -al kube-scheduler.log 
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 21479967994 Mar  8 14:48 kube-scheduler.log
```

And about 99% of those logs were just these kinds of lines:

```
I0308 14:41:44.900343       1 scheduler_binder.go:133] FindPodVolumes for pod "e2e-tests-density-30-8-fzpjw/density60000-7-d7ba3921-22d8-11e8-a055-0a580a3c9dc0-srs4v", node "e2e-3-minion-group-9f72"
I0308 14:41:44.900375       1 scheduler_binder.go:133] FindPodVolumes for pod "e2e-tests-density-30-8-fzpjw/density60000-7-d7ba3921-22d8-11e8-a055-0a580a3c9dc0-srs4v", node "e2e-3-minion-group-qhkb"
I0308 14:41:44.900072       1 scheduler_binder.go:133] FindPodVolumes for pod "e2e-tests-density-30-8-fzpjw/density60000-7-d7ba3921-22d8-11e8-a055-0a580a3c9dc0-srs4v", node "e2e-3-minion-group-l75c"
I0308 14:41:44.900470       1 scheduler_binder.go:133] FindPodVolumes for pod "e2e-tests-density-30-8-fzpjw/density60000-7-d7ba3921-22d8-11e8-a055-0a580a3c9dc0-srs4v", node "e2e-3-minion-group-j4jf"
```

They're coming from the scheduler volume-binder:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b3ba80b223bb3d21807d473eb4ed3ca0735d6f9f/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/scheduler_binder.go#L129-L133

FMU that log would be printed ~O(#nodes*#pods) which is way too much for our officially supported (5k nodes, 150k pods) limit.
Also seems like `--v=4` is default verbosity level in our GCE config-default/test setups (correct me if I'm wrong) and that can eat up the whole disk. Which is what happened in the 2k-node run:

```
shyamjvs@e2e-3-master /var/log $ df
Filesystem     1K-blocks     Used Available Use% Mounted on
/dev/root        1249792   471620    778172  38% /
...
/dev/sda1       47259264 47242880         0 100% /mnt/stateful_partition
```

As a result the apiserver started crash-looping and the test failed.

cc @kubernetes/sig-scheduling-bugs @kubernetes/sig-storage-misc @msau42 (who seems to have added that log) @wojtek-t

title: CVE-2017-1002102 - atomic writer volume handling allows arbitrary file deletion in host filesystem

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: official-cve-feed
labels.description: Issues or PRs related to CVEs officially announced by Security Response Committee (SRC)

body:
[CVSS:3.0/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:H](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.0#CVSS:3.0/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:H)

This vulnerability allows containers using a secret, configMap, projected or downwardAPI volume to trigger deletion of arbitrary files and directories on the nodes where they are running.

Thanks to Joel Smith of Red Hat for reporting this problem.

**Vulnerable versions:**
* Kubernetes 1.3.x-1.6.x
* Kubernetes 1.7.0-1.7.13
* Kubernetes 1.8.0-1.8.8
* Kubernetes 1.9.0-1.9.3

**Vulnerable configurations:**
* Clusters that run untrusted containers with secret, configMap, downwardAPI or projected volumes mounted (including auto-added service account token mounts).

**Vulnerability impact:**
A malicious container running in a pod with a secret, configMap, downwardAPI or projected volume mounted (including auto-added service account token mounts) can cause the Kubelet to remove any file or directory on the host filesystem.

**Mitigations prior to upgrading:**
Do not allow containers to be run with secret, configMap, downwardAPI and projected volumes (note that this prevents use of service account tokens in pods, and requires use of  [`automountServiceAccountToken: false`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/#use-the-default-service-account-to-access-the-api-server))

**Fixed versions:**
* Fixed in v1.7.14 by #60516
* Fixed in v1.8.9 by #60515
* Fixed in v1.9.4 by #60258
* Fixed in master by #58720 (included in v1.10.0-beta.1 and up, will be in v1.10.0)

**Fix impact:**
Secret, configMap, downwardAPI and projected volumes will be mounted as read-only volumes. Applications that attempt to write to these volumes will receive read-only filesystem errors. Previously, applications were allowed to make changes to these volumes, but those changes were reverted at an arbitrary interval by the system. Applications should be re-configured to write derived files to another location.

title: CVE-2017-1002101 - subpath volume mount handling allows arbitrary file access in host filesystem

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: official-cve-feed
labels.description: Issues or PRs related to CVEs officially announced by Security Response Committee (SRC)

body:
[CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.0#CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H)

This vulnerability allows containers using [subpath volume mounts](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes/#using-subpath) with any volume type (including non-privileged pods, subject to file permissions) to access files/directories outside of the volume, including the host’s filesystem.

Thanks to Maxim Ivanov for reporting this problem.

**Vulnerable versions:**
* Kubernetes 1.3.x-1.6.x
* Kubernetes 1.7.0-1.7.13
* Kubernetes 1.8.0-1.8.8
* Kubernetes 1.9.0-1.9.3

**Vulnerable configurations:**
* Clusters that allow untrusted users to control pod spec content, and prevent host filesystem access via hostPath volumes (or other volume types) using PodSecurityPolicy (or custom admission plugins)
* Clusters that make use of [subpath volume mounts](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes/#using-subpath) with untrusted containers or containers that can be compromised

**Vulnerability impact:**
A specially crafted pod spec combined with malicious container behavior can allow read/write access to arbitrary files outside volumes specified in the pod, including the host’s filesystem. This can be accomplished with any volume type, including emptyDir, and can be accomplished with a non-privileged pod (subject to file permissions).

**Mitigations prior to upgrading:**
Prevent untrusted users from creating pods (and pod-creating objects like deployments, replicasets, etc), or [disable all volume types](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/policy/pod-security-policy/#volumes-and-file-systems) with PodSecurityPolicy (note that this prevents use of service account tokens in pods, and requires use of  [`automountServiceAccountToken: false`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/#use-the-default-service-account-to-access-the-api-server))

**Fixed versions:**
* Fixed in v1.7.14 by #61047
* Fixed in v1.8.9 by #61046
* Fixed in v1.9.4 by #61045
* Fixed in master by #61044 (included in v1.10.0-beta.3, will be in v1.10.0)

**Action Required:**
In addition to upgrading, PodSecurityPolicy objects designed to limit container permissions must completely [disable hostPath volumes](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/policy/pod-security-policy/#volumes-and-file-systems), as the allowedHostPaths feature does not restrict symlink creation and traversal. Future enhancements (tracked in issue #61043) are required to limit hostPath use to read only volumes or exact path matches before a PodSecurityPolicy can effectively restrict hostPath usage to a given subpath.

**Known issues:**
* Status and availability of fixes for regressions in subPath volume mount handling are tracked in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/61563
