body:
### What happened?

In KubeVirt project, we now see a regression when running on Kubernetes `1.25.10 | 1.26.5 | 1.27.2`. If kubelet is restarted on a node, then all the existing and running workloads that use devices are terminated with `UnexpectedAdmissionError`:
```
Warning  UnexpectedAdmissionError  45s   kubelet            Allocate failed due to no healthy devices present; cannot allocate unhealthy devices devices.kubevirt.io/kvm, which is unexpected
Normal   Killing                   42s   kubelet            Stopping container compute
```
KubeVirt runs virtual machines inside pods and uses a device plugin to advertise e.g. `/dev/kvm` on the nodes.

Presumably, this PR changed the behavior: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116376
Original issue: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/109595

### What did you expect to happen?

A potential restart of kubelet should not interrupt the running workloads.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?
with KubeVirt:

- run a KubeVirt VM
- `pkill kubelet`
- observe that the workload pod gets terminated

or with https://github.com/k8stopologyawareschedwg/sample-device-plugin

- make deploy
- make test-both
- pkill kubelet
- the pod gets restarted

### Anything else we need to know?

body:
### What happened?

This happened after upgrading to Kubernetes 1.26 from 1.24

The succession of events we have observed:
- Our workloads use HorizontalPodAutoscaler to scale up due to traffic increase
- Cluster Autoscaler provisions new nodes to accommodate the new replicas
- Traffic goes down
- HPA downsize replicas
- Cluster Autoscaler notices nodes under the threshold of usage and PODs can be accommodated into other nodes
- Nodes are drained and downscaled
- Kubernetes still reports PODs in a "Running" or "Terminating" state in the node that no longer exists
- Kubernetes control plane reports "Orphan pods" on its audit logs

### What did you expect to happen?

Kubernetes Garbage collector to clean up these PODs after the node is gone

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Deploy the following yaml deployments into a K8s cluster 1.26 and terminate one of the nodes

(duplicated port key "containerPort + protocol")
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nginx
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: nginx
    app.kubernetes.io/instance: nginx
    app.kubernetes.io/component: deployment
spec:
  replicas: 100
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: nginx
      app.kubernetes.io/instance: nginx
      app.kubernetes.io/component: deployment
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: nginx
        app.kubernetes.io/instance: nginx
        app.kubernetes.io/component: deployment
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Always
      containers:
        - name: nginx
          image: "nginx:latest"
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
              name: http
              protocol: TCP
            - containerPort: 8080
              name: metrics
              protocol: TCP
```

title: APIServices can be deleted at the apiserver startup

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent

body:
### What happened?

Initially reported at 1.24.10, but it seems to be present in master as well:

We observe that a part of apiservices objects have been removed by "system:apiserver" right after the kubernetes upgrade.

It looks like there is race between "autoregister controller" [1] deleting apiservices and "crd-autoregister controller" populating a map of desired apiservices, i.e. in logs we see:
```
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.070841Z Starting autoregister controller
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.070858Z Waiting for caches to sync for autoregister controller
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.071116Z Starting crd-autoregister controller
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.071128Z Waiting for caches to sync for crd-autoregister
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.270943Z Caches are synced for autoregister controller
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.471323Z Caches are synced for crd-autoregister
```

The unwanted APIServices delete happened at 14:21:35.438 GMT so between crd-autoregister sync and autoregister controller.

It looks like we attempt to wait with "autoregister controller" for crd-autoregister to initialize here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c1d2d4295f9b4eb12bfbf6429fdf989f2ca8a02/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/aggregator.go#L148-L154

but for some reason we don't enter the if branch.

@liggitt tried adding this diff at HEAD:
```
diff --git a/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/aggregator.go b/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/aggregator.go
index 397c151e66a..8b755ab3179 100644
--- a/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/aggregator.go
+++ b/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/aggregator.go
@@ -148,7 +148,11 @@ func createAggregatorServer(aggregatorConfig *aggregatorapiserver.Config, delega
 			// this prevents the autoregistration controller's initial sync from deleting APIServices for CRDs that still exist.
 			// we only need to do this if CRDs are enabled on this server.  We can't use discovery because we are the source for discovery.
 			if aggregatorConfig.GenericConfig.MergedResourceConfig.ResourceEnabled(apiextensionsv1.SchemeGroupVersion.WithResource("customresourcedefinitions")) {
+				klog.Infof("waiting for initial CRD sync...")
 				crdRegistrationController.WaitForInitialSync()
+				klog.Infof("initial CRD sync complete...")
+			} else {
+				klog.Infof("CRD API not enabled, starting APIService registration without waiting for initial CRD sync")
 			}
 			autoRegistrationController.Run(5, context.StopCh)
 		}()
```
and then started a default cluster with local-up-cluster gave:
```
I0518 08:31:16.826743   94479 aggregator.go:155] CRD API not enabled, starting APIService registration without waiting for initial CRD sync
```

which suggest we have a bug in master and the bug is around the "customresourcedefinitions if"

### What did you expect to happen?

APIServices are not deleted, there is no race between crd-autoregister and autoregister controllers

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Restart apiserver with apiservices from crds?

Add a patch proposed by liggit@ and watch the initialization race.

### What happened?

This is a bit hard to reproduce, as it happens in a very specific setup, the problems only happens with `kubelet` 1.27.1, downgrading to 1.26.4 fixes the problem.

In a single-node cluster controlplane pods run as static pods, Rook/Ceph is deployed, and some PVs/PVCs backed by Ceph.

After a unclean shutdown related to some PVs backed by Ceph not being unmounted (this is not a Kubernetes), the `kubelet` which comes up after a reboot doesn't start controlplane static pods, which essentially blocks every other pod from starting (as API server is done).

After a reboot, kubelet is running, but it keeps reporting an error about static pods like:

```
172.20.0.2: {"ts":1683110056228.5916,"caller":"kubelet/kubelet.go:1875","msg":"Unable to attach or mount volumes for pod; skipping pod","pod":{"name":"kube-apiserver-talos-default-controlplane-1","namespace":"kube-system"},"err":"unmounted volumes=[audit secrets config], unattached volumes=[], failed to process volumes=[]: timed out waiting for the condition"}
```

All of the volumes are `hostPath` volumes in a static pod:

```yaml
        volumes:
            - hostPath:
                path: /system/secrets/kubernetes/kube-apiserver
              name: secrets
            - hostPath:
                path: /system/config/kubernetes/kube-apiserver
              name: config
            - hostPath:
                path: /var/log/audit/kube
              name: audit
```

The kubelet is stuck in this state "forever", I tested at least for 8 hours.

If I downgrade the kubelet (without machine reboot) to 1.26.4, it immediately starts the static pods bringing up the node online.

If I try same scenario with reboot with kubelet 1.26.4, the problem doesn't occur either.

Kubelet should run static pods after a reboot.

title: `poststarthook/apiservice-registration-controller` check blocks apiserver readiness for 1 minute if discovery cannot be completed

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent

labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

I’m seeing some odd behavior with 1.28.2 that was not present in earlier releases, with regards to aggregated api services. It appears that the `poststarthook/apiservice-registration-controller` is now blocking the apiserver from becoming ready for 1 minute, if discovery for an aggregated apiservice is not available when the apiserver is started. Note that this only happens if the apiservice is marked available when the apiserver is started; if it is unavailable at startup (Available status: false), or the service has no endpoints, the health check does not block and readyz returns `ok` without delay.

I am seeing this behavior in 1.28.1 and 1.28.2, but not v1.27.6 or v1.27.5

### What did you expect to happen?

apiserver becomes ready without any additional delays

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Deploy metrics-server to a Kubernetes cluster
2. Wait for api registration for `v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io` to complete (Available status is `true`).
3. Kill the kubelet and pods on the node hosting the metrics-server pod, such that the metrics-server service continues to show available endpoints, but the endpoint is not reachable.
4. Restart the apiserver before the `v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io` apiservice is marked unavailable
5. Note that the `poststarthook/apiservice-registration-controller` check blocks readiness for 1 minute. After 1 minute the Available status is updated to `false`, and the health check passes.

### Anything else we need to know?

Other notes:
* Does not appear to make any difference if `AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint` feature-gate is set to false.
* If the metrics-server service has no endpoints available, the apiservice status reason is updated to `MisssingEndpoints` and the check passes quickly.
* If there is an available endpoint, but it is not reachable, the check seems to be stuck retrying the endpoint, with the following message repeated in the logs:
    `Sep 18 20:37:01 systemd-node-1 k3s[8000]: E0918 20:37:01.403911    8000 available_controller.go:460] v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io failed with: failing or missing response from https://10.42.0.2:10250/apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1: Get "https://10.42.0.2:10250/apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1": net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)`


Odd error from GC that I don't remember seeing in the past:
`Sep 18 20:34:30 systemd-node-1 k3s[7903]: I0918 20:34:30.744555    7903 garbagecollector.go:816] "failed to discover some groups" groups="<internal error: json: unsupported type: map[schema.GroupVersion]error>"`

body:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118384 updated evanphx/json-patch from 4.12.0 to 5.6.0, but `v5.6.0+incompatible` is *older* than `v4.12.0+incompatible` (both were tagged on master, and the `+incompatible` bit means this is referencing the content in the root of the repo and not the content inside the `v5` subdirectory) ... and dropped the following fix:

https://github.com/evanphx/json-patch/compare/v5.6.0...v4.12.0

This probably regresses https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105896

It's not clear why that PR bumped to 5.6.0, or if there's a newer commit we can use on master that will result in a pseudoversion off the 5.6.0 stream.

(We can't actually switch to /v5 of the module without also picking up v5 content that caused us compatibility problems in the past (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/91622#issuecomment-637087847))

/priority critical-urgent

initContainers should complete in order before app containers could start on node reboot. Also, all initContainers should run rather than skipped before app-container could start.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a pod with multiple initContainers (which wait for about 2-3 mins) and an app container. On node reboot, app-container is started in parallel to initContainer.

title: NodeAffinity/NodeUnschedulable QueueingHint may miss Node related events that make Pod schedulable

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

/kind bug
/triage accepted
/priority urgent
/sig scheduling
/assign

NodeAffinity QueueingHint may miss Node related events that make Pod schedulable because of preCheck.
It's similar to: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119177#issuecomment-1820091877

So:
1. Node is added. But, it's filtered out by preCheck (due to node's unready or whatever) and the scheduling queue doesn't receive NodeAdded. (noderesourcefit cannot receive NodeAdded.)
2. Node is updated and ready now. But, this event is NodeUpdated.

In such scenarios, NodeAffinity may return `QueueSkip` to the event due to (2).
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/nodeaffinity/node_affinity.go#L94-L131

### What did you expect to happen?

We have to loosen the filtering in `isSchedulableAfterNodeChange` until preCheck is removed.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/110175

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a Pod with NodeAffinity under the situation where no Node can accommodate the Pod.
2. Create a new Node.

It may cause the above problematic scenario.

### What happened?

### What did you expect to happen?

we expect the kube-controller-manage will work well.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The following example can reproduce this problem:
```
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nginx
  labels:
    app: nginx
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 80
    name: web
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: nginx
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  serviceName: "nginx"
  replicas: 100
  podManagementPolicy: Parallel
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
          name: web
        volumeMounts:
        - name: www
          mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: www
      labels:
        a: b
    spec:
      accessModes: [ "ReadWriteOnce" ]
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 1Gi
```

### Anything else we need to know?

After digging into the source code, we found that when using the `Parallel` pod management policy, the statefulset controller will use `slowStartBatch` to start parallel processing.
But the `getPersistentVolumeClaims` which is called during parallel processing may directly update the claims' labels without a lock. This finally causes a concurrent map-accessing problem.

title: Issues with runtime handler supported feature lookup

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
There were a couple changes to merged in v1.30 to guard user namespaces & recursive read only mounts based on runtime self-reported support. When looking through the code, I noticed the following issues:

1. Lookup is done by `runtimeClassName`, rather than `runtimeHandler`:
    - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/634fc1b4836b3a500e0d715d71633ff67690526a/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L2453
    - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/634fc1b4836b3a500e0d715d71633ff67690526a/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/util/util.go#L104-L107
    - Should be using `LookupRuntimeHandler` https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/634fc1b4836b3a500e0d715d71633ff67690526a/pkg/kubelet/runtimeclass/runtimeclass_manager.go#L61
2. Version skew is not handled in the case where the container runtime doesn't provide any RuntimeHandlers, which results in a lot of log spam:
    ```
    Mar 12 19:17:29 kind-control-plane kubelet[719]: E0312 19:17:29.342999     719 kubelet_pods.go:2464] "unknown runtime class" runtimeClassName=""
    Mar 12 19:17:29 kind-control-plane kubelet[719]: E0312 19:17:29.347115     719 kubelet_pods.go:2464] "unknown runtime class" runtimeClassName=""
    Mar 12 19:17:30 kind-control-plane kubelet[719]: E0312 19:17:30.286822     719 kubelet_pods.go:2464] "unknown runtime class" runtimeClassName=""
    Mar 12 19:17:30 kind-control-plane kubelet[719]: E0312 19:17:30.286858     719 kubelet_pods.go:2464] "unknown runtime class" runtimeClassName=""
    Mar 12 19:17:30 kind-control-plane kubelet[719]: E0312 19:17:30.286864     719 kubelet_pods.go:2464] "unknown runtime class" runtimeClassName=""
    ```

/cc @haircommander

body:
### What happened?

We have encountered a situation when a Job controller is stuck constantly failing on the `syncJob`. It fails with the validation message 
like this `job_controller.go:600] "Unhandled Error" err="syncing job: tracking status: adding uncounted pods to status: Job.batch \"pi\" is invalid: status.uncountedTerminatedPods.failed[0]: Duplicate value: \"ca8e72a0-735a-45c9-925d-d82c91256b86\"" logger="UnhandledError"`.

The Job:
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  generation: 1
  namespace: default
spec:
  backoffLimit: 6
  completionMode: NonIndexed
  completions: 1
  parallelism: 1
  suspend: false
  ...
status:
  failed: 1
  ready: 0
  ...
  uncountedTerminatedPods:
    succeeded:
    - xyz
  ```
  Pod:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  ...
  finalizers:
  - batch.kubernetes.io/job-tracking
  ...
  uid: xyz
spec:
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - preference:
          matchExpressions:
          - ...
        weight: 100
...
status:
  conditions:
  - message: 'Taint manager: deleting due to NoExecute taint'
    reason: DeletionByTaintManager
    status: "True"
    type: DisruptionTarget
  - status: "True"
    type: Initialized
  - reason: PodFailed
    status: "False"
    type: Ready
  - reason: PodFailed
    status: "False"
    type: ContainersReady
  - status: "True"
    type: PodScheduled
  containerStatuses:
  - state:
      terminated:
        exitCode: 137
        finishedAt: null
        message: The container could not be located when the pod was terminated
        reason: ContainerStatusUnknown
        startedAt: null
  message: 'Pod was rejected: Predicate NodeAffinity failed'
  phase: Failed
  qosClass: Guaranteed
  reason: NodeAffinity

```

### What did you expect to happen?

Job controller does not get stuck. It might be that the issue originated from user actions, or kubelet bug which transitioned the Pod first to `Succeeded`, then to `Failed`. However, Job controller should be resilient to a situation like this.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

It remains unclear what happened exactly - if the pod was transitioned to `Succeeded`, and after to `Failed`.
See below an artificial scenario which reproduces the Job controller getting stuck.



### Anything else we need to know?

This scenario renders the Job controller stuck in v1.30.0. It involves a pod transitioning first to `Succeeded`. then to `Failed`. We had a similar issue in the past with pods being categorized first as Failed, then Succeeded: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/111646/

1. Create the Job as follows:
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: pi
  labels:
    environment: test
spec:
  completions: 2
  parallelism: 2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        environment: test
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 1
      containers:
        - name: busybox
          image: busybox
          command: ["sleep", "5m"]
      restartPolicy: Never
  backoffLimit: 1
```
2. Create CEL validation `kubectl create -f cel.yaml` to make sure the Pod finalizer removal request fails:
```yaml
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: "demo-policy.example.com"
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:   [""]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations:  ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
      resources:   ["pods"]
  validations:
    - expression: "size(object.metadata.finalizers) > 0"

The crash happens [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7c48c2bd72b9bf5c44d21d7338cc7bea77d0ad2a/pkg/scheduler/schedule_one.go#L502) because the `len(nodes)` is `0` in certain cases. 

### What did you expect to happen?

`kube-scheduler` should not crash, on v1.29.4 it doesn't happen.

On v1.29.4 the `kube-scheduler` is just printing these error logs, but doesn't crash:

```
E0517 13:19:26.611504       1 schedule_one.go:1003] "Error scheduling pod; retrying" err="nodeinfo not found for node name \"invalid-node\"" pod="default/break-kube-scheduler"
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a pod like this:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: break-kube-scheduler
spec:
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        nodeSelectorTerms:
        - matchFields:
          - key: metadata.name
            operator: In
            values:
            - invalid-node # a node that doesn't exist
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: alpine
    command: ["cat"]
    stdin: true
```
The important part is that the affinity doesn't match a real/valid node.

Once this pod is being processed by `kube-scheduler` it will crash and continue to do so until the pod is deleted.

### Anything else we need to know?

This issue was triggered during the rotation of control-plane nodes. In our setup we update the control plane by scaling from 1 to 2 instances. Once both a ready, the old is being terminated via EC2 API. At this stage the kube-controller-manager _sometimes_ manages to create a replacement daemonset pod once the old node is being deleted. This results in a pod targeting a no longer existing node via `affinity` as illustrated in the example above. For some reason, when the `kube-scheduler` is crashing the `kube-controller-manager` doesn't delete the extra/invalid daemonset pod. Not sure if this is another issue or it has always happened in our setup, but only v1.30 makes `kube-scheduler` crash which causes an actual issue.

title: DeltaFIFO TransformFunc can result in a data race on re-sync

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: triage/accepted

body:
We use a `TransformFunc` to nil out the `ManagedFields`:

```
func(obj interface{}) (interface{}, error) {
    resourceUtil.MustToMeta(obj).SetManagedFields(nil)
    return obj, nil
})
```

However on a re-sync, this results in a data race that was observed when running unit tests:

```
WARNING: DATA RACE
Write at 0x00c0006accc0 by goroutine 81:
  runtime.mapdelete_faststr()
      /usr/lib/golang/src/runtime/map_faststr.go:301 +0x0
  k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured.RemoveNestedField()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/apimachinery@v0.29.3/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured/helpers.go:274 +0x1e6
  k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured.(*Unstructured).SetManagedFields()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/apimachinery@v0.29.3/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured/unstructured.go:476 +0x87
  github.com/submariner-io/admiral/pkg/syncer.NewResourceSyncer.func3()
      /go/pkg/mod/github.com/submariner-io/admiral@v0.18.0-m2.0.20240415195632-6c525b3cb5e9/pkg/syncer/resource_syncer.go:260 +0x4c
  k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache.(*DeltaFIFO).queueActionLocked()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/client-go@v0.29.3/tools/cache/delta_fifo.go:456 +0x101
  k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache.(*DeltaFIFO).syncKeyLocked()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/client-go@v0.29.3/tools/cache/delta_fifo.go:746 +0x154
  k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache.(*DeltaFIFO).Resync()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/client-go@v0.29.3/tools/cache/delta_fifo.go:717 +0x1b6
  k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache.(*Reflector).startResync()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/client-go@v0.29.3/tools/cache/reflector.go:378 +0x351
  k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache.(*Reflector).ListAndWatch.func2()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/client-go@v0.29.3/tools/cache/reflector.go:356 +0x5d

Previous read at 0x00c0006accc0 by goroutine 82:
  runtime.mapaccess2_faststr()
      /usr/lib/golang/src/runtime/map_faststr.go:108 +0x0
  k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured.NestedFieldNoCopy()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/apimachinery@v0.29.3/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured/helpers.go:61 +0x10f
  k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured.nestedMapNoCopy()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/apimachinery@v0.29.3/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured/helpers.go:195 +0x66
  k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured.NestedStringMap()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/apimachinery@v0.29.3/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured/helpers.go:167 +0x6e
  k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured.(*Unstructured).GetLabels()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/apimachinery@v0.29.3/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured/unstructured.go:400 +0x94
  github.com/submariner-io/admiral/pkg/syncer.getClusterIDLabel()
      /go/pkg/mod/github.com/submariner-io/admiral@v0.18.0-m2.0.20240415195632-6c525b3cb5e9/pkg/syncer/resource_syncer.go:681 +0x65
  github.com/submariner-io/admiral/pkg/syncer.(*resourceSyncer).shouldSync()
      /go/pkg/mod/github.com/submariner-io/admiral@v0.18.0-m2.0.20240415195632-6c525b3cb5e9/pkg/syncer/resource_syncer.go:647 +0x4d
  github.com/submariner-io/admiral/pkg/syncer.(*resourceSyncer).processNextWorkItem()
      /go/pkg/mod/github.com/submariner-io/admiral@v0.18.0-m2.0.20240415195632-6c525b3cb5e9/pkg/syncer/resource_syncer.go:448 +0x3ad
  github.com/submariner-io/admiral/pkg/syncer.(*resourceSyncer).processNextWorkItem-fm()
      <autogenerated>:1 +0x89
  github.com/submariner-io/admiral/pkg/workqueue.(*queueType).processNextWorkItem.func1()
      /go/pkg/mod/github.com/submariner-io/admiral@v0.18.0-m2.0.20240415195632-6c525b3cb5e9/pkg/workqueue/queue.go:103 +0x59
```

The read had occurred previously during a `ResourceEventHandler` callback.

On re-sync, the `DeltaFIFO` retrieves every object from the `knownObjects` cache,  invokes the transform function, and re-queues them.  However, the object instances are the same as those stored in the cache so mutating them outside the cache without lock protection is unsafe. It is documented that the "_TransformFunc sees the object before any other actor, and it is now safe to mutate the object in place instead of making a copy_" however this is not the case on a re-sync. The `DeltaFIFO` should make a copy of the objects retrieved from the cache store on a re-sync or perhaps elide the `TransformFunc` on a re-sync since the objects would already have been transformed.

As a workaround, I changed our `TransformFunc` to only nil the `ManagedFields` if not already nil but this is a latent bug that others will likely run into.

title: Potential conflict of apiserver_storage_size_bytes label (cluster) with Prometheus HA pair dedup logic

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/instrumentation
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Instrumentation.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
Hi,

I stumbled upon https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/metrics/#list-of-alpha-kubernetes-metrics

> **apiserver_storage_size_bytes**
> Size of the storage database file physically allocated in bytes.
> **Stability Level**:ALPHA
> **Type**: Custom
> **Labels**:cluster
> 

Using `cluster` as label sounds intuitive and valid , but ... I believe this has the potential for unexpected consequences for k8s users using Prometheus HA pair deduplication logic in remote storage, for which the default labels are `cluster` and `__replica__`, where `cluster` does not necessarily refers to the k8 cluster.  See:
https://cortexmetrics.io/docs/guides/ha-pair-handling/
https://grafana.com/docs/mimir/latest/configure/configure-high-availability-deduplication/#how-to-configure-prometheus
https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/send-data/metrics/metrics-prometheus/#sending-data-from-multiple-high-availability-prometheus-instances
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prometheus/latest/userguide/Send-high-availability-data.html
https://github.com/timescale/promscale/blob/master/docs/high-availability/prometheus-HA.md

Could a different label be considered before marking this metric [stable](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123342)?

body:
### What happened?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/126799 seems to have broken the vendor by adding a transitive dependency at a version that no longer exists

### What did you expect to happen?

`./hack/update-vendor.sh` should not fail

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

body:
### What happened?

Listing `v1alpha3.ResourceSlice`s on v1.31.0 returns an object with a `listMeta` field instead of the standard `metadata` field for (list) objects:

```sh
$ curl -kL --cert client.pem --key client.key.pem 'https://127.0.0.1:39987/apis/resource.k8s.io/v1alpha3/resourceslices'

{
  "kind": "ResourceSliceList",
  "apiVersion": "resource.k8s.io/v1alpha3",
  "listMeta": {
    "resourceVersion": "522"
  },
  "items": []
}
```

Listing `v1alpha2.ResourceSlice`s on v1.30.3 behaves correctly:

```sh
$ curl -kL --cert client.pem --key client.key.pem 'https://127.0.0.1:34519/apis/resource.k8s.io/v1alpha2/resourceslices'

{
  "kind": "ResourceSliceList",
  "apiVersion": "resource.k8s.io/v1alpha2",
  "metadata": {
    "resourceVersion": "422"
  },
  "items": []
}
```

This is also propagated to the Swagger spec (which is how I noticed it, since I maintain the Rust bindings for the client API). v1.31.0:

```json
    "io.k8s.api.resource.v1alpha3.ResourceSliceList": {
        "listMeta": {
          "$ref": "#/definitions/io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1.ListMeta",
          "description": "Standard list metadata"
        }
```

v1.30.3:

```json
    "io.k8s.api.resource.v1alpha2.ResourceSliceList": {
        "metadata": {
          "$ref": "#/definitions/io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1.ListMeta",
          "description": "Standard list metadata"
        }
```

### What did you expect to happen?

As explained above.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Deploy v1.31.0 with `DynamicResourceAllocation` feature gate enabled and runtime config `resource.k8s.io/v1alpha3=true`. With kind, this is:

    ```yaml
    kind: Cluster
    apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
    featureGates:
      DynamicResourceAllocation: true
    runtimeConfig:
      'resource.k8s.io/v1alpha3': 'true'
    ```

2. Perform the API server request as in the above curl command in any way you like as long as it lets you see the raw JSON response.

title: Pod status phase misses Pending transition after node reboot

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

When a kubernetes node is rebooted, all the containers running on the node are terminated and then created & started over again. When the pod has a list of init containers runing, and if the init container takes a little bit time (longer than PLEG period), the pod is supposed to have `status.phase: Pending`, but instead, during the whole operation, `status.phase` is always `Running`.

This new behavior (always has `status.phase: Running`) started when "restartable init container" was [introduced][1]. After node reboots, all the regular init containers are started one by one, so `pendingInitialization` is supposed by larger than 0 (unless the init container is completed pretty fast that PLEG doesn't catch any running init container), and should report `Pending` phase. But the behavior has changed to check further whether there are any other regular containers that have started. In the case of node reboot, all the other regular containers are already terminated, and then considered as "yes, they have started", and then no longer reported as `Pending`.

I think this behavior change is unexpected, as that violates the [definition][2] of "Running":

> // PodRunning means the pod has been bound to a node and all of the containers have been started.
	// At least one container is still running or is in the process of being restarted.

None of the containers are started or running, and they are not in the process of being started or restarted since init containers are still running.

[1]: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/099a88370d017dacf16e67306ebcdec8394fae83/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L1675-L1685
[2]: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/099a88370d017dacf16e67306ebcdec8394fae83/pkg/apis/core/types.go#L2871


### What did you expect to happen?

I expect that pods with init containers should transition into "Pending" when kubelet observed that its regular init container is still running and none of its main containers are started.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Launch a cluster with minikube:

```console
$ minikube start --nodes=2 --kubernetes-version=v1.30.3
```

2. Create the following pod:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: sleep
spec:
  restartPolicy: Always
  containers:
  - name: sleep
    image: busybox
    command:
    - sleep
    - infinity
  initContainers:
  - name: snap
    image: busybox
    command:
    - sleep
    - "10"
```

3. Log in the node and simulate "reboot"

```console
$ minikube ssh --node <node-which-runs-the-pod-above>
...
# systemctl stop kubelet
# docker stop $(docker ps -aq)
# systemctl start kubelet
```

4. Observe the pod status via:

```console
$ k get pods -w -o jsonpath='{$.status.phase}{"\n"}'
```

On 1.30.3, the output from 4 is `Running` constantly, while in previous kubernetes version (for e,g, v1.23.17), it will show "Pending" while the init container is still Running.

body:
A downstream e2e test creating / attaching / mounting / writing to a GCE PD CSI volume is working on latest 1.31 releases and failing with a 1.32.0-rc.0 kubelet. Nothing else changed between the passing and failing run (same OS level, same versions of all other components including CSI driver,  etc).

Bisected to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127076, when kubelet started being built with go 1.23.

[Many things changed in go 1.23 around filesystem handing](https://tip.golang.org/doc/go1.23#ospkgos), and it doesn't look like kubelet volume code reacted to those.

Building the kubelet with `winsymlink=0` resolved the issue.

> On Windows, the mode bits reported by [Lstat](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/os#Lstat) and [Stat](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/os#Stat) for reparse points changed. Mount points no longer have [ModeSymlink](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/os#ModeSymlink) set, and reparse points that are not symlinks, Unix sockets, or dedup files now always have [ModeIrregular](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/os#ModeIrregular) set. This behavior is controlled by the winsymlink setting. For Go 1.23, it defaults to winsymlink=1. Previous versions default to winsymlink=0.

> On Windows, [EvalSymlinks](https://tip.golang.org/pkg/path/filepath#EvalSymlinks) no longer evaluates mount points, which was a source of many inconsistencies and bugs. This behavior is controlled by the winsymlink setting. For Go 1.23, it defaults to winsymlink=1. Previous versions default to winsymlink=0.

There are other stdlib windows fs behavior changes as well:

> On Windows, Readlink no longer tries to normalize volumes to drive letters, which was not always even possible. This behavior is controlled by the winreadlinkvolume setting. For Go 1.23, it defaults to winreadlinkvolume=1. Previous versions default to winreadlinkvolume=0.

> On Windows, EvalSymlinks no longer tries to normalize volumes to drive letters, which was not always even possible. This behavior is controlled by the winreadlinkvolume setting. For Go 1.23, it defaults to winreadlinkvolume=1. Previous versions default to winreadlinkvolume=0.

There is still code throughout kubelet like this (as well as many uses of stat / lstat), which may not be correct in go 1.23 on windows any more:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/04ac01e9b64ca7006be0f88f0937122226723028/pkg/util/filesystem/util_windows.go#L45-L91

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2b472fe4690c83a2b343995f88050b2a3e9ff0fa/staging/src/k8s.io/mount-utils/mount.go#L258-L270

We're still trying to narrow down what code in the Kubelet needs to be adjusted and was failing with default go 1.23 behavior, but wanted to raise this now for visibility to the 1.32 release.

/cc @msau42 @BenTheElder @aojea 
/cc @kubernetes/release-team 
/milestone v1.32

title: [release-1.33] Land etcd v3.5.21 in K8s 1.33.0

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Etcd.

body:
As mentioned in https://etcd.io/blog/2025/upgrade_from_3.5_to_3.6_issue/, we fixed an upgrade issue (3.5 -> 3.6) in 3.5.20, and the root cause is the membership data may become inconsistent between v2store (deprecated, but remain source of truth for membership data in 3.5) and v3store (source of truth in 3.6).

Without it, the K8s 1.33.0 → 1.34 upgrades may fail due to https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/issues/19557.

So we should land etcd v3.5.20+ (latest 3.5.21) in k8s 1.33.0 instead of 1.33.1

title: Excessive conntrack cleanup causes high memory (12GB) and CPU usage when any Pod with a UDP port changes

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/network
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Network.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened? We are encountering a severe performance issue in kube-proxy (v1.32) when any Pod with a UDP port is updated (e.g., CoreDNS). In the new kube-proxy implementation, changes to Services or Pods that expose UDP ports trigger a full conntrack cleanup. This cleanup process iterates over the entire conntrack table, leading to extremely high resource consumption—sometimes up to 12 GB of memory and 1.5 CPU cores per kube-proxy instance. In a simple test, we observed 2,780 instances of the log message "Adding conntrack filter for cleanup", which caused an OOM when kube-proxy was limited to 256 MB of memory. Without that limit, kube-proxy memory usage spiked to 12 GB. On nodes with large conntrack tables, kube-proxy effectively becomes stuck, consuming all available memory each time there is a UDP endpoint change. This issue appears to be systemic; every change in a Pod with a UDP port triggers all kube-proxy instances to perform the extensive cleanup. Currently, there is no option to disable or throttle this behavior, which disrupts cluster stability and can lead to service degradation or outages. We request that the cleanup logic be revised to target only the relevant conntrack entries or that a mechanism be provided to disable or limit this aggressive cleanup behavior. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127318 https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126130 ### What did you expect to happen? We expected kube-proxy to handle conntrack cleanup in a more efficient and targeted way. Even if it needs to scan a significant portion of the conntrack table, it should do so without causing a spike to 12 GB of memory usage. Ideally, it would either: - Limit its cleanup to entries relevant to the specific changed UDP endpoint. - Provide a way to configure or disable this aggressive cleanup process so it does not risk out-of-memory (OOM) events or excessively high CPU usage. ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? - Deploy multiple Pods that generate a high volume of DNS requests, for example: - A simple Golang application making repeated DNS lookups without any caching mechanism. - Observe kube-proxy resource usage (memory and CPU) on that node. - Delete or update the coredns Pod (which also uses UDP DNS). - Watch the logs and resource usage of kube-proxy closely, noting the surge in memory (potentially up to 12 GB) and CPU usage as it performs the conntrack cleanup. ### Anything else we need to know? ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f75f0bc0-e394-45fa-b323-2f6fc0570386) ### Kubernetes version

title: ServiceCIDR breaks conversion from Single to DualStack

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/network
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Network.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
When converting a cluster form single to dual stack, operators change the configured `--service-cluster-ip-range string` to add a new range, per example `--service-cluster-ip-range 10.96.0.0/24`  will be updated to `--service-cluster-ip-range 10.96.0.0/24,2001:10:96::/112`.

Moving from single to dual stack is a fully supported operation, since is adding a new range to the cluster

Moving from IPv4 to IPv6 or from dual to single it is "allowed" by the system, but it is not supported, since there is no guarantee that the services that you have working will keep working https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114743 , same as having different apiserver with differnet ranges configured.

Current ServiceCIDR implementation tries to solve that problem by generating an unique object `ServiceCIDR` with an special name `kubernetes` that guarantees the consistency in the cluster. It also offers now a safe mechanisms for admins that wants to perform those disruptive operations, before operators had to recreate their clusters, but with ServiceCIDR they can automate the migration, this is supported and tested (though not well documented (AI @aojea to document this)

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b15dfce6cbd0d5bbbcd6172cf7e2082f4d31055e/test/integration/servicecidr/migration_test.go#L40-L48

The problem is that with current implementation, if the cluster moves to dual stack, it is waiting for the operator to perform the migration, and that is a breaking change in behavior, so we must keep allowing the migration from single to dual stack without any manual intervention

/sig network
/assign @aojea

### Since when has it been flaking?

[2025-12-11 00:08:52 +0000 UTC](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-ipv6/1998907708706656256)

{ failed [FAILED] 1 errors:
pod pod-terminate-status-0-6 on node kind-worker container unexpected exit code 2: start=2025-12-11 00:21:17 +0000 UTC end=2025-12-11 00:21:17 +0000 UTC reason=Error message=
In [It] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/node/pods.go:1381 @ 12/11/25 00:21:49.467
}

### Anything else we need to know?

When runc's execution of a container is sent a sigterm / sigkill signal before it has handed off to the container process with execve, it exits with exit code 2.

This is actually orthogonal to what this test was *trying* to verify, which is that stopped containers do not report *success*, and do not re-run, and stay failed.

Possible fix for improving runc's mapping of signal-terminated runs to expected error codes in 
https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/pull/5189

Relaxing the e2e test to tolerate exit code 2 as another possible expected non-success code in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137749

title: StatefulSet pod revisions not updated when MaxUnavailableStatefulSet enabled

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
### What happened?

I decided to open this issue after investigating https://github.com/stackabletech/trino-operator/issues/854.

The high level description of the problem is that the stateful set controller doesn't update the pods according to the latest STS revision and the pods are left crashlooping **if the first revision is faulty** and can never become available. This doesn't happen if the `MaxUnavailableStatefulSet` feature is disabled.

Unfortunately I cannot create a much simpler example, but I attach the relevant controller log messages below.

Based on these logs you can see that:

1. The Stackable Operator for Trino (`trino-op` from now on) creates two `StatefulSet` objects with a single replica. They both expose the same problem, so for simplicity, I will use only one of them from now on (`trino-coordinator-default`).
2. The initial revision of this sts is `trino-coordinator-default-5f5598d4c8`. This first STS  revision has a faulty command args  and can never become available.
3. The `trino-op` updates the sts rapidly to the revision `trino-coordinator-default-787556ff59`. Now the STS command args are correct and the pods should be able to become ready.
4. The pod created initially is never updated so it never becomes ready.

To summarize my understanding, the sts revision is never updated if the pod never becomes ready, and the pod doesn't become ready because it has an old revision.

In the logs you see that `currentRevision` is never the same as `updateRevision`:

```
I0304 15: 25:06.514308       1 stateful_set_control.go: 146]"StatefulSet revisions" statefulSet = "kuttl-test-distinct-turtle/trino-coordinator-default" currentRevision = "trino-coordinator-default-5f5598d4c8" updateRevision = "trino-coordinator-default-787556ff59"
```

### What did you expect to happen?

The pod should become ready according to the `updateRevision` of the sts.
Again, this was indeed the case until `MaxUnavailableStatefulSet` feature gate was enabled.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I can reproduce this bug using the `trino-op` but unfortunately I don't have a minimal example.

Attached are the relevant kube controller logs.

title: EasyCLA blocks website main to dev branch-sync PRs on kubernetes-prow[bot] merge commits

labels.name: priority/critical-urgent
labels.description: Highest priority. Must be actively worked on as someone's top priority right now.

labels.name: sig/contributor-experience
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Contributor Experience.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
### What happened?

Weekly "Merge main branch into dev-1.37" sync PRs against `kubernetes/website` fail the **EasyCLA** check with `Missing CLA Authorization`, and the only committer flagged is the bot identity `kubernetes-prow[bot]`.

These sync PRs merge `main` into the release dev branch, which by design pulls in the merge commits that Prow created when merging earlier PRs. EasyCLA evaluates every commit author in the PR, finds the `kubernetes-prow[bot]`-authored merge commits, and reports them as not covered by a signed CLA. Every human contributor on the branch passes; only the bot fails.

Key detail: in the same EasyCLA report, the older bot identity **`k8s-ci-robot` (name "Kubernetes Prow Robot") passes** the CLA check, while the newer GitHub App identity **`kubernetes-prow[bot]` fails**. So merge commits that used to be authored by the CLA-authorized `k8s-ci-robot` are now authored by `kubernetes-prow[bot]`, which has no CLA association - that identity change appears to be what newly breaks these sync PRs.

Examples:
- https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/56271 — EasyCLA `fail`. `k8s-ci-robot` ✅ (e.g. `373112ed5c7fe7c2a5e502bb61b3aad9b917cf87`), but `@kubernetes-prow[bot]` ❌ (35 merge commits, e.g. `1797afad91da7d36ecf0ca3ed975a71e6716a860`).
- https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/56300 — fresh sync PR, same failure on the same bot identity.

This blocks the routine weekly branch sync during the v1.37 cycle: `tide` reports "Not mergeable. Needs ... cncf-cla: yes" because the bot commits aren't CLA-authorized.

### What did you expect to happen?

Merge commits authored by `kubernetes-prow[bot]` that arrive via a `main` → `dev-*` sync merge should not block EasyCLA / the `cncf-cla: yes` label - the same way the older `k8s-ci-robot` identity is already treated - so the routine weekly branch sync can proceed.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Follow the [documented weekly branch-sync flow](https://github.com/kubernetes/sig-release/blob/master/release-team/role-handbooks/docs/Release-Timeline.md#weekly-branch-sync-prs) for `kubernetes/website`: fetch `upstream/main` and `upstream/dev-1.37`, fast-forward `dev-1.37`, then `git merge upstream/main` onto a `merged-main-dev-1.37` branch.
2. Push the branch and open a PR targeting `dev-1.37`.
3. The merge brings in `kubernetes-prow[bot]` merge commits from `main`.
4. EasyCLA runs and reports `Missing CLA Authorization`, flagging only `@kubernetes-prow[bot]` (while `k8s-ci-robot` on the same PR passes).

### Anything else we need to know?

Rebasing/squashing is not a viable fix here: the entire purpose of the sync PR is to carry `main`'s merge history into the dev branch, so dropping those bot merge commits would defeat the sync. Looking for guidance on the right path - e.g. giving `kubernetes-prow[bot]` the same CLA treatment that `k8s-ci-robot` already has (allowlisting the bot identity in EasyCLA), an admin merge/override for sync PRs, or a different recommended sync procedure that avoids carrying bot-authored merge commits.

Filing as a tracking issue per advice in Slack to get direction from the owning SIG. Marking priority critical-urgent for now since it blocks the v1.37 weekly docs branch sync; happy to lower it once a fix path is confirmed.

body:
### Which jobs are flaking?

sig-release-master-blocking#gce-cos-alphafeatures-master (`ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-master`)
sig-release-1.37-blocking#gce-cos-alphafeatures-1.37 (`ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-beta`, the fork of the same job)

Triage: https://storage.googleapis.com/k8s-triage/index.html?job=%5Eci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-master%24&test=%5ETimeout%24

Status 2026-09-23: tracked as FLAKY on the CI Signal board per the Release Signal lead, triage accepted by SIG Node (harche), priority/critical-urgent as set at triage. I hold the Release Signal follow-up.

Next step per upodroid is a test-side improvement by SIG Node. No test owner is confirmed yet. Release-impact assessment: @kannon92 stated in the SIG Node thread that this should not block v1.38.0-alpha.1 and that it should still be fixed for v1.38. No mitigation has been agreed yet.

Master count from the 2026-09-16 00:57 UTC run through the 2026-09-23 18:44 UTC run is 23 of 93 completed runs timed out (25%), 2 of the last 13. On 1.37 it is 1 of its last 4.

The recent failures share one pattern: suite passed, teardown interrupted by the timer. The numbers further down are the 2026-09-21 06:00 UTC snapshot.

### Which tests are flaking?

`kubetest.Timeout`. The e2e suite passes in all but one of the timed-out runs; in that one the timeout interrupted the suite.

### Since when has it been flaking?

Snapshot 2026-09-21 06:00 UTC. On master, 15 of the 61 runs since 2026-09-16 00:57 UTC hit the timeout: the first at 2026-09-17 13:04 UTC, the last two at 2026-09-21 00:16 UTC and 02:19 UTC, with passing runs in between. On the 1.37 fork, 7 of the 21 runs since 2026-09-16 01:00 UTC, the latest at 2026-09-20 13:03 UTC.

Examples:
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-master/2101858636748820480 (2026-09-21 02:19 UTC)
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-master/2101736329489420288 (2026-09-20 18:13 UTC)
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-master/2101281830744363008 (2026-09-19 12:07 UTC)
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-beta/2101658314709405696 (1.37, 2026-09-20 13:03 UTC)

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-release-master-blocking#gce-cos-alphafeatures-master

### Reason for failure (if possible)

The job runs out of its kubetest budget, not out of tests. It passes `--timeout=120m` to kubetest, which covers cluster up, the tests and teardown. Up and teardown are steady at about 15 minutes together, which leaves roughly 105 minutes for the suite. In 14 of the 15 timed-out master runs the suite finished with `91 Passed | 0 Failed` after 105 to 112 minutes and the budget ran out in the teardown steps; in the other run ginkgo was interrupted at 113 minutes with one spec still running (`90 Passed | 1 Failed`).

The suite's runtime is not fixed. The same 91 specs took 76 minutes in a passing run on 2026-09-19 at 14:08 UTC (https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-master/2101312282582585344) and 106 minutes in the timed-out run two hours earlier (https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-alphafeatures-master/2101281830744363008), on the same Kubernetes commit (`v1.38.0-alpha.0.948+96b5e4e3ae3f8d`) and the same COS image. So a code or image change alone does not explain the timeouts; whether something makes the resize path slower under some conditions is open. Across the 59 runs since 2026-09-16 the test phase ranged from 76 to 113 minutes; the 45 passing runs took 76 to 103 minutes with a median of 87, and passing and timed-out runs occur on the same commits.

Almost all of that variance sits in one feature. `[Feature:InPlacePodVerticalScaling]` is 63 of the 91 specs and took 57 minutes in the fast run and 86 in the slow one; the other 28 specs took 19 minutes in both. 62 of the 63 resize specs are slower in the slow run, by 20 seconds at the median and up to 83 seconds, with no single spec standing out, so the extra time is inside the resize specs themselves. What inside them is slower I have not established; the kubelet logs of both runs show no deferred or infeasible resizes.

This is the same shape as #141186 on `ci-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce-alpha-features`, which runs almost the same focus. That was resolved by kubernetes/test-infra#37724: kubetest to `--timeout=180m`, the prow timeout to 3h20m, and the job moved to release-informing, on the basis that alpha-feature lanes do not fit the two-hour release-blocking budget. The note on that issue that the 1.37 blocking board shows the same thing (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/141186#issuecomment-5316283473) was not followed up for the sig-release jobs, which still have `--timeout=120m` and a 2h20m prow timeout in `config/jobs/kubernetes/sig-release/gce-cos-e2e-master.yaml` and `release-branch-jobs/1.37.yaml`.

### Anything else we need to know?

Update after upodroid's comment (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/142262#issuecomment-5759352510): the next step is on the test side. SIG Node is asked to look at reducing the resize specs' execution time or their run-to-run variance while keeping the coverage. Skipping the resize tests is not on the table, and a timeout increase or dashboard change is not agreed; it would come after that attempt, if at all. A test-side owner is not confirmed yet.

Background for whoever picks it up: InPlacePodVerticalScaling is Stable since 1.35, and this lane is the only blocking coverage the 63 resize specs have. The sig-node node-e2e lanes skip `[Feature:InPlacePodVerticalScaling]` explicitly or do not focus on it; the node alpha-features lane (`ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-alpha-features`) ran 3 memory-backed-volume resize specs in its latest build, none of the 63. The job runs ginkgo with `--nodes=1`, and the presubmit alpha-features job sets `--ginkgo-parallel=1` explicitly, so I have not assumed parallelism is safe for these specs. The sibling job's uncensored timing distribution is in the comments.

The alpha.1 assessment is complete: this issue was assessed as non-blocking for that cut. The issue remains open because the flake still needs a v1.38 fix. Release impact should be reassessed for later cuts if it remains unresolved. FLAKY on the CI Signal board is a tracking category and says nothing about the cut.

This is not #142205. That one is a single spec (the allocated pods endpoint test) failing on the kind alpha-beta lane. Here the specs pass, apart from the one interrupted run, and the job runs out of its time budget.

### Relevant SIG(s)

/sig testing
/sig node
/sig release

/kind flake
/priority critical-urgent
/cc @kubernetes/release-team-release-signal

body:
/sig cluster-lifecycle
/sig etcd
/kind bug
/priority critical-urgent

## Summary

All currently supported Kubernetes versions (v1.34.x, v1.35.x, v1.36.x)
ship `registry.k8s.io/etcd:3.6.6-0`, which contains **61 known
vulnerabilities** in the etcd binary alone including **2 Critical**.
The upstream etcd project has released v3.7.1.

etcd 3.6.6-0 has the **oldest dependencies of any Kubernetes control
plane component**, compiled with Go 1.24.10 and gRPC 1.71.1.

## Confirmed Across All Supported K8s Versions
```
$ kubeadm config images list --kubernetes-version v1.35.1
registry.k8s.io/etcd:3.6.6-0

$ kubeadm config images list --kubernetes-version v1.35.7
registry.k8s.io/etcd:3.6.6-0

$ kubeadm config images list --kubernetes-version v1.36.3
registry.k8s.io/etcd:3.6.6-0
```

## Scan Results
```
$ trivy image registry.k8s.io/etcd:3.6.6-0

etcd binary: 61 CVEs (CRITICAL: 2, HIGH: 32, MEDIUM: 23, LOW: 1, UNKNOWN: 3)
etcdctl: 42 CVEs (CRITICAL: 2, HIGH: 20, MEDIUM: 17, LOW: 1, UNKNOWN: 2)
etcdutl: 59 CVEs (CRITICAL: 2, HIGH: 30, MEDIUM: 23, LOW: 1, UNKNOWN: 3)
```

## CRITICAL Vulnerabilities

| CVE | Library | Installed | Fixed | Title |
|-----|---------|-----------|-------|-------|
| CVE-2026-33186 | google.golang.org/grpc | **v1.71.1** | 1.79.3 | **gRPC-Go: Authorization bypass due to improper HTTP/2 path validation** |
| CVE-2025-68121 | Go stdlib | **v1.24.10** | 1.24.13 | **Incorrect certificate validation during TLS session resumption** |

**Both are directly exploitable in etcd:**
- etcd IS a gRPC server — gRPC is its primary communication protocol
- etcd uses mTLS for peer-to-peer and client communication

## etcd-Specific CVEs 

etcd 3.6.6 has additional CVEs due to its older Go stdlib (1.24.10):

| CVE | Severity | Title |
|-----|----------|-------|
| CVE-2025-61726 | HIGH | Memory exhaustion in net/url query parameter parsing |
| CVE-2025-61729 | HIGH | DoS via excessive resource consumption in crypto/x509 |
| CVE-2025-61727 | MEDIUM | x509 subdomain constraint doesn't restrict wildcard SANs |
| CVE-2025-61728 | MEDIUM | Excessive CPU in archive/zip |
| CVE-2025-61730 | MEDIUM | TLS handshake messages at incorrect encryption level |
| CVE-2025-47913 | HIGH | SSH client panic (x/crypto 0.36.0 specific) |
| CVE-2025-47914 | MEDIUM | SSH Agent DoS via malformed messages |
| CVE-2025-58181 | MEDIUM | DoS via unbounded GSSAPI memory consumption |
| CVE-2025-47911 | MEDIUM | Quadratic HTML parsing complexity |
| CVE-2025-58190 | MEDIUM | Infinite HTML parsing loop |

## Impact

etcd stores **all Kubernetes cluster state** including secrets,
configmaps, RBAC policies, and service accounts. A compromise of
etcd means complete cluster compromise. The CRITICAL gRPC
authorization bypass (CVE-2026-33186) and TLS certificate
validation failure (CVE-2025-68121) in the component that guards
all cluster data is an urgent concern.

## Request

1. **Bump etcd to 3.7.1** (or latest compatible) in upcoming
   patch releases for v1.35.x and v1.36.x
2. If 3.7.x has compatibility concerns, at minimum bump to a
   newer 3.6.x patch (if one exists with updated dependencies)
3. Is there a tracking issue for etcd version updates?

## How to Reproduce

```bash
trivy image registry.k8s.io/etcd:3.6.6-0

body:
### Which jobs are failing?

All serial node e2e jobs that run the CPU Manager or Memory Manager suites:

- ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-containerd-resource-managers
- ci-node-crio-resource-managers
- ci-kubernetes-node-swap-ubuntu-serial
- ci-node-crio-swap-serial
- ci-containerd-node-e2e-serial-ec2
- ci-containerd-node-arm64-e2e-serial-ec2
- presubmits pull-kubernetes-node-kubelet-serial-cpu-manager and pull-kubernetes-node-kubelet-serial-cpu-manager-kubetest2 (for PRs rebased on master)

### Which tests are failing?

The first failure lands in the CPU Manager and Memory Manager suites that disable the PodLevelResources feature gate. After that, every later [Serial] test in the run fails in its BeforeAll or BeforeEach step with:

```
[FAILED] Failed to get successful response from /configz: context deadline exceeded
In [BeforeAll] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e_node/kubeletconfig/kubeletconfig.go:186
```

Triage clusters (126 and 51 test names, same root cause, split only by ginkgo phase):

- https://storage.googleapis.com/k8s-triage/index.html?xjob=azure%7Ckops%7Ccrio%7Cautoscaling%7Ccapz%7Cci-kubernetes-verify%7Ccluster-api%7C-cos-%7Cfedora%7Cwindows%7Clocal-e2e%7Calpha-enabled-default%7Cci-gcp%7Cdocker-docker%7Cdocker-containerd%7Cci-minikube%7Ckvm-docker%7Cci-cloud-provider-gcp%7Cnpd-%7Cagentic-sandbox#fe142f553034eead5bbc
- https://storage.googleapis.com/k8s-triage/index.html?xjob=azure%7Ckops%7Ccrio%7Cautoscaling%7Ccapz%7Cci-kubernetes-verify%7Ccluster-api%7C-cos-%7Cfedora%7Cwindows%7Clocal-e2e%7Calpha-enabled-default%7Cci-gcp%7Cdocker-docker%7Cdocker-containerd%7Cci-minikube%7Ckvm-docker%7Cci-cloud-provider-gcp%7Cnpd-%7Cagentic-sandbox#2624ca6d5446537c85a5

### Since when has it been failing?

Since 2026-07-22. The last green build ran commit faba7e6a94df (merged 01:11 UTC). The first failing builds ran commit 39c618b5c30c (merged 04:09 UTC).

The clusters also contain builds from 2026-07-15 to 2026-07-17. That was the same failure mode, caused by #137150 and fixed by #140631. See the history section below.

### Reason for failure

The kubelet panics at startup while loading the config file the test wrote:

```
panic: failed to merge global and in-flight KubeletConfiguration while setting defaults,
error: PodLevelResourcesFixDefaulting is enabled, but depends on features that are
disabled: [PodLevelResources]
```

Mechanism:

1. #140514 (merged 2026-07-22 02:55 UTC) added the feature gate `PodLevelResourcesFixDefaulting`, enabled by default at Beta, with a declared dependency on `PodLevelResources` in `pkg/features/kube_features.go`.
2. `configureCPUManagerInKubelet` and `configureMemoryManagerInKubelet` in test/e2e_node set `PodLevelResources: false` in the kubelet config for some test variants, and do not disable the new gate.
3. `SetDefaults_KubeletConfiguration` (`pkg/kubelet/apis/config/v1beta1/defaults.go:72`) merges the config gates into a copy of the global gates with `SetFromMap`. The dependency check fails and the code panics.
4. systemd restarts the kubelet, it panics again on the same config, and /configz returns 503 through the API server proxy until the test times out. Every later Serial test in the run then fails the same way.

Evidence: [prow build](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-containerd-resource-managers/2079792906901655552) and the [kubelet.log with the panic](https://storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-containerd-resource-managers/2079792906901655552/artifacts/n2d-standard-32-cos-125-19216-532-25-913c732d/kubelet.log).

History: this is the second time this exact pattern broke these jobs. #137150 added `PodLevelResourcesFixKubeletQOSClass` (also enabled by default, also depending on PodLevelResources) and broke the same jobs from 2026-07-15 to 2026-07-17. #140631 fixed the tests by disabling that gate by name, so the fix does not cover the new gate. The presubmit that runs these suites (pull-kubernetes-node-kubelet-serial-cpu-manager) is optional and did not run on #140514.

### Anything else we need to know?

This is not only a CI problem. Any kubelet config file that sets `featureGates: {PodLevelResources: false}` now crashes the kubelet at startup, and disabling a Beta gate is a normal thing for a cluster admin to do.

Two possible fixes:

- Short term, repeat #140631 for the new gate: also set `PodLevelResourcesFixDefaulting: false` next to the existing lines in `test/e2e_node/cpu_manager_test.go` and `test/e2e_node/memory_manager_test.go` when the test disables PodLevelResources.
- Longer term, stop the kubelet from panicking here. Either the dependency check should treat a gate that is only enabled by default as off when its dependency is off, or config loading should return an error instead of panicking. Without that, every future gate that depends on PodLevelResources and ships enabled by default will break these jobs again.

### Which jobs are flaking?

Other configurations of the `SharedPodGroupResourceClaimTemplate` tests may be susceptible, but only the `1podgroup_1000pods` variant has flaked in CI so far.

https://storage.googleapis.com/k8s-triage/index.html?text=SharedPodGroupResourceClaimTemplate

### Since when has it been flaking?

Since the tests were added in #138775.

### Testgrid link

_No response_

### Reason for failure (if possible)

The scheduler's `DRAManager`'s `AssumeCache` of ResourceClaims is getting stuck with an old version of the shared ResourceClaim without an allocation after that allocation has already been persisted through the API server. I think the issue is how the DRA plugin is invoking the AssumeCache rather than something with the AssumeCache itself. I'm still digging in to determine the exact bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon

body:
i know that the project is growing like mad, it's still in its early days, and that scalling is always an issue but...
... regardeless of that i think that there are small steps that could taken to smooth things a lot, and avoid some to feel lost or alienated too fast. 
-  for releases and RCs ship with _real_ release notes, that point at least the new features, or feature/flag/behavioural changes
- make sure that anytime a new PR gets merged that changes/adds behaviour _shortly_ the docs get updated to match it, as right now there are too much 'assymetry' in the docs as it's very, very hard, (without ending to have to dig in to the source too many times)  to know which specific rev they are targeting/refering to. (heck - i suspect that even the googlebot could get trained to flag/open issues for a good chunck of that ...) 
- as a stop gap it _may_ make sense to, also, add some sort of 'tag' field / header to all docs/examples stating explicitly which version they are last know to work with (we already have that in https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/kubernetes/tree/master/docs/getting-started-guides/README.md but i would go further and embed that in _every_ doc/examples page/file (as often one lands on them via Google, the Search Engine))

imho gradually implementing those small steps would help a lot a lot of people :smile:

title: NodeController should only compare timestamps it generated locally

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

milestone.title: v1.0
milestone.description: Issues that need to be resolved for v1.0 of Kubernetes.

body:
As some folks pointed out in the discussion for #5399, NodeController (in the mode where kubelet updates NodeStatus rather than NodeController probing kubelet health) is currently detecting node timeout based on comparing a timestamp written by kubelet (LastProbeTime in NodeReady condition in NodeStatus) vs. NodeController's own local clock. This doesn't work in the presence of clock skew. #6159 has been filed to address the clock skew issue more generally, but we can (and should) fix this specific problem in NodeController so that it is robust to clock skew.

The proposal is as follows: NodeController should maintain a map from node to timestamp, where timestamp is the last clock time on the NodeController when the NodeController saw the given node update its NodeStatus. For example, this expression (from MonitorNodeStatus())

```
nc.now().After(lastReadyCondition.LastProbeTime.Add(gracePeriod)) 
```

would use the value from the map rather than lastReadyCondition.LastProbeTime. (There are two more similar comparisons at the bottom of MonitorNodeStatus(), where we delete pods, that also need to change.) Of course we also have to add code to keep this map up-to-date as NodeController sees changes to NodeStatus.

Whenever a node is created (including when an existing node is re-added if master crashes and then comes back up), it is added to the map with a timestamp of whenever the node was added. Thus after startup, nodes will not be transitioned to NodeReady==Unknown until the timeout has passed. It's safe to be a bit aggressive in transitioning nodes to Unknown, because the timeout for actually evicting pods due to NodeReady==Unknown is much longer than the timeout for marking a node as NodeRead==Unknown (5m vs. 8s or 30s).

title: Document API/system design principles and patterns

labels.name: kind/design
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to design.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: kind/documentation
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to documentation.

body:
Related to #5476, #2003, #1007, #5620, and other issues.

The PR creation rate and number of contributors are both growing. In order to scale the effort, we need to better document the patterns we want additions to the system and API to follow, so that we can better parallelize the design and review effort. I'm filing this issue to solicit important principles and patterns to document. I volunteer to create the actual document and/or presentation slides.

What do you think isn't sufficiently covered by existing design docs and/or isn't sufficiently discoverable? What principles/patterns do you find yourself explaining over and over again? What properties would you be unhappy to have violated/degraded/changed by new PRs? 

I'm thinking more about reasonably general issues rather than implementation-oriented invariants that apply to very specific/narrow parts of the code. 

Examples (some areas, some principles):
- Declarative APIs, desired state and current state
- Level-based operation: Functionality must be level-based, meaning the system must operate correctly given the desired state and the current/observed state, regardless of how many intermediate state updates may have been missed. Edge-based behavior must be just an optimization.
- Status must be 100% reconstructable by observation. Any history kept must be just an optimization and not required for correct operation.
- Phase, Reason, Message, Conditions, etc. vs. a single state machine with lots of states
- Composable, a la carte functionality
- Transparent, no glass to break
- More generally, [Eric Raymond's 17 UNIX rules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_philosophy#Eric_Raymond.E2.80.99s_17_Unix_Rules)
- Only the apiserver should communicate with etcd/store, and not other components (scheduler, kubelet, etc.).
- Compromising a single node shouldn't compromise the cluster (not that we've achieved that yet)
- Components should continue to do what they're told in the absence of new instructions.  
- Open world assumption: continually verify assumptions and gracefully adapt to external events and/or actors (example: we allow users to kill pods under control of a replication controller; it just replaces them)
- Don't assume a component's decisions will not be overridden or rejected, nor for the component to always understand why. For example, etcd may reject writes. Kubelet may reject pods. The scheduler may not be able to schedule pods.
- When to use labels vs. annotations vs. object references
- Watch vs. polling
- Bootstrapping-related principles

Let's brainstorm first, and argue and prioritize afterward.

@smarterclayton @derekwaynecarr @thockin @erictune @lavalamp

title: Potential pod scheduling bug

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
The cluster level e2e test is failing when previously it worked flawlessly. Nothing has changed with the test. The log below shows that the test fails because of a timeout that waits for a synthetic logging pod to enter to success or failure state i.e. the container should run and then terminate without being restarted. Here is the pod definition with `countTo=100`:

```
        _, err := c.Pods(ns).Create(&api.Pod{
            ObjectMeta: api.ObjectMeta{
                Name:   podName,
                Labels: map[string]string{"name": name},
            },
            Spec: api.PodSpec{
                Containers: []api.Container{
                    {
                        Name:    "synth-logger",
                        Image:   "ubuntu:14.04",
                        Command: []string{"bash", "-c", fmt.Sprintf("i=0; while ((i < %d)); do echo \"%d %s $i %s\"; i=$(($i+1)); done", countTo, i, taintName, podName)},
                    },
                },
                Host:          node.Name,
                RestartPolicy: api.RestartPolicyNever,
            },
        })

```

So this pod should run very briefly (enough to emit 100 log lines) and then terminate. However, it remains in the `Running` state.

I worry that some change has been introduced which has broken this test and perhaps exposes an underlying problem. This is perhaps the only test that uses pods that need to run to completion.

Full log for internal Google folks can be found by looking at Jenkins GCE run 3913.

body:
See issue #6079 as the roll-up for node upgrades.

**tl;dr:**
Update MIG template, then call a MIG rollingupdate. 

**More details:**
When upgrading nodes, an in-place upgrade must worry about leftover state on the boot disk, VM configuration like IP tables, and the idempotency of salt. Getting a fresh VM instead would remove these concerns and provide a clean state for a new node.

Furthermore, a versioned node spec (#4855) includes the tuple of (kubelet, kube-proxy, docker, kernel/OS). In the general case, changing docker or the kernel/OS means we have to stop the running pods. Once know we have to stop the pods, the simplest upgrade mechanism is to totally down the node and provision a new one.

Provisioning a new node is also a great backup to have for node repairs. To be clear, though, this issue is entirely separate from node repairs; once we have the capability to grow the cluster by adding new nodes, this mechanism, and other repair mechanisms, will build on top of that capability.

This was blocked by:
- #6087 nodes joining a running cluster
- #7912 (template-only metadata)

**References:**
- The most relevant discussion regarding the worries of complications with state while doing in-place upgrades is #3333.

body:
See issue #6079 as the roll-up for node upgrades, including the specification of the minimum requirement that this issue will fulfill, as well as improvements that will come after.

This is the worklist item for a minimum viable node upgrade mechanism for 1.0. 
### Plan:
- in-place: **yes**; restart the node
- provider: **GCE, then GKE**
### Outline:

Provisioning a new node is blocked on allowing new nodes to dynamically join a running cluster (#6087). In the mean time, the mechanism will do an in-place upgrade, blowing away as much as is necessary.
- For each node:
  1. Stop running binaries
  2. Get the node back to a "blank" state as much as possible. This involves trying to un-configure what salt did. Ideally, this looks like running salt in reverse.
  3. Grab the latest config from the metadata server (including the new startup script)
  4. Upgrade the kernel/OS
  5. Reboot the machine, which also runs the new startup script, which also runs salt
