title: Overlapping jobs are easy to create and hard to debug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

milestone.title: v1.2
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/wiki/Release-1.2

body:
A user had created a job with a matches-all selector while playing with jobs.  Then the user made a second job (details unimportant).  The second job would start a pod.  The job controller would notice a pod was created. It would try to match the created pod with a job.  It would match both.  It matched the first because that selector matched everything.  It matched the second because that created it.  In case of multiple matches, the job controller sorted the jobs by creation time and picked the oldest one.
But the oldest/first job saw the pod as not needed because it had parallelism 0 and/or was completed.  So it deleted the pod immediately.  This happened so fast that it looked like no pods were ever created.

This took me many hours to debug, in part because there were so many spurious error message and other red herrings.  

This needs to be easier to debug, or prevented entirely.

I don't think the details matter, but for reference the first job looked like this:

```
apiVersion: extensions/v1beta1
kind: Job
metadata:
  generateName: test-job-
spec:
  completions: 1
  parallelism: 0
  selector: {}
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - command:
        - ls
        image: busybox
        name: c
        resources: {}
        terminationMessagePath: /dev/termination-log
      restartPolicy: Never
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
```

milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
I thought I wrote this down somewhere, but apparently not. Mentioned in #20293.

We change kubectl behavior in order to improve UX. Uses in scripts depend on stable behavior, however. We should provide guidance about how to achieve that.

Off the top of my head:
- Use json or go templates and don't rely on default column output from get
- Specify --output-version, since templates are version-specific
- Specify generator versions if using generator-based commands like kubectl run
- Don't rely on context, preferences, or other implicit state

cc @kubernetes/kubectl @erictune

title: Reboot tests fail for kubernetes-e2e-gke-ci (reason: Nodes refuse to reboot)

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: kind/flake
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a flaky test.

body:
After all known issues which cause reboot test failure, we have a new incident: kubernetes-e2e-gke-ci/10456/

```
Reboot [Disruptive] each node by ordering clean reboot and ensure they function upon restart

/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/reboot.go:90 Jan 26 06:09:15.184: Test failed; at least one node failed to reboot in the time given.
```

I triaged the issue, and ruled out the follow causes which are tracked by separated issues:

1) version screw which causes kube-proxy image being updated during the test.
2) heapster / influxdb crashloop: kube-system pods are ready on all nodes
3) aufs issue, which cause node cannot come back
4) NodeController doesn't assign podcidr: Network configuration is done and ready
... 

It turns out the node doesn't reboot at all, and always at Ready state:

```
06:07:13 Jan 26 06:07:13.328: INFO: Calling nohup sh -c 'sleep 10 && sudo reboot' >/dev/null 2>&1 & on gke-jkns-gke-e2e-ci-be0af821-node-q9ys
06:07:13 Jan 26 06:07:13.376: INFO: Waiting up to 2m0s for node gke-jkns-gke-e2e-ci-be0af821-node-q9ys condition Ready to be false
...
06:07:13 Jan 26 06:07:13.930: INFO: Condition Ready of node gke-jkns-gke-e2e-ci-be0af821-node-q9ys is true instead of false. Reason: KubeletReady, message: kubelet is posting ready status
...
06:09:15 Jan 26 06:09:15.184: INFO: Node gke-jkns-gke-e2e-ci-be0af821-node-q9ys didn't reach desired Ready condition status (false) within 2m0s
06:09:15 Jan 26 06:09:15.184: INFO: Node gke-jkns-gke-e2e-ci-be0af821-node-q9ys failed reboot test.
```

title: mitigate slowness of Go 1.5 builds

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

body:
Per https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/19985#issuecomment-174053620 (and the [Go 1.5 release doc](https://golang.org/doc/go1.5#performance)) build performance is expected to be at least twice as slow compared to 1.4:

> Builds in Go 1.5 will be slower by a factor of about two. The automatic translation of the compiler and linker from C to Go resulted in unidiomatic Go code that performs poorly compared to well-written Go. Analysis tools and refactoring helped to improve the code, but much remains to be done. Further profiling and optimization will continue in Go 1.6 and future releases.

We started seeing some slowdown in PR builds when we started using Go 1.5 for unit/integration tests in December, but moving all builds to Go 1.5 last week have pushed things off a cliff.

I'm trying to mitigate some of the problem by bringing up additional Jenkins slaves and thinning out the number of executors on each slave (currently trying a maximum of 2 e2e and 2 unit/integration), but we maybe need to see if there are other places we can optimize (e.g. if we are unnecessarily building things, or building them multiple times).

Maybe there are also some knobs we can tune, so at least the builds are a little more isolated from each other?

@kubernetes/goog-testing @david-mcmahon

title: Collect logs of failed containers in kube-system namespace

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: kind/flake
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a flaky test.

body:
We are running heapster, dns server, kube-proxy etc. in kube-system namespace. Some e2e tests try to make sure all those kube-system pods are at ready state before firing the real tests, others just simply ingore them. But both cases might cause e2e flakiness when some of those kube-system containers are in crashloop, for example, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/19986#issuecomment-174089670 for heapster crashloop, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/19189#issuecomment-173419306 for influxdb crashloop, etc. When such cases happen, the developer doesn't have much information on why since the nodes might be teared down. 

We should watch those kube-system pods, and onContainerFailure, we should collect the related logs. One simple way is using kubectl logs <Pod> <Container> --previous

cc/ @kubernetes/goog-node @kubernetes/goog-testing

title: Make it easier for users to understand the reason for scheduling decisions and pending pods

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

body:
I was debating whether to file separate issues, but they're similar enough that one issue is probably better.

(1) Make it easier for users to understand the reason for scheduling decisions. For example, when a pod is scheduled, attach an annotation to it with something like this (suggested by @brendandburns )

```
Node-1: Priority =  1234 [1000 (zonal spreading) + 200 (machine spreading) + 30 (balanced resources) + 4 (image affinity)]
Node-2: Priority =  1014 [ ... ]
Node-3: Failed predicate XXX
...
Node-N: ...
```

Also possibly add a kubectl porcelain command to easily fetch this information about a pod.

(2) Make it easier for users to understand the reason for pending pods. This is really the same as (1) except all of the nodes will be marked as "Failed predicate XXX" and the pod in question will be pending rather than running.

In both cases it is also useful to present some kind of summary -- it's not possible to extract a useful signal by reading thousands of lines of this information per pod, as you'd have in a large cluster. There are some fairly obvious ways to summarize the information, but I don't want to stifle anyone's creativity by suggesting anything specific here. :)

title: Nodecontroller reassigns CIDR of first node on restart

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: kind/flake
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a flaky test.

body:
If the node controller ever restarts (like we do periodically in the daemon restart test, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/19023) it will reassign the CIDR of the first node. This can cause all sorts of problems like docker and container restart, pod phase changing etc. 

This code seems to be at fault:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/node/nodecontroller.go#L545

I feel like I'm missing some context here, which is why I haven't uploaded a pr. 
We don't generate available cidrs before checking that the first node is in the set (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/node/nodecontroller.go#L550). But then break out of the loop to generate cidrs a little later, saving the other nodes (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/node/nodecontroller.go#L568). 

Do we only need to generate available cidrs once on startup? that sounds like the sensible thing unless there's a GKE subnet requirement I'm missing.
@kubernetes/goog-control-plane @cjcullen

title: kubectl logs -l

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/cli
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG CLI.

body:
When I run a job, I want to check on the progress being made by the pods.   Likewise with an RC (either directly created or via `kubectl run`.

For listing the pods, I use the `-l` option, like this:

``` console
kubectl run foo --image bar -- /bin/blorp
kubectl get pods -l run=myrunname
```

But, usually the next thing I want to do is check logs.
I want to be able to do this:

```
kubectl logs -l run=myrunname
```

That doesn't work.  This is a request to implement it.

Something like this:
1. when -l option passed to `logs`, get a list of matching pods
2. for each pod name, get its logs.
3. print some kind of separator between logs from multiple pods.

title: kube-up scripts should not assume that all nodes have to be ready.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

milestone.title: v1.2-candidate
milestone.description: Things to consider for next minor release.

body:
Currently even if one Node is NotReady startup scripts fail. We should drop this requirement as we're allowing bigger clusters now. In big clusters few Nodes may fail to register in time (or at all), as e.g. virtual machine startup may fail (various cloud providers have different SLO's on machine startup success rates).

We should decide on percentage, smaller than 100, of machines that are requires for us to say that cluster startup were successful and update startup scripts. We also need to decide on what to do with fail machines - how do we tell user that some of them are not working and how can we help him/her with returning them to the provider.

Ref. #18969

title: Add priority function for NodeNotReady count to probabalistically quarantine flapping nodes safely

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: lifecycle/rotten
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

body:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/19118#issuecomment-172102534 refers.

I think that we should potentially have a mechanism in place for quarantining nodes that fail often/repeatedly. We will of course need to be careful of "poisoned pods" which, when launched on a node, cause it to fail often and get quarantined. If the poison pod then gets rescheduled to another node in the cluster, eventually all nodes could become quarantined. That would be very bad. But repeated hardware or system problems on a node should ultimately cause pods not to scheduled there, somehow, safely.

A good approach might be to use a basic [priority function](kubernetes/docs/devel/scheduler.md). For example, keep a sliding window not ready count per node (how many times a node has gone not ready in a given time window), and add a priority function to put nodes with high not ready counts at the bottom of the list when selecting nodes. That works around the poisoned pod problem outlined above, as we wouldn't actually lose real capacity by hard quarantining nodes. Only probabalistically avoid scheduling onto more flaky nodes. I think that's both simple and effective. Unless @mml or @davidopp have better ideas, I think that we should add this feature to the backlog.

body:
the public API documentation on kubernetes.io is very challenging to understand compared with projects like Docker, OpenStack.

The first and most challenging issue is that all of the API operations
are listed on one massive page, there isn't any grouping or index. I
have to use the browser find to search within the page and guess what
I'm looking for.

The second issue is that the docs are automatically generated so a lot
of the descriptions are not helpful, for example "proxy PUT requests
to Pod" : PUT /api/v1/proxy/namespaces/{namespace}/pods/{name} - I
have no idea what this does or what it is supposed to do.

Third issue is that the models 'required' for each of the fields are
not entirely correct. I was trying to create a pod. The docs say :
http://kubernetes.io/v1.1/docs/api-reference/v1/definitions.html#_v1_pod
that a pod spec is required, but none of the fields are required.
The API returns and gives an error saying fields are missing. I had to
use trial and error to discover which fields are required at a minimum
(turns out, metadata.name, containers[0].name and
containers[0].image).

@caesarxuchao
@brendandburns
@bgrant0607

title: BUG: Leaking go routines in kubelet

body:
In testing cpu performance as part of #19341 , I uncovered leaking go routines from within cadvisor on the kubelet.  

---

Stack 1:  Worst case
fedora 23 
tip of master 
golang 1.5.2 
etcd 2.2.1 
docker 1.9.1 

```
$ sudo ./hack/local-up-cluster.sh 
$ submit single pause with replica of 1
<measure pprof goroutine data on kubelet as the initial control>
```

wait till running

```
$ kubectl scale --replicas=50 rc/wide-pause
<wait till kubelets starts pods> 
$ kubectl scale --replicas=1 rc/wide-pause
<wait till kubelets starts terminating pods> 
$  kubectl scale --replicas=100 rc/wide-pause
<notice overlap, total pod count over 100> 
```

The system becomes remarkably slow and takes > 20 minutes to fill! repros in other condition, see below.

```
$ kubectl scale --replicas=1 rc/wide-pause
<measure pprof goroutine again and check for changes, and repeat experiment> 
```

recorded iteration1 (with only 1 pod running): 
336 @ (*realFsHandler).trackUsage+0x482 /home/tsclair/work/spaces/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/Godeps/_workspace/src/github.com/google/cadvisor/container/docker/fsHandler.go:82

recorded iteration2 (with only 1 pod running): 
528 @ github.com/google/cadvisor/container/docker.(*realFsHandler).trackUsage+0x482 /home/tsclair/work/spaces/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/Godeps/_workspace/src/github.com/google/cadvisor/container/docker/fsHandler.go:82

**LEAK** 

---

I can reproduce a much smaller leak using a production EL stack

Stack 2: 
rhel7.2
tip of master 
golang 1.4.2 
etcd 2.1.1 
docker 1.9.1 

same procedure: 
iteration1: 
 4 @ github.com/google/cadvisor/container/docker.(*realFsHandler).trackUsage+0x3ff  /home/cloud-user/kubernetes/Godeps/_workspace/src/github.com/google/cadvisor/container/docker/fsHandler.go:82

iteration2:
10 @ github.com/google/cadvisor/container/docker.(*realFsHandler).trackUsage+0x3ff  /home/cloud-user/kubernetes/Godeps/_workspace/src/github.com/google/cadvisor/container/docker/fsHandler.go:82

iteration3:
14 @ github.com/google/cadvisor/container/docker.(*realFsHandler).trackUsage+0x3ff  /home/cloud-user/kubernetes/Godeps/_workspace/src/github.com/google/cadvisor/container/docker/fsHandler.go:82

---

I'm not entirely certain why the fedora case is so much worse.  Either golang 1.5, or possibly some changes in systemd/cgroups which is causing cadvisor to loose it.

/cc @kubernetes/sig-node @mattf @jeremyeder @jimmidyson

body:
Just a small papercut: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9fda7f181299e49dd5f28405952ee76821eab74c/pkg/kubectl/rolling_updater.go#L408

``` go
return nil, false, fmt.Errorf("Invalid controller spec for %s; required: > 0 replicas, actual: %d\n", controller.Name, controller.Spec)
```

The last argument should be `controller.Spec.Replicas` to match the format verb `%d`. I would do a PR, but getting the corporate CLA signed is much too time-consuming, compared to the size of this issue.

title: DamonSet pods should not evict when node is NotReady

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

body:
I have a situation where my nodes go between `NodeNotReady` and `NodeReady` status due to a diff issue that's opened and being discusses.  The problem seems to be that as part of the `SyncLoop` updates the DS nodes get killed every single time going between those statuses.

Perhaps a slower determination should be used for DS just like it is for normal RC controlled Pods before marking the pods for deletion.

Cloud: `AWS` OS: `Ubuntu 14.04.03 LTS` Kubernetes `v1.1.3`

body:
kubectl fails to create deployment resource and emits the following:
`error validating "/examples/extensions/deployment.yaml": error validating data: couldn't find type: v1beta1.Deployment; if you choose to ignore these errors, turn validation off with --validate=false`

I guess that is because deployment is disabled by default.

I could be wrong, but I think this used to work before. Not sure if we changed some validation code recently.

Steps I did:
`
 RUNTIME_CONFIG=extensions/v1beta1/deployments=true ./hack/local-up-cluster.sh
./cluster/kubectl.sh create -f examples/extensions/deployment.yaml
`

cc @kubernetes/sig-api-machinery @kubernetes/goog-csi @janetkuo

I've run this repeatedly, and all I can tell so far is that it's flaky. ```

We should investigate if/how to do this for all of our tests, and perhaps for all invocations of `gcloud`.

title: BufferQueueLimitError in the fluentd container of the master

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

body:
I have a cluster in GCE. `Major:"1", Minor:"2+", GitVersion:"v1.2.0-alpha.3"`. I have enabled logging to GCP. Updated from a previous 1.1 version in November.

Yesterday the fluentd container of the master started emitting these errors twice per second approximately:

```
[warn]: emit transaction failed: error_class=Fluent::BufferQueueLimitError error="queue size exceeds limit" tag="fluent.warn"
[warn]: emit transaction failed: error_class=Fluent::BufferQueueLimitError error="queue size exceeds limit" tag="fluent.warn"
[warn]: emit transaction failed: error_class=Fluent::BufferQueueLimitError error="queue size exceeds limit" tag="kubelet"
[warn]: suppressed same stacktrace
```

It kept that way until I manually restarted the Docker container today. It didn't send any logs to the console in the meantime.

Some logged errors had more details:

```
[error]: failed to emit fluentd's log event tag="fluent.warn" event={"error_class"=>"Fluent::BufferQueueLimitError", "error"=>"queue size exceeds limit", "tag"=>"kubelet", "message"=>"emit transaction failed: error_class=Fluent::BufferQueueLimitError error=\"queue size exceeds limit\" tag=\"kubelet\""} error_class=Fluent::BufferQueueLimitError error=#<Fluent::BufferQueueLimitError: queue size exceeds limit>
```

Tags are always `kubelet`, `kube-apiserver` or `fluent.warn` in all errors I have seen.

There were some `Faraday::Timeout` and `Faraday::SSLError` some hours before, but no other sign of malfunction. I have the minions fluentd pods in a permanent `Terminating` status which expired in November, but the containers are still alive and working and I think it has been solved in this other issue: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/17929

If the real cause of this error can't be found at least the fluentd container of the master should be prepared to restart itself if it cannot work correctly anymore.

title: Remove validation of ResourceVersion in the Update() methods of typed clients

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
Some Update() methods in the typed clients checks if `len(ResourceVersion)==0` and if so invalidates the update. Such clients include that for endpoints, events, limit_ranges, namespaces, persistentvolumeclaim and persistentvolumes.

We should keep a thin client so we shouldn't do such validations at the client side. And our server has implemented the same validation: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/api/validation/validation.go#L321

The twist is that at server side, for some objects we `AllowUnconditionalUpdate`, e.g., https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/registry/namespace/strategy.go#L101. That means the server will default the ResourceVersion if the received object has an empty one, so the update will be valid. Hence, removing the client-side checks will change the behavior of some typed clients (e.g, client for namespace), they will no longer report an validation error for empty ResourdeVersion, which IMO is the correct behavior. Please let me know if you agree @kubernetes/goog-csi

title: Where to define common api machinery objects used by genericapiserver and client

labels.name: kind/design
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to design.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
There are lots of objects like RESTMapper, GroupMeta (almost all of latest.go and registered.go), etc that are currently defined in `pkg/api` and are used by both `pkg/genericapiserver` and `pkg/clients`.

I want to remove `pkg/genericapiserver`'s dependency on `pkg/api` and hence want to move those objects somewhere else.

I was thinking of moving them to genericapiserver pkg, but @caesarxuchao pointed out that client should not depend on genericapiserver.
I am now thinking of moving them to a new `pkg/apimachinery` package. Both genericapiserver and client can depend on it.
But then, when we move `pkg/genericapiserver` to a separate repository (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/2742), it will still depend on apimachinery package in kubernetes repo.

Thoughts?

@lavalamp @smarterclayton @caesarxuchao @kubernetes/goog-csi

title: Verify device is unmounted before detach via open O_EXCL

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

milestone.title: v1.4
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.4/Release-1.4.md

body:
@kubernetes/sig-storage  @thockin 
Kubernetes requires that volumes are unmounted in all mount namespaces before letting the system know that it is safe to detach. While the kernel provides a simple technique for ext4 (namely seeing if /sysy/fs/ext4 has any entry for the mounted filesystem) this is not a portable solution. 

Luckily there is a portable solution. We can use the O_EXCL flag. From the [open(2) man page](http://linux.die.net/man/2/open) 

```
O_EXCL
Ensure that this call creates the file: if this flag is specified in conjunction with
O_CREAT, and pathname already exists, then open() will fail.

When these two flags are specified, symbolic links are not followed: if pathname is a 
symbolic link, then open() fails regardless of where the symbolic link points to.

In general, the behavior of O_EXCL is undefined if it is used without O_CREAT. There is
one exception: on Linux 2.6 and later, O_EXCL can be used without O_CREAT if pathname
refers to a block device. If the block device is in use by the system (e.g., mounted),
open() fails with the error EBUSY. 
```

We can use this as a check before detaching to ensure the kernel does not have any unexpected mounts on the volume.

title: Handle systemd cgroups driver in docker runtime

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
Kubelet has a feature that lets users specify the parent cgroups hierarchy to use for docker containers - `--cgroup-root`. This flag is currently defaulted to "", which means that the runtime can choose to parent the containers under any cgroup of their choice.
#27204 is adding support for pod level cgroups and improving Quality Of Service. Kubelet will be managing cgroups as part of this feature. Kubelet requires runtimes to instruct pods to be nested under a specified cgroups hierarchy. Since cgroups naming format is not compatible between cgroups and systemd, this makes implementing #27204 harder.

Between kubelet and docker, there are four possible operating modes wrt. cgroups:
- Kubelet can use cgroupfs or systemd for managing cgroups
- Docker can use cgroupfs or systemd for managing cgroups

For a simple UX, we want kubelet to support all its features irrespective of how docker is configured. The default kubelet configuration should _just_ work with all supported configurations.
- To achieve that simple UX, we need kubelet to understand the cgroups driver that it has to use and that docker is using. 
- There is an existing proposal to add `--cgroups-driver` flag to kubelet to instruct kubelet to use cgroupfs or systemd. It is not clear what a sane default would be for this flag since recent versions of systemd prevent other processes from writing to cgroups.
- Kubelet and docker will have to use the same cgroups driver.
- As of docker versions >= v1.11, it is possible to introspect the cgroups driver that docker is using. On versions prior to that, how can kubelet detect the cgroups driver that docker is using?
  - One option is to use `--cgroup-driver` flag if it is not possible to infer the driver from docker. Given that the default docker configuration is to use `cgroupfs`, kubelet should also default to `cgroupfs`. If kubelet is asked to use systemd, then docker should also be configured to use systemd.
  - Another option is to declare that systemd cgroups driver is not supported for docker versions <= v1.10.x

The main reason for filing this issue is that #27204 requires kubelet to choose a default value for `--cgroup-root`. What default value should kubelet choose? 

Since #27204 is an opt-in feature, it is possible to require the user to specify a valid option for `--cgroup-root`, whenever they enable QOS Cgroups. 

To make this feature opt-out in the future, kubelet will have to choose a sane default though. To keep the UX simple, kubelet will have to ensure that its configuration matches that of docker. 
We can either have the user specify the cgroups driver to use or let Kubelet auto-detect it. I prefer the latter because it leads to one-less knob that the user has to understand.

The first milestone for #27204 does not involve supporting systemd. Our node e2e test framework does not support a heterogeneous testing environment. Since #27204 is the first feature that manages cgroups for docker containers, it is necessary to keep the node e2e testing environment homogeneous. 

As of now, excepting CoreOS, all other distros are using the cgroups driver with docker. To make progress on #27204, it is necessary to make the CoreOS image not use systemd. Once ConfigMaps support lands in kubelet #27980, it will be possible to support systemd cgroups driver for specific test images. cc @euank 

cc @derekwaynecarr @dchen1107 @dubstack 

Action items:
- [x] Convert CoreOS node e2e image to not use systemd
- [ ] Identify how to support docker versions <= v1.10.x (One option is to require the users to setup kubelet appropriately)
- [ ] Identify defaults for `--cgroup-root` flag for cgroupfs and systemd

title: Authorizer.Authorize() should return (bool, error)

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: sig/auth
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Auth.

body:
The [Authorizer interface](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/auth/authorizer/interfaces.go#L76) only returns an error today. This means that clients tend to treat any error as a "No" and return forbidden (e.g. our main [apiserver handler](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/apiserver/handlers.go#L484)).

Our authorizers have become more complicated (and have upstream dependencies in the case of the webhook). If the authorizer cannot make a decision, the apiserver should return a retryable error (probably a 503 or 504) rather than a 403 that the client will most likely not retry.

title: federation: non-federation DNS lookup can return federation CNAME

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/multicluster
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Multicluster.

body:
With the current KubeDNS code, it can happen that a pod requests `mysvc.somens` and resolve.conf adds `myns.svc.cluster.local` as a search path so that KubeDNS gets `mysvc.somns.myns.svc.cluster.local`.
If there is a federation with the name `myns`, isFederationQuery in KubeDNS will think this is a federation query and try to resolve `mysvc.somens.svc.cluster.local`. If there is a local service resolving to that DNS, then user will get that as expected (all is fine). But if there isnt, then KubeDNS will return `mysvc.somens.myns.svc.myzone.myregion.mydomain`. If there is no federation service with that name and in that namespace, then user will still get an NXDOMAIN as expected. But if there is, then user might be pointed to a service in another cluster, which user may or may not have wanted.

We can consider this a feature, if users want it or should fix it, if we consider it a bug.

Filing this to keep track.

body:
# **Description**

Two deployments were created both with selectors `app: logstash` added, the second deployment also had unique selectors added but because they both match on `app:logstash` and each had different replica amounts, the scheduler kept trying to satisfy an impossible situation.

If you have 2 Deployments with the same selector and different replication conditions the scheduler will keep creating and terminating pods. 
## **Expected**

The scheduler should throw an error on creation of a new deployment if the deployments have matching selectors.

title: Attach controller should not start detach until the node status has been updated

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/27567 introduced logic to make kubelet volume manager wait for attach detach controller to finish attach before it starts mount.

The controller should also not start a detach operation until the node status has been updated removing the volume from the list of attached volumes. Otherwise if a pod is rapidly created and deleted on the same node, it could result in a mount starting immediately before a detach starts.

Props to @bprashanth and his pet set tests for helping catch this.

title: Set --federations kube-dns flag when FEDERATION=true

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

body:
(Blocking #27739)

`kube-dns` needs to know what federation it belongs to, so we need to set `--federations=${FEDERATION_NAME}=${DNS_ZONE_NAME}` in `kube-up`.

Note that cloud DNS names domain names _with_ a trailing dot, but `kube-dns` needs (or at least wants: #27815) the name _without_ a trailing dot.  If that is in fact a restriction, there is the convenient shell hack `${DNS_ZONE_NAME%.}`, but in the end we should make the go code more flexible about the dots.

title: Build federation-controller-manager docker image with ca-certificates

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
Current the federation-controller-manager docker images does not include a root ca cert bundle which causes syncing with DNS providers to fail:

```
E0619 04:21:56.993123       1 endpoint_helper.go:88] Failed to sync service: Get https://www.googleapis.com/dns/v1/projects/hightowerlabs/managedZones?alt=json: x509: failed to load system roots and no roots provided, put back to service queue
```

To fix this issue I created my own container image using the following Dockerfile:

```
FROM ubuntu
MAINTAINER Kelsey Hightower <kelsey.hightower@gmail.com>
RUN apt-get update
RUN apt-get install -y ca-certificates
ADD federation-controller-manager /federation-controller-manager
ENTRYPOINT ["/federation-controller-manager"]
```

This resulted in a working image with a root cert bundle. Syncing with the GCE DNS provider now works.

title: find a cleaner alternative for salt configs on distros that do not support salt

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: sig/cluster-lifecycle
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Cluster Lifecycle.

labels.name: lifecycle/rotten
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

body:
Kubernetes maintains most of the node/master configuration as jinja templates at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/cluster/saltbase/salt. These templates are evaluated using saltstack on the nodes. This requires that the distro running on the nodes support python and jinja evaluators.
This is undesirable for several reasons:
1. the syntax is complex and difficult to maintain (example: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cluster/saltbase/salt/kube-apiserver/kube-apiserver.manifest)
2. node OS (like GCI and CoreOS) find it undesirable to support salt (mainly because of heavy dependency on several python modules - https://gitweb.gentoo.org/repo/gentoo.git/tree/app-admin/salt/salt-2015.8.8.ebuild#n29)

Current status:
1. CoreOS:
   (This is just my understanding, but coreos devs can comment here)
   CoreOS today has forked the templates and maintain their own manifests - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/cluster/gce/coreos/kube-manifests
   This has drawback that they don't support all k8s features and so cannot pass all tests.
2. GCI
   In order to be backwards compatible to old containervm and to support all tests, GCI adopted to resolve existing salt templates using 'sed' commands - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cluster/gce/gci/configure-helper.sh#L567.
   This is ugly and keeps breaking and no one wants to do this.
   (Please add if any other distros have any other concerns w.r.t. salt).

The purpose of this bug is two fold:
1. If not salt, what should be the other (hopefully simpler and cleaner) way to specify node configuration
2. Figure out how to migrate existing salt configurations to the new way

I had a brief meeting with @dchen1107 and @mikedanese last week about this. Options discussed in that meeting were:
1. Do the salt config evaluation locally (rather than on remote k8s node) -- this may not be possible in certain cases where or node specific info is needed (like ipaddress or hostname, etc).
2. Use some other template mechanism and evaluator ... preferably one with statically linked binary evaluator. This can be provided in a container  or as-is alongwith other kubernetes packages. And the host simply runs it during setup. https://github.com/google/jsonnet was suggested.

@kubernetes/goog-node @roberthbailey @dchen1107 @mikedanese @kubernetes/sig-cluster-lifecycle

title: cloudprovider/aws: EBS attachment fails: /dev/sdba is not a valid EBS device name (v1.3.0-beta.0)

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
I am having trouble on my AWS 1.3.0beta0 cluster to attach EBS with the controller-manager based attacher.

```
2016-06-16T10:50:46.081028537Z I0616 10:50:46.080908       1 reconciler.go:126] Started AttachVolume for volume "kubernetes.io/aws-ebs/aws://eu-west-1a/vol-9aa4532b" to node "ip-172-20-130-252.eu-west-1.compute.internal"
2016-06-16T10:50:46.594535809Z E0616 10:50:46.594230       1 attacher.go:78] Error attaching volume "aws://eu-west-1a/vol-9aa4532b": Error attaching EBS volume: InvalidParameterValue: Value (/dev/sdba) for parameter device is invalid. /dev/sdba is not a valid EBS device name.
2016-06-16T10:50:46.594571007Z  status code: 400, request id: 
2016-06-16T10:50:46.594578574Z E0616 10:50:46.594286       1 attacher_detacher.go:124] Attach operation for device "kubernetes.io/aws-ebs/aws://eu-west-1a/vol-9aa4532b" to node "ip-172-20-130-252.eu-west-1.compute.internal" failed with: Error attaching EBS volume: InvalidParameterValue: Value (/dev/sdba) for parameter device is invalid. /dev/sdba is not a valid EBS device name.
2016-06-16T10:50:46.594585498Z  status code: 400, request id: 
```

There problem is here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.3/pkg/cloudprovider/providers/aws/aws.go#L1302

This is failing as the kube-controller-manager is running in a pod via kubelet manifests. I think if you have a cluster with different instance types mixed you ran into trouble as well, as the device names will be either (sdX or xvdX) and the cluster will do it based on the state of the master (controller-manager).

My work around for now is to enable a host mount of `/dev` for the controller manager. But this need to be addressed at some point.

```
    volumeMounts:
    - mountPath: /dev
      name: dev-host
  volumes:
  - hostPath:
      path: /dev
    name: dev-host
```
- Is there any way we get the correct name from the AWS api?
- I think it's depending on the kernel version if it is xvdX or sdX. Am I right on this?
- A more ugly solution could be to annotate the node during registration, if it's has `xvdX` or `sdX` 
  device names

@justinsb maybe you can help me get a proper solution for this. I am happy to contribute a PR

title: Kubelet Volume Manager Reconciler should backoff on retries after mount failure

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
Some mount calls (like secret volumes, for example), make calls to the API server (to fetch, for example, the secret object). If the mount operation fails (because, maybe the secret object doesn't exist), the volume manager retries on its next iteration. To prevent hammering the API server, the volume manager should implement backoff on retires after mount failures.

Based on https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/26290

title: Kubelet Volume Manager Should Wait For Attach Detach Controller To Verify Attach

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
Currently the Kubelet Volume Manager determines whether a volume is attached by calling the `WaitForAttach()` method of the `volume.Attacher` interface.

The GCE volume plugin implements the `WaitForAttach()` method by looking at the `/dev/disk/by-id/google-*` file to show up. This is problematic because the existence of the disk file is not sufficient to ensure that the volume is ready to be mounted. This assumption leads to flakes where the volume manager tries to mount the volume before it is ready.

The AWS volume plugin implements the `WaitForAttach()` method by calling out to the AWS API to verify volume is attached. This is problematic because it requires node machines to have cloud provider credentials.

Both these issues can be fixed by having the kubelet volume manager wait on a signal from the attach/detach controller indicating the volume is attached before attempting to mount it. We already do this in the reverse direction with the attach/detach controller waiting for nodes to stop "using" (unmount) a volume before it proceeds with detach.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
Right now, to start federation control plane, users first need to build and push the images (for federation-apiserver, federation-controller-manager) into a repository that their cluster can access.

We can eliminate this step by providing public images.
We can generate and push these images as part of our general release process.

body:
I am currently trying `1.3.0-beta.0` on AWS. Everything works fine, but all worker kubelets are not schedulable, because of `NoRouteCreated`:

```
# kubectl get nodes -o yaml 
[...]
    - lastHeartbeatTime: null
      lastTransitionTime: 2016-06-14T08:01:20Z
      message: Node created without a route
      reason: NoRouteCreated
      status: "True"
      type: NetworkUnavailable
[...]
```

Node events:

```
  FirstSeen     LastSeen        Count   From                                                            SubobjectPath   Type            Reason                  Message
  ---------     --------        -----   ----                                                            -------------   --------        ------                  -------
  9m            9m              1       {kubelet ip-172-20-130-39.eu-west-1.compute.internal}                           Normal          Starting                Starting kubelet.
  9m            9m              1       {kubelet ip-172-20-130-39.eu-west-1.compute.internal}                           Normal          NodeHasSufficientDisk   Node ip-172-20-130-39.eu-west-1.compute.internal status is now: NodeHasSufficientDisk
  9m            9m              1       {kubelet ip-172-20-130-39.eu-west-1.compute.internal}                           Normal          NodeHasSufficientMemory Node ip-172-20-130-39.eu-west-1.compute.internal status is now: NodeHasSufficientMemory
  9m            9m              1       {controllermanager }                                                            Normal          RegisteredNode          Node ip-172-20-130-39.eu-west-1.compute.internal event: Registered Node ip-172-20-130-39.eu-west-1.compute.internal in NodeController
  8m            8m              1       {kubelet ip-172-20-130-39.eu-west-1.compute.internal}                           Normal          NodeReady               Node ip-172-20-130-39.eu-west-1.compute.internal status is now: NodeReady
  8m            8m              1       {kube-proxy ip-172-20-130-39.eu-west-1.compute.internal}                        Normal          Starting                Starting kube-proxy.

```

Though `kubectl get nodes` output makes you think, everything is ok:

```
core@ip-172-20-128-156 ~ $ kubectl get nodes
NAME                                           STATUS                     AGE
ip-172-20-128-156.eu-west-1.compute.internal   Ready,SchedulingDisabled   4m
ip-172-20-130-39.eu-west-1.compute.internal    Ready                      2m
ip-172-20-130-40.eu-west-1.compute.internal    Ready                      2m
```

No pod can be scheduled:

```
I0614 08:54:47.986353       1 event.go:216] Event(api.ObjectReference{Kind:"Pod", Namespace:"kube-system", Name:"kubernetes-dashboard-4126893489-lkymq", UID:"00b35fe4-320d-11e6-adba-0ae6bf41bde9", APIVersion:"v1", ResourceVersion:"136", FieldPath:""}): type: 'Warning' reason: 'FailedScheduling' no nodes available to schedule pods
```

I suspect it's maybe related to this new options for the controller-manager:

```
--allocate-node-cidrs[=false]: Should CIDRs for Pods be allocated and set on the cloud provider.
--configure-cloud-routes[=true]: Should CIDRs allocated by allocate-node-cidrs be configured on the cloud provider.
```

On my vagrant version of the same cluster (same coreos version, almost the same config), 1.3.0.beta0 works fine.

A few more bullet points about the setup:
- 1 master behind ELB
- 2 worker 
- All on coreos 1010.5
- cloud-provider="aws" on kubelets, apiserver, controller-manager
- flannel vxlan
- same config works fine on kubernetes version 1.2.4
- everything runs via kubelet (cf. https://coreos.com/kubernetes/docs/latest/kubernetes-on-aws.html)
- [ ] Better docs/elease notes about this NetworkUnavailable check
- [ ] Better `get nodes` output, a node should show up as NetworkUnavailable instead of ready
- [ ] Log debugging information to the events of the node 

How to debug further? I assume kubelet sets this status `"NoRouteCreated", Message:            "Node created without a route"`, but it's not overriden by the controller-manager later.

title: SELinux label on the mounted volume

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: lifecycle/rotten
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

body:
There is a field named `SELinuxOptions` in `PodSecurityContext`, however this is only used for the running process in containers.

For example, the following spec:

``` yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: ubuntu3
  labels:
    app: ubuntu
spec:
  containers:
  - image: ubuntu:14.04
    command:
    - sleep
    - "3600"
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    name: ubuntu
    volumeMounts:
    - name: log-dir
      mountPath: /var/log/ubuntu3
  volumes:
  - name: log-dir
    hostPath:
      path: /var/log/ubuntu3
  restartPolicy: Always
  securityContext:
    seLinuxOptions:
      user: system_u
      role: object_r
      type: svirt_sandbox_file_t
      level: s0:c100,c200
```

What I am hoping is that the files under `/var/log/ubuntu3` would have type `svirt_sandbox_file_t`, however it was set on the process, not the volumes.

``` console
# ps auxZ | grep sleep
system_u:object_r:svirt_sandbox_file_t:s0:c100,c200 root 8633 0.1  0.0 4348 636 ? Ss 10:12   0:00 sleep 3600
```

My question is: Is there a way to set selinux labels for the volumes(something like `-v ${hostpath}:${containerpath}:z` in docker)?

title: PVClaim deletion should be graceful wrt running pods

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: lifecycle/stale
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR has remained open with no activity and has become stale.

body:
The scheduler knows which pods are on which nodes. It figures out all volumes on a node by the sum of its pods.  It does this to enforce constraints in a cloud environment.

It is possible to delete a PVC while a pod is still running.  The pod will continue to function, the PV remains attached to a node.  

When the scheduler attempts to place new pods on the node, it looks up all its existing PVs and their backing PVCs , except the PVC has been deleted, an error is thrown, and the scheduler fails.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/plugin/pkg/scheduler/algorithm/predicates/predicates.go#L157

The user gets an ugly error message about a namespace they don't own. Their pod won't run and the error message is confusing.

title: Possible Bug: Garbage Collection Not Triggered

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

body:
## what

I’m struggling to trigger image garbage collection (GC) by the kubelet process by simulating disk usage. In short, I can’t get it to work and can’t figure out if it’s a bug or a misunderstanding.  
## expectations
- Upon disk usage crossing the 90% threshold (default setting for `image-gc-high-threshold`) the kubelet will output messages to stdout or stderr indicating that it's vacuuming images
- A reduction of disk space below the high-watermark of 90%
## related

One of our problems was probably as a result of using a symlinked docker-root (see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/17994). We’ve since deployed the kubelet with `—docker-root=/vol/docker` as well as explicitly passed the `—graph=/vol/docker` directory to the docker daemon.  Despite these changes images are not being gc'd.
## reproduction

To simulate being out of space, I’ve created a `tmpfile` that uses up 89% of free space. 

```
dd if=/dev/zero of=/vol/docker/tmpfile bs=1G count=75
```

(I should have used a smaller volume!)

Disk space is now at 89% utilization as reported by `df`

Then I’ve downloaded 11G of docker images with `docker pull` by iterating over every release of an internal project to take me over the line to 91% as reported by `df`.

From what I observe from `journalctl` is that the `kubelet` is not performing any GC and the `df` does not change. I’ve also tried restarting the kublet to no avail.
## kubernetes version

```
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"2", GitVersion:"v1.2.4", GitCommit:"3eed1e3be6848b877ff80a93da3785d9034d0a4f", GitTreeState:"clean"}
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"2", GitVersion:"v1.2.4", GitCommit:"3eed1e3be6848b877ff80a93da3785d9034d0a4f", GitTreeState:"clean"}
```

title: Downward API for resource specification should default to node capacity when limits are not set.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
As of now the downward API for resource specification defaults to `0` for `limits` when `limits` are not specified in the pod spec. This behavior is not ideal for applications. 
What does a limit of `0` mean? 
In reality, not having a limit translates to being limited by node capacity as of now, and node allocatable in the future once it is enforced. 
We should default to node capacity instead of setting `limit.memory` to `0` when `limits` are not set.
And for `limits.cpu` we should again default to node capacity and allocatable in the future.

title: Race condition in Informer

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: kind/flake
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a flaky test.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
### What's the issue?

Informer could end up in wrong state.
### Example?

I have been stress testing RC of 100 replicas. I kept deleting the pod and let RC recover it to 100. The program will do informer.store.List() to check if there are 100 pods. But at the end of day it returned more than 100 (e.g. 131), while listing directly from apiserver returned 100.
### Why?

Informer has a queue and a store (aka indexer) internally.
- The store relies on the queue to do blocking [pop()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0d3be6a316b39a71b62d45272d339f7fa9162165/pkg/controller/framework/controller.go#L127-L128) and and then [updates itself](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0d3be6a316b39a71b62d45272d339f7fa9162165/pkg/controller/framework/shared_informer.go#L200-L224) in [Process()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0d3be6a316b39a71b62d45272d339f7fa9162165/pkg/controller/framework/controller.go#L127-L128).
- The queue (delta fifo) is used to queue events from watcher. For [each operation in reflector](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0d3be6a316b39a71b62d45272d339f7fa9162165/pkg/client/cache/reflector.go#L384-L392), e.g. Delete, we will [enqueue an event to the queue](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0d3be6a316b39a71b62d45272d339f7fa9162165/pkg/client/cache/delta_fifo.go#L200).
- However, in DeltaFIFO.Delete(), it will [check the store](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0d3be6a316b39a71b62d45272d339f7fa9162165/pkg/client/cache/delta_fifo.go#L192-L198) first to see if it needs to send a delete event. **This logic is wrong because the queue and store are run concurrently. There could be an ADD event not processed by store yet thus queue won't enqueue DELETE event.**

title: kubernetes-e2e-gce-master-on-cvm has been broken since 5/31

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
We have a test suite called `kubernetes-e2e-gce-master-on-cvm` running to allow us to, in theory, switch back from GCI masters to Container VM masters at any point. 

We succeeded at http://kubekins.dls.corp.google.com/job/kubernetes-e2e-gce-master-on-cvm/lastStableBuild/ (c1c0567e37b699) and then failed at http://kubekins.dls.corp.google.com/job/kubernetes-e2e-gce-master-on-cvm/338 (ee412efcefc75b), and it's all consistently DNS related issues, so I'm pretty sure #26335 broke this suite entirely.

It's also somewhat blocking me from evaluating a new version of Container VM, but not really - I think we're safe to evaluate it on nodes only for now.

cc @roberthbailey @thockin

labels.description: Denotes an issue that needs help from a contributor. Must meet "help wanted" guidelines.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG CLI.

labels.name: lifecycle/rotten
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

body: From [stackoverflow question](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/37555281/create-kubernetes-pod-with-volume-using-kubectl-run/37621761), the user was adding `"containers"` to the wrong object. Rather than reporting an error, the mismatched fields were silently ignored.  More generally, any arbitrary fields added (`"foo": "bar",`) are silently ignored, making the config difficult to debug.

body:
I noticed that this week of kubernetes-soak-weekly-deploy-gce failed due to #23545

Build #104 (May 31, 2016 12:13:01 AM)

00:13:38 ERROR: gcloud crashed (error): [Errno 111] Connection refused

The issue is filed for test-infra improvement. No matter what cause for kubernetes-soak-weekly-deploy-gce, shouldn't we re-try? So that soaking test can be unblocked.

title: Unable to use EBS/GCE PV when AWS/GCE host is registered via another cloud provider

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: lifecycle/rotten
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

body:
Kubernetes 1.2.4

In Rancher we support Kubernetes as an orchestration framework, while Rancher acts as an infrastructure platform for various cloud providers (DO, AWS, GCE, etc). Rancher is registered as a cloud provider in Kubernetes, and acts as a proxy for other cloud provider's hosts. It was done to enable extra functionality provided by Rancher (overlay network as an example) in addition to functionality given by providers themselves.

Starting 1.2.4, we were unable to use Kubernetes Persistent volumes feature; the commit below disabled it for us:

```
commit c04108e90ca28e341af2bd72bcef6e09e7400763
Author: saadali <saadali@google.com>
Date:   Fri Apr 1 16:40:36 2016 -0700

    Ensure volume GetCloudProvider code uses cloud config
```

In our case, the provider in the code below is returned as a Rancher provider, not AWS cloud provider, and the error is raised.

```
cloudProvider := plugin.host.GetCloudProvider()
       awsCloudProvider, ok := cloudProvider.(*aws.AWSCloud)
       if !ok || awsCloudProvider == nil {
               return nil, fmt.Errorf("Failed to get AWS Cloud Provider. plugin.host.GetCloudProvider returned %v instead", cloudProvider)
        }
```

I wonder what is the recommended approach to unblock Persistent Volumes use for a use case like ours?

title: kube-addon-manager is using ~2CPUs

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

body:
It wakes up every 10 seconds and bursts the usage to 2CPUs when it available.

It's shouldn't cause any problems, as it has only 5 CPU shares, but it seems a lot for a process that monitors the status of few addons. I'm not sure how well it behaves when it's starved on CPU - it may be worth rewriting it to go (or anything other than bash really).

cc @wojtek-t @davidopp @mikedanese @luxas @thockin

title: Federation-e2e flake - federation-apiserver connection refused

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/multicluster
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Multicluster.

body:
The kubernetes-e2e-gce-federation jenkins jobs in consistently flaking with the following output.

```
â€¢ Failure [5.905 seconds]
[k8s.io] Federation apiserver [Feature:Federation]
/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/framework/framework.go:641
  should allow creation of cluster api objects [It]
  /go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/federation-apiserver.go:63

  creating cluster: Post https://146.148.36.68:443/apis/federation/v1alpha1/clusters: dial tcp 146.148.36.68:443: getsockopt: connection refused
  Expected error:
      <*url.Error | 0xc8209cc6f0>: {
          Op: "Post",
          URL: "https://146.148.36.68:443/apis/federation/v1alpha1/clusters",
          Err: {
              Op: "dial",
              Net: "tcp",
              Source: nil,
              Addr: {
                  IP: "\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\xff\xff\x92\x94$D",
                  Port: 443,
                  Zone: "",
              },
              Err: {
                  Syscall: "getsockopt",
                  Err: 0x6f,
              },
          },
      }
      Post https://146.148.36.68:443/apis/federation/v1alpha1/clusters: dial tcp 146.148.36.68:443: getsockopt: connection refused
  not to have occurred

  /go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/federation-apiserver.go:53
------------------------------
```

This is kubectl attempting to open a connection with the federation-apiserver via a loadbalancer service.

There are two possible underlying causes here, which are not mutually exclusive:
- federation-apiserver pod is not yet ready
- GCE loadbalancer has not finished initializing

I plan to remedy this by introducing some more "is it ready yet?" logic to `federated-up` procedure:
- wait until the federation-apiserver pod stays ready for 10 seconds. right now we only wait until it's running
- attempt to do `kubectl version` for another 30 seconds before allowing the e2e tests to start, to verify loadbalancer is initialized. right now we assume the loadbalancer is ready to serve traffic after the service ingress metadata becomes available. this is most likely a poor assumption

\cc @quinton-hoole @nikhiljindal @madhusudancs

body:

title: Scheduling of pods with RWO volumes

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen

body:
Since RWO volumes work only on a single host, wouldn't it be reasonable for the scheduler to schedule pods for a {RC,RS,D,etc.} that uses such a volume on the same node? Otherwise, pods that land on different nodes are essentially blocked. Deployments are the most affected since you can have a Deployment with just one pod and maxSurge=1 (which is actually the default currently) and with a RWO volume, it will block.

@kubernetes/sig-scheduling @kubernetes/deployment @kubernetes/sig-storage

title: e2e flake: tests are failing with "net/http: TLS handshake timeout" in large clusters

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scalability
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scalability.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
We are running a standard e2e suite that we are running in gce-e2e in large 2000-node clusters now.

And on every run, we have few random tests failing with "net/http: TLS handshake timeout" error.

Examples:

```

  /go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/pods.go:1100

  getting pod liveness-http
  Expected error:
      <*url.Error | 0xc820e55f20>: {
          Op: "Get",
          URL: "https://104.196.136.191/api/v1/namespaces/e2e-tests-pods-uvjef/pods/liveness-http",
          Err: {},
      }
      Get https://104.196.136.191/api/v1/namespaces/e2e-tests-pods-uvjef/pods/liveness-http: net/http: TLS handshake timeout
  not to have occurred

title: Build infrastructure: Eliminating flakes at the source.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

body:
So I ran a number of experiments locally trying to reproduce a number of test flakes in the registry.

When running 100's of iterations I had 0 failures. So I decided to try testing to see what happens when I do too many tests in parallel. Using a simple script:

```
#!/bin/sh

for i in {1..20}
do
    go test -timeout 120s k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/registry/generic/registry &
done
```

I can essentially peg my cpu, hit swap, and cause timeouts. In general, I think a lot of these flakes are due to running too many concurrent jobs. Ideally, we should use kubernetes to build kubernetes, monitor resource usage, and quarantine each build+test.  Our build and test mechanics are far to resource intensive and we should move to try and reduce the load as well. 

/cc @kubernetes/sig-testing

title: Allow auto-population of environment variables from ConfigMap

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/service-catalog
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Service Catalog.

body:
The current approach for populating environment variables from ConfigMaps ends up pretty verbose. With the following ConfigMap:

```
apiVersion: v1
data:
  space-ships: 1
  ship-type: battle-cruiser
  weapon: laser-cannon
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: space-config
```

I have to manually expose each variable separately:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: space-simulator
spec:
  containers:
  - name: space-simulator
    image: foo/space-simulator
    env:
    - name: SPACE_SHIPS
      valueFrom:
        configMapKeyRef:
          name: space-config
          key: space-ships
    - name: SHIP_TYPE
      valueFrom:
        configMapKeyRef:
          name: space-config
          key: ship-type
    - name: WEAPON
      valueFrom:
        configMapKeyRef:
          name: space-configs
          key: weapon
```

This seems unnecessary and error-prone if all I want to express is that the pod should pull all the data from the ConfigMap and populate environment variables from them.

It would be nice if this could be done in more concise manner, perhaps by introducing an `envFrom` field. For example:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: space-simulator
spec:
  containers:
  - name: space-simulator
    image: foo/space-simulator
  - envFrom:
      configMap: space-config
```

The idea being that `envFrom` could support other ways of auto-population, e.g. secrets.

title: Master PD file location inconsistent between Debian & GCI

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
The location of apiserver auth certs and keys and the kube-apiserver SSH keys are inconsistent between Debian and GCI.  This means that master upgrades from Debian to GCI are broken.

In Debian, Salt puts these files in `master-pd/srv/kubernetes` (via `/srv/salt-overlay/salt/kube-apiserver/basic_auth.csv` and `/srv/kubernetes/basic_auth.csv`, see [configure-vm.sh](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1ef19062096c4fcf8ddeaf3a46731d9f262a0c04/cluster/gce/configure-vm.sh) and [init.sls](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1ef19062096c4fcf8ddeaf3a46731d9f262a0c04/cluster/saltbase/salt/kube-apiserver/init.sls)), whereas GCI expects it in `master-pd/etc/srv/kubernetes` (see [configure-helper.sh](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1ef19062096c4fcf8ddeaf3a46731d9f262a0c04/cluster/gce/gci/configure-helper.sh), originally introduced in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/20463).

title: OS_DISTRIBUTION should be split into two vars

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
This came up while I was working on #25977, for which I am adding support to run clusters with the master on GCI and nodes on Debian. I find it difficult to do within current framework that uses a single env var, `OS_DISTRIBUTION`, to select the OS distro for both the master and nodes. Different distros tend to have different configs, ranging from instance metadata to initialization instructions, e.g., Debian uses salt but GCI uses systemd.

If we are going to support hybrid clusters for a while, I think we should have two vars as opposed to one, maybe something like `MASTER_OS_DISTRIBUTION` and `NODE_OS_DISTRIBUTION`, so that we could avoid hacks like [this](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cluster/gce/util.sh#L732).

title: On large cluster, routecontroller takes forever to program routes due to rate limit errors / reconcile

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

body:
On a large cluster, the routecontroller basically makes O(n) `Routes.Insert` requests all at once, and most of them error out with "Rate Limit Exceeded". We then wait for operations to complete on the ones that _did_ stick, and damn the rest, they'll be caught next reconcile (which is a _while_).

In fact, in some cases it appears we're spamming hard enough to get rate limited by the upper-level API DOS protections and seeing something akin to https://github.com/golang/go/issues/14627, e.g.:

```
E0523 22:00:21.772924      22 routecontroller.go:101] Could not create route 5a40e42e-212a-11e6-9ac7-42010af00002 10.9.170.0/
24 for node gke-jenkins-e2e-default-pool-1-b4d62c45-58a8 after 238.128126ms: Get https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projec
ts/kubernetes-scale/zones/us-east1-a/instances/gke-jenkins-e2e-default-pool-1-b4d62c45-58a8?alt=json: http2: no cached connec
tion was available
```

We can do better than this!

title: Racy controller from framework.NewInformer?

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
When I stress-test PersistentVolume controller I sometimes get (correct) "PersistentVolumeClaim deleted" event followed by (wrong) "PersistentVolumeClaim added". This happens very rarely (<0.01%) when I delete a PersistentVolumeClaim and the controller is under heavy load.

I use `framework.NewInformer` ([link](https://github.com/jsafrane/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/framework/controller.go#L213) ) like everybody else. Reading its code, what happens when the controller is processing 'PVC deleted' event at line [251](https://github.com/jsafrane/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/framework/controller.go#L251), i.e just **before** `Delete()` is called and at the same time periodic sync starts? The PVC that is being deleted is still in the cache and a 'PVC Sync' will be added into `Queue` and my controller gets  `OnDelete()` callback followed by `OnAdd()`.

My PersistentVolume controller then sees an old claim and tries to do stuff with it and sometimes it updates the claim in etcd. So the claim gets 'resurrected' in etcd even though user deleted it.

It is possible that my controller does something terribly wrong - I checked it twice, but it's pretty complicated piece of code. I am 100% sure that `OnAdd()` is called as reaction to `cache.Sync` event, I did a debug log in `Process` function of Informer.

labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to cleaning up code, process, or technical debt.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
Forked from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/26001

To make debian-based node compatible with docker 1.11.X, I updated both /proc/sys/kernel/keys/root_maxkey and /proc/sys/kernel/keys/root_maxbytes. Also other kubernetes components do the similar thing. For example, kube_proxy: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dae5ac482861382e18b1e7b2943b1b7f333c6a2a/cmd/kube-proxy/app/conntrack.go#L42

We should clean up those configurations into one common place.

title: pre-bound claim remains Pending

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
This is based on the recently merged PR #24331:

```
v1.3.0-alpha.4.129
```

I created 2 PVs (pv1,pv2) followed by 2 pvcs (claim1,claim2) where claim2 is pre-bound to pv2 via _volumeName_:

```
NAME      CAPACITY   ACCESSMODES   STATUS      CLAIM                REASON    AGE
nfs-pv1   1Gi        RWO           Available                                  1m
nfs-pv2   1Gi        RWO           Bound       default/nfs-claim1             1m

NAME         STATUS    VOLUME    CAPACITY   ACCESSMODES   AGE
nfs-claim1   Bound     nfs-pv2   0                        1m
nfs-claim2   Pending   nfs-pv2   0                        1m     <--------------- 
```

claim1 finds pv2 before claim2 finds pv2 (which it is pre-bound to). This is ok due to timing.
If I change the order and create pv2,pv1 followed by claim2,claim1 then I again see claim2 in the Pending phase:

```
NAME      CAPACITY   ACCESSMODES   STATUS    CLAIM                REASON    AGE
nfs-pv1   1Gi        RWO           Bound     default/nfs-claim1             3s
nfs-pv2   1Gi        RWO           Bound     default/nfs-claim2             4s

NAME         STATUS    VOLUME    CAPACITY   ACCESSMODES   AGE
nfs-claim1   Bound     nfs-pv1   0                        3s
nfs-claim2   Pending   nfs-pv2   0                        3s    <------------------- 
```

This time **all** pvs are Bound but claim2 remains Pending even though pv2 shows it as being bound to.
If repeat the above test (order: pv2,pv1,claim2,claim1) in a loop (deleting the pvs and claims each iteration) I see a Pending claim2 about 50% of the time. The other times all objects are Bound.

Here are the spec files for pv2 and claim2:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: nfs-pv2
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 1Gi
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  nfs:
    path: /opt/nfs  #export dir
    server: 192.168.122.73
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: nfs-claim2
spec:
  volumeName: nfs-pv2                   # <----------------------- pre-bound
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
```

title: kubelet container manager cgroup detection should error if cpu and memory differ

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
`kubelet` container manager setup node routine should ensure that cpu and memory cgroups for container runtime are of the same value, and warn if they are equal to `/`.

For background, on systemd environments, the default unit file for `docker` has CPU and Memory accounting not enabled, so the /proc/.../cgroup file reports `/` as cpu cgroup.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/25907#issuecomment-220449234

title: density tests fail with "System error: The minimum allowed cpu-shares is 1024"

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
I have a 10-node kubernetes 1.2 cluster running on AWS m3.medium instances with CoreOS 1010.1.0. When I run the kubernetes density e2e tests, containers fail to start with the error "System error: The minimum allowed cpu-shares is 1024". I have not seen this error when using AWS m3.large instances. According to the docker team, this issue is fixed in docker 1.11. Therefore we are asking CoreOS to back port the fix or support docker 1.11. Note that this failure is reliably reproducible.

A link to the ticket docker ticket:

https://github.com/docker/docker/issues/22818

An example of the error:
