title: Using annotations for new API features creates the potential for security lapses

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: kind/cleanup
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to cleaning up code, process, or technical debt.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
Our current API strategy is to add annotations for new features.  These annotations are expected to overlay on top of the existing API fields, and alter system behavior in other components.  Our primary reason for annotations today:
1. They are unstructured and can be preserved in etcd even after the feature is graduated from alpha.
2. They can contain arbitrarily complex values (like init containers) or simple fields (like hostname for pods)

Annotations come with a set of issues:
1. Alpha annotations are not discoverable and do not show up in our docs - users don't know how to use the features, and we get no automatic benefits from swagger or other tools
   1. No way to communicate lifecycle via `kubectl explain` to end users
2. Developers who implement those annotations must merge the value in to the internal or external types at various points in the lifecycle - conversion, validation, in client libraries, and in nested utilities.
   1. Client utilities that receive a partial struct (like `api.PodSpec`) must also receive a list of annotations that alter that pod spec (for things like init containers) and potentially merge those
   2. When an alpha feature is graduated, we typically change the implementation of that feature significantly as well (moving from annotation to field) which causes extra churn in the implementation, and the potential for new bugs
3. Some alpha features may be missed by a developer unfamiliar with the annotation - without any of the normal tools to introspect code (code completion, reflective tests on structs) it is more likely that the impact of an annotation is missed when adding new code.
4. The security implications of an annotation are harder to convey than a field, and code that allows annotation mutation but _not_ field annotation can be exposed to malicious authors accidentally (bind, status, and a few other sub resources that protect spec can be abused to mutate init containers, for example).
5. A malicious user can introduce an annotation for an upcoming alpha feature on a cluster before the feature is introduced, which means that prior to enabling an alpha feature a cluster admin has to sweep all possible objects to ensure no dangerous annotations are set.
   
   This occurred for init containers - podsecuritypolicy is applied at creation time, but because init containers are represented as annotations a malicious user can set an init container annotation before Kube 1.3 is rolled out, and as soon as the cluster is upgraded that container would be executed.  This means that admins have to run a pre-upgrade migration to purge any dangerous / out of policy annotations.

For these reasons, I believe we should not be using annotations for alpha level fields internally, and probably not externally.
## Alternative

Instead, I believe we should represent alpha level fields in our Go structs and clearly denote them as alpha (perhaps with an named prefix).  Once the feature is out of alpha, we would leave the alpha level field in the external struct for at least 1 major version to allow upgraders to use that field.  We would then drop the alpha field, which would clean the database of that value.  Internal code would simply rename the field, and ignore the external field.

Alpha level fields would be denoted by struct tags that allowed them to show up in swagger.  Once we dropped support for the field, swagger would no longer show them.  We would have to have a "drop by default" rule in place for swagger validations on fields that are no longer recognized for old alpha fields that aren't supported, but that's what we want for alpha.

E.g.:

Kube 1.2:

```
pod:
  spec:
    alphaInitContainers:  # silently dropped by the storage layer
    - name: init-1
```

Kube 1.3:

```
pod:
  spec:
    alphaInitContainers: # visible in swagger
    - name: init-1
       ...

$ kubectl explain pod.spec.alphaInitContainers
This field allows you to provide specify "init containers" - run before other containers.
...
Feature is alpha and may change without notice.
```

Kube 1.4:

```
pod:
  spec:
    alphaInitContainers: # ignored, but visible in swagger.  kubectl validate could flag this as unsupported
    - name: init-1
    initContainers:
    - name: init-1

$ kubectl explain pod.spec.alphaInitContainers
This field has been removed - use pod.spec.initContainers
```

Kube 1.5

```
pod:
  spec:
    alphaInitContainers: # fails kubectl validate - alpha is no longer supported
                         # silently dropped from storage whenever a pod is updated
    initContainers:
    - name: init-1

$ kubectl explain pod.spec.alphaInitContainers
This field has been removed - use pod.spec.initContainers
```

title: Local storage handling in Nodes

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
As of today Kubelet can consume storage via multiple devices & partitions. 
[This proposal](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/docs/proposals/disk-accounting.md) on disk accounting lists some of the well understood storage configurations,
1. Root partition
2. Docker Images partition - primarily meant for device mapper storage driver

However there are various other means by which Kubelet can consume local storage. 
1. Volumes can exist in non-root partition `--root-dir`
2. Hostpath volumes can use any partition or device
3. `/var/log` could exist in non-root partition.
4. `/var/lib/docker` (docker root dir) can exist in a different partition.
There could be more options.

Why does kubelet care about storage configuration?
1. Kubelet provides storage accounting for volumes, pods and nodes.
2. Kubelet attempts to ensure that local storage doesn't get full and evicts pods if necessary to free up storage.
3. Kubelet in the future will support storage isolation and allow pods to express disk requests & limits.

To avoid complicating the kubelet, I have the following proposal.

Restrict Kubelet's non-volume storage usage to a single partition excepting image filesystem. Kubelet on bootup will verify that the above mentioned storage modalities are all landing up on the same partition. 
A typical use case for a user to customize storage is to provide additional storage for volumes or to work around a small root partition. 
If a user does not intend to use the root filesystem, then they are expected to make `/var/lib/docker`, `/var/log` and `--root-dir` to point to the same storage partition. 
Images can continue to be optionally in a separate partition. 

Alternate approaches include kubelet tracking individual devices and supporting accounting, evictions and isolation on all of them. This is very tedious.

Use cases of HostPath volumes include mapping in SSDs and other HDDs. Volumes interface can be expanded to provide access to local storage. Assuming that users will want to share storage devices, kubelet will have to track additional storage devices via volume plugin interface and let pods consume these additional storage devices via volumes.

Given that HostPath volumes can be shared, kubelet does not account for them. By expanding scope of volumes interface to all local storage devices, it will allow for accounting and isolation and avoid usage of HostPath volumes except for read-only use cases.
In the future, kubelet will have to expose these additional devices to the scheduler in-order to find the node that can fit a pod with `disk` requirements for containers and volumes.

There is still the problem of freeing up storage on additional storage devices / partitions exposed via volumes. One easy way to work around that would be to place all pods that do not have a disk limit on the primary partition that kubelet tracks. Volumes with limits do not require disk reclamation by kubelet.

By forcing a single partition, `disk` resources expressed on a container or pod can be easily handled by kubelet. `disk` resource on a volume can be handled by the volume directly. K8s metrics API need not have to deal with storage configuration of individual nodes. 

Consider this proposal as a draft. The main purpose is to start a discussion & come up with some high level design conclusions. 

cc @derekwaynecarr @thockin @smarterclayton @matchstick @saad-ali @pmorie

title: mkfs.ext4 is slow when run by kubelet

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

body:
Here's logs from `kubelet` formatting a 10GB HDD disk in Azure as ext4:

```
Aug 17 07:30:22 colemick-kany04-node-0 docker[6700]: I0817 07:30:22.450752    6891 mount_linux.go:342] Disk "/dev/sdc" appears to be unformatted, attempting to format as type: "ext4" with options: [-E lazy_itable_init=0,lazy_journal_init=0 -F /dev/sdc]

Aug 17 07:37:52 colemick-kany04-node-0 docker[6700]: I0817 07:37:52.538305    6891 mount_linux.go:347] Disk successfully formatted (mkfs): ext4 - /dev/sdc /var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/azure-disk/mounts/kubetestdisk0

Aug 17 07:37:52 colemick-kany04-node-0 docker[6700]: I0817 07:37:52.592955    6891 operation_executor.go:720] MountVolume.MountDevice succeeded for volume "kubernetes.io/azure-disk/kubetestdisk0" (spec.Name: "disk-azuredisk") pod "cddd37fc-644b-11e6-88b3-000d3af71bc2" (UID: "cddd37fc-644b-11e6-88b3-000d3af71bc2").                                                                                                                                                                 

Aug 17 07:37:52 colemick-kany04-node-0 docker[6700]: I0817 07:37:52.599067    6891 operation_executor.go:755] MountVolume.SetUp succeeded for volume "kubernetes.io/azure-disk/kubetestdisk0" (spec.Name: "disk-azuredisk") pod "cddd37fc-644b-11e6-88b3-000d3af71bc2" (UID: "cddd37fc-644b-11e6-88b3-000d3af71bc2").
```

It took seven and a half minutes to complete `mkfs`.

Here's me doing it manually from the node:

```
kube@colemick-kany04-node-0:~$ time sudo mkfs.ext4 -E lazy_itable_init=0,lazy_journal_init=0 -F /dev/sdc
mke2fs 1.42.13 (17-May-2015)
/dev/sdc contains a ext4 file system
        created on Wed Aug 17 07:52:59 2016
Discarding device blocks: done
Creating filesystem with 2621440 4k blocks and 655360 inodes
Filesystem UUID: 3fedd79f-3064-48ad-9c94-990d6ae83d2d
Superblock backups stored on blocks:
        32768, 98304, 163840, 229376, 294912, 819200, 884736, 1605632

Allocating group tables: done
Writing inode tables: done
Creating journal (32768 blocks): done
Writing superblocks and filesystem accounting information: done


real    0m3.388s
user    0m0.020s
sys     0m0.232s
```

And even from a container, somewhat emulating kubelet:

```
kube@colemick-kany04-node-0:~$ sudo docker run -it --privileged -v /dev:/dev ubuntu:xenial
root@3f3c3f796fa9:/# time mkfs.ext4 -E lazy_itable_init=0,lazy_journal_init=0 -F /dev/sdc
mke2fs 1.42.13 (17-May-2015)
/dev/sdc contains a ext4 file system
        created on Wed Aug 17 07:53:13 2016
Discarding device blocks: done
Creating filesystem with 2621440 4k blocks and 655360 inodes
Filesystem UUID: 98c150f0-17b4-4ebe-8e9c-31506722a785
Superblock backups stored on blocks:
        32768, 98304, 163840, 229376, 294912, 819200, 884736, 1605632

Allocating group tables: done
Writing inode tables: done
Creating journal (32768 blocks): done
Writing superblocks and filesystem accounting information: done


real    0m3.421s
user    0m0.024s
sys     0m0.224s
```

**Kubernetes version** (use `kubectl version`):

**Environment**:
- **Cloud provider or hardware configuration**: Azure
- **OS** (e.g. from /etc/os-release): Ubuntu (Xenial) 16.10
- **Kernel** (e.g. `uname -a`): Linux 3f3c3f796fa9 4.4.0-34-generic #53-Ubuntu SMP Wed Jul 27 16:06:39 UTC 2016 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
- **Install tools**: kubernetes-anywhere / static pods with kubelet / kubelet in container

**What happened**:
It took seven and a half minutes to format, causing the overall pod startup time to take over 10 minutes by time attachment occurred

**What you expected to happen**:
It to take a matter of seconds, similar to how it does if I execute the command manully.

**How to reproduce it** (as minimally and precisely as possible):
Build `kubernetes` with [the azure disk PR](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/29836) on top. Deploy a cluster. Try to attach an unformatted VHD. Observe `watch -n1 "ps ax | grep mkfs` along with watching `kubelet` logs and confirm it really does take that long.

**Anything else do we need to know**:
I'm running `kubelet` containerized. Like this: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes-anywhere/blob/f3c6143cfebf97d11bf36191721ea528a63e01a8/phase2/ignition/vanilla/kubelet.service

body:
Hi,
While creating a new cluster, we noticed that kube-node-unpacker failed to import kube-proxy docker image, because docker itself failed to run. Here is the log:

```
Aug 17 03:13:44 g113-node-n1-standard-1-do3v docker[14738]: time="2016-08-17T03:13:44.627082774Z" level=fatal msg="Error starting daemon: Error initializing network controller: Error creating default \"bridge\" network: bridge device with non default name cbr0 must be created manually"

labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
We need an issue to track this.

Recently we added the memory eviction test https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/28693.
Currently, it is running in the serial test job. However, after adding it all test running after it could not start pod.

They all failed with the reason `Evicted: The node was low on compute resources.`.

Currently, we are not sure that:
- Is this because the memory is not reclaimed?
- Is this because cadvisor probe interval is too long?
- Is this because there is any bug in current memory eviction implementation?

Anyhow, currently all serial node e2e builds are red, we should fix this or disable the test.

@derekwaynecarr @vishh @mtaufen 
/cc @kubernetes/sig-node

body:
HPA decided to rescale from 37 pods to 70.  For 11 minutes, it was blocked waiting for status on the new pods.  Of those 11 minutes, 8 mins were waiting for CPU usage of 2 pods and 7 mins were waiting for a single pod.

Impact: Presumably it could have had enough statistical significance on the 68 pods' resource usage to make scaling decisions more quickly.  More worrisome: if a single pod were blocked for much longer, HPA would from a user perspective not be working.  It should be more robust.

Aside, file as a different issue if you like, but it's not clear why HPA decided to go from 37 to 70 -- a jump of almost 2x, nor why it decided to scale down afterwards.  Is the workload really that unstable?

body:
Not sure if this is the right place to request this update...

http://kubernetes.io/docs/user-guide/accessing-the-cluster/
Under the title heading "Without kubectl proxy"

Testing with v1.3.2, this documentation no longer works correctly.

``` sh
TOKEN=$(kubectl config view | grep token | cut -f 2 -d ":" | tr -d " ")
```

Returns blank.

``` sh
TOKEN=$(kubectl describe secret $(kubectl get secrets | grep default | awk '{print$1}') | grep -E '^token' | awk -F: '{print$NF}' | tr -d '\t')
```

Where `$(kubectl get secrets | grep default | awk '{print$1}')` is `default-token-<random>` generated by the system.

title: Declarative update of a configmap from the contents of a file

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: sig/cli
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG CLI.

body:
I'm trying to integrate configmaps into our continuous delivery flow. It's important for us that the deploys are idempotent.

Typically we'd create the configuration from files by doing
`kubectl create configmap myconfig --from-file=file1.yml --from-file=file2.yml`

However, if this is run more than once we get this since the command is a create
`Error from server: configmaps "myconfig" already exists`

There are `apply` and `replace` commands for file or stdin resources but no `apply configmap`. We could grab all the contents of each file and pipe that into a resource YML then pass that through to `apply` but it seems awkward.

What is the current accepted practice for updating a configmap that is file driven?

There is some overlap with this and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/24744 plus https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/22368.

title: Storage should not allow multiple users of a PVclaim, if the claim is RWO, even if the PV is RWX

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

body:
This is hard to validate, but it is a bug.  We need to clarify the meaning of a claim's mode.  Today it means "at least" but I think we also need to express "this pod demands exclusive access" vs "shared access is OK".  That is more of an app-level semantic than infrastructure.

Concretely, assume my app needs a RWO volume.  I get bound to an NFS share that is RWX (which is "greater than" RWO).  My app _does not_ tolerate multiple writers to the volume.  It is possible to schedule another pod against the claim, and have it succeed since the PV is RWX underneath.  Now my app is corrupted.

This pattern could maybe apply to RWO PVs, too, if the pods land on the same machine, but that is a more subtle discussion.

body:
PRs either need attention from reviewer(s) or author(s). It will be helpful for both authors and reviewers if the state of the PR is explicit. 

As of today, it is difficult to say if a PR has been reviewed or if the author has addressed all comments.

One way to address this will be for reviewers to close PRs that need attention from authors before being merged. This approach has the downside of running all tests even on trivial PRs and might also send a wrong message to new contributors.

Another option is to add labels - e.x. `needs-review` & `needs-update`. 
Given that we have bot automation, we can let all PR authors automatically apply `needs-review` label by posting a `needs-review` message in the PR.
The same bot logic can be used to apply `needs-update` label too.

This will help reviewers ignore PRs that haven't been updated since the last review.

title: Removing terminated pod's Cgroup

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: lifecycle/rotten
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

body:
For reference: For work in #27204 which is introducing pod level cgroups into Kubernetes. As a part of which we create cgroups for each pod and each of the pod's containers are brought under its pod cgroup. 

We need to cleanup the pod's cgroup once the pod is terminated. 
But we need to be careful about how we delete the cgroup. 

Some Points to consider: 
- Once the pod is terminated we can reduce it's cgroup's CpuShares to ensure that it doesn't take up significant CPU resources.
- We cannot  set memory limit to `0`  as there might be anonymous pages (tmpfs) that cannot be swapped out.
- Hence for memory, we need to ensure that all the pages are reclaimed before deleting the pod's cgroups, otherwise they would be simply moved to its parent cgroup which is highly undesirable and causes system memory pressure.
- We should delete the pod's cgroup only after the pod's volumes have been cleaned up because of the same reason as above.
- We need to ensure that no processes are attached to the cgroup. If any processes are found, they must be killed in-order to be able to delete the cgroup. 

On @vishh suggestions we were able to come up with the following logic for destroying pod cgroups.
1. Once the pod is terminated we reduce it's cgroup's CpuShares to 2(the lowest possible value).
2. Once a pod's volumes have been successfully cleaned up we spawn a separate go routine to destroy all the unwanted pod's cgroups.
3. The go routine is per pod cgroup and will run until the cgroups are successfully deleted.
4. As part of the goroutine we would attempt the following steps.
   - SIGKILL all the processes attached to cgroup. We repeatedly attempt killing the processes until success. If unsuccessful for 10 iterations we start logging failure messages and generate events.
   - Use cgroup's memory.force_empty interface to force the kernel to reclaim all pages.
5. We repeatedly reduce the cgroups memory usage until it falls below a small threshold(0.1 Mb seems to be a reasonable value).
6. In each iteration, if the current memory usage is x bytes we first limit the cgroup memory usage by writing x to memory.limit_in_bytes, then we write 0 to memory.force_empty to further reduce the memory usage, and we continually do this until the memory usage falls below the threshold.

Thanks to @vishh for the suggestions. This should provide a really safe method of deleting cgroups.

To implement this we would first need to add support for force_empty in libcontainer as it currently doesn't support force empty. 

Once we finalize the logic here I would be adding this note to the [proposal](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/docs/proposals/pod-resource-management.md).
@derekwaynecarr @Random-Liu @vishh PTAL.
Please cc anyone else who can provide feedback.

cc @kubernetes/sig-node

title: Delete all containers, including dead ones, for `Failed` pods

labels.name: priority/important-soon

milestone.title: v1.4
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.4/Release-1.4.md

body:
Kubelet evicts pods whenever there is memory or disk pressure. It marks the pods as `Failed` to evict them. To help with reducing disk pressure,  kubelet should delete all containers belonging to `Failed` pods right away. 
This will result in loss of logs. In the future, we can copy out logs from dead containers before deleting them. Logs can be rotated separately from dead containers. 
IMO, this feature is required for disk usage based evictions to work reliably in kubelet.

title: Volume Manager Data Structure Should Use Pod UID in Key

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: lifecycle/rotten
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

body:
**Problem**
This issue is related to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/29555 which was fixed by PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/29673. That issue fixed name collisions for non-attachable volumes (which is much more common), but not for attachable volumes.

Specifically, if a single pod references the same attachable disk via two different volume names (possibly to refer to different partitions), the names will collide.

**Suggested Fix**

There are three main `volumemanager` data structures:
- Actual State of the World (ASW)
- Desired State of the World (DSW)
- Nested Pending Operations (formerly goroutinemap)

Instead of using the same key (unique volume name) for all these data structs, the key for ASW and DSW should be a struct that includes unique volume name and unique pod name. Nested pending operations can continue to operate on unique volume name to keep the existing protection against multiple operations on the same volume.

**Suggested Cleanup**
Move `GetVolumeName()` to `Attacher` volumes interface (instead of required for all volumes). With PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/29673 non-attachable volumes auto-generate the volume name. Ensure that `MarkVolumeAsAttached()` has all the information it needs to either generate the name in either case (instead of passing in an override).

title: Race in `Downward API volume should update annotations / labels on modification`

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

body:
Ref https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/28462
Ref https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/28416

I believe these two flakes have the same root cause:

When there's a pod UPDATE event to kubelet, kubelet will invoke the `volume manager` to update the pod state to introduce the updated annotation:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/volume_manager.go#L298

The `volume manager`:
- 1, Tells the `desiredStateOfWorld populator` to reprocess the volume mount in the next loop.
- 2, Mark the volume in `actualStateOfWorld` to be remounted.
  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/volume_manager.go#L311-L312

However in the reconciler's reconciling loop, it does not always pick up the latest pod state with the latest annotation in the memory cache as the `populator` is running asynchronously.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler.go#L150

But when it reads the `actualStateOfWorld`, it does get notified that the volume needs to be remount, 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler.go#L223

So when remounting the volume, it ends up thinking that the annotation in the pod is not changed, and thus not modifying the content on the disk.

Although the annotation updates on the disk will happen eventually after another periodic pod SYNC event received by kubelet, but it will results in the timeout of the e2e tests.

cc @kubernetes/sig-storage

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

milestone.title: UX Backlog - Stack Ranked
milestone.description: Closed by @calebamiles after talking with @pwittrock please contact calebamiles (on Slack) with complaints

body:
I have a ThirdPartyResource object. The resource is as follows:

resource.yaml

```
metadata:
  name: cron-tab.stable.example.com
apiVersion: extensions/v1beta1
kind: ThirdPartyResource
description: "A specification of a Pod to run on a cron style schedule"
versions:
  - name: v1
  - name: v2
```

crontab.yaml

```
apiVersion: "stable.example.com/v1"
kind: "CronTab"
metadata:
  name: hello-world
cronSpec: "*/1 * * * *"
image: hello-world
```

I create the resource and object

```
$ kubectl create -f resource.yaml
$ kubectl create -f crontab.yaml
```

However, when I run apply I fails to update the properties.

```
$ cat crontab.yaml 
apiVersion: "stable.example.com/v1"
kind: "CronTab"
metadata:
  name: hello-world
cronSpec: "*/5 * * * *"
image: hello-world

$ kubectl apply -f crontab.yaml
crontab "hello-world" configured
```

kubectl is sending a request to the API and if I watch the object I get a modified event but it is still the old value. Getting the object also returns the old value.

```
$ kubectl get crontab hello-world -o json | jq '.cronSpec'
"*/1 * * * *"
```

I suspect that kubectl is not diffing the object properly and neglects to send the updated object JSON data.

labels.name: kind/bug

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
**Problem:**

If a node with a GCE PD attached is deleted (before the volume is detached), subsequent attempts by the attach/detach controller to detach it continuously fail, and prevent the controller from attaching the volume to another node.

**Repro steps:**
1. Create a pod referencing a GCE PD
2. Wait for pod to get scheduled and running.
3. Delete the node VM (using gcloud) that the pod is scheduled to.
4. Check if volume is detached by attach/detach controller:
   - _Expected:_ Volume detached.
   - _Actual:_ Volume continuously fails detach.

**Logs:**
<details>
From `/var/log/kube-controller-manager.log`:

```
I0721 03:21:43.464087       7 reconciler.go:134] Started DetachVolume for volume "X" from node "Y" due to maxWaitForUnmountDuration expiry.
E0721 03:21:43.591941       7 gce.go:2580] getInstanceByName/single-zone: failed to get instance Y; err: googleapi: Error 404: The resource 'projects/[project]/zones/[zone]/instances/Y' was not found, notFound
E0721 03:21:43.591985       7 attacher.go:215] Error checking if PD ("[pdname]") is already attached to current node ("Y"). Will continue and try detach anyway. err=instance not found
E0721 03:21:43.698786       7 gce.go:2580] getInstanceByName/single-zone: failed to get instance Y; err: googleapi: Error 404: The resource 'projects/[project]/zones/[zone]/instances/Y' was not found, notFound
E0721 03:21:43.698828       7 attacher.go:225] Error detaching PD "[pdname]" from node "Y": error getting instance "Y"
```

</details>

**Workarounds:**
- Restart the kube-controller-manager binary on the master.

-or-
- Recreate a node with the same name.

**Proposed Fix:**

If GCE PD detach fails with `instance not found`, assume successful detach.

title: Determine correct Deployment scaling behavior during rollout

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

body:
In 1.4 we are changing the scaling behavior for Deployments during a rollout from
Scale the newest ReplicaSet
to
Scale all active ReplicaSets proportionally by their current number of replicas.

This issue is to discuss the desired behavior when the deployment controller-manager observes both rolling-out and scaling are required in the same controller sync loop.
# Example of proportional scaling:
## In 1.3:

Deployment: 5 replicas + 1 maxsurge **RS B is newest**
- RS B: 1 replica
- RS A: 5 replicas

**_Scale 6 -> 12 results**_

Deployment: 10 replicas + 2 maxsurge
- RS B: 7 replicas
- RS A: 5 replicas
## In 1.4:

Deployment: 5 replicas + 1 maxsurge **RS B is newest**
- RS B: 1 replica
- RS A: 5 replicas

**_Scale 6 -> 12 results**_

Deployment: 10 replicas + 2 maxsurge
- RS B: 2 replicas
- RS A: 10 replicas
# Description of choices for proportional scaling with rollout

When the control loop sees that changes need to be made to the total number of RS replicas (scaling) AND a new RS needs to be created (rollout) in the same iteration, it can proceed in 1 of 2 ways:

1: Create a new RS + (if scaling up add all new replicas to the new RS, if scaling down let the rollout process scale down old RSs)
- Good: This more accurately matches the system to the state desired by the user.  The user may want to only ever have X replicas of the new release, but never have more than X of a previous release.
- Bad: This behaves differently from what happens when the changes are seen in separate loops iterations.  Since the control loops are level-based and not edge-based, it is non-deterministic whether the user will see proportional scaling or not EVEN when doing separate events (the control loop may observe changes from 2 separate updates in a single iteration).

2: Proportionally scale the replicas and then create a new RS + perform rollout
- Good: This results in behavior that closely matches what happens both when the control loop sees scale then rollout and when the control loop sees rollout then scale in separate syncs (separate events)
- Bad: This creates a desired state that the user never actually asked for since the user never asked for the old RSs to be scaled up.

_It is worth noting that with ANY proportional scaling it is possible for the system to create a state that the user never actually wanted if the user creates an update, k8s creates a new RS for the update, and then the user scales by increasing the number of replicas._
# Examples of proportional scaling with rollout
## A) Update image, then Scale

Deployment: 5 replicas + 1 maxsurge
- RS A: 5 replicas

**_Update image**_

Deployment: 5 replicas + 1 maxsurge
- RS B: 1 replicas
- RS A: 5 replicas

**_Scale 6 -> 12 results**_

Deployment: 10 replicas + 2 maxsurge
- RS B: 2 replicas
- RS A: 10 replicas
## Scale, then update image

Deployment: 5 replicas + 1 maxsurge
- RS A: 5 replicas

**_Scale 6 -> 12 results**_

Deployment: 10 replicas + 2 maxsurge
- RS A: 10 replicas

**_Update image**_
...

Deployment: 10 replicas + 2 maxsurge
- RS B: 2 replicas
- RS A: 10 replicas
## Scale + Update Option 1 (new RS first)

Deployment: 5 replicas + 1 maxsurge
- RS A: 5 replicas

**_Update Image + Scale 6 -> 12 results**_

Deployment: 10 replicas + 2 maxsurge
- RS B: 7 replicas
- RS A: 5 replicas
## Scale + Update Option 2 (scale first)

Deployment: 5 replicas + 1 maxsurge
- RS A: 5 replicas

**_Update Image + Scale 6 -> 12 results**_

Deployment: 10 replicas + 2 maxsurge
- RS B: 2 replicas
- RS A: 10 replicas
# Questions
1. For proportional scaling, is option 1 or option 2 the better choice?
2. Should the scaling strategy be a configurable field in Deployment so users can force non-proportional scaling?

title: Federation: Cloud resources (DNS records) need to be cleaned up in CI environments.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/multicluster
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Multicluster.

body:
1. We don't generally want to delete the DNS records created by the Federated Service Controller when it terminates, as this might break the clients of those federated services in real-world scenarios (e.g. upgrades of the federation control plane).
2. But we do need an easy way to delete all of the records created in some cases (e.g. after a CI test run).

Currently there are over 4,000 DNS records in left over in the project that our CI tests run in.  We will presumably eventually hit some sort of quota limit there.

A few options available.
1. write an independent tool which can delete all of the DNS records in a given DNS zone, and invoke that automatically after our CI test runs.
2. systematically delete all of the created federated services as part of our tests, and ensure that the service controller deletes all of the DNS records when that happens.

But before that, to prepare for the node conformance test, there are several working items we should do to improve the **test coverage and the reliability** of the test framework.
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/28807 #29536 #29806 Make it possible to share test case between e2e test and node e2e.
  - This makes it much easier to improve the test coverage.
  - Ideally, all node e2e compatible e2e test should be shared between the 2 test suites.
  - [x] [Optional] #32986 Add image white list. [Related issue: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/29155]
- [x] #29806 #29807 #29809 #29814 Consolidate existing e2e and node e2e test, and move them into the shared diretory.
  - This directly improves the test coverage.
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/29020 Start namespace controller in node e2e test framework. [Related issue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/28320]
  - This makes it easier to improve the test coverage.
    - Originally the automated namespace cleanup is not enabled in node e2e, becaue of lack of namespace controller. When migrating test from e2e to node e2e, we have to carefully take care of the cleanup. 
    - After this, we can directly migrate test from e2e, and the test framework will automatically handle cleanup as what it has done in the e2e test.
  - This makes the test framework more reliable.
  - This also improves the user experience if we provide the node conformance test to the user.
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/29092 Run node e2e test in parallel. [Related issue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/26215]
  - This makes it easier to improve the test coverage.
    - Most tests are time consuming. Now all node e2e tests run sequentially. As we improve the test coverage, the test duration will increase quickly.
    - In fact most time the test is just sleeping and waiting for specific state. Parallelize the tests could significantly decrease the test duration.
  - This also improves the user experience if we provide the node conformance test to the user.
- [ ] [Optional] #32427 Add system verification test to validate system configurations.

More working items: TBD

XRef https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/28408, because kubelet verify is considered to be a subset of node conformance test.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
Hey,

I upgraded a small (3 node) GKE cluster to 1.3 yesterday. After about 30-50 minutes everything had settled down and was running fine.

Within about an hour after that (I'm unsure about the correct timestamp) something caused two pods that were using `gcePersistentDisk` volumes to restart and upon mounting the disks again, something (presumably k8s) reformatted the file system on those disks, leading to data loss.

Deployment specs: [1](https://github.com/Goonswarm/infrastructure/blob/fce4e440499a1aef473c928058d8bb719da4dc58/slapd/ldap.yaml) [2](https://github.com/Goonswarm/infrastructure/blob/fce4e440499a1aef473c928058d8bb719da4dc58/forum/forum.yaml#L43)

The pods started up fine afterwards, as both OpenLDAP and MariaDB just initialised new (empty) databases on those volumes. When I noticed it I snapshotted the empty volumes, stopped the pods and reverted the volumes to a backup snapshot - which worked fine.

Digging into those empty volumes revealed that filesystem had been reinitialised / volume formatted, the blocks from the previous FS instance were still present on the disk.

Has anyone else experienced this?

title: PVC Volume not detached if pod deleted via namespace deletion

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

milestone.title: v1.3
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.3/release-1.3.md

body:
**Problem:**
An attachable volume referenced by a pod via a PVC object (instead of directly) is not detached if the pod is deleted via namespace deletion (i.e. deleting the pod's namespace instead of the pod object directly).

**Repro steps:**
1. Create a new volume
   - `gcloud compute disks create --zone=us-central1-b  test-0b`
2. Create a new namespace.
   - `kubectl create ns testns`
     - `namespace "testns" created`
3. Create PV and PVC objects:
   - `kubectl create -f volumetest_pvc-pv.yaml`
     - `persistentvolume "pv-test-detach" created`
     - `persistentvolumeclaim "claim-test-detach" created`
4. Verify PV/PVC objects are in bound state
   - `kubectl get pv`
     - `pv-test-detach     50Gi       RWO           Bound     testns/claim-test-detach               2m`
5. Create pod object that references the volume via PVC
   - `kubectl create -f volumetest_pod_pvc.yaml`
     - `replicationcontroller "sleepypod" created`
6. Verify pod gets into running state without issue (i.e. volume is attached)
   - `kubectl get pods --namespace testns`
     - `sleepypod-0b0eq   1/1       Running   0          3m`
7. Delete the namespace
   - `kubectl delete ns testns`
     - `namespace "testns" deleted`
8. Wait for pod to terminate
   - `kubectl get pods --namespace testns`
9. Check if volume remains attached after a few minutes
   - Expected: Volume is detached.
   - Actual: Volume remains attached indefinitely.

<details>
`volumetest_pvc-pv.yaml` is:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name : pv-test-detach
spec:
  claimRef:
    name: claim-test-detach
    namespace: testns
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  capacity:
    storage: 50Gi
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  gcePersistentDisk:
    fsType: ext4
    pdName: test-0b

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: claim-test-detach
  namespace: testns
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 50Gi
```

And `volumetest_pod_pvc.yaml` is:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ReplicationController
metadata:
  name: sleepypod
  namespace: testns
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    name: sleepy
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        name: sleepy
    spec:
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: claim-test-detach
      containers:
      - name: sleepycontainer1
        image: saadali/sleepy:v0.2
        env:
        - name: "FOO"
          value: " "
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: "0.002"
            memory: "4Mi"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data
          readOnly: false
```

</details>

**Workarounds:**
1. Delete the pod object directly before deleting the namespace.
   - In step 7 above do `kubectl delete -f volumetest_pod_pvc.yaml` instead
   - If the attachable volume is referenced by a pod using a PVC object, and the pod object is deleted directly (instead of the namespace first),  the volume is correctly detached.
2. Reference volume directly in pod (without a PVC object).
   - If the attachable volume is referenced by a pod directly (without a PVC object), namespace deletion results in the volume being correctly detached.

title: Have kubelet delete all pods

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
As of now kubelet deletes pods that have a graceful termination period > 0 seconds. Why not have kubelet delete all pods, even ones that have graceful termination == 0 ?

Having kubelet delete pod objects will make it possible to identify pods that are still being cleaned up kubelet, and hence occupying some resources. Ideally, a pod should not be considered as deleted until all its resources have been reclaimed, including volumes. Having kubelet delete the pod object after it has successfully cleaned up a pod on the node is ideal.

This feature will make it possible to introduce pod level cgroups in kubelet. Pod level resources cannot be reclaimed until volumes belonging to a pod have been removed successfully, at-least tmpfs based ones to begin with. Until the resources are reclaimed, we don't want the scheduler to incorrectly assume that those _yet to be reclaimed_ resources are available on the node.

cc @davidopp who proposed this idea.

cc @smarterclayton @kubernetes/sig-node

milestone.title: v1.4
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.4/Release-1.4.md

body:
The vsphere volume [calls out to cloud provider to attach a volume](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/volume/vsphere_volume/vsphere_volume_util.go) as part of the `setup(...)` step in the `mounter` plugin interface. 

_The vsphere volume plugin should be refactored to implement the volume [`Attacher` plugin interface](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/volume/volume.go#L136)._ This will enable it take advantage of the attach/detach controller and let volume_manager better control device mounting (prevent multiple concurrent operations, do retries, etc).

CC @abithap

title: Guaranteed scheduling of critical pods

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

body:
We want to ensure that pods deemed "critical" (this is _not_ official terminology -- I am just using it in the colloquial English sense) are guaranteed to schedule if there are sufficient resources for them in an "empty" cluster, even if the cluster is non-empty and non-critical pods are currently occupying node resources that the critical pods would need in order to schedule.

Examples of critical pods are infrastructure pods like heapster and DNS.

cc/ @piosz @fgrzadkowski

milestone.title: v1.4
milestone.description: https://github.com/kubernetes/features/blob/master/release-1.4/Release-1.4.md

body:
I've just faced the problem of corrupted cache in scheduler. Basically the problem was the following:
- scheduler tried to bind a pod X
- binding was rejected (in this case because of http didn't reach apiserver due to network overload, but the type of error doesn't really matter)
- then after some time we are scheduling this pod again, but this time we are binding it to a different node
- the binding succeeds

After those operations, schedulercache will be corrupted, because second Assume will be processed incorrectly.

@davidopp @hongchaodeng @xiang90 @kubernetes/sig-scheduling

title: If CIDRAllocator fails to update CIDR in Node object it won't retry.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

body:
Currently CIDRAllocator observes only Node creations and deletions. When Node is created it tries to assign a CIDR to it. If it fails for any reason (no available CIDRs, run out of Node update retries) it won't ever retry, as the Node won't be "created" again. We need to add a mechanism for retrying assignments in such cases.

title: Pet set upgrades

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/apps
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Apps.

body:
One should be able to upgrade a petset through the standard kubectl rolling-update syntax. While it's desirable to have a controlled upgrade strategy (eg: deployments), it may not be necessary for beta. 

The tricky part is making sure that `pet-v1-0` and `pet-v2-0` come up with the same data. For beta I propose we just make `kubectl rolling-update` on petset update the image and kill pets one by one (as opposed to creating a new petset like a classic rolling-update). If any pet doesn't become ready within a timeout, the rolling-update reverts. 

Node upgrade: mark node as unschedulable, delete pets one by one, wait till they show up on new node as ready, upgrade node. Can we get away with just documenting this (upgrading kubelet on a node shouldn't lead to container restarts anyway)? 

@smarterclayton @kubernetes/sig-apps Is this enough? 
- To improve the upgrade UX we could use 2 new events: `pre-delete` and `pre-update`. We can use `terminationGrace` simply to leave the cluster, `pre-delete` to do something drastic like backup all data, and `pre-update` to do something like give-up leadership (but retain data). When a member is removed/rejoined the rest of the cluster should receive `on-change`. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/24957 should help with the events.
- To improve master/slave upgrade UX, we need to avoid "chasing" the master, i.e by picking the master to upgrade, while the upgrade is happening a new master is elected, the next pod we pick is this new master, and so on. 

This might work as follows: 
- upgrade all slaves
- send `on-upgrade` to master so it gives up mastership, and doesn't compete in re-election
- wait for new master
- upgrade old master

A leader election service might help here (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/28658). 
- To improve active-active upgrade UX, the `on-change` sent to all other members needs to exclude the upgrading member by re-writing the config, so writes aren't blocked on its ack. The upgraded member will have to play catchup when it rejoins. 
- Some databases like Cassandra have special roles, like seed provider. These need to be dealt with in a  similar way as leadership transfer (promote new seed, update peers, upgrade existing seed).
- To improve node upgrade UX, we could teach `kubectl drain` to move pets off a node slowly. If people are running 1 pet per node (eg: pod anti-affinity), we have less of a problem.

title: Kubelet tears down and sets up cbr0 traffic shaping every 30s

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/network
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Network.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
After I turned on my verbose logging, I'm getting this every 30 seconds:

```
I0707 02:52:45.813461   22220 linux.go:56] Running: tc qdisc delete dev cbr0 root handle 1:
I0707 02:52:45.815029   22220 linux.go:59] Output from tc: 
I0707 02:52:45.815048   22220 linux.go:56] Running: tc qdisc add dev cbr0 root handle 1: htb default 30
I0707 02:52:45.816622   22220 linux.go:59] Output from tc: 
```

Probably harmless, but also pointless (especially given that there is a bunch of checks to avoid this!).

The logic (`util/bandwidth/linux.go`, `ReconcileInterface()`) looks wrong for what `tc` is returning:

``` go
    if len(fields) != 12 || fields[1] != "htb" || fields[2] != "1:" {
```

Here's the output of `tc`:

```
$ tc qdisc show dev cbr0
qdisc htb 1: root refcnt 2 r2q 10 default 30 direct_packets_stat 12 direct_qlen 1000
```

In other words, it's returning 14 fields, not 12. In general, the heuristic is pretty bad. I should check for the things that it knows, which are:

``` go
    return t.execAndLog("tc", "qdisc", "add", "dev", t.iface, "root", "handle", "1:", "htb", "default", "30")
```

In other words, to be entirely correct it should check for the presence of the interface name, `root`, the handle, `htb` and the `default 30` thing. Any keywords it doesn't know ought to be ignored.

Kubernetes 1.2.0, Linux 4.4.0, Ubuntu 16.04.

title: Ubernetes lite is not working on GCE

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/cluster-lifecycle
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Cluster Lifecycle.

body:
I run commands from http://blog.kubernetes.io/2016/03/building-highly-available-applications-using-Kubernetes-new-multi-zone-clusters-a.k.a-Ubernetes-Lite.html and it doesn't work. The problem is in the second command which adds nodes in the second zone:

```
KUBE_USE_EXISTING_MASTER=true MULTIZONE=true KUBERNETES_PROVIDER=gce 
KUBE_GCE_ZONE=us-central1-b NUM_NODES=3 kubernetes/cluster/kube-up.sh
```

and specifically in `get-master-env`:

```
function get-master-env() {
  # TODO(zmerlynn): Make this more reliable with retries.
  gcloud compute --project ${PROJECT} ssh --zone ${ZONE} ${KUBE_MASTER} --command \
    "curl --fail --silent -H 'Metadata-Flavor: Google' \
      'http://metadata/computeMetadata/v1/instance/attributes/kube-env'" 2>/dev/null
}
```

There are few problems:
- `KUBE_MASTER` is never set
- `ZONE` points to the new zone with just the nodes so obviously there's no master there

I think the most reasonable solution is to:
1. Add call to `detect-master` before calling `get-master-env`, and
2. Add support in `detect-master` to find master in other zones (in the same region?)

title: Amount of skydns pods does not scale with cluster needs

body:
We are running kubernetes 1.2.4 on GKE. We observed that when we increased load on our system by 20% our outbound connections from our pods started to fail 80% of the time. After much diagnosing we found that our cluster was running with just one `kube-dns` pod. This pod was being hammered and resulted in failures to resolve DNS requests.

Our cluster started smaller (3x VM 8 core if i remember correctly) and is currently almost doubled in size/cores (10x VM 4 core).

Creating a new cluster in GKE of the same size gave us three `kube-dns` pods. My expectations would be that the amound of `kube-dns` pods would scale by load (using a HPA?) or that the pods would scale by cluster size (using deamonsets?). Not that the amound of `kube-dns` pods would be based on the initial cluster size when creating it in GKE.

```

title: PodGC default threshold causes OOMs on small master machines.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

body:
I've seen a cluster (from 1.2.4) where there is a job and the pods it is starting are simply crashing.
The problem is that those failed pods are not being garbage collected.

In the example cluster I've seen, we were able to produce ~13.000 failed pods over the week and it seems it none of these were ever garbage collected.

This basically results in constantly increasing memory usage of master components.

title: Release tarballs are too big

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Release.

labels.name: lifecycle/stale
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR has remained open with no activity and has become stale.

body:
The Kubernetes 1.3 release tarball is 1.4G.  That is insane.  While we know that much of this is due to the fact that we include all architectures, it make kubernetes feel heavier than it is.

Much of the space is the fact that 4 server platforms are now created and packaged with everything else.  Each target is a ~325M tarball.  These tarballs include both individual binaries along with Docker images that include those binaries.  They include kubectl (which is available naked in the release).

We also have 9 copies of kubectl for various targets totaling 450MB.

Things we can do to slim this down:
- [x] Start building release tars per-architecture.  Either include non-arch specific stuff in every tar or break that out too. (#28629, owner?)
- [ ] Finish transition to hyperkube and deprecate the individual binaries.  . We could move the individual binaries into a different tar for those that still need them.  For `amd64` hyperkube is 132M uncompressed and 26M compressed.  This means we could go from a 350M compressed tar for the amd64 target down to 26M. (#16508, owner?)
- [ ] Have the ability to build the Docker images on the fly.  It should be easy to automate (as part of the binary) creating a Dockerfile, referencing the running binary and driving docker.  `hyperkube admin create-container-image` could do this. We could also support `hyperkube admin create-container-image --aci` and `hyperkube admin create-container-image --docker --just-dockerfile`. (#28630, owner?)
  - I understand that gzip does a decent job of de-duping stuff here.  But the uncompressed footprint balloons and looks bad.
- [ ] Break out kubectl as a separate download from the server components.  `gcloud` already ships it separately.  The user cases here differ dramatically. (#28631, owner?)
- [ ] Reevaluate all of our targets.  Do we really need 32bit Windows? (#28632, owner?)
- [x] Why are the federation targets new binaries? They add 150M uncompressed for amd64. (I don't know enough to say here but could these be folded in to hyperkube?  I'm guessing they could.) (#28633, @madhusudancs)
- [x] Don't ship binaries that we don't really need.  We included `kubemark` here.  No end users will actually use that.  This is 100M uncompressed. (#28635, owner?)

Also related: #27444 (Builds are taking too long)

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

body:
Hello,

There is an [upstream problem with docker's json-file log driver](https://github.com/docker/docker/issues/23913). The command 'docker logs --follow' (and subsequently 'kubectl logs --follow') stops generating log output when the node that hosts the given container rotates the container logs.

**Environment:**

Running kubernetes 1.2.4 on AWS.

**Impact**

logspout or other tools that rely on 'docker logs --follow' / 'kubectl logs --follow' break during log rotation.

**Steps to reproduce:**
- Launch a pod that generates regular stdout.
- Launch `kubectl logs --tail POD` for the pod above.
- Instead of waiting for log rotation, force it: SSH into the node that hosts that pod/container, and run `sudo /usr/sbin/logrotate --force /etc/logrotate.conf`
- Observe output stop. Restarting the kubectl logs command will resume log streaming.

To reproduce at the docker level, repeat the procedure above using 'docker logs' on the node, e.g.:

```
sudo DOCKER_HOST=unix:///var/run/docker.sock docker logs --tail=0 --follow CONTAINER_ID
```

title: federation: kubectl --cascade should be false by default for federation

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/multicluster
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Multicluster.

body:
Ref https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/33612.

Cascading deletion is true by default for kubectl.

For federation, we want it to be false since deleting a federation resource with cascade=true will delete the resource from all clusters as well which can lead to a global outage. So we want --cascade to be false by default but users can pass --cascade=true if they do want cascading deletion.

cc @kubernetes/sig-federation-misc @kubernetes/sig-cli-misc @quinton-hoole @caesarxuchao

It seems to hit [ResourceConsumer.CleanUp()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/autoscaling_utils.go#L301) and hang. I think it's attempting to write to a blocking channel because we never see any cleanup messages from the framework functions that would be called right after the channel writes.

Found while investigating https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/37981

title: CRI: Support docker 1.10

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
In K8s v1.5, we focus on supporting docker 1.11. We should also support docker 1.10 which is still supported by Kubernetes.

There are 2 known issues of current CRI integration (forked from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/29478#issuecomment-248197665):
1) **Separator in seccomp configure is changed from 1.10 to 1.11.**
Docker >=1.11 is using `=` as separator, e.g. `seccomp=unconfined`; while docker <= 1.10 is using `:` as separator, e.g. `seccomp:unconfined`. This will cause error `failed to create a sandbox for pod "XXX": Error response from daemon: Invalid --security-opt: "seccomp=unconfined"` (See docker/docker#24810)
2) ~~**oomScoreAdj is only supported in docker >= 1.11.** Currently we rely on docker to apply oom_score_adj in dockershim, which is only supported in docker >=1.11. If we want to support docker <=1.10, we need to [apply oom score adj ourselves](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/dockertools/docker_manager.go#L1684-L1710) in dockershim.~~

There may be other issues with supporting 1.10, we should add comment if we found more.

@yujuhong @feiskyer 
/cc @kubernetes/sig-node

title: Can't list PodDisruptionBudgets after upgrade if v1alpha1 PDBs exist

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

body:
<!-- Thanks for filing an issue! Before hitting the button, please answer these questions.-->

**Is this a request for help?** (If yes, you should use our troubleshooting guide and community support channels, see http://kubernetes.io/docs/troubleshooting/.):

-->

**Kubernetes version** (use `kubectl version`):

```
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"5+", GitVersion:"v1.5.0-beta.2", GitCommit:"0776eab45fe28f02bbeac0f05ae1a203051a21eb", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2016-11-24T22:35:03Z", GoVersion:"go1.7.3", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"5+", GitVersion:"v1.5.0-beta.2", GitCommit:"0776eab45fe28f02bbeac0f05ae1a203051a21eb", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2016-11-24T22:30:23Z", GoVersion:"go1.7.3", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
```

**Environment**:
- **Cloud provider or hardware configuration**: GCE
- **OS** (e.g. from /etc/os-release):
- **Kernel** (e.g. `uname -a`):
- **Install tools**:
- **Others**:


**What happened**:

If a `policy/v1alpha1` PDB still exists after upgrading the master from `v1.4.6` to `v1.5.0-beta.2`, `kubectl get poddisruptionbudget` is broken (even for subsequently-created `policy/v1beta1` PDBs). The alpha PDB cannot be deleted through `kubectl` (neither v1.4.6 nor v1.5.0-beta.2), so the user is stuck in this broken state and must roll back the master.


**What you expected to happen**:

The existence of the alpha PDB should not break interactions with beta PDBs.

**How to reproduce it** (as minimally and precisely as possible):

1.  Launch a `v1.4.6` cluster from an official release build.
1.  Create an alpha PDB:
    ```yaml
    apiVersion: policy/v1alpha1
    kind: PodDisruptionBudget
    metadata:
      name: web
    spec:
      selector:
        matchLabels:
          app: nginx
      minAvailable: 4
    ```
1.  Upgrade the master to `v1.5.0-beta.2`: `cluster/gce/upgrade.sh -M v1.5.0-beta.2`
1.  Attempt to run `kubectl get poddisruptionbudget`

With kubectl v1.4.6:

```console
$ kubectl get poddisruptionbudget
error: group map[certificates.k8s.io:0xc8203eb2d0 componentconfig:0xc8203eb340 extensions:0xc8203b6070 policy:0xc8203b60e0 rbac.authorization.k8s.io:0xc8203b6150 apps:0xc8203eae70 authorization.k8s.io:0xc8203eb030 autoscaling:0xc8203eb0a0 storage.k8s.io:0xc8203b61c0 batch:0xc8203eb260 federation:0xc8203ea930 :0xc8203eae00 authentication.k8s.io:0xc8203eaee0] is already registered
```

With kubectl v1.5.0-beta.2:

```console
$ kubectl get poddisruptionbudget
Error from server: no kind "PodDisruptionBudget" is registered for version "policy/v1alpha1"
```

**Anything else do we need to know**:

If I try to create a beta PDB with the same name, it says:
```
Error from server (AlreadyExists): error when creating "pdb-beta.yaml": poddisruptionbudgets.policy "web" already exists
```

Attempting to delete the alpha PDB (either by name or by file) fails with:

```console
$ kubectl delete poddisruptionbudget web
Error from server: no kind "PodDisruptionBudget" is registered for version "policy/v1alpha1"
$ kubectl delete -f pdb-alpha.yaml 
Error from server: error when deleting "pdb-alpha.yaml": no kind "PodDisruptionBudget" is registered for version "policy/v1alpha1"
$ kubectl delete -f pdb-beta.yaml 
Error from server: error when deleting "pdb-beta.yaml": no kind "PodDisruptionBudget" is registered for version "policy/v1alpha1"
```

I can successfully create a beta PDB with a different name and I can specifically `kubectl get poddisruptionbudget beta-pdb`. However, listing all PDBs (`kubectl get poddisruptionbudget`) remains broken.

title: Expose Kubelet logs via Kubelet `/logs` endpoint

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: lifecycle/rotten
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

body:
Kubelet currently exposes all log files stored under `/var/log` directory on a node via its `/logs/` endpoint. This interface is very convenient for accessing kubelet and runtime logs remotely. 

However this interface requires log files to be available under `/var/log` directory.

Given that many deployments use journald today, it would be helpful if `/logs/` REST endpoint in kubelet can expose journal logs for a select subset of system services like kubelet and the runtime.

cc @kubernetes/sig-node

title: Race in service ipallocator in portallocator

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/network
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Network.

body:
There is a race in ipallocator (and the same for portallocator) that may lead to 2 services sharing the same IP (or port).

How can it happen:
1. We have this "Repair" thread responsible for reporting bugs in IP allocations:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fbd187af4544c3734c2ddf45024972857bf44583/pkg/registry/core/service/portallocator/controller/repair.go
2. What it does is in the "runOnce" method it:
-  Gets allocated IPaddresses
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fbd187af4544c3734c2ddf45024972857bf44583/pkg/registry/core/service/portallocator/controller/repair.go#L81
- Lists all services:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fbd187af4544c3734c2ddf45024972857bf44583/pkg/registry/core/service/portallocator/controller/repair.go#L97
And then processes those services and based on them updates IPaddresses.
3. However, in etcd allocating an IPaddress and service is NOT atomic with creating a service - we first allocate an IPaddres in etcd and only then create/update a service object in etcd.
4. That means that having already allocated IPaddres in etcd for service that is not yet written in etcd is valid usecase.
5. If ```runOnce``` is called in exactly that time, it will clean up the IPaddress from etcd as unallocated.
6. As a result, we may end-up with two services sharding the same IPaddres after that.

The same holds for ports.

@thockin @bprashanth  @kubernetes/sig-network

title: fix some issues with kubectl drain

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

body:
In writing some documentation for `kubectl drain` I noticed some issues with the implementation.

I think the simplest user experience is that the command doesn't return until all the user pods are drained off the machine. In particular this means
* wait until all graceful termination is finished
* infinitely retry evictions that are rejected due to insufficient PodDisruptionBudget

The current implementation does not do this, in particular
* wait for graceful termination appears to be [capped](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubectl/cmd/drain.go#L257) at 10 sec * number of pods, which may be much shorter than the max graceful termination
* we only retry evictions [maxPatchRetry](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubectl/cmd/drain.go#L236) number of times

My suggestion is to change the behavior so that
* we compute how long to wait for graceful termination, by taking max(grace periods of all pods that we want to delete) (or the value of --grace-period command line argument instead, if that is specified), and wait exactly that amount of time plus a small buffer
* we retry evictions infinitely

@ymqytw @erictune WDYT? I think we should do this in 1.5 because the current behavior is very non-obvious.

**Environment**:
- **Cloud provider or hardware configuration**: GKE
- **OS** (e.g. from /etc/os-release): default
- **Kernel** (e.g. `uname -a`):
- **Install tools**:
- **Others**:


**What happened**:
I was trying to reproduce https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/34772 using [these instructions](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/34772#issuecomment-260594667). Due to bug in scheduler we were assigning too many pods per node. In most cases kubelet was correctly discarding them by marking them as `OutOfcpu`. However two strange things happened:
* upon kubelet restart, it tried to re-add all such `OutOfcpu` pods, run predicate check for them etc.
* for two pods that were incorrectly assigned (due to scheduler bug) during kubelet restart kubelet completely ignored them - they are still pending, with node assigned for 12h.

I have a cluster that I can add someone to investigate.

**What you expected to happen**:

* `OutOfcpu` pods should not be retried after restart
* new pods, assigned during kubelet restart, should be discarded with `OutOfcpu` error.

**How to reproduce it** (as minimally and precisely as possible):

Run [these instructions](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/34772#issuecomment-260594667).

**Anything else do we need to know**:

Marking as `release-blocker` until it's triaged by node team.

title: Container logs rotation

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

body:
Recently I was running some load test on the logging subsystem in docker and after a while, fluentd (logging agent) started to write warning in it's logs:

```
2016-11-22 12:31:09 +0000 [warn]: pattern not match: ".go:67] 657735 PUT /api/v1/namespaces/kube-system/pods/av6r 470\\n\",\"stream\":\"stderr\",\"time\":\"2016-11-22T12:23:50.785896269Z\"}"
2016-11-22 12:32:22 +0000 [warn]: pattern not match: "stderr\",\"time\":\"2016-11-22T12:24:39.791492844Z\"}"
2016-11-22 12:33:33 +0000 [warn]: pattern not match: "6Z\"}"
2016-11-22 12:34:44 +0000 [warn]: pattern not match: ":11.205065       5 logs_generator.go:67] 680385 PUT /api/v1/namespaces/default/pods/lpp 460\\n\",\"stream\":\"stderr\",\"time\":\"2016-11-22T12:26:11.205087538Z\"}"
2016-11-22 12:36:04 +0000 [warn]: pattern not match: "/pods/8r5 404\\n\",\"stream\":\"stderr\",\"time\":\"2016-11-22T12:27:57.625483865Z\"}"
2016-11-22 12:37:23 +0000 [warn]: pattern not match: ":12.287898957Z\"}"
```

So it seems like the lines read from docker log files (in json format by default) are somehow damaged. Further investigation showed that container logs are constantly being rotated and the hypothesis is that lines are somehow being damaged during the process of rotation. It would be not that much of an issue if it wasn't the reason why fluentd after some time entered weird "infinite crash loop" state with the following error:

```
error_class="ArgumentError" error="invalid byte sequence in UTF-8"
```

Which may also indicate a partial read of the log file content.

The question is: can this be an issue in the real setup? Because this is very bad situation: from the outside everything seems to work, but in reality no logs are being exported from the node.

@piosz @repeatedly

title: Strategic patch forgets a edge case

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
Strategic patch doesn't work on an edge case:
```
original:
  mergingIntList:
  - 1

current:
  mergingIntList:
  - 1
  - 2

modified:
  {}
```
The expected state is:
```
  mergingIntList:
  - 2
```
But we get:
```
  {}
```
The cause is we send a patch looks like this which will delete the whole list.
```
  mergingIntList: null
```
The patch we should send is
```
  mergingIntList:
  - 1: null
  - 2: null
```
This case is not covered in #35647. We should add a test case in `strategicpatch`.

Similar issue has been found in list of maps.

cc @pwittrock

title: etcd rollback tool panics when the initial data comes from "etcdctl backup"

labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery

body:
I have been performing some tests using a tarball taken from an apiserver filesystem and some tests using the output of `etcdctl-2.2.1 backup`.  In the latter case, the `rollback` tool will crash.

[data-crash.tar.gz](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/files/601123/data-crash.tar.gz) contains data that will crash `rollback`.  It is the data after having upgraded from 2.2.1 -> 2.3.7 -> 3.0.14.

[etcdctl-backup.tar.gz](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/files/601124/etcdctl-backup.tar.gz) contains both the original data (`etcd/data.orig`) and the output of `etcdctl-2.2.1 backup` (`etcd/data`) before any upgrades.

@wojtek-t @xiang90 @hongchaodeng

title: e2e logic for matching pods to ReplicationControllers is broken

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

body:
The logic to account for all pods being ready is incorrectly counting some pods as being controlled by a replication controller. This is causing the 1.3-1.5 upgrade tests to fail. See https://k8s-gubernator.appspot.com/build/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/kubernetes-e2e-gke-container_vm-1.3-container_vm-1.5-upgrade-cluster/99 as an example.

```
Nov 16 10:52:49.437: INFO: expected 4 pod replicas in namespace 'kube-system', 5 are Running and Ready.
```

Since `5 != 4`, the pre-flight checks fail and the rest of the tests never run. I think this was exposed by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/36008 which changed some things from ReplicationControllers to Deployments. There's a pod being created by a deployment that also matches the selector of a replication controller, and is therefore being incorrectly counted by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/framework/util.go#L441

cc @kubernetes/sig-testing @saad-ali

title: StatefulSets with the same selector interfere with each other

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/apps
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Apps.

body:
**What happened**:
When two statefulsets are created with the same labels, only one manages to come up.
This is caused by the same issue as https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/36855#issuecomment-260828249.

**What you expected to happen**:
Two StatefulSets should be created, instead, one was created, and another was unable to come up.

```
~ kubectl get pods --watch
NAME      READY     STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
ss2-0     1/1       Running   0          7s
ss2-1     1/1       Running   0          6s
ss2-2     1/1       Running   0          4s
NAME      READY     STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
ss1-0     0/1       Pending   0          1s
ss1-0     0/1       Pending   0         1s
ss1-0     0/1       ContainerCreating   0         1s
ss1-0     1/1       Running   0         2s
ss1-0     1/1       Terminating   0         2s
ss1-0     1/1       Terminating   0         2s
ss1-0     0/1       Pending   0         0s
ss1-0     0/1       Pending   0         0s
ss1-0     0/1       ContainerCreating   0         1s
ss1-0     1/1       Running   0         2s
ss1-0     1/1       Terminating   0         2s
ss1-0     1/1       Terminating   0         2s
```


**How to reproduce it** (as minimally and precisely as possible):

```
apiVersion: apps/v1beta1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: ss1
spec:
  serviceName: "ss1"
  replicas: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ss
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: alpine
        image: alpine
        command: 
        - /bin/sleep
        - "1000000"
```

```
apiVersion: apps/v1beta1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: ss2
spec:
  serviceName: "ss2"
  replicas: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ss
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: alpine
        image: alpine
        command: 
        - /bin/sleep
        - "1000000"
```

**What we should be doing**:

- Do not filter on the label selector to find the pods associated with a PetSet.

cc @kubernetes/sig-apps

body:
There are about 23 update scripts and it is not obvious which ones have to be run for a given PR. These update scripts take anywhere between 20 - 30 minutes on a beefed up machine. I can't imagine running them on a laptop. 
We need to either
1. Make the script `hack/update-all.sh` be smart and run only the scripts necessary based on the dirty files in a branch, or
2. Optimize the update-* scripts to run faster.
