- Install tools:

kubeadm

- Others:

Calico 3.0.1

The symptoms are similar to issue #39823. I tried the resolution suggested in one of the comments, (iptables -P FORWARD ACCEPT), although that seems like a hack. I'm wondering if I missed a configuration options somewhere, as it seems like the pods in my environment are not getting IP address from the pod CIDR range provided to kubeadm init. Here is a pod list:

title: CRI: Implement container log rotation

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

body:
TL;DR: We want to allow kubelet to rotate the container stdout/stderr logs, and add a CRI call to ask the runtime to reopen the log file.

kubelet decides the log directory structure and passes to the runtime the path where container log should be stored. Given the level of knowledge and control kubelet has, it is currently the best candidate to rotate the logs (vs. runtime or a separate daemon). The detailed evaluation is in the [proposal doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1oQe8dFiLln7cGyrRdholMsgogliOtpAzq6-K3068Ncg/edit?usp=sharing).

IMO, the initial version should target a simple policy of size limit per file. We can iterate and add more advanced features based on disk management in the future. The stretch goal for this release will be supporting reading logs (`kubectl logs`) from rotated log files.

As for the docker integration (i.e., `--container-runtime=docker`) that does not fully implement CRI logging, kubelet should skip log rotation.

/cc @kubernetes/sig-node-feature-requests @dchen1107 @Random-Liu @mrunalp @resouer @feiskyer

**What happened**:
The service sync loop is too aggressive and does not respect ```--service-sync-period``` as documented here https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kube-controller-manager/ nor does it default to 5 mins. Calls are spawn off immediately to cloud provider's ```EnsureLoadBalancer()```

**What you expected to happen**:
Service Controller respecting the ```--service-sync-period``` period argument 

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

1- Create a cluster on any environment (This test was done on Azure, but wouldn't be different for any cloud provider).
2- Create Service (type=LoadBalancer) via
```
kubectl run n01 --image nginx --replicas 3 
kubectl expose deployment n01 --type=LoadBalancer --port 80
```
3- Watch service creation on load balancer via ```watch kubectl get svc``` or just watch controller logs as it calls cloud provider's ```EnsureLoadBalancer()```
4- The behavior is the same when deleting a service

The test ran with a controller with ```--service-sync-period=6m``` argument

title: at large scale, kube-apiserver CPU-starves to death at 8qps of "Endpoints PATCH"

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/network
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Network.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scalability.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

body:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

/kind bug
@kubernetes/sig-api-machinery-bugs 
@kubernetes/sig-scalability-bugs 
/priority important-soon
FYI @shyamjvs @gmarek @wojtek-t 

**What happened**:

In a 5k-node cluster, the `kube-apiserver` running on a 64-core master, is unable to handle 8qps of `Endpoints` PATCH requests. Its CPU usage exceeds 60 cores for extended amounts of time, at which point kubelet's liveness checks fail, and apiserver is killed.

![repro](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/489420/34760018-559eaa80-f5de-11e7-97f3-993f3286877b.png)

In the above graph, the blue line is `kube-apiserver`'s CPU usage in cores, and the red line is the request rate of `PATCH /api/v1/namespaces/default/endpoints/endpoints-test`.

The PATCH requests above are simply fliping a single `Endpoints` object back and forth between two states: one in which it has 400 fake child addresses, and another in which it has 401 of them. There are no associated `Service`s, `Deployment`s or `Pod`s. Just mutating the `Endpoints` object is enough.

I plan to run this again to collect a profile, but I suspect it will be very similar to the one in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/55779#issuecomment-356282189 - i.e. CPU is burned in memory management due to the expensive `Endpoints` deep-copying when serving the 5000 watches from kube-proxy.

**What you expected to happen**:

For one thing, propagating `Endpoints` objects should scale better. Some ideas on improvements in this area are in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/55779#issuecomment-354453653 and two comments which follow it, and generally revolve around caching the serialized representation of `Endpoints` objects.

I think there should also be a more generic load shedding mechanism in the API server that would protect against meltdown is these kinds of problems.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

1. create a 5000 node cluster
2. log into the master and write the following files:
```
==> aa <==
apiVersion: v1
kind: Endpoints
metadata:
  name: endpoints-test
subsets:
- addresses:

==> xx <==
  - ip: 10.64.105.3
    nodeName: e2e-test-porridge-minion-group-1-3f94
    targetRef:
      kind: Pod
      name: kube-dns-6c857864fb-zrxsn
      namespace: kube-system
      resourceVersion: "30570"
      uid: 2a89ce5a-f1f4-11e7-86f6-000000000000

==> zz <==
  ports:
  - name: dns
    port: 53
    protocol: UDP
  - name: dns-tcp
    port: 53
    protocol: TCP
---

==> stress.sh <==
#!/bin/bash

function size() {
  local len=$1
  local i
  if [ ! -e "cache-$len" ]; then
    { cat aa ;
    for i in `seq $len`
    do
      sed -e "s/000000000000/$(printf %012d $i)/" xx ;
    done;
    cat zz ; } > cache-$len
  fi
  cat cache-$len
}

( echo 400 12 2.5;
  echo 400 30 1;
  echo 400 60 0.5;
  echo 400 120 0.25;
  echo 400 240 0.125;
  echo 400 480 0.0625; ) | while read size count half_delay
do
  echo "$(date -u +'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%3N'),$size,$count,$half_delay"
  rm -f cache-$size cache-$((size+1))
  for i in `seq $count`
  do
    size $size
    sleep $half_delay
    size $((size+1))
    sleep $half_delay
  done | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null
done
```
3. optional: start the following command to collect CPU usage of the API server to graph it later:
```
pid=$(pgrep kube-apiserver);prev=0;while sleep 0.2;do read f1 f2 f3 f4 f5 f6 f7 f8 f9 f10 f11 f12 f13 curu curs rest < /proc/$pid/stat;cur=$((curu+curs));if ((prev));then echo "$(date -u +'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%3N'),$cur,$prev,20.0";fi;prev=$cur;done > /tmp/cpu-$pid.csv &
```
4. bash stress.sh > 400.csv
5. optional: `kill %1` to stop CPU usage gathering

**Anything else we need to know?**:

The above may at first seem like a use case which nobody would ever exercise. However the opposite is true: an `Endpoints` is created for every `Service`, so the above scenario will happen for example when a moderately-sized (compared to cluster size) `Deployment` which exposes a `Service` is resized by a few dozen pods.

In fact this is how this problem was initially found. See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/55779 for the epic story of tracking this down from an apparent TLS connection flake in a sig-cli end-to-end test. That is why the toy `Endpoints` in the repro resembles a `kube-dns` one.

I suppose the same may also happen in case of a crashlooping `Deployment`. In that case, because of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/57405, API server will likely stay down indefinitely.

I think that with a larger `Endpoints` object, and/or more of them and/or at a higher request rate, this will also be reproducible on somewhat smaller clusters.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.10 alpha
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: GCE
- OS (e.g. from /etc/os-release): Container-Optimized OS 10032.71.0
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 4.4.86+
- Install tools: kubetest --up

body:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:
/kind bug

**What happened**:
I'm running a single node cluster on AWS EC2, ie. scheduling work on the master as well. Now that I tried to add an ELB for my service, the EC2 instance is not associated with the ELB. The ELB gets created but there are 0 EC2 instances associated with it. I'm using ELB for SSL termination, if you wonder why I'd like to load balance a single node cluster.

The service controller logs this message:

```
I0628 17:54:48.853175       1 event.go:221] Event(v1.ObjectReference{Kind:"Service", Namespace:"default", Name:"nginx", UID:"59980933-7afc-11e8-9a8c-0621b993d602", APIVersion:"v1", ResourceVersion:"2052", FieldPath:""}): type: 'Warning' reason: 'UnAvailableLoadBalancer' There are no available nodes for LoadBalancer service default/nginx
```

**What you expected to happen**:
The EC2 instance is associated with the ELB.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
- Boot an EC2 instance with correct IAM permissions
- Install a single node cluster using `kubeadm` and `cloud-provider=aws`
- Untaint the node
- Schedule eg. nginx
- Create an external load balancer for nginx
- View the ELB in AWS console and note the `Status: 0 of 0 instances in service`

**Anything else we need to know?**:
The reason for this seems to be the `node-role.kubernetes.io/master` label. [This](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/82d600bb5c34b2c7352643d4d811941e063a8215#diff-56c9c66bf151b9d7268939da6ebf3613R609) blocks associating a load balancer with the node. On the other hand [this](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/976e046f7a8d220dfd1df2e2f61d4630bcfbaf4c) changed what is included, because `includeNodeFromNodeList` did not check if a node is a master. I'm not sure what would be correct fix. I could try submit a PR, if you guide me how this should behave. Is my scenario even a supported one?

I think this bug should be reproducible on other clouds as well.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):


title: gce-scale-performance suite is failing

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

body:
I'm opening this issue as an umbrella for sharing thoughts about recent failures coming from it.

In particular:
- run 169: https://k8s-gubernator.appspot.com/build/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-scale-performance/169

This seems to be a flake cause by rescheduler. Rescheduler is implemented in a pretty inefficient way listing all pods to decide for rescheduling.
In this particular run, it send ~4k "List all pods" requests (usually it's 2-3 orders of magnitude lower).

Given that we're going to deprecate rescheduler in favor of priority-preemption in 1.12, I don't think we should spend much time on it.


- run 170: https://k8s-gubernator.appspot.com/build/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-scale-performance/170

That seems like a more serious issue (we will see if that was flake or a real issue).
A couple of observations about it:
- there is huge amount of extremely long LIST requests for *all* endpoint and service - coming mostly from DNS instances (and a couple originating from kube-proxy)
- I've seen in a log requests that took 6m+
- Looking into traces, it clearly seems that "sending response" is the step that it takes time:
```
I0622 13:42:43.247670       1 trace.go:76] Trace[65977088]: "List /api/v1/endpoints" (started: 2018-06-22 13:41:58.017796843 +0000 UTC m=+19963.167330595) (total time: 45.         229842024s):
 9166720 Trace[65977088]: [45.229839176s] [45.139721246s] Writing http response done (16408 items)
```
Even though this steps involves serializing the response, I'm fairly convinced that that's not our limiting factor - I spent some time looking into logs, and all other requests around those long requests very served pretty quickly (which suggests there wasn't any resource starvation there).
My hypothesis is network issues (or components themselves weren't able to read the data maybe due to resource starvation on their side?)

But that's not the only problem. There were also problems with individual nodes.
As an example, on node `gce-scale-cluster-minion-group-2-6k9s` Kubelet became unhealthy:
```
16:46:42.390386    1669 kuberuntime_container.go:329] getKubeletContainers failed: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
E0622 16:46:42.390721    1669 generic.go:197] GenericPLEG: Unable to retrieve pods: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
I0622 16:46:42.493526    1669 kubelet.go:1794] skipping pod synchronization - [container runtime is down PLEG is not healthy: pleg was last seen active 4m8.565421981s ago; thr     eshold is 3m0s]
kubelet.service: Service hold-off time over, scheduling restart.
Stopped Kubernetes kubelet.
Started Kubernetes kubelet.
```
That was a reason for some pods starting for a really long time.

There were also issues at the end of the test where we weren't able to delete the namespace (I guess it's because some Kubelet was down, but didn't have time to confirm that - it should be verified).

But all those issues need to be better understand.

title: If kubelet is unavailable, AttachDetachController fails to force detach on pod deletion

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

body:
/kind bug

**What you expected to happen**:
When a pod using an attached volume is deleted (gracefully) but kubelet in the corresponding node is down, the AttachDetachController should assume the node is unrecoverable after a timeout (currently 6min) and forcefully detach the volume. 

**What happened**:
The volume is never detached.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
* Create a pod with a volume using any of the attachable plugins (I used GCE PD to test).
* Stop kubelet inside the node where the pod is scheduled.
* Delete the pod.
* Wait for 6min+
* Check to see if the volume is still attached.

**Anything else we need to know?**:
This doesn't happen if the pod is force-deleted.

It's likely due to the last condition checked in [this line](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5e9a5659b751bd1d765758548273198fe8e40642/pkg/volume/util/util.go#L649). Once kubelet is down, the container  status is no longer reported correctly. Inside the Attach Detach Controller, This function is called by the pod update informer handler, which sets whether the volume should be attached in the desired state of the world. On pod force deletion, the pod object is deleted immediately, and this triggers the pod delete informer handler, which doesn't call this function.

/sig storage
/cc @saad-ali @gnufied @jingxu97 @NickrenREN 
/assign

labels.name: kind/bug

<!-- This form is for bug reports and feature requests ONLY!

If you're looking for help check [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/kubernetes) and the [troubleshooting guide](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/debug-application-cluster/troubleshooting/).

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/.
-->

**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:
@kubernetes/sig-storage-bugs 

**What happened**:
CSI spec allows for an empty fstype string.  This is intended for non-block plugins like nfs and gluster where filesystems are not separately created on the volume.
```
  // Indicate that the volume will be accessed via the filesystem API.
  message MountVolume {
    // The filesystem type. This field is OPTIONAL.
    // An empty string is equal to an unspecified field value.
    string fs_type = 1;
  }
```

The Kubernetes CSI volume source API defaults fstype to "ext4" and doesn't allow an empty string:
```
        // Filesystem type to mount.
        // Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system.
        // Ex. "ext4", "xfs", "ntfs". Implicitly inferred to be "ext4" if unspecified.
        // +optional
        FSType string
```

This makes it impossible for Kubernetes to pass in an empty fs_type to the plugin.  

**What you expected to happen**:
Since we currently leave fs creation and formatting up to the plugin, the plugin should be the one to decide the default.

<!-- This form is for bug reports and feature requests ONLY!

If you're looking for help check [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/kubernetes) and the [troubleshooting guide](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/debug-application-cluster/troubleshooting/).

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/.
-->

**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

/kind bug

/sig windows

**What happened**:

When deploying Kubernetes pods, the Linux containers will contain the following entries in the ``/etc/resolv.conf`` file:

    nameserver 10.0.0.10
    search e2e-tests-dns-x649p.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local jqfxe3n5w2rubdex0hknvvd1kf.bx.internal.cloudapp.net
    options ndots:5

However, these are not set on Windows containers; the container's DNS suffix search list is not applied. Only the "Connection-specific DNS suffix" to "svc.cluster.local" (on acs-engine 0.18.0) is set. This means that:

    - kubernetes
    - kubernetes.default
    - kubernetes.default.cluster
    - other pods / services in other namespaces
    
are not all resolvable.

For consistency with the Linux containers, the DNS suffix search list could be applied globally inside the Windows containers:

    $dnsSuffixes = @("namespace.svc.cluster.local", "default.svc.cluster.local", "svc.cluster.local", "cluster.local")
    Set-DnsClientGlobalSetting -SuffixSearchList $dnsSuffixes

**What you expected to happen**:

The following names should be resolvable:

    - kubernetes
    - kubernetes.default
    - kubernetes.default.cluster
    - other pods / services in current or other namespaces


**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Create a Windows pod:

    kubectl create namespace e2e-tests-dns-x649p
    kubectl create -f windows_pod.yaml  # https://paste.ubuntu.com/p/ZgfQS9Wgcf/

    kubectl exec -n e2e-tests-dns-x649p dns-test-2ed58282-6d85-11e8-89cc-000c29738e2c -c querier -- cmd /S /C ipconfig /all
    kubectl exec -n e2e-tests-dns-x649p dns-test-2ed58282-6d85-11e8-89cc-000c29738e2c -c querier -- cmd /S /C nslookup kubernetes
    kubectl exec -n e2e-tests-dns-x649p dns-test-2ed58282-6d85-11e8-89cc-000c29738e2c -c querier -- cmd /S /C nslookup kubernetes.default
    kubectl exec -n e2e-tests-dns-x649p dns-test-2ed58282-6d85-11e8-89cc-000c29738e2c -c querier -- cmd /S /C nslookup kubernetes.default.svc
    kubectl exec -n e2e-tests-dns-x649p dns-test-2ed58282-6d85-11e8-89cc-000c29738e2c -c querier -- cmd /S /C nslookup dns-test-service
    
    
And a Linux pod for comparison:

    kubectl create namespace e2e-tests-dns-x649p
    kubectl create -f linux_pod.yaml  # https://paste.ubuntu.com/p/kcFcfxYjm3/

    kubectl exec -n e2e-tests-dns-x649p dns-test-2ed58282-6d85-11e8-89cc-000c29738e2c -c querier -- cat /etc/resolv.conf
    kubectl exec -n e2e-tests-dns-x649p dns-test-2ed58282-6d85-11e8-89cc-000c29738e2c -c querier -- nslookup kubernetes
    kubectl exec -n e2e-tests-dns-x649p dns-test-2ed58282-6d85-11e8-89cc-000c29738e2c -c querier -- nslookup kubernetes.default

**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

/kind feature

**What happened**:

`ImageLocalityPriority` has been implemented for quite a while (PRs: #18248 #20140). But due to scheduler cache is not ready at that time, this priority is not enabled by default considering the potential performance impact. See: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/20140#discussion_r51342913

I think we can move this priority to default now. If anyone has concerns, please let me know. 

I will use this issue as a tracker.
 
The tasks in my mind includes:
- [x] Refactor the implementation with scheduler cache #63345 #63528 
   - We have a [benchmark report](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dxmQ9yDwW2NXlFu82_w4KrOsPeekj_07Zoui12Cpv20/edit#) by @silveryfu , I believe the performance concern has been addressed
- [ ] Fix inconsistency with CRI runtime #63354 (Not the target for 1.12)
- [x] Enabled this feature by default and include Integration tests ~~and e2e tests~~ #68081

title: [CustomResourceSubresources] document and codes are not the same

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
the [doc](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ed9b25c90241b2b8a1fa10b96381c57f99ca952a/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apis/apiextensions/types.go#L168) said:
```
PUT requests to the /status subresource take a custom resource object and ignore changes to anything except the status stanza.
```

However the [codes](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ed9b25c90241b2b8a1fa10b96381c57f99ca952a/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/registry/customresource/status_strategy.go#L42) are different, it does not allow to set spec and metadata, but other changes are not ignored. And updates to other parts are *not* validated.

title: Kubelet config: Validate new config against future feature gates

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
Today, Kubelet config validation is performed against the currently set feature gates. This ignores the fact that configs can modify feature gates. We should, instead, validate against the future combination of currently set feature gates and feature gates from the config. 

WRT dynamic config, this is somewhat complicated by the flag precedence rules we enforce, because until the `--feature-gates` flag is removed from the Kubelet, validation also needs to take the flag layer into account. This may mean validation has to be lifted out of the dynamic config controller (because the controller exists below the flag precedence enforcement), which complicates the config loading workflow, status reporting, etc. (alternatively, we could inject the feature gate overrides into the controller...)

This must be fixed before dynamic Kubelet config can go beta.

body:
<!-- This form is for bug reports and feature requests ONLY!

If you're looking for help check [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/kubernetes) and the [troubleshooting guide](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/debug-application-cluster/troubleshooting/).

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/.
-->

**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

> Uncomment only one, leave it on its own line:
>
/kind bug
> /kind feature


**What happened**: My [local docker cluster setup](https://sigs.k8s.io/kind) broke after https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/68890, after much debugging we discovered that the API server could not reach itself on `localhost`, further debugging showed that DNS lookups for localhost were occuring. Long story short, while we have `/etc/hosts` entries for localhost, the api server was not respecting them.

**What you expected to happen**: our standard control plane deployments should not lookup localhost via dns. they should respect /etc/hosts

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**: create a cluster and monitor network traffic. then try again after adding a minimal `/etc/nsswitch.conf` to the api server pod.


**Anything else we need to know?**: Prior art: https://github.com/gliderlabs/docker-alpine/issues/367#issuecomment-424546457

This happens because we build with go's build in DNS resolution, which respects glibc's nsswitch.conf, but we build images based on busybox for some components (like the apiserver) which does not ship with one.



**Environment**: kubernetes using [kind](https://sigs.k8s.io/kind)
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): `v1.13.0-alpha.0.1636+e9fe3f77e9b181`

/sig release

body:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

/kind bug
This is more of an enhancement.

**What happened**:
The Plugin Watcher is setup to trigger on file activities when they occur in the subdirectory that it scans. During startup, the Watcher is passed (from within the Kubelet) the Kubelet's root plugin directory as a location to scan for newly added plugins - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8346631860ca5d7253198415cf67b56183c33b49/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L789  

Because the kubelet's plugins subdirectory is also used by existing in-tree drivers (including csi) as a location to store plugins artifacts, the Plugin Watcher is getting triggered by directory/file activities occurring in that subdirectory that has nothing to do with plugin registration as shown in the output below:

title: CR validation error from 1.11 server was not correct, lacks details of errors

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: lifecycle/stale
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR has remained open with no activity and has become stale.

body:
A 1.11 server returned a CRD validation error that does not correctly split up errors by fields with individual causes:

```
{
  "kind": "Status",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "metadata": {},
  "status": "Failure",
  "message": "ProwJob.prow.k8s.io \"origin-v4.0-20180916211224-e2e-aws\" is invalid: []: Invalid value: map[string]interface {}{\"spec\":map[string]interface {}{\"agent\":\"kubernetes\", \"job\":\"release-openshift-origin-installer-e2e-aws-master\", \"pod_spec\":map[string]interface {}{\"containers\":[]interface {}{map[string]interface {}{\"command\":[]interface {}{\"echo\", \"SUCCESS\"}, \"name\":\"echo\", \"resources\":map[string]interface {}{}}}}, \"report\":true, \"type\":\"periodic\"}, \"status\":map[string]interface {}{\"prev_report_state\":\"\", \"startTime\":interface {}(nil)}, \"apiVersion\":\"prow.k8s.io/v1\", \"kind\":\"ProwJob\", \"metadata\":map[string]interface {}{\"creationTimestamp\":\"2018-09-18T06:34:55Z\", \"generation\":1, \"uid\":\"f4facbd1-bb0c-11e8-aac3-42010a8e0004\", \"selfLink\":\"\", \"clusterName\":\"\", \"name\":\"origin-v4.0-20180916211224-e2e-aws\", \"namespace\":\"clayton-test-2\"}}: validation failure list:\nmust validate at least one schema (anyOf)\nmust not validate the schema (not)",
  "reason": "Invalid",
  "details": {
    "name": "origin-v4.0-20180916211224-e2e-aws",
    "group": "prow.k8s.io",
    "kind": "ProwJob",
    "causes": [
      {
        "reason": "FieldValueInvalid",
        "message": "Invalid value: map[string]interface {}{\"kind\":\"ProwJob\", \"metadata\":map[string]interface {}{\"name\":\"origin-v4.0-20180916211224-e2e-aws\", \"namespace\":\"clayton-test-2\", \"creationTimestamp\":\"2018-09-18T06:34:55Z\", \"generation\":1, \"uid\":\"f4facbd1-bb0c-11e8-aac3-42010a8e0004\", \"selfLink\":\"\", \"clusterName\":\"\"}, \"spec\":map[string]interface {}{\"report\":true, \"type\":\"periodic\", \"agent\":\"kubernetes\", \"job\":\"release-openshift-origin-installer-e2e-aws-master\", \"pod_spec\":map[string]interface {}{\"containers\":[]interface {}{map[string]interface {}{\"name\":\"echo\", \"resources\":map[string]interface {}{}, \"command\":[]interface {}{\"echo\", \"SUCCESS\"}}}}}, \"status\":map[string]interface {}{\"prev_report_state\":\"\", \"startTime\":interface {}(nil)}, \"apiVersion\":\"prow.k8s.io/v1\"}: validation failure list:\nmust validate at least one schema (anyOf)\nmust not validate the schema (not)",
        "field": "[]"
      }
    ]
  },
  "code": 422
}
```

The `causes` array that kubectl and other clients use to display field specific errors is incorrect.  Each field should have its own `cause`, and the `field` should be a valid JSONPath pointer to the field (`status.state`).  

The summary message is also incorrect.

In general this made it almost impossible for me to debug why my object was incorrect, which is the entire point of the validation error type, so I consider this a serious usability blocker for CRD.  Validation needs to convey the field and a reasonably human readable message and be consistent with regular API object errors.

title: Kubelet does not launch static pods while waiting for bootstrapping

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: sig/auth
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Auth.

body:
The kubelet currently blocks trying to attempt to get a bootstrap client before it starts its worker loops for running static pods, which means a static pod that provides functionality on a node that bootstrapping may need (talking to an HSM, calling out externally, providing a plugin for bootstrapping, or even running a control plane pod) is blocked.  There is no actual functionality in the Kubelet that depends on this (waiting for bootstrap has no use case value), it's just a historical legacy of how the code evolved.  As people start to leverage bootstrapping and rotation, it becomes more obvious how this doesn't work in practice.

In the long run we want bootstrap credentials to be pluggable and extensible so that an HSM or other trust store on the machine can deal with the problem.  Having secret key material for bootstrapping stored on disk that allows you to join a cluster is undesirable, and having a callout to make that flow less error prone is very desirable for both cloud and metal provisioned environments.

In addition, the bootstrapping and client cert rotation flows are slightly duplicated today - using the client cert to rotate itself means that when a client cert expires (very possible with quicker rotations if the api goes down for a period of time) the bootstrap credential is consulted - but that could be arbitrarily far in the future and means we tend to fail in those cases (bootstrap credential expired).  Since the long term desire is for bootstrap to be out of process, it would be better for us to continually go back to bootstrap on cert expiration rather than retrying our flow.

For 1.13, we should fix the kubelet to not pause when bootstrapping and instead delegate to the rotation flow to provide that credential.  This has the side effect of reducing duplicated code for procuring CSRs between the two code paths, and hiding the details of client cert acquisition inside of the cert manager so that future changes can allow call outs.

@awly @mikedanese as discussed this week, @kubernetes/sig-auth-misc / @kubernetes/sig-node-bugs, @liggitt because you and discussed this, @aaronlevy because we wanted to push allow static pods for bootstrap control planes in bootkube not to block when using bootstrapping kubelets..

**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:
/kind bug

**What happened**:
I cannot have a resource which has a field named ```items``` it doesn't pass validation.
As an example I will modify sample-controller (https://github.com/kubernetes/sample-controller) and add ```items``` to ```artifacts/examples/example-foo.yaml```:

```
apiVersion: samplecontroller.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: Foo
metadata:
  name: example-foo
spec:
  deploymentName: example-foo
  replicas: 1
  items: # <-- cannot be set
  - "foo"
  - "bar"
```

after executing:

```kubectl create -f artifacts/examples/example-foo.yaml```

I receive an error:

```
The Foo "example-foo" is invalid: []: Invalid value: map[string]interface {}{"apiVersion":"samplecontroller.k8s.io/v1alpha1", "kind":"Foo", "metadata":map[string]interface {}{"name":"example-foo", "namespace":"default", "generation":1, "creationTimestamp":"2018-09-10T10:31:05Z", "uid":"9f41ebca-b4e4-11e8-ab9b-525500d15501", "selfLink":"", "clusterName":""}, "spec":map[string]interface {}{"deploymentName":"example-foo", "items":[]interface {}{"foo", "bar"}, "replicas":1}}: validation failure list:
type in spec is required
```

Validation expects that I will set a ```type``` field as well, spec below doesn't return the error:
```
apiVersion: samplecontroller.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: Foo
metadata:
  name: example-foo
spec:
  deploymentName: example-foo
  replicas: 1
  items:
  - "foo"
  - "bar"
  type: array  # <-- with 'type' it works
```

After all, in my opinion, it is a bug. I think this connected to OpenApi schema validation, that ```items``` keyword should always be in pair with ```type```.

**What you expected to happen**:
I would expect that I am able to use a field named ```items``` in CRD spec and it passes validation.
Similar to ConfigMap, it has an ```items``` field, https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-pod-configmap/#add-configmap-data-to-a-specific-path-in-the-volume.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
The easiest way is to use https://github.com/kubernetes/sample-controller,
change ```artifacts/examples/example-foo.yaml```
from:
```
apiVersion: samplecontroller.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: Foo
metadata:
  name: example-foo
spec:
  deploymentName: example-foo
  replicas: 1
```
to:
```
apiVersion: samplecontroller.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: Foo
metadata:
  name: example-foo
spec:
  deploymentName: example-foo
  replicas: 1
  items:
  - "foo"
  - "bar"
```
then execute:

```kubectl -f create artifacts/examples/crd-validation.yaml``` (it doesn't matter if you will change something here)

```kubectl -f create artifacts/examples/example-foo.yaml```

After mentioned steps, you should receive the error (btw you don't have to change the ```Foo``` structure to reproduce this)

No.

title: Conversion of Unstructured broken in apimachinery

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
Follow-up of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/68035 which uncovered deep issues with Unstructured in apimachinery:

We have conversions to `__internal` in our handlers, e.g.

- create: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5f364a0b84669a2dc086a35292db088b912d1c3c/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/create.go#L80
- update: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5f364a0b84669a2dc086a35292db088b912d1c3c/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/update.go#L93

Still CustomResource no-op conversion works, somehow. Why?

One of the reasons (possibly among others) is that
- versioning decoders do not care much about GroupVersions, but mostly about type equality of target objects, compare https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime/serializer/versioning/versioning.go#L106
- passed GroupVersion in CR decoders is effectively ignored, compare 
  - for the handler scope serializer: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5b82745cafec1b8fb0d767fc33fa4609354d2cc0/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/customresource_handler.go#L614. Decoding a CR to `__internal` 
 should fail, but doesn't.

Maybe our main problem is that we don't have rigorous apimachinery tests using `Unstructured`, but many ad-hoc patches in many places to handle `Unstructured` in a good enough way to make it work with CustomResources.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Auth.

labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

body:
ref https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/67359#issuecomment-415463989

/sig auth

The minimum supported token lifetime for projected service account tokens is 10 minutes, and renewal occurs at ~80% of token lifetime, so reloading once per minute is sufficient to ensure a reload occurs between renewal and expiration.

If reload from file fails, the last-read token should be used to avoid breaking clients that make token files available on process start and then remove them to limit credential exposure.

title: Specifying idle timeout on ELB-backed service publicly exposes an internal ELB

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/cli
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG CLI.

labels.name: sig/cloud-provider
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Cloud Provider.

body:
/kind bug

**What happened**:

When using AWS and a Service of type LoadBalancer:

If the annotation `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-connection-idle-timeout` is added to a Service that has been designated to use an internal-only ELB (via `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-internal: "0.0.0.0/0"` annotation), the ELB will be created as a public-facing ELB. 

**This is a potential security risk**, as it can expose an internal-only service to the public internet, potentially without any network ACLs.

Furthermore, the external Route53 record as specified by the `dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/external` annotations are not created when this idle timeout annotation is added.



**What you expected to happen**:

I expected the idle timeout to be applied to an internal-facing ELB.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Create a service definition like this:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  labels:
    application: proxy
  name: proxy
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-internal: "0.0.0.0/0"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: "http"
    dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/external: proxy.mycompany.com
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 80
    targetPort: 80
    protocol: TCP
  selector:
    application: proxy
```

```
% kubectl apply -f service.yaml
```

Wait for the service to finish provisioning the ELB and then observe that the internal-facing service is configured properly:

```
% kubectl describe svc proxy

Name:                     proxy
Namespace:                default
Labels:                   application=proxy
Annotations:              dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/external=proxy.mycompany.com
                          kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration={"apiVersion":"v1","kind":"Service","metadata":{"annotations":{"dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/external":"proxy.kube.webflow.services","service.beta.kuber...
                          service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol=http
                          service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-internal=0.0.0.0/0
Selector:                 application=proxy
Type:                     LoadBalancer
IP:                       100.68.210.2
LoadBalancer Ingress:     internal-aa1111111111111111111111111-222222222.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com
Port:                     http  80/TCP
TargetPort:               80/TCP
NodePort:                 http  32206/TCP
Endpoints:                100.96.249.27:80,100.97.79.3:80
Session Affinity:         None
External Traffic Policy:  Cluster
```

Now, add the `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-connection-idle-timeout` annotation to your service so that your definition looks like this:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  labels:
    application: proxy
  name: proxy
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-internal: "0.0.0.0/0"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: "http"
    dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/external: proxy.mycompany.com
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-connection-idle-timeout: 10
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 80
    targetPort: 80
    protocol: TCP
  selector:
    application: proxy
```

Delete your old service resource:

```
% kubectl delete svc proxy
```

...and give Kube/AWS a few moments to remove the ELB...

Then recreate the new service:

```
% kubectl apply -f service.yaml
```

...and wait a couple of minutes for the service and ELB to be provisioned...

Observe that the service is _not_ using an internal-facing ELB:

```% kubectl describe svc proxy
Name:                     proxy
Namespace:                default
Labels:                   application=proxy
Annotations:              kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration={"apiVersion":"v1","kind":"Service","metadata":{"annotations":{},"labels":{"application":"proxy"},"name":"proxy","namespace":"default"},"spec":...
Selector:                 application=proxy
Type:                     LoadBalancer

Port:                     http  80/TCP

NodePort:                 http  30087/TCP
Endpoints:                100.96.249.27:80,100.97.79.3:80
Session Affinity:         None
External Traffic Policy:  Cluster
Events:

  ----    ------                ----  ----                -------
  Normal  EnsuringLoadBalancer  15s   service-controller  Ensuring load balancer
  Normal  EnsuredLoadBalancer   13s   service-controller  Ensured load balancer
```

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
```
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"10", GitVersion:"v1.10.4", GitCommit:"5ca598b4ba5abb89bb773071ce452e33fb66339d", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2018-06-06T08:13:03Z", GoVersion:"go1.9.3", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
```

AWS

Linux ip-10-27-61-32.ec2.internal 4.14.63-coreos #1 SMP Wed Aug 15 22:26:16 UTC 2018 x86_64 Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8175M CPU @ 2.50GHz GenuineIntel GNU/Linux

**What happened**:
We are running `etcd` as a static pod with an HTTP liveness probe. For some reason, our `etcd` container died. The `kubelet` then attempted to restart it, but could not succeed as it could not determine that the `etcd` container was alive. title: Pod Dns Policy not implemented on Windows, leaves incomplete suffix list

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon

body:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:
/kind bug

**What happened**:
Windows pods are not getting the expected DNS suffix list. They are only getting the one for their current namespace and the Pod DnsPolicy is ignored


**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Windows pods still only get the dns search suffix for their namespace. They should also have svc.cluster.local and cluster.local so that services can be resolved for other namespaces.

Here's /etc/resolv.conf on Linux
```
kubectl exec -i busybox-sleep cat /etc/resolv.conf
nameserver 10.0.0.10
search default.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local g5hqkyfpy0nuzckf3igv405gkg.xx.internal.cloudapp.net
options ndots:5
```


Windows should have the same DNS search suffix results, but it only has the current namespace:
```
$ kubectl exec iis-1803-688b96c57b-s6657 ipconfig

Windows IP Configuration


Ethernet adapter vEthernet (f6667ee9-eth0):

   Connection-specific DNS Suffix  . : default.svc.cluster.local
   Link-local IPv6 Address . . . . . : fe80::8193:c234:bebb:93db%27
   IPv4 Address. . . . . . . . . . . : 10.240.0.136
   Subnet Mask . . . . . . . . . . . : 255.240.0.0
   Default Gateway . . . . . . . . . : 10.240.0.1
```

**Anything else we need to know?**:

- Also reported at https://github.com/azure/azure-container-networking/issues/206
- Issue #61579, PR #63905, (pending revert #66588) was an attempt to fix this, but it didn't work because the DNS server list needs to be passed to CNI, not Docker.

Also reported at https://github.com/Azure/azure-container-networking/issues/206

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.11.1
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: Azure (acs-engine v0.20)
- OS (e.g. from /etc/os-release): Windows Server version 1803

/sig windows
cc @daschott

title: Scheduler checks feasibility and scores a subset of all cluster nodes

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

body:
<!-- This form is for bug reports and feature requests ONLY!

If you're looking for help check [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/kubernetes) and the [troubleshooting guide](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/debug-application-cluster/troubleshooting/).

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/.
-->

**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:
/kind feature

Today, kube-scheduler checks feasibility of all of the nodes in a cluster for every pod in every scheduling attempt. All of those feasible pods are then scored. Our performance data shows that 90th percentile of running predicate and priority functions takes about 30ms per pod and 99th percentile is as high as 60ms/pod.

We would like to build a feature in the scheduler that once the scheduler finds a certain number of feasible nodes in a cluster, it stops and passes those nodes for scoring. This can help improve the scheduler's performance.
Such a feature must ensure that nodes from various regions and zones are considered for each pod. It must also avoid considering the same set of nodes every time, for example, it should avoid trying the first 100 nodes every time. It must instead try to consider various nodes of the cluster in different scheduling cycles.

Today, kube-scheduler checks all the feasible nodes and picks the highest score in the whole cluster. Once this feature is built, the chosen node may not be the best node in the whole cluster. The chosen node will be the highest score among those nodes found feasible.

/sig scheduling
/assign

labels.description: Indicates an issue on api area.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
In CRD OpenAPI validation we disallow `additionalProperties` in parallel to `properties`. But `patternProperties` is allowed without restriction.

But, `patternProperties: {".*": foo}` is equivalent to `additionalProperties: foo`. So we should add the same restriction to `patternProperties`, for the same reasons we had for the  `additionalProperties` case.

title: kubectl get pods.v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io fails, but should succeed

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/autoscaling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Autoscaling.

labels.name: sig/cli
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG CLI.

body:
Metrics v1beta1 resources can't be listed by kubectl 1.10.  It's probably an artifact of kind vs resource split, but this is broken and should work (this is a valid aggregated api with a valid discovery doc).

```
$ kubectl get pods.v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io
error: the server doesn't have a resource type "pods"
$ kubectl describe pods.v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io
error: the server doesn't have a resource type "pods"
$ kubectl get --raw /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/
{"kind":"APIResourceList","apiVersion":"v1","groupVersion":"metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1","resources":[{"name":"nodes","singularName":"","namespaced":false,"kind":"NodeMetrics","verbs":["get","list"]},{"name":"pods","singularName":"","namespaced":true,"kind":"PodMetrics","verbs":["get","list"]}]}
```

Expected:

kubectl get should have listed the types by trying to get custom columns for the metrics endpoint (which will be the next bug) or fall back to default display output.  This violates our rules that well formed aggregated APIs should be automatically be listable or describable via the CLI.

I consider this a 1.12 release blocker since this is a beta api that is part of the core

@kubernetes/sig-cli-bugs @kubernetes/sig-autoscaling-bugs

title: Umbrella issue - Update DropDisabled[Alpha]Fields behavior

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
Over the past several months, there have been multiple discussions about how to safely evolve API types in a way that enables safe rolling upgrade, safe single-version downgrade, and safely disabling a problematic feature even with existing persisted data.

One of the outcomes was a tweak to the guidance around how fields for disabled features are dropped and validated. https://github.com/kubernetes/community/pull/3040 contains the updated guidance.

This issue tracks sweeping the handling of existing conditional fields to follow that approach.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/70490/commits/de96583d8cc3b8ab63b53d64f7af88430e862b0f demonstrates the desired approach, and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/70490/commits/c4a02542015c9812ef0c6df9fd0c8d96dbfa902a demonstrates dropping the problematic validation.

For the specific fields below, either make them follow the same approach, or if their feature gates are getting promoted to GA in 1.14, drop the field dropping behavior and conditional validation entirely.

* Prep work
  * [x] s/DropDisabledAlphaFields/DropDisabledFields/g - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/72172
  * [x] pass new and existing object to the DropDisabledFields functions - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/72172
* PersistentVolume
  * [x] `VolumeMode` - #72251
  * [x] `PersistentVolumeSource.CSI`
* PersistentVolumeClaim
  * [x] `VolumeMode` - #72251
* StorageClass
  * [x] `AllowVolumeExpansion` - #72250
  * [x] ~~`VolumeBindingMode`~~ feature gate is unused in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/72382 instead
  * [x] ~~`AllowedTopologies`~~ feature gate is unused in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/72382 instead
* Node
  * [x] `Spec.ConfigSource` - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/72390
* Job
  * [x] `TTLSecondsAfterFinished` - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/72436
* CustomResourceDefinition
  * [x] `Versions[*].Schema` - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/72190
  * [x] `Versions[*].Subresources` - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/72190
* PodSpec
  * [x] `Priority` / `PriorityClassName` - #72171
  * [x] `Containers[*].VolumeMounts[*].SubPath` - #70490
  * [x] `RuntimeClassName` - #72184
  * [x] `Containers[*].SecurityContext.ProcMount` - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/72213
  * [x] `Volumes[*].EmptyDir.SizeLimit` - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/72371
  * [x] `Containers[*].VolumeDevices` - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/72375
  * [x] `SecurityContext.RunAsGroup` / `Containers[*].SecurityContext.RunAsGroup` - #72351
* PodSecurityPolicy
  * [x] `AllowedProcMountTypes` - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/72389
  * [x] `RunAsGroup` - #72351

title: kube-scheduler is missing permissions for delegated authentication

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: sig/auth
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Auth.

body:
**What happened**:
The kube-scheduler crashes with v1.13 as it is missing the required permissions for delegated authentication:
```
W1205 10:35:37.728989       1 authentication.go:248] Unable to get configmap/extension-apiserver-authentication in kube-system.  Usually fixed by 'kubectl create rolebinding -n kube-system ROLE_NAME --role=extension-apiserver-authentication-reader --serviceaccount=YOUR_NS:YOUR_SA'
configmaps "extension-apiserver-authentication" is forbidden: User "system:kube-scheduler" cannot get resource "configmaps" in API group "" in the namespace "kube-system"
```

kube-scheduler runs in a different kubernetes cluster.

v1.12 does not have the `--authentication-kubeconfig` flag - and it does not try to load the ConfigMap kube-system/extension-apiserver-authentication

v1.13 without `--authentication-kubeconfig` uses the in-cluster client - pointing to the wrong cluster & fails loading the ConfigMap kube-system/extension-apiserver-authentication

v1.13 with `--authentication-kubeconfig` uses the provided kubeconfig, but still fails loading the ConfigMap kube-system/extension-apiserver-authentication as the user `system:kube-scheduler` does not have the required permission to read it.

**What you expected to happen**:
1. The kube-scheduler has the correct permission by default to handle delegated authentication
2. The kube-scheduler handles this case gracefully by not serving on the secure port. See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/71743#issuecomment-444561450

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Start a v1.13.0 kube-scheduler (Not inside the cluster) with the following flags:
```
--kubeconfig /etc/kubernetes/kubeconfig/kubeconfig
--authentication-kubeconfig /etc/kubernetes/kubeconfig/kubeconfig
```

**Anything else we need to know?**:
The environment:
kube-scheduler runs in a different kubernetes cluster.

Introduced in #69663
This is a tracking issue triggered by: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/71743

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.13.0

title: k/k is the canonical source of all build artifacts.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Cluster Lifecycle.

labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.description: Issues or PRs related to the Release Engineering subproject

labels.name: sig/release
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Release.

labels.name: lifecycle/active
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR is actively being worked on by a contributor.

body:
xref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/71530

The release-repo contains aspects of the release that we know it should not own.  For example, it owns the publishing of .deb and .rpm artifacts and they are not properly maintained and versioned.  This has been the state of affairs for far too long. 

This issue exists as a tracking/umbrella issue to factor out the build artifacts such that k/k contains all the necessary tools+scripts+etc in order to build these artifacts.  Signing and publishing should likely still be a separate step.  

The following are aspirational requirements that we will need to support this effort
- [x] Investigate simplified build tooling that supports both rpm+.deb artifact building from a single conf-file (https://github.com/goreleaser/nfpm) 
- [ ] Create a builder container w/Dockerfile that can be used as part of the build.
- [ ] decouple bazel to strictly function as a variable override for a smaller set of kubernetes specific steps.  (the current state is conflating and pathological) 
    - For Example:
        - 1. conf step - nfpm.yaml.in -> bazel -> nfpm.yaml(out) 
        - 2. build step - nfpm.yaml -> (Builder Container) -> .debs & rpms. (could be linked to bazel as a separate step) 
- [ ] Update release repo to remove artifact building but to consume artifacts from the build process 
- [ ] BONUS: - Create a meta-installer container which host the rpm/deb repo to allow for a local install via local script on entry:  `e.g. docker run kubeadmer`

There are several more possible steps we could do, but this is an MVP to decouple.  

/kind feature

This came up during a recent 1.13 release team meeting.  Event delivery is not actually guaranteed, so any e2e tests that rely on events are susceptible to flakes.  These will become more evident as a cluster is under load.

We should identify which e2e tests are using this anti-pattern, and determine if there is a recipe we can use to rewrite them to be less flaky.  For example, we could likely use polling instead of waiting for an event.

Trying to set up a validating admission webhook on my GKE cluster using the following yaml:

```
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  name: test-admission-webhook
webhooks:
  - name: my-admission-webhook.io
    rules:
      - apiGroups:
          - ""
        apiVersions:
          - "v1"
        operations:
          - "CREATE"
        resources:
          - "pods"
    failurePolicy: Ignore
    clientConfig:
      url: "https://192.168.99.1:8080"
      caBundle: %%TEST_BUNDLE%%
```

And my server is still down, I can't run any pod on my cluster, getting the following error:

```
Error creating: Timeout: request did not complete within allowed duration
```

Even when I removed the `failurePolicy` field from my yaml file (which is supposed to default to `Ignore` as mentioned in the [official doc](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.11/#webhook-v1beta1-admissionregistration-k8s-io)) and I'm getting the same error.

body:
**What happened**:

I got a 404 Not Found error from the apiserver for a custom resource that exists. The 404 error only persisted for one request, after which 200s were returned as normal.

I originally observed this on GKE at the end of a control plane upgrade, but have also reproduced this using https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kind and sending SIGTERM to etcd.

**What you expected to happen**:

apiserver shouldn't return 404 for existing resources.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

1. Install [kind](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kind#installation-and-usage) and create a cluster.
1. Start a proxy for test requests:
    ```
    KUBECONFIG=$(kind get kubeconfig-path) kubectl proxy &>dev/null &
    ```
1. Start sending test requests to etcd:
    ```
    while true; do
        curl -m 1 -s -D- http://localhost:8005/apis/example.com/v1/namespaces/default/testcrs/my-test-cr
    done | grep ^HTTP | uniq -c
    ```
1. Periodically kill etcd:
    ```
    while true; do
        sudo kill $(ps ax | grep "etcd[ ]--ad" | awk '{print $1}')
        sleep 2m
    done
    ```

Because of the pod restart backoff, it may take some time to reproduce the issue: I ran for about half an hour and saw the following:

```
  16006 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
    618 HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
      1 HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
    911 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
   4213 HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
  17700 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
   6136 HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
      3 HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
  50668 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
    997 HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
      1 HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
  11817 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
   5023 HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
      1 HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
   6367 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  22570 HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```

Note the few `404 Not Found` errors occurring after the `502 Bad Gateway` errors that indicate the unavailability of etcd.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

- Kubernetes version: v1.12.2 (also observed on GKE with versions 1.10.9 and 1.11.2)

title: Changing CRD validation causes existing WATCH requests to silently hang

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

body:
**What happened**:

If you establish a WATCH request on a list of CRs, then edit the CRD's `validation` object, you will stop getting MODIFIED events on the WATCH request. The WATCH request doesn't fail or report an error, but will not return more MODIFIED events until the request is restarted.

This causes problems for custom controllers, which become unresponsive until their requests expire.

**What you expected to happen**:

Either the request should end (so it can be restarted safely) or it should continue to return MODIFIED events.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

I've attached [repro.sh.txt](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/files/2590209/repro.sh.txt). It does the following:

- Create CRD and an initial CR.
- Start a proxy, wait for it to come up, then start a watch request.
- Change the CR. (This change to the CR results in a MODIFIED event)
- Change the `validation` section of the CRD.
- Make another change to the CR. (This change to the CR doesn't result in an event).

I've tested this against GKE masters on 1.9, 1.10 and 1.11, as well as a kubeadm 1.12.2 cluster. The output looks like:

```
customresourcedefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io/testcrs.example.com created
testcr.example.com/my-test-cr created
Starting to serve on 127.0.0.1:8303
{"type":"ADDED","object":{"apiVersion":"example.com/v1","kind":"TestCR","metadata":{"creationTimestamp":"2018-11-16T17:08:48Z","generation":1,"name":"my-test-cr","namespace":"default","resourceVersion":"471","selfLink":"/apis/example.com/v1/namespaces/default/testcrs/my-test-cr","uid":"4845b766-e9c2-11e8-a427-02423c385d1a"},"spec":{"a":"asdf"}}}
testcr.example.com/my-test-cr replaced
{"type":"MODIFIED","object":{"apiVersion":"example.com/v1","kind":"TestCR","metadata":{"creationTimestamp":"2018-11-16T17:08:48Z","generation":1,"name":"my-test-cr","namespace":"default","resourceVersion":"474","selfLink":"/apis/example.com/v1/namespaces/default/testcrs/my-test-cr","uid":"4845b766-e9c2-11e8-a427-02423c385d1a"},"spec":{"a":"This change to the CR results in a MODIFIED event."}}}
The first modification has been made.
customresourcedefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io/testcrs.example.com replaced
testcr.example.com/my-test-cr replaced
The second modification has been made.
testcr.example.com "my-test-cr" deleted
customresourcedefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io "testcrs.example.com" deleted
curl: (18) transfer closed with outstanding read data remaining
```

Note that you only see MODIFIED once despite the CR being changed twice.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.11.2-gke.18, 1.12.2
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: GKE, kubeadm on amd64
- OS (e.g. from /etc/os-release): Ubuntu 16.04
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 4.15.0-36-generic #39~16.04.1-Ubuntu SMP

title: tests must use SetFeatureGateDuringTest instead of DefaultFeatureGate.Set

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to cleaning up code, process, or technical debt.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: sig/testing
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Testing.

body:
while reviewing tests in #65829, we realized some unit tests originally set up to test behavior when an alpha gate was enabled, were leaking changes to feature gates out of their packages by attempting to reset them to the old, default, disabled values.

there is a test utility that allows setting a gate to a value and automatically reverting to the original value when the test is complete:

```
defer utilfeaturetesting.SetFeatureGateDuringTest(t, utilfeature.DefaultFeatureGate, features.<FeatureName>, true|false)()
```

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/71100 added tests to ensure the packages that were leaving gates changed from their default were fixed

Once that merges, we should:
* Convert remaining instances of `DefaultFeatureGate.Set` and `DefaultFeatureGate.SetFromMap` in unit tests to `SetFeatureGateDuringTest`
* Add a verification script to ensure no new uses are added in test files and that packages that set features also run the verification test to ensure gates are unmodified on package completion
* update development/community docs to describe the right way to test feature gates


To locate offending files:
```
grep -l --include *_test.go -R 'DefaultFeatureGate.Set' .
```

To find files calling SetFeatureGateDuringTest and not deferring calling the resulting function:
```
grep  --include *_test.go -R 'SetFeatureGateDuringTest' . | grep -v defer
grep  --include *_test.go -R 'SetFeatureGateDuringTest' . | grep -v ")()"
```

/kind bug
/kind cleanup

**What happened**:
When configure Admission Webhook to use (external) url, if client authentication is enabled & configured, ValidatingWebhook requests to external AdmissionWebhook server fails because of client authentication.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. Configure /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml 
    Add --admission-control-config-file={path of admissionControlConfig.yaml} & make sure admissionControlConfig.yaml & admissionKubeConfig.yaml(contains client BASE64-encoded cert/key) can be accessed from kube-apiserver
2. Deploy AdmissionWebhook in-cluster service
3. Configure ValidatingWebhookConfiguration/MutatingWebhookConfiguration with the in-cluster AdmissionWebhook service ( using 'service' under clientConfig )
4. Now deploy some other pods. It works well. Observation on the in-cluster AdmissionWebhook REST server shows it's mutual authentication(both server & client authentication)
5. Set up an external AdmissionWebhook server (ex. https://admission.mytest13579.com:443). It loads the same clientRootCA.pem as the in-cluster AdmissionWebhook  server.
6. Set up a custom web client(in Go) and make sure it could send simulated ValidatingWebhook request to the external AdmissionWebhook server with mutual authentication
(now we are sure the client&server authentication for the external AdmissionWebhook server functions well)
7. Re-configure ValidatingWebhookConfiguration/MutatingWebhookConfiguration to use 'url' under clientConfig (cabundle is changed to the one for the external AdmissionWebhook web server as well)
8. In admissionKubeConfig.yaml, change users.name to 'admission.mytest13579.com'
9. Restart kube-apiserver
    Make sure  admission.mytest13579.com can be resolved correctly in kube-spiserver
10. Now deploy some other pods. It fails.
      => Kubectl shows logs like: 
      Error from server (InternalError): error when creating "mytest.yaml": Internal error occurred: failed calling admission webhook "admission.mytest13579.com": Post https://admission.mytest13579.com:443/validate?timeout=30s: remote error: tls: bad certificate
      => External AdmissionWebhook server shows
      http: TLS handshake error from 10.1.107.1:40682: tls: client didn't provide a certificate

If I configure kube-apiserver to not using --admission-control-config-file, ValidatingWebhook request to external AdmissionWebhook server works fine with only server authentication.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
  Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"11", GitVersion:"v1.11.3", GitCommit:"a4529464e4629c21224b3d52edfe0ea91b072862", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2018-09-09T17:53:03Z", GoVersion:"go1.10.3", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}

<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!-->

**What happened**:
I have ValidationWebhookConfiguration that checks the deployments for the availability of `spec.template.spec.tolerations` and throws an error if it does not have `tolerations`. Thus enforcing deployments to have `tolerations`. I enforce `tolerations` on staging namespaces only in order to enforce deployments to run on pre-emptive nodes. 

After I add the `tolerations` because of the above enforcement(ie.update the deployment with tolerations). The deployment maintains two of its underlying ReplicaSet. Thus keeping the old pods and new pods as well. It is important to note that I cannot simply delete old RS by --force too, it is just recreated again.

When I remove the  ValidationWebhookConfiguration, I have no problems, I can update the deployments with tolerations(or for that matter any other key/map) and the deployment maintains only one RS i.e., it has only new pods. I can also delete the old RS(if needed).

**Please find below, the ValidationWebhookConfiguration that I am using:-**
```
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  name: deny-absence-of-tolerations
webhooks:
  - name: deny.absence.of.tolerations
    rules:
      - apiGroups: ["apps","extensions"]
        apiVersions: ["v1","v1beta1","v1beta2"]
        operations: [ "CREATE","UPDATE" ]
        #operations: [ "*" ]
        resources: ["deployments","replicasets"]
    namespaceSelector:
      matchExpressions:
      - key: namespace
        operator: In
        values:
        - test-namespace
    failurePolicy: Fail
    clientConfig:
      url: "https://deny_absence_of_tolerations"
      caBundle: cabundlevaluehere 
```


**And the core part of my backend server goes like this:-**

```
  var admissionResponse = {
    allowed: false
  };

  var found = false;

  if (!object.spec.template.spec.tolerations) {

      console.log("Workload is not using tolerations");

      admissionResponse.status = {
        status: 'Failure',
          message: "On Staging/Testing please use tolerations",
        reason: " Workload ( ie.,deployment ) Requirement Failed",
        code: 402
      };

      found = true;

  };

  if (!found) {
    admissionResponse.allowed = true;
  }

  var admissionReview = {
    response: admissionResponse
  };

  res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');
  res.send(JSON.stringify(admissionReview));
  res.status(200).end();
```


 

**What you expected to happen**:
Expected behaviour of deployment i.e., deployment should maintain only one RS.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

   2).  Create a deployment(without tolerations) in a namespace(lets call it :- test-namespace)
   3).  Add validationWebhookConfiguration now to test-namespace in order to enforce tolerations.
   4).  Now update the  deployment with tolerations and apply it.
   5). As mentioned above in detail, now the ValidationWebhookConfiguration causes deployments to maintain two underlying RS at the same time

body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!-->


**What happened**:

Kubernetes readonly flags are a mess (see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/70503), and readonly flags are broken in the beta implementation of CSI.

We should explicitly define and implement what the mapping of Kubernetes readonly flags is for CSI before moving CSI to GA.

**What you expected to happen**:

*Current (CSI beta) behavior:*

1. PVC/PV access modes may be `ReadOnlyMany`.
    * PVC Access Mode
      * Set by end user.
      * Controls "required access mode" of volume to provision.
        * Passed to CSI via `CreateVolumeRequest.volume_capabilities`.
        * external-provisioner ([link](https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/external-provisioner/blob/a8d9d8dd0a1aebba48d15811e38026f53203380e/pkg/controller/controller.go#L531))
    * PV Access Mode
      * Set by provisioner: Copy of PVC access modes.
      * Used for PV/PVC binding.
      * If PV is created without error, the assumption is that the provisioned volume satisfied all the PVC access modes, so PV access mode should just be copied from the PVC access mode (https://github.com/container-storage-interface/spec/pull/82).     
2. `Pod.spec.volumes.persistentVolumeClaim.readOnly` boolean
    * Specified by end user.
    * Controls if volume is **mounted** readonly.
      * Passed to CSI via `NodePublishVolumeRequest.readonly`.
      * kubelet ([link](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/populator/desired_state_of_world_populator.go#L503))
3. `PersistentVolume.spec.CSIPersistentVolumeSource.readOnly` boolean
    * Specified by CSI provisioner: but not currently set (so always defaults to false).
      * See [link](https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/external-provisioner/blob/a8d9d8dd0a1aebba48d15811e38026f53203380e/pkg/controller/controller.go#L538)
    * Controls if volume is **attached** readonly.
      * Passed to CSI via `ControllerPublishVolumeRequest.readonly`.
      * external-attacher ([link](https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/external-attacher/blob/master/pkg/controller/util.go#L187))
4. `Pod.spec.containers.volumeMounts[x].readOnly` boolean.
    * Specified by end user.
    * Controls if last mile bind **mount** in to container is readonly
      * Controlled entirely by Kubernetes and container via CRI. Not passed to CSI.
      * See [link](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L240).

Number 3 is NOT doing the right things. Problems include:
* 3 is being used but never set -- and suffers from all the problems pointed out in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/70503#issuecomment-434876013.

*Proposal:*

1. Add new  `csiControllerPublishVolumeReadOnly` `StorageClass` parameter to CSI `external-provisioner`.
    * This will enable control of the `PersistentVolume.spec.CSIPersistentVolumeSource.readOnly` boolean for newly provisioned volumes.
2. Automatically set `PersistentVolume.spec.CSIPersistentVolumeSource.readOnly` based on PVC access mode.
    *  Specifically, if the `csiControllerPublishVolumeReadOnly` StorageClass parameter is not specified, and the PVC for which the volume is being provisioned has only one access mode `ReadOnlyMany`, then set  `PersistentVolume.spec.CSIPersistentVolumeSource.readOnly` for the newly provisioned PV `CSIPersistentVolumeSource.readOnly` to `true`.
    * This will enable more intuitive control of the `PersistentVolume.spec.CSIPersistentVolumeSource.readOnly` boolean for newly provisioned volumes.

This will fix the issue of not being able to control `CSIPersistentVolumeSource.readOnly` but the value, once set will still be immutable, and will still require user to manually create a new PV object if they want to change it.

CC @msau42 @jsafrane @vladimirvivien @cduchesne @thockin

body:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

> /kind bug

**What happened**:

At any given time, one of our apiservers will have rapidly increasing memory (and goroutine counts) until OOM.  At that time a new apiserver will start leaking memory.  This is on etcd2.  It seems very similar to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/65732 .

We believe we have identified the trigger for this as the datadog-agent leader watching events from `resourceVersion=0`.

**What you expected to happen**:

Memory and goroutines to not be leaked.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

We've not been able to reproduce directly as this requires a cluster with a large number of events.

We found three different patterns of goroutines that appear to be related to this from an affected apiserver:

