And we see log messages indicating that `w.etcdIncoming` and `w.outgoing` queues are full (e.g. `1 etcd_watcher.go:146] watch (*core.Event): 100 objects queued in outgoing channel.`)

We believe what is happening is that in the process of trying to write events to `w.etcdIncoming` from `etcdGetInitialWatchState`, `w.etcdIncoming` becomes full (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7eab6a49736cc7b01869a15f9f05dc5b49efb9fc/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd/etcd_watcher.go#L257 , first goroutine stack). The `w.translate` goroutine (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7eab6a49736cc7b01869a15f9f05dc5b49efb9fc/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd/etcd_watcher.go#L300) should be draining that channel, but we see from the second goroutine stack that that one is blocked on emit (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7eab6a49736cc7b01869a15f9f05dc5b49efb9fc/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd/etcd_watcher.go#L149) because `w.outgoing` is full.  `w.outgoing` appearing as `ResultChan()` seems to be drained from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7eab6a49736cc7b01869a15f9f05dc5b49efb9fc/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/watch.go#L190-L197 to the client.  The third goroutine stack shows that we are no longer doing that as we are stuck in `Stop()` (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7eab6a49736cc7b01869a15f9f05dc5b49efb9fc/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/watch.go#L179).  `Stop()` is waiting for the `w.stopLock` mutex that is held by the first goroutine via https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7eab6a49736cc7b01869a15f9f05dc5b49efb9fc/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd/etcd_watcher.go#L179 .

It's likely that `w.outgoing` stopped being drained when either the client closed connection or the timeout expired: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7eab6a49736cc7b01869a15f9f05dc5b49efb9fc/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/watch.go#L193-L196.

It seems that this deadlock could occur any time a client closes the connection or the timeout is reached when there are still more than 100 events to send from `etcdGetInitialWatchState`.

<!-- This form is for bug reports and feature requests ONLY!

If you're looking for help check [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/kubernetes) and the [troubleshooting guide](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/debug-application-cluster/troubleshooting/).

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/.
-->

**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

/kind bug

/sig windows

**What happened**:

When deploying Kubernetes pods, the Linux containers will contain the following entries in the ``/etc/hosts`` file:

    # Kubernetes-managed hosts file.
    127.0.0.1       localhost
    ::1     localhost ip6-localhost ip6-loopback
    fe00::0 ip6-localnet
    fe00::0 ip6-mcastprefix
    fe00::1 ip6-allnodes
    fe00::2 ip6-allrouters
    10.240.0.67     dns-querier-1.dns-test-service.e2e-tests-dns-x649p.svc.cluster.local    dns-querier-1

However, these are not set on Windows containers; the container's ``C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts`` file does not contain any entry. This can be attributed to the fact that individual files cannot be mounted on Windows containers the same way they are on Linux containers.

It can be fixed with a change to the kubelet once Windows Server 2019 has shipped, and once CRI-ContainerD is enabled on Windows. We cannot fix it for Windows Server 1803 or earlier with dockershim.

**What you expected to happen**:

The ``:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts`` file should be managed and populated by Kubelet.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Spawn a Windows pod, and check its container's ``:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts`` file.

    kubectl create namespace e2e-tests-dns-x649p
    kubectl create -f windows_pod.yaml  # https://paste.ubuntu.com/p/ZgfQS9Wgcf/
    kubectl exec -n e2e-tests-dns-x649p dns-test-2ed58282-6d85-11e8-89cc-000c29738e2c -c querier -- cmd /S /C type C:\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\etc\\hosts

Compare the result with a Linux pod's container's ``/etc/hosts`` file.

    kubectl create namespace e2e-tests-dns-x649p
    kubectl create -f linux_pod.yaml  # https://paste.ubuntu.com/p/kcFcfxYjm3/

    kubectl exec -n e2e-tests-dns-x649p dns-test-2ed58282-6d85-11e8-89cc-000c29738e2c -c querier -- cat /etc/hosts

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.12
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: N/A
- OS (e.g. from /etc/os-release): Windows Server 1803 (10.0.17134.48)
- Install tools: acs-engine v0.24.0
- Others:

body:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

/kind bug


**What happened**:

After running some tests, we're seeing that the combined usage of kubelet + docker can be around 2Gi. We need to be able to account for this in scheduling to avoid crashing these services. The first step towards this is using kube-reserved and system-reserved to avoid oversubscribing the virtual memory space available on the Windows nodes with too many containers.


**What you expected to happen**:

It should reduce node allocatable memory by kube-reserved + system-reserved.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

`kubelet.exe … --enforce-node-allocatable=kube-reserved --kube-reserved=memory=2Gi`

The Kubernetes components running on Windows (kubelet, kube-proxy) should be testable and pass conformance tests. SIG-Windows is working to fix the last known conformance test bugs for tests that make sense on Windows and get results up on testgrid.

In order to make the right tests pass on Windows nodes, we need to:

- [x] Configure the test framework to replace Linux containers with Windows equivalents (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/60848, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/61097)

- Use the same method to enable Windows-specific tests where needed (examples: #69904, #69905)

Options for test selection

1) Since there are already some tests that are Linux distro-specific, #69871 proposes to use `--node-os-distro=windows` to select the right tests
2) Add `[Linux]` to the test case titles, and use regex to ignore them
Other suggestions are welcome and will be added to this list

title: Promote CSR API out of beta

labels.name: priority/important-soon

body:
This is an umbrella issue tracking items to be discussed and dispositioned as part of promoting the CSR API to v1

* API shape/issues
  * Requires requesters to know all the info about the end certificate.
  * Use for higher-level requests (“give me a node client cert”, “give me a serving cert for a pod backing a service”).
  * Requested certificate attributes are split unthoughfully between encoded CSR and fields in request spec which create difference in semantics.
  * No clear way for signers to provide intermediates cert recipients should use (xref https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/67436)
  * No clear way for signers to indicate/distribute trust roots for issued certs
  * Current signer does not support URL SANs or issuing CA intermediates (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/80057)
* Approval flow/issues
  * Cannot limit or add components to request (limit or add SANs, usages, etc)
* Signing flow/issues
  * Method for multiple signers to interact (or approver to indicate what signer should be used)
* Guarantees on issued certificates
  * No (current) guarantee all requested extensions/SANs are issued (xref https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/64547)
  * No (current) guarantee issued client certificates will be accepted as API client certs

### Original Description

[CSR API](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tls/managing-tls-in-a-cluster/#create-a-certificate-signing-request-object-to-send-to-the-kubernetes-api) seems like an integral part of bootstrapping clusters and issuing certificates.

As of today it is possible to use CSR API on some clusters, but disable client X509 certificates on the clusters:

https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/authentication/#x509-client-certs

This makes it impossible to use the API in some cases.

This issue is a proposal to graduate CSR API out of beta and include X509 client support in the conformance suite.

title: ReplicaSetController can miss handling the deletion of a ReplicaSet

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/apps
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Apps.

body:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:
/kind bug

**What happened**:

@ncdc's description hoisted from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/69376#issuecomment-427453571:

I was about to file this. I spent yesterday triaging it and have determined the root cause. The issue is that the `ReplicaSetController` can "miss" handling the deletion of a `ReplicaSet` if things happen quickly enough. Here's the flow:

1. Client creates rs
1. `ReplicaSetController` sees new rs, starts working on creating pods
1. Client deletes rs
1. `ReplicaSetController`'s `rsInformer` see the rs deletion and calls `rsc.enqueueReplicaSet`, which adds the namespace/name of the rs to the work queue
1. Client recreates rs with the exact same name as before
1. `ReplicaSetController`'s `rsInformer` see the rs addition and calls `rsc.enqueueReplicaSet`, which adds the namespace/name of the rs to the work queue (again)
1. `ReplicaSetController`'s sync handler processes the entry from the queue
1. Because the rs was recreated with the same name, when `syncReplicaSet` calls `rsLister` to get the rs, it's there (it's the 2nd one)

This is a timing issue. The `ReplicaSetController` doesn't check the rs's UID, and if the order of operations is "just right", the controller's sync handler won't "see" the deletion, so it never calls `rsc.expectations.DeleteExpectations(key)` to reflect that the rs was deleted.

/sig apps


Original description follows:

In #69344 I had to re-run the integration test 4 times to get it to work.

Log outputs:

* [attempt 1](https://k8s-gubernator.appspot.com/build/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/69344/pull-kubernetes-integration/29684/)
* [attempt 2](https://k8s-gubernator.appspot.com/build/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/69344/pull-kubernetes-integration/29685/)

title: CSI: races in CSISkipAttach tests

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: do-not-merge/hold
labels.description: Indicates that a PR should not merge because someone has issued a /hold command.

body:
This is somewhat related to #68261.

[CSISkipAttach tests](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/860d3cb32c2b52836e1acbacb564698cbaeaacb4/test/e2e/storage/csi_volumes.go#L124) do these things:

1.
    1. Create CSIDriver CRD (in BeforeEach).
    2. (Optionally) create CSIDriver instance.
    3. Create a pod and check that VolumeAttachment was (not) created.
2. 
    1. Delete pod
    2. Delete CSIDriver instance
    3. Delete CSIDriver CRD (!!!)

What happens in A/D controller (and in kubelet too):

a. Kubelet and A/D controller create informer on CSIDriver. When the CRD does not exists, it tries periodically every second until the CRD is created.
b. When creating a pod, A/D controller looks into the informer cache if it has CSIDriver for that volume. If not, it creates VolumeAttachment.

Thing is that A/D controller (and kubelet) informer does **not** react to CSIDriver CRD deletion. It keeps watching the old CSIDriver CRD and it won't get events when new CRD and its CRs are created. So A/D controller still sees the CSIDriver created by the first test.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
With #69331 merger, run the cluster:

```
RUNTIME_CONFIG= ALLOW_PRIVILEGED=1 FEATURE_GATES="BlockVolume=true,MountPropagation=true,KubeletPluginsWatcher=true,CSINodeInfo=true,CSIDriverRegistry=true"  hack/local-up-cluster.sh -O
```

Run e2e tests:
```
go run hack/e2e.go -- --provider=local --test --test_args="--ginkgo.focus=CSI.attach.test.using.HostPath.driver"
```

In addition, the test does not give kubelet/A/DController enough time to get a newly created CSIDriver, so it's racy even if CSIDriver CRD was installed only once.

title: Race condition of securityGroup/routeTable/loadBalancer setup in Azure cloud provider

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

Azure cloud provider configures securityGroup, routeTable and loadBalancer by invoking ARM APIs. But on cluster initialization stage, it may update them even when the create operation from provisioning tools doesn't finish. Because the later PUT would cancel a previous ongoing one, this would introduce troubles for provisioning tools.

We should check the status of securityGroup and routeTable, and only do updates for them when they are in state `Succeeded | Failed | Canceled`.

Also for a running cluster, other components may also update those resources. So ETAG for each resource should be honored when the cloud provider updates them.

**What you expected to happen**:

Cloud provider shouldn't cancel operations from provisioning tools.

title: server-side apply takes ownership of fields that don't get set due to status wiping

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

labels.name: wg/api-expression
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to WG API Expression.

body:
The API server wipes status changes on calls to the normal endpoints (not /status) at the storage registry layer (right next to etcd).  This means that calls to `<resource>/<name>` can't change status.  However, if you send a server-side apply patch, the server-side apply logic still takes ownership of any fields you *try* to set, despite the fact that they don't get set.

Reproduced on HEAD (8af1bf313efeeafb94c01ce04965ad8fe9cea21a).

Reproducer: 
- Send a server-side apply patch setting any field in status to `/api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/pods/<name>`
- Observe that ownership of that field has been taken
- Observe that the field isn't set

cc #73723 
cc @jennybuckley @apelisse

title: Remove kube-proxy's automatic clean up logic

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/network
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Network.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

body:
**What would you like to be added**:
Remove any logic in kube-proxy that tries to automatically clean up proxy rules based on the proxy mode. Only attempt to clean up if `--cleanup` is set.

**Why is this needed**:
This is a continuation of a discussion from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/75377. There's a lot of complexity that comes with switching the proxy mode on kube-proxy because it tries to delete proxy rules created from other proxy modes. This has a lot of side-effects and we should be encouraging users to reboot thier nodes along with switching proxy modes. One example of this can be found https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/75360.

<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

When the Idle Timeout annotation was set to "3" which isn't a supported case, kube-controller-manager is stuck in deleting Azure LB. New service with the same name couldn't be created again even without the annotation.

**What you expected to happen**:

New service should be created successfully.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

```yaml
kind: Service
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: nginx
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/azure-load-balancer-tcp-idle-timeout: "3"
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  loadBalancerIP: "51.145.136.123"
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: http
    - name: https
      port: 443
      targetPort: https
  selector:
    app: nginx
```

```sh
kubectl create -f nginx.yaml
kubectl get svc

kubectl delete -f nginx.yaml
kubectl get svc

kubectl create -f nginx.yaml
```

title: Volumes fail to clean up when kubelet restart due to race between actual and desired state

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: lifecycle/rotten
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

body:
We have tests to delete pods while kubelet restarts, the test is a little bit flaky because the following race condition 
1. stop kubelet, delete pod gracefully and restarts kubelet
2. pod's volumes are first put into the volume desired state. Then populator will try to remove it because pod is deleted. However, it is normally failed because we check whether actual state already has the volume record or not.
3. actual state verify volume is attached and have a record of it, but it does not record it as mounted yet
4. desired state remove the volume right after step 3 happened.
5. reconciler never has a chance to umount volume because actual state does not has it as mounted (only has it as attached)

I think in step 3, we should check actual state has this volume as mounted or not, instead of just checking whether it exists or not (attached).

title: Vsphere Cloud Provider: failed to detach volume from shutdown node

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
**What happened**:
I have a pod with a pv attached to it running on node1.
When I shutdown node1 to simulate node-failure, Kubernetes detects the unhealthy node in the configured timeframe and tries to re-schedule the pod on node2 following the --pod-eviction timeout.
When trying to start the pod on node2, the pv can not be attached as it is still attached to the shutdown node1:
```
  Warning  FailedAttachVolume      6m               attachdetach-controller  Multi-Attach error for volume "pvc-db44144b-457f-11e9-a7b0-005056af6878" Volume is already exclusively attached to one node and can't be attached to another
```
Also, the pod on the shutdown node does not get deleted.

**What you expected to happen**:
As documented [here](https://vmware.github.io/vsphere-storage-for-kubernetes/documentation/high-availability.html):
The disk should be detached from the shutdown node and attached to the new node where the pod is scheduled on

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. Schedule single pod using pvc on node1
1. Shutdown node1
1. Watch FailedAttachVolume event on the new pod on node2

**Anything else we need to know?**:
Also, kube-controller-manager does not log anything about this failure.
Detachment and attachment to another nodes works fine, as long as all nodes are healthy.
Force-deletion of the pod on the shutdown node also does nothing.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.12.5
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: vsphere
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): Ubuntu 16.04
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): Linux k8s-dev-master3 4.4.0-139-generic #165-Ubuntu SMP Wed Oct 24 10:58:50 UTC 2018 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
- Install tools: Kubespray 2.8.3 using kubeadm
- Others: VSphere 6.5

Thanks in advance! :)

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/.

**Issue**: Many e2e are using optional condition fields such as Reason or Message to verify whether pod is failed or reached to the expected state having known expected reason and message. 

These are valid scenarios but we can not promote such e2e to Conformance as these Reasons and Messages may change over a period of time. 

This is observed mostly if we are expecting Pods/Jobs to get failed due to certain expected reason and message but failure may have tons of other reasons.

References:
1) https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/74979#discussion_r263207428
2) https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/75018#pullrequestreview-213817494
3) https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/60d0ec579b376b357ca6029f8cc1cd6e70a54601/test/e2e/apps/cronjob.go#L183
4) https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/apps/cronjob.go#L222
5) https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/60d0ec579b376b357ca6029f8cc1cd6e70a54601/test/e2e/autoscaling/cluster_size_autoscaling.go#L181
6) https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/60d0ec579b376b357ca6029f8cc1cd6e70a54601/test/e2e/common/init_container.go#L298 [Conformance e2e]
7) https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/60d0ec579b376b357ca6029f8cc1cd6e70a54601/test/e2e/common/init_container.go#L408 [Conformance e2e]
........

**So how such situations can be taken care while writing e2e?**
_- verifying status and message against non-empty field would resolve this issue but there would not be preciseness of e2e behavior._

<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
Some portions of the build scripts do not allow the Kubernetes version to contain semver build metadata, which is delineated using a `+`, such as `v1.13.4+foo.bar.baz`.

**What you expected to happen**:
We should allow semver build metadata.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Create a git tag such as `v1.13.4+foo` and try to get all the builds & tests to pass.

**Anything else we need to know?**:
There is also code in kubeadm that replaces all "disallowed" characters in the Kubernetes version with an underscore (`_`). This includes replacing `+` with `_`. I'm not sure if we'd want to change this, as it potentially could break people, although I'd be curious to know what disallowed characters they're using in the git tag other than `+`. Personally I'd rather replace disallowed characters with a dash `-`, but it might be too late to change things now.

title: Many ConfigMaps and Pods slow down cluster, until it becomes unavailable (since 1.12)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Cluster Lifecycle.

body:
**What happened**:

I schedule multiple jobs in my cluster. Each job uses a different ConfigMap which contains the configuration for that job.

This worked well on version 1.11 of Kubernetes. After upgrading to 1.12 or 1.13, I've noticed that doing this will cause the cluster to significantly slow down; up to the point where nodes are being marked as NotReady and no new work is being scheduled.

For example, consider a scenario in which I schedule 400 jobs, each with its own ConfigMap, which print "Hello World" on a single-node cluster would.

On v1.11, it takes about 10 minutes for the cluster to process all jobs. New jobs can be scheduled.
On v1.12 and v1.13, it takes about 60 minutes for the cluster to process all jobs. After this, no new jobs can be scheduled.

**What you expected to happen**:

I did not expect this scenario to cause my nodes to become unavailable in Kubernetes 1.12 and 1.13, and would have expected the behavior which I observe in 1.11.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

The easiest way seems to be to schedule, on a single-node cluster, about 300 jobs:

```yaml
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: job-%JOB_ID%
data:
# Just some sample data
  game.properties: |
    enemies=aliens
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: job-%JOB_ID%
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: busybox
        image: busybox
        command: [ "/bin/echo" ]
        args: [ "Hello, World!" ]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-volume
          mountPath: /etc/config
      volumes:
        - name: config-volume
          configMap:
            name: job-%JOB_ID%
      restartPolicy: Never
  backoffLimit: 4
```

I can consistently reproduce this issue in a VM-based environment, which I configure using Vagrant. You can find the full setup here: https://github.com/qmfrederik/k8s-job-repro

**Anything else we need to know?**:

Happy to provide further information as needed

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.12 through v1.13
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: bare metal
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): 18.04.1 LTS (Bionic Beaver)
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): Linux vagrant 4.15.0-29-generic #31-Ubuntu SMP Tue Jul 17 15:39:52 UTC 2018 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
- Install tools: kubeadm
- Others:

<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What happened**:
Problem found by accident during cluster stability testing. The application consumes nearly 7MB of memory per pod. 
While the helm chart was written the way that the deployment have set too low limits - see the snippet:
`containers:
......
  resources:
    limits:
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 4Mi
    requests:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 4Mi `

_A pod was started; once initialized, it started consuming more memory than the limit allowed (7MB > 4MB) and pod was deleted by the system
It was happening fast enough to cause the hosting VM crash and in case of many replicas all the worker nodes crashed within a few minutes._

**Impact**:
It will lead to whole cluster crash.

**What need to enhance for K8s**
And here's the problem: we have no control over the chart contents in this area, and logical error may lead to crash of a whole cluster. There must be some mechanism introduced, which prevents the system from such tight loop of killing and restarting pods with memory limits set incorrectly**:

**Environment**:
Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.12.2 and v1.12.2.
It shall be common issue, doesn't matter with releases.

title: Admission Webhook Review Requests Don't Include GVK in Raw Object

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
The admission webhook review requests seem not to include a GVK in the raw object.  It's included elsewhere in the review request, so it's generally not an issue, except that the unstructured codec *requires* GVKs to be present (it's not a technical requirement AFAICT, just a check done in the codec logic).  This means that trying to use `codec.Decode` or `json.Unmarshal` on an Unstructured fails.

A workaround in the mean time is to use `json.Unmarshal(data, &unstructuredObj.Object)`, but it would be nice if this just worked properly (fixes to the review request logic *and* the unstructured codec logic.

### Reproducer

<details>
<summary>server.go</summary>

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"io/ioutil"
	"net/http"
)

func main() {
	http.HandleFunc("/review", func(resp http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {
		defer resp.WriteHeader(http.StatusInternalServerError)
		bodyRaw, err := ioutil.ReadAll(req.Body)
		if err != nil {
			panic(err)
			return
		}
		fmt.Println(string(bodyRaw))
	})

	fmt.Println("starting serving at /review")
	if err := http.ListenAndServeTLS("127.0.0.1:8675", "/tmp/serving.crt", "/tmp/serving.key", nil); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
}
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>hook.yaml</summary>

```yaml
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  name: testcase
webhooks:
- name: testcase.metamagical.io
  rules:
  - apiGroups: ["*"]
    apiVersions: ["*"]
    operations: ["*"]
    resources: ["*"]
  clientConfig:
    caBundle: <ca here>
    url: "https://localhost:8675/review"
```

</details>

1. create serving CA and certs (at serving.crt and serving.key)
2. `go run server.go`
3. edit webhook with CA bundle
4. `kubectl create -f hook.yaml
5. Observe that the output object doesn't have GVK in the `object` field
6. Observe https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured/helpers.go#L324

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): master-ish (a92729a301c8928d8e108418e6e4625a9e0d6733)

/sig api-machinery

body:
Reproduced on 1.11.7 as well as master-ish (a92729a301c8928d8e108418e6e4625a9e0d6733)

Deleting a CRD doesn't seem to cause the API server to terminate watches referencing the corresponding CRs, but the watches also don't properly resume if the CRD is created again, meaning that you have to wait for watch timeouts to actually get new watch events.

We should probably kill open watches on CRD deletion, so that clients are notified and are forced to re-watch.  Either that, or seamlessly resume watches if a CRD is recreated.

### Minimal reproducer:

<details>
<summary>crd.yaml</summary>

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: testcrds.metamagical.io
spec:
  group: metamagical.io
  version: v1
  names:
    kind: TestCRD
    plural: testcrds
  scope: Namespaced
  validation:
    openAPIV3Schema:
      properties:
        apiVersion:
          type: string
        kind:
          type: string
        metadata:
          type: object
        spec:
          type: object
          properties:
            count: {type: integer}
```

</details>
<details>
<summary>cr.yaml</summary>

```yaml
apiVersion: metamagical.io/v1
kind: TestCRD
metadata:
  name: testcr
spec:
  count: 3
```

</details>

1. Create the above CRD: `kubectl create -f crd.yaml`
2. Create the above CR: `kubectl create -f cr.yaml`
3. (elsewhere) `kubectl proxy`
4. `curl localhost:8001/apis/metamagical.io/v1/testcrds` and grab a resource version
5. (elsewhere) `curl localhost:8001/apis/metamagical.io/v1/testcrds?watch=1&resourceVersion=<above>`
6. `kubectl delete -f cr.yaml`
7. `kubectl delete -f crd.yaml`
8. `kubectl create -f crd.yaml`
9. `kubectl create -f cr.yaml`
10. Observe the lack of watch events

After watches time out, things can re-establish, but that can be a while.

**What happened**:

**What you expected to happen**:

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): HEAD (commit: 08d05227303b8f0b7d9c203c7d942788df1cbc97)
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: GCE
- OS (e.g. from /etc/os-release): Windows 1803, Windows 1809
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Others:

High cpu usage on the Windows nodes:
```
PS C:\> Get-Counter '\Process(*)\% Processor Time' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty countersamples| Select-Object -Property instancename, cookedvalue,path| ? {$.instanceName -notmatch "^(idle|_total|system)$"} | Sort-Object -Property cookedvalue -Descending| Select-Object -First 25| ft InstanceName,@{L='CPU';E={($.Cookedvalue/100/$env:NUMBER_OF_PROCESSORS).toString('P')}} -AutoSize

InstanceName CPU
------------ ---
powershell   71.15%
powershell   13.07%
powershell   5.08%
powershell   4.36%
msmpeng      2.90%
powershell   2.90%
services     0.73%
kubelet      0.00%
```

Multiple processes running `Get-NetAdapterStatistics`
```
PS C:\> Get-WmiObject Win32_Process | Select-Object CommandLine | Select-String powershell

@{CommandLine=powershell}
@{CommandLine=powershell /c " Get-NetAdapterStatistics | ConvertTo-Json"}
@{CommandLine=powershell /c " Get-NetAdapterStatistics | ConvertTo-Json"}
@{CommandLine=powershell /c " Get-NetAdapterStatistics | ConvertTo-Json"}
@{CommandLine=powershell /c " Get-NetAdapterStatistics | ConvertTo-Json"}
```
I can reproduce this reliably when creating windows 1803 or 1809 nodes in GCE. 

PR #70121 added support for network stats on Windows by calling `powershell /c Get-NetAdapterStatistics | ConvertTo-Json`. 
This function will be called every time kubelet gets queried for stats (`/stats/summary`, `/metrics`). Monitoring agents usually call periodically (e.g., 10s, 60s), etc. Kubelet itself also queries this to perform important functions such as eviction. I patched kubelet to disable the network stats on Windows, and was able to verify that the patch fixed the issue.

I'm not sure why `Get-NetAdapterStatistics` can be so slow and consuming so much CPU. @PatrickLang, @adelina-t have you seen this when testing on Azure. I assume the CI test job is using the latest kubelet binary with network stats.

Regardless, we'd need to cache the information since users can easily overload kubelets/nodes by querying the stats. /cc @feiskyer 

/cc @kubernetes/sig-windows-bugs 
/cc @pjh @jingxu97 @mtaufen 
/cc @dashpole

title: Operations on custom resources with multiple versions fails when validating and mutating web hooks are configured on it

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
**What happened**:

Here is a brief explanation of my environment (I'll explain how to reproduce it in the relevant section below):

I'm on the latest stable 1.13, which is 1.13.2. I'm using `microk8s` to be able to test this on multiple versions.

I have both a ValidationWebHookConfiguration and mutatingWebHookConfiguration defined.

ValidatingWebhookConfiguration:
```
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  name: application-validation-webhook-configuration
webhooks:
- clientConfig:
    caBundle: 
    service: null
    url: https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/validate-applications
  name: applications.shipper.booking.com
  failurePolicy: Ignore
  rules:
  - apiGroups:
    - '*'
    apiVersions:
    - '*'
    operations:
    - CREATE
    - UPDATE
    resources:
    - applications

```

MutatingWebhookConfiguration:

```
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: MutatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  name: application-mutation-webhook-configuration
webhooks:
- clientConfig:
    caBundle: 

    service: null
    url: https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/mutate-applications
  failurePolicy: Ignore
  name: applications.shipper.booking.com
  rules:
  - apiGroups:
    - '*'
    apiVersions:
    - '*'
    operations:
    - CREATE
    - UPDATE
    resources:
    - applications
```

I also have a CRD, which defines multiple versions. `v1` is the older version which we were using before Kubernetes supported versioning. Now that Kubernetes allows us to define multiple versions, we want to move to `v1alpha1`. That's why you will see the object being _served_ as `v1`, but not _stored_ as `v1`:

```
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: applications.shipper.booking.com
spec:
  additionalPrinterColumns:
  - JSONPath: .metadata.creationTimestamp
    description: |-
      CreationTimestamp is a timestamp representing the server time when this object was created. It is not guaranteed to be set in happens-before order across separate operations. Clients may not set this value. It is represented in RFC3339 form and is in UTC.

      Populated by the system. Read-only. Null for lists. More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/api-conventions.md#metadata
    name: Age
    type: date
  conversion:
    strategy: None
  group: shipper.booking.com
  names:
    categories:
    - all
    - shipper
    kind: Application
    listKind: ApplicationList
    plural: applications
    shortNames:
    - app
    singular: application
  scope: Namespaced
  validation:
    openAPIV3Schema:
      properties:
        spec:
          properties:
            template:
              properties:
                clusterRequirements:
                  properties:
                    capabilities:
                      items:
                        type: string
                      type: array
                    regions:
                      items:
                        type: object
                      type: array
                  required:
                  - regions
                  type: object
                strategy:
                  properties:
                    steps:
                      items:
                        properties:
                          capacity:
                            properties:
                              contender:
                                maximum: 100
                                minimum: 0
                                type: integer
                              incumbent:
                                maximum: 100
                                minimum: 0
                                type: integer
                            required:
                            - incumbent
                            - contender
                            type: object
                          name:
                            type: string
                          traffic:
                            properties:
                              contender:
                                minimum: 0
                                type: integer
                              incumbent:
                                minimum: 0
                                type: integer
                            required:
                            - incumbent
                            - contender
                            type: object
                        required:
                        - name
                        - traffic
                        - capacity
                        type: object
                      type: array
                  required:
                  - steps
                  type: object
                values:
                  type: object
              required:
              - clusterRequirements
              - strategy
              - values
              type: object
          required:
          - template
          type: object
  version: v1alpha1
  versions:
  - name: v1alpha1
    served: true
    storage: true
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: false
```

Now, if you create an Application like this:

```
  apiVersion: shipper.booking.com/v1alpha1
  kind: Application
  metadata:
    name: super-server
  spec:
    revisionHistoryLimit: 3
    template:
      chart:
        name: nginx
        repoUrl: https://storage.googleapis.com/shipper-demo
        version: 0.0.1
      clusterRequirements:
        regions:
        - name: local
      strategy:
        steps:
        - capacity:
            contender: 1
            incumbent: 100
          name: staging
          traffic:
            contender: 0
            incumbent: 100
        - capacity:
            contender: 100
            incumbent: 0
          name: full on
          traffic:
            contender: 100
            incumbent: 0
      values:
        replicaCount: 3
```

Now, if you restart the server and try to edit this application with `kubectl edit app super-server` (noting that the file you're editing has the version as `v1` and not `v1alpha1`), you will get an error like this:

```
Internal error occurred: no kind "Application" is registered for version "shipper.booking.com/v1" in scheme "k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/apiserver.go:52"
```

Now, if you do the same edit, but change the version to `v1alpha1` by hand, all subsequent patches to this object will work without a problem, until the next restart.

The restart is very important: this problem is 100% reproducable after a restart. We have observed it happening in production as well, but the way to reproduce it without waiting for it to happen is to restart `kube-apiserver` and edit the application with `kubectl edit app super-server`.

Here is what we've found through our testing:

1. As I said before, this happens 100% after a restart.
2. Changing the version to `v1alpha1` by hand while editing causes `kubectl` to send a patch to the `v1alpha1` endpoint instead of the `v1` endpoint, and from then on there won't be any problems interacting with this object.
3. Step number 2 works per object only. In other words, if you do step 2 for `app1` and not `app2`, `app1` will not have a problem but `app2` will have problems.
4. If you add `namespaceSelectors` to the ValidatingWebhookConfiguration and MutatingWebhookConfiguration so that they don't apply to your Application objects anymore, it will solve the problem for all the objects in this cluster. This issue will not occur again for an indeterminable amount of time if you remove the `namespaceSelectors`. In other words, if you remove the `namespaceSelectors`, we've observed that the issue will happen, but within weeks or days.

Note that step 4 will fix the issue for *all* Applications, while step 2 will fix it for *only one* Application object.

**What you expected to happen**:

Sending a patch request to the `v1` endpoint should convert the object to `v1alpha1` and store it as `v1alpha1` instead of throwing an error about the version not defined. Also, having a ValidatingWebhookConfiguration and MutatingWebhookConfiguration shouldn't cause this to happen.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

1. Use microk8s to get the latest Kubernetes version.
2. Download the attached tarball and untar it with `tar -xzf v1alpha1.tar.gz`
3. `cd` into the directory, and set up your environment by running the following commands:
    
    ```
    $ kubectl apply -f v.yaml
    $ kubectl apply -f m.yaml
    $ kubectl apply -f app-crd.yaml
    ```
    
4. Run the script called `test-kubernetes-application-bug.sh` which will reproduce the problem for you. Basically, you can also create an Application object with whatever version you like, restart the server, and edit it with `kubectl` to add a label.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.13.2
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g. from /etc/os-release): CentOS 7
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 3.10.0-862.14.4.el7.x86_64
- Install tools: microk8s
[v1alpha1.tar.gz](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/files/2832903/v1alpha1.tar.gz)

- `[sig-storage] CSI Volumes [Driver: pd.csi.storage.gke.io][Serial] [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (filesystem volmode)] volumeMode should create sc, pod, pv, and pvc, read/write to the pv, and delete all created resources`

**Since when has it been failing**:
January 31st, 2019

**Testgrid link**:
https://gubernator.k8s.io/build/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-new-master-upgrade-cluster-new-parallel/1176

**Reason for failure**:
Seem to be different versions of timeouts:

PersistentVolumeClaims [pvc-9447w] not all in phase Bound within 5m0s
```

```
timed out waiting for the condition

```
Gave up after waiting 5m0s for pod "pod-subpath-test-pd-csi-storage-gke-io-dynamicpv-rwlf" to be "success or failure"
```

```
Gave up after waiting 5m0s for pod \"csi-injector-22rh\" to be \"success or failure\""
```

**Anything else we need to know**:
- Coincides with the test-infra commit 1c0a3d856 ([diff since last passing commit](https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/compare/e62114bdc...1c0a3d856))
- Some sig-cluster-lifecycle tests started failing at the same time (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/73705)

cc @mortent @kacole2 @alejandrox1 @smourapina

body:
/sig api-machinery
/kind bug

@kubernetes/sig-api-machinery-bugs 

One controller revision can be un-updatable if its content's order isn't forced by k/k codec stack

**What happened**:

Initially I found some error logs in garbage-collector/kube-controller-manager which was trying to orphaning a ControllerRevision to perform a cascading deletion:


> {"kind":"Status","apiVersion":"v1","metadata":{},"status":"Failure","message":"ControllerRevision.apps \"holiday-78b7ffcd54\" is invalid: data: Invalid value: runtime.Unknown{TypeMeta:runtime.TypeMeta{APIVersion:\"\", Kind:\"\"}, Raw:[]uint8{0x7b, 0x22, 0x61, 0x66, 0x66, 0x69, 0x6e, 0x69, 0x74, 0x79, 0x22.....<omitted>... ContentEncoding:\"\", ContentType:\"application/json\"}: field is immutable","field":"data"}]},"code":422}

but actually it wasn't trying to update any content but `ownerReferences` in that controller revision, and the patch request body was:

> {"metadata":{"ownerReferences":[{"$patch":"delete","uid":"e620de7e-26aa-11e9-9276-00163e000b8d"}],"uid":"e628e563-26aa-11e9-9e54-00163e000652"}} 

After digging into the error and i find that the update validation is failing b/c the data content in controller revision is re-ordered when it's deserialized from storage. here i caught their dumps by adding some logs:

the old controllerRevision.Data in the failing update validation:

> "{"containers":[{"name":"holiday","image":":20190130003346413-master.01fc4fb8","resources"
:{"limits":{"cpu":"1","memory":"1Gi"},"requests":{"cpu":"500m","memory":"512Mi"}},"terminationMessagePolicy":"File","imagePullPolicy":"Always"}],"restartPolicy":"Always","
terminationGracePeriodSeconds":30,"dnsPolicy":"Default","securityContext":{},"affinity":{"nodeAffinity":{"requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution":{"nodeSelectorTerms":[{"matchExpre
ssions":[{"key":"failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/cell","operator":"In","values":["",""]}]}]}}},"schedulerName":"default-scheduler"}"

the new controllerRevision.Data in the failing update validation:

> {"affinity":{"nodeAffinity":{"requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution":{"nodeSelectorTerms":[{"matchExpressions":[{"key":"failure
-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/cell","operator":"In","values":["",""]}]}]}}},"containers":[{"image":":2019013000
3346413-master.01fc4fb8","imagePullPolicy":"Always","name":"holiday","resources":{"limits":{"cpu":"1","memory":"1Gi"},"requests":{"cpu":"500m","memory":"512Mi"}},"terminati
onMessagePolicy":"File"}],"dnsPolicy":"Default","restartPolicy":"Always","schedulerName":"default-scheduler","securityContext":{},"terminationGracePeriodSeconds":30}"

The content of that controller revision wasn't decoded by k/k's codec stack, and it's just roughly decoded by calling `json.Unmarshal`. so the `containers` field is placed before the `affinity` but when it is deserialized again by apiserver in memory, the order changed as is shown above.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Just create a controller revision w/ direct HTTP call (instead of creating via `kubectl`) and w/ a json body:

```json
{
  "apiVersion": "apps/v1",
  "kind": "ControllerRevision",
  "metadata": {
    "name": "test2-holiday-78b7ffcd54",
    "namespace": "default"
  },
  "data": {
    "containers": "foo",
    "affinity": "bar"
  },
  "revision": 1
}
```

👿then any update on this object will fail due to the order forced by k/k codec stack

title: Long running request definition in the kube-aggregator

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

body:
Kube-API server has a set of long-running pattern check defined [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8b98e802eddb9f478ff7d991a2f72f60c165388a/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/server.go#L408-L411) that are applied to the operations taking longer than the default timeout of 60 seconds. 
Unfortunately, our kube-aggregator has hard-coded the same configuration [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8b98e802eddb9f478ff7d991a2f72f60c165388a/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/cmd/server/start.go#L127-L130) which makes it impossible for other API servers to define their own endpoints that will allow long running requests.

There are several possible solutions that I can think of at this point in time:
1. kube-aggregator will always just passes through and does not define long-running checks at all. The downside of this approach is that we always rely on the remote API server to behave properly and does not provide the safety net we currently have.
2. kube-aggregator is notified about long-running endpoints from remote API servers. This leaves the safety net I've mentioned before, at the cost of additional complexity which defines long-running requests endpoints.

@deads2k @sttts

**What happened**:

When running a container with `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` the pid 1 process and its children have `NoNewPrivs:     1`. If I start an additional process in the same container using exec, the flag is set to 0.

**What you expected to happen**:

Processes started by exec should share the same settings as defined for the pid 1 process. This is true for capabilities for example.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: privs-test
spec:

  - name: busybox

**What happened**:
I deployed Kubernetes v1.11.5 and v1.13.0 using kubespray.

After doing this, I ran conformance tests using [heptio's kube-conformance image](https://console.cloud.google.com/gcr/images/heptio-images/GLOBAL/kube-conformance) (v1.11 and v1.13, respectively.

When I ran the conformance tests, the following two test cases failed after a 10 minute timeout period:

* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5818be6205c38936e1218609e29e524a9e35e063/test/e2e/network/dns.go#L44
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5818be6205c38936e1218609e29e524a9e35e063/test/e2e/network/dns.go#L75

The failure output looks like the following:
```
TODO: (accidentally deleted my previously-saved test results)
```

I believe that the problem is here:
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/56e88f5b47da3dfc0a95e0bc9be6a0c6c3275345/test/e2e/network/dns_common.go#L515-L522

The reason I believe this to be the problem is that it looks like that request builder is not adding a query parameter to specify the container from which to retrieve test results even though there are three containers running in the dns test pod:
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5818be6205c38936e1218609e29e524a9e35e063/test/e2e/network/dns_common.go#L397-L437

I expected the tests to pass since I have run them in the past against clusters provisioned with tectonic.

body:
This is a follow-up to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/72169 to sweep API object validation to remove conditional logic that can cause problems for existing objects across skewed API servers, or if a feature gate is disabled after having been enabled.

This is the list of feature gates that are currently checked in validation, and the work required to make them safe for skewed apiserver scenarios:

title: Rethink pod affinity/anti-affinity

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scalability
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scalability.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

body:
Pod Affinity/AntiAffinity is causing us a bunch of pain from performance/scalability perspective.

Although scheduling SIG has done tremendous effort to improve it, it's still the very significant (most?) factor for scheduling throughput.

The reason why this is so painful, is that it is cluster-wide function, i.e. we need to know the state of the whole cluster to compute feasibility/priority of a single node. This is unique (I'm consciously ignoring aggregation in priority function (e.g. normalization based on scores of all nodes), which is the only other exception) and this is the reason of our issues.

I think that in order to significantly improve throughput, we need to somehow strenghten this predicate/priority.

(I know it will be painful due to deprecation process), but here I propose that we say that the only allowed topology for pod affinity/anti-affinity is "node".

What would this buy us:
- computations of feasibiliyt/priority of a node is local to that node only
- we can fully parallelize all the computations across nodes

What do we lose:
- the predicate/priority is no longer generic
However, I claim that this function (as is) is not super useful in a generic case (the usecase is spreading across failure domains). And given that predicate is "at most one per FD" (not spread ~evenly), it's not generic enough to solve many cases.

I think that if we would strenghten pod affinity/anti-affinity topology to be always "node" and in addition to that will introduce "spread evenly" function, that would be more beneficial.

Thoughts?


/kind feature
/sig scheduling

@davidopp @bsalamat @kubernetes/sig-scheduling-feature-requests

title: [Feature:FSQuota] Ensure projects are reflected in /etc on kubelet startup

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: lifecycle/rotten
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

body:
In some OS configurations, `/etc` is reset upon node reboots.  It is conventional to record projects being used in `/etc/projects` and `/etc/projid` to allow actors on the node to avoid project id collisions, so losing information in `/etc` could potentially allow project id collisions to occur.

Currently, [Quotas for Ephemeral Storage](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-node/20180906-quotas-for-ephemeral-storage.md) will only use a project if it has no recorded usage (and thus hasn't been applied to a directory).  This means that the kubelet is guaranteed to never re-use projects it has placed on empty-dir volumes _even if the contents of /etc are wiped_.  However, if other actors on the node use project quotas and only check `/etc/projects` and `/etc/projid`, they may collide with the kubelet's projects if /etc is wiped.

To fix this corner case, the kubelet should record the projects it has applied to empty-dir volumes in  `/etc/projects` and `/etc/projid` after a restart.

cc @RobertKrawitz

1. No entry was written for ``AuthenticatedWindowsNanoServer``, causing one of the tests to try to spawn a pod with the image name ``/``.
2. The registry set for ``WindowsNanoServer`` was ``e2eRegistry``, which is set to a dockerhub registry (``e2eteam``) in all sig-windows jobs, which is not the purpose of the test itself (the test tries to spawn a pod using an image from gcr.io). The reason why ``e2eRegistry`` is set to ``e2eteam`` is because that registry contains the Windows images needed for all the Kubernetes E2E tests.

**Anything else we need to know**:

/sig windows

body:
@mborsz (SIG Scalability) started a [thread](https://groups.google.com/d/topic/kubernetes-sig-scale/6V60w-ABYCw/discussion) to inquire if we had a mechanism for revert-only approvers, which as far as I know isn't something that exists today.

I haven't seen policy on graduating into the top-level OWNERS file, but as stated in the SIG Scalability charter and mentioned by @mm4tt:
> We can rollback any merged PR if it has been identified as a cause of any performance/scalability SLOs regression (identified by the set of release blocking scalability/performance tests). The offending PR should only be merged again after proving to pass tests at scale.

So they should have this power.

Suggestion:
- Add to `OWNERS_ALIASES`:
  - `revert-approvers`
  - `sig-scalability-approvers`
  - `sig-scalability-reviewers`
- Add aforementioned groups to top-level reviewers and approvers stanzas

Additionally, I think we should also use the opportunity to [prune/update the current top-level reviewers/approvers](https://groups.google.com/d/topic/kubernetes-dev/B7fsNnR3Rxw/discussion).

I'm assigning the current top-level approvers to this for advice on policy, nominations for new reviewers/approvers, and suggestions on who to remove.

title: Upgrade tests do not check pod instances and restart counts are identical for workload objects

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Testing.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

body:
**What happened**:

An upgrade of only the API server should not result in pod recreations or container restarts.

Today, this can accidentally be triggered by introducing new defaults to types within PodSpec (c.f. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/69988, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/69445, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/78633).

The workload upgrade tests do not currently check if pod instances and container restart counts are identical.

**What you expected to happen**:

At the end of the upgrade test setup step, record the pod instances for the workload object in question, their uids, container restart counts, and associated node names and versions.

In the verification step post-upgrade, if the associated nodes still exist at the same versions, verify the same pod instances still exist with the same container restart counts.

For bonus points, an unrelated update (e.g. adding an annotation to the workload object) should be performed, to verify that no defaults are added in the update path that would result in a spurious rollout of new pods.

(note that test/e2e/upgrades tests are not currently running at all, see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/94487)

/sig testing
/sig apps
/priority important-soon

title: Flexvolume master driver is blocking controller-manager from moving to distroless

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

labels.name: area/dependency
labels.description: Issues or PRs related to dependency changes

body:
There is an effort underway to move to core k8s component images to distroless. One side effect is that shell access is unavailable inside these containers.

Dummy Flexvolume drivers in e2e tests are written as shell scripts, and it's possible that many drivers are written this way as well. These drivers are a problem for controller managers going distroless - the driver Init() call will fail.

Going forward here are some of the possible options:
1. Don't move to distroless for controller manager
2. Deprecate Flex (but we've already issued a statement that k8s 1.x is always going to support Flex)
3. Limit Flexvolume support on master to only drivers that don't require shell
4. Ban Flexvolume master installations.

If distroless for controller manager is a definite requirement, #3 sounds the most reasonable. Translating the Flexvolume API from shell to a different language shouldn't be too bad, and presumably drivers running in production already have something written in non-shell.

SIG storage what do you think?

/sig storage
/cc @yuwenma @tallclair @saad-ali @chakri-nelluri 
/priority important-soon

title: Some CRDs that duplicate built-in group/version/kinds reap built-in etcd data on deletion

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

body:
**What happened**:

Created a CRD:
```
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: foos.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  scope: Namespaced
  version: v1
  names:
    singular: foo
    plural: foos
    kind: Foo
    listKind: FooList
```

Created another CRD defining an overlapping type with CustomResourceDefinition:
```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: customresourcedefinitions.apiextensions.k8s.io
spec:
  group: apiextensions.k8s.io
  version: v1beta1
  scope: Cluster
  names:
    plural: customresourcedefinitions
    singular: customresourcedefinition
    kind: CustomResourceDefinition
    listKind: CustomResourceDefinitionList
  validation:
    openAPIV3Schema:
      type: object
      properties:
        readonly:
          type: boolean
```

Verify both exist:
```
$ kubectl get crds
NAME                                             CREATED AT
customresourcedefinitions.apiextensions.k8s.io   2019-06-04T19:37:46Z
foos.example.com                                 2019-06-04T19:48:35Z
```

Deleted the one overlapping with the in-tree CRD type:
```
kubectl delete crd/customresourcedefinitions.apiextensions.k8s.io --wait=false
```

Verify only the overlapping CRD remains:
```
$ kubectl get crd
NAME                                             CREATED AT
customresourcedefinitions.apiextensions.k8s.io   2019-06-04T19:37:46Z
```
and is stuck deleting:
```
$ kubectl get crd -o yaml
...
  status:
    conditions:
    ...
    - lastTransitionTime: "2019-06-04T19:49:40Z"
      message: CustomResource deletion is in progress
      reason: InstanceDeletionInProgress
      status: "True"
      type: Terminating
```

**What you expected to happen**:

Creation and deletion of the overlapping type CRD would have no effect on the in-tree data.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

The only types in the kube-apiserver (currently) that store data under a group prefix are:
* APIService (`<prefix>/apiregistration.k8s.io/apiservices/...`)
* CustomResourceDefinition (`<prefix>/apiextensions.k8s.io/customresourcedefinitions/...`)
* Custom resources (`<prefix>/<group>/<pluralResource>/...`)

When a CRD is deleted, all instances of the type it defines are first removed. That means that defining and deleting a CustomResourceDefinition that defines an overlapping APIService or CustomResourceDefinition type will remove existing APIService or CustomResourceDefinition data.

We can special-case these two resources in the CRD deletion code, but we need a more robust solution before CRD v1.

/cc @sttts @deads2k @jpbetz 
/sig api-machinery
/priority important-soon
/area custom-resources

Created a CRD with a group/version/kind that defines a CustomResourceDefinition type overlapping with the in-tree kubernetes type (**WARNING**: do not create this CRD on a cluster you care about, see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/78707)

kubectl get --raw /openapi/v2 | \

In CamelCase. More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/api-conventions.md#types-kinds",
>       "type": "string"
>     },
>     "metadata": {
>       "$ref": "#/definitions/io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1.ObjectMeta"
>     },
>     "spec": {
>       "description": "Spec describes how the user wants the resources to appear",
>       "$ref": "#/definitions/io.k8s.apiextensions-apiserver.pkg.apis.apiextensions.v1beta1.CustomResourceDefinitionSpec"
>     },
>     "status": {
>       "description": "Status indicates the actual state of the CustomResourceDefinition",
>       "$ref": "#/definitions/io.k8s.apiextensions-apiserver.pkg.apis.apiextensions.v1beta1.CustomResourceDefinitionStatus"
>     }

>       "kind": "CustomResourceDefinition",

>     }
>   ]
> }
> ```

```sh
kubectl get --raw /openapi/v2 | \
  jq '.definitions["io.k8s.apiextensions.v1beta1.CustomResourceDefinition"]'
```

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "apiVersion": {
      "description": "APIVersion defines the versioned schema of this representation of an object. Servers should convert recognized schemas to the latest internal value, and may reject unrecognized values. More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/api-conventions.md#resources",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "kind": {
      "description": "Kind is a string value representing the REST resource this object represents. Servers may infer this from the endpoint the client submits requests to. Cannot be updated. In CamelCase. More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/api-conventions.md#types-kinds",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "metadata": {
      "description": "Standard object's metadata. More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/api-conventions.md#metadata",
      "$ref": "#/definitions/io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1.ObjectMeta"
    },
    "readonly": {
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  },
  "x-kubernetes-group-version-kind": [
    {
      "group": "apiextensions.k8s.io",
      "kind": "CustomResourceDefinition",
      "version": "v1beta1"
    }
  ]
}
```

Because both specify a `x-kubernetes-group-version-kind`, and do not overlap in their generated definition type name, both are published in openapi (even though the handler for the CRD-defined one is not actually used to serve that group/version/kind)

**What you expected to happen**:

published openapi only includes the in-tree type, which has precedence

body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
When a client's oidc token has expired, even on passing the latest token to create a client, newOIDCAuthProvider() returns the old client with the expired tokens.

In https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/79226fe1949a01066ee9e3a3f4c53546d72e1194/plugin/pkg/client/auth/oidc/oidc.go#L122
newOIDCAuthProvider()

Cached Client is retrieved as shown below

// Check cache for existing provider.
if provider, ok := cache.getClient(issuer, clientID); ok {
return provider, nil
}

However, when after token expiration, when we make a new call to create a client, the refresh token would be different. Since we use (key := cacheKey{issuer, clientID}) as cached key in this case it will still return old token.

**What you expected to happen**:
On passing the new refresh token, the code should return new client

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. Create a go-client to a cluster with oidc based auth
2. Use the client for cluster based operations, this verifies client works.
3. Do not stop the process using the client.
4. After the token expiry, the code will use the new Kubeconfig with the new token to create a new client.
5. Use the client for cluster based operation. It will fail with token expired error.


**Anything else we need to know?**:
Similar issue opened few years back.
https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/issues/268

**Environment**:
- Go client version.
    `@k8s.io/client-go` v11.0.0
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
  1.14.1
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
  Ubuntu
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
 4.15.0-1037-aws

title: RemainingItemCount is serialized in proto messages even when unset

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
**What happened**:
As part of [adding skew testing for serialized API responses](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/78309), we discovered a diff in serialized proto responses when roundtripping data from 1.14:

```
    --- FAIL: TestRoundTripExternalTypes/.v1.Status (0.02s)
        --- FAIL: TestRoundTripExternalTypes/.v1.Status/fixtures-v1.14.0 (0.02s)
            fixtures.go:195: proto data differed from fixture
            fixtures.go:205: fixture vs reserialized:
                  strings.Join({
                  	... // 7 identical lines
                  	`    2: "8551505577692297499"`,
                  	`    3: ""`,
                + 	"    4: 0",
                  	"  }",
                  	"  2 {",
                  	... // 21 identical lines
                  }, "\n")
```

This is due to the RemainingItemCount field in ListMeta, which is always serialized in proto messages, because it is not a pointer.

**What you expected to happen**:
Proto messages do not include the optional field when unset.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
* Check out https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/78309
* Run `go test ./vendor/k8s.io/api -run TestRoundTripExternalTypes//1.14` (tests round-tripping serialized API content for all types we shipped in 1.14)

This needs to be resolved before 1.15 ships.

/milestone v1.15
/kind bug
/sig api-machinery
/priority important-soon
/assign @caesarxuchao

title: Discuss the feasibility of aws-ebs provisioner to get node zone info from k8s instead of cloud provider

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: area/provider/aws
labels.description: Issues or PRs related to aws provider

labels.name: sig/cloud-provider
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Cloud Provider.

body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
We've seen scalability issues with the current aws-ebs volume provisioner impl, which is querying possible zones from cloud provider directly (#76975). The improvement proposed in #76976 did make api calls more efficient, but also raises people's concern about whether it will create regression or not, or is there any more reliable ways to improve.

To summarize, there are 2 major concerns:

1. Is zone info in Node label trustworthy?
My answer is **yes**, since currently the zone labels (beta version only) are maintained by node controller, the information is retrieved from cloud provider directly and is always updated during node reconciliation, it can be trusted. Even if kubelet can be misconfigured by wrong zone information, node controller is going to override them.
See: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/cloud/node_controller.go#L222
Once we have the GA version of zone labels pushed out, we should update node controller to maintain both zone labels. It's fair enough to assume that if user wants kubelet to report zone/region, the information should be correct.


2. Are the master/minion labels trustworthy?
My answer is **"semantic wide they are equivalent to checking node labels from cloud provider"** - just as people are not required to set master/minion labels in v1.Node, well-known labels in cloud provider is not guaranteed to be set as well. Therefore besides mainstream cluster provisioners, which maintains these sets of labels in both Kubernetes and cloud provider, the function's behavior will remain unchanged: the original impl skips nodes that are **explicitly labeled** with well-known master labels, same here.

Please suggest.

/sig aws
/sig cloud-provider
/kind bug
/priority important-soon

/cc @liggitt @smarterclayton @mcrute @micahhausler @jsafrane @justinsb

title: Add Bind extension point of the scheduling framework

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

body:
**What would you like to be added**:
The [scheduling framework KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-scheduling/20180409-scheduling-framework.md) is now implementable. We have [already added](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/75848) plugin interfaces and a few extension points, such as "[reserve](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-scheduling/20180409-scheduling-framework.md#reserve)" and "[prebind](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-scheduling/20180409-scheduling-framework.md#pre-bind)" plugins.

[Bind](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-scheduling/20180409-scheduling-framework.md#bind) plugins are used to bind a pod to a Node. Bind plugins will not be called until all pre-bind plugins have completed. Each bind plugin is called in the configured order. A bind plugin may choose whether or not to handle the given Pod. If a bind plugin chooses to handle a Pod, the remaining bind plugins are skipped.

Bind plugin interface should be designed so that the existing bind logic of the scheduler can be converted to a bind plugin.
**Please send your proposal for the interface of this extension point before sending a full PR and let us discuss and approve it first.**

This is needed for 1.16. A PR can be sent after 1.15 code freeze.

/sig scheduling
/priority important-soon
ref/ kubernetes/enhancements#624
