<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

Node is not ready. The startup script fails with the following error:

```
sudo systemctl status kube-node-configuration
WARNING: terminal is not fully functional
● kube-node-configuration.service - Configure kubernetes node
   Loaded: loaded (/etc/systemd/system/kube-node-configuration.service; enabled; vendor preset: enabled)
   Active: failed (Result: exit-code) since Tue 2019-07-02 11:28:18 UTC; 2 weeks 6 days ago
 Main PID: 2079 (code=exited, status=1/FAILURE)

Jul 02 11:28:18 gke-operator-tidb-n1-standard-4-375-9f7ddad4-k0sn configure-helper.sh[2079]: Making /var/lib/kubelet executable for kubelet
Jul 02 11:28:18 gke-operator-tidb-n1-standard-4-375-9f7ddad4-k0sn configure-helper.sh[2079]: tune2fs: Bad magic number in super-block while trying to open /dev/disk/by-id/google-local-ssd-0
Jul 02 11:28:18 gke-operator-tidb-n1-standard-4-375-9f7ddad4-k0sn configure-helper.sh[2079]: tune2fs 1.44.1 (24-Mar-2018)
Jul 02 11:28:18 gke-operator-tidb-n1-standard-4-375-9f7ddad4-k0sn configure-helper.sh[2079]: /dev/disk/by-id/google-local-ssd-0 contains a LVM2_member file system
Jul 02 11:28:18 gke-operator-tidb-n1-standard-4-375-9f7ddad4-k0sn configure-helper.sh[2079]: Formatting '/dev/disk/by-id/google-local-ssd-0'
Jul 02 11:28:18 gke-operator-tidb-n1-standard-4-375-9f7ddad4-k0sn configure-helper.sh[2079]: mke2fs 1.44.1 (24-Mar-2018)
Jul 02 11:28:18 gke-operator-tidb-n1-standard-4-375-9f7ddad4-k0sn configure-helper.sh[2079]: /dev/disk/by-id/google-local-ssd-0 is apparently in use by the system; will not make a filesystem 
Jul 02 11:28:18 gke-operator-tidb-n1-standard-4-375-9f7ddad4-k0sn systemd[1]: kube-node-configuration.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
Jul 02 11:28:18 gke-operator-tidb-n1-standard-4-375-9f7ddad4-k0sn systemd[1]: kube-node-configuration.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
Jul 02 11:28:18 gke-operator-tidb-n1-standard-4-375-9f7ddad4-k0sn systemd[1]: Failed to start Configure kubernetes node.
```

This is because the block device is used as a member of LVM. So `tune2fs -l /dev/disk/by-id/google-local-ssd-0` in [cluster script](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cluster/gce/gci/configure-helper.sh#L213) fails.

**What you expected to happen**:

The node becomes ready.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

- create a GKE cluster
- combine the disks into an LVM disk or raid array
- restart the node
- the node will fail to initialize

**Anything else we need to know?**:

- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.12.8-gke.10
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: GCP/GKE

body:
**What happened**:

Using a `scale` command such as:
```
kubectl scale -n kube-system machinedeployment marko-1-pool1 --replicas=2
```

fails with the following error:

```
The machinedeployments "marko-1-pool1" is invalid: metadata.resourceVersion: Invalid value: 0x0: must be specified for an update
```

This bug happens on each run and started occurring as of `kubectl` v1.15.0. With `kubectl` v1.14 or older, I don't have such problem, i.e. it works flawlessly.


**What you expected to happen**:

The `kubectl scale` command succeeds:

```
machinedeployment.cluster.k8s.io/marko-1-pool1 scaled
```

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Create a CRD that has the scale subresource and try to scale a CR using `kubectl`. Example of such CRD can be found [here](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/access-kubernetes-api/custom-resources/custom-resource-definitions/#scale-subresource).

**Anything else we need to know?**:

Regarding the `kubectl` bug, it seems that it started appearing as of #75210. Before the PR, we always fetched the resource and it worked because it had the resource version, while now we are only fetching it in case preconditions are provided (preconditions are not provided by default/when using `kubectl`).

Here is the `-v8` output of a `kubectl scale` command:
```

F0724 13:21:31.208216    9001 helpers.go:114] The machinedeployments "marko-1-pool1" is invalid: metadata.resourceVersion: Invalid value: 0x0: must be specified for an update

If I manually craft the request that has the resource version (or use the `--resource-version` flag), it works.

```
{"kind":"Scale","apiVersion":"autoscaling/v1","metadata":{"name":"marko-1-pool1","namespace":"kube-system","creationTimestamp":null,"resourceVersion":"6229"},"spec":{"replicas":3},"status":{"replicas":0}}
```

Is it as expected that the `autoscaling/v1` Scale resource requires the resource version in order for update to succeed? Shouldn't it always pick the latest resource version in case it isn't provided?

On that note, I also noticed that if you want to update a CR by crafting the request manually and using `curl`, you also need to specify the resource version or you will get the same error. I'm not sure if this is expected and related, but I'm writing it down as it might be related. As far as I know, this is not required for some native resources at all, but I'm not sure is this the case for CRDs.

```

title: PDBs using minUnavailable prevent draining unready pods

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/apps
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Apps.

body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->

**What happened**:

We were unable to drain pods on an unhealthy node that were stuck in pod initializing. The disruption budget has a `minAvailable` of 2. We had two healthy pods and a pod stuck in initializing thus it's unhealthy. A drain on the node with the unhealthy pod stuck in initializing was prevented. 

**What you expected to happen**:

The pods should have been evicted because they are in a not Ready state. 

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Using a PDB with `minAvailable` attempt to drain a node with a pod in a not Ready state. 

**Anything else we need to know?**:

The reason this is prevented is because the disruption controller determines the number of allowed disruptions by looking at [`currentHealthy - desiredHealthy`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a07b027261383127494fc6d4e3ca2c544fb4a464/pkg/controller/disruption/disruption.go#L749-L752). When `minAvailable` is used your `desiredHealthy` count becomes that value, which in our case is 2. The `currentHealthy` count is 2 also because the 3rd pod is stuck in an initializing state on the bad node. This leaves the PDB with an allowed disruption of 0 and thus blocks the drain. 

The eviction logic in the storage only allows pods in a terminal state to bypass the PDB. 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/registry/core/pod/storage/eviction.go#L124-L133

If they're not in a terminal state the eviction will only be allowed to occur if there are allowable disruptions available on the PDB.

It seems that the storage logic should allow draining pods that are not ready instead of just allowing terminal pods. 

/sig apps

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

* In Kubernetes v1.14 new API validation was added requiring an exiting field (`quobyte.Tenant`) to be populated.
* This breaks existing Kubernetes v1.13 API objects on upgrade, and violates Kubernetes Deprecation Policy.
* It was introduced in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/68925/files#diff-81c0c668d90c62bb5b7a2334c09c7e50R877

**What you expected to happen**:

Per [Kubernetes API Deprecation Policy](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-policy/), "Users must be able to upgrade to a new release of Kubernetes[...], without converting anything to the new API version or suffering breakages (unless they explicitly used features only available in the newer version)."

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

* On a Kubernetes v1.13 cluster, create a pod referencing a `QuobyteVolumeSource` volume
* Leave the `QuobyteVolumeSource.Tenant` field empty.
* Upgrade cluster to Kubernetes v1.14.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

Fix should be backported to Kubernetes v1.14 and v1.15.

title: Admission webhooks affected by dead tcp connections

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->
**What happened**:

I was doing some tests regarding mutating webhook (especially for istio), and i found a strange behavior.

Stopping a worker instance with a pod of the webhook running on it seems to break the admission controller for this webhook during approximatively 15 minutes.

After some debugging, the admission controller seems to cache the pod ip associated with this webhook service.


kubectl get events are full of:
```
0s          Warning   FailedCreate             replicaset/sleep-1-d64b54564   Error creating: Internal error occurred: failed calling admission webhook "sidecar-injector.morven.me": Post https://sidecar-injector-webhook-svc.webhook.svc:443/mutate?timeout=30s: context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
```

Solutions to mitigate these errors:
 * Remove the label sidecar-injector=enabled from the namespace, wait the scheduling of the pods, add the label again, and delete each pod to reschedule the pods (and the mutating webhook associated with it)


The logs of kubernetes master are full of things like:
```
I0717 17:00:35.211387 1 event.go:221] Event(v1.ObjectReference{Kind:"ReplicaSet", Namespace:"default", Name:"sleep", UID:"d5faa2cf-a8ad-11e9-83cc-0a4693bb62ee", APIVersion:"apps/v1", ResourceVersion:"5094155", FieldPath:""}): type: 'Warning' reason: 'FailedCreate' Error creating: Internal error occurred: failed calling admission webhook "sidecar-injector.morven.me": Post https://sidecar-injector-webhook-svc.webhook.svc:443/inject?timeout=30s: read tcp 10.50.1.212:58344->10.50.0.77:443: read: connection timed out
```

The 10.50.0.77 ip matches the ip of the pod which was killed because of the shutdown of the node.



**What you expected to happen**:

Mutating webhook admission controller should invalidate the cache associated with the webhook once the first timeout occurred.


**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

On a running kubernetes cluster:
  1. Install a mutating webhook: https://github.com/morvencao/kube-mutating-webhook-tutorial#deploy  + an application using this webhook; TLDR:
```
kubectl create namespace webhook

git clone https://github.com/morvencao/kube-mutating-webhook-tutorial;

cd kube-mutating-webhook-tutorial;

./deployment/webhook-create-signed-cert.sh \
    --service sidecar-injector-webhook-svc \
    --secret sidecar-injector-webhook-certs \
    --namespace webhook

cat deployment/mutatingwebhook.yaml | \
    deployment/webhook-patch-ca-bundle.sh > \
    deployment/mutatingwebhook-ca-bundle.yaml


# Add failurePolicy: Fail to the mutating webhook configuration to trigger the timeout error, and update the namespace:
head -n 14 deployment/mutatingwebhook-ca-bundle.yaml

apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: MutatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  name: sidecar-injector-webhook-cfg
  labels:
    app: sidecar-injector
webhooks:
  - name: sidecar-injector.morven.me
    failurePolicy: Fail
    clientConfig:
      service:
        name: sidecar-injector-webhook-svc
        namespace: webhook
        path: "/mutate"
...


kns webhook;
kubectl create -f deployment/configmap.yaml
kubectl create -f deployment/deployment.yaml
kubectl create -f deployment/service.yaml
kubectl create -f deployment/mutatingwebhook-ca-bundle.yaml

kns default;
kubectl label namespace default sidecar-injector=enabled
kubectl create -f deployment/nginxconfigmap.yaml

cat <<EOF | kubectl create -f -
apiVersion: extensions/v1beta1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: sleep
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        sidecar-injector-webhook.morven.me/inject: "yes"
      labels:
        app: sleep
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: sleep
        image: tutum/curl
        command: ["/bin/sleep","infinity"]
        imagePullPolicy:
EOF

```

At the end, you should have something like :

```
kubectl get pods -n default; kubectl get pods -n webhook
NAME                              READY   STATUS     RESTARTS   AGE
sleep-d64b54564-zfhcx             2/2     Running    0          10s
NAME                                                  READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
sidecar-injector-webhook-deployment-c89cb69b6-n8kff   1/1     Running   0          76s

```

  2. Shutdown the worker where the mutating webhook is running. (kubectl get pods -o wide to see the node)
  3. Wait the node to be down (take a look at the rescheduling of the mutating webhook; kubectl get pods -n webhook)
  4. Scale up the deployment (in this case, the "sleep" deployment) or add some pods within a namespace with the label sidecar-injector=enabled:

```
k scale deployment -n default sleep --replicas=5
```

  4. Nothing happens, except "timeout" errors:
```
kubectl get events -n default
1s          Warning   FailedCreate              ReplicaSet   Error creating: Internal error occurred: failed calling admission webhook "sidecar-injector.morven.me": Post https://sidecar-injector-webhook-svc.webhook.svc:443/mutate?timeout=30s: net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
...
```

You have to wait 15min to see the pods be scheduled.


**Anything else we need to know?**:

Related issues on istio side :
   * Automatic injection fails in AWS  (closed) : https://github.com/istio/istio/issues/14267
   * Istio sidecar injection fails on scale down in EKS (open) : https://github.com/istio/istio/issues/13762
   * Rolling upgrade of the worker nodes results in brief outage of application pods (open) : https://github.com/istio/istio/issues/13840


Doing a kubectl drain on the specific node instead of a shutdown seems to work.

**What happened**:
After a deployment is created with PVC, a node hosting the pod shuts down. After 6 mins timeout, the replacement/new pod is created but cannot come up since the volume is attached to a terminating pod on a shutdown node. If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
I was using kubeadm to generate cluster ca:

```
kubeadm init phase certs ca --cert-dir /etc/kubernetes/pki/
```

The CA generation failed because of 502 bad gateway returned and the response body isn't empty when it's trying to fetch stable version from internet. In this case, the `KubernetesReleaseVersion` function returns error instead of falling back to local client version:

```
unable to fetch file. URL: "https://dl.k8s.io/release/stable-1.txt", status: 502 Bad Gateway
failed to run commands: exit status 1
```

[here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.13.7/cmd/kubeadm/app/util/version.go#L176) is how kubeadm fetches stable version and [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.13.7/cmd/kubeadm/app/util/version.go#L90) is how the error is handled for `fetchFromURL`.

Should kubeadm always fall back to client version when there is any internet issue? Otherwise, this sounds defeat the purpose of fallback.

/sig cluster-lifecycle

**What you expected to happen**:
kubeadm falls back to local client version when there is any internet issue.

title: Adaptive retry-after interval on rate limiting to prevent request overload

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:
In our  cluster (1K Nodes/1W Pods), we found that a large number of logs with a return code of 429 will appear for a long time when kube-apiserver is started:

`I0704 17:28:00.800884 227416 maxinflight.go:111] GET /api/v1/services?resourceVersion=0: (7.054μs) 429 [[kubelet/7bff6911345 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/801b699] 10.10.10.10:41957]
`
In turn, the service will be unavailable for a long time, and such an error is more likely to occur in a large cluster.

The reason for this problem is that all clients need to re-list&watch when restarting, which causes the concurrent requests to be too many. After the flow control limit is exceeded, the _**429**_ response code is returned. At the same time, add Retry-After in the response header to tell client 1s and try again(FYI:https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7bbc130f5e2f99e5d29dbb58e163c405cf6cef32/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/filters/maxinflight.go#L37), but 1s obviously can not meet all the circumstances, which caused long-term overload of APIServer.

**Why is this needed**:

This is a very dangerous risk for the user, we need an adaptive flow control algorithm to deal with this problem.Just like **TODO** in the comment: _maybe make this dynamic? or user-adjustable?_

I think we need to raise its priority and solve it.

/area apiserver
/kind bug
/priority important-soon
/assign

labels.description: Denotes an issue ready for a new contributor, according to the "help wanted" guidelines.

body:
If you create a private cluster via kube-up using provider GCE, you won't be able to restart your master nodes.
If you restart you master, the nodes won't be able to connect to your master.

This is due to this line - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/127c47caf49bec4a59a0500f99b1b1d4cdbf340e/cluster/gce/util.sh#L2922
It gets executed on master on cluster-up, but it won't be re-executed on master restart.

We should fix that, especially if we're to implement https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/86484

/sig scalability
/priority important-soon

<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:

Server-side dry-run is being promoted from beta to GA in v1.18.

For the server-side dry-run integration in kubectl, we are making a few changes:

- we're extending the `--dry-run` flag to support the options `client`, `server` and `none`
- we're deprecating no value for the `--dry-run` flag, such that setting a value will be required in the future
- we're deprecating the boolean values for the `--dry-run` flag and will remove these values in the future
- we're deprecating the `kubectl apply` `--server-dry-run` flag

We need to document these changes accordingly on the website and in comments and tests.

Documentation includes:

- [x] document server-side dry-run feature state as stable for v1.18 (update Hugo shortcode) https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/19549
- [x] dry-run auth requirements @julianvmodesto https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/18235
- [ ] document all API requests, including server-side dry-run, are single-resource requests https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83562 https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/86026 https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/19550
- [x] deprecation notices for `--dry-run`: covered by release notes
- [x] deprecation notice for `--server-dry-run`: covered by release notes
- [x] all usage and examples on the website https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/19549
- [x] all usage in code comments and tests

**Why is this needed**:

Server-side dry-run is graduating to GA, so we need to document usage and examples for users for how to use the feature.

Because we're extending an existing flag and deprecating aspects of this existing feature, we need to have consistent documentation for the flag that reflects the changes.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/85652
GA umbrella issue: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/68514
KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/0015-dry-run.md

cc @apelisse 
/sig cli
/sig api-machinery
/priority important-soon
/help

title: Namespace controller cannot keep up with e2e namespace deletion rate

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

body:
**What happened**:
e2e tests deleting namespaces timed out waiting for namespace cleanup. this was the root cause of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/86181.

I graphed namespace controller lag times:
* from namespace delete to start of processing by the namespace cleanup controller (average 3:36, min 0:05, max 5:41)
* from start of processing to end of processing by the namespace cleanup controller (average 0:43, min 0:01, max 23:35)

https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1hYxDyvZ9o-3T0WrOJ7LgW-sxQn62fU8RWfDjm02OoLc/edit#gid=1101829529

The namespace controller, as configured, can't keep up with the parallelism of the e2e jobs. For most tests, this doesn't fail the test because the e2e job waits at the end for namespace deletion to complete. For the GCEPD test, namespace deletion is a synchronous part of the test. Depending on where the GCEPD test fell, the controller was sometimes too backed up to finish removing the namespace in time.

Things we could do:
* improve reuse of discovery information; currently, the controller fully rediscovers before every namespace sync. Instead, we could only rediscover if cached discovery data is stale or older than the deletionTimestamp of the namespace being synced
* increase the number of parallel workers from the current default of 10 (might need to adjust qps/burst settings as well)
* parallelize deletecollection calls when syncing a single namespace
* lengthen max retry backoff so that accumulating a few dozen namespaces that need retrying because of finalizing objects doesn't overwhelm the queue

/sig api-machinery
/cc @deads2k @msau42 

Note that this blocks moving https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/86181 back into the main e2e (at least as written)

title: cluster/get-kube.sh pulls from wrong bucket with prerelease versions

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.description: Issues or PRs related to the Release Engineering subproject

labels.name: sig/testing
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Testing.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Release.

body:
If you give a prerelease version to `cluster/get-kube.sh`, it'll match both `KUBE_CI_VERSION_REGEX` and `KUBE_RELEASE_VERSION_REGEX`.

Based on this logic:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6e38a0f46e8485a76fe504e51b0f163eaa5141d3/cluster/get-kube.sh#L193-L200

We'll end up trying to pull binaries for this prerelease from the CI bucket (https://dl.k8s.io/ci) rather than the release bucket (https://dl.k8s.io).

These pre-release versions are usually* pushed to the release bucket as part of the release process (e.g. [v1.14.11-beta.0](https://gcsweb.k8s.io/gcs/kubernetes-release/release/v1.14.11-beta.0/)), and so `get-kube.sh` should probably prefer these over the CI versions (which may or may not exist, depending on whether a commit was pushed to the release branch between when the tag was created and the build occurred).

More explicitly, the current logic is:
1. Prefer the release bucket by default.
2. If a version matches the CI regex, use the CI bucket.
3. Else, if a version matches the release regex, we're good - continue to use the default (release bucket).
4. Else, bail out - invalid version.

The correct logic would probably be something like
1. Prefer the release bucket by default.
2. If a version matches the release version regex, continue to use the release bucket.
3. Else, if a version doesn't match the release version regex, but it matches the CI regex, use the CI bucket.
4. If it matches neither, bail out.

**Important note**: due to our hotfix for https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/86182, there is a somewhat fake prerelease tag ([v1.14.11-beta.1](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/releases/tag/v1.14.11-beta.1)) which doesn't have any bits in the release bucket, and we expect others soon. We should not fix this bug in `get-kube.sh` until the latest pointers in the CI bucket do not point to valid release/prerelease versions.

title: Need tests of KUBE-MARK-DROP

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
We have apparently been accidentally deleting the

    -t nat -A KUBE-MARK-DROP -j MARK --set-xmark 0xXXXX

rule for a few weeks (#85527), and no one noticed.

I suspect this is because `KUBE-MARK-DROP` is really only needed if the host accepts all incoming packets by default, and if you have any sort of plausible firewall, then `KUBE-MARK-DROP` is redundant, and so therefore the e2e tests that might otherwise catch `KUBE-MARK-DROP` failures don't actually catch them.

The iptables proxier uses `KUBE-MARK-DROP` in two cases, on cloud platforms where we create iptables rules for LoadBalancer IPs (eg, GCE but not AWS), when a service has a load balancer IP, and it has endpoints, and a packet arrives on the node whose destination is the load-balancer IP:
  1. If the service specifies `spec.loadBalancerSourceRanges`, and the packet's source IP is not in the source ranges, then [we call `KUBE-MARK-DROP` on the packet](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2b9aeabf/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L1126) to drop it later.
      - This is theoretically tested by [`"It should only allow access from service loadbalancer source ranges"`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2b9aeabf/test/e2e/network/service.go#L1533). However, if the `KUBE-MARK-DROP` rule becomes a no-op, then the pod-to-LoadBalancer-IP connection will fall through the firewall chain, never hit the XLB chain, and eventually just get masqueraded and delivered to the LoadBalancer IP like it would for any other cluster-external IP. Since the cloud loadbalancer is *also* programmed with the source ranges, and the source range in this test is a single pod IP, the load balancer will then reject the packet (since it has the node's IP as its source at this point).
      - I think we can fix this test to fail in the absence of the drop rule by adding the node's IP to the source range. Then the expected-to-fail connection would (erroneously) not get dropped by the node, get passed to the cloud load balancer, which would accept it, and then get passed back to the service, causing the test case to fail.
  2. If the service has `ServiceExternalTrafficPolicyTypeLocal` and no local endpoints then [we call `KUBE-MARK-DROP` on the packet](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2b9aeabf/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L1365) to drop it later.
      - This does not get tested by [`"It should only target nodes with endpoints"`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2b9aeabf/test/e2e/network/service.go#L2190), because if the load balancers are working correctly then they won't send any traffic to the nodes that are creating the drop rules anyway.
      - It also does not get tested by [`"It should work from pods"`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2b9aeabf/test/e2e/network/service.go#L2261) because a pod-to-LoadBalancer-IP connection [will be rewritten to be pod-to-ClusterIP](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2b9aeabf/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L1339) before the only-local check and bypass the drop rule.
      - I think it should be possible to test this by trying to connect to an only-local LoadBalancer service from a `hostNetwork` pod on a node that has no endpoints for the service. The drop rule ought to cause that connection to fail, but if the drop rule was missing then it would make a connection directly to the LoadBalancer and then succeed.

The ipvs proxier *refers* to the `KUBE-MARK-DROP` chain, but I think it doesn't actually *use* it...

/sig network
/priority important-soon

title: Convert interpod affinity priority to a "map-reduce" pattern

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

body:
**What would you like to be added**:

The pre-work for this is done, so converting it to map-reduce should be straightforward and includes the following steps:

1) Factor out [topologyPairToScore calculation](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/algorithm/priorities/interpod_affinity.go#L103-L211) to be run in PriorityMetadataProducer, and store the result in [priorityMetadata](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/algorithm/priorities/metadata.go#L54)


2) The [node count calculation](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/algorithm/priorities/interpod_affinity.go#L216-L219) is the map function.

3) The [score normalization logic](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/algorithm/priorities/interpod_affinity.go#L230-L242) is the reduce function. Reduce will include calculating maxCount/minCount as well.

**Why is this needed**:
This is required as a pre-request to converting it to a Score plugin.


/sig scheduling
/help

title: update `k8s.io/client-go` release process docs to stop adding major version tags

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: kind/documentation
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to documentation.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

body:
go modules require libraries that are module-aware (contain a go.mod file) and use a semver tag >=2.0 to include the major version as a suffix of the module name (e.g. `example.com/library/v2`).

https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/Modules#semantic-import-versioning
> As a result of Semantic Import Versioning, code opting in to Go modules must comply with these rules:
>
> * If the module is version v2 or higher, the major version of the module must be included as a /vN at the end of the module paths used in go.mod files (e.g., module github.com/my/mod/v2, require github.com/my/mod/v2 v2.0.1) and in the package import path (e.g., import "github.com/my/mod/v2/mypkg"). This includes the paths used in go get commands (e.g., go get github.com/my/mod/v2@v2.0.1. Note there is both a /v2 and a @v2.0.1 in that example. One way to think about it is that the module name now includes the /v2, so include /v2 whenever you are using the module name).

The fact that this was required was unclear previously. go1.13 begins enforcing this and refuses to build a module required at v2.0.0 whose name does not end in `/v2`

The existing `v12.0.0` tag is not a valid module (the `kubernetes-1.15.0` tag is), and go1.13 will refuse to fetch/build it.

with go1.13:
```sh
go get k8s.io/client-go@v12.0.0
go: finding k8s.io/client-go v12.0.0
go: finding k8s.io/client-go v12.0.0
go get k8s.io/client-go@v12.0.0: k8s.io/client-go@v12.0.0: invalid version: module contains a go.mod file, so major version must be compatible: should be v0 or v1, not v12
```

Note that non-semver tags are still addressable via go get (e.g. `k8s.io/client-go@kubernetes-1.15.0`) and require directives (using resolved `v0.0.0-$date-$sha` "pseudoversions").

with go1.13:
```sh
$ go get k8s.io/client-go@kubernetes-1.15.0
go: finding k8s.io kubernetes-1.15.0
go: finding k8s.io/client-go kubernetes-1.15.0
go: downloading k8s.io/client-go v0.0.0-20190620085101-78d2af792bab
go: extracting k8s.io/client-go v0.0.0-20190620085101-78d2af792bab
```

/sig api-machinery
cc @sttts @nikhita @BenTheElder

title: Add unit test to catch scheduler's node order evaluation regressions

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

body:
**What would you like to be added**:
A unit test that verifies the evaluation order of the nodes in the scheduler.

**Why is this needed**:
The scheduler evaluates the nodes in a specific order until it finds a pre-defined minimum number of feasible nodes. To give all nodes a fair chance of being evaluated,  in each scheduling cycle, the scheduler starts evaluating from where it left off in the previous cycle. This is captured by the ```lastProcessedNodeIndex``` parameter in [```generic_scheduler.go```](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/core/generic_scheduler.go)

We need to add a unit test that captures regressions related to this behavior to avoid bugs like https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/84222

/sig scheduling
/priority important-soon
/help

**What happened**:

A reporter testing their CSI driver at scale noticed issues:

Specifically they reported that the pod startup time is impacted by the number of concurrent CSI volume attachments in progress across a cluster.

According to the reporter, the pod start up time jumps from order of seconds (when there are a few volume attachments happening concurrently), to 1-2 minutes once there are >1300 concurrent volume attachments for pods using those attachments.

Similarly the reporter indicates that volume detach operations jump from order of seconds (when there are a few volume attach/detach operations happening concurrently), to 3-4 minutes once there are >1300 concurrent volume attachments.

The reporter mentioned that the slowness, once it is encountered, does not go away until the number of concurrent volume attaches is reduced below <500.

**What you expected to happen**:

Ideally, as the number of CSI volume attachments started in parallel increases the time it takes to start pods remains constant. We should identify the bottle necks and remove as many as possible.

title: PriorityQueue is far from FIFO for same priority Pods

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: lifecycle/rotten
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
By default, user Pod does not have priority (i.e. 0), so usually, they expect **FIFO** scheduling in this case, even if for the PriorityQueue.
In this requirement, the **FI(First In)** should be determined by the [Pod CreationTimestamp instead of last queued time](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83826), i.e. the **user expect longest Pending Pod since creation should be scheduled first in most cases**.
However, we found that the PriorityQueue is far from FIFO, i.e. >40% Pods cut in line, see **How to reproduce it** for more details.

**What you expected to happen**:
The PriorityQueue should be **near FIFO** for same priority Pods, i.e. <5% Pods cut in line.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. Cluster Setup: 7 Nodes each has 4 total free GPUs
2. Submit ReplicaSet RSX, which contains 28 Pods, and each Pod request 1 GPU and just sleep forever in its command.
3. Wait all Pods in RSX is running.
4. Submit Job JA, which contains 200 Pods to run to complete, and each Pod request 1 GPU and just sleep 20s in its command.
5. Wait all Pods in JA is queued in scheduler. (Because no free GPUs, so all Pods in JA are pending)
6. Submit Job JB, which has the same spec with JA except for its name JB is different with JA. (Here, we ensures JB is totally later than JA)
7. Delete ReplicaSet RSX, so JA and JB will compete to schedule.

We obeserves below result consistently:
| Timestamp (normalized) | JA completed Pods | JB completed Pods| Pods cut in line rate|
|:---- |:---- |:---- |:---- |
| 1 | 72 | 56 | 56/200 |
| 2 | 108 | 76 | 76/200 |
| 3 | 138 | 101 | 101/200 |
| 4 | 169 | 131 | 131/200 |
| 5 | 182 | 153 | 153/200 |
In avarage, >40% Pods cut in line.

**Anything else we need to know?**:
This issue can be fixed, i.e. cut in line rate decreased <5%, after we used the **Pod creation time instead of the last queued time to sort Pod for the same priority**, as suggested in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83826, and fixed by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/83835.

After the fix https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/83835, we obeserves below result consistently (for the same repro steps above):
| Timestamp (normalized) | JA completed Pods | JB completed Pods| Pods cut in line rate|
|:---- |:---- |:---- |:---- |
| 1 | 160 | 1| 1/200 |
| 2 | 181 | 1| 1/200 |
| 3 | 191 | 3| 3/200 |
| 4 | 194 | 21| 21/200 |
In avarage, <5% Pods cut in line.


**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
```

title: Should use Pod creation time instead of its last queued time to sort Pod for the same priority

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: lifecycle/rotten
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

body:
**What happened**:
Currently (after https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/73700), we use the **Pod last queued time by scheduler** to sort Pod for the same priority:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0599ca2bcfcae7d702f95284f3c2e2c2978c7772/pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L717-L721
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0599ca2bcfcae7d702f95284f3c2e2c2978c7772/pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L361-L362

Usually, it produces the same Pod ordering as the **Pod creation time** (If Pod are submitted one by one **slowly**, and previous Pods are **always allocated**).

However, if scheduler is restarted, or switched to another leader, etc, all pending Pods will be re-informed to local cache, and the scheduler will **see** the Pod comes in a **undefined order**, possibly very different with the Pod ordering produced by the **Pod creation time**.

And even if the scheduler is not re-informed by restarting etc, using last queued time still causes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83834. And the reason is that after a Pod is poped for scheduling and then added back to queue again, its **last queued time** is updated to now (above `newPodInfo `is called again). So, if still sort by the time, it is no longer represent the **Pod pending time since created**, it just represent the **Pod pending time since last scheduled** which user does not aware and does not care, they just know the former Pod pending time.

**What you expected to happen**:
The scheduler should be **near FIFO** for the same priority Pods, and the **FI(First In)** should be determined steadily by the **Pod CreationTimestamp**, instead of the unsteady **Pod last queued time**, to measure the user cared, awared, true and steady **Pod Pending time**.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Case1: Many Pods at the same priority are waiting, then restart scheduler. You will see Pods are scheduled in a **Far from FIFO** way (e.g. easy to see a Pod will not be allocated, but a Pod with the same spec except for naming submitted 2hrs later than it will be allocated).

Case2: Same as the repro steps in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83834


**Anything else we need to know?**:
I see Pod CreationTimestamp is first introduced to sort by PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/71488, however, it is later removed by PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/73700.
Is it a degradation? And Why?
BTW, I tried to fix this by PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/83835

title: Scalability dimension: # access tokens

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scalability
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scalability.

labels.name: sig/auth
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Auth.

body:
There's some practical limit on the number of concurrent access tokens that can be used in a Kubernetes cluster before it begins to spend all of its time in the authn stack verifying them. Absent fixes to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/78766 it was < 500; with the fixes linked there it's still not infinitely scalable-- I still hit (what I believe to be) https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83259 with ~ 5k unique tokens @ ~700QPS.

This request is to
1. Give this dimension an official name & definition, and list it with others, e.g. here: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/sig-scalability/configs-and-limits/thresholds.md
2. Measure it
3. Make it have a useful value (I think it should be > 10k)

/kind bug
/sig scalability

labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

body:
The TokenReview REST handler constructs a new request and passes it through the authentication handler. Any deadline associated with the original context is not passed down.

We should propagate the original context deadline/cancellation, either by wrapping the parent context, or by extracting/propagating the deadline, or by waiting on the original context's Done() channel and propagating a cancellation

/sig auth
/cc @enj @mikedanese

<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
When using kubectl, authentication fails with the below error
`E0331 10:18:17.205561   46266 azure.go:154] Failed to acquire a token: refreshing the expired token: refreshing token: adal: Refresh request failed. Status Code = '400'. Response body: {"error":"invalid_resource","error_description":"AADSTS500011: The resource principal named spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:**spn** was not found in the tenant named **tenant ID**. This can happen if the application has not been installed by the administrator of the tenant or consented to by any user in the tenant. You might have sent your authentication request to the wrong tenant.\r\nTrace ID: **trace ID**\r\nCorrelation ID: **correlation ID**\r\nTimestamp: 2020-03-30 23:18:17Z","error_codes":[500011],"timestamp":"2020-03-30 23:18:17Z","trace_id":"**trace ID**","correlation_id":"**correlation ID**","error_uri":"https://login.microsoftonline.com/error?code=500011"}`

For some reason kubectl is adding a lot of `spn:`s to the start of the SPN - this can be observed in ~/.kube/config:
```users:
- name: azure-active-directory
  user:
    auth-provider:
      config:
        apiserver-id: spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:spn:**SPN**
```

**What you expected to happen**:
Authentication works as in previous versions of Kubectl

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Create a cluster using Azure AD authentication. Authenticate from a client and wait until the token expires. Use Kubectl and have it automatically refresh the token; it will fail due to the extra 'spn:' entries.

title: SystemOOMs not reported for containers

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
**What happened**:

A SystemOOM event was not reported even when the memory limit hit was the root cgroup memory limit.

**What you expected to happen**:

A SystemOOM event should have been reported.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Do not set `--system-reserved` or `--kube-reserved`, and set `--eviction-hard=` to disable memory eviction on the kubelet.  Run a pod without memory limits which slowly consumes memory, such as with `k8s.gcr.io/stress:v1` from https://github.com/vishh/stress.  Use arguments -mem-alloc-size", "100Mi", "-mem-alloc-sleep", "10s".  This should trigger an OOM on the root cgroup, but no event will be generated.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

cAdvisor populates ContainerName and VictimContainerName from matching the regexp: [`Task in (.*) killed as a result of limit of (.*)`](https://github.com/google/cadvisor/blob/master/utils/oomparser/oomparser.go#L29).  A SystemOOM should mean VictimContainerName == "/", as we are looking for OOMs that are "killed as a results of limit of /".  However, we incorrectly [check ContainerName](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/oom/oom_watcher_linux.go#L75) instead in the kubelet. 

cc @kubernetes/sig-node-bugs @derekwaynecarr @sjenning @dchen1107

**What happened**:
On server-side apply, we should make sure not to write to etcd if there are no changes.

**What happened**:

regarding nodeserver.go - yes it polls every second, but if /dev/... is not there (findDiskByLun returns "") it returns fmt.Errorf("azureDisk - findDiskByLun(%v) failed within timeout", lun). and exits from wait.Poll
It causes to kubelet retry NodePublishVolume with exponensial backoff, and because /dev/disk/azure/... can appear 15-60s after first first call it can reach 2m timeout.
So I suggest to just return false, nil and let wait.Poll to retry instead of kubelet.
see https://github.com/codefresh-io/azuredisk-csi-driver/blob/03a3b6d4809b0b263fd6774c2d6ef94a99ceaa18/pkg/azuredisk/nodeserver.go#L478

title: Discovery should return error if Forbidden

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

body:
In Kubernetes 1.14, anonymous API discovery has been dropped (the cluster role-binding that enabled it is no longer applied). This means, when using `client-go` for any unauthenticated, non-dynamic/unstructured requests, an HTTP 403 will be the result. However, `client-go` discovery eats HTTP 403 (and also does 404) which effectively means to the caller there was no error.
In my case I am seeing something like _can't find Kind{} for Resource{} in Group{}_.

I think the culprit is in https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/discovery/discovery_client.go#L164-L177 and https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/discovery/discovery_client.go#L200-L207, which means retro-compatibility is preferred even against versions (1.0?) that are no longer supported.

Also, and if my assumption is correct, there are places in this discovery code where retro-compatibility can go away, e.g. https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/discovery/discovery_client.go#L425-L431.

Thanks to @ncdc for helping my figure out I was getting a 403 and @lavalamp for suggesting I open an issue because this just doesn't seem right.

**What happened**:

* Created a service including a finalizer
* Triggered deletion of the service

  E0128 08:15:36.920837       1 repair.go:237] the cluster IP 10.0.0.81 for service foo/default is not allocated; repairing
  ```
* After about 10 minutes I'm able to create the service, the apiserver shows the following log lines when it is repairing it:
  ```
  E0128 08:28:51.429642       1 repair.go:184] the node port 30003 appears to have leaked: cleaning up
  E0128 08:28:51.436350       1 repair.go:311] the cluster IP 10.0.0.81 appears to have leaked: cleaning up

docker run -d -p 2379:2379 --name=kube-etcd -v $(pwd)/etcd:/tmp/ --rm k8s.gcr.io/etcd:3.3.15 /usr/local/bin/etcd --data-dir /tmp/etcd --advertise-client-urls=http://0.0.0.0:2379 --listen-client-urls=http://0.0.0.0:2379

touch $KUBECONFIG
kubectl config set-cluster etcd-local --server=http://localhost:8080
kubectl config set-context etcd-local --cluster=etcd-local
kubectl config use-context etcd-local

cat <<EOF > service.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: foo
  finalizers:
  - foo.bar/some-finalizer
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 80
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: 8080
    nodePort: 30003
  selector:

EOF

for i in {1..200}; do
  echo "[$(date +%Y-%m-%d-%H:%M:%S)] # $i"

  kubectl delete svc foo --wait=false
  sleep 1
  kubectl patch svc foo --type='json' -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/metadata/finalizers"}]'

title: Improve CRD openapi serving speed

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scalability
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scalability.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

body:
CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI e2e tests are [flaky](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/86418) because the time for a given CRD change to get reflected in the openapi spec exceeds the 30s timeout. 

Here is a analysis for the worst case-- assuming three CRD changes were made at the same time (change A&B by tests running in parallel, and change C by the current test), it may take up to three 200OK downloads before the current e2e test sees change C in the openapi spec. The 30s timeout can be reached before the test starts the third 200OK download.  

![Copy of Untitled drawing](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6629765/72006696-0cd91500-3205-11ea-9877-7910a0dc70e8.png)

Things that we can improve:
1. [openapi service update](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b34c96b62c74c22ac9ac135fc787016786845a69/vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/handler/handler.go#L106-L139) (for both kube-aggregator and CRD) is most expensive. [Adding log](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/86564) shows both the first [marshaling](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b34c96b62c74c22ac9ac135fc787016786845a69/vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/handler/handler.go#L107) and [ToProtoBinary](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b34c96b62c74c22ac9ac135fc787016786845a69/vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/handler/handler.go#L115) can cost more that 5s for kube-aggregator. The time spent also varies a lot even though the spec size should be rather stable (due to CPU pressure?). More efficient ways to do the marshaling and generate proto binary would help.
2. although the CRD openapi spec is much smaller compared to kube-aggregator,  openapi service update still costs 0.5~1.5s to apiextensions-apiserver for each CRD change. Since openapi service update requires lock, the time queues up when there are lots of CRD changes at the same time (e.g. three CRD changes in the image above). Solving the previous point also helps here
3. apiextensions-apiserver supports serving openapi spec in PB and gzip, but kube-aggregator downloads and deserializes the spec through JSON (which makes sense for aggregated apiservers). Potentially kube-aggregator can use PB when it's talking to apiextensions-apiserver. 

cc @liggitt @sttts @wojtek-t

<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:

Add mandatory plugins that can't be removed from the default plugins.

**Why is this needed**:

body:
**What happened**:

Kubernetes is poised to ship 1.19 based on go1.14 (as of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/88638)

Per https://golang.org/doc/go1.14#runtime:

> Goroutines are now asynchronously preemptible. As a result, loops without function calls no longer potentially deadlock the scheduler or significantly delay garbage collection. This is supported on all platforms except windows/arm, darwin/arm, js/wasm, and plan9/*.
> 
> A consequence of the implementation of preemption is that on Unix systems, including Linux and macOS systems, programs built with Go 1.14 will receive more signals than programs built with earlier releases. This means that programs that use packages like syscall or golang.org/x/sys/unix will see more slow system calls fail with EINTR errors. Those programs will have to handle those errors in some way, most likely looping to try the system call again. For more information about this see man 7 signal for Linux systems or similar documentation for other systems.

Based on discussion in reported issues (golang/go#36644, golang/go#38033, golang/go#38836), it appears that some stdlib methods can also encounter EINTR errors more frequently, and do not handle them in go1.14.

A stdlib mitigation [is in place for go1.15](https://go-review.googlesource.com/c/go/+/232862/), but [will not be backported to go1.14](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/39026#issuecomment-627589315) due to impact.

The asynchronous preemption introduced in go1.14 can be disabled by setting `GODEBUG=asyncpreemptoff=1`.

At the very least, we should document this possibility and workaround. If we see evidence that this error is being encountered by our components, we should consider disabling asynchronous preemption in the images/environments/manifests we control until we get to go 1.15.

/sig release cluster-lifecycle
for awareness

/sig node api-machinery scheduling network
owners of long-running components

/sig docs

title: hyperkube kubelet: KillPodSandboxError ... networkPlugin cni failed to teardown pod ... network: neither iptables nor ip6tables usable

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

* I attempted to bump the 1.16, 1.17, and 1.18 versions in my team's kubernetes image repo to 1.16.11, 1.17.7, and 1.18.4, respectively.
* The images built successfully but none of the e2e tests we run, including the kubernetes conformance e2e tests, ever actually ran correctly without a clear indication as to why -- ginkgo was just mysteriously succeeding without any tests passed, skipped, or failed. this prompted me to take a closer look a 1.18.4 cluster.
* I expected corednes pods to be in "Running" status but instead found:
```
kube-system   coredns-6b6854dcbf-tqxgn          0/1     Completed   0          5h24m
kube-system   coredns-6b6854dcbf-wztzn          0/1     Completed   0          5h24m
```
* ...and the following event on one of those pods:
```
  Normal  SandboxChanged  98s (x627 over 136m)  kubelet, test-1-18-4-0b8b9360-3fhas  Pod sandbox changed, it will be killed and re-created.
```
* This even prompted me to log on to a worker node and notice repeated messages like the following in the kubelet logs:
```
Jun 18 21:41:53 test-1-18-4-06729635-3f4er docker[1211]: E0618 21:41:53.316852    1291 pod_workers.go:191] Error syncing pod f364dc8e-6e7d-4869-976a-678a3ce913ac ("coredns-6b6854dcbf-2t9cv_kube-system(f364dc8e-6e7d-4869-976a-678a3ce913ac)"), skipping: failed to "KillPodSandbox" for "f364dc8e-6e7d-4869-976a-678a3ce913ac" with KillPodSandboxError: "rpc error: code = Unknown desc = networkPlugin cni failed to teardown pod \"coredns-6b6854dcbf-2t9cv_kube-system\" network: neither iptables nor ip6tables usable"
```

This led me to grep through the kubernetes repo at v1.18.4 for the message `network: neither iptables nor ip6tables usable` but I didn't find anything. So I did the same thing in the containernetworking plugins repo and found the following references:

* https://github.com/containernetworking/plugins/blob/ad10b6fa91aacd720f1f9ab94341a97a82a24965/plugins/meta/portmap/portmap.go#L120
* https://github.com/containernetworking/plugins/blob/ad10b6fa91aacd720f1f9ab94341a97a82a24965/plugins/meta/portmap/portmap.go#L384

It's kind of hard to tell which of the possible `maybeGetIptables` function failures occurred because it doesn't lift the error into the calling context but this led me to believe that there is something different about the iptables installed in the hyperkube container that we are are using to run our kubelets. And I did find a potentially significant difference at least between 1.18.3 and 1.18.4 (i haven't compared the patch level versions on 1.16 and 1.17 yet):

```
zsh/4 10048 % docker run --rm -it --entrypoint "" gcr.io/google-containers/hyperkube:v1.18.3 iptables --version
iptables v1.6.0
```

```
zsh/4 10047 % docker run --rm -it --entrypoint "" gcr.io/google-containers/hyperkube:v1.18.4 iptables --version
iptables v1.8.2 (nf_tables)
```

I'm not familiar enough with iptables to say with any kind of certainty that this is really the root cause of the problem, but if not then it's a pretty good red herring.

**What you expected to happen**:

I was hoping that `1.16.11`, `1.17.7`, and `1.18.4` would "just work" similar to the previous patch level versions.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

I'm so far from really understanding what's going on at pretty much all times that it's actually kind of depressing but without just dumping a bunch of configuration files that I don't think would be very helpful, here is what I think may be happening:

We have `--network-plugin=cni` passed to kubelet in our systemd unit file, and some part of kubelet is somehow delegating networking stuff to the CNI binaries that appear to be copied into the hyperkube image:
```
zsh/4 10049 % docker run --rm -it --entrypoint "" gcr.io/google-containers/hyperkube:v1.18.4 ls /opt/cni/bin
bandwidth  bridge  dhcp  firewall  flannel  host-device  host-local  ipvlan  loopback  macvlan  portmap  ptp  sbr  static  tuning  vlan
```

So I'm guessing that `portmap` here corresponds to the code I linked to above in the cni plugins repo.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

I considered the possibility of *not* filing this bug and instead chiming in on #92242 or #92250 but I thought it would be better to post a new issue rather than risk the information I've gathed being lost in the noise of comments.

**Environment**: 
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
1.16.11, 1.17.7, and 1.18.4
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
Digitalocean
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
```
zsh/4 10051 % docker run --rm -it --entrypoint "" gcr.io/google-containers/hyperkube:v1.18.3 cat /etc/os-release
PRETTY_NAME="Debian GNU/Linux 9 (stretch)"
NAME="Debian GNU/Linux"
VERSION_ID="9"
VERSION="9 (stretch)"
ID=debian
HOME_URL="https://www.debian.org/"

BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugs.debian.org/"
```

title: GetLabelsForVolume panic issue for azure disk PV

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.description: Issues or PRs related to azure provider

labels.name: sig/cloud-provider
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Cloud Provider.

body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
Overview
========

A persistent volume claim / storage class configured in a certain way can cause all the Kube API servers on an ARO cluster to crashloop.

We’ve seen this issue on a production cluster (ICM 192488792).  In development we have proven one vector by which the cluster could have got into this state but it doesn’t seem that likely.  We wonder if there are other vectors.

We don’t currently have a good way to rescue a cluster that gets into this state because our service accesses are predicated on API server availability.

Request
=======

We would like help:

1. to agree and expedite an appropriate fix in order to protect all other production clusters.
2. with suggestions on how we might fix the broken production cluster.

Causes
======

1. In certain cases upon PV create, the persistentvolume admission controller attempts to retrieve the managed disk object via the Azure API, but in ARO the relevant client object is a nil pointer.  The pointer is dereferenced and the kube API server panics.

2. The PVC controller repeatedly attempts to create the PV object, which DoSes the kube API server.

3. The client object in (1) is nil because of ARO’s cloud provider authentication architecture, which differs from that of OCP.  More information below.

Technical detail
================

For a panic stack trace and reproducer, see

* Creation of an Azure Disk persistent volume is attempted
* The persistentvolume admission controller runs, (l
*persistentVolumeLabel) Admit(), in
vendor/k8s.io/kubernetes/plugin/pkg/admission/storage/persistentvolume/label/admission.go:104
* In our possible reproducer, the admission controller does not return early in (l *persistentVolumeLabel) findVolumeLabels(), admission.go:182 because the zone labels are not set.
* A cloud provider is (incorrectly) instantiated via:
   - getAzurePVLabeler(), admission.go:354
   - cloudprovider.GetCloudProvider(), admission.go:333
   - NewCloud(),
vendor/k8s.io/kubernetes/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/azure/azure.go:262
   - (az *Cloud) InitializeCloudFromConfig, azure.go:283
* We see the following loglines:
   - Azure cloud provider is starting without credentials
   - Azure cloudprovider using try backoff: retries=%d, exponent=%f, duration=%d, jitter=%f
* We believe that an early return occurs at azure.go:444, before c.DisksClient is initialised, because servicePrincipalToken is nil
* Later, a nil pointer dereference of c.DisksClient occurs in (c *Cloud) GetAzureDiskLabels,
vendor/k8s.io/kubernetes/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/azure/azure_managedDiskController.go:301

OCP 4.3 cloud provider authentication architecture ==================================================

* The installer lays down an Azure managed identity (MSI) resource, grants it Contributor access to cluster resource group and to any pre-existing virtual network (VNET).
* In the context of the Kube API server, the persistentvolume admission controller uses MSI to authenticate to Azure for its API calls.

ARO 4.3 cloud provider authentication architecture ==================================================

* ARO can’t follow OCP 4.3’s architecture because of the following chicken-and-egg problem:
   - As an Azure service, ARO is not permitted to add role assignments to the customer’s pre-existing virtual network - the customer must explicitly do this.
   - No cluster managed identity can exist before the customer runs `az aro create` (by definition), so there is nothing for the customer to grant the role assignment to.
* As a result, ARO does not use a managed identity at all, and instead uses a user-created cluster service principal.
* ARO carries a patch to the installer which creates a kube-config/azure-cloud-provider Secret during cluster install.  The controller manager merges the cloud config with this Secret at start-up time (see `InitializeCloudFromSecret()`), however this code path does not run in the API server.  In ARO, any calls to the Azure API from the API server are probably broken.
* Prior to GA, ARO wrote the cloud config secret raw into the cloud config.  Reverting to this behaviour would work around this issue, but is clearly suboptimal.

The file may already have people listed who are secuirty contacts. In that case, simply remove any PSC members who aren't also security contacts for the repo.

**What happened**:
Below are the **27 unit tests** that panic and FAIL while I run "make test"

Also the analysis says that the failure started occurring after the below PR merge:
#https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/90582/commits/283d9f7483d9a5b30746921a68e7a5e586c2c80e
This commit **updates github.com/golang/protobuf from v1.3.3 to v1.4.2.**
The invalid Type failures that occur are from the newer implementation of protobuf that is added at "kubernetes/vendor/google.golang.org/protobuf" which did not exist prior to this commit.

25.	pkg/registry/storage/csidriver/storage TestList
26.	pkg/registry/storage/storageclass/storage TestUpdate
27.	vendor/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/registry/customresource

**What you expected to happen**:
The unit tests must pass without error message.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. Setup Go lang 1.13.5
2. Clone kubernetes source code : git clone git@github.com:kubernetes/kubernetes.git
3. Ensure you are on master branch : git checkout master
4. cd kubernetes/hack/tools
5. GO111MODULE=on go install gotest.tools/gotestsum
6. make generated_files
7. make test WHAT=<Path of any one test from above failures>
         eg: make test WHAT=k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/registry/apps/deployment/storage/

title: Early filtering at PreFilter extension point

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: help wanted
labels.description: Denotes an issue that needs help from a contributor. Must meet "help wanted" guidelines.

body:
Update the semantics of ```PreFilter``` extension point to allow it to act as an early filtering stage. PreFilter can be used to reject pods before evaluating each node at the Filter extension point. This is useful to quickly reject unschedulable pods in cases that don't depend on the particular node (e.g., pod requesting unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims).

A non ```Success``` PreFilter gets converted to Error: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5dbe3e308af1598536cda3b785fb05b30505990f/pkg/scheduler/core/generic_scheduler.go#L398

We should change that and support proper rejection of the pod at PreFilter. The only acceptable unschedulable status for now should be  ```UnschedulableAndUnresolvable```.


/sig scheduling

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

body:
when a pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims, it's unscheduable and unresolvable as the pod must wait for the PV controller to bind these PVCs. ~~In VolumeBinding plugin, we can return an `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable` error to eliminate unnecessary retries~~ (not right, they have the same effect, but `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable` is more meaningful). Once the PVC(s) are bound, pods will be [moved to the active or backoff queue again](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1bc526aa6c310b915e7ad57b4442deec7328aad2/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L55-L61).

ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/91679#discussion_r434554404

title: Can't run two pods with read-only iSCSI volumes

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

body:
**What happened**:
Running two pods that use the same iSCSI volume, one of them fails with:

```
Warning  FailedMount  6s (x5 over 14s)  kubelet, 127.0.0.1  MountVolume.WaitForAttach failed for volume "test-volume" : iscsi: create /var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/iscsi/iface-default/127.0.0.1:3260-iqn.2003-01.io.k8s:jsafrane-
lun-0/iscsi.json err open /var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/iscsi/iface-default/127.0.0.1:3260-iqn.2003-01.io.k8s:jsafrane-lun-0/iscsi.json: read-only file system
```

**What you expected to happen**:
Both pods should be running

**Anything else we need to know?**:
It's caused by iscsi volume plugin persiting iSCSI settings into the mount directory itself (e.g. `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/iscsi/iface-default/127.0.0.1:3260-iqn.2003-01.io.k8s:jsafrane-lun-0`):

1. The volume plugin creates the global mount directory.
2. The volume plugin creates iscsi.json there.
3. The volume plugin mounts the volume there. This shadows the iscsi.json file, but it's fine, as long as no other pod uses the same volume on the same node.
4. User creates a second pod that uses the volume.
5. The volume plugin tries to create iscsi.json in the global volume directory. Since the volume is mounted, it will either writes the file to the volume (!) or fails, if the volume is read-only.

title: WatchCache may accept watches that it should not

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: needs-sig
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `sig/foo` label and requires one.

body:
Opening as an follow up analysis from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/91367

Merging #91260 unexpectedly resulted in a huge flakiness of at least one of the apimachinery tests: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/91367 
That is definitely unexpected, because that PR only changes the size of watchcache, which no e2e tests should rely on.

So I started digging deeper into it and indeed that PR also uncovered the bug that was introduced earlier.

Here is what is happening:
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/90091 made the watch cache size dynamic
- however, there was a place in watch cache that relied on the following invariant:
 "when watchache becomes full, it is full until the next relist"
 that place is this one:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6249f287e1d3d9fb63b60961c8625a82d7db360e/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/watch_cache.go#L537-L544

- with the change that made watchcache size dynamic, it may no longer be true, i.e.:
 (a) watch cache was full
 (b) we are increasing its size
 (c) it is no longer full, but we no longer can't serve (at least not always) everything since listResourceVersion

This is exactly what was happening in the failed tests:
- the service was updated well back in the past
- the watchcache initially rotated couple times (no need to increase it) [which pulled our change out of it]
- the its size was increased
- that resulted in cache becoming not full
- so the incoming watch should have returned "too old", but was accepting it (due to the listResourceVersion > 0 condition being true), but in fact wasn't able to serve it


Bonus point: in "kind" tests we were observing tests taking 30+ minutes - this seem to be a bug in kube-apiserver configuration, because the watch in the test doesn't set TimeoutSeconds, and:
(a) in GCE it is default in kube-apiserver to sth random from [5m, 30m]: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/get.go#L248-L250
(b) in kind apparently it isn't...


/kind bug
/sig apimachinery

/assign @gongguan @wojtek-t 

@liggitt @hasheddan @jpbetz - FYI

title: fieldManager errors can fail create/update/non-apply-patch API calls

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: priority/important-soon

labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a regression from a prior release.

labels.name: wg/api-expression
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to WG API Expression.

body:
**What happened**:

FieldManager errors were encountered in an Update API request (xref https://github.com/openfaas/faas-netes/issues/630#issuecomment-625440515):
```
Unexpected status: 500, message: failed to update object (Update for openfaas.com/v1, Kind=Function) managed fields: failed to convert live object to proper version: /, Kind= is unstructured and is not suitable for converting to "openfaas.com/v1"
```

This error blocked an update request that worked in prior Kubernetes versions.

**What you expected to happen**:

The particular error that occurred there should be tracked down and resolved separately, but I would expect field manager errors only block apply requests, not create/update/non-apply-patch requests.

In these non-apply handler locations, fieldManager errors are a "should not happen" type of failure. If a fieldManager-related error is encountered, I'd expect to log the error (and perhaps bump a server-side-apply-error metric), but to then recover and allow the create/update/patch request to continue (potentially by resetting the managedFields to avoid persisting bad data):

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:

  versions:

  scope: Namespaced

        intorstr:
          x-kubernetes-int-or-string: true
---

kind: IntOrString

  name: int
intorstr: 1
---

customresource_handler.go:652] error building openapi models for intorstrings.stable.example.com: ERROR $root.definitions.com.example.stable.v1.IntOrString.properties.intorstr has invalid property: anyOf

body:
**What would you like to be added**:
Remove the need to call remote KMS for every new Secret.

**Why is this needed**:
Due to the serial processing of List requests, the initialization of informers may take significant time due to the large number of consecutive trips to KMS. For example, assuming a 40 milliseconds round-trip to a KMS and two thousand secrets, the initialization of an informer may take 80 seconds.

Relevant PRs:
Reduce the number of trips to KMS by caching DEKs. #87438
Transform from storage concurrently during List operation. #88633

title: "Services should be rejected when no endpoints exist" is flaky

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.
