body:
The test "`Services should be rejected when no endpoints exist`" is flaky. eg, currently on https://testgrid.k8s.io/presubmits-kubernetes-blocking#pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce there are 4 flakes in the last 10 days (or whatever it is):

- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/directory/pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce/1257830397484470272
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/directory/pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce/1257779311427981312
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/directory/pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce/1256390316848582660
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/directory/pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce/1253832987678609409

The problem is that the test assumes that *every* bad connection will be rejected with an ICMP Destination Unreachable, but in fact [the kernel rate-limits ICMP errors](https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/networking/ip-sysctl.txt):

```
icmp_ratelimit - INTEGER
	Limit the maximal rates for sending ICMP packets whose type matches
	icmp_ratemask (see below) to specific targets.
	0 to disable any limiting,
	otherwise the minimal space between responses in milliseconds.
	Note that another sysctl, icmp_msgs_per_sec limits the number
	of ICMP packets	sent on all targets.
	Default: 1000

...

icmp_ratemask - INTEGER
	Mask made of ICMP types for which rates are being limited.
	Significant bits: IHGFEDCBA9876543210
	Default mask:     0000001100000011000 (6168)

	Bit definitions (see include/linux/icmp.h):
		0 Echo Reply
		3 Destination Unreachable *
		4 Source Quench *
		5 Redirect
		8 Echo Request
		B Time Exceeded *
		C Parameter Problem *
		D Timestamp Request
		E Timestamp Reply
		F Info Request
		G Info Reply
		H Address Mask Request
		I Address Mask Reply

	* These are rate limited by default (see default mask above)
```

so depending on what else is going on, the ICMP replies expected by this test might get suppressed.

There is some variation on just how flaky this test is; it flakes much more in OpenShift than in upstream kubernetes. It's not clear yet if this is because of stuff in OpenShift or just because of different base Linux distros between the two test environments. (eg, OpenShift on RHEL 7 flakes much more than OpenShift on RHEL 8.)


So, minimally, the test should retry a few times so that it's more likely to get the expected result even when rate-limiting is happening.

Possibly we could rewrite the test so that rather than relying on _actually_ getting an ICMP Destination Unreachable, we just use iptables tracing to ensure that we are hitting the `-j REJECT` rule as expected, and call that good enough.

Although, either way, we're effectively saying that  "services should be rejected when no endpoints exist" is an ideal but not actually a promise...

/sig network
/priority important-soon

title: Pods in Node are deleted even if the NoExecute taint that triggered deletion is removed

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
**What happened**:

A Pod was scheduled for deletion because a taint w/ effect `NoExecute` was observed in the Node the Pod was assigned to, and after the taint is removed from the Node, the Pod scheduled deletion isn't canceled.

After scheduling pod deletion, the *`NoExecuteTaintManager` only cancels pod deletion if all `NoExecute` taints are removed from the node*, including any taints that the user relies on for their use-cases (example below).

**What you expected to happen**:

After the taint that triggered scheduling pod deletion is removed, `NoExecuteTaintManager` cancels the scheduled pod deletion.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

- A node `MyNode` is tainted w/ `OnlyForMyUsage:NoExecute`, so any workloads already assigned to it which don't tolerate this taint are evicted.
- A pod `MyPod` is created w/ tolerations: `OnlyForMyUsage:NoExecute` w/ unspecified `tolerationSeconds` and `NotReady:NoExecute` w/ `tolerationSeconds: 300`.
- `MyPod` is assigned to `MyNode`.
- At some point in time after the previous steps took place, `MyNode` is tainted as `NotReady:NoExecute`.
- `NoExecuteTaintManager` gets an update event for `MyNode` and observes two `NoExecute` taints. It proceeds to calculate the minimum time (in seconds) that `MyPod` tolerates for the two taints which at this point is 300 seconds, and marks `MyPod` for deletion in ~300 seconds - this happens in-memory, in a timed-queue.
- At some point in time after the previous steps took place, and before the 300 seconds trigger happen, `NotReady:NoExecute` taint is removed from `MyNode`.
-  `NoExecuteTaintManager` gets an update event for `MyNode` and observes only one `NoExecute` taint, `OnlyForMyUsage:NoExecute`. It proceeds to calculate the minimum time (in seconds) that `MyPod` tolerates for the this taint which is _infinity_, and returns, not canceling the previous deletion. It *completely ignores the fact that the taint that triggered `MyPod` deletion is no longer observed*.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

- Worked w/ @bobveznat to figure this out after all pods in a node got evicted without apparent reason.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.17.3 (but looking at the code seems to affect all of 1.17.x and 1.18.x and master.
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: N/A
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): N/A
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 5.x
- Install tools: N/A

- Others: N/A

body:
With the `IPv6DualStack` feature gate disabled, kube-controller-manager accepts a `--node-cidr-mask-size` argument, but with `IPv6DualStack` enabled, it only accepts `--node-cidr-mask-size-ipv4` and `--node-cidr-mask-size-ipv6` and rejects `--node-cidr-mask-size`.

title: HPA conversion serializes internal struct to annotation

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/autoscaling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Autoscaling.

labels.name: kind/api-change
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to adding, removing, or otherwise changing an API

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

body:
**What happened**:
Found while fixing #88738 in #89963

The internal Spec.Behavior field is serialized to annotations when converting to v1 or v2beta1 HPA types. This causes several problems:
* The internal type does not have json tags, so the data is serialized upper-case
* The internal type is not guaranteed to preserve field layout/names, so the serialized data can become incompatible if that happens

To fix this, we should do something like the following:

1. Freeze the internal Behavior type schema
2. Update the unmarshaling in conversion to first try to unmarshal to a v2beta2 Behavior struct, and fall back to unmarshaling to an internal Behavior struct on error or if the result is an empty struct
3. Release
4. Update the marshaling in conversion to convert to a v2beta2 Behavior struct and marshal that to the annotation
5. Determine a way to force existing HPA objects with a serialized behavior annotation to remarshal on upgrade
6. Release
7. Unfreeze the internal Behavior type schema

@kubernetes/sig-autoscaling-api-reviews 
cc @DirectXMan12 @smarterclayton

title: Missing labels in kubelet's cAdvisor metrics

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

I'm using cri-containerd as container runtime for Kubernetes. Due to architecture needs I have containerd socket at custom location of `/u01/data/run/containerd/containerd.sock` instead of standard path `/run/containerd/containerd.sock`
My kubelet is started with parameters `--container-runtime=remote --container-runtime-endpoint=unix:///u01/data/run/containerd/containerd.sock` and works well with one exception.
With such configuration, cAdvisor in kubelet can't connect to containerd and does not populate container releated fields ie. in such metrics as `container_cpu_usage_seconds_total` or `container_memory_working_set_bytes` there is no label "container" that provides container name.

With container label missing, there is no data for container level resources consumption (`kubectl top pod --containers`) and it brakes queries used in Prometheus-Adapter / Metrics Server since they relay on that label:
```
containerQuery: sum(irate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{<<.LabelMatchers>>,container!="POD",container!="",pod!=""}[5m])) by (<<.GroupBy>>)  
containerQuery: sum(container_memory_working_set_bytes{<<.LabelMatchers>>,container!="POD",container!="",pod!=""}) by `(<<.GroupBy>>)
```

**What you expected to happen**:

Kubelet should pass socket provided in parameter `--container-runtime-endpoint` to its cAdvisor, where it can be used to connect to container runtime (containerd in my case.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Place your container runtime socket in other location than cAdvisor expects it, and pass it to  kubelet with `--container-runtime-endpoint` parameter. So it can not be at `/run/containerd/containerd.sock` when using cri-containerd or `unix:///var/run/docker.sock` when using Docker.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

I have two workarouds for now, but both are somewhat inacceptable:

1. Create directory `/run/containerd` with symbolic link pointing to real socket file. In my case `/run/containerd/containerd.sock` is symbolic link to `/u01/data/run/containerd/containerd.sock`
File `/run/containerd/containerd.sock` is default location for containerd socket in cAdvisor implementation https://github.com/google/cadvisor/blob/master/container/containerd/factory.go#L34 so it can find and use it. But I don't use the custom location for this socket to have it linked to the default one.

2. Use deprecated parameter to kubelet: `--containerd=/u01/data/run/containerd/containerd.sock`

That works because it points cadvisor to real containerd socket, and that value is passed to paramater mentioned above. Kubelet started with that parameter logs warning: 
`kubelet[6694]: Flag --containerd has been deprecated, This is a cadvisor flag that was mistakenly registered with the Kubelet. Due to legacy concerns, it will follow the standard CLI deprecation timeline before being removed.`

That is because that parameter is marked as DEPRECATED and mistakenly registered with the kubelet in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/kubelet/app/options/globalflags_linux.go#L55 and will be deleted in future releases of Kubernetes. So this is a very short term solution.

title: Kubelet should evict before hitting the allocatable threshold for PIDs

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: lifecycle/rotten
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

body:
This is a follow-up to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/89284.  cc @gongguan

/kind enhancement
/sig node
/priority important-soon

**What would you like to be added**:
The kubelet should perform eviction before the node allocatable threshold for PIDs is hit.  

**Why is this needed**:
In the current state, if the node allocatable threshold is hit before the node eviction threshold is hit, container processes will fail to fork indefinitely.  While this is better than the node running out of pids, it is still not ideal.

For memory, the kubelet solves this problem by performing eviction before the node allocatable threshold is hit.

We would need to add Pid stats to SystemContainers in the summary API. 
 It may require adding container-level pid metrics. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/apis/stats/v1alpha1/types.go#L40

This would needs to be set when constructing the summary API in both the [cri_stats_provider](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/stats/cri_stats_provider.go) and the (cadvisor_stats_provider)[https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/stats/cadvisor_stats_provider.go]

The eviciton manager needs to be taught a new signal, similar to the memory allocatable signal: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/eviction/helpers.go#L154

It will need a new eviction node e2e test for Pids in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e_node/eviction_test.go.  It will be similar to the Allocatable Memory eviction test, but for pids.

title: Filesystem resize is required after snapshot restore / volume clone

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
Kubernetes should resize filesystem on a volume when it's created as a clone of a smaller volume / smaller snapshot is restored into it.

Example:
1. User takes a snapshot of 1 GiB volume with ext3 filesystem on it.
2. User restores the snapshot into 2 GiB volume.
    2.1 CSI driver restores the snapshot into a bigger volume, but ext3 filesystem still uses only 1 GiB of space.
3. CSI driver should make sure that the filesystem on the volume has been resized before the volume is mounted into a pod.

There are few steps needed:

* [x] Clarify behavior of `CreateVolume` CSI call, https://github.com/container-storage-interface/spec/pull/452
* [ ] Update CSI drivers to the new behavior.
  * [x] Move filesystem resize code from kubernetes/kuberenetes to kubernetes/mount-utils, so all CSI drivers can re-use the same code https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/99039 
  * [x] Enhance the code above to compare the volume size from block device perspective and from filesystem perspective. See https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/aws-ebs-csi-driver/pull/595 for proof of concept. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/99042
  * [ ] File issues in all community CSI drivers that we care about & fix them.
* [ ] Update csi-tests to (optionally?) check for volume size when cloning / restoring snapshot to a bigger size. https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/csi-test/issues/325

title: CRI getFsInfo logs errors for valid filesystems mounted after kubelet start

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
**What happened**:

New overlay filesystems created for Pods after kubelet start trigger repeated error messages. For example:

```
cri_stats_provider.go:375] Failed to get the info of the filesystem with mountpoint "/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay/2243263dc8ba6c55d8867d3e47bcaaa145d15f0ace19420824d639d86defe2e3/merged": failed to get device for dir "/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay/2243263dc8ba6c55d8867d3e47bcaaa145d15f0ace19420824d639d86defe2e3/merged": could not find device with major: 0, minor: 83 in cached partitions map.
```

Error messages are logged every 10 seconds for every filesystem created after kubelet start. For large kubelet nodes, this issue creates an excessive amount of error logs.

**What you expected to happen**:

New overlay filesystems created for Pods after kubelet start should not log error messages.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Use cri_stats_provider with cri-o and configure overlay storage. UsingLegacyCadvisorStats() needs to return false per https://github.com/cri-o/cri-o/pull/3054 for cri_stats_provider to be used. Start with an empty /var/lib/containers/storage and schedule Pods on the node.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

As part of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/59475, cadvisor.GetFsInfoByFsUUID() was changed to cadvisor.GetDirFsInfo() in getFsInfo(); however, the test for cadvisorfs.ErrNoSuchDevice was not modified, changing how getFsInfo() handles a cache miss from cadvisor. 

cadvisor caches UUIDs/partitions/mounts on kubelet start and the cache is never refreshed. Given that it's expected that getFsInfo() will fail to retrieve data from cadvisor (see comments in ImageFsStats() and https://github.com/kubernetes/heapster/issues/1793), this condition should not be logged as an error. Alternatively, cadvisor fs could be modified to refresh on cache miss enabling getFsInfo() to return data on these filesystems.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.18.6
- CRI: CRI-O

https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/migrating-to-v1-metadata-server

>Warning: The v0.1 and v1beta1 metadata server endpoints are deprecated and scheduled for shutdown on September 30, 2020.

This test (which runs in most e2e jobs that run on GCE): https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/auth/metadata_concealment.go#L34

Schedules a container that runs this: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/images/metadata-concealment/check_metadata_concealment.go

Resulting in a number of legacy metadata endpoints getting hit.

To see if this test is going to start failing across all release branches on Sep 30th, we could try disabling the endpoints ahead of time via: https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/storing-retrieving-metadata#disable-legacy-endpoints. In fact https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/69593 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/70253 added support for expecting different results based on whether `disable-legacy-endpoints` is set.  

My concern is the test expects 200 for some root endpoints, and 403 for disabled endpoints. However the e-mail I received as a GCP customer tells me any legacy endpoints may return 404.

I'm inclined to suggest we remove the legacy endpoints from the check, bump the image version, and cherry-pick use of the new image version back to all release-branches.

title: node e2e test tags: dedupe [Node.*Feature:Foo][Feature:Foo] anti-pattern

body:
turning https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/94231#discussion_r478088074 into an issue

ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-testing/e2e-tests.md#kinds-of-tests

The `[NodeFeature:Foo]`, `[NodeSpecialFeature:Foo]`, `[NodeAlphaFeature:Foo]` tags are undocumented, and probably shouldn't exist.  They've led to an anti-pattern of `[NodeAlphaFeature:Foo][Feature:Foo]` in tests because `[Feature:.+]` is part of a commonly used skip-regex used by jobs that want to run "the default" set of e2e tests.

Instead of `[NodeAlphaFeature:Foo][Feature:Foo]`, let's use `[NodeAlphaFeature][Feature:Foo]` (and same for the other tags).  This retains the ability to:
- skip non-default features in most e2e jobs (skip `[Feature:.+]`)
- focus on all node alpha features (focus `[NodeAlphaFeature]`)
- focus/skip a specific node alpha feature (focus/skip `[NodeAlphaFeature][Feature:Foo]`)

https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/blob/4c9668b157f83ba4bcad2b9c67c307cbb92feeba/config/jobs/kubernetes/sig-node/node-kubelet.yaml#L234 leads me to believe this is the way things used to be? I'm not clear how or why they've evolved to where they are now

I suggest PR's to kubernetes/test-infra to use the old+new tags first, then PR's to this repo to migrate to new tags, then removal of old tags from kubernetes/test-infra.  It would be preferable if we could do this across all actively supported release branches.

/priority important-soon
/area test
FYI @alejandrox1 (is there a test tag hygiene issue to link to?)

/sig node
FYI @SergeyKanzhelev @vpickard (node ci group)

title: Allow ratcheting validation on custom resources

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
(hoisted from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/94060#issuecomment-677644185)

To support improving validation on a custom resource definition when there is existing persisted custom resource data that only passes the old less restrictive validation, allow a CR update that fails custom CRD schema validation IFF the existing object fails the custom CRD schema validation with identical errors (object-level ratcheting)

---

original description:

<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:
The ability to make updates to certain fields that are used in the deletion flow (like (ownerReferences, finalizers, managedFields) ), on objects that would otherwise fail validation.

**Why is this needed**:
For the VolumeSnapshot CRDs, we wanted to introduce stricter validation on some fields, but found it very difficult to accomplish this in a way that could retain backwards compatibility. The procedure we came up with was:

1. Introduce a validating webhook for an existing v1beta1 version that does ratcheting validation - existing invalid objects continue to be invalid while new objects or updates to valid objects that would cause them to be invalid are rejected. Proactively detect and reach out to consumers to clean up their invalid objects.
2. 1+ releases later, add v1 as a serving version, but keep v1beta as the storage version, so that we have the ability to rollback the CRD schema to drop v1 if that's causing trouble in the controllers.
3. Once we are 100% sure no invalid objects exist in the cluster, update the storage version to v1.

The main challenge right now is that we cannot upgrade the storage version to v1 until we are absolutely sure no invalid objects exist in the cluster. Otherwise, updates like removing finalizers would fail validation.

xref: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1902#discussion_r468782652

title: [sig-node] TestInvalidPodFiltered flakes with "Expected no update in channel" error

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: kind/flake
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a flaky test.

body:
**Which test(s) are flaking**:

TestInvalidPodFiltered

**Reason for failure**:

```
--- FAIL: TestInvalidPodFiltered (0.00s)
    config_test.go:126: Expected no update in channel, Got types.PodUpdate{Pods:[]*v1.Pod{(*v1.Pod)(0xc0000b4000)}, Op:1, Source:"test"}
FAIL
```

This is flaking rarely enough that it is not caught by our CI jobs, which currently tolerate up to 2 unit test failures per run (!).

With that toleration removed in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/93605, this flake has been seen (https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/93605/pull-kubernetes-bazel-test/1293289839906525184).

Reproducible with the following steps:

1. Build a test binary for the affected package:

```
go test -race -c ./pkg/kubelet/config
```

2. Stress the affected test using the [stress](https://godoc.org/golang.org/x/tools/cmd/stress) tool:

```
stress ./config.test -test.run TestInvalidPodFiltered
```

5. Once failures are seen, look at the logs to see the details about the error:

```sh
ls -lat $TMPDIR/go-stress*
cat $TMPDIR/go-stress...<filename>
```

/sig node
cc @kubernetes/sig-node-test-failures

<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
kube-controller-manager got into a state where it was not assigning a value to `spec.podCIDR` on newly added nodes. This occurred during an upgrade from 1.15 to 1.16.

**What you expected to happen**:
Expected behavior would be that kube-controller-manager assigned a podCIDR

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
We have been unable to systematically reproduce this but we saw the same behavior on at least 3 clusters.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

We replace instances with new ones during the upgrade process. Here's the sequence of events that we observed on the 3 master nodes that we run (A, B, C):

- At the start of the upgrade A was the leader for kube-controller-manager
- A was torn down and B became the the leader
- A was upgraded from 1.15 to 1.16
- B was torn down
- A became the leader, running 1.16 while the remaining control plane components continued running 1.15

At this point over the next 15-20 minutes the controller manager running 1.16 showed the following error for each node in the cluster:

E0625 15:59:37.100676       1 range_allocator.go:364] Failed to update node node-8c-192-168-40-34.novalocal PodCIDR to [172.16.189.0/24] after multiple attempts: failed to patch node CIDR: Node "node-8c-192-168-40-34.novalocal" is invalid: [spec.podCIDR: Forbidden: node updates may not change podCIDR except from "" to valid, []: Forbidden: node updates may only change labels, taints, or capacity (or configSource, if the DynamicKubeletConfig feature gate is enabled)]

As workers nodes were replaced they received names that were already in the list of failed nodes and no attempt was made by the controller manager to assign a podCIDR to them, leading to failure of calico at startup.

title: Instance metadata region mismatch

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.description: Issues or PRs related to azure provider

labels.name: sig/cloud-provider
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Cloud Provider.

body:
**What happened**:

In certain azure regions instance metadata is returning location in camel case. This metadata is being propagated to nodes label
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/539b0a5a0f8c1d96ee6752f2aa5d6d949eb0f513/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/node/node_controller.go#L501-L510. This results in label on the node:
`failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/region=CanadaCentral`

Cloud-provider config code base uses location as lower case.

In these regions there instance metadata service returns CamelCase we have an issue with provisioning storage/PVCs.

Storage controller reads location from cloud-config, and is trying to match with Node label:

```
oc get pv pvc-d8bef6f0-c06d-495b-addf-5122821625f5 -o json | jq ".spec.nodeAffinity.required.nodeSelectorTerms "
[
  {
    "matchExpressions": [
      {
        "key": "failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/region",
        "operator": "In",
        "values": [
          "canadacentral"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
]
```
Where nodes have `failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/region=CanadaCentral`
PVC provisioning fails.

```
Example from 3 different regions: curl -H Metadata:true --noproxy "*" "http://169.254.169.254/metadata/instance?api-version=2019-06-01" | jq .

CanadaCentral:
 "compute": {                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
    "azEnvironment": "AzurePublicCloud",                                                                                                                                                                                                      
    "customData": "",                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
    "location": "CanadaCentral",                                                                                                                                                                                                              
    "name": "master-0",                                                                                                                                                                                                        

EastUS:
  "compute": {
    "azEnvironment": "AzurePublicCloud",
    "customData": "",
    "location": "eastus",
    "name": "master-0",

WestEurope:
{
  "compute": {
    "azEnvironment": "AzurePublicCloud",
    "customData": "",
    "location": "westeurope",
    "name": "master-0",
```

**What you expected to happen**:

Success

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

1. Create a cluster in Azure Canada Central. 
2. Set cloud provider `UseInstanceMetadata=True`
3. Create PVC using dynamic storage class.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

Fix required here is from 2 parts:
1. Location, read from instance metadata service in cloud provider code should be set to lowercase.
2. Location, set/read from cloud-config should be set to lower case so we have consistency 

/cc @feiskyer @andyzhangx

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

Whenever a node is added or updated, there is a small window where pods are scheduled to that node, before any beta labels are applied to it. This can cause issues with pods that are queued up to be scheduled and that have a NodeAffinity (in our case) to the now deprecated `beta.kubernetes.io/os` label.

**What you expected to happen**:

The proper labels to be applied to workers before the scheduling of pods on that node.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

(Not 100 percent success rate)
- deploy 1.19 cluster with no workers
- apply a deployment with a node affinity for the beta.kubernetes.io/os label
- add worker

**Anything else we need to know?**:

I have been told this step used to be done on the worker side, but is now done on the master side. Which could explain why this is happening. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.19.0-rc.2/pkg/controller/nodelifecycle/node_lifecycle_controller.go#L1534-L1578

title: Plugins should access listers during instantiation

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

body:
SelectorSpread plugin currently accesses listers directly from SharedInformer: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/selectorspread/selector_spread.go#L182-L185

The issue is that if we don't access the lister before the informer is started, the lister will never be populated. The informer is started right after scheduler initialization, and so we have to access the listers in the instantiation function New of the plugin.

This should be checkerrypicked to 1.18 as well.

/sig scheduling
/priority important-soon
/assign @adtac

**What happened**:
the CRI-O CI tests have been in a bad shape recently. In debugging, I have found that the kubelet logs are filled with:
```
Timed out while waiting for StopUnit(kubepods-besteffort-pod867fd309_03ba_4715_a044_29393f495cea.slice) completion signal from dbus. Continuing...
```
```shell

352562
```
AFAICT, this is from a combination of bumping to go 1.14.4, and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/a03db636daef0417218ef8c108c0a6530d2ef368

as I ran two different PRs that dropped each of these commits, and there were no similar problems.

I am fairly certain this is NOT a problem with kubernetes directly, but rather some odd interaction between go 1.14 and either libcontainer, go-systemd, or godbus. but I figure it can be opened here to start the conversation

**What you expected to happen**:
StopUnit should not time out

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
run a node with cgroupv1

build hyperkube with go 1.14.4 (as is now required)

body:
For CVE-2020-8554, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/97076, we decided we couldn't patch it in-tree, and instead provided workarounds to disable (or allowlist) the feature through admission controls. Now that the issue is public, I'd like to open the conversation about a long-term fix.

Unless we missed something (entirely possible), I see a few possible paths forward:

1. Decide to stop supporting external IPs, deprecate and eventually remove the feature
2. Attempt to redesign the external IP feature, deprecate the old behavior, and manage the migration to the new feature
3. Accept the current state, and promote the [externalip-webhook](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/externalip-webhook) to a built-in admission controller
4. Accept the current state, and support the [externalip-webhook](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/externalip-webhook) as a long-term solution

/sig network architecture
/area security
/priority important-soon

title: Fibre channel volume plugin corrupts volumes on detach

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
**What happened**:
When a pod that uses a multipath Fibre Channel (FC) volume is deleted, the volume gets sometimes corrupted:

```
[ 6489.218162] XFS (dm-152): Metadata CRC error detected at xfs_inobt_read_verify+0x79/0xb0 [xfs], xfs_inobt block 0x18
[ 6489.218456] XFS (dm-152): metadata I/O error: block 0x18 ("xfs_trans_read_buf_map") error 74 numblks 8
[ 6489.222223] XFS (dm-152): Metadata CRC error detected at xfs_inobt_read_verify+0x79/0xb0 [xfs], xfs_inobt block 0x18
[ 6489.222589] XFS (dm-152): metadata I/O error: block 0x18 ("xfs_trans_read_buf_map") error 74 numblks 8
[ 6489.222890] XFS (dm-152): Metadata CRC error detected at xfs_inobt_read_verify+0x79/0xb0 [xfs], xfs_inobt block 0x18
[ 6489.223154] XFS (dm-152): metadata I/O error: block 0x18 ("xfs_trans_read_buf_map") error 74 numblks 8
[ 6489.505911] XFS (dm-152): Internal error XFS_WANT_CORRUPTED_GOTO at line 1637 of file fs/xfs/libxfs/xfs_alloc.c. Caller xfs_free_extent+0xaa/0x140 [xfs]
[ 6489.506006] [<ffffffffc03a13db>] xfs_error_report+0x3b/0x40 [xfs]
```

**What you expected to happen**:
No filesystem corruption.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. Set up multipath FC volume + its PV+PVC.
2. Use it in a pod that "aggressively" writes to it (`dd if=/dev/random of=/mnt/the-mounted-volume/foo`)
3. Delete the pod.
4. Start the pod again.
-> sometimes the volume is corrupted.

**Anything else we need to know?**:
Red Hat recommends to flush/delete the multipath device before deleting its individual paths (`multipath -f`): https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/7/html/storage_administration_guide/removing_devices

iSCSI volume plugin already does so: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fbe5daed7380ae640c2c6e66530593e3de67ce4b/pkg/volume/iscsi/iscsi_util.go#L559
We need to do the same in FC plugin too.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.20.beta2
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): "CentOS Linux 7 (Core)"
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 3.10.0-957.12.2.el7.x86_64
- Install tools: local-up-cluster.sh is enough

body:
**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. Make /var/lib/kubelet a symlink
    ```
    mkdir -p /tmp/data/kubelet
    ln -s  /tmp/data/kubelet /var/lib/kubelet
    ```

1. Run  kubelet
    ```
    hack/local-up-cluster.sh
    ```

1. Create a block PVC + a pod that uses it.
1. Delete the pod.

-> The pod is `Terminating` forever. In kubelet logs:
```
W1126 13:11:25.728798    4415 volume_path_handler_linux.go:61] couldn't find loopback device which takes file descriptor lock. Skip detaching device. device path: "/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/aws-ebs/volumeDevices/aws:/us-east-
1d/vol-0b1729094ca87a001/7e04362d-39c9-4417-874a-618d5c9a9924"
```

The reason is that `losetup -j /var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/aws-ebs/volumeDevices/aws:/us-east-1d/vol-0b1729094ca87a001/7e04362d-39c9-4417-874a-618d5c9a9924` shows:
```
/dev/loop0: [0005]:53278 (/tmp/data/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/aws-ebs/volumeDevices/aws:/us-east-1d/vol-0b1729094ca87a001/7e04362d-39c9-4417-874a-618d5c9a9924)
```

kubelet can't find `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins...` there, because losetup shows real path `/tmp/data/kubelet/plugins...`.

Related:

- Part of: https://github.com/kubernetes/k8s.io/issues/1522

We should migrate away from the google.com-owned gcr.io/kubernetes-e2e-test-images and instead use the community-owned k8s.gcr.io/e2e-test-images repository.

Affected images are those that use `E2eRegistry` or `E2eVolumeRegistry`.  ~We may also want to consider pushing `DockerLibraryRegistry` images into k8s.gcr.io/e2e-test-images~ (moved to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/97027)

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1d4c0ad6f33f2bc42555becdb5d74e570c0730f3/test/utils/image/manifest.go#L203-L245

My guess at the steps required:
- push old images from `gcr.io/kubernetes-e2e-test-images` to `gcr.io/k8s-staging-e2e-test-images`
- promote images used by latest supported patch releases and in-development release
- create postsubmit jobs for each test/image dir (done via https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/96432)
- PR change values of `E2eRegistry` and `E2eVolumeRegistry` to `k8s.gcr.io/e2e-test-images`, remove `PromoterE2eRegistry`
- subsequent trial PRs to run through building/promoting an e2e image

This is release-notes worthy and possibly announcement worthy.

title: Process Handle Leak on Windows Nodes

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Windows.

labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
**What happened**:

We have an internal hybrid Kubernetes Cluster which is setup with kubeadm, containing 3 master nodes, 3 linux worker nodes, and 2 windows worker nodes. During the process of migrating internal workloads from our old application platform (Windows Scheduled Tasks) to Kubernetes, we noticed that after a while the windows nodes become unresponsive because of continuously using 100% CPU, if they don't run out of memory first. Apart from the flannel and kube-proxy daemonsets, we currently run only Kubernetes Jobs on these nodes (via TZCronjob).

We noticed the process handle count increasing continually, and with it memory and CPU consumption. This does not correspond to the number of active pods, but rather increases over time with every pod that gets created. Which are a lot since we have jobs that are triggered every minute.

I managed to reproduce the resource leak with a 3 node cluster on the Azure platform, without even creating a single job. I just installed the cluster, activated monitoring for the Guest OS via the Azure facilities and let it sit for a few days. This is what it looks like now:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8522449/98729083-a976c100-239a-11eb-9c64-bac915020505.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8522449/98729254-ecd12f80-239a-11eb-96d1-f688e377e82c.png)

This is all that is running on the cluster: 
```
PS C:\WINDOWS\System32> kubectl get pods --all-namespaces
NAMESPACE     NAME                                    READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
kube-system   coredns-f9fd979d6-gkg25                 1/1     Running            0          11d
kube-system   coredns-f9fd979d6-hwbcd                 1/1     Running            0          11d
kube-system   etcd-kubemaster-01                      1/1     Running            0          11d
kube-system   kube-apiserver-kubemaster-01            1/1     Running            0          11d
kube-system   kube-controller-manager-kubemaster-01   1/1     Running            0          11d
kube-system   kube-flannel-ds-626q7                   1/1     Running            8          11d
kube-system   kube-flannel-ds-kq4pz                   1/1     Running            0          11d
kube-system   kube-flannel-ds-windows-amd64-q4lmm     1/1     Running            0          11d
kube-system   kube-proxy-p42l8                        1/1     Running            0          11d
kube-system   kube-proxy-windows-cxklq                0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   3000       11d
kube-system   kube-proxy-x8msx                        1/1     Running            0          11d
kube-system   kube-scheduler-kubemaster-01            1/1     Running            0          11d
```

I guess the kube-proxy crashloop created enough pods over time so I didn't even need to create a job to see the resource drain.

**What you expected to happen**:

The system resource consumption should correspond to the number of active pods. Instead it continuously grows over time, regardless of the number of currently active pods.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

I was able to reproduce this on the Microsoft Azure platform doing the following:

  * Create 3 VMs (I used the size Standard_B2s for each, don't know if it matters)
    * 2 VMs using the Ubuntu 20.04 Server image from Canonical (you probably only need the Kubernetes master for a minimal repro though)
    * 1 VM using the Windows Server 2019 Datacenter image with containers

  * Setup the Kubernetes Cluster with kubeadm using the documentation [here](https://kubernetes.io/docs/setup/production-environment/tools/kubeadm/create-cluster-kubeadm/) and [here](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubeadm/adding-windows-nodes/), designating one of the Linux VMs as master, using an overlay network with flannel as CNI
  * Setup the Azure monitoring to see resource usage of the windows machine
  * Create a Kubernetes Cronjob that continuously creates new pods in short order on the windows node (or, as in my case, send the kube-proxy into a crash loop. I don't know how it got there - at the start it was working properly - but the current error message is "failed to make a new HNSEndpoint: error while ipam.ExecAdd: failed to allocate for range 0: no IP addresses available in range set: 10.244.2.1-10.244.2.254", so I guess specifying a small enough IP range for the container network would be an easy repro)
  * Wait a few days to see the resource drain. I suppose this can be sped up by creating more jobs/pods

**Anything else we need to know?**:

Please tell me if the repro works for you. I can provide more details if it does not. If this is a known issue, I was not able to find it in the issue tracker. If there is a workaround I should try, please tell. The only thing that works for us right now is automatically draining and restarting the Windows VMs every few days.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.19.3
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: Microsoft Azure VMs (repro), VMware vSphere ESX VMs (original issue)
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): Windows Server 2019
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools: kubeadm
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug): sigwindowstools/flannel:0.12.0
- Others:

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**: 

Using `kubectl debug --set-image` without specifying `--image` should modify existing container images without trying to create a new one. Instead it tries to create a new container and returns an error that `--image` isn't set:

```
% kubectl debug myapp --copy-to=myapp-debug --set-image=*=ubuntu
Defaulting debug container name to debugger-mfzpc.
error: you must specify image when creating new container
```

**What you expected to happen**:

This command should change all container images to `ubuntu` instead of returning an error.

/kind bug
/priority important-soon

<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

In k8s 1.19.2

If the seccomp annotations of psp doesn't contain `runtime/default`, pod with seccomp annotations `seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod: 'docker/default` would not start with error:
```
pods "coredns-7b78847794-vzmmz" is forbidden: PodSecurityPolicy: unable to validate pod: [pod.metadata.annotations[container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/coredns]: 
Forbidden: runtime/default is not an allowed seccomp profile. Valid values are docker/default]'
```

psp with `runtime/default` works
```
metadata:
  name: kube-system-psp
  annotations:
    seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/allowedProfileNames: 'runtime/default, docker/default'
    seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/defaultProfileName:  'docker/default'
```

psp without `runtime/default` doesn't work
```
metadata:
  name: kube-system-psp
  annotations:
    seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/allowedProfileNames: 'docker/default'
    seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/defaultProfileName:  'docker/default'
```

Is this due to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/90948 ?

**What you expected to happen**:
In k8s 1.18, psp annotations without `runtime/default` works. I think in k8s 1.19, it should also work.

**What happened**:
While I was watching grafana for a single run, I noticed that GET requests are reported as LIST requests, e.g. grafana shows ~1K QPS for LIST of pods
![8vS47hgQ9GxtJhL](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2559168/95988213-dd58d800-0e28-11eb-9687-7c7c80dbc373.png)
while kube-apiserver's logs show:

title: volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node never cleared for non-existent nodes on PVC without PVs

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon

body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:

* PVC was created, & pod consuming this PVC. PVC is using the WaitForFirstConsumer policy. 
* controller with SA `persistent-volume-binder` in `kube-system` namespace edited the PVC, attached the following labels:

```
    volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-provisioner: ebs.csi.aws.com
    volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node: ip-10-0-92-212.ec2.internal
```
* PVC is pending phase, it wasn't bound to the PV. 
* The node in question was deleted, by cluster autoscaler 1.20 before the PV was provisioned and attached to the node. 
* The annotation remains
* The https://github.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/tree/master/cluster-autoscaler v1.20 cannot scale up the node since there's the `volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node` annotation pointing to the deleted node. The cluster autoscaler sees this PVC bound to the Pod already bound to the node, but the node isn't there. 
* The pod stays forever in pending state
* Deleting this annotation allows cluster autoscaler to do its job, scaling up the cluster and the pod gets scheduled on a newly provisioned node. 
* The end. 

#### What you expected to happen:

* Upon node deletion, the `volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node` annotation should be cleared. 

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

* You're playing with race conditions, but the previously mention story should be sometimes replicable. 

#### Anything else we need to know?:

#### Environment:

title: NodeStage is not called after NodeUnstage error

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

1. Run a pod that uses a CSI volume that supports NodeStage (such as Ceph RBD)
2. Delete the pod
3. The CSI driver times out when processing NodeUnstage call. It is un-staging the volume in the background and eventually succeeds. (Ceph RBD talks to the storage backed in NodeUnstage and there was some network disruption)
4. Create new pod that uses the same volume on the same node

#### What happened:
kubelet calls only NodePublish. Since the previous NodeUnstage did not succeed, it wrongly assumes that the volume is still NodeStaged.

#### What you expected to happen:
kubelet calls NodeStage + NodePublish, because it can't be sure if the volume is staged or not.
After NodeUnstage error, we should mark volumes as uncertain to make sure NodeStage is called after NodeUnstage returns error.

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.21

#### What happened:
I ran conformance tests on a cluster that had a controller enabled that syncs a configmap across all clusters. It failed:
```
/workspace/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/framework/framework.go:629
Mar  5 11:07:41.670: Unexpected error:
    <*errors.StatusError | 0xc001452500>: {
        ErrStatus: {
            TypeMeta: {Kind: "", APIVersion: ""},
            ListMeta: {
                SelfLink: "",
                ResourceVersion: "",
                Continue: "",
                RemainingItemCount: nil,
            },
            Status: "Failure",
            Message: "configmaps \"test-configmap\" is forbidden: exceeded quota: test-quota, requested: configmaps=1, used: configmaps=2, limited: configmaps=2",
            Reason: "Forbidden",
            Details: {
                Name: "test-configmap",
                Group: "",
                Kind: "configmaps",
                UID: "",
                Causes: nil,
                RetryAfterSeconds: 0,
            },
            Code: 403,

occurred
/workspace/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/apimachinery/resource_quota.go:336

body:
#### What happened:

- My exec plugin overrode the static certs I had in my kubeconfig.

#### What you expected to happen:

- The static certs I had in my kubeconfig should take precedent over whatever is configured by my exec plugin.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

With admin-like privileges, do the following.
```bash
# Generate CSR.
openssl req -nodes -subj /CN=some-username -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout /tmp/aaa.key -out /tmp/aaa.csr

# Create CSR.
cat <<EOF | kubectl replace -f -
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: aaa
spec:
  request: $(cat /tmp/aaa.csr | base64 | tr -d '\n')
  signerName: kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client
  usages: [client auth]
EOF

# Issue certificate.
kubectl certificate approve aaa
kubectl get csr aaa -o jsonpath={.status.certificate} | base64 -d > /tmp/aaa.crt

# Make request with both certificate and exec plugin that returns token.
cat <<EOF >/tmp/aaa.sh
#!/bin/bash
echo '{"kind":"ExecCredential","apiVersion":"client.authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1","status":{"clientKeyData":"bad","clientCertificateData":"bad"}}'
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/aaa.sh
kubectl config set-credentials aaa --client-certificate=/tmp/aaa.crt --client-key=/tmp/aaa.key --exec-api-version client.authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1 --exec-command=/tmp/aaa.sh
kubectl --user aaa get pods
```

#### Anything else we need to know?:

- This seems like unexpected behavior because other statically configured credentials (i.e., basic auth, bearer token) take precedent over the stuff returned by the exec plugin.
- This was pointed out by @enj when he was reviewing some exec plugin integration tests.

body:
#### What happened:

A PDB object with an invalid selector was allowed to be created. This was the root cause of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/98702

#### What you expected to happen:

Invalid selectors to be rejected by API validation, and all selectors that pass `ValidateLabelSelector()` to be able to be passed to `LabelSelectorAsSelector` without error.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

create the following PDB:
```yaml
apiVersion: policy/v1beta1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
 name: mypdb
spec:
 minAvailable: 2
 selector:
   matchExpressions:
   - key: name
     operator: In
     values: ["test","bad#value"]
```

Observe events emitted by the controller manager because the selector is invalid:

`4s          Warning   NoPods   poddisruptionbudget/mypdb   Failed to get pods: values[1][name]: Invalid value: "bad#value": a valid label must be an empty string or consist of alphanumeric characters, '-', '_' or '.', and must start and end with an alphanumeric character (e.g. 'MyValue',  or 'my_value',  or '12345', regex used for validation is '(([A-Za-z0-9][-A-Za-z0-9_.]*)?[A-Za-z0-9])?')`

#### Anything else we need to know?:

Tightening this validation function in place will be almost impossible to do compatibly.

A second method that validates the delta will need to be created (or changing the signature of this function to indicate if label values should be validated) . Validation methods that want to tighten validation will have to do so using validation ratcheting:
* apply tighter validation on create
* apply tighter validation on update *only* if the existing object also passes the tighter validation

/sig api-machinery 
as primary owner of the package

There are many APIs that use this validation method. Tagging other sigs with affected APIs:

* admission webhook namespace and object selectors
* statefulset, daemonset, deployment, replicaset, job selectors
* pvc selector
* pod affinity selector
* network policy pod and namespace selectors
* pdb pod selector
* rbac AggregationRule selector
* csi NodeTopology selector

/sig auth apps networking storage

- [x] Ephemeral Containers API has been in alpha for at least 2 releases.
  - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.16.md#alpha
- [x] Ephemeral Containers support namespace targeting.
  - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/84731
- [x] Metrics for Ephemeral Containers are added to existing contain creation metrics.
  - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/99000
- [x] CLI using Ephemeral Containers for debugging checked into a Kubernetes project repository (e.g. in `kubectl` or a `kubectl` plugin).
  - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/88004

- [x]  Ephemeral Container creation is covered by e2e-node tests.
  - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/103372
- [x] Update via `/ephemeralcontainers` validates entire PodSpec to protect against future bugs
  - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105293

Implementation Checklist:

- [x] Update API documentation
- [x] Enable feature gate by default

labels.name: priority/important-soon

body:
Many e2e tests today have a `[sig-foo]` tag in their name, which lets us know which sig is responsible for fixing failing or flaky e2e tests.

However, not all tests have such a tag.  We should:
- assign `[sig-foo]` tags to all e2e tests that don't yet have them
- enforce that no new e2e tests can be added without a `[sig-foo]` tag in their name

EDIT: proposed path forward (pulled out of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/98326#issuecomment-782744493 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/98326#issuecomment-783571637)
- rearrange e2e tests into sig-owned packages, 
  - `test/e2e/{sig}/...` - e2e tests that run as part of node_e2e
  - `test/e2e/common/{sig}/...` - e2e tests that run as part of e2e and node_e2e
  - add `test/e2e/common/imports.go` that imports sub-packages so e2e binaries can continue to import `test/e2e/common` to pick up test definitions ([example](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/cloud/imports.go))
  - ensure each sig-owned package has:
    - a package-local `func SIGDescribe(text string, body func()) bool` ([example](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/apimachinery/framework.go))
    - an OWNERS files with sig members and `labels: sig/{sig}` ([example](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/network/OWNERS)
- follow these conventions:
  - top-level `SIGDescribe` calls are required, nested `SIGDescribe` calls are not allowed
    - remove usage of `SIGFooDescribe(text)`, `SIGDescribe(sig, text)`, `KubeDescribe("[sig-foo]" + text)`, and `ginkgo.Describe("[sig-foo]")` in favor of `SIGDescribe`
  - nested `ginkgo.Describe` calls are ok, nested `SIGDescribe` calls are not
- enforce these conventions via some combination of:
  - static analysis
  - regex enforcement against names output during a `e2e.test --dry-run` run
- while we are here, `KubeDescribe` is vestigial and can be removed (ref: (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/98326#issuecomment-781663980))


EDIT: Everything now conforms to policies defined above
```
$ ./hack/verify-e2e-test-ownership.sh
# ...
run at datetime: 2021-03-17T20:46:49Z
based on commit: ffb47ca3960 - 2021-03-17T16:19:25-04:00 - add verify-e2e-test-ownership.sh

[]
INFO: e2e tests in total                                : 5745
PASS: ..failing should pass all policies                : 0
PASS: ..failing must not use nested SIGDescribe         : 0
PASS: ..failing should not have multiple [sig-foo] tags : 0
PASS: ..failing must use top-level SIGDescribe          : 0
PASS: ..failing must start with [sig-foo]               : 0
PASS
```

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/99698 will close this out by adding a blocking test and docs to test/e2e/README.md

/sig testing
/area test
for enforcement (FYI @BenTheElder)
/sig architecture
/area conformance
some of these are conformance tests (FYI @derekwaynecarr @dims @johnbelamaric)
/wg reliability
for helping determine appropriate sig ownership (FYI @deads2k @stevekuznetsov @wojtek-t )
/sig release
since this is relevant to figuring out who should fix release-blocking tests (FYI @kubernetes/ci-signal)
/priority important-soon
/milestone v1.21
I think it's reasonable to aim to accomplish this prior to code freeze for v1.21

title: Inconsistent garbage collection behavior when any ownerReference is unresolvable and the parent is deleted

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
**What happened**:

- create a namespaced parent object (for example a `Secret`)
- delete the parent object
- create a cluster-scoped object (for example. an `ApiService`) with the parent as an `ownerReference`, which is unresolvable since the parent is namespaced.
- create a namespaced object (for example another `Secret`) in the same namespace, with the parent as an `ownerReference`, which should be valid.
- The namespaced child and the cluster-scoped child are not garbage collected.

**What you expected to happen**:

The namespaced child should be garbage collected immediately after being created, the cluster-scoped child should not be.

**Reproduction**:

**Setup**:
`kubectl create namespace test-owner-reference`

parent-secret.yaml:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: parent-secret
  namespace: test-owner-reference
data:
  a: Yg==
```

`kubectl apply -f /path/to/parent-secret.yaml`
`kubectl get secrets/parent-secret -n test-owner-reference -o yaml | grep uid`

cluster-scoped-child.yaml:
```
apiVersion: apiregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: APIService
metadata:
  name: v1alpha1.cluster-scoped-child
  ownerReferences:
  - apiVersion: v1
     kind: Secret
     name: parent-secret
     uid: <parent uid>
  spec:
   group: cluster-scoped-child
   groupPriorityMinimum: 1000
   versionPriority: 15
   service:
     name: api
     namespace: cluster-scoped-child
   version: v1alpha1
```
namespaced-child.yaml
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: namespaced-child
  namespace: test-owner-reference
  ownerReferences:
    - apiVersion: v1
      kind: Secret
      name: parent-secret
      uid: <parent uid>
data:
  a: Yg==
```

**Scenario 1**:
1. In one terminal, run `kubectl get secrets -n test-owner-reference --watch`
2. In another, `run kubectl get apiservice --watch`
3. In a third, run `kubectl delete secrets/parent-secret -n test-owner-reference && kubectl apply -f /path/to/cluster-scoped-child.yaml && kubectl apply -f /path/to/namespaced-child.yaml`

See that the cluster scoped child and namespaced child are both created but not deleted.

**Scenario 2**:
1. In one terminal, run `kubectl get secrets -n test-owner-reference --watch`
3. In another, run `kubectl delete secrets/parent-secret -n test-owner-reference &&  kubectl apply -f /path/to/namespaced-child.yaml`

See that the namespaced child is created and immediately deleted.

My expectation is that the garbage collection of `namespaced-child` should not depend on `cluster-scoped-child`, however scenarios 1 and 2 do not seem consistent.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.20.0

title: Device manager silently fails to restore checkpoint after upgrading to 1.20+

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
#### What happened:
After upgrading kubelet from version <= 1.19 to version >= 1.20, the device manager will fail to restore its state from the checkpoint. The change was introduced in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/a8b8995ef241e93e9486d475126450f33f24ef4e .

The restore fails silently (it actually writes a warning in the logs, but keeps going). Because of this the device manager state is inconsistent up until the device plugins register themselves again, which can take minutes, depending on the specific device plugin. We seen up to 5 minutes on real clusters the for SRIOV device plugin.

Because of the inconsistent state, the kubelet will **NOT** update the device availability to zero, so the scheduler will send pods towards the inconsistent kubelet.
At admission time, the device manager allocation will not trigger, again because of the incosistent state, so pods will be admitted without device plugins actually being allocated to them.

#### What you expected to happen:
Any of the following wouls be acceptable
1. the kubelet recovers the checkpoint state correctly
2. the kubelet sets its own state as inconsistent, so pods aren't scheduled until the node heals
3. the kubelet sets its own state as inconsistent, so pods aret scheduled, but aren't admitted until the node heals

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):
1. run pods requesting devices on <= 1.19 kubelet
2. drain the node
3. upgrade the kubelet to a version >= 1.20
4. run pods on the upgraded node typically as soon as the node gets Ready

#### Anything else we need to know?:

The issue was discovered first in openshift, but turns out is not openshift specific.

The bug triggers only after a upgrade, so kubelet is stopped, updated (<= 1.19 to >= 1.20) and started again.
There are no more know ways to trigger this bug.

The updated kubelet fails to restore the checkpoint data. See this excerpt from the logs
```
Jun 15 07:31:49.743990 openshift-worker-1 hyperkube[4852]: I0615 07:31:49.743846    4852 manager.go:236] Starting Device Plugin manager

[...]

Jun 15 07:31:49.744795 openshift-worker-1 hyperkube[4852]: W0615 07:31:49.744770    4852 manager.go:244] Continue after failing to read checkpoint file. Device allocation info may NOT be up-to-date. Err: json: cannot unmarshal array into Go struct field PodDevicesEntry.Data.PodDeviceEntries.DeviceIDs of type checkpoint.DevicesPerNUMA
```
The kubelet keep going, but this means the internal devicemanager maps will be **completely** empty. The expected state after recovery is that the *key* of the relevant devices will be present.
This is a critical point to understand the impact of this bug.
After the failed recovery, the kubelet will happily run, but the node update callback (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.20.7/pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/manager.go#L516) will **not** update the node objects.

This is another critical point to understand the impact of this bug.
The expected behaviour is to reset the allocatable device counters to 0 (zero) up until the device plugins register themselves again.
So the scheduler will send pods on this node, while it should not (devices not ready).

In the pod admission flow, and we call `DeviceManager.Allocate()`, which ultimately calls `allocateContainerResources` https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.20.7/pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/manager.go#L830

Each loop, we have a call to `isDevicePluginResources` (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.20.7/pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/manager.go#L843). Problem is: exactly because the **empty healthyDevices** maps, it always return false.
Worth stressing that the bug is that the maps are completely empty. The expected flows is to have the **keys** in the map, but with zero values (until the device plugin registers itself again). Should that have been the case, an device allocation request should have been performed.

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): any kubernetes >= 1.20
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: any
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): any
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): any
- Install tools: N/A
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug): N/A
- Others: N/A

title: Windows Pod with RunAsUserName and a Projected Volume does not honor file permissions in the volume

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Windows.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
#### What happened:

When a Windows Pod is created with a Projected Volume and `RunAsUserName` set, file permissions are not handled in the projected volume. In addition if a Windows Pod is created with a Projected Volume and `RunAsUser` set, 
```yaml
    securityContext:
      runAsUser: 1000640000
      windowsOptions:
        runAsUserName: ContainerAdministrator
```
the Pod will be stuck at `ContainerCreating`:
```
E0611 17:38:46.666139    2260 atomic_writer.go:404] pod win-webserver/win-webserver-6dd6cd7d9-ng62b volume kube-api-access-62z59: unable to change file c:\var\lib\kubelet\pods\a7bddda2-a355-48cd-8ee2-71776d6de78f\volumes\kubernetes.io~projected\kube-api-access-62z59\..2021_06_11_17_38_46.035861910\token with owner 1000640000: chown c:\var\lib\kubelet\pods\a7bddda2-a355-48cd-8ee2-71776d6de78f\volumes\kubernetes.io~projected\kube-api-access-62z59\..2021_06_11_17_38_46.035861910\token: not supported by windows
E0611 17:38:46.666139    2260 atomic_writer.go:175] pod win-webserver/win-webserver-6dd6cd7d9-ng62b volume kube-api-access-62z59: error writing payload to ts data directory c:\var\lib\kubelet\pods\a7bddda2-a355-48cd-8ee2-71776d6de78f\volumes\kubernetes.io~projected\kube-api-access-62z59\..2021_06_11_17_38_46.035861910: chown c:\var\lib\kubelet\pods\a7bddda2-a355-48cd-8ee2-71776d6de78f\volumes\kubernetes.io~projected\kube-api-access-62z59\..2021_06_11_17_38_46.035861910\token: not supported by windows
```

#### What you expected to happen:

The Pod should go to `Running` with the project volume files having the correct container user ownership.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

Create a Windows Pod with a Projected Volume and `runAsUserName` set (optionally with runAsUser to cause the stuck at `ContainerCreating` issue).

#### Anything else we need to know?:

The KEP, [proposal for file permission handling in projected service account volume](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1598) and its [implementation](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/3db7275b549559696c42c0b5f51c9a2397e9571d) did not take Windows in to account. An [os.Chown()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/3db7275b549559696c42c0b5f51c9a2397e9571d#diff-f4218ebfe0ced84087844da9d87b126752414e347e727c0455687d69e8e3d912R403) was introduced which is not supported on Windows. In addition `RunAsUserName` being set on Windows Pods was not taken into account.

- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.21.1
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: AWS / Azure 
- OS: Windows Server 2019 1809
- Kernel:

title: Hitting 34s timeouts with server-side apply on large custom resource objects

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: priority/important-soon

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to WG API Expression.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
#### What happened:

Performing server-side apply on a CR of at least 700KB in size results in 34 second timeout with Kubernetes 1.19.10+ and Kubernetes 1.20+.

#### What you expected to happen:

Like the creation and deletion events, I expected the update event to take a minimal amount of time. Understandably, our particular CR in question has a large `status` field (which is being trimmed down to reasonable size anyway). However, it is interesting that we have never faced a timeout here in Kubernetes v1.19.9 and below.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

1. Use a Kubernetes 1.19.10 or 1.20.6 cluster
1. Create a 700KB+ sized custom resource object, client-side (e.g. `kubectl create`) or server-side
1. Update the object, client-side (e.g. `kubectl edit`) or server-side
1. Server-side apply will timeout in 34s

#### Anything else we need to know?:

I'm currently testing server-side apply behavior on CRs with/without their `openAPIV3Schema` populated. It may be possible this issue only affects CRDs that preserve unknown fields for unpopulated `openAPIV3Schema` fields, and/or it only affects CRDs with large `status` fields:
```
schema:
  openAPIV3Schema:
    properties:
      spec:
        x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
      status:
        x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
```

This is a comment with details of our investigation for `rancher/rancher`. It may be relevant for further context, but I do not want to inundate maintainers with a huge comment if need be: https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/32419#issuecomment-849000867

I've also narrowed down some potential suspects, but have not yet been able to test them:
- Structured Merge Diff v4.0.2: Possible (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/structured-merge-diff/compare/v4.0.1..v4.0.2)
- Lease Manager Changes in apiserver: Doubtful (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/3820a5d819582d4f6b4652757a3cc6c1a04692b4, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/537b8d3c06e869a6c00e9b645607ab03a09c9adb, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/42a3d75bf87a59c402ac72dd369ffe898cf8eb7b)
- Protobuf v1.3.2: Doubtful (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/15596cedd26c3afacf719a92c79c28e51051a959)

CRD in question:
- Source: https://github.com/rancher/rancher/blob/v2.5.8/pkg/apis/management.cattle.io/v3/catalog_types.go
- In cluster:
```
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1                                                                                                                                                           
kind: CustomResourceDefinition                                                                                                                                                                
metadata:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  name: catalogs.management.cattle.io                                                                                                                                                         
spec:
  conversion:
    strategy: None
  group: management.cattle.io
  names:
    kind: Catalog
    listKind: CatalogList
    plural: catalogs
    singular: catalog
  preserveUnknownFields: true
  scope: Cluster
  versions:
  - name: v3
    served: true
    storage: true
```

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.19.10, 1.20.6 (server)
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: Digital Ocean Droplet (2 CPU / 8GB RAM)
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): Ubuntu 20.04 LTS
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 5.4
- Install tools: [RKE v1.2.8](https://rancher.com/docs/rke/latest/en/)
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug): n/a
- Others: n/a

Thank you in advance for any and all help! I'd be happy to provide more detail that may help, and I hope to even find the code that caused this as well. This is an ongoing investigation, but I thought I'd file the issue since I believe we have had enough reproduction scenarios to warrant so.

EDIT: I believe `wg-api-expression` was the best to assign based on this: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/structured-merge-diff#community-discussion-contribution-and-support

body:
Follow up from https://github.com/kubernetes/klog/issues/211

Currently importing `k8s.io/component-base/logs` results both `text` and `json` logging format available by default.
