title: Short running pods take very long to teardown

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
In master we continue to see instances of short running pods failing to terminate quickly, due to races between sources of truth.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/102025#issuecomment-843622820 stops e2e tests from "cheating" and bypassing kubelet shutdown, and as a result some tests fail predictably (garbage collection lots of short running pods for testing various behaviors).  The linked comment shows a pod that is racing between container start and pod delete.  The problem is that dispatchWork invokes `podAndContainersAreTerminal()` on the containerstart event, but the cache that `podAndContainersAreTerminal` checks is not yet up to date (that's handled inside UpdatePod / syncPod).

In general, the pod worker is the one who should be managing shutdown.  We added optimizations to dispatchWork to skip the pod worker, and we historically had a race condition where the pod worker was shut down too early and thus termination never happened, but the right thing to do is to stop trying to optimize the pod worker knowing the state of the pod (it's job is to sync the pod) and instead make sure that a) the pod worker is running until a pod is deleted from api (which should be true today) and b) if we need to reduce latency of shutdown, we should do so by ensuring the pod worker gets that update.

The failures here are a significant violation of our performance goals around pods, and our e2e tests are demonstrating the failures pretty cleanly, so we need to put this race condition to bed.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/102025 can trigger the issue trivially, so for now using that to debug failure reasons.

labels.name: priority/important-soon

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
#### What would you like to be added:
#101034 changed the Kind used with the `/ephemeralcontainers` subresource from `EphemeralContainers` to `Pod`. This change will break old clients. (The ephemeral containers API is still in alpha, so this is acceptable.)

Currently, compatibility is broken in both directions:
1. kubectl versions prior to 1.22 are incompatible with server version 1.22
2. kubectl version 1.22 is incompatible with server versions prior to 1.22

Remediating the first requires complex server-side backwards compatibility logic which is not worth implementing for an alpha API.

Remediating the second for `kubectl debug` should be much easier. The `EphemeralContainer` struct hasn't changed, only the path in the object. We could detect the kind returned by the server and change the path used in the JSON patch (or even just naively try the previous path if the server returns an error).

This behavior would be removed after the old server version falls out of the support window.

#### Why is this needed:

This isn't strictly needed, but it would improve UX for what I expect is a common scenario: using the latest kubectl with older servers.

/sig cli
/priority important-soon

labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
#### What happened:
On a busy machine, kubelet was restarted while a pod was deleted in the API server. Newly started kubelet tried to reconstruct the volume, but it failed with:

```
could not get consistent content of /proc/mounts after 3 attempts
```

Everything went wrong from here. Since kubelet can't reconstruct the volume, it only unmounts the pod local mount, leaving the global mount still mounted. And kubelet removed the volume from `volumesInUse`, therefore allowing the mounted volume to be detached + attached somewhere else. In case of FibreChannel or iSCSI, that don't have 3rd party attach, the volume ends up mounted on two different nodes and the volume gets corrupted. In clouds, the volume may get stuck attached to the node (because some clouds refuse to detach mounted volumes) or it gets force-detached, possibly corrupting the volume.

Exact sequence:

```
I0507 14:02:18.951820    4790 reconciler.go:411] "Could not construct volume information, cleaning up mounts" podName=8ca6b5d0-40f8-4232-a7f3-38e1000252e6 volumeSpecName="pv1" error="could not get consistent content of /proc/mounts after 3 attempts"
I0507 14:02:18.951847    4790 reconciler.go:444] "Reconciler sync states: could not find volume information in desired state, clean up the mount points" podName=8ca6b5d0-40f8-4232-a7f3-38e1000252e6 volumeSpecName="pv1"
...
I0507 14:02:18.952092    4790 subpath_linux.go:226] Cleaning up subpath mounts for /var/lib/kubelet/pods/8ca6b5d0-40f8-4232-a7f3-38e1000252e6/volume-subpaths/pv1
I0507 14:02:18.952170    4790 mount_helper_common.go:99] "/var/lib/kubelet/pods/8ca6b5d0-40f8-4232-a7f3-38e1000252e6/volumes/kubernetes.io~fc/pv1" is a mountpoint, unmounting
I0507 14:02:18.952180    4790 mount_linux.go:266] Unmounting /var/lib/kubelet/pods/8ca6b5d0-40f8-4232-a7f3-38e1000252e6/volumes/kubernetes.io~fc/pv1
W0507 14:02:18.960657    4790 mount_helper_common.go:129] Warning: "/var/lib/kubelet/pods/8ca6b5d0-40f8-4232-a7f3-38e1000252e6/volumes/kubernetes.io~fc/pv1" is not a mountpoint, deleting
I0507 14:02:18.960745    4790 operation_generator.go:829] UnmountVolume.TearDown succeeded for volume "pv1" (OuterVolumeSpecName: "") pod "8ca6b5d0-40f8-4232-a7f3-38e1000252e6" (UID: "8ca6b5d0-40f8-4232-a7f3-38e1000252e6"). InnerVolumeSpecName "pv1". PluginName "kubernetes.io/fc", VolumeGidValue ""
E0507 14:02:18.960775    4790 operation_generator.go:844] UnmountVolume.MarkVolumeAsUnmounted failed for volume "" (UniqueName: "pv1") pod "8ca6b5d0-40f8-4232-a7f3-38e1000252e6" (UID: "8ca6b5d0-40f8-4232-a7f3-38e1000252e6") : no volume with the name "pv1" exists in the list of attached volumes
```

\+ the next node sync removed the volume from `volumesInUse`.

#### What you expected to happen:
The volume is not corrupted.
Ideally, the volume is unmounted from global mount using UnmountDevice, however, it's not possible without reconstructed volume.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):
I injected error to [ConstructVolumeSpec of FibreChannel](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6c658a86f9e75943024b0b4f792a37938a96a31f/pkg/volume/fc/fc.go#L235).
I don't know how to reproduce it without it - it's hard to get `GetMountRefs` / `ConsistentRead` to return an error.

Previously there was a change made in Windows to ensure that NodeUnstageVolume finishes before continuing with the test; however, this needs to also to be included in other distros as well. NodeUnpublish, which removes the bind mount, does not force the caches to flush.

labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
#### What happened:

I tried to run the apiserver image for v1.21.0-rc.0 (k8s.gcr.io/kube-apiserver:v1.21.0-rc.0) on top of another Kubernetes cluster. I took a working manifest which was using v.1.20.5 and was working without issues, and changed the image version.

The apiserver failed to start with `standard_init_linux.go:219: exec user process caused: operation not permitted`

#### What you expected to happen:

I was expecting to have a working apiserver.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

Trying to run the apiserver on top of kubernetes with a restricted pod security policy and without adding capabilities to my pod.

#### Anything else we need to know?:

I managed to make it work by adding a `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE` capability to my apiserver pod.

I found nothing related to this change in the changelog. I found  this commit (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/99145) which add `RUN setcap cap_net_bind_service=+ep /${BINARY}` to the apiserver image. and I think it can be the source of the issue.
I'm surprised by this change, which seems to be done for a specific use case but will, if I'm not wrong, impact everyone using the image.

#### Environment:

- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.21.0-rc.0
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: Exoscale
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): `20.04.1 LTS (Focal Fossa)`
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): `5.4.0-62-generic`
- Install tools: A deployment on top of another Kubernetes cluster.

title: Remove DynamicKubeletConfig from node tests

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a feature/enhancement marked for deprecation.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
/kind cleanup
/sig node
/area test

Deprecation issue: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/281

Currently, our e2e tests have a dependency on the deprecated DynamicKubeletConfiguration feature. At minimum, we use the feature to set the KubeletConfiguration, and we check metrics from it (e.g. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/104041).

We've also seen that the use of this feature in our serial tests is unreliable. Sometimes the kubelet fails to restart, which causes the tests to crash/fail: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/104038

The node e2e test suite was written before the component config APIs existed, and so right now the only way to configure a kubelet for tests is with extra command line flags, passed through our current test harness. The only way it's possible to set KubeletConfiguration values that don't have a corresponding command line flag is with a test code change using the DynamicKubeletConfiguration feature. It would be much better to refactor to just support a custom KubeletConfiguration provided at launch time.

Suggested path forward:

- [ ] Update our test runner such that we can provide a KubeletConfiguration file, rather than configuring jobs with command-line flags
- [ ] Determine some mechanism to either update the config and restart the kubelet during test runs, or guidelines for how to manage custom KubeletConfigs in test jobs that need to exercise features outside of the default set
- [ ] Remove all use of the DynamicKubeletConfiguration from e2e tests

/milestone v1.23
/priority important-soon

/assign @endocrimes 
/cc @SergeyKanzhelev

title: Incorrect initContainers order when using server-side apply

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: wg/api-expression
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to WG API Expression.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
#### What happened:

The order of `initContainers` is significant, but when using `kubectl apply --server-side` to change this field, the intended order is not preserved.

#### What you expected to happen:

I expected the order of `initContainers` to match my submitted intent.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

Files:

```yaml
==> 00.yaml <==                                                            
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:                                                                  
  name: init-container-order
spec:                
  clusterIP: None                                                          
---                                                                        
apiVersion: apps/v1                                                        
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:                                                                  
  name: init-container-order
spec:
  serviceName: init-container-order
  selector:
    matchLabels: { name: init-container-order }
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: { name: init-container-order }
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - { image: busybox, name: original }
      containers:
      - { image: busybox, name: main }

==> 01.yaml <==
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: init-container-order
spec:
  clusterIP: None
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: init-container-order
spec:
  serviceName: init-container-order
  selector:
    matchLabels: { name: init-container-order }
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: { name: init-container-order }
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - { image: busybox, name: first }
      - { image: busybox, name: original }
      - { image: busybox, name: last }
      containers:
      - { image: busybox, name: main }
```

```diff
● diff -u 00.yaml 01.yaml 
--- 00.yaml     2021-08-27 20:39:10.000000000 -0500
+++ 01.yaml     2021-08-27 20:39:08.000000000 -0500
@@ -18,6 +18,8 @@
       labels: { name: init-container-order }
     spec:
       initContainers:
+      - { image: busybox, name: first }
       - { image: busybox, name: original }
+      - { image: busybox, name: last }
       containers:
       - { image: busybox, name: main }
```

---

Create the StatefulSet and see it has one init container:

```
● kubectl apply --server-side -f 00.yaml 
service/init-container-order serverside-applied
statefulset.apps/init-container-order serverside-applied

● kubectl get sts/init-container-order -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.initContainers[*].name}{"\n"}'
original
```

Add two more init containers, one before and one after the original. See that they are **both added to the end**:

```
● kubectl apply --server-side -f 01.yaml 
service/init-container-order serverside-applied
statefulset.apps/init-container-order serverside-applied

● kubectl get sts/init-container-order -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.initContainers[*].name}{"\n"}'
original first last
```

#### Anything else we need to know?:

`kubectl replace` puts them in the intended order:

```
● kubectl replace -f 01.yaml 
service/init-container-order replaced
statefulset.apps/init-container-order replaced

● kubectl get sts/init-container-order -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.initContainers[*].name}{"\n"}'
first original last
```

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
  ```
  Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"22", GitVersion:"v1.22.0", GitCommit:"c2b5237ccd9c0f1d600d3072634ca66cefdf272f", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2021-08-04T17:56:19Z", GoVersion:"go1.16.6", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"darwin/amd64"}
  Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"21", GitVersion:"v1.21.4+k3s1", GitCommit:"3e250fdbab72d88f7e6aae57446023a0567ffc97", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2021-08-19T19:09:53Z", GoVersion:"go1.16.6", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}

<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:

Shutdown a node gracefully. E.g. with `systemctl reboot`.

#### What you expected to happen:

Expected to see pods being evicted, and pods being started on another nodes.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

Let a deployment create one pod, configure Graceful Node Shutdown as described in https://kubernetes.io/blog/2021/04/21/graceful-node-shutdown-beta/, then just `systemctl reboot` that node. Then, the pod will get a state of `Terminated` or `Completed`, but no new pod is being created and scheduled on a different node. Then, when the node comes back, the terminated pod stays in such a state:

```
home-assistant-5dfcb44d74-rg2zs                       1/1     Terminated   2          30m   10.112.0.69    k8s-node13   <none>           <none>
```

Effectively, the pod is running on the node which has been rebooted gracefully, but is in a `Terminated` state.

#### Anything else we need to know?:

This worked as expected in v1.21

body:
#### What would you like to be added:

/cleanup
[Structured Logging KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/1602) proposed to introduce alternative JSON logging format, that is injected into klog by providing a [logr.Logger](https://github.com/go-logr/logr) interface implementation. 

When Json format was originally implemented we decided to write our own logr.Logger implementation to speed up work and skip taking a dependency on implementation that might not be matching specification given in KEP. 

Our implementation: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/logs/json/json.go

As we added more testing and logr.Logger released 1.0.0, it doesn't make sense to maintain this code as it's very similar to existing logr.Logger implementation called zapr. https://github.com/go-logr/zapr

Not to person that will work on it:
We can either wait for klog and k/k to switch to logr 1.0.0 or migrate now when we are still on 0.4.0. I prefer to do it earier as it will reduce work needed to migrate to 1.0.0.


#### Why is this needed:
Reduce maintanance cost of library and consolidate work on JSON logr implementation.
It should also help when transitioning to logr 1.0.0


/cc @kubernetes/wg-structured-logging-members 
/wg structured-logging
/sig instrumentation
/priority important-soon
/cc @timhockin @pohly

body:
#### What happened:
Our operator had a StatefulSet with 3 pods, and a PDB with `maxUnavailable: 1`. First 2 pods were ready, the 3rd one was not ready (and will never be ready). The operator tried to evict the 3rd (unready) pod, but the API call was repeatedly forbidden with `Cannot evict pod as it would violate the pod's disruption budget`. Yet, that isn't true - the PDB accounts only for ready pods (the first 2) so the 3rd one that isn't ready should be evictable without an effect on the PDB.

#### What you expected to happen:
Unready pods should be freely evictable as they are not accounted for in the PDB (currentHealthy).

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):
1. Create 2 ready pods and 1 unready
2. Create a PDB with `maxUnavailable: 1`
3. Try to evict the unready pod

#### Anything else we need to know?:
For more context this originates from https://github.com/scylladb/scylla-operator/issues/730#issuecomment-888030132
The full yamls can be seen at https://cloudius-jenkins-test.s3.amazonaws.com/801e256a-2bca-4c72-be78-40711c7838c9/20210724_185703/kubernetes-801e256a.tar.gz but the relevant parts are the following:

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:

When testing #102344 against OpenShift CI, I discovered a panic in the kubelet: https://github.com/openshift/kubernetes/pull/851#issuecomment-877469501

Further investigation revealed that it is possible for `syncTerminatedPod` to panic under certain circumstances: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a0d77e5763ac04ddc713bf2e284580d32fd4b079/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L685-L713

We hit this case when `update.Options.RunningPod != nil` (podStatus remains nil) and `update.WorkType == TerminatedPodWork` (nil will be passed along to `syncTerminatedPod`). I'm not sure why exactly that would happen but it seems possible.

#### What you expected to happen:

Don't panic!

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

Unclear, I've been trying to trace the code/find evidence of this happening in k8s CI but haven't found a match yet. (https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/issues/22851 would be nice :smile:)

title: Nil pointer dereference in KCM after v1 HPA patch request

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.description: Denotes an issue that needs help from a contributor. Must meet "help wanted" guidelines.

labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
### What happened?

If we create a v2beta2 HPA object with fields specified for the scaleUp or scaleDown behavior, these values can be modified through the v1 version of the same object by changing the annotation for autoscaling.alpha.kubernetes.io/behavior. If we patch the scaleUp or scaleDown field in the annotation to null, the patch request will get accepted without the default values for scaleUp or scaleDown being applied. This will result in a panic in KCM when it tries to deference a nil pointer:
```
E1207 02:43:43.082791      10 runtime.go:78] Observed a panic: "invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference" (runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference)
goroutine 2238 [running]:
k8s.io/kubernetes/vendor/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime.logPanic(0x41c0960, 0x747b350)
    /go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/vendor/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime/runtime.go:74 +0x95
k8s.io/kubernetes/vendor/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime.HandleCrash(0x0, 0x0, 0x0)
    /go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/vendor/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime/runtime.go:48 +0x86
panic(0x41c0960, 0x747b350)
    /usr/local/go/src/runtime/panic.go:965 +0x1b9
k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/controller/podautoscaler.(*HorizontalController).stabilizeRecommendationWithBehaviors(0xc000a700b0, 0xc0004bd760, 0x1a, 0x0, 0xc001a4c570, 0x500000004, 0x100000004, 0x0, 0x7fe0a1a18988, 0x7fe0a1a26ef8, ...)
    /go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/controller/podautoscaler/horizontal.go:885 +0x3c
...
```
This is panic is occurring here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.21.2/pkg/controller/podautoscaler/horizontal.go#L885 

### What did you expect to happen?

The patch request to the v1 HPA object should have applied the default value for the scaleUp or scaleDown fields when the annotation edit set it to null. When the v2beta2 object is updated, omitting the scaleUp or scaleDown properties will result in default values being applied so it is assumed that no fields in this struct are nil: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6ac2d8edc8606ab387924b8b865b4a69630080e0/pkg/apis/autoscaling/v2/defaults.go#L104

  name: coredns-scaler
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: coredns
  minReplicas: 4
  maxReplicas: 5
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 50
  behavior:
    scaleDown: 
      policies: 
      - type: Pods 
        value: 4 
        periodSeconds: 60 
      - type: Percent
        value: 10 
        periodSeconds: 60
      selectPolicy: Min 
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300 
EOF
```
2. Edit the v1 version of the HPA object to set scaleUp as null in the annotation:
```
kubectl edit hpa.v1.autoscaling coredns-scaler -n kube-system
```

```

```

body:
### What happened?

It looks like default HTTPS port for kube-scheduler has changed from 10251 to 10259 between 1.22.4 and 1.23.0 releases and it has not been mentioned in the changelog.
```
I1208 11:30:46.202095       1 deprecated_insecure_serving.go:54] Serving healthz insecurely on [::]:10251
```

```
I1208 09:17:41.523334       1 secure_serving.go:200] Serving securely on [::]:10259
```

EDIT: Actually, I see now that 1.22.4 listens on 10259, but also on 10251 and 1.23.0 just stopped listening on 10251.


### What did you expect to happen?

Breaking changes to be included in the changelog.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

With kube-prometheus-stack installed, with kube-scheduler scraping configured, upgrade kube-scheduler from 1.22.4 to 1.23.0.

body:
### What happened?

 Windows client pods in the cluster see intermittent connection failures when attempting to access a Linux service of type load balancer using its external VIP under the following conditions:
  * Linux service has externalTrafficPolicy: Local set.
  * The backend pods are distributed across >1 Linux nodes.

### What did you expect to happen?

In kube-proxy Linux, it appears there are special iptables rules to redirect pod -> external VIP traffic to service clusterIP instead:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.22/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L1455

Something similar presumably also needs to be added to Windows.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Deploy azure CNI  + calico cluster with 3 linux nodes in system nodepool, and a win nodepool 
2. Deploy service with basic nginx ingress controller or azure load balancer and set to External Traffic Policy Local. These will run in the linux system nodepool.
3. Create a pod on the win nodepool 
4. Curl the LB IP or the external IP 
5. As soon as the replicas are distributed across multiple nodes, we will get intermittent failures.  

### Anything else we need to know?

The scenario can be made to work successfully when one or more of the following applies:
  * Connecting using the cluster service IP instead of external LB frontend VIP (Windows pod -> Linux cluster svc IP)
  * The destination service is backed by Windows pods (Windows pod -> Windows VIP). 
  * If using a Linux client pod instead of Windows pod (Linux pod -> Linux VIP).
  * Destination pods backing the service are all located on a single Node.

title: Test should be demoted from Conformance: [sig-node] Events should be sent by kubelets and the scheduler about pods scheduling and running

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: kind/cleanup
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to cleaning up code, process, or technical debt.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: sig/architecture
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Architecture.

labels.name: area/conformance
labels.description: Issues or PRs related to kubernetes conformance tests

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
Related:
- Noticed this as part of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/106506
- Opened in response to: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/106506#issuecomment-972164628

According to our [rules for Conformance tests](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/conformance-tests.md), the `[sig-node] Events should be sent by kubelets and the scheduler about pods scheduling and running` e2e test is ineligible for Conformance.  Specifically, the test in question is looking for guaranteed delivery of Events from specific sources (kubelet and default scheduler).  This cannot be reasonably expected of all Kubernetes clusters, and thus the test should be demoted from Conformance.

For historical context:
- It looks like this has been part of Conformance sometime since sometime prior to 2015-10-17 (we introduced the [Conformance] tag in 1.2, ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/15228
- We overhauled Conformance testing policy (including exclusion of Events) on 2018-10-08 (ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/pull/2459 )

If I wanted to be a language lawyer about this, I could say the policy covers ineligibility for _promotion_ but said nothing about the existing corpus of tests.  But I think this was just an honest oversight when we reviewed the existing Conformance tests.

Due to the very nature of what this test is verifying, I don't think it's possible to rewrite to avoid Events.  Thus, I think it should be demoted from Conformance.  SIG Node is free to continue to treat this as release-blocking, but it's not something we can reasonably expect of any Kubernetes cluster

/kind cleanup
/priority important-soon
/milestone v1.23

/sig architecture
/area conformance
because conformance

/sig node
because it's a sig-node test

body:
### What would you like to be added?

When using `InfoS` or `ErrorS` with a key/value that has a multi-line string as value, that value will appear as quoted string in the log message, i.e. the log message will still be a single line.

It would be nicer to print the value in text mode so that it goes across multiple lines, with clear indicators for start and end of the value. Indention could be used to avoid mistaking some embedded line as the start of a new log message.

In JSON mode, the value should be formatted normally.

/sig instrumentation
/wg structured-logging


### Why is this needed?

Always printing as a single line can can make the log output unreadable (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/104868).

body:
### What would you like to be added?

Kubelet credential provider is in alpha since 1.20 release, we need to add e2e tests to move it to beta.

**Current e2e tests for intree credential providers:**
[1]  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e_node/runtime_conformance_test.go#L61 (uses intree docker config credential provider) 
[2] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/apps/rc.go#L68 (uses intree gcp credential provider)
[3] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/apps/replica_set.go#L113 (uses intree gcp credential provider)

The job pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce-ubuntu-containerd fails with replica sets private image tests if external credential provider is enabled by default

**Problems in adding e2e tests for external credential providers**
-  The credential provider binary and config file needs to be installed on node VM before Kubelet starts, external cloud providers credential providers like GCP only supported to install with external cloud providers
- Tests using intree docker config provider are part of node conformance tests


**Work needs to be done**
1.  Provide a way to run existing node conformance tests[1] with external credential provider
A sample-credential-provider repo needs to be created under k8s-sigs which can be build and installed via node e2e tests to run existing node conformance tests

2. Migrate the replica set tests [2] & [3] to out of tree gcp credential provider 
Need help from gcp cloud provider team to work on this.

/sig cloud-provider node
/ cc @cheftako @dims @endocrimes @DangerOnTheRanger @andrewsykim @SergeyKanzhelev

title: EndpointSlice Mirroring Controller does not cleanup EndpointSlices when a Selector is added to a Service

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon

labels.name: triage/accepted

body:
### What happened?

1. Service with Selector is created
2. Selector is removed
3. Both Endpoints and EndpointSlice controllers do not clean up Endpoint(Slice)s
4. EndpointSlice mirroring controller starts mirroring the Endpoints resource originally created by the Endpoints controller
5. Selector is added back to the Service
6. Pods backing Service change
7. EndpointSlice created by mirroring controller still references original IP from step 4

### What did you expect to happen?

At least one of the following:

1. The Endpoints and EndpointSlices to be cleaned up when the Service has the selector removed (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/103576)
2. The mirrored EndpointSlice to be removed when the Service has a selector added back

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

See "What Happened"

Most noticeable in Kubernetes 1.19+ since that's when kube-proxy starts reading from EndpointSlices by default.

title: [KEP-2400] Address swap impact on memory-backed volumes

body:
Some volumes (notably secret volumes) are memory-backed in order to ensure they do not hit disk.

When swap is enabled, we need to ensure the content of memory-backed volumes continue to not touch disk.

* On cgroupsv2, the kubelet should set cgroupv2 controls to prevent memory-backed volumes from swapping out
* On cgroupsv1, where these controls are not available
  * document (in PRR / KEP / docs) the impact of running with swap on memory-backed volumes
  * consider not supporting swap on cgroupsv1 because of this impact?

/sig node storage
/assign @ehashman

        /usr/local/go/src/runtime/map_faststr.go:21
net/textproto.MIMEHeader.Get
        /usr/local/go/src/net/textproto/header.go:34
net/http.Header.Get(...)
        /usr/local/go/src/net/http/header.go:46
net/http.(*Request).UserAgent(...)
k8s.io/kubernetes/vendor/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/httplog.(*respLogger).LogArgs(...)
        k8s.io/kubernetes/vendor/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/httplog/httplog.go:185 
```

### What did you expect to happen?

Not to crash

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I was able to reproduce it by "slowing down" deleting headers in Authentication filter (staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/filters/authentication.go):

```
		req.Header.Del("Authorization")
		if strings.Contains(req.URL.Path, "itsnotworkingisit") {
			for i := 1; i < 100000000; i++ {
				req.Header.Add("Authorization", "test")
				req.Header.Del("Authorization")
			}
		} 
```
And making requests (around 5-10 requests to trigger this race condition):
```
 kubectl get --raw='/api/v1/namespaces/kube-system/configmaps/itsnotworkingisit?timeout=1s'
```

### Anything else we need to know?

Crash was caused by race condition - one goroutine was modifying headers of requests (for example authentication filter). The other goroutine was trying to get UserAgent from request, which is also taken from request's headers map. This causes unrecoverable panic.

title: Orphaned pod found, but error not a directory occurred when trying to remove the volumes dir

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
#### What happened:

One of our nodes had a hard reboot. After this, the following message was occurring in the kubelet logs every 2 seconds:

```
Oct 07 12:46:32 k8s-master2-staging kubelet[7310]: E1007 12:46:32.359145    7310 kubelet_volumes.go:245] "There were many similar errors. Turn up verbosity to see them." err="orphaned pod \"1d4bfc07-3469-4eaa-992f-6d23c17f3aee\" found, but error not a directory occurred when trying to remove the volumes dir" numErrs=1
```

Indeed, the orphaned pod directory exists and contains 1 stale volume directory with a file in it (probably explaining the "not a directory" error):

```
sjors@k8s-master2-staging:~$ sudo ls -la /var/lib/kubelet/pods/1d4bfc07-3469-4eaa-992f-6d23c17f3aee/volumes/kubernetes.io~csi/pvc-13c81b28-4038-40d5-b6e8-4194e1d7be0e
total 12
drwxr-x--- 2 root root 4096 Oct  7 12:37 .
drwxr-x--- 3 root root 4096 Oct  2 19:37 ..
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root  270 Oct  7 12:37 vol_data.json
```

Deleting this file manually leads to immediate resolving of the Kubelet error 2 seconds later:

```
Oct 07 12:46:40 k8s-master2-staging kubelet[7310]: I1007 12:46:40.359957    7310 kubelet_volumes.go:160] "Cleaned up orphaned pod volumes dir" podUID=1d4bfc07-3469-4eaa-992f-6d23c17f3aee path="/var/lib/kubelet/pods/1d4bfc07-3469-4eaa-992f-6d23c17f3aee/volumes"
```

#### What you expected to happen:

I know that the Kubelet tries to clean up orphaned pod directories, and various issues have been fixed regarding this in the past, such as figuring out stale mounts and deleting old directories (#60987 for example).

However, it looks like when there are files present, it fails to remove the stale directory.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

I think, but have not attempted, it can be reproduced by these steps:

1. start a Pod with a mounted PVC
2. manually create a file inside a Pod's `volumes/kubernetes.io~csi/pvc-...` directory
3. hard-reboot the machine, so that the kubelet gets no chance to clean up the Pod directory, i.e. directory becomes orphaned
4. (If creating the file of step 2 was not possible before, it can also be done after the reboot, but before the kubelet comes up.)
5. observe error in the Kubelet logs.

#### Anything else we need to know?:

The CSI provider used is Hetzner Cloud (hcloud-csi-driver:1.6.0), I'm not sure if it's responsible for creating the file.

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.22.1
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: bare-metal, 3 masters
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): Ubuntu 20.04.3 LTS
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 5.4.0-88-generic
- Install tools: kubeadm 1.22.1

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/109184 found that our vet checks are not running under the `/staging` dir.

Once it ran those checks, it revealed exposure to real issues in non-test files:

```
staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/managedfields/gvkparser.go:61:39: copylocks: literal copies lock value from *typeSchema: sigs.k8s.io/structured-merge-diff/v4/schema.Schema contains sync.Once contains sync.Mutex (govet)

staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/counter.go:215:15: copylocks: literal copies lock value from *v: k8s.io/component-base/metrics.CounterVec contains k8s.io/component-base/metrics.lazyMetric contains sync.RWMutex (govet)

staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/gauge.go:192:24: copylocks: newGaugeFunc passes lock by value: k8s.io/component-base/metrics.GaugeOpts contains sync.Once contains sync.Mutex (govet)
func newGaugeFunc(opts GaugeOpts, function func() float64, v semver.Version) GaugeFunc {
                       ^
staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/gauge.go:208:24: copylocks: NewGaugeFunc passes lock by value: k8s.io/component-base/metrics.GaugeOpts contains sync.Once contains sync.Mutex (govet)
func NewGaugeFunc(opts GaugeOpts, function func() float64) GaugeFunc {
                       ^
staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/gauge.go:211:22: copylocks: call of newGaugeFunc copies lock value: k8s.io/component-base/metrics.GaugeOpts contains sync.Once contains sync.Mutex (govet)

staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/gauge.go:218:13: copylocks: literal copies lock value from *v: k8s.io/component-base/metrics.GaugeVec contains k8s.io/component-base/metrics.lazyMetric contains sync.RWMutex (govet)

staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/histogram.go:202:17: copylocks: literal copies lock value from *v: k8s.io/component-base/metrics.HistogramVec contains k8s.io/component-base/metrics.lazyMetric contains sync.RWMutex (govet)

staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/metric.go:172:26: copylocks: assignment copies lock value to r.markDeprecationOnce: sync.Once contains sync.Mutex (govet)

staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/metric.go:173:17: copylocks: assignment copies lock value to r.createOnce: sync.Once contains sync.Mutex (govet)

staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/summary.go:196:15: copylocks: literal copies lock value from *v: k8s.io/component-base/metrics.SummaryVec contains k8s.io/component-base/metrics.lazyMetric contains sync.RWMutex (govet)
```

While it looks like many of these were present in previous releases, copying locks by value breaks them. These should be fixed to ensure we don't race/panic.

/milestone v1.24


_Originally posted by @liggitt in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/109184#issuecomment-1084528954_

That is not correct if both metadata.name and metadata.generateName are set in the create request.

Rather than changing behavior from <1.23, then changing it again if/when we are able to distinguish when the user only set generateName, I think we should leave that behavior as is until we can distinguish.

/kind bug
/kind regression
/milestone v1.24
/assign @joejulian 
/sig api-machinery
/priority important-soon

body:
### What happened?

We have a controller that creates a job for unpacking the contents of a container image hosted in a container registry. After updating to kube 1.23.5, the Jobs created by the controller sometimes don't transition to `Complete:True`, despite the fact that the underlying pod runs to completion. Instead, the underlying pod is listed in `status.uncountedTerminatedPod.succeeded` indefinitely.

### What did you expect to happen?

If the underlying pod completes successfully, the Job status should reflect that in it's `status.conditions`, where the pod is listed as `Complete:True`

### What happened?

There seem to be increased resource usage for the kube-api-server in the `kubemark-500nodes` job:
CPU:
http://perf-dash.k8s.io/#/?jobname=kubemark-500Nodes&metriccategoryname=E2E&metricname=LoadResources&PodName=apiserver%2Fapiserver&Resource=CPU

![Screenshot from 2022-03-30 16-49-13](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12381034/160823005-b5e52b83-285b-4407-a10f-57c4c77559e7.png)

`etcd/etcd/data` also sees a similar spike.

We see a similar increase in `kubemark-100`
http://perf-dash.k8s.io/#/?jobname=kubemark-100Nodes&metriccategoryname=E2E&metricname=LoadResources&PodName=apiserver%2Fapiserver&Resource=CPU

and `gce-100Nodes`
http://perf-dash.k8s.io/#/?jobname=gce-100Nodes-master&metriccategoryname=E2E&metricname=LoadResources&PodName=kube-apiserver-e2e-big-master%2Fkube-apiserver&Resource=CPU

which means its probably not kubemark specific

FYI
Memory (at least the 99 and 90th percentile):
http://perf-dash.k8s.io/#/?jobname=kubemark-500Nodes&metriccategoryname=E2E&metricname=LoadResources&PodName=apiserver%2Fapiserver&Resource=memory

fwiw - The `gce-5000Nodes` has not yet run with the above-mentioned change.

/sig scalability
/cc @kubernetes/sig-scalability 
/cc @pacoxu 

### Anything else we need to know?

It seems like the change with which the kubemark-500Node job was run that had the first peak was: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/101566 
https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-kubemark-500-gce/1508923569499803648/

With the kubemark-100Node job, between the last "normal" and the spike, there was the above PR and a documentation-related PR (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/109121) merged.

Upstream thread: https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C09QZTRH7/p1648636053781389 

### Kubernetes version

1.24 +

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
### What happened?

I started API call like:

```
2022-03-17 08:01:17.003 PDT
""HTTP" verb="LIST" URI="/apis/external.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/namespaces/ns-1/custom.googleapis.com%7Ctarget?labelSelector=resource.labels.namespace_id+in+%28default%2Cdummy%29%2Cresource.labels.pod_id%2Cresource.type%3Dgke_container"
```

Based on kube-apiserver logs I think that this call has taken `maximumSeats` for entire duration of the call (which was 10s due to reentrant call made by service handling this call and using the same priority-level).

In my opinion we shouldn't use `maximumSeats` in case of delegated calls as they do not consume much kube-apiserver resources + (practically speaking) can block for quite a long time for external reasons blocking significant part of priority level.

What happens:
* Such calls are not longrunning according to definition in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4348c8ecaf87d91503718a42a930c397c3c82569/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/server.go#L387-L390 so they are being a subject of throttling in priority and fairness
* we hit ObjectCountNotFoundErr as we don't know how many objects of type like "external.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1" we have (which is expected), https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4348c8ecaf87d91503718a42a930c397c3c82569/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/flowcontrol/request/list_work_estimator.go#L70-L70 and return `maximumSeats`

### What did you expect to happen?

* InitialSeats for LIST calls to external API services is lower than `maximumSeats` (aka 10). Something like 1 is more expected as kube-apiserver is only redirecting traffic which involves limited CPU and memory, compared to other LIST calls.
* LIST calls to external API services are not handled by "error handling path", rather there is some explicit check for them

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

From https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/108524 which describes some observed problem caused by this:

* `kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/k8s-stackdriver/master/custom-metrics-stackdriver-adapter/deploy/production/adapter_new_resource_model.yaml`
* `kubectl get --raw "/apis/external.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/namespaces/triton-batch/s0-prometheus-gpu_utilization?labelSelector=scaledobject.keda.sh%2Fname%3Dtriton"`

The second call will take 10 seats.

### Anything else we need to know?

body:
### What happened?

We observe a high CPU usage of apiserver replicas while other replicas are idling:

```
$ k top po -l role=apiserver
kube-apiserver-786785f6fc-q2fwc               49m          737Mi
kube-apiserver-786785f6fc-r2bxz               50m          690Mi
kube-apiserver-786785f6fc-tbph4               11387m       898Mi
kube-apiserver-786785f6fc-zjfvj               35m          544Mi
```

After investigations we managed to drill down to a custom resource create/update requests that cause this high CPU usage (See the steps to reproduce for more details). It makes sense to mention that the above `k top po` output is from a single Node cluster.

We observe that after such request, the CPU usage does not cool down in seconds or a minute. We see that an apiserver replica is affected by high CPU usage for 10-20min. So it takes 10-20min until the apiserver replica's CPU usage goes down again to values from before the request.

Note also the huge imbalance between the apiserver replica's CPU usage. The replica that get's the requests from the client that operates on the custom resources vs the other 3 replicas that are simply idling wrt CPU usage.



### What did you expect to happen?

I would expect a create request for a custom resource to do not fail with a timeout after 30 seconds.
I would expect such request to do not cause > 1000% CPU usage increase for the concrete apiserver replica for more than 10min.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Example CRD and CR can be found in https://gist.github.com/ialidzhikov/a27fdcea78bd3a0fe726b25c0dfc53c0.

1. Create the `clusterserviceplans.servicecatalog.k8s.io` CRD

   ```
   $ k create -f https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ialidzhikov/a27fdcea78bd3a0fe726b25c0dfc53c0/raw/244d78024c31b3ebd870319f83fe53455f2b374c/clusterserviceplans-crd.yaml
   ```
   
2. Try to create a CR:

   ```
   $ k create -f https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ialidzhikov/a27fdcea78bd3a0fe726b25c0dfc53c0/raw/244d78024c31b3ebd870319f83fe53455f2b374c/clusterserviceplan-sample.json --dry-run=server
   ```
   
   Make sure that this create requests times out after >30 seconds with:
   ```
   (on K8s 1.21.10)
   Error from server (Timeout): error when creating "clusterserviceplan-sample.json": Timeout: request did not complete within requested timeout context deadline exceeded
   ```
   ```
   (on K8s 1.20.15)
   Error from server (Timeout): error when creating "clusterserviceplan-sample.json": Timeout: request did not complete within requested timeout 34s
   ```
   
3. Make sure that the apiserver replicas CPU usage is increased by 1000%.

   ![Screenshot 2022-03-29 at 11 38 39](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9372594/160570280-2795a61f-9d02-4f28-bc51-22124d6ae231.png)
   
   The graph confirms the CPU spike. Before the dry-run create request the apiserver replicas CPU usage was avg. `40-50m`. After the create request it went up to more than `1200m`. And this high CPU usage lasts for around 10-15min and it takes apiserver to cool down such high amount of time. The apiserver container does not have any cpu limits set.
   Note that this graph is from an idling cluster and the graph demonstrates the reflections on the CPU usage of single apiserver replica for ONLY 1 dry-run create request. Now, image the CPU usage on a busy cluster with a controller that operates on such custom resources.


### Anything else we need to know?

Maybe related issue - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/102749. But we are already running K8s versions that have the fix for this issue.

I am able to reproduce the issue on 1.18.20, 1.19.16, 1.20.15, 1.21.10, 1.22.7 and 1.23.4.

body:
### What happened?

This test fails on Kubernetes cluster in "westus" region (without any number) and with CSI migration enabled:

`[sig-storage] In-tree Volumes [Driver: azure-disk] [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (delayed binding)] topology should provision a volume and schedule a pod with AllowedTopologies`

Error:
`
failed to provision volume with StorageClass "e2e-topology-84vk7sp": error generating accessibility requirements: topology map[topology.disk.csi.azure.com/zone:] from selected node "ci-op-9j1nby77-e54d5-9zlwv-worker-westus-ljw4g" is not in requisite: [map[topology.disk.csi.azure.com/zone:0]]
`

StorageClass generated by the test:

```yaml
allowedTopologies:
- matchLabelExpressions:
  - key: failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone
    values:
    - "0"
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: e2e-topology-84vk7sp
provisioner: kubernetes.io/azure-disk
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
```

PVC created by the test:
<details>

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  annotations:
    volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-provisioner: disk.csi.azure.com
    volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node: ci-op-9j1nby77-e54d5-9zlwv-worker-westus-ljw4g
    volume.kubernetes.io/storage-provisioner: disk.csi.azure.com
  creationTimestamp: "2022-03-24T12:36:08Z"
  finalizers:
  - kubernetes.io/pvc-protection
  generateName: pvc-
  name: pvc-ph9tb
  namespace: e2e-topology-84
  resourceVersion: "135683"
  uid: 7596de95-b733-46d3-93f2-f1309a244d20
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
  storageClassName: e2e-topology-84vk7sp
  volumeMode: Filesystem
```

</details>

Labels of the selected node:
```yaml
    beta.kubernetes.io/arch: amd64
    beta.kubernetes.io/instance-type: Standard_D4s_v3
    beta.kubernetes.io/os: linux
    failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/region: westus
    failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone: "0"
    kubernetes.io/arch: amd64
    kubernetes.io/hostname: ci-op-9j1nby77-e54d5-9zlwv-worker-westus-ljw4g
    kubernetes.io/os: linux
    node-role.kubernetes.io/worker: ""
    node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: Standard_D4s_v3
    node.openshift.io/os_id: rhcos
    topology.disk.csi.azure.com/zone: ""
    topology.hostpath.csi/node: ci-op-9j1nby77-e54d5-9zlwv-worker-westus-ljw4g
    topology.kubernetes.io/region: westus
    topology.kubernetes.io/zone: "0"
```

The external-provisioner does not even call the CSI driver and reports this event:

```
failed to provision volume with StorageClass "e2e-topology-84vk7sp": error generating accessibility requirements: topology map[topology.disk.csi.azure.com/zone:] from selected node "ci-op-9j1nby77-e54d5-9zlwv-worker-westus-ljw4g" is not in requisite: [map[topology.disk.csi.azure.com/zone:0]]
```


### What did you expect to happen?

The volume should get provisioned.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

See above, "westus" region with no availability zones seems to be the key.

### Anything else we need to know?

It looks like the translation from in-tree StorageClass to CSI one translates topology requirements to `topology.disk.csi.azure.com/zone: "0"`, but the CSI one expects `topology.disk.csi.azure.com/zone: ""`

body:
### What happened?

go1.18 dropped support for certificates signed with the SHA-1 hash function - https://tip.golang.org/doc/go1.18#sha1

While this does improve security, and publicly trusted Certificate Authorities no longer issue such certificates, it is possible that user-provided certificates issued by private Certificate Authorities and used in webhooks or aggregated API servers do still use this.

Similar to removal of support for certificates without subjectAltNames in go1.17, we need to:
- [x] add metrics when webhook/conversion/aggregated certificates with this hash are encountered - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/109024
- [x] document use of `GODEBUG=x509sha1=1` and the metric from 1 as a mitigation for clusters which still need to identify and replace use of such certificates - added to release note and known issues
- [x] add audit annotation when SHA-1 cert is encountered - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/109107
- [x] update docs at https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/labels-annotations-taints/#annotations-used-for-audit and https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/labels-annotations-taints/audit-annotations/ - https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/32648

/sig api-machinery instrumentation docs
/priority important-soon
/milestone v1.24
/kind bug documentation

### What did you expect to happen?

Upgraded 1.23 clusters to continue working as-is

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Configure an admission webhook, conversion webhook, or aggregated server with a serving certificate signed with the SHA-1 hash function. Upgrade to HEAD of 1.24. The certificate will no longer work by default

        reason: ContainerStatusUnknown
        message: The container could not be located when the pod was terminated
        startedAt: null
        finishedAt: null
    lastState: {}
    ready: false
    restartCount: 0
    started: false
    # ...
```

**What you expected to happen**:

The main container should stay in `Waiting` since it hasn't started (as described [in the docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle/#container-state-terminated): "_A container in the Terminated state began execution and then either ran to completion or failed for some reason_").

```yaml
initContainerStatuses:
  - state:
      terminated:
        exitCode: 103
        reason: Error
        startedAt: '2022-03-15T07:00:00Z'
        finishedAt: '2022-03-15T07:00:00Z'
        # ...
    lastState: {}
    ready: false
    restartCount: 0
    # ...
containerStatuses:
  - state:
      waiting:
        reason: PodInitializing
    lastState: {}
    ready: false
    restartCount: 0
    started: false
    # ...
```

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Create a pod with an initContainer that will fail. After the pod fails, inspect the main container status and you should see it in `Terminated` state instead of the `Waiting` expected state.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

I believe it might be a regression from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105462 that was [backported in v1.22.3](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105496) since we removed the `|| status.ContainerStatuses[i].State.Waiting != nil` check that was making sure only previously-running containers could end up as `Terminated`.

I noticed there was a test added in [kubernetes/kubernetes/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager_test.go#L639](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7152825c0695d62fe06b47cc3e1699095290d73f/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager_test.go#L639) as part of this PR so I'm not sure if this change was intentional (and undocumented) or just overlooked.

This is problematic since many systems expect `Terminated` containers to have started as documented in the docs. A workaround might be to rely `containerStatuses[i].state.terminated.startedAt` in addition to `containerStatuses[i].state.terminated` but I'm curious to know if this was an intentional change and the documentation should be updated or if it's a regression that should be fixed.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version: First saw in `v1.22` and was able to reproduce it in `master`.

/kind bug
/sig node

title: Kubelet reports Ready=true for pod and containers conditions during kubelet level evictions

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

In 1.22+, when kubelet evicts a pod, it updates the pod status to api-server marking the pod phase as failed / succeeded. However, the kubelet continues to report Ready=true pod condition until the all of the containers are fully terminated by the container runtime. 

As a result, since the pod is still considered ready, external controllers (e.g. the endpoint controller), utilize the pod ready condition and will continue to send traffic to these pods marked in terminal phase. These pods are often not ready to serve traffic since they are in progress of being shutdown. 

This is regression from prior to 1.22, since prior to 1.22, kubelet did not send any pod/container conditions to the api-server for evicted pods. 

xref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/105358#issuecomment-932470027 for difference between kubelet status for evicted pods before and after 1.22

One of the areas where this issue manifests is with Kubelet graceful shutdown. In 1.22+, if a pod takes a long time to shutdown, during the entire shutdown process the kubelet will report Ready=true condition, and traffic will be sent to the pod. 

Additionally, If the node is shutdown before the pod fully terminates, the pod will be stuck in this state where Phase=Failed, but Ready=true. As a result, the pod will be seen incorrectly as ready by services and will be sent traffic (which the pod will likely be unable to handle due to either the pod being in progress of terminating or the node already being shutdown). 

I suspect this is issue not only for graceful shutdown, but for any type of kubelet initiated eviction. 

### What did you expect to happen?

Kubelet should maintain the same behavior as prior to 1.22. Kubelet should report Ready=false condition at the same time as marking Phase=Failed for evicted pods. Having pods in terminal phases (i.e. Failed / Succeeded), but Ready=true should not be a possible status update from kubelet to api-server. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a 1.22+ cluster with the following kubelet configuration

```
shutdownGracePeriod: 120s
shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods: 10s
```

Create the following pod (pod blocks SIGTERM and has 60s termination grace period)

```
curl -s https://gist.githubusercontent.com/bobbypage/5ef251d4d2224983472bde01c7620f6f/raw/term_pod.yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```

Trigger a graceful shutdown (either by actually shutting down machine or by sending message to dbus)

```
# on the node where term_pod is scheduled
sudo dbus-send --system /org/freedesktop/login1 org.freedesktop.login1.Manager.PrepareForShutdown boolean:true
```

Observe that the pod reports phase=Failed, but Ready=true for the entire 60s duration of shutdown

title: Deprecate IPs with Leading Zeros ( CVE-2021-29923 )

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/network
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Network.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

body:
To summarize the situation:

1. Since golang 1.17 IPv4 addresses with leading zeros are considered invalid. #100895
2. Kubernetes decided to keep compatibility with stored data so it forked previous parsers to allow IPs with leading zeros. #104368
3. The rest of the Kubernetes ecosystem seems to prefer to use default parsers and consider that data invalid https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/107552#issuecomment-1033137581

We are in a situation where users can have IPs with leading zeros in their API objects, but may not be able to use it because the CNI, DNS, Ingress, ... implementation doesn't consider it valid

The proposal is (quoting thockin) 

> How about something like:

> 1) Any new builtin APIs should use ParseIP/ParseCIDR (not sloppy) and we let validation fail.
> 2) For the places we know of (service, ingress, netpol, pod, node, ...) we set a condition like "AmbiguousAddressSyntax", log them, maybe a metric.
> 3) Allow updates to otherwise immutable fields as long as the IP adress is changing from a malformed value to a correct value.
> 4) Ship that in 1.24.
> 5) Warn that in 1.25 or 1.26 such IPs will be tolerated if they exist, but rejected for new usage.
> 6) Implement (5)
> 7) Warn that in N+1 or N+2 we will fix such IPs upon read, effectively purging them from k8s
> 8) Implement (7) and ship
> 9) Maybe put these updates in a repair loop, ship that, then eventually remove sloppy parsing entirely

_Originally posted by @thockin in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/107552#issuecomment-1035630181_

I think this is a problem of `kubelet` passing `kubeClient` into `VolumeManager` without checking if it is nil.

Related code snippet:

+ In `pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go`, `NewMainKubelet()` passed the nil `kubeClient` into `NewVolumeManager()`:

  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/559b798e25c8f8a77d380af27e696f3a68341d7e/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L799-L805

+ In `pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/volume_manager.go`, `NewVolumeManager()` passed the nil `kubeClient` into `reconciler`:
   https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/559b798e25c8f8a77d380af27e696f3a68341d7e/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/volume_manager.go#L218-L220

+ In `pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler.go`, `reconciler` used the nil `kubeClient` without checking:
  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a753dace544bbc64b4ea56c7e0adab174dbda62d/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler.go#L589-L590

### What happened?

We have a K8S 1.22.3 environment using containerd (no docker) where pods are not being consistently cleaned up. The basic idea is that we have a process that spawns several pods every couple of minutes, and those pods are subsequently deleted. They do not show up doing a 'kubectl get pods'. However, running 'crictl pods' shows that these pods sometimes stick around in a NotReady state. For example:

```
[root@node1 ~]# crictl -r unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock pods | grep prepull

8eb8b1a3a217b       45 minutes ago       NotReady            prepull-ds-uqyvjtgb-bwbmr                             delme2              0                   (default)
```

If I examine one of those pods, such as **prepull-ds-nasjpdvl-lcbzp**, then kubectl doesn't show it existing:

```
[root@node1 ~]# kubectl -n delme1 get pod prepull-ds-nasjpdvl-lcbzp
Error from server (NotFound): pods "prepull-ds-nasjpdvl-lcbzp" not found
```

The kubelet log output related to that pod, if of any value:

```
[root@node1 ~]# journalctl -u kubelet -n 100000 | grep prepull-ds-nasjpdvl-lcbzp
Feb 10 11:31:47 node1 kubelet[3123]: I0210 11:31:47.892981    3123 reconciler.go:224] "operationExecutor.VerifyControllerAttachedVolume started for volume \"tmp\" (UniqueName: \"kubernetes.io/empty-dir/8ce16f07-3fb3-42c5-ab0b-7b9c4b5c5672-tmp\") pod \"prepull-ds-nasjpdvl-lcbzp\" (UID: \"8ce16f07-3fb3-42c5-ab0b-7b9c4b5c5672\") "

FATA[0002] listing pod sandboxes: rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = grpc: trying to send message larger than max (16783177 vs. 16777216)
```

In that case no NotReady pods stick around long term like we're seeing on 1.22.3. In case it's relevant, we also see a lot of the sandbox containers persisting:

```
[root@node1 ~]# nerdctl --namespace k8s.io ps -a | grep prepull | grep Created

body:
### What happened?

We have kubernetes 1.20.8/9 with rke2. If we spawn like 100 new pods each mounting only a single pvc like this:
```
volumeMounts:
    - mountPath: /mnt
      name: vol-3689
```
which is NFS provisioned volume (a single volume on host and mount --bind attached to the pods).
We got whole node stuck in container creating as the mount is not possible with the error:
```
E0208 15:56:39.797423    3771 pod_workers.go:190] "Error syncing pod, skipping" err="unmounted volumes=[vol-3689], unattached volumes=[vol-3689]: timed out waiting for the condition" po
d="acgt-ns/nf-8e456597c72f1450bfe4e8dd7dce0595" podUID=8588a78f-fea7-4552-9458-8ad8264d69bd
```

It seems that even any other volume cannot be mounted.

All is fixed just by restarting `kubelet` but if we continue to spawn pods in parallel, it gets stuck again. Restart fixes it again. The kubelet is not stuck in any other way, just it is unable to mount any other PVC.

We use democratic-csi driver (https://github.com/democratic-csi/democratic-csi).

I recorded goroutine with the command:
```
kubectl get --insecure-skip-tls-verify=true --server="https://10.16.62.21:10250" --raw='/debug/pprof/goroutine' > goroutine.log
```
and it is attached. I have whole kubelet logs before it stuck if needed (but it is 50MB file).
[goroutine.log](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/files/8025281/goroutine.log)


### What did you expect to happen?

Kubelet should continue to mount PVCs.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Spawn many (100+) pods in parallel required to mount a PVC.

In Kubernetes 1.23 we are seeing some static pods fail to start. These static pods failures are on quick remove and adds leaving the static pod not started.

We need to revert kubernetes/kubernetes#104743.

cc @gjkim42

All static pods should restart.

```diff

body:
### What happened?

I'm running k3s with kube `1.21.x` and I am currently impacted by google/cadvisor/pull/2868 which was fixed in cadvisor `v0.40.0`. All maintained branches are currently running cadvisor `v0.39.0` except `1.23.x` which is under the latest cadvisor.

### What did you expect to happen?

Bump all supported branches of Kubernetes to cadvisor > `0.40.0`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

* Deploy the [Concourse Helm chart](https://github.com/concourse/concourse-chart)
* Deploy a test pipeline using the [concourse tutorial](https://concoursetutorial.com/)
* Introspect the metric endpoint `kubectl get --raw /api/v1/nodes/${NODE}/proxy/metrics/cadvisor`
* Container metrics will disappear after few minutes and `container_scrape_error` will start emit `1`.

Concourse workers run a lots of short lived containers using containerd. They causes cadvisor to cache miss when pulling latest container metrics and hence, completely interrupt the metric gathering.

The kubelet logs will start tracing this logs when the problem occurs:
```
W0101 23:17:43.322433    3000 prometheus.go:1856] Couldn't get containers: partial failures:
```

title: Computation of the StorageVersionHash is incorrect for overridden storage versions in unit test

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
Storage version defaults to the preferred version for a given group, but can be overridden when constructing API server storage.

This is done here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/035f22d7810a8970e42d60f276f71a519b174a44/pkg/kubeapiserver/default_storage_factory_builder.go#L60-L67

Reasons the preferred version might be overridden:
* A given resource/kind does not yet exist in the preferred version (like when introducing a new alpha type in an existing API group with more stable versions)
* A given resource/kind is continuing to store in etcd in an older version for compatibility with n-1 API servers

The etcd integration test verifies that we're actually storing the correct versions in etcd, but the computation of the StorageVersionHash is not honoring the overridden version.

on master, this code reports v1 CSIStorageCapacity:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/035f22d7810a8970e42d60f276f71a519b174a44/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/installer.go#L398-L408

even though the etcd test verifies we're still persisting v1beta1

/kind bug
/priority important-soon
/sig api-machinery

cc @pohly

_Originally posted by @liggitt in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/109394#issuecomment-1164608879_

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
### What happened?

Kubelet was not able to attach + mount an iSCSI PV when it has IPv6 server address.

### What did you expect to happen?

Volume is mounted + attached.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Set up iSCSI target that's reachable over IPv6 and create a PV for it.

For example:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: iscsi-pv
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  capacity:
    storage: 5Gi
  iscsi:
    targetPortal: "[2001:db8:0:f101::1]:3260"
    iqn: iqn.2003-01.io.k8s:jsafrane
    lun: 0

body:
### What happened?

During scale testing, as sig-scalability, we observed that node-lifecycle-controller (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/nodelifecycle/node_lifecycle_controller.go) was unable to process nodes  in reasonable time due to lock contention. 

Example log:
```
2022-04-19 19:06:29.860 GMT
Node ... is NotReady as of 2022-04-19 19:06:09.872955473 +0000 UTC m=+592959.664121666. Adding it to the Taint queue.
```
The difference between log timestamp 19:06:29.860 and decision timestamp 19:06:09.872955473 is around 20s. 
As a part of method `processTaintBaseEviction` I can see that `markNodeForTainting` was executed, which takes `evictorLock`. 
My suspicion is that it was waiting on this lock for ~20s. I can see that this lock might be taken by other goroutines that execute api calls under lock, for example https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/451e1fa8bcff38b87504eebd414948e505526d01/pkg/controller/nodelifecycle/node_lifecycle_controller.go#L666

The whole `monitorNodeHealth` loop took around 40 minutes in total for one pass through all nodes in this cluster.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected node-lifecycle-controller to process nodes in reasonable time

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This test was run on large cluster and we removed significant portion of nodes - around 4k nodes out of 15k nodes. 

### Anything else we need to know?

Related issue that was opened before: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83954
Related comment in code: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/451e1fa8bcff38b87504eebd414948e505526d01/pkg/controller/nodelifecycle/node_lifecycle_controller.go#L281

title: The current use of etcd Leases in Kubernetes violates the invariants needed for watch to function correctly

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
We're currently (potentially) attaching the same etcd Lease to multiple objects based on the LeaseManager configuration:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/lease_manager.go#L34

However, when the lease expires in etcd, all objects that are attached to that lease are actually deleted in a single transaction:
https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/e02ac59cfc4e750f4b0a2a121e20db8e6775d5cd/server/lease/lessor.go#L338-L356

This basically means, that deletions of all of them  will have exactly the same ResourceVersion.

The above violates the invariant that we need in order to ensure that watch requests can be resumed at any point:
- let's say that a watch breaks (e.g. TCP connection gets closed or sth) in the middle of processing objects from a given transaction (which by definition all have the same RV)
- then the client will try to resume from the last receive RV
- but that would mean that the ones from that transaction that wasn't processed previously will get missed and not delivered to that client

Fortunately, the TTL function (that is what decides whether an etcd Lease will be attached to the object or not) is only configured for events:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/registry/core/event/storage/storage.go#L42

so we don't seem to be exposed for the bug in any core controllers.

That said we are still exposed to a bug that even when used correctly, WATCH requests for events may miss some DELETE events.

/sig api-machinery
/priority important-soon
/kind bug

@liggitt @deads2k @lavalamp @stevekuznetsov @kubernetes/sig-api-machinery-bugs 
@mm4tt @mborsz
