body:
### What happened?

We have a HorizontalPodAutoscaler configured on all of our fleet. The issue arises when we are scaling down, a node is being drained and a pod on that node is part of the `FC` service. We get around ten exceptions each time, Sentry reporting `AbortedException`s in FC and `CompletionException`s with "Socket timed out" in the `OS` service, which calls `FC`. 

The timeline each time is roughly the following:

Kubernetes logs that a node is being shut down, and lists the pods to be rescheduled, and announces they're being deleted:

```
2022-05-05 11:29:31
{"verb":"ADDED","event":{"metadata":{"name":"cluster-autoscaler-status.16ec2ec153756434","namespace":"kube-system","uid":"db99aeed-834e-46a0-bb89-0931987fce36","resourceVersion":"100272736","creationTimestamp":"2022-05-05T10:29:31Z","managedFields":[{"manager":"cluster-autoscaler","operation":"Update","apiVersion":"v1","time":"2022-05-05T10:29:31Z"}]},"involvedObject":{"kind":"ConfigMap","namespace":"kube-system","name":"cluster-autoscaler-status","uid":"24c310d4-f20e-11e9-94e1-42010a9a013d","apiVersion":"v1","resourceVersion":"2436651783"},"reason":"ScaleDown","message":"Scale-down: removing node gke-gke-web-gb-lh-packages-04-93b2f460-z7kx, utilization: {0.13707037643207856 0.25945028981080676 0 memory 0.25945028981080676}, pods to reschedule: FC-55c779745f-7xtv7","source":{"component":"cluster-autoscaler"},"firstTimestamp":"2022-05-05T10:29:31Z","lastTimestamp":"2022-05-05T10:29:31Z","count":1,"type":"Normal","eventTime":null,"reportingComponent":"","reportingInstance":""}}
```
```
2022-05-05 11:29:31
{"verb":"ADDED","event":{"metadata":{"name":"FC-55c779745f-7xtv7.16ec2ec1542e4d59","namespace":"sas","uid":"e6de5ba1-a55a-4674-8ecd-681072cd9a71","resourceVersion":"100272764","creationTimestamp":"2022-05-05T10:29:31Z","managedFields":[{"manager":"cluster-autoscaler","operation":"Update","apiVersion":"v1","time":"2022-05-05T10:29:31Z"}]},"involvedObject":{"kind":"Pod","namespace":"sas","name":"FC-55c779745f-7xtv7","uid":"8a2c56ec-90d3-4177-851c-dbc2dbd2d711","apiVersion":"v1","resourceVersion":"2436185076"},"reason":"ScaleDown","message":"deleting pod for node scale down","source":{"component":"cluster-autoscaler"},"firstTimestamp":"2022-05-05T10:29:31Z","lastTimestamp":"2022-05-05T10:29:31Z","count":1,"type":"Normal","eventTime":null,"reportingComponent":"","reportingInstance":""}}
```

3-5 seconds later, the exceptions begin: 

```
2022-05-05 11:29:34
"Servlet.service() for servlet [dispatcherServlet] in context with path [] threw exception [Request processing failed; nested exception is java.util.concurrent.CompletionException: org.springframework.web.client.ResourceAccessException: I/O error on GET request for \"http://FC.local:": Read timed out; nested exception is java.net.SocketTimeoutException: Read timed out] with root cause",
```

(no root cause reported).

The errors end within a few seconds. 30 seconds later we get the readiness/liveness probes failing:

```
2022-05-05 11:32:03 
{"verb":"ADDED","event":{"metadata":{"name":"FC-55c779745f-7xtv7.16ec2ee4e1c36c9a","namespace":"sas","uid":"d020c795-28ce-4d89-9880-5f49e19e20a1","resourceVersion":"100273164","creationTimestamp":"2022-05-05T10:32:03Z","managedFields":[{"manager":"kubelet","operation":"Update","apiVersion":"v1","time":"2022-05-05T10:32:03Z"}]},"involvedObject":{"kind":"Pod","namespace":"sas","name":"FC-55c779745f-7xtv7","uid":"8a2c56ec-90d3-4177-851c-dbc2dbd2d711","apiVersion":"v1","resourceVersion":"2436182151","fieldPath":"spec.containers{radar}"},"reason":"Unhealthy","message":"Readiness probe failed: Get \"http://10.133.33.11:8080/actuator/health/readiness\": dial tcp 10.133.33.11:8080: connect: connection refused","source":{"component":"kubelet","host":"gke-gke-web-gb-lh-packages-04-93b2f460-z7kx"},"firstTimestamp":"2022-05-05T10:32:03Z","lastTimestamp":"2022-05-05T10:32:03Z","count":1,"type":"Warning","eventTime":null,"reportingComponent":"","reportingInstance":""}}
```

We can see on the FC pod logs that it continues serving requests (some requests complete successfully) until 11:29:56.

Eventually pod does shut down, usually with a KillContainerException because the heap dump process hasn't terminated in time.

```
2022-05-05 11:32:31 
{"verb":"ADDED","event":{"metadata":{"name":"FC-55c779745f-7xtv7.16ec2eeb593d395d","namespace":"sas","uid":"b0b50f18-f6b1-493f-bc27-edcfb59ad817","resourceVersion":"100273218","creationTimestamp":"2022-05-05T10:32:31Z","managedFields":[{"manager":"kubelet","operation":"Update","apiVersion":"v1","time":"2022-05-05T10:32:31Z"}]},"involvedObject":{"kind":"Pod","namespace":"sas","name":"FC-55c779745f-7xtv7","uid":"8a2c56ec-90d3-4177-851c-dbc2dbd2d711","apiVersion":"v1","resourceVersion":"2436182151"},"reason":"FailedKillPod","message":"error killing pod: failed to \"KillContainer\" for \"ship-heap-dump\" with KillContainerError: \"rpc error: code = Unknown desc = operation timeout: context deadline exceeded\"","source":{"component":"kubelet","host":"gke-gke-web-gb-lh-packages-04-93b2f460-z7kx"},"firstTimestamp":"2022-05-05T10:32:31Z","lastTimestamp":"2022-05-05T10:32:31Z","count":1,"type":"Warning","eventTime":null,"reportingComponent":"","reportingInstance":""}}
```

So far we have no idea why these errors occur. We have grace period configured:

```
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 180
```
and we have a preStop hook in each container too:
```
        - name: FC
          env:
             ...
          lifecycle:
            preStop:
              exec:
                command:
                - /bin/sh
                - -c
                - sleep 150
```
We are also using an internal GCP load balancer on this service, but we haven't established any link between it and the errors.

So shutdowns should be as graceful as possible, but they aren't. Any idea what's going on?









### What did you expect to happen?

Expect the node draining and shutdowns to be graceful.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Try the kubernetes settings listed - but they should work just fine. Let me know if you need any additional info to repro.

body:
### What happened?

When we add custom annotations to PodSandboxConfig.Annotations in function generatePodSandboxConfig， kubelet crashes with errror:
kubelet[2257292]: fatal error: concurrent map read and map write

The role of function generatePodSandboxConfig(located at kuberuntime_sandbox.go) is to create SandboxConfig that is used to RunSandbox. In some scenarios, we want to pass custom annotations to runtime  through PodsandboxConfig.Annotations .

In kubelet,  multiple goroutins access *v1.Pod fetched from podManager at the same time with no lock. For example, syncPod goroutin and  volumeManager goroutin get *v1.Pod from podManager， when there is  writing pod.Annotations operations,  kubelet will panic.

So, in function generatePodSandboxConfig，a deep copy of pod.Annotations  should be performed.




### What did you expect to happen?

Kubelet process won't panic when we add custom annotations to PodSandboxConfig.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Writing podSandboxConfig.Annotations in function generatePodSandboxConfig

- (No, really, you MUST read this before you upgrade) Before you upgrade to Kubernetes 1.24, if you use a CNI network plugin that complies with [Container Network Interface](https://github.com/containernetworking/cni) (CNI) versions earlier than v1.0.0 and you plan to use any of the following container runtimes, you must specify the CNI version as described in [Declaring the CNI version of your plugin](TBD). - For Kubernetes v1.24 GA, when you upgrade one of the following container runtimes, safely drain (cordon) your node, upgrade your CNI plugins to the latest versions, and confirm that your CNI config files specify/match the correct versions for your plugins. ### What happened?

```

  annotations:

  managedFields:
  - apiVersion: v1
    fieldsType: FieldsV1
    fieldsV1:
      f:data:
        .: {}
        f:key: {}
      f:metadata:
        f:annotations:
          .: {}
          f:kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration: {}
    manager: kubectl-client-side-apply
    operation: Update
    time: "2022-04-20T20:37:52Z"
  name: test1
  namespace: default
  resourceVersion: "19304095"
  uid: 5fb6f9b3-9d9b-475b-89f8-b0d0fe3f2348
```

```
kind: ConfigMap

sleep 5

kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
kind: ConfigMap
```

body:
### What happened?

The scheduler cache entered a corrupted state where a Pod, according to the cache dump, was nominated to node A, while the status said it was nominated to node B.

This lead to unschedulable low priority pods due to the phantom pod in the nominator cache.

### What did you expect to happen?

The cache to match the Pod status

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Setup: two nodes with all the resources used. A high priority pod comes in that is able to preempt at least one pod.

This might cause these sequence of events

1. Pod X doesn't fit, it gets nominated to `node-y` and added back to scheduling queue.
2. We start a second scheduling attempt for Pod X.
3. We get a Pod update for the `.status.nominatedPodName`. This puts the pod back into the scheduling queue.
4. The second scheduling attempt finishes and schedules the pod successfully in `node-y`
5. We start a third scheduling attempt for Pod X (due to 3)
6. We get a Pod update for the `.spec.nodeName`. This should have cleared the nominated node in the cache, but there is nothing currently there.
7. In the third scheduling attempt, the pod doesn't fit, so the scheduler nominates it to `node-z`. Nothing clears this nomination afterwards

Usually step 2 happens after 3, so everything works as expected. But in a busy cluster, 3 might be delayed.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

`1.21.9`

title: Change in semantics for the device plugin registration process

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: lifecycle/stale
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR has remained open with no activity and has become stale.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

The following refactoring of the kubelet's devicemanager was done as part of the 1.25 release: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/db88676c20629354d8eeb4b7014ae7884481ffca

As part of this, a change in semantics was (unintentionally) introduced which is breaking at least one 3rd party plugin. The logic required to go back to the old semantics is fairly straight forward. However, it's not obvious that we should actually go back to the old semantics because (at least in my opinion) the new semantics are actually more correct.

Previously, the kubelet's devicemanager would do the following upon receiving a plugin registration request:
1. Register the plugin
2. Launch a go-routine to connect to the gRPC service being served by the plugin (with a timeout of 10s)
3. Return

This gave the plugin the opportunity to first register itself with the kubelet and then (within a 10s time window) start its gRPC server.

The new semantics are similar, except that no go-routine is launched to connect to the gRPC service. The connection is attempted synchronously. This means that the plugin must now start serving its gRPC server *before* registering itself with the kubelet. Otherwise the registration call will fail.

As mentioned before, this change was not necessarily intentional, but it's also not clear if it should be reverted. It brings the device plugin's custom registration process more in line with the kubelet's standard registration process and the order is actually a bit more intuitive. Why bother registering if you aren't able to start serving your API?

The first plugin to report this problem was the KubeVirt plugin and a discussion of the issue can be found here:
https://groups.google.com/g/kubevirt-dev/c/HE2lVvsLd3Y

The question now is -- should we revert the kubelet code to the old semantics to avoid breaking plugins that rely on this (somewhat awkward) ordering. Or do we leave the new semantics in place and send out an announcement of this (potentially) breaking change?

One thing to keep in mind -- if we go with the second option (i.e. keep the new semantics and force plugins to update), the updated plugins will continue to work on older versions of kubernetes since the ordering now implied in the new semantics has always been correct.

### What did you expect to happen?

Plugins relying on the old semantics would continue to work on kubernetes 1.25

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Write a plugin that:
1. Registers itself with the kubelet
2. Only then starts to server the plugin API via a gRPC server

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

body:
### What happened?

StatefulSet spec's template was updated:

<details>

```apiVersion: v1
items:
- apiVersion: apps/v1
  kind: StatefulSet
  # many other unrelated stuff
  spec:
    replicas: 5
    minReadySeconds: 300
    podManagementPolicy: Parallel
    updateStrategy:
      rollingUpdate:
        maxUnavailable: 1
```
</details>

Kubernetes has updated all pods one-by-one in a quick succession, the next pod was updated as soon as previous one has passed the startup probe.
`status.availableReplicas` has dropped from 5 to 0 over the course of the push (which took ≈3 minutes).

### What did you expect to happen?

I did expected that kubernetes would update pods one-by-one, taking `minReadySeconds` into account, the next pod was expected to be updated `minReadySeconds` seconds after previous one has passed the startup probe.
`status.availableReplicas` should not have been dropped below 4 at any point (as `maxUnavailable` is explicitly set to 1).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a `StatefulSet` with the spec above, and update its `spec.template` field to trigger a rollout.
`MaxUnavailableStatefulSet` and `StatefulSetMinReadySeconds` feature gates must be enabled.

title: Using exec auth in kubectl triggers one connection per applied/described object

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: sig/auth
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Auth.

labels.name: sig/cli
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG CLI.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

Switching from the gcp auth provider to the exec auth provider in 1.25 made `kubectl apply` requests which previously made a single connection to the API server make one connection per applied object.

If enough items are applied, the connections can start to fail because of ephemeral port exhaustion

/kind bug
/milestone v1.25
/sig auth cli api-machinery

### What did you expect to happen?

Switching to the exec auth plugin would allow commands that previously worked to continue to work

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Reproducer integration test at https://github.com/liggitt/kubernetes/commits/exec-auth-reproducer demonstrating one transport (and therefore a new connection) for each item in an applied file when using exec auth

on that branch:
```
go test ./test/integration/client/ -run TestApplyMultipleItemsWithExecPlugin -v
```
and observe 10 transport creations to apply 10 items (plus a couple others for discovery):
```
before apply
creating transport
creating transport
creating transport
creating transport
creating transport
creating transport
creating transport
creating transport
creating transport
creating transport
creating transport
creating transport
after apply
```

### Anything else we need to know?

This happens because exec auth setup unconditionally sets the GetCert field in transport config here (even if the plugin is only going to return token credentials):

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/58c10aa6eb5adfb1f3aa4d6cb898b8c347ba9e72/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/plugin/pkg/client/auth/exec/exec.go#L303

That makes the transport config uncacheable here:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/58c10aa6eb5adfb1f3aa4d6cb898b8c347ba9e72/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/transport/cache.go#L141-L144

Commands like `kubectl describe` and `kubectl apply` repeatedly construct transports when dealing with multiple objects. This poor behavior was masked in past configurations by the transports being cached.

### Kubernetes version

tried with 1.24 and 1.25, reproduced with both

title: kube-proxy should report events when the proxier failovers

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/network
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Network.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What would you like to be added?

kube-proxy should report k8s events of critical cases instead of just logging, e.g., kube-proxy failovers to iptables proxier when it should be running ipvs proxier, see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.24.3/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server_others.go#L588

There might be other critical cases need sysadmin's attention, maybe we should check everywhere.

### Why is this needed?

The background is: we recently had kube-proxy’s ipvs scheduling algorithm changed, but one of the nodes didn’t have the corresponding kernel module. When the kube-proxy agent restarts, it failed to enable ipvs proxier, and failovered to iptables proxier. As a result, the ipvs rules and iptables rules are mixed together, causing network issues. I think this kind of failover is rather important, should be reported as k8s events.

title: kubelet: The Plugin Watcher not working as intended on Windows

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/windows
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Windows.

labels.name: sig/testing
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Testing.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
### What happened?

Looking at [1], we can see that the plugin Watcher is traversing the plugin directory, and check whether a new file is a unix socket or not. However, ``mode&os.ModeSocket != 0``, will never be True on Windows. We can also see this in the logs when running the unit test ``TestDevicePluginReRegistrationProbeMode``:

```
I0726 14:24:39.533351    8104 plugin_watcher.go:149] "Ignoring file" path="C:\\Users\\capi\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\device_plugin302605223\\device-plugin.sock" mode="-rw-rw-rw-"
I0726 14:24:39.533351    8104 plugin_watcher.go:149] "Ignoring file" path="C:\\Users\\capi\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\device_plugin302605223\\server.sock" mode="-rw-rw-rw-"
```

Those file should not have been ignored.

Instead of using ``mode&os.ModeSocket != 0``, we should use instead ``util.IsUnixDomainSocket``, which also has a Windows implementation [2].

This issue may also cause the unit tests ``TestPluginRegistration`` and ``TestPluginRegistrationAtKubeletStart`` to flake [3].

[1] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7a8f8a32092ede759519f600ca4ac1a319a0bc1d/pkg/kubelet/pluginmanager/pluginwatcher/plugin_watcher.go#L139
[2] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7a8f8a32092ede759519f600ca4ac1a319a0bc1d/pkg/kubelet/util/util_windows.go#L140
[3] https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/110981/pull-ci-kubernetes-unit-windows/1546592017314746368

### What did you expect to happen?

Instead of using ``mode&os.ModeSocket != 0``, we should use instead ``util.IsUnixDomainSocket``, which also has a Windows implementation [2]. This will result in the plugin Watcher to work as intended.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run the ``TestDevicePluginReRegistrationProbeMode`` unit test.

title: Prolonged etcd reelection causes api-server to close all watchers.

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: wg/reliability
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to WG Reliability

body:
### What happened?

When etcd is unable to elect leader for 3 election cycles, etcd returns "no leader" error through watches.
This can be seen in api-server logs as `watch chan error: etcdserver: no leader`.
Also, when apiserver receives this error, it terminates all watchers: `Terminating all watchers from cacher  ...`.

In large clusters, this can destabilize master, as all these watchers need to be recreated almost at the same time, overwhelming api-server quite often. 

I propose adding new api-server flag that allows to specify timeout, during which we are retrying to reestablish apiserver <-> etcd watches, without terminating all api-server watchers. If we are unable to reestablish watches within this specified timeout, we start terminating all watchers.


### What did you expect to happen?

Losing etcd leader for ~2-3s does not destabilize api-server.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Trigger prolonged reelection of etcd leader.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

Observed in all kubernetes versions 1.19-1.24

title: Node lifecycle controller takes too long to mark pods NotReady

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/network
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Network.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
### What happened?

We run a cluster spread across 3 sites/availability zones, and when an entire site becomes unreachable at once we observe that the node lifecycle controller takes too long to mark all the pods NotReady.

Example logs:
```
I0713 16:03:36.538269       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:1092] node ... hasn't been updated for 20.062703613s.
…
I0713 16:04:48.014322       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:1092] node ... hasn't been updated for 1m27.527087635s.
```

We set `--node-monitor-grace-period=20s`, and the first node is processed right at the 20s mark. But it takes over a minute until it processes the last node.

I believe this is because the main loop in monitorNodeHealth processes each node serially.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/17bf864c1fc20e4badc9a6e0659c5190310462e1/pkg/controller/nodelifecycle/node_lifecycle_controller.go#L796
And processing each node requires setting the ready status of each of its pods to false, serially.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/17bf864c1fc20e4badc9a6e0659c5190310462e1/pkg/controller/util/node/controller_utils.go#L119

With enough nodes and pods, this time quickly adds up and leaves unreachable pods in endpoints for too long.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected the node lifecycle controller to mark pods on unreachable nodes NotReady soon after the nodes exceeded the node monitor grace period.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

We observe this with a cluster of ~150 nodes spread evenly across 3 sites, so ~50 nodes become unreachable at once when we drop a site.

### Anything else we need to know?

This is somewhat similar to #110341, but at a different stage. We tested with 1.25.2 as well (it contains the fix for #110341) and observed the same behavior.

We have tested a small patch to `monitorNodeHealth` to process nodes in their own goroutines, using a semaphore to bound the concurrency to `scheduler.UpdateWorkerSize` (matching the concurrency of `doNodeProcessingPassWorker`). This is working well for us since most of the time marking pods NotReady is just waiting on i/o. I’ll follow up with a PR with the patch.

### Kubernetes version

We noticed this in 1.21.13, but verified the same behavior exists in 1.25.2.

title: PV handling of beta topology labels

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
### What happened?

Offshoot discussion from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114120 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/89477

There has been a lot of work since 1.14 to start using the GA topology labels instead of the beta topology labels.

The intree volume provisioning logic has been updated to create PVs with the GA topology labels (both as a label, and in PV.NodeAffinity) and the CSI migration library has been updated to understand both beta and GA labels and convert them in-memory to the CSI equivalent labels in order to support old PVs with only beta labels: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/98281

However, there's still a few gaps:
1. The CSI migration logic only handles conversion of the beta labels for intree volume types. External volume types are not covered.
2. The [VolumeZone](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumezone) scheduling plugin does not exercise the csi migration logic. The original plan was that with csi migration we could remove the VolumeZone plugin entirely because its functionality is replaced by the [VolumeBinding](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumebinding) plugin. Again, this assumption is only true for intree volume types that we provision and does not account for users that may have their own custom provisioning logic.

These issues mean that if we remove the beta label on nodes, we can break existing PVs that only use the beta label, for both intree and external volume types.


### What did you expect to happen?

There's a couple of options (not necessarily mutually exclusive) that we can pursue:
1. Anywhere we look at PV labels (scheduler, kubelet), translate beta labels to GA labels in-memory regardless of csi migration. This method requires the fewest user changes but since the object itself is not changed, users may still see warnings about use of the beta labels.
2. Relax PV.NodeAffinity mutability to allow changing the beta label to GA label (changing PV.Labels should already be allowed). And then
    a. Require the user to change all the labels themselves. This is quite burdensome but gives the user the most control over when and how to change it.
    b. Provide tooling/controller that updates all the objects. Convenient, but could possibly break the user if they had tooling/workflows that were depending on the beta label.
3. Never remove the beta topology label from the node and continue supporting it forever. Similar to how we say beta annotations are part of the API, and stable APIs are supported forever: https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-policy/#deprecating-parts-of-the-api

I think we should do some form of option 2 regardless.

If 3 is out of the question, then I would say 1 + 2a, which gives us the benefit removing the label from nodes and letting users convert on their own time. But this would probably apply more to just PVs; anywhere we allow users to specify the labels needs to be able to handle this.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Remove the beta zone label on a Node and try to schedule a Pod using PV.labels with the beta zone label.

Analyzing the flake in https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/114171/pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce-ubuntu-containerd/1597607186182180864/


> I1129 15:36:57.958493       1 proxier.go:303] "Iptables sync params" ipFamily=IPv4 minSyncPeriod="10s" syncPeriod="1m0s" burstSyncs=2

> minSyncPeriod is the minimum period that iptables rules are refreshed

every change will be queued until the minimum period has expired,


The test `Kubernetes e2e suite: [It] [sig-network] Services should not be able to connect to terminating and unready endpoints if PublishNotReadyAddresses` works as follows:
- create a NodePort Service with one backend Pod
- check NodePort Service works
- make the backend Pod unready
- check that the NodePort Service doesn't work (kube-proxy should not forward traffic to the unready Pod)

body:
### What happened?

When OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement admission plugin is enabled, StatefulSetAutoDeletePVC feature cannot delete PVCs when scaling down a StatefulSet.

### What did you expect to happen?

StatefulSetAutoDeletePVC deletes PVCs when scaling down a StatefulSet

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Run Kubernetes with OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement admission & StatefulSetAutoDeletePVC feature gate enabled

    For example, using local-up-cluster.sh:
    ```
    export FEATURE_GATES=StatefulSetAutoDeletePVC=true
    export ENABLE_ADMISSION_PLUGINS=NamespaceLifecycle,LimitRanger,ServiceAccount,DefaultStorageClass,DefaultTolerationSeconds,Priority,MutatingAdmissionWebhook,ValidatingAdmissionWebhook,ResourceQuota,NodeRestriction,OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement
    export ENABLE_HOSTPATH_PROVISIONER=true
    export ALLOW_PRIVILEGED=true
    hack/local-up-cluster.sh
    ```

2. Create a StatefulSet with some replicas and:
    ```
    persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy:
      whenDeleted: Delete
      whenScaled: Delete
    ```

3. Scale down the statefulset.
4. Check PVCs are still present && `kubect describe statefulset` complains:

>   Warning  FailedUpdate      2m39s                  statefulset-controller  update Pod web-2 in StatefulSet web failed error: Could not update claim www-web-2 for delete policy ownerRefs: persistentvolumeclaims "www-web-2" is forbidden: cannot set an ownerRef on a resource you can't delete: , <nil>


### Anything else we need to know?

title: Endpoints doesn't reconcile in some cases from instance that is shutting down

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a regression from a prior release.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

Hi,

At the time of shutdown process of an control-plane instance,   apiserver attemps to remove it's `master Lease-object` from etcd, and it may not find the lease-object in storage  if the leases already expire by the time APIServer attempts to delete it from storage [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controlplane/reconcilers/lease.go#L123) , in such cases it will error out [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controlplane/controller.go#L214) with following error depending on the k8s version it's on
```
controller.go:184] StorageError: key not found, Code: 1, Key: /registry/masterleases//172.18.100.37, 
```
because of this line [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controlplane/reconcilers/lease.go#L316) errors out to delete from storage 

And endpoint won't be reconciled during the shutdown process from behind the Kubernetes service backend. Due to this some clients may still attempt connecting to old instance for some period of time as kube-proxy won't update the endpoints until new controller reconciler loop from another instances kicks off and removes the old endpoint.


Example of  `connection refused` errors that clients experience on client applications because of the above issue 
 ```
no more retries error: unable to recognize \""/tmp/manifest.yaml\"": Get \""https://10.100.0.1:443/api?timeout=32s\"": dial tcp 10.100.0.1:443: connect: connection refused"",""object"":{""apiVersion"":""v1"",""count"":1,""eventTime"":null,""firstTimestamp"":""2022-11-09T22:25:21Z"",""involvedObject"":
```





### What did you expect to happen?

Given there can be potential cases where our shutdown can take longer or don't end gracefully, our shutdown process can be more resilient and tolerate errors from storage and continue with reconciling anyway IIUC,
so I propose a fix  [here]( https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.20/pkg/controlplane/reconcilers/lease.go#L299) , basically swallow/log this error when you have issues deleting a lease-object from storage and continue with reconciling to update endpoint object.


^^^ what this gives us is, incases when there was no expiry of `master-leaseobject` from `etcd`,  it will be a no-op and continue to work the way it is i.e remove it from storage successfully and then reconcile. But in cases of `master-lease object` from etcd  expires, it will fail to find the key in etcd like in this case but because of this potential fix(swallowing the error and logging it), it will continue to reconcile the endpoints and this code [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controlplane/reconcilers/lease.go#L204)  will have updated master endpoints from etcd anyway at the time of reconciliation and help keep endpoints behind K8s service up-to-date during the shutdown process and doesn't have to wait until next periodic reconciler/new instance controller reconciler loop kicks in.


If you like above proposed solution, I can submit a PR for this. Please let me know. Thank you.



### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1) Let clients continue to make new connections every sec to instance you are about to terminate
2)  Delay the shutdown process until `master-lease` object in etcd expires for a given instance
2) Let APIServer continue with shutdown down process so it fails with the error 
```
controller.go:184] StorageError: key not found, Code: 1, Key: /registry/masterleases//172.18.100.37, 
```
4) Check error in client logs saying ```connection refused``` because it was trying to connect to old instance (tcp dump may help here to help look at it clearly that it was making a  connection to IP/endpoint of old instance and failing because `connection refused` error at network layer.

_No response_

title: dynamic resource allocation: delete generated ResourceClaims

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
At the moment, dynamic resource allocation relies on the garbage collector to delete a ResourceClaim that was created from a template for a specific pod. But that garbage collection only happens when the pod actually gets deleted.

That means that for pods that linger after having failed or completed (manually created test pods, jobs), resources remain allocated for extended periods of time although they are not needed anymore and could be reused for other claims.

The solution outlined in the KEP is to make the `resourceclaim` controller also responsible for deleting ResourceClaims when it detects that a pod no longer needs the claim.

title: Support topology aware routing (node and zone)

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/network
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Network.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
**How to categorize this issue?**
/sig networking
/kind feature
/priority important-soon

**What would you like to be added**:
Currently there is no way to achieve topology aware routing (`kubernetes.io/hostname`, `topology.kubernetes.io/zone`, `topology.kubernetes.io/region`) and define _deterministic_ rules like the ones offered from the already deprecated and removed [`ServiceTopology`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service-topology/):
> - Prefer endpoints on the same node, fall back on any available endpoint if none are available for this node: `["kubernetes.io/hostname", "*"]`.
> - Prefer enpoints on the same zone, but fallback on any available endpoint if none are available within this zone: `["topology.kubernetes.io/zone", "*"]`.
> - Prefer endpoints on the same node, fall back to endpoints in the same zone, followed by the same region, and failing otherwise: `["kubernetes.io/hostname", "topology.kubernetes.io/zone", "topology.kubernetes.io/region"]`. This may be useful, for example, in cases where data locality is critical.

The `ServiceTopology` feature was deprecated (and removed in K8s 1.22) in favor of [`TopologyAwareHints`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/topology-aware-hints/):
> Note: This feature, specifically the alpha topologyKeys API, is deprecated since Kubernetes v1.21. Topology Aware Hints, introduced in Kubernetes v1.21, provide similar functionality.

Although that the docs write that TopologyAwareHints "provide similar functionality", this is not reflecting the reality. TopologyAwareHints is a feature that is applicable only in particular use cases and is not a replacement for the feature offering of ServiceTopology.

Drawbacks of TopologyAwareHints:
- Sometimes the CPU-balance heuristic is wrong. For example, if we know that the whole zonal CPU pool does not model the set of clients which will access a service, then we may erroneously disable hints. (ref https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/110714#issuecomment-1178163573)
- Hints do not work at low-endpoint counts. (ref https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/110714#issuecomment-1178163573)
- Hints are not deterministic.
- ...

Scenarios from the topology aware routing story that TopologyAwareHints do not cover:
- Prefer endpoints on the same node, fall back on any available endpoint if none are available for this node: `["kubernetes.io/hostname", "*"]`.
- Prefer enpoints on the same zone, but fallback on any available endpoint if none are available within this zone: `["topology.kubernetes.io/zone", "*"]`.

**Why is this needed**:
To allow end users to configure topology aware rounting. For example cross-zone traffic is charged from most of the cloud providers.

**References**:
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/110714 - issue that discusses that not every scenario is covered by TopologyAwareHints.
- https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3642 - TopologyAwareHints KEP update PR that proposes support for `service.kubernetes.io/topology-aware-hints=always`
- https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3293 - KEP that proposes support for `["kubernetes.io/hostname", "*"]`
- https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3765 - TopologyAwareHints KEP update PR that proposes SameZone heuristic

body:
While working on generalizing tests to somehow better define spec for storage interface (and share them across all implementation of storage.interface - in particular etcd3 and watchcache), I found an unexpected inconsistency in Delete operation in etcd3.

What is happening is that it effectively returns the state of the object from just before the deletion:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.25/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/store.go#L325

However, this is inconsistent with how our watch is working, which is returning the state of the object from just before the deletion, *but* it sets the RV to the moment of deletion (which Delete call isn't doing).


This sounds like a bug to me, but given this is a long-standing behavior we may need to take additional care when fixing this.

/kind bug
/sig api-machinery
/priority important-soon

/cc @liggitt @deads2k @lavalamp @kubernetes/sig-api-machinery-bugs

body:
### What happened?

``go get`` for installing golang binaries has been deprecated in Go 1.17 in favor of ``go install``. Starting with Go 1.19, we can no longer install binaries through ``go get``. [1]

We've recently switched to Go 1.19, and because of this, the ``sample-apiserver`` E2E image has started failing to build recently [2] with the error:

```
 go: go.mod file not found in current directory or any parent directory.
	'go get' is no longer supported outside a module.
	To build and install a command, use 'go install' with a version,
	like 'go install example.com/cmd@latest'
	For more information, see https://golang.org/doc/go-get-install-deprecation
	or run 'go help get' or 'go help install'. 
```

Using ``go install`` for ``k8s.io/sample-apiserver~v0.17.0`` directly doesn't work either:

```
go install k8s.io/sample-apiserver@v0.17.0
go: downloading k8s.io/sample-apiserver v0.17.0
go: k8s.io/sample-apiserver@v0.17.0 (in k8s.io/sample-apiserver@v0.17.0):
        The go.mod file for the module providing named packages contains one or
        more replace directives. It must not contain directives that would cause
        it to be interpreted differently than if it were the main module.
```

[1] https://go.dev/doc/go-get-install-deprecation
[2] https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/post-kubernetes-push-e2e-sample-apiserver-test-images/1580625892458106880

### What did you expect to happen?

The image should be buildable.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```
cd kubernetes/test/images
make all-push WHAT=sample-apiserver
```

body:
### What happened?

I deployed a CRD (`teleportroles`) with the shortnames `role` and `roles`, conflicting with `roles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1`.

Initially `kubectl get role` and `kubectl get roles` were both returnning `roles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1` resources.

I ran `kubectl get teleportrole`.

Now, `kubectl get role` return my CRs instead of `roles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1` resources.

However `kubectl get roles` continues to return `roles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1` resources.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect kubectl's behaviour to be consistent. The outcome of `kubectl get X` should not depend on the order the APIs were discovered and cached. I also expect exact names to be preferred over shortnames.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

On a freshly kubectl context (not one you already used and might have cached RESTMappings):
- create a CRD with a shortname conflicting with another resource, `role` for example
- run `kubectl get role -n kube-sytem` (because there are roles by default there) and `kubectl get roles -n kube-system`
- observe the kube rbac resources are properly returned
- run `kubectl get yourcrd` once
- run `kubectl get role -n kube-sytem` (because there are roles by default there) and `kubectl get roles -n kube-system`
- observe the `kubectl get role` no longer returns the kubernetes roles, but `kubectl get roles` still does. 

### Anything else we need to know?

During initial resolution, [exact name matches are preferred](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/58861). It seems this property is not true anymore when doing cache lookups. When cache was populated by `kubectl get teleportroles`, it overrode the mapping `role` -> `roles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1`

I believe this is the same issue as https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/59812

body:
### What would you like to be added?

As described here: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/647#issuecomment-1078834288, we want current calls to k8s.io/utils/trace to create OpenTelemetry spans and span events if tracing is enabled in that component.

Requirements:

* Keep existing log-based tracing intact.
* Allow using log-based tracing and OpenTelemetry tracing simultaneously.
* Only create OpenTelemetry traces or spans if OpenTelemetry is enabled (via feature flag) in that component.

Implementation Plan:

* [x] Introduce a new API for tracing which bridges _both_ OpenTelemetry and k8s.io/utils/trace tracing
    * The API should not require plumbing an OpenTelemetry tracer provider
    * It will require using opentelemetry attributes
    * It won't use OpenTelemetry unless the current context is a child of a context that already uses OTel
    * https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/113183
* [x] Update users of k8s.io/utils/trace in kubernetes/kubernetes to use the new trace API.
    * https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/113172
* [x] Update [filterlatency](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a2ad9f9e4aba6aae6657a3189bdced6dbc8ba4b5/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/filterlatency/filterlatency.go) to record opentelemetry spans for APIServer filters.
    * https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/113217
* [x] Extend unit and integration tests for APIServerTracing to check for additional spans and span events.
    * Refactor tests: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/113233
    * Add additional checks: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/113642

### Why is this needed?

This is a beta graduation requirement of the APIServerTracing enhancement: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-instrumentation/647-apiserver-tracing#graduation-requirements

Kep: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/647

/sig instrumentation
/priority important-soon

After https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/112043 merged, build logs for e2e tests have started showing stack traces that look like:
```

	test/e2e/framework/node/helper.go:125 +0x58
# ...
k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/framework/node.AllNodesReady({0x0?, 0x0?}, 0x0?)
	test/e2e/framework/node/helper.go:108 +0x25
k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/framework/node/init.init.0.func1.1()
	test/e2e/framework/node/init/init.go:33 +0x2f
```

It seems like the `ClientSet` used in this `AfterEach` is nil
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d0e735a664e723628773b23e5f22f8b90b91ec14/test/e2e/framework/node/init/init.go#L32-L34

I have a suspicion this is happening for storage tests that skip

### What did you expect to happen?

No new stack traces in build logs

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run e2e tests against the in-development version of kubernetes

I identified when this started happening by looking for an increase in build-log size

body:
### What would you like to be added?

Add [metrics](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/v1.25.2/pkg/kubelet/metrics) to enable observability of the cpumanager.

### Why is this needed?

This is required to [GA the feature](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3350) but it's also useful in general.

To the best of my knowledge, it's very hard to observe the behavior of cpumanager without peeking into the pod and/or use the podresources interface (kubelet >= 1.24). But even for the latter, no well known components expose metrics consuming this information.

I believe anyway kubelet some expose some basic metrics about cpumanager behaviour, while deferring more fine grained metrics to external components (NFD, node_exporter, is fine)

title: `creationTimestamp: null` still causes unnecessary etcd-write with SSA

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: wg/api-expression
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to WG API Expression.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

Sending a patch built from a typed client to SSA will force a write to etcd (and bump resourceVersion) since creationTimestamp is serialized to null. This is a follow-up of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/106388 which doesn't solve the issue properly.

### What did you expect to happen?

Sending a no-op SSA request with creationTimestamp to null shouldn't do anything

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Kubectl apply an object with creationTimestamp null twice and see that it updates the object.
Probably something like this would cause it:
```
for i in "$(seq 1 10); do kubectl apply --server-side=true -f - -o yaml <<EOF
kind: ConfigMap
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
    name: some-configmap
    creationTimestamp: null # This is unfortunately done automatically when using typed client
data:
EOF
done
```

title: Memory leak in kubelet volume_manager populator processedPods

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

If a pod is created and then deleted an entry in processedPods map remains forever (sometimes, it's racy).

The problem comes from the fact that `podWorker` calls volume_manager `WaitForUnmount()` asynchronously. If the last call happens after populator cleaned up resources, an entry is added to processedPods and will never be seen.

### What did you expect to happen?

An entry in processedPods map must be deleted if pod doesn't exist and pod runtime should removed according to `dswp.podStateProvider`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

To verify that the issue really exists I applaied a simple [patch](https://github.com/jsafrane/kubernetes/commit/40ffc8e62836244ea6cffde8b9dff2c402d058c5) printing resources in `processedPods` map. Here is a reproducer:

1. Start brand-new fresh k8s cluster with `hack/local-up-cluster.sh`
2. Check entries in `processedPods`:
```
I0321 15:03:42.131049    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:264] JSAF: processed pod ac109c78-ce77-4426-9421-53fbcfe2175b: true
I0321 15:03:43.131815    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:262] JSAF: processed pods size: 1
```
3. Create a pod, check its uid:
```
$ k get po fdroot -o yaml |grep uid
  uid: a0158a6e-3b23-4a68-a50b-5d44e0fc009a
```
4. Verify that this uid is accurately reported:
```
I0321 15:05:06.193326    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:262] JSAF: processed pods size: 2
I0321 15:05:06.193412    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:264] JSAF: processed pod ac109c78-ce77-4426-9421-53fbcfe2175b: true
I0321 15:05:06.193434    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:264] JSAF: processed pod a0158a6e-3b23-4a68-a50b-5d44e0fc009a: true
```
5. Delete the pod, wait for a few mins, check for `processedPods` again:
```
I0321 15:48:29.113233    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:262] JSAF: processed pods size: 3
I0321 15:48:29.113252    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:264] JSAF: processed pod ac109c78-ce77-4426-9421-53fbcfe2175b: true
I0321 15:48:29.113259    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:264] JSAF: processed pod a0158a6e-3b23-4a68-a50b-5d44e0fc009a: false
I0321 15:48:29.113262    2149 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:264] JSAF: processed pod 213bcdcb-c9e7-4d96-af41-353d651cbd86: true
```

The entry `a0158a6e-3b23-4a68-a50b-5d44e0fc009a: false` will be kept forever because kubelet doesn't know anything about this pod anymore:
```
$ k get pods --all-namespaces -o yaml |grep "a0158a6e-3b23-4a68-a50b-5d44e0fc009a"
$
```
so no more events will ever come to populater for this uid, and the loop in `findAndRemoveDeletedPods()` won't find it because it was already deleted from `dswp.desiredStateOfWorld`.

### Anything else we need to know?

n/a

title: dual-stack proxies share healthz and metrics, corrupting the results

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/network
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Network.

labels.name: help wanted
labels.description: Denotes an issue that needs help from a contributor. Must meet "help wanted" guidelines.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
In a dual-stack proxy there is only a single healthz server, and likewise none of the proxy metrics are differentiated by IP family. Thus, the IPv4 and IPv6 sub-proxies are both updating the same data.

For the healthz server, this means that the "becoming unhealthy" timer starts counting whenever *either* proxy queues an update, and gets reset whenever *either* proxy successfully syncs. (So, eg, if every IPv6 sync fails, it could still be reporting healthy as long as IPv4 syncs are succeeding frequently enough.)

For metrics:
- Some are just broken:
  - The `SyncProxyRulesLastQueuedTimestamp` and `SyncProxyRulesLastTimestamp` metrics are broken in the same way as the health check; at any given time it's possible that one of them was set by the IPv4 proxy and the other was set by the IPv6 proxy.
  - The `IptablesRulesTotal` and `SyncProxyRulesNoLocalEndpointsTotal` metrics report the most-recently-observed value for either IPv4 or IPv6, whichever synced last.
  -  The `ServiceChangesPending` and `EndpointChangesPending` metrics report the most-recently-observed value for either IPv4 or IPv6, whichever synced or processed an event last.
- Some may or may not be useful depending on cluster configuration:
  - `SyncProxyRulesLatency` will be based on the duration of both IPv4 `syncProxyRules` calls and IPv6 `syncProxyRules` calls, which will skew the results if you have either way more IPv4 Services than IPv6 ones or vice versa.
  - Likewise, `NetworkProgrammingLatency` will include both IPv4 programming latency and IPv6 programming latency, which could potentially be very different.
- Some other metrics are fine:
  - `IptablesRestoreFailuresTotal` and `IptablesPartialRestoreFailuresTotal` correctly report the total number of IPv4 and IPv6 failures combined.
  - `ServiceChangesTotal` and `EndpointChangesTotal` correctly report the total number of IPv4 and IPv6 changes combined.

/sig network
/area kube-proxy
cc @khenidak

title: Refactor prober_manager to update the runtime state vs. API state

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: lifecycle/rotten
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
- This is part of pre-work for sidecar KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/753
- See also uber issue: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/115934

In sidecar container KEP we plan to use the Startup probes state as a way to decide whether the next Init container need to start being initialized. Before this KEP probes results were not used in any of Pod lifecycle decisions. In order to implement this we need to have a probe status at a time we call `findNextInitContainerToRun`. This may need some refactoring on how prober_manager is initialized and used.

Today we calculate changes needed to be performed on Pod including the next init container to run. Then we apply these actions and update the Status of a Pod on API server using `convertStatusToAPIStatus` from `generateAPIPodStatus`. Once we converted the runtime status to API status, we also call `kl.probeManager.UpdatePodStatus(pod.UID, s)` passing the API status object to be updated with the probes results. Thus the probe results are not visible to the `findNextInitContainerToRun` function.

The proposal is to refactor the `prober_manager.go` to operate on `kubecontainer.PodStatus` instead of `v1.PodStatus`. This will require adding the probes status to the `kubecontainer.PodStatus`. We will also move the call into the `prober_manager.go` early in the `syncPod` execution so we know the startup probes result before we call into `findNextInitContainerToRun`.

cc @smarterclayton 

/sig node
/kind feature
/priority important-soon

body:
### What happened?

The same ResourceRequirements struct is used in two only loosely related entities (Container and PersistentVolumeClaim). Extending ResourceRequirements for dynamic resource requirement had the unintended effect that the new `Claims` field also became available in a PersistentVolumeClaim.



### What did you expect to happen?

Extending one should not affect the other.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/111023#pullrequestreview-1302112278:

> We just ran across this while reviewing https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/107776
>
> The ResourceRequirements type is also used within the PersistentVolumeSpec type (which is also used indirectly in pod specs via ephemeral volumes), and the "clear if feature-gate is disabled" logic is only wired to podspec-handling. That means in 1.26 PVC objects or PodSpecs with ephemeral volumes defined can persist data in this field even if the feature is disabled.
>
> Can you open a PR to clear this field in PVC and ephemeral volume create/update flows, and file a follow-up issue to consider splitting the type used in PVCs so it doesn't continue inheriting work done that is targeted at pods?

body:
### What happened?

If you create a pod that mounts a volume from a secret or a config-map and then you delete that pod, it takes an abnormally long time to delete the pod.  



### What did you expect to happen?

I would expect a similar time for deletion from a successful case as an unsuccesful case.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

If you have the following yaml:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: config-map-mount
spec:
  containers:
    - name: test-container
      image: registry.k8s.io/busybox
      command: [ "sleep", "100" ]
      volumeMounts:
      - mountPath: /clusters-config
        name: clusters-config-volume
  volumes:
    - configMap:
        name: clusters-config-file
      name: clusters-config-volume
```
And you create it with no config-map and delete the pod it takes around 60-75 seconds to delete the pod.  

If you create that config-map/secret it only takes a few seconds to delete the pod.  

Secret example:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secret-example-pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: secret-test-container
      image: busybox
      command: [ "/bin/sh", "-c", "cat /etc/secret-volume/*" ]
      volumeMounts: 
          - name: secret-volume
            mountPath: /etc/secret-volume 
            readOnly: true 
  volumes:
    - name: secret-volume
      secret:
        secretName: test-secret 
  restartPolicy: Never
```

title: CSI migration race condition can cause unexpected detach and data loss

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

body:
### What happened?

After the cluster was updated to enable PD CSI Driver, there was a race condition where AD Controller (kube-controller-manager) started to [populate the desired state of world](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dc2898b20c6bd9602ae1c3b51333e2e4640ed249/pkg/controller/volume/attachdetach/attach_detach_controller.go#L438-L447) BEFORE the PD CSI Driver was up, thus AD Controller gave us the error 

```
Error creating spec for volume "elasticsearch", pod "XXX"/"elasticsearch-0": error performing CSI migration checks and translation for PVC "dXX"/"elasticsearch-elasticsearch-0": in-tree plugin kubernetes.io/gce-pd is migrated on node gke-stage-XXXXX but driver pd.csi.storage.gke.io is not installed.
```

Then AD Controller triggered the disk detach because the disk/volume was not populated in the desired state of world.

Unfortunately the disk was in use during this detach and got corrupted.

### What did you expect to happen?

Since cluster upgrades can cause the controller manager and CSI drivers to start at different times, the AD controller needs to be more conservative when detaching

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

We have not been able to reproduce this, it came up from a customer.

body:
### What happened?

In case of online volume expansion of raw block volumes, some of the CSI plugins may not need file system resize or any related handling and thus NodeExpandVolume API call can be skipped for the same. In order to do this, plugin must set NodeExpansionRequired to false, in ControllerExpandVolumeResponse.
However, it is observed that kubelet does call NodeExpandVolume API, after successful resize done by CSI plugin in ControllerExpandVolume API call with NodeExpansionRequired=false in response.
Even though CSI plugin can skip handling in NodeExpandVolume API as per its requirement, is it expected to get this API call from kubelet when NodeExpansionRequired set to false by plugin in ControllerExpandVolumeResponse?

### What did you expect to happen?

During CSI volume online expansion, if CSI plugin returns NodeExpansionRequired=false in ControllerExpandVolumeResponse, to indicate no FS resize handling needed, then kubelet should not call NodeExpandVolume API for such volume(s).

body:
### What happened?

While discussing the ReferenceGrant kep, I learned that there is a distinction between "resource" and "kind". The biggest takeaway is that "group + kind" is not uniquely identifiable for arbitrary resources (for in-tree apis we can enforce).

refs:
https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#kind-vs-resource
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3767/files#r1084662831


### What did you expect to happen?

The implications are that we should be using `resource` instead of `kind` in `PVC.dataSourceRef` and `VolumePopulator.sourceKind`.

We need to resolve this before volume populators goes GA.

title: VolumeZone scheduling plugin should handle csi migration

body:
### What happened?

In https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114268, we discovered that our plan for eventually removing the [VolumeZone](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumezone) scheduling plugin when CSI migration is GA is not possible because the plugin also applies to non-migratable volume types.

However, if we leave the plugin as is, then even migratable PVs will be broken if we remove beta topology labels from Nodes in the future. This is because the plugin does not have any handling for migrated volumes.


### What did you expect to happen?

I suggest we add CSI migration handling to the VolumeZone plugin. I think we just need to detect if the volume is migrated, and if so, skip the VolumeZone processing. For migrated volumes, we translate `PV.Labels` into `PV.NodeAffinity` so they end up getting processed by the [VolumeBinding](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumebinding) plugin.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

In a cluster with csi migration for a specific intree volume type enabled,
1. create an intree PV with beta topology labels
2. remove the beta topology label from a node
3. try to schedule a pod using that pv

body:
### Failure cluster [6140da152b810b30d99b](https://go.k8s.io/triage#6140da152b810b30d99b)

##### Error text:
```
[FAILED] timed out waiting for the condition
In [It] at: test/e2e/node/pods.go:276 @ 01/02/23 10:40:40.11

```
#### Recent failures:
[1/9/2023, 3:08:19 PM pr:pull-kubernetes-e2e-kind](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/114879/pull-kubernetes-e2e-kind/1612541338065047552)
[1/9/2023, 12:37:26 PM pr:pull-kubernetes-e2e-kind-ipv6](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/batch/pull-kubernetes-e2e-kind-ipv6/1612502921440661504)
[1/9/2023, 9:57:40 AM pr:pull-kubernetes-e2e-kind-ipv6](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/114846/pull-kubernetes-e2e-kind-ipv6/1612463069030518784)
[1/6/2023, 6:35:47 PM pr:pull-kubernetes-e2e-kind-ipv6](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/113744/pull-kubernetes-e2e-kind-ipv6/1611506307183939584)
[1/6/2023, 4:48:42 PM pr:pull-kubernetes-e2e-kind-ipv6](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/114883/pull-kubernetes-e2e-kind-ipv6/1611479334852235264)


/kind failing-test
/kind flake
<!-- If this is a flake, please add: /kind flake -->

/sig node

#### Additional Information

It looks like the [test](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2f6c4f5eab85d3f15cd80d21f4a0c353a8ceb10b/test/e2e/node/pods.go#L232) does the following:
1. [Creates a pod that has a container that immediately exits (command is `/bin/true`)](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2f6c4f5eab85d3f15cd80d21f4a0c353a8ceb10b/test/e2e/node/pods.go#L237-L265)
2. [Confirms that the pod has completed successfully](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2f6c4f5eab85d3f15cd80d21f4a0c353a8ceb10b/test/e2e/node/pods.go#L271)
3. [Attempts to read the events for the pod](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2f6c4f5eab85d3f15cd80d21f4a0c353a8ceb10b/test/e2e/node/pods.go#L276-L292)

When this test flakes/fails, it seems like steps 1 and 2 are successful, but it times out on step 3 because apparently the pod no longer exists.

This makes me wonder if, under certain load conditions, the pod GC is cleaning up the terminated pod before step 3 (or even step 2) can do its thing.

It [looks like the default value for `--terminated-pod-gc-threshold` is 12500](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e01ff1641c7321ac81fe5775f6ccb21aa6775c04/pkg/controller/podgc/config/v1alpha1/defaults.go#L34),

That seems high enough that it would be unlikely that the threshold would be reached (could there really be 12500 completed pods?), but I wonder if something in the e2e tests is lowering it.  I noticed [this line which sets `TERMINATED_POD_GC_THRESHOLD` to 100](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/545835e28826d888b3d236f71fbbd88107d3b635/cluster/gce/config-test.sh#L163), but that is gce-specific.  Is it possible something similar is being set to lower the threshold for the e2e-kind tests?  I did a search but didn't see anywhere that it was being set.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
As discussed [in the KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/3063-dynamic-resource-allocation#user-permissions-and-quotas), most likely useful quotas need to be implemented by resource drivers because only they know how much resources get consumed by a specific claim.

What can be limited in Kubernetes itself is the number of ResourceClaims per namespace. For this, two new ResourceQuota resource names get added:

* ` resourceclaims` limits the number of ResourceClaim objects in a namespace across all resource class.
* `<resource-class-name>.resourceclass.node.k8s.io/resourceclaims` limits the number of ResourceClaim objects for the specific resource class.

body:
### What happened?

When kube-scheduler does preemption and the PodDisruptionConditions feature gate is enabled, it might leak the namespace and name of a pod in a different namespace.

### What did you expect to happen?

While debuggability is important, this is too much information to give to an end user. This information could be just in logs, which are only accessible to administrators.

We could print the name of the pod only it's in the same namespace, but I don't think it's worth the complexity.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Have PodDisruptionConditions enabled and generate a case of preemption. The PodDisruption condition message in the preempted pod will have the name of the Pod.

body:
### What happened?

I have a daemonset with the rolling update strategy. I have `maxSurge` parameter set to a non zero value [which means](https://github.com/openshift/kubernetes/blob/cb4b47e5ddfbaf7844237b2e2eb2b0acfed5f1b5/pkg/apis/apps/validation/validation.go#L394-L402) that the `maxUnavailable` parameter is set to `0`. When I replace the toleration in the daemonset's template spec from the one which helped me to be scheduled on the master node into any other toleration, I see the new pods still trying to be scheduled on the master nodes. The old pods from the tolerated nodes can be lucky enough to be recreated but only if they go before any pod from the intolerable node.

```
$ kubectl -n openshift-dns get ds dns-default -o yaml | yq .spec.updateStrategy
rollingUpdate:
```

I don't expect the new pods to be scheduled on the nodes which are not tolerated by the new DamonSet's template spec. body:
The problem that we need to solve for cluster autoscaling when the cluster uses dynamic resource allocation is to simulate how adding new nodes will affect pod scheduling. This matters when some DRA driver depends on resources on such new nodes.

One possible solution is outlined in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/3063-dynamic-resource-allocation#cluster-autoscaler

Another idea was to enable loading and calling WASM plugins. This would allow vendors to publish portable plugins and avoid inter-process communication. https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kube-scheduler-wasm-extension is exploring that as alternative for normal scheduler plugins. However, WASM has several challenges, primarily that all data exchanged between host and plugin guest needs to be encoded and decoded, which makes one of the goals (similar performance and overhead as built-in plugins) impossible.

body:
When compared to client-side apply that doesn't send empty `{}` patches, server-side apply always sends the manifest.
When no-op apply is sent, it triggers the full mutation/admission which can cause a lot of stress on webhooks.

It might be useful to not call the validating webhooks if the resource hasn't changed.

title: Server-Side Apply should return a proper http status when validation fails

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to WG API Expression.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
Server-Side Apply has different constraints for updating the managed fields and applying than typical objects, and sometimes the discrepency can cause problem.

When trying to update the `managedFields`, if the object doesn't validate, then the whole `managedFields` list is removed, the error is ignored as to continue with the normal process. But then such an object can't ever be applied, since it can't be converted into the type of objects that server-side apply uses.

Right now, when this happens, the server-side apply request fails with a generic 500. We're trying decide what code should be returned in that case (solving the problem of applying such an object is a separate issue), so that the client can possibly try a different way. Here's the problem though: there is fundamentally nothing wrong with the client request, so 4xx doesn't really fit, and yet, the client should take an action since there isn't much we can do server-side, so a 5xx doesn't really fit either.

cc @thockin @alculquicondor @aojea @jpbetz

title: Pod graceful deletion hangs if the kubelet already rejected that pod at admission time

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
### What happened?

We observed the following series of events:

1) Pod is created with some attributes that later result in the pod being rejected at kubelet admission time
2) The pod is scheduled to a node
3) The pod is gracefully deleted by a controller, i.e. a deletion timestamp is set on the pod
4) The pod is rejected at kubelet admission time
5) The pod never gets deleted and is stuck: despite having the deletion timestamp set. It seems that kubelet does not issue the final force delete for the pod.

This is problematic in many scenarios, but one specific case it was hit was when the pod is backed by a daemonset controller. This issue manifested in way where since the pod never got deleted in step 5 above, the daemonset controller did not create a new pod to run the on the node and thus node was was not running a replica of the daemonset controller pod.

This seems to a be regression in k8s 1.27, I was not able to repro this behavior in 1.26.

### What did you expect to happen?

It is expected at during the series of events above, after the pod is failed at kubelet admission time, since the pod has a deletion timestamp set, the kubelet should forcefully delete the pod. The pod should not hang in deletion forever. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a 1.27 kind cluster:

```
kind delete cluster


kind_config="$(cat << EOF
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
networking:
  ipFamily: ipv4
nodes:
# the control plane node
- role: control-plane
- role: worker
  kubeadmConfigPatches:
  - |
    kind: JoinConfiguration
    nodeRegistration:
      kubeletExtraArgs:
        v: "4"
        read-only-port: "10255"
EOF
)"

kind create cluster --config <(printf '%s\n' "${kind_config}") --image  kindest/node:v1.27.1@sha256:b7d12ed662b873bd8510879c1846e87c7e676a79fefc93e17b2a52989d3ff42b
```

Stop kubelet
```
$ docker exec -it kind-worker /bin/bash
root@kind-worker:/# systemctl stop kubelet
```

Create a pod bound to the node which will trigger a admission error. The below node selector label does not exist, so we expect that the pod should be rejected in admission.

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: ubuntu-sleep-2
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    this-label: does-not-exist
  nodeName: "kind-worker"
  containers:
  - name: ubuntu
    image:  gcr.io/google-containers/ubuntu:14.04
    command: ["/bin/sleep"]
    args: ["infinity"]
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: "1"
        memory: "10Mi"
      limits:
        cpu: "1"
        memory: "10Mi"
```

While kubelet is down issue a graceful deletion to set a deletion timestamp on the pod

```
kubectl delete pod ubuntu-sleep-2
```

body:
Apparently, the bug happens in 1.26.3 but not in 1.27.1 so maybe it's been fixed somewhere.

Here are the steps to reproduce:
```
cat > testhpa.yaml <<EOF
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: test-hpa
  namespace: default
spec:
  maxReplicas: 5
  metrics:
  - external:
      metric:
        name: foo
      target:
        averageValue: "10"
        type: AverageValue
    type: External
  minReplicas: 1
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: test-depl
EOF

kubectl apply --server-side=true -f testhpa.yaml
kubectl apply --dry-run=server --server-side=true -o yaml -f testhpa.yaml
```

Note that the metrics list is atomic, so the list should be entirely replaced every-time, not merged/appended.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.2/staging/src/k8s.io/api/autoscaling/v2/types.go#L67-L77
