body:
### What happened?

Apply this patch:

```
diff --git a/pkg/volume/git_repo/git_repo_test.go b/pkg/volume/git_repo/git_repo_test.go
index 3ef1cab0ad9..5e4806f152b 100644
--- a/pkg/volume/git_repo/git_repo_test.go
+++ b/pkg/volume/git_repo/git_repo_test.go
@@ -390,6 +390,7 @@ func doTestSetUp(scenario struct {
 	var fakeOutputs []fakeexec.FakeAction
 	var fcmd fakeexec.FakeCmd
 	for _, expected := range expecteds {
+		expected := expected
 		if expected.cmd[1] == "clone" {
 			fakeOutputs = append(fakeOutputs, func() ([]byte, []byte, error) {
 				// git clone, it creates new dir/files
```

Then run:

    make test WHAT=./pkg/volume/git_repo

The test fails:

```
+++ [0521 00:30:39] Setting GOMAXPROCS: 48
+++ [0521 00:30:39] Running tests without code coverage and with -race
--- FAIL: TestPlugin (0.01s)
    git_repo_test.go:277: Unexpected failure for scenario: target-dir - [unexpected command calls in scenario: expected 3, saw: 1 unexpected commands: [[git clone -- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes.git target_dir]], expected: [[git clone -- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes.git target_dir] [git checkout 2a30ce65c5ab586b98916d83385c5983edd353a1] [git reset --hard]] unexpected directories: [/tmp/git_repo_test.109792826/pods/poduid/volumes/kubernetes.io~git-repo/vol1], expected: [/tmp/git_repo_test.109792826/pods/poduid/volumes/kubernetes.io~git-repo/vol1 /tmp/git_repo_test.109792826/pods/poduid/volumes/kubernetes.io~git-repo/vol1/target_dir /tmp/git_repo_test.109792826/pods/poduid/volumes/kubernetes.io~git-repo/vol1/target_dir]]
    git_repo_test.go:277: Unexpected failure for scenario: no-target-dir - [unexpected command calls in scenario: expected 3, saw: 1 unexpected commands: [[git clone -- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes.git]], expected: [[git clone -- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes.git] [git checkout 2a30ce65c5ab586b98916d83385c5983edd353a1] [git reset --hard]] unexpected directories: [/tmp/git_repo_test.1084130303/pods/poduid/volumes/kubernetes.io~git-repo/vol1], expected: [/tmp/git_repo_test.1084130303/pods/poduid/volumes/kubernetes.io~git-repo/vol1 /tmp/git_repo_test.1084130303/pods/poduid/volumes/kubernetes.io~git-repo/vol1/kubernetes /tmp/git_repo_test.1084130303/pods/poduid/volumes/kubernetes.io~git-repo/vol1/kubernetes]]
FAIL
FAIL	k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/volume/git_repo	0.172s
FAIL
make: *** [Makefile:184: test] Error 1
```


### What did you expect to happen?

Test should pass.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

See above.


### Anything else we need to know?

The full loop is:

```
	for _, expected := range expecteds {
		if expected.cmd[1] == "clone" {
			fakeOutputs = append(fakeOutputs, func() ([]byte, []byte, error) {
				// git clone, it creates new dir/files
				os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(fcmd.Dirs[0], expected.dir), 0750)
				return []byte{}, nil, nil
			})
		} else {
			// git checkout || git reset, they create nothing
			fakeOutputs = append(fakeOutputs, func() ([]byte, []byte, error) {
				return []byte{}, nil, nil
			})
		}
	}
```

The first problem is that fakeOutputs is capturing expected.dir, so all the funcs on that list use the expected.dir from the final iteration, not the one from the iteration with the expected.cmd[1] == "clone". But then this problem appears to be covering up a different problem in the test scenarios themselves. I looked at it for a little bit but I haven't puzzled out what the test is trying to do exactly. Hopefully someone with more knowledge of the test can take a look. 

It seems like a buggy test, accidentally passing due to this other loopvar sharing bug.

body:
### What would you like to be added?

# Short description

OpenAPI v2 is very expensive, specifically when installing a lot of CRDs. I'm opening this issue to track what's going on and the work that we've been doing, are doing, or planning to do to improve the situation.

Right now, there's mostly three dimensions that are interesting:
1. OpenAPI v2 is not lazy, and aggregates the information from CRDs on a very regular basis
2. OpenAPI is subtly called by various processes in kubectl which probably shouldn't exist. Once the OpenAPI v2 is lazy, then we should definitely make sure we have as few calls as possible to it.
3. Some processes are very slow in the OpenAPI v2. These have mostly been fixed.

# Existing issues and pull-requests

## OpenAPI v2 is not lazy
```[tasklist]
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-openapi/pull/371
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116445
- [ ] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118212
- [ ] Issue missing for CRD controller not being lazy
```

## OpenAPI v2 is being used
```[tasklist]
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115324
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114439
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115119
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114294
- [ ] We need to create a few issues for the things that are still pulling the OpenAPI in kubectl.
```

## OpenAPI v2 processing is slow

That is mostly done, 
```[tasklist]
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-openapi/issues/324
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-openapi/issues/315
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-openapi/pull/368
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-openapi/pull/361
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-openapi/pull/339
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-openapi/pull/325
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-openapi/pull/319
- [ ] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118204
- [ ] We need to create an issue for openapi v3 serialization
```

## Misc
```[tasklist]
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114191
```

cc @sttts @Jefftree 

### Why is this needed?

We need to be able to create more CRDs on Kubernetes clusters than we can today. Schema is the main limitation of most of the memory allocated, in-use memory and almost certainly of processing time (though that's usually harder to measure since you need to measure WHILE the cpu is being used).

body:
We are using `client-go` (and `kubectl`) to interact with Kubernetes clusters behind a couple of proxy layers. One of these proxies completes the `Content-Type` headers to include character encoding details.

This was working fine until recently, when client-go/kubectl have started to fail when interacting with the discovery API. It seems that a recent change has made kubectl more restrictive of the content-type that it expects. I suspect that it is related to this commit: https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/commit/25d5761bfa0603c77cf5efefb14fd2e63a03a773

For example, this is an error from a kubectl command:
```
...
E0422 16:28:02.626222   86629 memcache.go:265] couldn't get current server API group list: Unknown discovery response content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
I0422 16:28:02.626258   86629 cached_discovery.go:120] skipped caching discovery info due to Unknown discovery response content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
I0422 16:28:02.626346   86629 shortcut.go:100] Error loading discovery information: Unknown discovery response content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
...
```

We can of course try to fix it on our end, removing that charset information. However, it is a valid content-type and the way kubectl is handling the content-type there seems like it is relying on implementation details of kube-apiserver (that it does not add metadata to the content-type). I propose to fix this issue in `kubectl`, by properly parsing and handling the content-type.

```
I0419 06:40:41.571553      21 request.go:1188] Response Body: {"paths":{".well-known/openid-configuration":{"serverRelativeURL":"/openapi/v3/.well-known/openid-configuration?hash=BF1C8CB94CEB72F9853EDF554520390667FFB0AA92BDAD649C8B70C28C0F7594D8E877E9A0682773E8301D0289D288DF118C90A0155A647A7A27AF26C02CBEC2"},"api":{"serverRelativeURL":"/openapi/v3/api?hash=2DCF3BF7BF6FAAB0A535BC865BE6C3613FAB37EB2A5650DAD1FA4DCCF5658086E5D15896598112DAB5591BF089A327C60E7A98F88D37AEB5F99DAB7E1B2704EC"},"api/v1":{"serverRelativeURL":"/openapi/v3/api/v1?hash=17C7EEA4DFF6156193C13E441C8A8BA5D552BCA97017070ADC5688AF4B3FFCA305B4708D83CF883B522E33958A3812631C33E90C5556DDF482DB7CC4D5286C6F"},"apis":{"serverRelativeURL":"/openapi/v3/apis?hash=3D55D9A351386B8FD26B41F214DD2D0C34328BA69DB2E4E0FC54EE6FC5693DF7B5094439ABE2A3ADA31CCCBB22A9FC9372769CB2ACCD3A165CC30A6D281251D6"},"apis/admissionregistration.k8s.io":{"serverRelativeURL":"/openapi/v3/apis/admissionregistration.k8s.io?hash=D3B2D7397ED883146045CE57DD02E66B442A7ED8FF25480FAFB1238044B0F1241140493C55AADB6C87AC8BB317DB28B15CBA569930FB85747AC2EF6 [truncated 13515 chars]
```

Command should work normally.

Maybe write a unit test that starts apiserver with a URL path and test how discovery works?

### What happened?

Because of #117356, the webhook converter may receive an object to convert that has no metadata. In that scenario, it returns an error, because it expects the input object to have metadata.

### What did you expect to happen?

No error

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

https://github.com/LittleWat/conversion-webhook-test-with-flux

### Anything else we need to know?

Ideally the converter should always receive an object with metadata. Until then, it should match its output expectations to the input object; i.e., if the input does not have metadata, it should not require that the output does have it.

From 1.28 user could run **Sidecar containers** in `initContainers`, those sidecar containers remain running during the entire life of the Pod, it should be calculated in [pod autoscaler](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4f874a224a31a5dc5745a0c140d3769bb178f811/pkg/controller/podautoscaler/replica_calculator.go#L424).

If missing the sidecar resources, we will get a wrong pod resource utilization.

We should also correct the related Cadvisor metrics.

The timeout filter aborted the request and sent a `504` to the caller:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/953be8927218ec8067e1af2641e540238ffd7576/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/filters/timeout.go#L146

The goroutine that the timeout handler spawned to execute the request (rest of the handler chain) was in flight for more than `60s`, and it is recording a `429` response code, implying that apf rejected the request.
```
{
  "kind": "Event",
  "apiVersion": "audit.k8s.io/v1",
  "level": "Request",
  "auditID": "caa77d18-9f66-4d8e-a29d-146a2efbb22c",
  "stage": "ResponseComplete",
  "requestURI": "/api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/pods?pretty=true&allowWatchBookmarks=false&labelSelector=<selector>&resourceVersion=862900435&watch=false",
  "verb": "list",
  "user": {
    "username": "system:serviceaccount:<sa>",
    "uid": "5ab073d0-5c0e-4985-bca3-20038108d401",
    "groups": [
      "system:serviceaccounts",
      "system:serviceaccounts:<sa>",
      "system:authenticated"
    ],
    "extra": {
      "authentication.kubernetes.io/pod-name": [
        "<pod-name>"
      ],
      "authentication.kubernetes.io/pod-uid": [
        "11916349-428e-4d9f-9167-899fcacbf6d5"
      ]
    }
  },
  "sourceIPs": [
    "10.100.150.226"
  ],
  "userAgent": "Kubernetes Java Client/16.0.0-SNAPSHOT",
  "objectRef": {
    "resource": "pods",
    "namespace": "<ns>",
    "apiVersion": "v1"
  },
  "responseStatus": {
    "metadata": {},
    "code": 429
  },
  "requestReceivedTimestamp": "2023-07-26T22:17:10.740109Z",
  "stageTimestamp": "2023-07-26T22:18:10.904195Z"
}
```

This means that the request was waiting in the queue for `60s` before it was removed from the queue and rejected. We are already aware of the fact that the removal check happens upon arrival of a new request for the priority level. But we only check the queue that has been selected for the newly arrived request, there could be other queues in the queueset that could have old requests that are candidate for rejection.

When a new request arrives, we assign it to a queue first and then remove old requests from the selected queue. This means, the logic for selecting a queue for the new request takes into account the work in seat-seconds of these "should be rejected now" requests waiting in the set of queues being considered. 

So a queue with more work in seat-seconds is less likely to be selected and this phenomenon may contribute to a request waiting for more than `15s`
Also there is the extreme case of new request not arriving for the given priority level.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1620473a9a01dd6bbef3398c0acb2e581d0a13c3/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/flowcontrol/fairqueuing/queueset/queueset.go#L568-L576

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1620473a9a01dd6bbef3398c0acb2e581d0a13c3/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/flowcontrol/fairqueuing/queueset/queueset.go#L619-L620


Other observations:
- Maximum observed time from audit logs was 61.9922s out of the thousands of examples
- The given priority level (`workload-low`) was maxed out, requests that failed to be dispatched were rejected with reasons cancelled or time-out 

How we can avoid this issue:
A: when a new request arrives:
- we scan all the queues of the queueset and reject the requests that have been waiting for more than `15s` 
- we select a queue for the new request
(we depend on new request arrival for the queueset, as we do today, and iterating trough the requests waiting in the queues for the queueset is costly to the O(n), n is the number of requests waiting)

B: we can use the context of the request, if it has a deadline (true for all non long-running requests - it's the `timeout` specified in the request URI, otherwise `60s`
- we derive a new context from the request context, and pass the new context to the promise that will be used by req.wait(). the new context has a deadline of 1/4 of the request timeout (`15s` at most)
This approach does not depend on arrival of new request - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105849 is a work in progress for this approach.


### What did you expect to happen?

Ideally, queue wait time of a request should not exceed its deadline or does not depend on arrival of any future request.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Hard to reproduce manually, but audit entry and httplog from production shows it's happening


### Kubernetes version

v1.23.17

body:
When PreFilter returns UnschedulableAndUnresolvable, we don't need to run the preemption, but currently we run.
This unexpected preemption could cause errors from the preemption by trying to read non-exist PreFilter data.

As @Huang-Wei pointed out ([ref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119770#issuecomment-1666418637)), actually we didn't run the preemption in such cases in the past versions, but https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/110894 introduced this bug.

/kind bug 
/kind regression
/sig scheduling
/triage accepted
/priority important-soon

body:
Move @sanposhiho 's https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119769#pullrequestreview-1563700339 here as a new discussion thread:

Kensei pointed out a potential bug in the scheduling path when we hit Unschedulable result in one of PreFilter plugins:

> - pluginA returns Unschedulable in its PreFilter.
> - (Because pluginA returns unschedulable, RunPreFilterPlugins() is aborted at that point and pluginB PreFIlter isn't executed)
> - a Pod is claimed as unschedulable (failed by pluginA)
> - calling a pluginB's AddPod/RemovePod during preemption, sometimes will abort the whole preemption as the logic tries to read info from cycleState.

/sig scheduling
/kind bug

title: Namespace stuck in Terminating when deleted if ApiService doesn't implement Aggregated Discovery

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

We implement a manual `APIService` API Extension in [Agones](https://github.com/googleforgames/agones).

Definition:
https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/blob/main/install/helm/agones/templates/service/allocation.yaml

Code for handling web requests:
https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/blob/main/pkg/util/apiserver/apiserver.go

The code is extremely lightweight as we only have no need for storage, and only accept CREATE requests at this time.

This issue was first reported by one of our users in May, but we only were able to reproduce it ourselves once we were on 1.27.x: https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/issues/3172

Testing on Kubernetes 1.27.x we noticed that when attempting to delete Namespaces, they would get stuck in termination with the following description:

```
❯ kubectl describe ns 1690585578
Name:         1690585578
Labels:       kubernetes.io/metadata.name=1690585578
              owner=e2e-test
Annotations:  <none>
Status:       Terminating
Conditions:
  Type                                         Status  LastTransitionTime               Reason                  Message
  ----                                         ------  ------------------               ------                  -------
  NamespaceDeletionDiscoveryFailure            True    Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:07:44 -0700  DiscoveryFailed         Discovery failed for some groups, 1 failing: unable to retrieve the complete list of server APIs: allocation.agones.dev/v1: stale GroupVersion discovery: allocation.agones.dev/v1
  NamespaceDeletionGroupVersionParsingFailure  False   Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:07:46 -0700  ParsedGroupVersions     All legacy kube types successfully parsed
  NamespaceDeletionContentFailure              False   Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:08:56 -0700  ContentDeleted          All content successfully deleted, may be waiting on finalization
  NamespaceContentRemaining                    False   Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:08:56 -0700  ContentRemoved          All content successfully removed
  NamespaceFinalizersRemaining                 False   Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:08:56 -0700  ContentHasNoFinalizers  All content-preserving finalizers finished
```

So far, I've not found a way to delete the Namespace.

Looking through the log for the webserver, i can see requests for `/apis` and the new Aggregated Discovery feature (`Accept:  "application/json;g=apidiscovery.k8s.io;v=v2beta1;as=APIGroupDiscoveryList"`), but we return a 404 to that response, since it's not implemented.

Looking through the code I can find (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.3/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/apiserver/handler_discovery.go) it seems that any response other than `http.StatusOK` would result in this issue -- which is breaking backward compatibility within `APIService` to assume that this API surface is implemented in some way.


### What did you expect to happen?

Namespaces would terminate as per normal.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Install Agones on a cluster (https://agones.dev/site/docs/installation/install-agones/)
2. `kubectl create ns foo`
3. `kubectl delete ns foo`
4. Watch as the ns gets stuck in Terminating.



### Anything else we need to know?

If I had a magic wand, I'd love a reference of all the API's that get called against an APIService and what their expected results should be.

So far it's a combo of using `kubectl proxy` and looking at the k8s API responses, crawling through code, and reading apiserver logs to try and reverse engineer this work.

title: Resource(CPU, memory, device, topology) managers don't consider restartable init containers

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

Resource(CPU, memory, topology) managers don't consider restartable init containers.

- [x] CPU manager: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119447
- [x] Memory manager: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120715
- [x] Device manager: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120461
- [ ] Topology manager:

---

When cpu-manager-policy is static and you create a guaranteed pod with a restartable init container,
a restartable init container shares its static CPUs with a regular container.


### What did you expect to happen?

A restartable init container should not share its CPU requirement with the regular containers.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```
$ cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f - 
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  initContainers:
  - name: init-1
    image: ubuntu
    command:
    - sh
    - -c
    - |
      grep Cpus_allowed_list /proc/self/status | cut -f2
    volumeMounts:
    - name: shared
      mountPath: /tmp/shared
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: 8
        memory: 100Mi
  - name: restartable-init-2
    image: ubuntu
    command:
    - sh
    - -c
    - |
      grep Cpus_allowed_list /proc/self/status | cut -f2
      sleep 300s
    volumeMounts:
    - name: shared
      mountPath: /tmp/shared
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: 4
        memory: 200Mi
    restartPolicy: Always
  containers:
  - name: regular-3
    image: ubuntu
    command:
    - sh
    - -c
    - |
      grep Cpus_allowed_list /proc/self/status | cut -f2
      sleep 300s
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: 4
        memory: 300Mi
    volumeMounts:
    - name: shared
      mountPath: /tmp/shared
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 1
  volumes:
  - name: shared
    emptyDir: {}
  restartPolicy: Never
EOF
pod/test created
...
$ kubectl logs test -c init-1
0-3,6-9
$ kubectl logs test -c restartable-init-2
0-1,6-7  # init container and restartalbe init container can share the CPUs, as "init-1" is already terminated and will not restart.
$ kubectl logs test -c regular-3         
0-1,6-7  # restartable init container and regular container should not share the CPUs, as they should run together.
```

body:
### What happened?

Kubernetes does not respect the `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` of a probe.

I found this while fixing the e2e tests.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119354

Test result:
```
a6890b361de8d5bc7e90005dc2c5c167d9d80093: Good
847f1758748ac357e79094c5e85029a10428e65f: Bad
```

/kind regression
/kind bug
/sig node

/priority important-soon

### What did you expect to happen?

The `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` of a container's probe should override the pod's `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a pod with long pod-level terminationGracePeriodSeconds and short probe-level terminationGracePeriodSeconds.

```sh
$ cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: regular-1
    image: registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/busybox:1.29-4
    startupProbe:
      exec:
        command:
        - /bin/false
      failureThreshold: 1
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 1
    command:
    - sh
    - -c
    - |
      sleep 300s
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 300
EOF
```

2. Check for the container not respecting the probe-level terminationGracePeriodSeconds
```
Every 2.0s: kubectl describe pods test | tail                                                                                                                                  gjkim-desktop: Tue Jul 18 00:19:23 2023
```

body:
### **What would you like to be added?**

gRPC built-in probes should be able to communicate with a server that is setup to use a secured connection.

### **Why is this needed?**

Setting up a gRPC server to use plaintext is not really acceptable in production, so built-in probes are kind of unusable.

### **How?**

The same way as http probe does it, with setting the field _InsecureSkipVerify_ to _true_, we could do:

```go
opts := []grpc.DialOption{}
tlsConfig := &tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true}
opts.append(opts, grpc.WithTransportCredentials(credentials.NewTLS(tlsConfig)))
```

Maybe there is a specific reason this has not been done already ?
I am willing to contribute if needed.

/sig node

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
/sig scheduling
/priority important-soon
/assign
/kind feature

Part of: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/122284#issuecomment-1853346333.

---

Plugins may miss Node-related events that make Pod schedulable because of preCheck.
It's similar to: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119177#issuecomment-1820091877

1. Node is added. But, it's filtered out by preCheck (due to node's unready or whatever) and the scheduling queue doesn't receive NodeAdded. (noderesourcefit cannot receive NodeAdded.)
2. Node is updated and ready now. But, this event is NodeUpdated.

So, no matter whether plugins have QueueingHint or not, plugins must register NodeUpdate event when they're interested in NodeAdd. Also, in case they have QHint, they should take this scenario into consideration.

title: Custom resource objects can be created during CRD Termination using server-side apply

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: help wanted
labels.description: Denotes an issue that needs help from a contributor. Must meet "help wanted" guidelines.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

After a CRD DELETE, while the CRD finalizer is deleting all custom resource objects of that type, and the `Terminating=True` status condition is set, it should not be possible to create objects of that type, but it is with server-side apply, because the creation prevention implementation blocks by method type and there's no check in the PATCH handler.

- CREATE is blocked: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/customresource_handler.go#L373
- PATCH is not blocked: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/customresource_handler.go#L390

In the Patch Apply handler, the `forceAllowCreate` flag is set to `true`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/patch.go#L646 This allows patching to always create objects.

### What did you expect to happen?

When the CRD is terminating, SSA should not be able to create new objects.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. apply a CRD
2. apply a CR with a manual finalizer to block CRD termination
3. delete the CRD
4. create a new CR with SSA

### Anything else we need to know?

There is another race condition allowing creation, but it's otherwise unrelated to this bug, which is not a race condition: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/99181

- tests use ssh to run commands on the control plane instance instead of using hostexec(look at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/103640 for an explanation)

title: NewVolumeManagerReconstruction: Volumes are reported as unmounted after reboot

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
### What happened?

Kubernetes 1.27 with `NewVolumeManagerReconstruction` feature gate **enabled** and `SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod` **disabled**, a rebooted node is not able to re-start pods that were running there before the reboot.

The node reports in Pod events:

```
Warning  FailedMount             2m4s (x5 over 11m)  kubelet                  Unable to attach or mount volumes: unmounted volumes=[myvol], unattached volumes=[], failed to process volumes=[]: timed out waiting for the condition
```

### What did you expect to happen?

The Pod should start just fine.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

On Kubernetes 1.27:
1. Enable NewVolumeManagerReconstruction feature gate.
2. Run a StatefulSet that uses a volume.
3. Force-reboot the node which runs the StatefulSet Pod.

### Anything else we need to know?

The reason is that kubelet's VolumeManager reconstructs the volume as _uncertain_ during startup and it uses a provisional _outer volume name_ for it, because it has not seen the API server and Pods in it yet. This provisional volume ID is then used in ActualStateOfWorld forever.

While kubelet _does_ mount the volume after reboot, it's not able to match it with the Pod that needs it. Kubelet reports `unmounted volumes=[myvol]`, while the volume is mounted with ID `pvc-6357c1ec-bac1-45fd-822f-2d6a014a9721` in my case (= the provisional name, we use PV.name for it) and not `myvol` (=`pod.spec.volumes[*].name`).

It is not reproducible with `SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod` enabled.

```console
$ kubectl version
```

title: DRA: structured parameters: network-attached resource

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: lifecycle/stale
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR has remained open with no activity and has become stale.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
### What would you like to be added?

A network- or fabric-attached resource is something that can be attached to a node when needed, but which isn't visible to kubelet before it is attached.

For structured parameters, this leads to some additional challenges:
- A ResourceSlice must be able to describe which nodes the resource instances can be attached to. More than one slice might be needed, so the "named resources" model must support more than one slice per driver. Helper code for publishing and syncing ResourceSlice objects in a driver would be useful.
- Pod scheduling cannot get delayed (doing so could lead to partial allocation where native resources are gone by the time that the resource is attached), so a network-attached resource needs to be allocated and only then does the kubelet plugin of the driver or some other, driver-specific control plane component "attach" the instance. Until then, the pod needs to wait in a retry loop in kubelet. Not all drivers will need to do some real attach operation.
- There may be attach limits per node (PCI switch for composable dissagregated infrastructure) and/or maximum number of overall users per resource instance (Akri).

/cc @diconico07
/sig node
/triage accepted
/priority important-soon


### Why is this needed?

Akri needs this for resources like IP cameras: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1XNkTobkyz-MyXhidhTp5RfbMsM-uRCWDoflUMqNcYTk/edit#heading=h.wjb5cok1vm2x

Composable disaggregated infrastructured needs it for GPUs connected to a node on demand:
https://kccnceu2024.sched.com/event/1ZPDw/iown-bof-challenges-of-kubernetes-for-composable-disaggregated-computing-naoki-oguchi-fujitsu-hidetsugu-sugiyama-red-hat-clara-li-intel-ryosuke-kurebayashi-ntt

### What would you like to be added?

Without claim parameters, it is unclear which structured model is meant to be used. If even it was clear, parameters for it might be useful.

We should add a default parameter reference to the ResourceClass. Then if a ResourceClaim has no parameter reference, that default gets used. If both are unset, the claim cannot get allocated.

### Why is this needed?

A claim without parameters may make sense depending on the hardware when users have no special needs.

Since the feature is expected to be stable, the scalability evaluation is expected including the performance impact of each operation related to the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy feature and the limitations to which the cluster degrades to be nonfunctional. 

### Why is this needed?

To provide a better idea on scalability of the feature.

body:
### What happened?

I created a pod with sidecar container with following manifest:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: simple-webapp
  labels:
    app: webapp
spec:
  tolerations:
  - key: "key1"
    operator: "Exists"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  initContainers:
    - name: init-service
      image:  busybox
      command:
        - sleep
        - 5s
    - name: sidecar
      image:  busybox
      command:
        - sleep
        - 30s
      volumeMounts:
        - name: shared-logs
          mountPath: /var/log/nginx
      readinessProbe:
        exec:
          command:
          - cat
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 5
      imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
      restartPolicy: Always
  containers:
  - name: main-application
    image: nginx
    volumeMounts:
      - name: shared-logs
        mountPath: /var/log/nginx
    resources:
      requests:
        memory: "100Mi"
        cpu: "0.5"
  volumes:
    - name: shared-logs
      emptyDir: {}
  restartPolicy: Never

```

watch the pod readiness. 
```
#before the sidecar container be restarted , the readiness is 2/2
watch kubectl  get pod
Every 2.0s: kubectl get pod                                                     

NAME                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
simple-webapp           2/2     Running   0          36s

#after the sidecar container be restarted, the pod readiness is 1/2, sidecar readiness result is not be used to the pod. 
NAME                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
simple-webapp           1/2     Running   2          2m15s

```
in [Sidecar containers and Pod lifecycle](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/sidecar-containers/#sidecar-containers-and-pod-lifecycle), it's mentioned "If a readinessProbe is specified for this init container, its result will be used to determine the ready state of the Pod."

it's true only for pod.spec.restartPolicy = Always, sidecar container readniess result will be used in Pod ready state, neither "Never" or "OnFailure".

I tested with v1.29.0

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect "If a readinessProbe is specified for this init container, its result will be used to determine the ready state of the Pod." also applicable to  pod.spec.restartPolicy = "Never" or "OnFailure".

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Set pod.spec.restartPolicy = "Never" or "OnFailure".

body:
### What happened?

The event `RecreatingTerminatedPod` is emitted ~10 times simultaneously after evicting pods of a Statefulset.



### What did you expect to happen?

The event should only be emitted at most once.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Create a 1.29 kind cluster:
```
kind create cluster --image kindest/node:v1.29
```
 (tested with `sha256:eaa1450915475849a73a9227b8f201df25e55e268e5d619312131292e324d570`)

- Deploy a statefulset:

```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
          name: web
```

- Get the initial `RecreatingTerminatedPod` event count for that sts:
```
kubectl get events  --field-selector involvedObject.kind=StatefulSet,involvedObject.name=web,reason=RecreatingTerminatedPod -o json | jq '.items[].count'
```

```
kubectl taint nodes kind-control-plane foo=bar:NoExecute
```

```
kubectl get events  --field-selector involvedObject.kind=StatefulSet,involvedObject.name=web,reason=RecreatingTerminatedPod -o json | jq '.items[].count'
```

```
        command:

        - -c
        - |
          sleep 3;
          exit 1
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
          name: web
```

body:
#### For 1.30:
- [x] decide on required kernel/`nft` versions (@danwinship, #124152)
  - discussion in the first half of #122296, plus some comments in this issue, and then #122743
- [ ] add some useful metrics (@aojea / @npinaeva ?)
  - we don't know exactly what these will be: [discussion in the KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-network/3866-nftables-proxy/README.md#monitoring-requirements)
  - [x] clean up existing metrics stuff a bit at the same time? (@danwinship, #124557)
- [x] add performance job (@aojea https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/32431)
  - Discussion on the KEP PR: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3824#discussion_r1107584724, https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3824#discussion_r1328756780
- [x] change `--nodeport-addresses` behavior to default to "primary node IP(s) only" rather than "all node IPs". (@nayihz, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122724)
  - [discussion in the KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-network/3866-nftables-proxy/README.md#the-iptables-mode-of-kube-proxy-has-grown-crufty)
  - Discussion in the KEP PR: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3824#pullrequestreview-1284130849, https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3824#issuecomment-1418010527, https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3824#discussion_r1334533161
- [x] `reject` connections on invalid ports of service IPs (@aroradaman, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122692)
  - [Discussion in the KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-network/3866-nftables-proxy/README.md#behavior-of-service-ips)
  - kube-proxy could watch [`ServiceCIDR` objects](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-network/1880-multiple-service-cidrs/README.md) to learn the full service CIDR(s) and reject connections on _all_ service IPs, not just currently-in-use-ones.
  - May involve some rewriting of the `@no-endpoints-services` / `@no-endpoints-nodeports` handling, in which case note that we're currently checking no-endpoints nodeports from more places than we need to be (#122687).
  - Resolve the `UNRESOLVED` section of the KEP after this is implemented.
- [X] add periodic and presubmit e2e tests (https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/31525)
- [x] move `danwinship/knftables` to `kubernetes-sigs/knftables` (and eventually declare a v0.1.0 API) (@danwinship, https://github.com/kubernetes/org/issues/4673, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122920)
  - [x] add basic CI (unit tests, gofmt, ...?) to `kubernetes-sigs/knftables` (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/knftables/pull/3)
- [x] drop the `ct state invalid drop` rule (@aroradaman, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122663)
  - This wasn't discussed in the KEP, but it's fallout from other changes that were happening at the same time; we have a better way of dealing with this bug now (`--conntrack-tcp-be-liberal`) so we should remove the ugly hack from the nftables proxy and push people to use that instead if they need it.
- [x] ensure unit test parity with iptables. (I think all that's left here is adding unit tests for the packet tracing code in `helpers_test.go`.) (@npinaeva, https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/knftables/pull/2, https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/knftables/pull/6, #123389)
- [x] decide whether to change NodePorts vs LoadBalancerSourceRanges behavior, and if so, do it. (NO)
  - [discussion in iptables proxier source](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.29.0/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L1167-L1169)
  - [discussion in the KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-network/3866-nftables-proxy/README.md#the-iptables-mode-of-kube-proxy-has-grown-crufty)
- [x] decide if we are going to change anything about session affinity. (NO)
  - [Discussion in the KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-network/3866-nftables-proxy/README.md#session-affinity). I'm not sure if anyone has suggested any particular benefits of the ipvs-like behavior vs the iptables-like behavior.
  - other discussion about changes to affinity behavior: #112806
  - also relevant on the LoadBalancer side (#123714); some LB implementations can't implement the current semantics.
  - Resolve the `UNRESOLVED` section of the KEP after a decision is made.
- [x] decide if we are using comments well in the ruleset. (I GUESS SO?)
  - We don't need many of the comments the iptables ruleset uses because our chain names are self-documenting.
  - In general I tried to put comments on objects (chains, sets, maps) rather than on individual rules, but there is some inconsistency. (But also, note that you won't see the chain/set/map comments with kernels < 5.10.)
  - Individual rules and set/map elements should have comments in some cases. E.g., [elements of `@no-endpoint-services` and `@no-endpoint-nodeports` have comments](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.29.0/pkg/proxy/nftables/proxier_test.go#L575-L577) so that you can see which IP/port goes with which service. But [elements of `@service-ips` and `@service-nodeports` don't](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.29.0/pkg/proxy/nftables/proxier_test.go#L570-L573) because you can already figure that out from the names of the chains that they jump to.

#### Things that depend on us having a perf job (and good metrics) first:
- [x] add iptables-style partial syncing (@npinaeva, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/126013)
- [ ] optimize memory allocation:
  - reuse the buffers used for building the `nft -f -` input, [like iptables does](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.29.0/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L185-L192). This could be done in a few ways. (Have `Proxier` keep buffers around like iptables does and pass a buffer to `nft.Run()`; have `knftables.realNFTables` keep buffers around itself and pass them to the `Transaction`; have `knftables.realNFTables` keep `Transaction`s around and reuse them (with the transaction storing its buffer); ...)
    - (@aroradaman, https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/knftables/pull/9)
  - maybe reuse the `knftables.Transaction.operation` arrays somehow?
  - consider optimizing `knftables.Rule` generation wrt `knftables.Concat`. Some discussion [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121046#discussion_r1367736334).
- [ ] rewrite masquerading to use an nftables set rather than using the mark, [as discussed in the KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-network/3866-nftables-proxy/README.md#masquerading)
- [ ] try out the alternative hairpin rule [suggested in the KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-network/3866-nftables-proxy/README.md#future-improvements).

#### Additional metrics for iptables mode to help users figure out if they'd have trouble migrating:
- [x] Metric to indicate if you are using localhost nodeports. This could be done by making sure there is always a separate rule to catch 127.0.0.1:nodeport rather than letting it be caught by a generic rule, and then checking the counters on those rules and exporting some metric with the result. (@aroradaman, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125015)
- [ ] More generally, metric to indicate if you are using non-primary-node-IP nodeports. (Maybe the metric could just indicate every IP/interface that you're making use of nodeports on?)
- [x] Metric to indicate if you are relying on the `--ctstate INVALID -j DROP` rule (and should be using `--conntrack-tcp-be-liberal` instead) (@aroradaman, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122812)
- [ ] Possibly other metrics if we change other behavior
- [ ] (We could also add metrics to ipvs mode to help ipvs users, but that's not a blocker for eventually changing the default like the iptables metrics are.)

#### For 1.31/beta:
- [x] Generally better documentation (mostly in `content/en/docs/reference/networking/virtual-ips.md` in k/website)
  - Document all [changes from iptables](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-network/3866-nftables-proxy/README.md#changes-from-the-iptables-kube-proxy-backend), including anything above not mentioned in the KEP.
  - Document different interaction with firewalls. ([Discussion in KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-network/3866-nftables-proxy/README.md#forcing-traffic-on-healthchecknodeports-to-be-accepted))
  - https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/46541
- [ ] periodic e2e test of migration/rollback between iptables/ipvs and nftables
- [x] consider the suggestion of [making it possible to run multiple instances of kube-proxy](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-network/3866-nftables-proxy/README.md#multiple-instances-of-kube-proxy) (@uablrek, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122814) (NO)
  - Discussion in the KEP PR: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3824#issuecomment-1574741149, https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3824#issuecomment-1576820872
  - Resolve the `UNRESOLVED` section of the KEP after a decision is made.
- [x] blog post (https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/46969)

- [x] Document the "API guarantees" for components interoperating with nftables kube-proxy.

body:
There are not any metrics tracking admission failures in the Kubelet. I propose adding the following to track this:

`kubelet_admission_rejections_total` - Counter of the number of pods rejected during admission.
- Labels:
  - `reason` - The reason given for the admission rejection.

This would be useful for identifying regressions leading to more pods being rejected in admission (e.g. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/105523).

/kind feature
/milestone v1.31
/sig node instrumentation

body:
### What would you like to be added?

Add support for CPU and memory affinity on windows by enabling the cpu, memory and topology managers for Windows, which are currently not enabled: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f386b4cd4a879e8e7c4c255900a755bd0a61f8f0/pkg/kubelet/cm/topologymanager/fake_topology_manager.go#

### Why is this needed?

Low latency workloads cohosted on the same nodes in Windows Server show noisy neighbor behavior preventing them to achieve their performance goals. This feature is needed to add the necessary isolation to accomplish both high performance and cohosting efficiency.

title: PersistentVolumeLabel admission plugin provides wrong Azure region

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon

labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

On Kubernetes 1.29 with PersistentVolumeLabel admission plugin enabled and no in-tree cloud provider configured in the kube-apiserver, the admission plugins adds label `topology.kubernetes.io/region: ""` to in-tree Azure Disk PVs.

The label is completely wrong - the Azure cloud provider is not initialized and [this](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d9d45306df052aa5824fd8b2dab4e61f5ecc481c/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/azure/azure_managedDiskController.go#L368) just provides empty string. This makes any pod that uses these PVs unschedulable.

As result, all in-tree PVs dynamically provisioned using CSI migration are not usable, because they have a wrong region.

### What did you expect to happen?

When there is no cloud config provided, PersistentVolumeLabel does not add any labels to PVs. PVs created by the CSI driver + CSI migration already have correct `nodeAffinity`, the labels are useless.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Enable PersistentVolumeLabel admission in your cluster and disable any cloud providers. It does not need access to Azure, you can run it anywhere.

    Example for `local-up-cluster.sh`:

    ```
    ENABLE_ADMISSION_PLUGINS="NamespaceLifecycle,LimitRanger,ServiceAccount,DefaultStorageClass,DefaultTolerationSeconds,Priority,MutatingAdmissionWebhook,ValidatingAdmissionWebhook,ResourceQuota,NodeRestriction,PersistentVolumeLabel"
    hack/local-up-cluster.sh
    ```

2. Create in-tree Azure Disk PV. Again, we're testing just the admission, we're not going to use the PV in a pod, so no access to Azure is needed. UUIDs were sanitized ;-)

    ```
    $ kubectl create -f <<EOF
    
    apiVersion: v1
    kind: PersistentVolume
    metadata:
      name: myvol
    spec:
      accessModes:
      - ReadWriteOnce
      capacity:
        storage: 5Gi
      azureDisk:
          cachingMode: ReadWrite
          diskName: pvc-ade30d58-5a51-4a62-a83a-142267b74f9e
          diskURI: /subscriptions/4347f140-6c74-4199-b4fc-1938eb6c16c0/resourceGroups/jsafrane-h-jsafrane-h-kxvpr/providers/Microsoft.Compute/disks/pvc-ade30d58-5a51-4a62-a83a-142267b74f9e
          fsType: ext4
          kind: Managed
          readOnly: false
    
    EOF
    ```

Actual result: wrong region label on the PV:

```
$ kubectl get pv --show-labels
LABELS
topology.kubernetes.io/region=
```

Expected result: no labels on the PV.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_


body:
### What happened?

In 1.30, the PersistentVolumeLabel admission plugin blocks creation of in-tree AzureDisk and vSphere PVs:

```
persistentvolumes "pvc-2d9b3999-f60d-4797-923f-210f1f75025d" is forbidden:
error querying AzureDisk volume pvc-2d9b3999-f60d-4797-923f-210f1f75025d:
unable to build Azure cloud provider for AzureDisk
```

The reason is that the cloud provider was removed (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122857), but the admission plugin still calls GetCloudProvider there, which fails: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/646fbe6d0a3fa1a100d90a429f039324de9c8138/plugin/pkg/admission/storage/persistentvolume/label/admission.go#L285


### What did you expect to happen?

The PV should be admitted + created.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Enable PersistentVolumeLabel admission plugin. For example, when running local-up-cluster.sh:
```
ALLOW_PRIVILEGED=true ENABLE_ADMISSION_PLUGINS="NamespaceLifecycle,LimitRanger,ServiceAccount,DefaultStorageClass,DefaultTolerationSeconds,Priority,MutatingAdmissionWebhook,ValidatingAdmissionWebhook,ResourceQuota,NodeRestriction,PersistentVolumeLabel" bash -x hack/local-up-cluster.sh
```

Create AzureDisk PV on _any_ 1.30 cluster, you don't need Azure cloud:

```
kubectl create -f <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: myvol
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  capacity:
    storage: 5Gi
  azureDisk:
    diskName: test2.vhd
    diskURI: https://someacount.blob.core.windows.net/vhds/test2.vhd
EOF
```

title: Endpoints do not reconcile with EndpointSlices for Services with selector

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/network
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Network.

labels.name: kind/regression
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a regression from a prior release.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
### What happened?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125675 was merged to 1.31, and backported and regressed the following releases:
* 1.31.0+
* 1.30.3+
* 1.29.7+
* 1.28.12+

After an upgrade to 1.28 (1.28.13), we have had significant problems with Services that use a `selector` to target Pods in a Deployment. This is likely happening only with very large services with 1000-2000 backing Pods. The Endpoints eventually appear to be "stuck" with LOTS of IPs as targets (these are large services) and they are not removing old Pod IPs from the Endpoints object, even long after the Pod is gone.

These services are Knative Services, and are operating under frequent and wide scaling. It does seem like Knative is still reading from the Endpoints API.

Deleting the Endpoints object causes it to be recreated and instantly resolves problems from things downstream which are relying on the Endpoints API.

I can show the behavior, but it is difficult to reproduce this without mimicking the scale and churn (scale out and scale in) of a. real service.

Here, I have a service `my-app` - it is in the failed state where Endpoints are not being updated. Note, the source `Service` we are concerned about here is `my-app-00112-private`.
```
% kubectl -n app get endpointslices | grep my-app-00               
my-app-00112-4vk84                   IPv4          8012,8112,8012               10.32.2.22,10.32.5.21,10.32.31.20 + 997 more...         40m
my-app-00112-private-5662t           IPv4          8012,8022,8112 + 3 more...   10.32.86.67,10.32.86.68                                 34m
my-app-00112-private-9mdgr           IPv4          8012,8022,8112 + 3 more...   10.32.210.18,10.32.210.12,10.32.210.32 + 3 more...      36m
my-app-00112-private-kzkxb           IPv4          8012,8022,8112 + 3 more...   10.32.222.22,10.32.222.21,10.32.222.29                  36m
my-app-00112-private-mrpt4           IPv4          8012,8022,8112 + 3 more...   10.32.217.26,10.32.86.63,10.32.86.64 + 12 more...       36m
my-app-00112-private-qnd6m           IPv4          8012,8022,8112 + 3 more...   10.32.139.22,10.32.139.16,10.32.139.20                  37m
my-app-00112-private-swrhv           IPv4          8012,8022,8112 + 3 more...   10.32.85.54,10.32.85.57,10.32.85.55                     34m
my-app-00112-private-xm2w7           IPv4          8012,8022,8112 + 3 more...   10.32.10.180,10.32.96.167,10.32.200.143 + 4 more...     40m
my-app-00112-private-zlp44           IPv4          8012,8022,8112 + 3 more...   10.32.217.21,10.32.217.29,10.32.217.16 + 6 more...      36m
```

And if we look at the scale of that Deployment:
```
% kubectl -n app get deploy my-app-00112-deployment                
NAME                         READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE   AGE
my-app-00112-deployment   28/28   28           28          40m
```

This seems correct. But when we look at the Endpoints, it is a much different story:
```
% kubectl -n app get endpoints my-app-00112-private
NAME                      ENDPOINTS                                                            AGE
my-app-00112-private   10.32.0.70:9091,10.32.10.180:9091,10.32.101.10:9091 + 5907 more...   40m
```

Nearly 6000 endpoints - at about 6 ports per pod (5 are from Knative, basically), that is 1000 pods, the over capacity limit for Endpoints API. In fact, we DO see this annotation:
```
Annotations:  endpoints.kubernetes.io/over-capacity: truncated
```

But that is supposed to come down when pods fall below 1k. Since this service is using a selector, and I think is managed by the Endpoints / EndpointSlices controller, the Endpoints object comes right back if it is deleted, effectively forcing reconciliation from EndpointSlices to Endpoints. And that is exactly what happens.
```
% kubectl -n app delete endpoints my-app-00112-private
endpoints "my-app-00112-private" deleted
% kubectl -n app get endpoints my-app-00112-private     
NAME                      ENDPOINTS                                                           AGE
my-app-00112-private   10.32.0.70:9091,10.32.10.180:9091,10.32.160.111:9091 + 81 more...   4s
```

So it does seem like EndpointSlices -> Endpoints reconciliation is broken in some fashion, under these conditions.


### What did you expect to happen?

Endpoints should be updated when EndpointSlices are changed, even on scale-in operations where Pods are removed.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

It is very difficult for me to provide clear details. But it happens with large Knative services, which are just Deployments that are autoscaled and feed a service.

### Anything else we need to know?

I see audit logs where `endpoint-controller/kube-system` is making frequent use of the permission `io.k8s.core.v1.endpoints.update` on that endpoints resource. But then the audit logs abruptly stop. Which seems to indicate that the controller is no longer even attempting to update the Endpoints resource. This appears to happend after. particularly rapid set of calls to update the endpoints - anywhere from 500ms to 5s apart and about a total of 15-20 times in a minute.

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
Client Version: v1.30.2
Kustomize Version: v5.0.4-0.20230601165947-6ce0bf390ce3
Server Version: v1.28.13-gke.1119000
```

title: [KEP-4639] Specify SELinux behavior for image volumes

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
Related to https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/47588 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/126806

SIG storage meeting notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-8KEG8AjAgKznS9NFm3qWqkGyCHmvU6HVl0sk5hwoAE/edit#heading=h.9rsna5zrjwc

From me:

https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/47588#discussion_r1727171579 It is related to image volume plugin and selinux. Is it a known limitation of all the volume plugins when using selinux? I have a different opinion. If two pods don't share the same mountpoint (hostpath), they can run the same node when the selinux is enabled. the current implementation of  cri-o is sharing the same hostpath when two pods use the same image volume. More details about my idea: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/126806#discussion_r1724826814 

From @jsafrane:

Sharing each volume between namespaces is kind of natural. Sharing PVs not possible but sharing image quite common.

From @gnufied: 

Although for most volume plugins it is true that, they can't be mounted with 2 different selinux context on same node, we want to understand why is this not possible for Imagevolume source. For a traditional storage persistent storage plugins - this limitation is underlying limitation of storage backend/Linux kernel etc.

For ImageVolume source, it seems like a simple solution which unpacks image to two different hostpath would work and not run into this limitation. @haircommander can you specify, why this limitation exists for ImageVolume plugins?

From @haircommander:

we choose to keep it simple and follow the lead of other volume types. supporting multiple selinux types would mean making more complicated the way we mount the image into the container AFAIR. But agreed we can chat about this elsewhere, in the meantime for the purposes of this PR: this is consistent with behavior of other volume plugins and is expected behavior.

Let's discuss the SELinux behavior for image volumes in this issue.

cc @gnufied @jsafrane @saschagrunert @haircommander

/sig node
/sig storage

Run `kube-apiserver` v1.31.0 with `--version=v1.31.0-example.123`

title: Cannot set kubelet config `resolvConf` with drop-in config files

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

body:
### What happened?

I created a kubernetes cluster with kubeadm and created a drop-in directory for kubelet configuration at `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d`.

I created a config file within the directory to change the value of `resolvConf`. After restarting kubelet, the value of `resolvConf` stayed same.

### What did you expect to happen?

The value of `resolvConf` is updated.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```sh
# Create custom resolv.conf
echo 'nameserver 8.8.8.8' | sudo tee /etc/resolv.kubelet.conf

# Create drop-in config directory
sudo mkdir /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d
sudo chmod 700 /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d

# Create drop-in config file
cat <<EOF | sudo tee /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d/99-resolv-conf.conf
apiVersion: kubelet.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: KubeletConfiguration
resolvConf: /etc/resolv.kubelet.conf
EOF
sudo chmod 600 /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d/99-resolv-conf.conf

# Add --config-dir flag
echo 'KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS=--config-dir=/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d' | sudo tee /etc/default/kubelet

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl restart kubelet

# Check if the value of resolvConf is changed.
kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/<node name>/proxy/configz" | jq
```

### Anything else we need to know?

I think this issue is particular to the drop-in config and `resolvConf` option because:

- I can configure `resolvConf` by editing `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`
- I can update another option like `streamingConnectionIdleTimeout` with drop-in config.

title: Terminated but not GC'd Pods should not be re-admitted on kubelet restart

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

Pods that already succeeded and waiting for finalizer are being readmitted, fail to be admitted and moving from Succeeded Phase to Failed (admission failed) phase.

### What did you expect to happen?

The correct behavior would be to not try to re-admit the succeeded (or failed) Pod.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Specific case:

- Node is exposing Devices using device plugin. Device plugin is implemented as a Pod
- Job's pod that is using the Device run to completion and waiting for Job Status finalizer
- kubelet is being restarted
- DevicePlugin pod is reconnecting to the kubelet. While it is reconnecting, kubelet don't have availability of devices
- kubelet re-admits the Pod, even though it is terminated already
- kubelet marks the pod as "failed to be admitted"

But the same can happen with the variations of GC speed and other admission handlers.

### Anything else we need to know?

/sig node
/priority important-soon
/cc @bobbypage @smarterclayton 

There is also a wider issue: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/123980, that concentrates on running pods. This issue is about terminated Pods, which is less controversial.

For sure on master, may be on earlier versions.

### What happened?

We observed a scenario that can cause APIServer to crash due to a CEL validation issue for CRD.
There's an edge case that when a CRD schema is updated after a CR instance is created, CRD finalizer can cause APIServer to crash when the CRD is being deleted.

title: Termination signals not sent to Native Sidecars when multiple Native Sidecars

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: sig/apps
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Apps.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

In a situation where during the init phase of a `Pod`, a native sidecar never becomes ready (because its `startupProbe` is failing), then the `Pod` is terminated, if there are multiple startup containers, a termination signal is never received by the init container and the Pod is stuck (until `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` is hit).

### What did you expect to happen?

All running initContainer to receive the termination signal correctly.  

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a `Dockerfile` with this bash script as an entrypoint:

```
#!/bin/bash
set -e 
trap 'echo "saw an exit signal"; sleep 5; exit' EXIT

while true; do
  echo "hello"
  sleep 1
done
```

Create a deployment with two init containers (one normal one sidecar).  Add an probe which means the startupProbe never passes

```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: karl-test-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app2: karl-test
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app2: karl-test 
    spec:
      securityContext:
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 600
      initContainers:
      - name: init-1
        image: eu.gcr.io/at-artefacts/karl-test
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        command: ["sh", "-c", "echo 'init container 1'"]
      - name: init-2
        image: eu.gcr.io/at-artefacts/karl-test
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        restartPolicy: Always 
        startupProbe:                                                                                                                                                                                                          
          failureThreshold: 600 
          httpGet:
            path: /whatever
            port: 1234
            scheme: HTTP
          periodSeconds: 1
          successThreshold: 1
          timeoutSeconds: 3
      containers:
      - name: karl-test
        image: eu.gcr.io/at-artefacts/karl-test
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

Create the deployment, and it'll be stuck in Init, as you'd expect:

```
karl-test-deployment-c979948d8-xghf4   0/2     Init:1/2   0          5s
```

`kubectl delete` the pod and you'll see the exit signal has been sent to `init-2`:
```
hello
hello
hello
saw an exit signal
```

Delete the deployment / clean everything up.  Now, add a third `initContainer`:

```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: karl-test-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app2: karl-test
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app2: karl-test 
    spec:
      securityContext:
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 600
      initContainers:
      - name: init-1
        image: eu.gcr.io/at-artefacts/karl-test
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        command: ["sh", "-c", "echo 'init container 1'"]
      - name: init-2
        image: eu.gcr.io/at-artefacts/karl-test
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        restartPolicy: Always 
        startupProbe:                                                                                                                                                                                                          
          failureThreshold: 600 
          httpGet:
            path: /whatever
            port: 1234
            scheme: HTTP
          periodSeconds: 1
          successThreshold: 1
          timeoutSeconds: 3
      - name: init-3
        image: eu.gcr.io/at-artefacts/karl-test
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        restartPolicy: Always 
        startupProbe:                                                                                                                                                                                                          
          failureThreshold: 600 
          httpGet:
            path: /whatever
            port: 1234
            scheme: HTTP
          periodSeconds: 1
          successThreshold: 1
          timeoutSeconds: 3
      containers:
      - name: karl-test
        image: eu.gcr.io/at-artefacts/karl-test
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

As before, the `init` process will be stuck on `init-2` because of the bad probe:
```
karl-test-deployment-5c547f8f86-s8nqh   0/3     Init:1/3   0          1s
```

However when you delete the pod this time, no exit signal is sent to `init-2`, the pod is now stuck until `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` is reached.

body:
### What happened?

Pod has been terminating, error: "Error syncing pod, skipping" err="rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = \"transport: Error while dialing: dial unix /run/containerd/containerd.sock: connect: connection refused\"" pod="" podUID=""， Actually, containerd is normal

### What did you expect to happen?

Pod pulled up normally

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Dec  5 23: Upgrade caas from 53 onwards
Dec  5 23: 56 Node Restart
Dec 5 23:56:52 containerd starts after power on
Since the start of the kubelet process on Dec 6 00:00:23, it has not been restarted yet. It should be at this point in time that the kubelet was upgraded
Dec 6 00:00:06 Crittl Check the start and run time of the container process for nbidataserver (cinit process inside the container)
Dec 6 00:01:16 ps Check the startup time of the business process. The probe may not be ready for a short period of time before starting, and the kubelet may only sync after reaching certain conditions 
Dec 6 00:01:37 nbidataservice updataPodContainerResources first reported failure containerdsock connection rejected and kept reporting errors afterwards
Dec 6 00:01:38 containerd upgraded and started up until now



Latest progress: This issue is caused by enabling the InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature
Event replay:
Event 1:2024-12-24 22:41:33 Machine Power On/Off
Event 2:2024-12-24 22:47:53 kubelet starts to start, Pod starts to be pulled up
Event 3:2024-12-24 22:49:03 containerd starts
Event 4:2024-12-24 22:49:04 kubelet started pulling up smauthservice, but received an error message "server is not initialized yet" when accessing containerd. After containerd started, smauthservice started normally.
Event 5:2024-12-24 22:54:12: The upgrade of smauthservice started, and the Kubernetes control plane set the pod smauthservice to Terminating state, which has been consistent until now.
Cause analysis:
1. The kubelet caches real pod information (also known as pod cache), which is synchronized from containerd by PLEG (PodLifecycle Event Generator) coroutine timing. PLEG itself also caches the real pod state (known as PLEG cache). If PLEG detects a difference between the real container state and its own cache, it will synchronize the real pod information to the pod cache.
2. After enabling the InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature, during the pod startup phase, if the pod is expanding, kubelet will query the real pod status from containerd and update the pod cache directly without PLEG. At this time, because containerd cannot access it, unknown status will be saved to the pod cache (Event 4). However, PLEG will not update the pod cache again because the actual pod status is no different from its own cache.
3. Later on, when upgrading the pod, the coroutine for handling pod deletion needed to retrieve the actual pod state from the pod cache for tuning. However, an unknown state was obtained, so the deletion of the pod was stopped and the pod remained in Terminating (Event 5).

title: Sweep and adjust Stat/Lstat/EvalSymlinks to go 1.23 behavior on Windows

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: sig/windows
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Windows.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
Context: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/129080

Go 1.23 changed stdlib behavior of filesystem calls Stat / Lstat / EvalSymlinks on Windows. This broke some kubelet handling of volumes on Windows, and possibly other use of those functions. For Kubernetes 1.32, the behavior was temporarily reverted via godebug switches in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129083, but this is not a long-term solution. Libraries like [k8s.io/mount-utils](https://github.com/kubernetes/mount-utils) can be used by downstream consumers building with go 1.23 and get unintended behavior, and the godebug opt-outs will eventually become unavailable, so we need to prepare Kubernetes to not require them as soon as possible.

As soon as possible in the 1.33 development cycle, sig-storage / sig-windows / sig-node need to sweep for use of Stat / Lstat / EvalSymlinks calls that would be impacted by the go 1.23 changes, and adjust them to work properly, and drop the change in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129083 to restore default go stdlib behavior.

A prereq to doing this safely is good test coverage (both unit test level and e2e level).
- There is currently no job running unit tests on Windows
- There are some e2e jobs exercising volumes on Windows, but the one that was broken (GCE PD) does not currently have working tests (see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/129080#issuecomment-2517810676 and https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/issues/33905)

/sig node storage windows
/priority important-soon
/milestone v1.33

title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Revisit ResizeStatus and state transitions

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
/kind feature

There are several problems with the current approach to pod ResizeStatus, including:

1. Race condition setting the status: the kubelet can overwrite the Proposed status set by the API server (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/125394)
2. Can technically have 2 parallel resize statuses: a {Proposed/Deferred/Infeasible} resize when desired resources != allocated resources, and an InProgress resize when allocated resources != actual resources. Currently the former just overrides the latter.
3. Separate mechanism for surfacing details related to error states (Deferred, Infeasible, stuck InProgress)
4. No status to capture desired memory limit < actual memory usage, which can lead to a resize stuck in InProgress (maybe this should move to the deferred state?)

Before graduating to Beta, we should revisit the design of ResizeStatus, and take a holistic look at the user experience.

/sig node
/priority important-soon
/milestone v1.33
/triage accepted
/cc @yujuhong

body:
/kind bug

Prior to Kubernetes v1.31, any defaulted change to the pod API could trigger running pods to restart on apiserver upgrade (fixed by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124220). Since v1.30 is still within the valid version we cannot set a default ResizePolicy.

Kubelet already handles an unset ResizePolicy as an implicit default (`NotRequired`), so all that is needed here is to remove the defaulting logic. This is probably the preferred behavior even without the version skew issue.

/sig node
/milestone v1.33
/priority important-soon
/triage accepted

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
There is an implicit minimum of `10m` for CPU limits, so the actual resource limit is always clamped at a minimum of 10m. If the desired CPU limit is below 10m, the comparison of desired == actual fails, and the resize status is set to in-progress.

This is very similar to the case of minimum shares addressed in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128680

/kind bug
/sig node
/priority important-soon
/milestone v1.32
