body:
### What happened?

When migrating a sidecar container to a native sidecar container (initContainer with restartPolicy=Always), traffic going via the Kubernetes Service did not reach the application container/sidecar container.

### What did you expect to happen?

The traffic should have reached the sidecar container like before the migration.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a Pod with a native sidecar container (initContainer) with a named port, as well as a Kubernetes Service using that named port as its targetPort. This port is not listed in the Endpoint.

Apply the following:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: sidecar-ports
  labels:
    app: sidecar-ports
spec:
  containers:
  - image: bloomberg/goldpinger:3.10.1
    name: goldpinger
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8000
      name: http
      protocol: TCP
  initContainers:
  # note: no envoy configuration is provided, the steps to reproduce involve reading other Kubernetes manifests (Endpoints)
  - image: envoyproxy/envoy:v1.73.7
    name: tls-terminator
    ports:
    - containerPort: 9443
      name: https
      protocol: TCP
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: sidecar-ports
spec:
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 80
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: http
  - name: https
    port: 443
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: https
  selector:
    app: sidecar-ports
  type: ClusterIP
```

The Endpoint backing the created Service "sidecar-ports" should contain two ports; "http" and "https", but it only contains "http":
```
k describe endpoints sidecar-ports
Name:         sidecar-ports
Namespace:    default
Subsets:
  Ports:
    Name  Port  Protocol
    ----  ----  --------
    http  8000  TCP

Events:  <none>
```

### Anything else we need to know?

The feature gate is enabled:

```
kubectl get --raw /metrics | grep kubernetes_feature_enabled | grep SidecarContainers
kubernetes_feature_enabled{name="SidecarContainers",stage="BETA"} 1
```

I was suggested to create this issue in [this Slack thread](https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C06JCTLFPFX/p1728475764781559)

Workarounds:

1) 

If we update the Service to contain numeric ports instead of named ports, they show up in the endpoint:
```diff
k diff -f reproduce.yaml
diff -u -N /tmp/LIVE-529307225/v1.Service.default.sidecar-ports /tmp/MERGED-1321372933/v1.Service.default.sidecar-ports
--- /tmp/LIVE-529307225/v1.Service.default.sidecar-ports 2024-10-09 14:40:30.518739432 +0200
+++ /tmp/MERGED-1321372933/v1.Service.default.sidecar-ports      2024-10-09 14:40:30.518739432 +0200
@@ -25,7 +25,7 @@
   - name: https
     port: 443
     protocol: TCP
-    targetPort: https
+    targetPort: 9443
   selector:
     app: sidecar-ports
   sessionAffinity: None
```

```
Name:         sidecar-ports
Namespace:    default
Subsets:
  Ports:
    Name   Port  Protocol
    ----   ----  --------
    https  9443  TCP
    http   8000  TCP

Events:  <none>
```

2)

If we specify the named port in the "main" container instead of in the initContainer, the port shows up in the endpoint:

```diff
spec:
  containers:
  - image: bloomberg/goldpinger:3.10.1
    name: goldpinger
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8000
      name: http
      protocol: TCP
+    - containerPort: 9443
+      name: https
+      protocol: TCP
  initContainers:
  # note: no envoy configuration is provided, the steps to reproduce involve reading other Kubernetes manifests (Endpoints)
  - image: envoyproxy/envoy:v1.73.7
    name: tls-terminator
-    ports:
-    - containerPort: 9443
-      name: https
-      protocol: TCP
```

```
Name:         sidecar-ports
Namespace:    default
Subsets:
  Ports:
    Name   Port  Protocol
    ----   ----  --------
    https  9443  TCP
    http   8000  TCP

Events:  <none>
```

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
Client Version: v1.29.9
Kustomize Version: v5.0.4-0.20230601165947-6ce0bf390ce3
Server Version: v1.29.8
```

</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>

</details>

body:
### What happened?

If a pod has an init container with restartPolicy "Always" (sidecar), it may lose the pending phase after the node reboot and start the regular containers before initializing the init containers.

/sig node
/priority important-soon
/kind bug

This is similar to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126650, but separated as it only affects the pod with restartable init containers.

### What did you expect to happen?

After the node reboot, the remaining pod should start from the pending phase and run the init containers one by one to initialize.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create and initialize the pod with an init container with "Always" container restart policy.
2. Restart the node.

### Anything else we need to know?

body:
The test panics in a goroutine after the test itself is finished, so it's only reproducible when this artificial delay is added to the test code:
```

diff --git a/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/plugin/registration_test.go b/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/plugin/registration_test.go
index 59f3099ab65..9dcb8613588 100644
--- a/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/plugin/registration_test.go
+++ b/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/plugin/registration_test.go
@@ -221,4 +221,5 @@ func TestRegistrationHandler(t *testing.T) {
                        assert.Equal(t, test.chosenService, plugin.chosenService, "chosen service")
                })
        }
+       time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
 }
```

body:
Resizing swap needs more consideration (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/130111). For the purposes of unblocking InPlacePodVerticalScaling beta, let's mark resizes affecting swap limit configuration as infeasible.

I thought this would just be a simple addition to `IsInPlacePodVerticalScalingAllowed`, but then realized we need to look at which resources on which containers are being resized, so it doesn't make sense with how that function is used. We should just add an additional check here:  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/22ff6b4918e9cec09842d6ca94584b81a03042cd/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2940

In case it's useful, here's my previous attempt: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/compare/master...tallclair:disable-swap-resize?expand=1

title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Memory request resizing should be acted on

labels.name: priority/important-soon

body:
Currently we don't actuate memory request resizes through the runtime, since memory requests aren't directly configured through cgroups. However, memory requests are indirectly configured through `OomScoreAdj`, and if MemoryQoS is enabled through `memory.high` (also swap, but that needs it's own separate discussion).

We should start issuing `UpdateContainerResources` requests for memory request resizing.

**Open question:** Should we restart the container if the memory restart policy is `RestartContainer`, but only the request is resizing? I think yes. Even if it doesn't seem necessary for OomScoreAdj, it might be for setting `memory.high`, and is generally more consistent.

/sig node
/priority important-soon
/triage accepted
/cc @esotsal @dchen1107 @vinaykul

body:
Currently, we compare the resource configuration reported by the container runtime to the allocated resources to determine whether a container resize was needed, but if anything mutates the resources between the Kubelet requesting them and getting them from the runtime (for example, an NRI plugin), then this leads to problems.

This is addressed in the v1.33 changes to the in-place resize KEP, see https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/1287-in-place-update-pod-resources#actuating-resizes

body:
### What happened?

When a PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) enters the Terminating state due to a deletion request, any pod mounting this PVC experiences a failure in ServiceAccount token refresh operations. This prevents the pod from receiving updated tokens once the current token expires.

### What did you expect to happen?

Token should be refreshed because pod is running.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Set up latest kubernetes cluster (i used [kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/quick-start/))
```
$ k get nodes
NAME                 STATUS   ROLES           AGE     VERSION
kind-control-plane   Ready    control-plane   5h29m   v1.32.2
```

2. Create pod mounting pvc with SA token
```
# token-test.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: simple-token-sa
  namespace: default
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: client-data-pvc
  namespace: default
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: token-client
spec:
  serviceAccountName: simple-token-sa
  containers:
  - name: client
    image: curlimages/curl:latest
    command:
      - sleep
      - infinite
    volumeMounts:
    - name: token-volume
      mountPath: /var/run/secrets/tokens
    - name: data-volume
      mountPath: /data
  volumes:
  - name: token-volume
    projected:
      sources:
      - serviceAccountToken:
          path: custom-token
          expirationSeconds: 600
          audience: my-custom-audience
  - name: data-volume
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: client-data-pvc
```
```
$ k apply -f  token-test.yaml
```

3. Request pvc deletion and the pvc enters terminating state because a pod is still mounting it.
```
$ k delete pvc client-data-pvc 
persistentvolumeclaim "client-data-pvc" deleted
```

4. Check if the token refreshes correctly before reaching its expiration time.
```
# monitor-token.sh
#!/bin/bash

# Colors for output formatting
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[0;33m'
CYAN='\033[0;36m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

echo -e "${CYAN}Token Renewal Monitoring Script${NC}"
echo -e "${CYAN}------------------------------${NC}"
echo -e "Checking for token updates every 30 seconds...\n"

# Initialize variables to track changes
previous_exp=""
first_run=true

while true; do
  # Get the current timestamp for logging
  current_time=$(date "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
  
  # Execute the command to get the token payload
  token_payload=$(kubectl exec -it token-client -- sh -c 'TOKEN=$(cat /var/run/secrets/tokens/custom-token); echo $TOKEN | cut -d. -f2 | base64 -d' 2>/dev/null)
  
  # Check if command was successful
  if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}[${current_time}] Error: Could not retrieve token. Check if the pod is running.${NC}"
    sleep 30
    continue
  fi
  
  # Extract expiration time
  exp_value=$(echo $token_payload | grep -o '"exp":[0-9]*' | cut -d':' -f2)
  
  # Format expiration time as human-readable
  exp_human=$(date -d "@$exp_value" "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
  
  # Calculate time until expiration
  now_seconds=$(date +%s)
  seconds_remaining=$((exp_value - now_seconds))
  minutes_remaining=$((seconds_remaining / 60))
  seconds_remainder=$((seconds_remaining % 60))
  
  # If first run, just display the token info
  if $first_run; then
    echo -e "${CYAN}[${current_time}] Initial token detected${NC}"
    echo -e "Token audience: $(echo $token_payload | grep -o '"aud":\[[^]]*\]' | sed 's/"aud":\["\(.*\)"\]/\1/')"
    echo -e "Service account: $(echo $token_payload | grep -o '"sub":"[^"]*"' | sed 's/"sub":"\(.*\)"/\1/')"
    echo -e "Expires at: ${exp_human} (in ${minutes_remaining}m ${seconds_remainder}s)"
    echo -e "JWT ID: $(echo $token_payload | grep -o '"jti":"[^"]*"' | sed 's/"jti":"\(.*\)"/\1/')"
    echo -e "${CYAN}------------------------------${NC}\n"
    previous_exp=$exp_value
    first_run=false
  else
    # Check if token has been renewed (expiration time changed)
    if [ "$previous_exp" != "$exp_value" ]; then
      echo -e "${GREEN}[${current_time}] Token renewed!${NC}"
      echo -e "New expiration: ${exp_human} (in ${minutes_remaining}m ${seconds_remainder}s)"
      echo -e "New JWT ID: $(echo $token_payload | grep -o '"jti":"[^"]*"' | sed 's/"jti":"\(.*\)"/\1/')"
      echo -e "${CYAN}------------------------------${NC}\n"
      previous_exp=$exp_value
    else
      echo -e "[${current_time}] Token unchanged. Expires in ${minutes_remaining}m ${seconds_remainder}s"
    fi
  fi
  
  # Wait for 30 seconds before checking again
  sleep 30
done
```

body:
Golang does not allow to call certain testing methods in goroutines

> New warning for invalid testing.T use in goroutines[¶](https://go.dev/doc/go1.16#vet-testing-T)
The vet tool now warns about invalid calls to the testing.T method Fatal from within a goroutine created during the test. This also warns on calls to Fatalf, FailNow, and Skip{,f,Now} methods on testing.T tests or testing.B benchmarks.

As consequence, framework that calls this methods internally can not be used in goroutines, this is the case. with testify https://github.com/stretchr/testify/issues/772#issuecomment-945166599

> Document in the assert package that failing assertions will call t.Errorf().
> Document in the testify (module root) package that require is not appropriate in a goroutine but assert is.


It seems there is a linter that helps to identify this incorrect usage https://github.com/Antonboom/testifylint#go-require

We need to fix existing issues on the root modules

```
testifylint --disable-all --enable=go-require ./...
/usr/local/google/home/aojea/src/kubernetes/test/utils/oidc/testserver.go:139:3: go-require: do not use require in http handlers

/usr/local/google/home/aojea/src/kubernetes/test/integration/apiserver/discovery/discovery_test.go:220:3: go-require: require must only be used in the goroutine running the test function
/usr/local/google/home/aojea/src/kubernetes/test/integration/apiserver/discovery/discovery_test.go:309:3: go-require: require must only be used in the goroutine running the test function

```

and submodules

body:
### What happened?

Current private image pull e2e tests for kubelet rely on hardcoded credentials to a public repo that is getting decommissioned as a part of https://github.com/kubernetes/k8s.io/issues/1469. These tests will permafail once that happens.

### What did you expect to happen?

The tests should be written in such a way that they don't depend on external infrastructure. A possible solution might be to stand up an in-cluster registry and populate it with the necessary images.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Wait for https://github.com/kubernetes/k8s.io/issues/1469 to finish and try running some of the tests that rely on the secret from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bdc15f9e19c9331fff685ea4ea264f07605a1fcb/test/e2e/common/node/runtime.go#L284-L291 like the `ImageCredentialProvider` tests.

**Node conformance** test `[sig-node] Container Runtime blackbox test when running a container with a new image should be able to pull from private registry with secret [NodeConformance]` is among those that will be affected.

### Anything else we need to know?

Raised by @BenTheElder in a couple places, like https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128372#discussion_r1918965807

body:
### What happened?

When mounting PVC to the Pod the volume will not mount and it will hang on
```
MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "pvc-d9734ad3-26f5-4fb9-8918-7643d2bf8c75" : kubernetes.io/csi: mounter.SetUpAt failed to get service accoount token attributes: failed to fetch token: serviceaccounts "default" is forbidden: audience "api://AzureADTokenExchange" not found in pod spec volume
```


### What did you expect to happen?

Volume mounted successfully with Pod running.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create Azure cluster with Kubernetes 1.32
2. Create PV claim
```yaml
kind: StorageClass
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: my-pv-claim 
provisioner: kubernetes.io/azure-file
parameters:
  skuName: Standard_LRS 
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: Immediate
```
3. Create Pod and mount PVC

### Anything else we need to know?

The error comes from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/plugin/pkg/admission/noderestriction/admission.go#L654
which was introduced in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128077

Admission plugin will work for CSI
https://github.com/openshift/kubernetes/blob/master/plugin/pkg/admission/noderestriction/admission.go#L689-L690

But when using CSI migration with in-tree azure-file provider the PVC fails to mount.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go#L141

title: vishvananda Netlink breaking changes in 1.2.1

labels.name: priority/important-soon

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Network.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
The vishvananda netlink library had a behavior change in 1.2.1 , see https://github.com/vishvananda/netlink/pull/1018 for more details

> Before https://github.com/vishvananda/netlink/pull/925 (in v1.2.1), the flag was ignored and results were returned without an error. With that change, response handling is aborted, results are discarded, and unix.EINTR is returned.

We are impacted by that change https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fc7520b32f1287b867377aaee89412482199d14a/go.mod#L63 

In order to recover the previous behavior and being more resilient to partial results we should adopt a similar solution to the one adopted by moby developers, wrapping the library to retry a few times

We need to implement something like https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/48407/commits/00bf437d84ac1aec5ce24ffc5f1b7dbb6309263b#diff-28da2a9c14d97c7755152d3ad995389ceda8cc7655c8e03e2874b6d44f977ec1

We also should have some way of linting to avoid adding new netlink calls that are susceptible to get interrupted without the wrapper

/sig network
/priority important-soon

title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Inconsistency between scheduler & kubelet admission logic

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
The scheduler uses `max(spec...resources, status...resources)` to determine the resources requested by a pod, but when the Kubelet is making internal fit decisions it just uses the allocated resources.

In most cases, disagreement between these two approaches would be due to a pending upsize, where the spec...resources are higher than the allocated resources (desired > allocated == actual). This case is working as intended: the scheduler should not schedule over a pending resize, but the Kubelet needs to be able to admit resizes when there are 2 competing resizes.

This is only problematic if there is a case where the scheduler thinks there are _more_ available resources than the Kubelet does, which could lead to a pod being rejected with `OutOf{CPU,Memory}` . In other words, if `max(spec...resources, status...resources) < allocated resources`. This can only happen if both of the following are true:
1. There is a pending (or deferred) downsize (spec...resources < allocated)
2. There is an in-progress upsize (actual resources < allocated)

**Repro steps:**
This repro hits the above conditions for CPU requests, and manipulates memory requests & limits to make the condition persistent.

1. Create a pod with memory & cpu requests & limits
2. In a single resize request, shrink the memory limit below usage, and increase the CPU request
    - Setting the memory limit below the usage will cause the resize to be stuck in progress, without the memory or CPU changes having been actuated.
    - Allocated CPU requests are now higher than the actual CPU requests (shares)
3. In a single resize request, shrink the CPU request back to the original amount, and increase memory requests & limits to more than the available memory (but below the allocatable capacity).
    - The resize will be deferred since there is insufficient available memory for the request
    - The desired CPU is now below the allocated amount
    - For CPU requests, desired == actual < allocated
4. Create a burstable pod with a CPU request, such that the CPU request is `allocatable cpu - sum(desired cpu)`
    - The scheduler will see this pod as fitting, but the kubelet will reject it with OutOfCPU

Moving the memory usage > limit check to allocation time (option 3 in [Handling Memory Limit Decreases for In-Place Pod Resize](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cEFLXKwNOSNLAkzyhoJUgkBW0OiX-9bXB_aJV7OAypw/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.y6xkh6jc1iat)) will mitigate this by making a persistent in-progress resize (step 2 above) less likely, but it doesn't entirely eliminate the issue.

/sig node
/priority important-soon

title: DRA resource claim controller: fails to clean up deleted ResourceClaims on startup

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

labels.name: wg/device-management
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to WG Device Management.

body:
### What happened?

* kube-controller-manager is stopped.
* A allocated claim with one pod in ReservedFor is marked as deleted (but not removed yet because of the finalizer).
* That pod gets deleted, terminates and gets removed.
* kube-controller-manager is restarted.

The ResourceClaim controllers logs:
```
I0616 15:55:01.290991       1 controller.go:390] "not enqueing deleted claim" logger="resourceclaim-controller" claim="dra-6273/external-claim-2"
I0616 15:55:01.291019       1 controller.go:401] "unrelated to any known pod" logger="resourceclaim-controller" claim="dra-6273/external-claim-2"
```

It does not do anything, so the claim remains pending.

This was triggered while working on upgrade/downgrade scenarios.

/wg device-management
/sig node

### What did you expect to happen?

The ResourceClaim controller should remove the pod from ReservedFor, the allocation, and the finalizer, thus unblocking the removal of the ResourceClaim.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Not easy, needs WIP test.

### Anything else we need to know?

This is a regression introduced by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127661.

The logic here is inverted:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blame/c2524cbf9b49f034053f758401ec3b08a4504e0e/pkg/controller/resourceclaim/controller.go#L330

The correct expression is `deleted := newObj == nil`.


This causes the enqueuing of the claim for processing to get skipped in

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c2524cbf9b49f034053f758401ec3b08a4504e0e/pkg/controller/resourceclaim/controller.go#L372-L377

Normally, this gets mitigated by pod removal which also has the desired effect, but in this particular case that removal is never observed - the pod is already gone when the kube-controller-manager starts.

Kubernetes >= 1.32.

title: Consistent paginated lists unnecessarily falling back to etcd in 1.33

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/scalability
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scalability.

labels.name: kind/regression
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a regression from a prior release.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
### What happened?


**When Paginated LIST calls with  rv="" and LIMIT=<x> and without continue token set, those are falling back to etcd instead of serving from cache in `1.33`**

#### TL;DR 

Issue is in Step 7 .5 below - Basically we shouldn't be returning `errors.NewResourceExpired` when snapshot is nil - [xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/544e7a63e2cb6646d19e6a17bd665b07f39843d1/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/watch_cache.go#L547-L548)

There is a performance impact angle to this bug - We do consistent reads to etcd with `LIMIT=1` in step 4 below, which wait until cache catches up to the RV or times out, but all of that is unnecessary cpu cycles spent on request because we are falling back to etcd (step 8) anyway, which in this case from below audit log for this specific request, it spent `721ms` unnecessarily iiuc.



### In 1.33  here the is the code flow for LIST request FMU :


1. Delegator decides if call needs to be served from cache or if it needs to be sent to etcd - [xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f20adaecd4743b3481af4240ed034003dacf7c9c/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/delegator.go#L183) 
2. Given RV=“” in this case, it will call ShouldDelegateConsistentRead -   [xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8d3fb9ee0a51b6a6ea135d991391c35806422c19/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/delegator/interface.go#L58)
3. Given consistentReads are enabled, this yields `{ ShouldDelegate : False , ConsistentRead : true}`  - [xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8d3fb9ee0a51b6a6ea135d991391c35806422c19/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/delegator/interface.go#L101) 
4. Given shouldDelegate is False and ConsistentRead is true from 3 , it makes the call to etcd to get current RV -[xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8d3fb9ee0a51b6a6ea135d991391c35806422c19/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/delegator.go#L210-L211)
5. Now  RV is set in LIST options because APIServer fetched latest RV from etcd -[xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8d3fb9ee0a51b6a6ea135d991391c35806422c19/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/delegator.go#L216) 
6. APIServer now tries to serve  LIST request from cache at the above RV -[xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8d3fb9ee0a51b6a6ea135d991391c35806422c19/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/delegator.go#L218)
7. **" If and only if there is an error listing from cache , which is always the case in 1.33 ( at the least) due to current code listitems func return error -[xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8d3fb9ee0a51b6a6ea135d991391c35806422c19/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L766-L769) . Why it returns error is because of following code path**":
    1. code flows to call listItems -[xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8d3fb9ee0a51b6a6ea135d991391c35806422c19/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L701) and then calls `c.watchCache.WaitUntilFreshAndList(ctx, listRV, key, opts)` - [xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8adc0f041b8e7ad1d30e29cc59c6ae7a15e19828/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/watch_cache.go#L499)
    2. Then it calls list function on watch-cache - [xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/544e7a63e2cb6646d19e6a17bd665b07f39843d1/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/watch_cache.go#L512)
    3. Given we have RV is set and limit is set, it falls to this case statement - [xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/544e7a63e2cb6646d19e6a17bd665b07f39843d1/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/watch_cache.go#L538-L540)
    4. Now listExactRV is called -[xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/544e7a63e2cb6646d19e6a17bd665b07f39843d1/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/watch_cache.go#L546)
    5. Given snapshot is nil as it won’t be enabled until `1.34`, it returns `errors.NewResourceExpired` - [xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/544e7a63e2cb6646d19e6a17bd665b07f39843d1/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/watch_cache.go#L548)
8. **when RV is expired ( too old)  fall back to etcd** - [xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8d3fb9ee0a51b6a6ea135d991391c35806422c19/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/delegator.go#L223) 
9. From 8, LIST call is served from etcd3 store.go -[xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8d3fb9ee0a51b6a6ea135d991391c35806422c19/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/store.go#L679),  if its a high latency call i.e above 500ms, it should log this trace log when serving LIST request - [xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8d3fb9ee0a51b6a6ea135d991391c35806422c19/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/store.go#L684-L691) 
10.  Given `LIMIT=500` with `label and field selector`, APISever fetches multiple pages from etcd using continueKey [xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8d3fb9ee0a51b6a6ea135d991391c35806422c19/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/store.go#L814) until either:
    1. It satisfies the client’s limit=X, - [xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8d3fb9ee0a51b6a6ea135d991391c35806422c19/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/store.go#L805-L807) OR
    2. It exhausts all etcd keys - [xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8d3fb9ee0a51b6a6ea135d991391c35806422c19/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/store.go#L773-L775) , it goes in a loop 
     If selectors filter out too many objects, the API server:
               Doubles the page size for every call (up to maxLimit = 10000) to reduce total number of etcd calls - [xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8d3fb9ee0a51b6a6ea135d991391c35806422c19/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/store.go#L825-L832)

### What did you expect to happen?

It should serve from cache.

I think it serves from cache in 1.32 iirc 


Code flow:

1. It fetches the RV with [LIMIT=1 ](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9894294ef13a5b32803e3ca2c0d620a088cc84d1/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L864)and make a [LIST call to cache ](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9894294ef13a5b32803e3ca2c0d620a088cc84d1/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L901)
2. It makes a call to [WaitUntilFreshAndList](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9894294ef13a5b32803e3ca2c0d620a088cc84d1/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/watch_cache.go#L455) which returns [list response ](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9894294ef13a5b32803e3ca2c0d620a088cc84d1/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/watch_cache.go#L470-L493)back  
3. Which gets filtered etc on the APIServer side before responding to client [xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7f50c56b1aee651924f39317329d33977f3c736a/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L766-L815)




Offending [commit](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130423/files#diff-dc9b33f648eee119a44322015b3c50f9dbd1c45ac7790084579dc0a4cd075de2R546-R561) which introduced code in Step 7.5 below in this [PR](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130423) iiuc as part of the efforts of [snapshottable-apiserver-cache KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/4988-snapshottable-api-server-cache/README.md) . Code changes we see in step 7.5 should be feature gated at the very least. 




### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Just make a paginated LIST call with `rv=""` , `LIMIT=500` with field and label selectors. Ensure you have around 150K pods to trigger trace logs or reduce trace span time from 500ms depending on your load.

title: kube-scheduler does not consider hostPort ports used by initContainers when scheduling

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
### What happened?

When running two pods that both use hostNetwork and have sidecar initContainers (restartPolicy: Always) using the same port, kube-scheduler allows the pods to be scheduled on the same node.



### What did you expect to happen?

kube-scheduler does not schedule these two pods on the same node, following the behavior for pods using hostNetwork ports via a main container.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a kind cluster: `kind create cluster`.  The cluster only has one node.
2. Apply p1:
   ```
   apiVersion: v1
   kind: Pod
   metadata:
     name: p1
   spec:              
     hostNetwork: true
     dnsPolicy: ClusterFirstWithHostNet
     initContainers:
     - name: init
       restartPolicy: Always    
       image: python:3.12                                                                                                                                                                                                            
       command:
       - /bin/bash
       - -c
       - python -m http.server 8081
       ports:
       - containerPort: 8081
     containers:
     - name: main
       image: python:3.12
       command:
       - /bin/bash
       - -c
       - sleep 10000
   ```
3. Apply p2:
   ```
   apiVersion: v1
   kind: Pod
   metadata:
     name: p2
   spec:
     hostNetwork: true
     dnsPolicy: ClusterFirstWithHostNet
     initContainers:
     - name: init
       restartPolicy: Always    
       image: python:3.12                                                                                                                                                                                                            
       command:
       - /bin/bash
       - -c
       - python -m http.server 8081
       ports:
       - containerPort: 8081
     containers:
     - name: main
       image: python:3.12
       command:
       - /bin/bash
       - -c
       - sleep 10000
   ```
4. p2 is scheduled (and crashing because p1 is already using the port).


### Anything else we need to know?

kube-scheduler already accounts for hostNetwork ports used by main containers.  For example:

1. Create a kind cluster: `kind create cluster`.  The cluster only has one node.
2. Apply p1:
   ```
   apiVersion: v1
   kind: Pod
   metadata:
     name: p1
   spec:              
     hostNetwork: true
     dnsPolicy: ClusterFirstWithHostNet
     containers:
     - name: main
       image: python:3.12
       command:
       - /bin/bash
       - -c
       - python -m http.server 8081
       ports:
       - containerPort: 8081
   ```
3. Apply p2:
   ```
   apiVersion: v1
   kind: Pod
   metadata:
     name: p2
   spec:
     hostNetwork: true
     dnsPolicy: ClusterFirstWithHostNet
     containers:
     - name: main
       image: python:3.12
       command:
       - /bin/bash
       - -c
       - python -m http.server 8081
       ports:
       - containerPort: 8081
   ```
4. p2 is not scheduled: `Warning  FailedScheduling  3m7s  default-scheduler  0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't have free ports for the requested pod ports. preemption: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 No preemption victims found for incoming pod.`

body:
### What happened?

Kubelet's swap related metrics were introduced in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118865. However, these swap-related metrics are missing from `/metrics/resource` endpoint. Only node-level swap usage metrics are visible. The pod-level and container-level swap usage are available from `/stats/summary` endpoint, but no metrics are visible from `/metrics/resource`.

```
kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/<node>/proxy/metrics/resource" | grep -i swap
                    
# HELP node_swap_usage_bytes [ALPHA] Current swap usage of the node in bytes. Reported only on non-windows systems
# TYPE node_swap_usage_bytes gauge
node_swap_usage_bytes 3.4340864e+07 1747937814848

kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/<node>//proxy/stats/summary" | jq ".pods[] | select(.swap.swapUsageBytes > 0)"       

{
  "podRef": {
    "name": "oom-test-pod-stress-ng",
    "namespace": "default",
    "uid": "4bc5b67c-d750-47d4-a36a-5cec6190d752"
  },
  "containers": [
    {
      "name": "memory-eater",
      # ... omitted
      "swap": {
        "time": "2025-05-22T18:19:01Z",
        "swapAvailableBytes": 0,
        "swapUsageBytes": 33554432
      }
    }
  ],
  # omitted...
  "swap": {
    "time": "2025-05-22T18:18:50Z",
    "swapUsageBytes": 33554432
  }
}
```

### What did you expect to happen?

Container-level swap usage `container_swap_usage_bytes` and pod-level swap usage `pod_swap_usage_bytes` metrics should be available from `/metrics/resource` endpoint.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a node with swap enabled (https://kubernetes.io/blog/2025/03/25/swap-linux-improvements/#install-a-swap-enabled-cluster-with-kubeadm)

Get the swap metrics `kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/<node-name>/proxy/metrics/resource"

### Anything else we need to know?

The node is using ~~cadvisor~~ CRI for resource metrics.

Also happened for kind: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kind/issues/3834

title: `YAMLOrJSONDecoder` could panic if YAML data length is shorter than JSON data read

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon

labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

`YAMLOrJSONDecoder` has the ability to read a first JSON message and then fallback to YAML for subsequent messages.  This behavior was introduced by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130666.

When the YAML data is shorter than the JSON data previously read, the decoder panics because https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c27fbaa63c7175ffdedeb918bd6a426987651afb/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/yaml/decoder.go#L343 results in a negative number.

### What did you expect to happen?

The decoder shouldn't panic

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```go
s := NewYAMLOrJSONDecoder(bytes.NewReader([]byte(`{\"foo\": \"bar\"}\n---\na: b`)), 100)

var obj any
err := s.Decode(&obj)
_ = err
```

title: CEL CIDR parser does not behave as documented

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/network
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Network.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
The docs for the CIDR-related CEL extensions say:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8e6d788887034b799f6c2a86991a68a080bb0576/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/cel/library/cidr.go#L47

but this is incorrect; the parser actually accepts that kind of string.

This seems to be a mistake: [we seem to have agreed in the original PR that we were going to add that restriction](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121912#discussion_r1395710965), but it accidentally only got added to the docs, not the actual implementation.

So now we need to decide between:
1. This is a bug, the function is not behaving as documented, so we should fix it.
2. People may be depending on the shipped behavior so it would be an API break to change it, so we need to just update the docs to reflect the actual behavior.

This was noticed while RH QE was testing the new UserDefinedNetwork types in ovn-kubernetes; some fields are validated with `isCIDR()` but were allowing non-subnet-like values that then didn't work. (Bug is https://issues.redhat.com/browse/CORENET-6423 but it's currently private.)

AdminNetworkPolicy is also using `isCIDR` for validation and expecting the "subnets/masks-only" semantics, not the "subnets/masks or ifaddr-style IP addresses" semantics...

/sig network
/priority important-soon
/cc @JoelSpeed @tssurya

title: Kubelet rejects pod with "NodeAffinity failed" due to stale informer data

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
#### What happened

This issue is similar to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/100467 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/92067.

We have a controller that adds labels to a node after it starts up. It looks like there are cases where the scheduler is able to see the new node labels and schedule a pod, but the kubelet somehow doesn't see the new labels - it has stale data in its informer cache. Whatever the reason for the stale data, the result is that the kubelet rejects the pod with "NodeAffinity failed".

#### What did you expect to happen

Kubelet to be able to detect the new node labels and not reject the pod. 

The only reason that we need to keep the node affinity / node selector check in the kubelet is in case someone sets `nodeName` directly on the pod, so that it does not go through the scheduler, so we can't just remove enforcement on the node level.

The short-term fix would be for the kubelet to synchronously fetch the node object when (and only when) it sees these "NodeAffinity failed" errors and try again. To ensure we do not introduce additional heavy traffic when there many pods being scheduled at once, we will have to keep a new cache, separate from the informer cache. The logic would be like:
- Read the node object from the informer
- If we get a NodeAffinity failed error, read the node object from our new cache
- If we still get a NodeAffinity failed error, fetch the node object synchronously from the api server
The cache should be updated whenever we see a node object that is newer than the one we are currently storing - this can come from either the informer or from the synchronous fetch. 

Long term, maybe we can re-consider the flow for `nodeName`, or leverage something like [kubelet synchronous admission](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1O9rDeYhGWMbtg-DQmhqKvNsQSHWJSwvSEeNpXTKMvZg/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.6ggs708p6vvu) to keep the scheduler and kubelet coordinated. There are also some more general discussions about what to do when informer data is stale, maybe the outcomes there can help here.

#### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

You'd probably have to restart kubelet a whole bunch of times, and have a controller that modifies the node labels whenever it restarts.

#### Environment
- Kubernetes version: The issue is reported as persistent from versions v1.18-v1.28+, and it is unlikely that it has been fixed in a more recent version.
- Cloud provider: GKE

/sig node
/assign
/cc @tallclair

body:
### Which jobs are failing?

pull-kops-kubernetes-e2e-ubuntu-gce-build

### Which tests are failing?

[sig-node] crictl should be able to run crictl on the node

### Since when has it been failing?

26.08.2025

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/kops-presubmits#pull-kops-kubernetes-e2e-ubuntu-gce-build

### Reason for failure (if possible)

Related to changes added by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133476:
```
exitCode=127 stdout="" stderr="sh: 1: /home/kubernetes/bin/crictl: not found\n", might retry
```

### Anything else we need to know?

The  path for the `crictl` binary has been hardcoded to `/home/kubernetes/bin/crictl`. This is something specific to ContainerOS.
Additionally, `crictl` is not a requirement for a node to run, so maybe this should be a feature-specific test like `[Feature:crictl]`.

body:
### What happened?

When using Kubernetes version 1.34 `kubelet_volume_stats_*` metrics such as `kubelet_volume_stats_available_bytes` are no longer present in `kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/$NODE/proxy/metrics"`.

I know that they are in Alpha state and Alpha metrics do not come with any guarantees, but since they are still [documented](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/metrics/#list-of-alpha-kubernetes-metrics) I expect them to be visible. If this change was intended, it doesn't seem to be documented.

I was not able to correlate this with anything mentioned in [CHANGELOG-1.34.md](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.34.md).



### What did you expect to happen?

I would expect these metrics to be present in the output (this cluster is running 1.33.x)

```
kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/$NODE/proxy/metrics" | grep kubelet_volume_stat
# HELP kubelet_volume_stats_available_bytes [ALPHA] Number of available bytes in the volume
# TYPE kubelet_volume_stats_available_bytes gauge
kubelet_volume_stats_available_bytes{namespace="default",persistentvolumeclaim="local-pvc"} 1.0881118208e+10
# HELP kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes [ALPHA] Capacity in bytes of the volume
# TYPE kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes gauge
kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{namespace="default",persistentvolumeclaim="local-pvc"} 6.2671097856e+10
# HELP kubelet_volume_stats_inodes [ALPHA] Maximum number of inodes in the volume
# TYPE kubelet_volume_stats_inodes gauge
kubelet_volume_stats_inodes{namespace="default",persistentvolumeclaim="local-pvc"} 3.907584e+06
# HELP kubelet_volume_stats_inodes_free [ALPHA] Number of free inodes in the volume
# TYPE kubelet_volume_stats_inodes_free gauge
kubelet_volume_stats_inodes_free{namespace="default",persistentvolumeclaim="local-pvc"} 1.476414e+06
# HELP kubelet_volume_stats_inodes_used [ALPHA] Number of used inodes in the volume
# TYPE kubelet_volume_stats_inodes_used gauge
kubelet_volume_stats_inodes_used{namespace="default",persistentvolumeclaim="local-pvc"} 2.43117e+06
# HELP kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes [ALPHA] Number of used bytes in the volume
# TYPE kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes gauge
kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes{namespace="default",persistentvolumeclaim="local-pvc"} 4.8573263872e+10
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create cluster:

```console
kind create cluster --name k8s-1-34 --image kindest/node:v1.34.0
```

Create the storage directory

```console
NODE=$(kind get nodes --name k8s-1-34)
docker exec -it $NODE mkdir -p /mnt/local-storage
```

Create files:

```yaml
# local-storageclass.yaml
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: local-storage
provisioner: kubernetes.io/no-provisioner
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
```

```yaml
# local-pvc.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: local-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: local-storage
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
```

```yaml
# local-pv.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: local-pv
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 1Gi
  volumeMode: Filesystem
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Delete
  storageClassName: local-storage
  local:
    path: /mnt/local-storage
  nodeAffinity:
    required:
      nodeSelectorTerms:
        - matchExpressions:
            - key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane
              operator: Exists
```

```yaml
# pod-with-local-pv.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: demo-pod-local
spec:
  containers:
```

title: ServiceCIDR is known to not work in some clusters, but blocking it via VAP violates conformance

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/network
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Network.

labels.name: area/conformance
labels.description: Issues or PRs related to kubernetes conformance tests

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
The ServiceCIDR API requires support from non-core-k8s components in some clusters, and thus is not guaranteed to work in all clusters. The [ServiceCIDR documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/network/extend-service-ip-ranges/#preventing-unauthorized-servicecidr-creation-update-using-validating-admission-policy) explains how you can use VAP to block usage of the API in this case. (Though there are some problems and https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/51748 updates those docs.)

However, it turns out that doing this violates conformance, because the test `[sig-network] ServiceCIDR and IPAddress API should support ServiceCIDR API operations [Conformance]` requires that `e2e.test` is able to modify the default ServiceCIDR.

The test case just adds an annotation, so we could hack up the VAP to allow the specific change that the conformance test makes, but this seems like cheating, and would also be fragile.

Does it make sense for conformance to require ServiceCIDR to be available as an API, given that it doesn't work in some clusters and we explicitly document how to disable it? (FWIW I guess the same question could be asked about NetworkPolicy, except that everyone has gotten used to the fact that the NP API exists even in clusters where it doesn't work so no one tries to disable it...)

/sig network
/area conformance
/triage accepted
/priority important-soon
cc @aojea

body:
### What happened?

```
$ cat cm.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2025-08-05T16:42:06Z"
  deletionTimestamp: 2025-08-05T16:42:06Z
  name: test
  namespace: kubevirt-vm

$ k apply --server-side -f cm.yaml
Warning: Detected changes to resource test which is currently being deleted.
configmap/test serverside-applied

$ k get cm test  -oyaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2025-08-05T16:45:59Z"
  deletionTimestamp: "2025-08-05T16:42:06Z"
  name: test
  namespace: kubevirt-vm
  resourceVersion: "257079249"
  uid: caa288c7-9b51-4365-a062-a4020d4bef93
```

Then deleting it causes it to go, so I am guessing this is rooted in insufficient event handling in the GC controller, since only SSA allows to create objects with a non-nil deletion timestamp:
```
$ k delete    -f cm.yaml
configmap "test" deleted

$ k get cm test  -oyaml
Error from server (NotFound): configmaps "test" not found
```

The CM to immediately be gone

title: main container never starts with restartPolicy: Never and sidecar container has a startupProbe and fails the first attempt

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon

body:
### What happened? There is a bug in `kubelet` `startupProbe` if sidecar container is configured. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.32/pkg/kubelet/prober/worker.go#L249 The worker's decision to continue (return true) or stop (return false) is based only on the pod's restart policy, not the containers (sidecar have restartPolicy:Always) This can lead to a racing condition if the sidecar container fails at the first time and prober incorrectly exits: If sidecar container restarted with no problem at second attempt, startupProbe will never run again. This leads kubelet to think the initContainer never successfully initialized. There is another bug in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/prober/prober_manager.go#L194 the probe can possibly get recreated here. However if there are more than one containers has startup probes, and the first container has a running probe, it will skip other containers (because of an early`return`). As a result, reproduction requires at least 2 startup probes. With the example in the "How to reproduce", the `main-container` is stuck in Initializing state. kubectl desribe pod
``` $ kubectl describe pod init-probe-bug-repro Name: init-probe-bug-repro Namespace: default Priority: 0 Service Account: default Node: gke-cluster-1-pool-3-7b56b326-2rxq/10.128.0.96 Start Time: Tue, 08 Jul 2025 23:38:27 +0000 Labels: Annotations: Status: Pending IP: 10.112.2.93 IPs: IP: 10.112.2.93 Init Containers: buggy-init-container: Container ID: containerd://5c44b517ecfe0d162a31759d1a7f2399c1954d3d80c3225a0d8bf24d0982e952 Image: busybox Image ID: docker.io/library/busybox@sha256:f85340bf132ae937d2c2a763b8335c9bab35d6e8293f70f606b9c6178d84f42b Port: Host Port: Command: sh -c if [ ! -f /work/first_run_done ]; then echo "First run: creating marker and exiting with 1." touch /work/first_run_done exit 1 else echo "Second run: marker found. Running as a sidecar." sleep infinity fi State: Running Started: Tue, 08 Jul 2025 23:38:28 +0000 Last State: Terminated Reason: Error Exit Code: 1 Started: Tue, 08 Jul 2025 23:38:27 +0000 Finished: Tue, 08 Jul 2025 23:38:27 +0000 Ready: True Restart Count: 1 Startup: exec [/bin/true] delay=5s timeout=1s period=2s #success=1 #failure=3 Environment: Mounts: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount from kube-api-access-grqbb (ro) /work from workdir (rw) Containers: main-container: Container ID: Image: registry.k8s.io/pause Image ID: Port: Host Port: State: Waiting Reason: PodInitializing Ready: False Restart Count: 0 Startup: exec [/bin/true] delay=5s timeout=1s period=5s #success=1 #failure=3 Environment: Mounts: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount from kube-api-access-grqbb (ro) Conditions: Type Status PodReadyToStartContainers True Initialized True Ready False ContainersReady False PodScheduled True Volumes: workdir: Type: EmptyDir (a temporary directory that shares a pod's lifetime) Medium: SizeLimit: kube-api-access-grqbb: Type: Projected (a volume that contains injected data from multiple sources) TokenExpirationSeconds: 3607 ConfigMapName: kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMapOptional: DownwardAPI: true QoS Class: BestEffort Node-Selectors: Tolerations: node.kubernetes.io/not-ready:NoExecute op=Exists for 300s node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoExecute op=Exists for 300s Events: Type Reason Age From Message ---- ------ ---- ---- ------- Normal Scheduled 19m default-scheduler Successfully assigned default/init-probe-bug-repro to gke-cluster-1-pool-3-7b56b326-2rxq Normal Pulled 19m kubelet Successfully pulled image "busybox" in 225ms (226ms including waiting). Image size: 2156518 bytes. Normal Pulling 19m (x2 over 19m) kubelet Pulling image "busybox" Normal Created 19m (x2 over 19m) kubelet Created container: buggy-init-container Normal Started 19m (x2 over 19m) kubelet Started container buggy-init-container Normal Pulled 19m kubelet Successfully pulled image "busybox" in 225ms (225ms including waiting). Image size: 2156518 bytes. ```
Timeline T=0s: The buggy-init-container starts. The prober creates a worker for it, which immediately begins its initialDelaySeconds: 10 wait. T=0.1s: The container's command runs, creates the /work/first_run_done file, and exits with code 1. The container is now in a Terminated state. T=0.1s to T=5s: The probe worker is still waiting for its initial delay to expire. It has not run a single probe. T=5s: The worker's delay is over, and it runs doProbe for the first time. It sees that the container is Terminated. The onHold flag is false because a probe has never completed. It proceeds to the check: if c.State.Running == nil. This is true. It executes the faulty return logic: return c.State.Terminated == nil || w.pod.Spec.RestartPolicy != v1.RestartPolicyNever. Since the pod's RestartPolicy is Never, this evaluates to false, and the probe worker terminates itself. Meanwhile: `kubelet` sees the terminated init container and, honoring its restartPolicy: Always, starts a new instance of it. The syncloop will attempt to recreate the probe. However due to the bug in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/prober/prober_manager.go#L194 , the loop will `return` early because the main container's probe already exists, it fails to check the initContainer's probe. Result: The new container instance starts, but its probe worker is gone. No new worker is created. The Kubelet sees a running container with a startup probe but not have a successful ran, assuming it's not ready. The main-container never starts. ### What did you expect to happen? startupProbe should honor the container's restartPolicy. The startupProbe should continue to probe even if the sidecar container has failed initially and restarts. The main container should eventually run if the sidecar container eventually start up healthy. ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? ``` apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: init-probe-bug-repro spec: # The Pod's restart policy is Never, a key condition for the bug. restartPolicy: Never volumes: - name: workdir emptyDir: {} initContainers: - name: buggy-init-container image: busybox # The container's restart policy is Always. restartPolicy: Always volumeMounts: - name: workdir mountPath: /work # This command fails very quickly on the first run. command: - sh - -c - | if [ ! -f /work/first_run_done ]; then echo "First run: creating marker and exiting with 1." touch /work/first_run_done exit 1 else echo "Second run: marker found. Running as a sidecar." sleep infinity fi startupProbe: # This delay MUST be long enough for the first container instance # to start, run its command, and terminate. initialDelaySeconds: 5 periodSeconds: 2 failureThreshold: 3 # The probe command itself is irrelevant, as it will never be run # by the first worker. exec: command: ["/bin/true"] containers: - name: main-container image: registry.k8s.io/pause # Added a startupProbe to the main container. startupProbe: initialDelaySeconds: 5 periodSeconds: 5 exec: command: ["/bin/true"] ``` ### Anything else we need to know? _No response_ ### Kubernetes version

body:
### What happened?

The `ci-kubernetes-unit-dependencies` CI job is failing after updating `go.opentelemetry.io/contrib/instrumentation/google.golang.org/grpc/otelgrpc` from v0.60.0 to v0.64.0.

**Failed job**: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-unit-dependencies/2002001097211777024

### Root Cause

Commit [07504e453](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib/commit/07504e45307f41b8b4e609324a3b62374ad6008f) in otelgrpc removed nil checks from `WithTracerProvider` and `WithMeterProvider` options. When Kubernetes passes a nil `TracerProvider` in `staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/storagebackend/factory/etcd3.go:326`:

```go
otelgrpc.WithTracerProvider(c.TracerProvider),  // c.TracerProvider can be nil
```

The nil now overwrites the default global provider, causing a panic in `NewClientHandler()` when it calls `c.TracerProvider.Tracer(...)`.

/priority important-soon

body:
### What happened?

We observed the e2e test `External Storage [Driver: disk.csi.azure.com] [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] read-write-once-pod [MinimumKubeletVersion:1.27] should preempt lower priority pods using ReadWriteOncePod volumes` causes flakes in other e2e tests in a downstream CI job with Azure Disk CSI driver.

[The test](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4e94e70dcad423e9f59f12ac5a048d2137d20e86/test/e2e/storage/testsuites/readwriteoncepod.go#L133) runs a default (low-prio) pod1 with a `ReadWriteOncePod` volume and then starts a high prio pod2 that tries to use the same volume. To run pod2, the scheduler has to evict pod1 to make the RWOP volume "free" for pod2. That works great, however, it may evict also pods of other e2e tests that run with the default priority.

What happened on a busy clusters, with all nodes at their attachment limit.

1. pod1 runs, pod2 is created.
2. The scheduler evicts pod1. That frees the RWOP volume and it also frees the last attachment slot on the node.
3. Some other e2e tests creates a Pod and scheduler puts it on the node, taking the last attachment slot.
4. The scheduler schedules pod2 agaian and it sees there is no node with a free attachment slot -> new round of eviction, now evicting a pod of unrelated e2e tests. The unrelated test will fail.  

We observed it with Azure, which can attach only 8 disks on the cheaper nodes, so it's more reproducible there.

### What did you expect to happen?

The preemption test should not affect other e2e tests

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

See above

title: [InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Move feasibility checks to admission

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
This is an umbrella issue to track the work of moving feasibility checks to admission.

Resizes can be considered infeasible for the following reasons:
- The requested resources exceed the node's total capacity.
- The pod is running on a node with an OS that does not support resize (like windows).
- The pod is a static pod.
- The feature gate is disabled on the node.
- Resize is not supported in combination with a few other features, which are:
  - Swap
  - Static CPU manager
  - Static memory manager


For infeasible resizes, the admission controller accepts the resize patch, with the feasibility check subsequently performed by the kubelet prior to resource allocation. If the resize is deemed infeasible, the kubelet adds a PodResizePending / Infeasible condition to the pod. An optimization we can make is to instead move these feasibility checks to admission, instead of accepting the patch and waiting for the kubelet to reject the resize.

The first 3 are trivial to move to admission. The remaining ones can be handled using the node declared features framework once we have commitment to implement those features so that we have a feature gate that we can tie the NDFs to.

/cc @tallclair @pravk03 
/assign

/sig node

title: failing device-plugin health checks causing kubelet SIGABRT by systemd watchdog during initialization.

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
### What happened?

We have Kubelet, version 1.34, running in a systemd service, configured to expect watchdog updates atleast every 20 seconds. 

If the updateRuntimeUp function does not run to completion within this deadline, it causes the `device-plugin` health check to fail, causing watchdog updates to not be sent to systemd, which causes kubelet to crash-loop. 

In our case, the updateRuntimeUp function was blocked on https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3ec72e2e973664a0690bc7122c9cd291702b5f36/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L3020

The device-plugin health check is failing because device manager service is initialized, but the device-plugin start is blocked by the delayed updateRuntimeUp. 




### What did you expect to happen?

device-plugin health check should not be expected to pass until kubelet is fully initialized?

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

run kubelet with the recommended watchdog timeout of ~15 seconds, and cause updateRuntimeUp to be blocked on first start.

title: (DRA) Requests field not set for config FromClass in ResourceClaim.status.allocation.devices.config

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

labels.name: wg/device-management
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to WG Device Management.

body:
### What happened?

When creating a ResourceClaim with 2 requests with 2 different device class that have a config, the config reported in the allocation devices status is not mentioning from which request the config is coming from. So the DRA-Drivers cannot identify the configuration belonging to the request it is supposed to handle.
```yaml
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceClaim
metadata:
  name: my-resource-claim
spec:
...
status:
  allocation:
    devices:
      config:
      - opaque:
          driver: resource-driver.example.com
          parameters:
            test: example-0
        source: FromClass
      - opaque:
          driver: resource-driver.example.com
          parameters:
            test: example-1
        source: FromClass
      results:
      - device: eth0
        driver: resource-driver.example.com
        pool: kind-worker2
        request: request0
      - device: eth1
        driver: resource-driver.example.com
        pool: kind-worker2
        request: request1
```

### What did you expect to happen?

For each config with the source as `FromClass`, I would expect the requests field to be set with the list of requests that are using the DeviceClass the config is coming from.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?


```yaml
kubectl apply -n blue -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: DeviceClass
metadata:
  name: deviceclass-0
spec:
  selectors:
  - cel:
      expression: device.driver == "resource-driver.example.com"
  config:
  - opaque:
      driver: resource-driver.example.com
      parameters:
        test: "example-0"
---
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: DeviceClass
metadata:
  name: deviceclass-1
spec:
  selectors:
  - cel:
      expression: device.driver == "resource-driver.example.com"
  config:
  - opaque:
      driver: resource-driver.example.com
      parameters:
        test: "example-1"
---
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceClaim
metadata:
  name: my-resource-claim
spec:
  devices:
    requests:
    - exactly:
        allocationMode: ExactCount
        count: 1
        deviceClassName: deviceclass-0
      name: request0
    - exactly:
        allocationMode: ExactCount
        count: 1
        deviceClassName: deviceclass-1
      name: request1
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: demo
  labels:
    app: demo
spec:
  containers:
  - name: alpine
    image: alpine:latest
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    command:
    - sleep
    - infinity
  resourceClaims:
  - name: my-resource-claim
    resourceClaimTemplateName: my-resource-claim
EOF
```

title: Event metadata for node reboot events is wrong

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon

body:
### What happened?

A node reboot event looks like this:
```
$ k get event kind-control-plane.186cd0d5e2253993 -oyaml
apiVersion: v1
count: 1
eventTime: null
firstTimestamp: "2025-10-09T11:59:31Z"
involvedObject:
  kind: Node
  name: kind-control-plane
  uid: kind-control-plane
kind: Event
lastTimestamp: "2025-10-09T11:59:31Z"
message: 'Node kind-control-plane has been rebooted, boot id: fda92249-bc38-49ea-b0c7-e664b214e43e'
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2025-10-09T11:59:34Z"
  name: kind-control-plane.186cd0d5e2253993
  namespace: default
  resourceVersion: "28264"
  uid: 7be02699-db88-4886-ae5c-f47be0b0c30c
reason: Rebooted
reportingComponent: kubelet
reportingInstance: kind-control-plane
source:
  component: kubelet
  host: kind-control-plane
type: Warning
```

This is missing `involvedObject.apiVersion`  and has the `uid` set to the name of the node rather than the uid.
This seems to be caused by using a `nodeRef` in the recorder as opposed to an actual node object: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3a53784ecbe4bed2aa0cbc159acbb56add05eef9/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_node_status.go#L646

/sig node

Correctly set involvedObject.apiVersion and uid fields

body:
### Which jobs are failing?

`ci-node-crio-swap-serial`

### Which tests are failing?

```
[sig-node] user namespaces kubeconfig tests [LinuxOnly] [Feature:UserNamespacesSupport] [Serial] test config using userNamespaces.idsPerPod honors idsPerPod in userns pods
```

`k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e_node/user_namespaces_test.go:71`

### Since when has it been failing?

Observed in job run [2034607623600345088](https://gcsweb.k8s.io/gcs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-swap-serial/2034607623600345088/artifacts/e2-standard-2-fedora-coreos-43-20260301-3-1-gcp-x86-64-117cbc54/).

### Testgrid link

N/A

### Reason for failure (if possible)

> **Note:** The following analysis is AI-summarized from the linked CI logs and source code.

The kubelet fatally crashes during restart when `userNamespaces.idsPerPod` is changed and a pod created with the previous `idsPerPod` value still has its directory on disk.

**Failing log line** (from [kubelet.log](https://gcsweb.k8s.io/gcs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-swap-serial/2034607623600345088/artifacts/e2-standard-2-fedora-coreos-43-20260301-3-1-gcp-x86-64-117cbc54/kubelet.log)):
```
E0319 12:51:56.731779  8547 run.go:72] "command failed" err="failed to run Kubelet: failed to create kubelet:
  create user namespace manager: record pod mappings for existing pod \"5982517a-d29a-4eae-887d-773f1f8a0548\":
  wrong user namespace length 131072"
```

**Sequence of events:**

1. The test sets `userNamespaces.idsPerPod = 131072` (65536 × 2) and restarts the kubelet.
2. A pod with `hostUsers: false` is created. The kubelet allocates a user namespace mapping with `length = 131072` and persists it to the pod's `userns` file on disk.
3. The pod succeeds and the test deletes it.
4. The AfterEach restores the original kubelet config (default `idsPerPod = 65536`) and restarts the kubelet.
5. During initialization, `MakeUserNsManager()` scans existing pod directories on disk (`pkg/kubelet/userns/userns_manager.go:185-190`). It finds the not-yet-cleaned-up pod directory, reads its `userns` file (which has `length = 131072`), and calls `record()`.
6. `record()` (`pkg/kubelet/userns/userns_manager.go:242-243`) performs a strict equality check:
   ```go
   if length != m.userNsLength {
       return fmt.Errorf("wrong user namespace length %v", length)
   }
   ```
   This fails because `131072 != 65536`, and the error is fatal — the kubelet never starts.
7. The AfterEach times out after 120s waiting for the kubelet health check, and the test is marked as FAILED.

**Impact:** This also means that outside of tests, changing `idsPerPod` in a kubelet config and restarting the kubelet will crash the kubelet if any pods using the old value still have directories on disk. The strict check in `record()` does not account for pods that were created with a different `idsPerPod`.

body:
### What happened?

After I create a pod using a Kubernetes deployment in an empty Kind cluster, I see an in-place update event that seems unnecessary:

```bash
kubectl get events --watch -A

default              0s          Normal    ResizeCompleted           pod/hamster-deployment-57445548f6-r27rn          Pod resize completed: {"containers":[{"name":"hamster1","resources":{"requests":{"cpu":"10m","memory":"10Mi"}}},{"name":"hamster2","resources":{}},{"name":"hamster3","resources":{}}],"generation":1}
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I don't expect to see an in-place update after deploying the pod to the cluster.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```bash
KIND_VERSION="kindest/node:v1.35.0@sha256:452d707d4862f52530247495d180205e029056831160e22870e37e3f6c1ac31f"

kind create cluster --image=${KIND_VERSION} --config <(cat <<EOF
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
featureGates:
  "InPlacePodLevelResourcesVerticalScaling": true
  "NodeDeclaredFeatures": true
EOF
)
```

```yaml
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: hamster
  name: hamster-deployment
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: hamster
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: hamster
    spec:
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu: 100m
          memory: 100Mi
      containers:
      - name: hamster1

      - image: registry.k8s.io/pause:3.1
        name: hamster2
      - image: registry.k8s.io/pause:3.1
        name: hamster3
EOF
```

body:
### What happened?

When a container's `restartPolicyRules[].exitCodes.values` length exceeds 255 elements, the validation error message says:

```bash
containers[0].restartPolicyRules[0].exitCodes.values: Too long: may not be more than 255 bytes
```

The validation uses field.TooLong (byte length checks) instead of field.TooMany (slice length checks).

### What did you expect to happen?

The field is []int32, and the length limit is at most 255 elements, not 255 bytes.
If I am not wrong, I think the correct error message should be:
```bash
containers[0].restartPolicyRules[0].exitCodes.values: Too many: 256: must have at most 255 items
```

title: Some crashed or OOMKilled containers fail to restart in v1.35

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon

body:
### What happened?

After upgrading Kubernetes from v1.34.2 to v1.35.0, we observed a scenario where a pod with multiple containers does not restart a crashed application container, leaving the pod in an Error state indefinitely.

This behavior was not observed on v1.34.2. Reverting the kubelet back to v1.34.2 causes the issue to disappear.

**Observed Behavior:**
The main container terminates but never restarts:
```
State:          Terminated
  Reason:       Error
  Exit Code:    2
  Started:      Tue, 27 Jan 2026 16:11:01 +0000
  Finished:     Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:08:55 +0000
Ready:          False
Restart Count:  0
```

The sidecar container continues to run normally:
```
State:          Running
Started:        Tue, 27 Jan 2026 16:10:54 +0000
Ready:          True
Restart Count:  0
```

Pod conditions show:
```
Conditions:
  Type                        Status
  PodReadyToStartContainers   True
  Initialized                 True
  Ready                       False
  ContainersReady             False
  PodScheduled                True
```

No useful logs or errors appear in `kubectl describe pod` output, events, or `kubelet` logs.

**Notes:**
- This issue seems to only affect pods with more than one container
- We are unsure whether it's just pods with an `initContainer` or does it also apply to `container` sidecars
- Manually killing the process in the sidecar container or deleting the pod helps getting it back to working state
- `RestartAllContainersOnContainerExits` is not enabled

**Possibly related?**
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134345

### What did you expect to happen?

Containers should reliably restart every time they crash.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The best way we found to reproduce this is by running a pod with 2 containers: an initContainer with `restartPolicy: Always` and an application container that we manually crash with `kill 1` command.
It might not work right first time, but we managed to reproduce this multiple times getting pods stuck in Error state that they never recover from automatically.

title: Container fail to create when env var contains $ followed by non-ASCII character (invalid UTF-8 gRPC error)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon

labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a regression from a prior release.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened? After upgrading our Kubernetes cluster from v1.33.5 to v1.34.2 (AWS EKS), pods scheduled on nodes running v1.34.2 fail during container creation with the following error: ```bash grpc: error while marshaling: string field contains invalid UTF-8 ``` The pods are created successfully, but containers fail to create. Important observation: Pods scheduled on nodes still running v1.33.5 continue to work correctly with the same manifests and environment variables. The failure occurs only on nodes upgraded to v1.34.2, strongly indicating a regression. Through isolation and testing, we observed that the failure occurs when an environment variable value contains a $ immediately followed by a non-ASCII character. This behaviour did not occur on v1.33.5 and appears to be a regression introduced in v1.34.x. ### What did you expect to happen? Pods and containers should start successfully when environment variable values contain valid UTF-8 characters, including non-ASCII characters and literal $ characters. This configuration worked as expected on v1.33.5 nodes, even within the same cluster during a rolling upgrade. ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? 1. Create a pod (or deployment) with an environment variable containing: - a $ - immediately followed by a non-ASCII UTF-8 character 3. Schedule the pod on a v1.34.2 node 4. Observe container creation failure with: - `grpc: error while marshaling: string field contains invalid UTF-8` Minimal reproducible example: ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: utf8-env-repro spec: containers: - name: test image: busybox command: ["sh", "-c", "echo started && sleep 3600"] env: - name: TEST_ENV value: "$£FOO" ``` Observed result: ❌ Fails on v1.34.2 nodes ✅ Works on v1.33.5 nodes Expected result: Container starts normally on all versions. ### Anything else we need to know? - We run a custom CRD/operator that propagates env vars from the CR spec into Deployments and multi-container Pods. - The failure occurs after Pod creation, during container creation / runtime interaction. - This reproduces across all containers in the pod that receive the env var. - This is reproducible in a mixed-version cluster: - Pods on v1.33.5 nodes work - Pods on v1.34.2 nodes fail ### Kubernetes version
```console $ kubectl version Client Version: v1.32.0 Kustomize Version: v5.5.0 Server Version: v1.34.2-eks-b3126f4 WARNING: version difference between client (1.32) and server (1.34) exceeds the supported minor version skew of +/-1 ```
### Cloud provider
AWS EKS Cluster upgrade from v1.33.5 → v1.34.2

title: [kubelet] Unnecessary continuous reconciliation loop for DRA Pods due to non-kubelet-owned fields comparison

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.
