labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to WG Device Management.

body:
new: add test and log for kubelet (Kubernetes v1.35.0).

### What happened?

For Pods using Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA), the kubelet status manager continuously logs "Pod status is inconsistent with cached status" and triggers a reconciliation loop (needsReconcile -> syncPod, every ~10s). This loop is unnecessary because no actual status changes are applied, but it adds avoidable load on kubelet, API server, and etcd.
kubelet log -v=4
```
I0115 16:58:36.998365  584662 status_manager.go:262] "Syncing all statuses"
I0115 16:58:36.999471  584662 status_manager.go:1175] "Pod status is inconsistent with cached status for pod, a reconciliation should be triggered" pod="default/dp-e7c13e09e5-5b4fd7bb6d-f95kc" statusDiff=<
	@@ -183,11 +183,5 @@
	    }
	   }
	  ],
	- "qosClass": "Guaranteed",
	- "resourceClaimStatuses": [
	-  {
	-   "name": "test-kubelet",
	-   "resourceClaimName": "dp-e7c13e09e5-5b4fd7bb6d-f95kc-test-kubelet-nh64j"
	-  }
	- ]
	+ "qosClass": "Guaranteed"
	 }
 >
I0115 16:58:36.999523  584662 kubelet_pods.go:1223] "Clean up pod workers for terminated pods"
......
I0115 16:58:37.002499  584662 status_manager.go:1065] "Patch status for pod" pod="default/dp-e7c13e09e5-5b4fd7bb6d-f95kc" podUID="d949fbdc-23b5-4a50-b57b-31ea53189032" patch="{\"metadata\":{\"uid\":\"d949fbdc-23b5-4a50-b57b-31ea53189032\"}}"
I0115 16:58:37.002510  584662 status_manager.go:1072] "Status for pod is up-to-date" pod="default/dp-e7c13e09e5-5b4fd7bb6d-f95kc" statusVersion=2
......
I0115 16:58:46.998609  584662 status_manager.go:262] "Syncing all statuses"
I0115 16:58:46.998627  584662 kubelet.go:2685] "SyncLoop (housekeeping)"
I0115 16:58:46.999152  584662 status_manager.go:1175] "Pod status is inconsistent with cached status for pod, a reconciliation should be triggered" pod="default/dp-e7c13e09e5-5b4fd7bb6d-f95kc" statusDiff=<
	@@ -183,11 +183,5 @@
	    }
	   }
	  ],
	- "qosClass": "Guaranteed",
	- "resourceClaimStatuses": [
	-  {
	-   "name": "test-kubelet",
	-   "resourceClaimName": "dp-e7c13e09e5-5b4fd7bb6d-f95kc-test-kubelet-nh64j"
	-  }
	- ]
	+ "qosClass": "Guaranteed"
	 }
 >
```


### What did you expect to happen?

The kubelet should ignore non-kubelet-owned fields (ResourceClaimStatuses, ExtendedResourceClaimStatus) during status comparison, and not trigger unnecessary reconciliation loops for DRA Pods.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Deploy a Kubernetes cluster with DRA enabled.
2. Create a Pod that uses DRA resources (with ResourceClaim).
3. Observe the kubelet logs and API server/etcd load.
4. Find the continuous "status inconsistent" logs and repeated reconciliation operations.

### Anything else we need to know?

This issue is caused by the `isPodStatusByKubeletEqual` function comparing the entire Pod status, including fields that are not managed by kubelet (populated by control plane components). A fix is provided in PR #136238.

body:
Currently, some components in Kubernetes have been migrated (or partially migrated) to [contextual logging](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-instrumentation/3077-contextual-logging/README.md). However, an incorrect pattern was introduced during the migration: Error-level logs are being called with verbosity methods (e.g., .V()).

The underlying package go-logr/logr, which contextual logging relies on, ignores the verbosity level when printing Error-level logs. For example, in the statement `logger.V(8).Error(nil, "Readiness probe already exists for container", "pod", klog.KObj(pod), "containerName", c.Name)`, the error log will be printed regardless of the verbosity level set.

This can lead to error log flooding, which may hinder users' ability to review normal logs for troubleshooting. More critically, according to the [Kubernetes logging policy](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-instrumentation/logging.md#what-method-to-use), logs should only be recorded when the information requires action from an administrator. This directly contradicts the practice of setting verbosity levels for Error logs, as administrators using the default logging level might miss these actionable errors. Therefore, these instances need to be fixed.

Using grep, I identified the following instances in the k/k repository where verbosity levels are incorrectly set for Error logs.
- [ ] /pkg/controller/garbagecollector https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136040
```
./pkg/controller/garbagecollector/garbagecollector.go:363:			logger.V(5).Error(err, "error syncing item", "item", n.identity)
./pkg/controller/garbagecollector/graph_builder.go:225:		logger.V(4).Error(err, "unable to use a shared informer", "resource", resource, "kind", kind)
```

```

title: DRA: allocator clears DeviceAllocationConfiguration.Requests too aggressively, widening a per-request config to the whole claim

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

labels.name: wg/device-management
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to WG Device Management.

body:
### What happened?

The DRA structured allocator post-processes allocated configs to drop a `DeviceAllocationConfiguration.Requests` list to `nil` when the config "applies to all requests" (the *empty means all* semantic). It decides this with a length comparison:

```go

for i := range allocationResult.Devices.Config {
    if len(allocationResult.Devices.Config[i].Requests) == len(claim.Spec.Devices.Requests) {
        allocationResult.Devices.Config[i].Requests = nil
    }
}
```

`len(config.Requests) == len(claim.Spec.Devices.Requests)` is **not** equivalent to "this config covers every request in the claim", because `config.Requests` entries may be sub-request references of the form `"<request>/<subRequest>"`  the allocator matches them that way a few lines earlier:

```go
subRequestName := fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s", request.Name, subRequest.Name)
if slices.Contains(config.Requests, subRequestName) { ... }
```

A config that references **N sub-requests of a single parent request** has `len(config.Requests) == N`. If the claim has **N top-level requests**, the lengths match even though the config covers only one of them  so its `Requests` is cleared and the config is silently re-scoped to **every** request in the claim.

The same defect is present in all three production implementations:
- `staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/structured/internal/experimental/allocator_experimental.go` (the cleanup loop)
- `staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/structured/internal/incubating/allocator_incubating.go`
- `staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/structured/internal/stable/allocator_stable.go`

### What did you expect to happen?

A config that references only sub-requests of one request should remain scoped to that request. `Requests` should be cleared to `nil` (the "applies to all" form) only when the config actually covers **all** top-level requests in the claim.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Add this case to the shared table in `staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/structured/internal/allocatortesting/allocator_testing.go` (`TestAllocator`) and run `go test ./structured/internal/experimental/ -run 'TestAllocator/repro-config-subrequests-not-all'` (fails identically for `incubating` and `stable`):

```go
"repro-config-subrequests-not-all": {
    features: Features{PrioritizedList: true},
    claimsToAllocate: objects(
        claim(claim0).withRequests(
            requestWithPrioritizedList(req0,
                subRequest(subReq0, classA, 1),
                subRequest(subReq1, classB, 1),
            ),
            deviceRequest(req1, classA, 1), // second top-level request, unrelated to the config
        ).withConfigs(objects(
            // references BOTH sub-requests of req0 only; must NOT apply to req1
            deviceClaimConfig([]string{req0SubReq0, req0SubReq1}, deviceConfiguration(driverA, "foo")),
        )),
    ),
    classes: objects(class(classA, driverA), class(classB, driverB)),
    slices: unwrapResourceSlices(sliceWithDevices(slice1, node1, pool1, driverA,
        device(device1, nil, nil), device(device2, nil, nil),
    )),
    node: node(node1, region1),
    expectResults: []any{allocationResultWithConfigs(
        localNodeSelector(node1),
        objects(
            deviceAllocationResult(req0SubReq0, driverA, pool1, device1, false),
            deviceAllocationResult(req1, driverA, pool1, device2, false),
        ),
        []resourceapi.DeviceAllocationConfiguration{{
            Source:              resourceapi.AllocationConfigSourceClaim,
            Requests:            []string{req0SubReq0, req0SubReq1}, // expected: stays scoped to req0
            DeviceConfiguration: deviceConfiguration(driverA, "foo"),
        }},
    )},
},
```

Device allocation comes out exactly as expected (`req-0/subReq-0` → `device-1`, `req-1` → `device-2`); the **only** difference is the config scope:

```text
expected: Requests: ["req-0/subReq-0", "req-0/subReq-1"]
actual:   Requests: nil      # == applies to ALL requests, including the unrelated req-1
```

title: CreateContainerError when secret env var contains invalid UTF-8 bytes (gRPC strict validation regression)

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: kind/regression
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a regression from a prior release.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

Pods fail with `CreateContainerError` and the following event (events.k8s.io/v1) message:

```
Error: grpc: error while marshaling: string field contains invalid UTF-8
```

When an environment variable sourced from a Kubernetes Secret contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8. The kubelet passes the raw secret bytes as a protobuf `string` field in the CRI `CreateContainerRequest` to containerd. Since gRPC v1.72+ (bundled in k8s 1.34) enforces strict UTF-8 validation on `string` fields, the container creation is rejected.

This is distinct from #136323 / #136325 which fixed env var *expansion* truncating multi-byte UTF-8 characters. That fix does not address this case - here the secret value itself contains raw bytes that were never valid UTF-8 in the first place.

The same pods work on kubelet v1.33.7 nodes in the same cluster because the older gRPC version did not enforce UTF-8 validation on string fields. This is a silent behavioral regression with no warning or migration path.

### What did you expect to happen?

Either:

1. The kubelet should validate secret values for UTF-8 correctness before sending them over CRI gRPC, and emit a clear warning/event identifying which env var contains the invalid value.
2. The CRI protobuf definition should use `bytes` instead of `string` for env var values (since secrets are fundamentally binary).
3. At minimum, the error message should identify which specific environment variable contains the invalid UTF-8, rather than the opaque gRPC marshaling error.

Currently there is no indication of which env var is problematic, making debugging difficult.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```bash
# 1. Create a secret containing invalid UTF-8 bytes
#    \xc3\x28 is an incomplete UTF-8 sequence (0xC3 expects a continuation byte 0x80-0xBF, not 0x28)
python3 -c "
import base64
invalid_bytes = b'hello\xc3\x28world'
encoded = base64.b64encode(invalid_bytes).decode()
manifest = f'''apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: utf8-invalid-secret
  namespace: default
data:
  test-key: {encoded}
'''
print(manifest)
" | kubectl apply -f -

# 2. Create a pod that uses this secret as an env var
kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: utf8-test-invalid
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - name: test
    image: busybox:latest
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
    env:
    - name: BAD_VAR
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: utf8-invalid-secret
          key: test-key
  restartPolicy: Never
EOF

# 3. Observe the pod enters CreateContainerError
kubectl get pod utf8-test-invalid
# NAME                READY   STATUS                 RESTARTS   AGE
# utf8-test-invalid   0/1     CreateContainerError   0          14s

kubectl describe pod utf8-test-invalid | grep -A2 "Warning.*Failed"
# Warning  Failed  kubelet  Error: grpc: error while marshaling: string field contains invalid UTF-8
```

Note: The same secret and pod spec works without error on k8s 1.33 nodes (older gRPC without strict UTF-8 enforcement).

title: In-place container memory resize does not work when pod is in status OOMKilled

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon

body:
### What happened?

I have a pod which is in status `OOMKilled`. I want to give the container more memory by doing an in-place container resource resize. Despite the pod having enough memory after the resize, it stays in an OOM crash loop and does not recover.

### What did you expect to happen?

I would have expected that after the resize, the pod recovers and it starts up correctly.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I'm attaching a standalone application which allows reproducing the bug, please follow the `README` in [memhog.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27365175/memhog.zip).

### Anything else we need to know?

- I stumbled upon this issue when trying to use in-place updates with the VPA controller. This bug made it fail but the problem is not specific to VPA which is why I'm reporting it here.
- The problem only occurs if the pod is in the status `OOMKilled` when the resize command is run.
- The new memory is set correctly in the cgroup of the **container**. You can see that in the logs of the pod.
- The new memory is **NOT** set correctly in the cgroup of the **pod**. Please check the `README` of the attached example where I show how I checked the cgroup memory on pod level.
- I have the same problem when using AWS EKS (v1.35), where I initially encountered it. The behaviour is the same as on K3d.

title: [sig-node] Summary API should report resource usage through the stats api failing on ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-alpha-features

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### Which jobs are failing?

`ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-alpha-features`

Example run: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-alpha-features/2044318744003481600

### Which tests are failing?

`[sig-node] Summary API [NodeConformance] when querying /stats/summary should report resource usage through the stats api`

Fails on both COS and Ubuntu nodes with:
```
.Pods[...::stats-busybox-{0,1}].Containers[busybox-container].CPU.UsageNanoCores:
    Expected <uint64>: 0 to be >= <int>: 10000
.Pods[...::stats-busybox-{0,1}].CPU.UsageNanoCores:
    Expected <uint64>: 0 to be >= <int>: 10000
```

### Since when has it been failing?

All available runs (90+) are failing, going back to at least `v1.36.0-alpha.0.647` (build 2011700799951867904).

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-containerd#cos-cgroupv2-containerd-node-e2e-alpha-features

### Reason for failure (if possible)

The job runs with `AllAlpha=true`, which enables `PodAndContainerStatsFromCRI=true`. This causes the kubelet to fetch stats via `ListPodSandboxStats` from containerd (built from main branch).

Containerd returns `UsageNanoCores` as a non-nil `UInt64Value{Value: 0}` rather than computing the actual value or leaving the field nil. Because the kubelet sees a non-nil value, it trusts it and bypasses its own cache-based delta computation (`cri_stats_provider.go:1002-1003`, `1026-1027`) that would correctly calculate nanocores from `UsageCoreNanoSeconds`.

The fix could be:
1. **containerd**: compute `UsageNanoCores` from the cgroup CPU delta, or leave the field nil so the kubelet's fallback kicks in.
2. **kubelet**: treat `UsageNanoCores.Value == 0` as "not provided" and fall through to the cache-based computation.
3. **test**: relax pod/container CPU expectations to allow 0 when `PodAndContainerStatsFromCRI` is enabled, similar to what was already done for system containers at `summary_test.go:105`.

### Anything else we need to know?

The system container CPU expectation already allows zero at `summary_test.go:105`:
```go
"UsageNanoCores": gomega.SatisfyAny(gstruct.PointTo(gomega.BeZero()), bounded(10000, 2e9)),
```
But pod container (`summary_test.go:184`) and pod-level (`summary_test.go:235`) expectations strictly require `bounded(10000, 1e9)`.

### Relevant SIG(s)

/sig node

title: MemoryQoS TieredReservation: pod-level memory.low is not updated on a request-only in-place memory resize

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

With `memoryReservationPolicy: TieredReservation`, an in-place resize that changes only the memory request updates the container's `memory.low` but leaves the pod cgroup's `memory.low` at the old request. It doesn't recover on later syncs.

Measured on v1.37.0 (kind, containerd, cgroup v2), Burstable pod, limit 512Mi:

| step | container memory.low | pod memory.low | pod memory.max |
|---|---|---|---|
| created, request 256Mi | 268435456 | 268435456 | 536870912 |
| request-only resize to 400Mi | 419430400 | **268435456** | 536870912 |
| 90s later | 419430400 | **268435456** | 536870912 |
| limit resize to 768Mi | 419430400 | 419430400 | 805306368 |

A limit resize does refresh the pod-level value (that was fixed in #140262), so the gap is only the request-only case.

### What did you expect to happen?

Pod-level `memory.low` should follow the pod's memory request after a request-only resize, as it does after a limit resize. KEP-2570 says that after an in-place resize, `memory.min`/`memory.low` "are recalculated during the next cgroup reconciliation cycle" ([KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/2570-memory-qos)).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```yaml
# kind node, KubeletConfiguration
featureGates: {MemoryQoS: true}
memoryThrottlingFactor: 0.9
memoryReservationPolicy: TieredReservation
```

Create a pod with memory request 256Mi and limit 512Mi, then:

```sh
kubectl patch pod b --subresource resize -p '{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"b","resources":{"requests":{"memory":"400Mi","cpu":"100m"},"limits":{"memory":"512Mi"}}}]}}'
# read memory.low in the pod cgroup (kubepods-burstable-pod<uid>.slice) on the node

### Anything else we need to know?

`setPodCgroupConfig` in `doPodResizeAction` returns early on a request-only memory resize ("Memory requests aren't written to cgroups"), but TieredReservation derives pod-level `memory.low` from the request, and nothing rewrites it later. The v1.38 `Soft`/`Hard` policies (kubernetes/enhancements#6362) go through the same path.

title: MemoryQoS: container memory.high is not reset when an in-place resize makes the memory request equal the limit

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

With MemoryQoS on and a `memoryThrottlingFactor` set, I resized a Burstable container's memory request up to its limit in place. The container kept the `memory.high` computed for its previous request, so it stays throttled below its limit. It doesn't recover on later syncs.

Measured on v1.37.0 (kind, containerd, cgroup v2, `memoryThrottlingFactor: 0.9`), container with limit 512Mi:

| memory request | container memory.high |
|---|---|
| 256Mi (created) | 510025728 |
| 400Mi (resize) | 525123584 (recomputed, correct) |
| 512Mi = limit (resize) | 525123584 (stale, should be `max`) |
| 90s later | 525123584 |

I saw the same on v1.36.1.

### What did you expect to happen?

When request equals limit the kubelet deliberately doesn't set `memory.high`, so after the resize the container should end up with `memory.high=max`, the same as a container created with request == limit.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```yaml
# kind node, KubeletConfiguration
featureGates: {MemoryQoS: true}
memoryThrottlingFactor: 0.9
```

```sh
kubectl run a --image=registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10 \
  --overrides='{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"a","image":"registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10","resources":{"requests":{"memory":"256Mi","cpu":"100m"},"limits":{"memory":"512Mi"}}}]}}'
kubectl patch pod a --subresource resize -p '{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"a","resources":{"requests":{"memory":"512Mi","cpu":"100m"},"limits":{"memory":"512Mi"}}}]}}'
# then read memory.high in the container's cgroup on the node
```

### Anything else we need to know?

I think the cause is in `generateLinuxContainerResources`. With MemoryQoS enforced, `memory.high` is added to `Unified` only when `memoryRequest != memoryLimitSpec` (and `memoryHigh > memoryRequest`). Otherwise the key is simply absent, and the runtime leaves an absent key untouched on `UpdateContainerResources`; CRI-O copies only the keys it's given. The MemoryQoS-off branch already writes `memory.high=max` for exactly this stale-after-resize reason, but the MemoryQoS-on branch has no equivalent.

This matters for VPA-driven resizes: a VPA `RequestsOnly` policy produces request == limit whenever the target is above the limit (kubernetes/autoscaler#9926).

body:
### What happened?

While implementing and testing https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137633; I realized that `admission.VersionedAttributes` does not override the `GetOldObject` method, which is used for admission webhooks. This means that the embedded `admission.Attributes`' `GetOldObject()` method actually becomes used, and returns the internal object (if core type) or previously stored (if CRD).

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/90b175c8760fcdfea7b9757fb3c366bbe1d4a1fa/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/conversion.go#L55-L60

/sig api-machinery

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected `GetOldObject` to be implemented for `VersionedAttributed`, so that the versioned old object is returned, not the unversioned one. It should work similarly to `GetObject`

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Example integration test, that was failing before overriding `GetOldObject` correctly: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141959/changes/3e9a132e3f7b8cfbb12189a4671289ab7aec5488

title: Kubelet emits spurious Pod status updates due to nondeterministic allocated resource health ordering

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

With `ResourceHealthStatus` enabled, kubelet can change the order of entries in `status.containerStatuses[*].allocatedResourcesStatus` even when device and claim health have not changed.

There are two nondeterministic paths in kubelet v1.36.3:

1. The device manager constructs each `ResourceStatus.Resources` slice by iterating a map of device IDs. The same resource IDs can therefore be emitted in a different order on later syncs.
2. The DRA manager rebuilds `AllocatedResourcesStatus` by iterating `resourceStatusMap`. This can reorder device-plugin and claim statuses, for example:

```text
[nvidia.com/gpu, claim:channel]
[claim:channel, nvidia.com/gpu]
```

The resulting Pod status is semantically unchanged but serialized differently. Kubelet treats it as a status change and sends a Pod status update. The API server then stores a new resource version and broadcasts a full `MODIFIED` watch event. This can create continuous status and watch churn for otherwise unchanged Pods.

### What did you expect to happen?

Kubelet should produce a stable `AllocatedResourcesStatus` representation when resource health is unchanged. Both the outer `[]ResourceStatus` and each inner `[]ResourceHealth` should have deterministic ordering, so repeated syncs do not cause unnecessary Pod status updates.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Run kubelet v1.36.3 with `ResourceHealthStatus` enabled.
2. Start a Pod whose container has at least two device-plugin devices and a DRA resource claim with health reporting. Generic test device-plugin and DRA drivers are sufficient.
3. Keep all reported health values unchanged.
4. Trigger or wait for repeated Pod status syncs and watch:

```console
kubectl get pod <pod> -w -o json
```

5. Observe that either:
   - entries in a `ResourceStatus.Resources` slice change order, or
   - entries in `AllocatedResourcesStatus` change order.

The Pod `resourceVersion` advances and a `MODIFIED` watch event is emitted despite no health change.

This can also be reproduced in unit tests by calling the two `UpdateAllocatedResourcesStatus` implementations repeatedly with multiple map entries and asserting that their output is canonical.

### Anything else we need to know?

The relevant v1.36.3 code paths are:

- Device ID map iteration while constructing `ResourceStatus.Resources`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/49c14f82ca9748897f0189be31cbf9c2f4085fc1/pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/manager.go#L1162-L1177
- DRA map iteration while rebuilding `AllocatedResourcesStatus`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/49c14f82ca9748897f0189be31cbf9c2f4085fc1/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/manager.go#L936-L943
- The device-manager-then-DRA call order: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/49c14f82ca9748897f0189be31cbf9c2f4085fc1/pkg/kubelet/cm/container_manager_linux.go#L1135-L1145

A minimal fix is to canonicalize the final status by `ResourceStatus.Name` and each resource list by `ResourceHealth.ResourceID`, with regression tests covering stable output across repeated calls.

/sig node

title: kubelet ignores the configured subordinate ID range for a local kubelet account when getent is not on PATH

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

Follow-up from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135870, which replaced `user.Lookup("kubelet")` with a `getent passwd` shell-out.

[`getentUserExists`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6bb42350227f0a714f4730165e7ba622c69bd99e/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L188-L191) returns early when `LookPath` fails:

```go
getent, err := exec.LookPath("getent")
if err != nil {
	return false, nil // no getent: same as "not configured"
}
```

[The caller](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6bb42350227f0a714f4730165e7ba622c69bd99e/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L151-L158) reads that as "no kubelet account", skips `getsubids` and returns the built-in default range. The account itself is never examined, so a local `/etc/passwd` entry is affected the same way, which is wider than the directory-service case the PR body describes.

Same node, with `getent` on PATH and then off it:

```
getent on PATH   firstID=1048576 rangeLen=8388608
getent off PATH  firstID=65536   rangeLen=4294901760
```

Before 6bb4235 the cgo `user.Lookup` resolved a local account without `getent`, so a node in this state used to get its configured range. I ran the two versions of that branch side by side against a real local account with `getent` off PATH: `user.Lookup` reports the account, `getentUserExists` reports it missing.

### What did you expect to happen?

The configured subordinate IDs to still be used when the account is in `/etc/passwd`, or something in the log saying they were skipped. Today it is a `V(5)` line and no error.

@kginonredhat suggested a fallback during review: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135870#discussion_r3966541751

That shape looks right to me with one adjustment. I would gate it on `exec.ErrNotFound` only, since `LookPath` also returns `ErrDot` alongside a usable path, and swallowing that turns a resolvable `getent` into a missing account.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run from anywhere inside a checkout of master. No root, cleans up after itself.

<details>
<summary>repro.sh</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
W=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$W" pkg/kubelet/zz_getent_repro_test.go' EXIT
mkdir -p "$W/with" "$W/without"

# stand-ins for a node whose /etc/passwd has a kubelet account and whose
# /etc/subuid delegates 1048576/8388608 to it
cat > "$W/with/getent" <<'G'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = passwd ] && [ "$2" = kubelet ] && { echo "kubelet:x:999:999::/var/lib/kubelet:/sbin/nologin"; exit 0; }
exit 2
G
cat > "$W/with/getsubids" <<'G'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = -g ] && shift
[ "$1" = kubelet ] && { echo "0: kubelet 1048576 8388608"; exit 0; }
exit 1
G
chmod +x "$W/with/getent" "$W/with/getsubids"
cp "$W/with/getsubids" "$W/without/"   # same node, only getent is off PATH

cat > pkg/kubelet/zz_getent_repro_test.go <<'T'
package kubelet

import (
	"os"
	"testing"

	"k8s.io/klog/v2/ktesting"
)

func TestGetentRepro(t *testing.T) {
	logger, _ := ktesting.NewTestContext(t)
	t.Setenv("PATH", os.Getenv("REPRO_PATH"))
	first, length, err := (&Kubelet{}).getKubeletMappings(logger, 65536)
	t.Logf("firstID=%d rangeLen=%d err=%v", first, length, err)
}
T

for d in with without; do
	printf -- '--- getent %s PATH ---\n' "$([ "$d" = with ] && echo on || echo off)"
	REPRO_PATH="$W/$d" go test ./pkg/kubelet/ -run '^TestGetentRepro$' -count=1 -v 2>&1 | grep firstID
done
```

</details>

```
--- getent on PATH ---
    zz_getent_repro_test.go:14: firstID=1048576 rangeLen=8388608 err=<nil>
--- getent off PATH ---
    zz_getent_repro_test.go:14: firstID=65536 rangeLen=4294901760 err=<nil>
```

### Anything else we need to know?

Two things a fix would have to deal with.

[`TestGetentUserExists`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6bb42350227f0a714f4730165e7ba622c69bd99e/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods_test.go#L8595-L8598) has a `"getent not installed"` case expecting `wantFound: false`, so that case has to change with the behavior. It also only asserts `found`, never the range `getKubeletMappings` ends up with, which is the part that matters here.

The second one is smaller. [The comment above the lookup](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6bb42350227f0a714f4730165e7ba622c69bd99e/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L145-L150) says the account is checked first so a getsubids backend that is unreachable can be told apart from one that simply has no entry. glibc's `getent` sets exit 2 whenever `getpwnam()` returns NULL without consulting errno, while the cgo `os/user` gave `UnknownUserError` for a genuine miss and a plain error otherwise. So an account-backend error that used to stop kubelet can now arrive as exit 2 and select the default range instead. I have not reproduced a real directory-service outage, so I would treat that as a question about the contract, not a second bug.

I am happy to send the PR if the fallback is the direction people want.

title: kubelet can fail to start when the user namespace ID pool changes while pods with user namespaces exist on the node

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

If the subordinate ID pool kubelet uses for user namespaces changes between restarts, and a pod on disk holds a mapping that falls outside the new pool, the kubelet does not start:

```
create user namespace manager: record pod mappings for existing pod "p": id 7340032 is out of range
```

[`record()`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/79f041dd524968a26c28398be9b5dc30ada1f841/pkg/kubelet/userns/userns_manager.go#L252-L255) rejects a persisted mapping outside the current pool, and [the replay loop](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/79f041dd524968a26c28398be9b5dc30ada1f841/pkg/kubelet/userns/userns_manager.go#L185-L189) returns on the first such pod, so `MakeUserNsManager()` fails and `NewMainKubelet()` with it. As far as I can tell the only ways out are to restore the previous pool or to delete the pod directory by hand, and the message points at neither.

Several ordinary things change the pool. Editing `/etc/subuid` to move kubelet's range does it. So does installing `getsubids` on a node that did not have it, or creating the `kubelet` account on a node where it did not exist, since both move the node from the built-in default range to whatever `getsubids` then reports. None of these involve cgo or #135870; that PR just adds one more way to get here, which is where I ran into it.

Whether a given node survives is luck. Blocks come from `allocator.NewAllocationMap`, which picks at random, so it depends on where the running pod happens to sit relative to the new pool. Going from the default pool to a delegated one is close to a certainty: the default holds 65535 blocks against a typical delegated pool of ~128.

`UserNamespacesSupport` has been GA with `LockToDefault` since 1.36, so the path is active on every Linux kubelet, but only nodes running pods with `hostUsers: false` are affected, since pods without a user namespace write no mapping file and are skipped on replay.

### What did you expect to happen?

Something recoverable. Failing the whole kubelet over one pod whose persisted mapping no longer fits seems heavy next to, say, refusing that pod and saying why, and either way the error could name the pod directory an operator would have to clear.

I do not know which is right, and it overlaps with #140190, which is looking at persisted-mapping replay from the terminal-ID angle and deliberately kept its guard on the allocation side so that older on-disk mappings stay replayable.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Drop this in `pkg/kubelet/userns/` and run `go test ./pkg/kubelet/userns/ -run TestPoolChangeReplay -v`. No cgo, no NSS, no changes to the host.

```go
package userns

import (
	"testing"

	v1 "k8s.io/api/core/v1"
	"k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/types"
	utilfeature "k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/feature"
	featuregatetesting "k8s.io/component-base/featuregate/testing"
	pkgfeatures "k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/features"
	"k8s.io/klog/v2/ktesting"
)

func TestPoolChangeReplay(t *testing.T) {
	logger, _ := ktesting.NewTestContext(t)
	featuregatetesting.SetFeatureGateDuringTest(t, utilfeature.DefaultFeatureGate, pkgfeatures.UserNamespacesSupport, true)

	hostUsers := false
	try := func(label string, fromFirst, fromLen, toFirst, toLen uint32) {
		dir, uid := t.TempDir(), types.UID("p")
		m, err := MakeUserNsManager(logger, &testUserNsPodsManager{podDir: dir, userns: true,
			maxPods: 110, mappingFirstID: fromFirst, mappingLen: fromLen}, nil)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s: %v", label, err)
		}
		pod := &v1.Pod{Spec: v1.PodSpec{HostUsers: &hostUsers}}
		pod.UID = uid
		uns, err := m.GetOrCreateUserNamespaceMappings(logger, pod, "")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s alloc: %v", label, err)
		}
		_, err = MakeUserNsManager(logger, &testUserNsPodsManager{podDir: dir, userns: true,
			maxPods: 110, mappingFirstID: toFirst, mappingLen: toLen,
			podList: []types.UID{uid}}, nil)
		res := "restarts OK"
		if err != nil {
			res = "FAILS: " + err.Error()
		}
		t.Logf("%-42s block %-6d %s", label, uns.GetUids()[0].GetHostId()/65536, res)
	}

	try("subuid range moved 1048576 -> 8388608", 1048576, 8388608, 8388608, 8388608)
	try("subuid range shrunk 128 -> 110 blocks", 1048576, 8388608, 1048576, 7208960)
	try("default pool -> delegated pool", 65536, 4294901760, 1048576, 8388608)
}
```

One run:

```
subuid range moved 1048576 -> 8388608      block 112    FAILS: record pod mappings for existing pod "p": id 7340032 is out of range
subuid range shrunk 128 -> 110 blocks      block 131    FAILS: record pod mappings for existing pod "p": id 8585216 is out of range
default pool -> delegated pool             block 15363  FAILS: record pod mappings for existing pod "p": id 1006829568 is out of range
```

All three depend on where the pod happened to land, so one run understates it. Over 20 runs:

```
subuid range moved 1048576 -> 8388608   19 fail,  1 restarts OK   [16..143] -> [128..255], survives on 16 of 128 blocks
subuid range shrunk 128 -> 110 blocks    2 fail, 18 restart OK    [16..143] -> [16..125],  survives on 110 of 128
default pool -> delegated pool          20 fail,  0 restart OK    [1..65535] -> [16..143], survives on 128 of 65535
```

which matches the geometry in each case. The third row is the one that matters in practice: a node coming from the default pool has roughly a 0.2% chance per userns pod of sitting somewhere a delegated pool can still replay.

### Anything else we need to know?

This is a unit-level reproduction in a checkout rather than something I have watched a real node do. It came out of #135870, where I raised it before @dims suggested splitting it into separate issues, but the PR is a trigger rather than the cause, so it stands on its own.

$ kubectl version
# N/A - reproduced against master at 79f041dd524968a26c28398be9b5dc30ada1f841
# with go1.27.1, not observed on a running cluster.
```

body:
### What happened?

On Kubernetes 1.36, kubelet starts a `NodeWatchResources` health stream for every registered DRA plugin whenever `ResourceHealthStatus` is enabled. It does this even when the plugin does not advertise the optional `DRAResourceHealth` service in its registration response.

When the service is not implemented, kubelet receives `codes.Unimplemented`, logs it as an error, and retries every five seconds:

```text
E0902 21:16:20.306285 manager.go:1045] "Error receiving from WatchResources stream" err="rpc error: code = Unimplemented desc = device health reporting is not supported by this driver" logger="DRA registration handler.dra-manager" pluginName="compute-domain.nvidia.com"
```

`ResourceHealthStatus` is Beta and enabled by default in 1.36, so this occurs on the default feature-gate configuration when a DRA plugin does not implement health reporting.

This does not appear to affect DRA workload correctness, but it continuously emits error-level kubelet logs. At one retry every five seconds, each unsupported plugin produces 17,280 error records per day per node. This creates unnecessary log storage and ingestion costs and makes genuine kubelet errors harder to identify.

### What did you expect to happen?

Kubelet should only start the health stream when the plugin advertises a supported `DRAResourceHealth` service.

If a plugin advertises the service but returns `codes.Unimplemented`, kubelet should treat that as a terminal indication that health reporting is unsupported and stop retrying until the plugin re-registers.

This is the behavior in Kubernetes 1.37.

### How can we reproduce it?

This was reproduced with a kind v1.36.1 cluster using the head of:

https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/pull/1243

The GPU plugin streams health normally when its health reporting feature is enabled. Kubelet nevertheless continues attempting `NodeWatchResources` every five seconds for `compute-domain.nvidia.com`, which does not advertise the health service.

The same driver configuration is quiet on kubelet 1.37.

Full reproduction findings and logs:

https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/issues/1423#issuecomment-5532233065

Although the report uses the NVIDIA DRA driver, the behavior is generic to any DRA plugin that registers without the optional health service.

### Anything else we need to know?

In release-1.36, `RegisterPlugin` receives the plugin's `supportedServices`, but the health stream is started without checking that list:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bf628307442eb90f0c503e6c8f9525bce1f14aa6/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/plugin/dra_plugin_manager.go#L324-L334

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bf628307442eb90f0c503e6c8f9525bce1f14aa6/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/plugin/dra_plugin_manager.go#L387-L407

Kubernetes 1.37 fixed this as part of #139477 by:

- selecting an advertised health service during registration;
- starting the stream only when such a service was advertised;
- stopping retries when the stream returns `codes.Unimplemented`.

This issue is intended to track a targeted backport of that behavior to release-1.36, not the larger v1 health API and kubeletplugin helper changes from #139477.

The proposed 1.36 fix would:

1. Start `NodeWatchResources` only if the plugin advertises `v1alpha1.DRAResourceHealth`.
2. Treat `codes.Unimplemented` as non-error and stop retrying.
3. Add regression tests for an absent health service and an `Unimplemented` stream.

A backport to 1.35 or earlier is not requested because `ResourceHealthStatus` was Alpha and disabled by default there.

cc @shivamerla @guptaNswati @pohly

### Kubernetes version

```console
$ kubectl version
Server Version: v1.36.1
```

The current release-1.36 source remains affected. Kubernetes 1.37 is not affected.

### Cloud provider

kind

### Related plugins

NVIDIA DRA driver, although the kubelet behavior is driver-independent:

https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu/issues/1423

title: [PodLevelResources] In-place Pod resize drops CPU/memory keys from PodStatus.Resources depending on resize dimension

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
### What happened?


After a successful in-place pod resize (`InPlacePodVerticalScaling` + `InPlacePodLevelResourcesVerticalScaling` enabled), `PodStatus.Resources` becomes inconsistent with `PodSpec`, `status.allocatedResources` and `status.containerStatuses[*].resources`.

Depending on *which* resource dimension was resized, `status.resources` loses keys:

* **CPU-only resize** (e.g., `cpu 10m→20m`, `memory 100Mi→100Mi`): `status.resources.limits` loses `cpu` (`limits.memory` remains). Example observed:
  ```yaml
  status:
    resources:
      requests: {cpu: 20m, memory: 100Mi}
      limits: {memory: 100Mi}   # cpu limit MISSING
  ```
  while `spec.container CPU limit = 20m`, `containerStatus CPU limit = 20m`, `Pod allocated CPU = 20m` are all correct.

* **Memory-only resize** (e.g., `cpu 10m→10m`, `memory 100Mi→200Mi`): `status.resources` loses `cpu` entirely:
  ```yaml
  status:
    resources:
      requests: {memory: 200Mi}   # cpu MISSING
      limits: {memory: 200Mi}     # cpu MISSING
  ```

* **CPU+memory resize** can appear correct and even *heal* a previously buggy state, making the bug state-dependent.

The actual cgroup allocation is correct; only `status.resources` is truncated. `status.allocatedResources` and `status.containerStatuses[*].resources` remain correct.

### What did you expect to happen?

Per https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/241138b4469f65f908c50b54094a0e776115d750/staging/src/k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go#L5744 and [KEP-5419](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-node/5419-pod-level-resources-in-place-resize/README.md), `PodStatus.Resources` is the *single source of truth for effective pod-level resources as applied* (cgroup-actuated when Running, spec-derived otherwise). For a Guaranteed pod (`requests == limits` 10m/100Mi) it should always contain both `cpu` and `memory` in `requests` and `limits` and equal the effective pod envelope (or aggregated container sum when pod-level `spec.resources` not set).

After `10m/100Mi → 20m/100Mi` CPU-only resize, expected:
```yaml
status:
  resources:
    requests: {cpu: 20m, memory: 100Mi}
    limits: {cpu: 20m, memory: 100Mi}
```

After `10m/100Mi → 10m/200Mi` memory-only resize, expected:
```yaml
status:
  resources:
    requests: {cpu: 10m, memory: 200Mi}
    limits: {cpu: 10m, memory: 200Mi}
```

Missing keys violate that invariant. Related bug fixed separately: #141606 (events `podResourceSummary` missing pod-level resources).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?


All scenarios use the **same Guaranteed baseline** pod. Use a **fresh pod for each scenario** — do not reuse a pod that has already been resized (bug propagates via `oldPodStatus.Resources`).

### Baseline pod (resize-test.yaml)

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: resize-test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: c1
    image: registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10
    resources:
      requests: {cpu: 10m, memory: 100Mi}
      limits: {cpu: 10m, memory: 100Mi}
```

```bash
kubectl apply -f resize-test.yaml
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/resize-test --timeout=60s
# baseline check — should be complete:
kubectl get pod resize-test -o json | jq '{spec: .spec.containers[0].resources, statusResources: .status.resources, allocated: .status.allocatedResources, cStatus: .status.containerStatuses[0].resources}'
```

**Helper — run after every patch** (bug persists after `ResizeCompleted`, check at 0s,5s,30s):
```bash
kubectl get pod resize-test -o json | jq '{
  spec: .spec.containers[0].resources,
  statusResources: .status.resources,
  allocated: .status.allocatedResources,
  cStatus: .status.containerStatuses[0].resources,
  cAllocated: .status.containerStatuses[0].allocatedResources,
  gen: .metadata.generation
}'
kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=resize-test --sort-by=.lastTimestamp
```

### Scenario A — resize CPU and memory together
```bash
kubectl patch pod resize-test --subresource resize --type merge -p '{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"c1","resources":{"requests":{"cpu":"20m","memory":"200Mi"},"limits":{"cpu":"20m","memory":"200Mi"}}}]}}'
sleep 5; kubectl get pod resize-test -o json | jq .status.resources
# Sometimes correct: {requests: {cpu:20m,memory:200Mi}, limits: {cpu:20m,memory:200Mi}} — masks bug
```

### Scenario B — resize CPU only (memory unchanged)
*Fresh pod `resize-test` (10m/100Mi baseline):*
```bash
kubectl patch pod resize-test --subresource resize --type merge -p '{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"c1","resources":{"requests":{"cpu":"20m","memory":"100Mi"},"limits":{"cpu":"20m","memory":"100Mi"}}}]}}'
sleep 5; kubectl get pod resize-test -o json | jq .status.resources
# BUG: {requests: {cpu:20m,memory:100Mi}, limits: {memory:100Mi}} — limits.cpu MISSING
```

### Scenario C — resize memory only (CPU unchanged)
*Fresh pod (10m/100Mi baseline):*
```bash
kubectl patch pod resize-test --subresource resize --type merge -p '{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"c1","resources":{"requests":{"cpu":"10m","memory":"200Mi"},"limits":{"cpu":"10m","memory":"200Mi"}}}]}}'
sleep 5; kubectl get pod resize-test -o json | jq .status.resources
# BUG: {requests: {memory:200Mi}, limits: {memory:200Mi}} — cpu MISSING entirely
```

### Scenario D — resize CPU+memory again (can heal)
From buggy state (after B or C):
```bash
kubectl patch pod resize-test --subresource resize --type merge -p '{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"c1","resources":{"requests":{"cpu":"20m","memory":"200Mi"},"limits":{"cpu":"20m","memory":"200Mi"}}}]}}'
sleep 5; kubectl get pod resize-test -o json | jq .status.resources
# Observed: CPU reappears: {requests: {cpu:20m,memory:200Mi}, limits: {cpu:20m,memory:200Mi}} — state-dependent
```

### Anything else we need to know?

* **What is NOT broken:** `spec.containers[*].resources`, `spec.resources` (pod-level), `status.containerStatuses[*].resources`/`allocatedResources`, `status.allocatedResources`, and actual cgroup (`cpu.weight`, `memory.max`) are all correct. Verified `cpu.weight` and `crictl` on node.

* **Suspected source:**  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/241138b4469f65f908c50b54094a0e776115d750/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L2202 `convertToAPIPodLevelResourcesStatus` (called from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/241138b4469f65f908c50b54094a0e776115d750/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L2177  when `InPlacePodLevelResourcesVerticalScaling` enabled). Asymmetric handling: memory request has `PodRequests` aggregation fallback when missing https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/241138b4469f65f908c50b54094a0e776115d750/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L2277, CPU request does not; CPU limits guard `> MinMilliCPULimit` can leave `resources.Limits[CPU]` empty without preserving old https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/241138b4469f65f908c50b54094a0e776115d750/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L2296; `preserveOldResourcesValue` copies from `oldPodStatus.Resources` — if old was already missing, missing propagates. `AllocatedResources` at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/241138b4469f65f908c50b54094a0e776115d750/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L2182 via `resourcehelper.PodRequests` is correct.

* **Not expected:** Per KEP-5419, `PodStatus.Resources` is the single source of truth for effective pod-level resources; for Guaranteed it must contain both CPU and memory.

* **Existing fix on this branch:** #141606 events bug (`podResourceSummary` missing pod-level) fixed in `fix/inplace-pod-resize-events-pod-level-resources` — this status bug is separate and should be a new issue/PR after triage.

title: [Failing Test] [sig-auth] Projected PodCertificate conformance test cannot bind port 443 under Restricted Linux settings

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/auth
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Auth.

labels.name: kind/failing-test
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a consistently or frequently failing test.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
### Which jobs are failing?

External Kubernetes v1.37.0 certified-conformance run.

This is not an upstream Kubernetes CI job. The failure is deterministic on Linux nodes using the default privileged-port setting:
`  net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=1024.`

### Which tests are failing?

[sig-auth] Projected PodCertificate [FeatureGate:PodCertificateRequest] [FeatureGate:ClusterTrustBundle] [FeatureGate:ClusterTrustBundleProjection] should allow server and client pods to establish an mTLS connection [MinimumKubeletVersion:1.37] [Conformance]

### Since when has it been failing?

 Observed recently during a Kubernetes v1.37.0 certified-conformance run.

The affected test configuration was introduced during the Pod Certificates beta e2e work in September 2025 and promoted to conformance for v1.37.

### Testgrid link

_No response_

### Reason for failure (if possible)

The test server container fails before the mTLS handshake:

`E0901 ... error while serving: while listening: listen tcp 0.0.0.0:443: bind: permission denied
`
The test creates the server with a Restricted security context (non-root, all capabilities dropped) but configures agnhost to listen on privileged port 443. On Linux with the default per-network-namespace setting:

 ```
 net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start = 1024
  CapEff: 0000000000000000
```

  binding port 443 requires root or CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE.

  The client therefore receives:

`  dial tcp <service-cluster-ip>:443: connect: connection refused
`
Validated fix: change the server listener to 8443 and explicitly set the Service targetPort to 8443 while retaining Service port 443. The original focused e2e test then passes with the actual PodCertificateRequest, ClusterTrustBundle projection, and mTLS flow.

### Anything else we need to know?

 ## Summary

  The v1.37 conformance test:

  [sig-auth] Projected PodCertificate ... should allow server and client pods to establish an mTLS connection

  fails deterministically on Linux nodes using the normal privileged-port boundary.

  The test creates the server with a Restricted security context, which runs it
  non-root with all capabilities dropped, while configuring agnhost to listen on
  `0.0.0.0:443`.

  ## Reproduction

  Kubernetes: v1.37.0
  OS: Oracle Linux 8.10
  Kernel: 5.15.0-322.203.3.5.el8uek.x86_64
  Runtime: CRI-O 1.36.3

  On each node, a Restricted non-root diagnostic pod reported:

  ```text
  /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_unprivileged_port_start: 1024
  CapEff: 0000000000000000

  The e2e server log:

  error while serving: while listening: listen tcp 0.0.0.0:443: bind: permission denied

  The client consequently reports:

  dial tcp <service-cluster-ip>:443: connect: connection refused

  ## Expected behavior

  The conformance test should pass on Linux nodes using the default privileged
  port boundary, without requiring a provider to relax it cluster-wide.

  ## Root cause

  test/e2e/auth/projected_podcertificate.go builds a Restricted security
  context, drops capabilities, and configures:

  "--listen=0.0.0.0:443",

  The Service has port 443 with no explicit targetPort, so it defaults to 443.

  ## Proposed fix

  Keep the Service port and client URL at 443, but use an unprivileged backend
  port:

  + "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/intstr"

  - "--listen=0.0.0.0:443",
  + "--listen=0.0.0.0:8443",

  - Ports: []v1.ServicePort{{Name: "https", Port: 443}},
  + Ports: []v1.ServicePort{{
  +   Name:       "https",
  +   Port:       443,
  +   TargetPort: intstr.FromInt(8443),
  + }},

  ## Validation

  We reran the original focused Sonobuoy test while applying only those two
  transient object changes. It passed with the real in-process signer,
  PodCertificateRequest issuance, projected certificates, ClusterTrustBundle
  projection, and mTLS assertion:

  passed: 8
  failed: 0
  skipped: 3205

### Relevant SIG(s)

/sig auth

title: Pod anti-affinity incorrectly evaluates NotIn namespace selectors

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: kind/regression
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a regression from a prior release.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
### What happened?

A required pod anti-affinity term incorrectly rejects a node when the matching existing pod belongs to a namespace excluded by `namespaceSelector`.

Example:

```yaml
labelSelector:
  matchExpressions:
  - key: example.com/workload-id
    operator: Exists
namespaceSelector:
  matchExpressions:
  - key: kubernetes.io/metadata.name
    operator: NotIn
    values:
    - workload-a
```
Both pods are in workload-a, so the existing pod should be excluded by the namespace selector. Instead, the candidate node is rejected with:

> node(s) didn't match pod anti-affinity rules

### What did you expect to happen?

The existing pod in workload-a should not contribute to anti-affinity evaluation, allowing the candidate pod to schedule on that node.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create namespace workload-a.
2. Run a pod labelled example.com/workload-id on a node.
3. Create another pod in the same namespace with the required pod anti-affinity term above.
4. Restrict the candidate pod to that node.
The candidate pod remains Pending with the anti-affinity error.

### Anything else we need to know?

This regression was introduced by #132457, which changed mergeAffinityTermNamespacesIfNotEmpty from accepting a pointer to accepting a value. The namespace set is updated, but clearing NamespaceSelector only modifies a copy. The negative selector is subsequently evaluated again against empty namespace labels.
Kubernetes 1.34-1.36 are affected. 

Master is not affected because #138198 restored pointer-based mutation.

title: DRA structured allocator overflows the native-int device-count sum in the per-claim limit check

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

labels.name: wg/device-management
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to WG Device Management.

body:
### What happened

The structured allocator adds device counts in native `int` before comparing to `resourceapi.AllocationResultsMaxSize`. `allocateOne` forms `len(results) + requestData.numDevices - r.deviceIndex`, and the pre-flight `Allocate` loop accumulates `minDevicesPerClaim += numDevices`. `DeviceRequest.Count` is validated only as `> 0`, never against the result limit, so several large-but-valid counts sum past the limit and wrap. Two counts of `math.MaxInt/2 + 1` wrap to a negative total, so `total > MaxSize` is false and the check is skipped; four wrap back near zero. A `FirstAvailable` request whose first alternative carries a huge count, sitting behind a device already allocated for the claim, drives the overflowing subtraction and misdirects the backtracking rather than pruning the oversized alternative.

### What you expected to happen

Each request is refused against the remaining capacity before the sum is formed, so no addition overflows and an oversized count is rejected with `number of requested devices exceeds the claim limit`.

### How to reproduce it

A single claim with two `ExactCount` requests of `math.MaxInt/2 + 1` each: the total overflows negative and is admitted today. A `FirstAvailable` request with a first subrequest of `math.MaxInt` behind one already-allocated device: the oversized alternative should be pruned and the small one taken. Both are covered by the tests in #141307, and the fix is applied identically across the stable, incubating, and experimental tiers.

### Anything else we need to know

`math.MaxInt` makes the counts overflow on 32-bit builds as well. This is worth a backport decision for the release branches that already carry the per-claim result-limit check.

### Related

This is the concrete in-tree instance behind #140424, which asks for an upper bound or overflow-safety contract on `DeviceRequest.Count`. #140424 observes that the structured allocator guards the single-count path; the gap here is the multi-count sum on that same path, one large count plus the devices already allocated for the claim, which was not guarded until #141307.

/kind bug
/sig node
/wg device-management

_This issue was written in part with the assistance of generative AI. I checked the allocator paths and the overflow cases against the code and the tests myself._

title: compatibility-versions-feature-gate-test always fails since the 1.37 cut: validator ignores MinCompatibilityVersion

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon

labels.name: sig/api-machinery

labels.name: kind/failing-test
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a consistently or frequently failing test.

labels.name: sig/architecture
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Architecture.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
**What happened**:

The periodic job [`ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-compatibility-versions-feature-gate-test`](https://prow.k8s.io/?job=ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-compatibility-versions-feature-gate-test) has failed on every run since 2026-08-06 12:48 UTC. The failure rate is 100 percent.

The validator reports one failure:

```
Validating features for emulated_version=1.37, current_version=1.38...
FAIL: feature 'DRAFractionalCapacityRange' expected value 1, got 0
```

The trigger is the release-1.37 branch cut, not a code change. The `v1.37.0-rc.0` tag moved master from `v1.37.0-beta.0` to `v1.38.0-alpha.0`. That shifted the version pair the job validates:

| | Build | Time (UTC) | k/k SHA | Validated pair |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Last green | [2085330939616956416](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-compatibility-versions-feature-gate-test/2085330939616956416) | 2026-08-06 11:45 | `4f5591ab57b` | emulated 1.36, current 1.37 |
| First red | [2085346290606018560](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-compatibility-versions-feature-gate-test/2085346290606018560) | 2026-08-06 12:48 | `b882c60b402` | emulated 1.37, current 1.38 |

The commit window holds one commit, `b882c60b402 CHANGELOG: Update directory for v1.37.0-rc.0 release`. It changes only CHANGELOG files, so it is not the cause.

`DRAFractionalCapacityRange` is absent from the `release-1.36` reference list. The job therefore never checked the gate before the cut.

**Root cause**

The kubelet and the control plane report the correct value. The validator expects the wrong one.

`pkg/features/kube_features.go` declares two specs at the same version:

```go
DRAFractionalCapacityRange: {
	{Version: version.MustParse("1.37"), Default: false, PreRelease: featuregate.Beta},
	{Version: version.MustParse("1.37"), Default: true, PreRelease: featuregate.Beta, MinCompatibilityVersion: version.MustParse("1.37")},
},
```

`SetEmulationVersion` sets the minimum compatibility version to `emulated - 1`. See `staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/featuregate/feature_gate.go`. The job passes only `--emulated-version=1.37`, so the minimum compatibility version is 1.36. The second spec needs 1.37 or higher. The runtime therefore selects the first spec and reports `0`. This matches the documented behavior of `MinCompatibilityVersion` and the plan in kubernetes/kubernetes#140594, which schedules the on-by-default promotion for 1.38.

Two problems in the tooling make the validator disagree:

1. The generator `test/compatibility_lifecycle/cmd/feature_gates.go` in kubernetes/kubernetes does not write `minCompatibilityVersion` into `versioned_feature_list.yaml`. In that file the two specs differ only in `default`, so no consumer can tell them apart.

   ```yaml
   - name: DRAFractionalCapacityRange
     versionedSpecs:
     - default: false
       lockToDefault: false
       preRelease: Beta
       version: "1.37"
     - default: true
       lockToDefault: false
       preRelease: Beta
       version: "1.37"
   ```

2. `get_target_spec` in `experiment/compatibility-versions/versioned_specs_util.sh` takes `last` of the matching specs. It selects the `default: true` spec and expects `1`.

`DRAFractionalCapacityRange` is the only feature in kubernetes/kubernetes that uses `MinCompatibilityVersion`. That is why the problem appears now.

**What you expected to happen**:

The job passes. The validator selects the spec that applies at the minimum compatibility version the job actually runs with.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

```bash
SPECS='[{"default":false,"lockToDefault":false,"preRelease":"Beta","version":"1.37"},
        {"default":true,"lockToDefault":false,"preRelease":"Beta","version":"1.37"}]'

# current get_target_spec behavior
echo "$SPECS" | jq -r --arg ver 1.37 \
  '[ .[] | select((.version|tonumber) <= ($ver|tonumber)) ] | last | .default'
# => true   (validator expects 1)

# what the control plane reports at --emulated-version=1.37
# kubernetes_feature_enabled{name="DRAFractionalCapacityRange",stage="BETA"} 0
```

**Please provide links to example occurrences, if any**:

- First red build: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-compatibility-versions-feature-gate-test/2085346290606018560
- Last green build: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-compatibility-versions-feature-gate-test/2085330939616956416
- TestGrid tab: https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-api-machinery-emulated-version#compatibility-versions-feature-gate-test

Of the 229 builds still in GCS, 150 passed and 79 failed. Every pass is before the boundary. Every failure is after it. No build interleaves, so this is not a flake.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Control that isolates the cause.** The job `ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-compatibility-versions-feature-gate-test-n-2` runs the same validator against the same master build, but it validates emulated 1.36 against current 1.38. It stays green. The break is specific to the 1.37 spec pair.

**Suggested fix, in two parts.**

Part 1 clears CI. Change `get_target_spec` to take the first spec at the highest matching version instead of the last. That selects the spec that applies at the default minimum compatibility version.

```jq
[ .[] | select((.version|sub("^v";"")|tonumber) <= ($ver|sub("^v";"")|tonumber)) ] as $c
| ($c | map(.version|sub("^v";"")|tonumber) | max) as $m
| ($c | map(select((.version|sub("^v";"")|tonumber) == $m)) | first)
```

I checked this against normal features at 1.31, 1.33 and 1.35. The result does not change. The result changes only when two specs share a version.

This part is necessary, not only convenient. The `release-1.37` reference list is frozen. It will never carry `minCompatibilityVersion`. The validator must therefore fall back to first-wins for the 1.37 pair whatever else changes.

Part 2 prevents the next occurrence. Write `minCompatibilityVersion` from the kubernetes/kubernetes generator, then compare against it in the validator for 1.38 and later.

**Related.** This validator has missed a feature gate lifecycle pattern twice before. See kubernetes/test-infra#34396 and kubernetes/test-infra#35179. Expect the problem to return at the 1.38 cut if the gate is promoted per kubernetes/kubernetes#140594 without matching validator work.

Owner is SIG API Machinery. The alert address on the job is `compatibility-version-test@google.com`. Feature owners are @sunya-ch and @pohly.

title: LimitRange maximum can be exceeded by declaring hugepages at the pod level

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

A `LimitRange` of type `Pod` with a `max` for `hugepages-*` does not constrain a Pod that
declares its hugepages through pod-level resources (`spec.resources`). Such a Pod is admitted
even when its effective hugepages consumption exceeds the configured maximum.

The LimitRanger admission plugin keeps a private copy of the "is this a pod-level resource?"
predicate that lists only cpu and memory:

```go
// plugin/pkg/admission/limitranger/admission.go
var supportedPodLevelResources = sets.New(api.ResourceCPU, api.ResourceMemory)

func isSupportedPodLevelResource(name api.ResourceName) bool {
	return supportedPodLevelResources.Has(name)
}
```

The canonical predicate in component-helpers also matches the `hugepages-` prefix. Because of the
drift, `podRequests`/`podLimits` skip the pod-level override for hugepages and evaluate the
aggregated **container** values instead.

API validation explicitly permits the pod-level value to exceed the container aggregate (it only
rejects the reverse: "pod level limit for %s is insufficient to cover the aggregated container
and node-allocatable DRA limits"), so the two numbers can legitimately differ.

### What did you expect to happen?

The Pod-scoped `LimitRange` maximum should be enforced against the effective pod-level hugepages
value, the same way it is enforced when the value is written at container level.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Requires the `PodLevelResources` feature gate (Beta, on by default since 1.34).

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: hugepages-max
  namespace: demo
spec:
  limits:
    - type: Pod
      max:
        hugepages-2Mi: 4Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: over-the-limit
  namespace: demo
spec:
  resources:                 # pod-level: 8Gi, twice the LimitRange max
    requests:
      hugepages-2Mi: 8Gi
    limits:
      hugepages-2Mi: 8Gi
  containers:
    - name: c1
      image: registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10
      resources:             # container aggregate stays within the max
        requests:
          hugepages-2Mi: 2Gi
        limits:
          hugepages-2Mi: 2Gi
```

Observed: the Pod is admitted.
Expected: rejected, as with `maximum hugepages-2Mi usage per Pod is 4Gi, but limit is 8Gi` -
which is exactly what happens if the same `8Gi` is written on the container instead.

Equivalent unit-level reproduction in `plugin/pkg/admission/limitranger`:

```go
err := PodValidateLimitFunc(&limitRange, &pod)  // returns nil; expected an error
```

### Anything else we need to know?

The duplicated helper carries a `TODO(ndixita): Find alternatives to avoid duplicating the code`
and a comment saying it exists "to avoid conversion of v1.Pod to api.Pod". That rationale does not
apply to this function - it takes only a resource name - so it can simply delegate to
`resourcehelper.IsSupportedPodLevelResource`.

The neighbouring duplicated helpers (`podRequests`, `podLimits`, `addResourceList`,
`maxResourceList`) carry the same TODO and are worth auditing for similar drift.

Found by source inspection plus a unit test at commit `b882c60b402` (v1.37.0-rc.0).

# Affects any release where PodLevelResources is enabled (Beta / default-on since 1.34).

title: Kubernetes v1.35.1 bundles CoreDNS v1.13.1 — 3 minor versions behind upstream v1.14.6, exposing clusters to 49+ known CVEs

body:
## Summary

Kubernetes v1.35.1 bundles `registry.k8s.io/coredns/coredns:v1.13.1` as the
default DNS provider. The upstream CoreDNS project has since released v1.14.6,
which addresses the vast majority of known vulnerabilities present in v1.13.1.

Since Kubernetes controls which CoreDNS version ships with each release, and
cluster administrators rely on the officially bundled version, we are requesting
that the CoreDNS version be bumped in an upcoming Kubernetes patch release.

/sig network
/area dns
/kind bug
/priority important-soon

## Environment

- **Kubernetes Version:** v1.35.1
- **Bundled CoreDNS:** registry.k8s.io/coredns/coredns:v1.13.1
- **Latest Upstream CoreDNS:** v1.14.6
- **OS:** Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.0 (Coughlan)
- **Scanners:** Dependency-Track, Trivy

## Why This Matters

Cluster administrators installing Kubernetes v1.35.1 via kubeadm or other
official tooling receive CoreDNS v1.13.1 by default. Most organizations
rely on the officially bundled versions and do not independently upgrade
individual control plane components.

While it is technically possible to manually upgrade CoreDNS to v1.14.6,
this is:
- Not documented as a supported configuration for v1.35.1
- A burden on every individual cluster administrator rather than a fix at source

## Vulnerability Comparison: v1.13.1 vs v1.14.6

We scanned both versions to quantify the security impact.

### Dependency CVEs

| Dependency | v1.13.1 Version | v1.14.6 Version | CVEs in v1.13.1 | CVEs in v1.14.6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| golang.org/x/crypto | 0.42.0 | 0.53.0 | 32 (7 Critical) | 1 (Unknown) |
| golang.org/x/net | 0.45.0 | (newer) | 8 | 0 |
| google.golang.org/grpc | 1.75.1 | 1.82.0 | 2 (1 Critical) | 1 (High) |
| github.com/quic-go/quic-go | 0.55.0 | (newer) | 4 | 0 |
| github.com/expr-lang/expr | 1.17.6 | (newer) | 2 | 0 |
| golang.org/x/sys | 0.36.0 | (newer) | 1 | 0 |
| **Total** | | | **49** | **2** |

### CoreDNS-Specific CVEs Fixed Between v1.13.1 and v1.14.6

| CVE | Severity | Fixed In | Description |
|-----|----------|----------|-------------|
| CVE-2026-26017 | HIGH | 1.14.2 | DNS access control bypass due to plugin execution order |
| CVE-2026-26018 | HIGH | 1.14.2 | DoS via predictable PRNG |
| CVE-2026-32934 | HIGH | 1.14.3 | DoS due to unbounded resource growth |
| CVE-2026-32936 | HIGH | 1.14.3 | DoS via oversized DNS-over-HTTPS GET requests |
| CVE-2026-33190 | HIGH | 1.14.3 | Auth bypass via flawed TSIG plugin verification |
| CVE-2026-33489 | HIGH | 1.14.3 | Info disclosure via incorrect ACL stanza selection |
| CVE-2026-35579 | HIGH | 1.14.3 | Auth bypass for TSIG-protected functionalities |
| CVE-2025-68151 | MEDIUM | 1.14.0 | DoS via unbounded connections |
| CVE-2025-47950 | HIGH | 1.12.2 | DoQ Memory Exhaustion |
| CVE-2023-28452 | HIGH | 1.11.0 | TuDoor Attacks |
| CVE-2024-0874 | MEDIUM | 1.11.2 | CD bit response caching issue |

## Impact Summary

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Total CVEs eliminated by bumping to v1.14.6 | ~47 dependency + 11 CoreDNS-specific |
| Critical CVEs eliminated | 8 |
| High CVEs eliminated | ~14 |
| Authentication bypass CVEs eliminated | 3 (CVE-2026-33190, CVE-2026-35579, CVE-2026-26017) |

## Remaining Vulnerabilities in v1.14.6

Even after upgrading to v1.14.6, a small number of issues remain. We are
reporting these separately to the CoreDNS PST (security@coredns.io):

| CVE/Advisory | Severity | Package | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| CVE-2026-56852 | HIGH | golang.org/x/text v0.38.0 | Fix in v0.39.0 |
| GHSA-hrxh-6v49-42gf | HIGH | google.golang.org/grpc v1.82.0 | Fix in v1.82.1 |
| GO-2026-5932 | UNKNOWN | golang.org/x/crypto v0.53.0 | openpgp deprecated |
| CVE-2022-2835 | MEDIUM | CoreDNS | No fix available |
| CVE-2022-2837 | MEDIUM | CoreDNS | No fix available |
| CVE-2023-30464 | MEDIUM | CoreDNS | No fix available |

## Request

1. **Can the Kubernetes release team bump CoreDNS to v1.14.6 (or latest
   compatible) in an upcoming v1.35.x patch release?**
2. Is there a defined process or cadence for CoreDNS version updates
   within Kubernetes patch releases?
3. Until a patch release is available, is manually upgrading CoreDNS
   to v1.14.6 within a Kubernetes v1.35.1 cluster a supported and
   tested configuration?
4. Are there any known compatibility issues between CoreDNS v1.14.6
   and Kubernetes v1.35.1?

## Additional Information
We have confirmed that Kubernetes v1.36.3 (the latest release) also ships CoreDNS v1.13.1
```
[root@kcp1 ~]# kubeadm config images list --kubernetes-version v1.36.3
registry.k8s.io/kube-apiserver:v1.36.3
registry.k8s.io/kube-controller-manager:v1.36.3
registry.k8s.io/kube-scheduler:v1.36.3
registry.k8s.io/kube-proxy:v1.36.3
registry.k8s.io/coredns/coredns:v1.13.1
registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10.1
registry.k8s.io/etcd:3.6.6-0
```

Last failure: 2026-08-05 08:31:33 UTC
https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gci-gce-alpha-features/2084837180517126144

## Reason for failure (if possible)
All failing steps are kubetest infrastructure lifecycle steps, not individual test failures. The job is configured with `--timeout=120m` within a 2h20m Prow deadline. On flaky runs the test suite hits the timeout, causing a cascade: `kubetest.Test` → `kubetest.Timeout` → `kubetest.TearDown` → `kubetest.DumpClusterLogs`. `kubetest.Up` and `kubetest.listResources After` flakes on separate runs suggest GCP Boskos project provisioning slowness.

Build log confirms the actual e2e test suite passes when the cluster comes up in time (91 Passed | 0 Failed on the 2026-08-05 run).

_No Response_

title: Liveness probe failure container restart leads to container starting up with started=true and liveness probes starting before startup probes have run

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: triage/accepted
