labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
When using the raw block PV feature, if your container is privileged, then the volumeDevices.devicePath specified in the Pod spec are silently ignored by the container runtime since all host devices are mapped into the container at /dev.

This is an issue with the raw block feature since its inception and impacts all volume plugins and most runtimes (docker, containerd to name a few)

**What you expected to happen**:
At least when the container's devicePath is non-conflicting with the host (ie not in /dev), it should be mapped correctly. 

I'm on the fence about what should happen if the devicePath is "/dev". Disallowing "/dev" entirely would be a breaking change (even though it's pretty non-functional today).  Overriding "/dev" could also be a breaking change?

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod 
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  containers:
  - image: debian:latest
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    name: nginx
    command: ["/bin/sh"]
    args:
      - "-c"
      - "while true; do sleep 10;done"
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
    volumeDevices:
    - devicePath: /my-disk
      name: disk1
  volumes:
  - name: disk1
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: disk1
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: disk1
spec:
  volumeMode: Block
  accessModes: [ "ReadWriteOnce" ]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi 
```

**Anything else we need to know?**:
Current workaround for this issue is to have an unprivileged init container that copies the devices to an emptydir shared with the privileged container.

body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->

**What happened**:
Had a audit-webhook configured for batch logging which received a large number of audit logs and because CPU throttled as a result. This caused the apiserver to OOM and resulted in a cluster outage.

**What you expected to happen**:
Using an audit-webhook in batch mode the expectation is that apiserver operation should be prioritized over audit logging and that failure or degradation of audit logging should be ignored by the apiserver. 

In this case the webhook being throttled delayed its ability to handle in coming logs. This in turn caused a build up of connections in the apiserver and resulted in it getting OOM killed. 

Expectation limitation on number of connections/TTL should protect it from unbounded audit logging connections and these should be dropped as needed to continue stable operation. Similar to dropping logs when the buffer is full.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. Run audit-webhook and set CPU limits such that it will be throttled. 
2. Increase apiserver requests until volume causes connection build up and memory consumption. 

**Anything else we need to know?**:
NA

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.14.602
- Cloud provider: AWS
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): Ubuntu 18.04.3
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 4.15.0-1052-aws

body:
**What would you like to be added**:
Ephemeral container can be removed from pod gracefully. 
**Why is this needed**:
In our K8s cluster, there are many deployed pods. We aim to use ephemeral containers as troubleshooting containers. Thus, for troubleshooting, many ephemeral containers are potentially created.
Once the need of an ephemeral container is gone, the container should be removed gracefully. Resource of the container should be released. The container should not be accessed any more for security. And the container also should be removed from pod.
Unless the pod which contains ephemeral container is destroyed, there are no ways to remove the ephemeral container totally.
However, this approach is really "intrusive". (For example, traffic may be impacted) We need a way to remove ephemeral container gracefully like how we creating it.

title: Node-local API cache

labels.name: sig/scalability
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scalability.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Instrumentation.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

body:
**What would you like to be added**:

A dedicated node-local API for retrieving node-local resources, including:
- Pods scheduled to the node
- The node object itself

The API should have clear semantics for adding additional resources as needed. This includes consistent API paths, SubjectAccessReview patterns, SLOs around cache accuracy, and cache-miss handling.

**Why is this needed**:

For large-scale clusters, an increasing number of Daemons are depending on the nodes `/pods` API. This API has a number of issues, including:
- Using the authenticated port, it share's a permission with the root-on-node `node/proxy` permission (see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83465)
- The API uses a different source of truth from the API server, and doesn't have any consistency guarantees.
- The API doesn't conform to Kubernetes API standards.

**Open design questions**:

- Should the cache be maintained & served by the Kubelet? Or a DaemonSet?
  - If the latter, should the Kubelet read from the local cache?
- If I can GET a specific through the k8s API, I should also be able to get it from the local cache. But its also convenient to be able to say "you can only get pods running on the same node". Do we need to support both use cases? How should this be structured?
  - Idea: the API could come in 2 "flavors", one would look exactly like the cluster API, and fallback to the cluster API on a cache-miss (list requests need to be handled differently). The second flavor would be the local-only version, that uses different SAR attributes, and has a different request path (e.g. prefix `local-api/`)
- Should the local API support full apiserver features? Including watch, filter, etc.? If so, it probably makes sense to reuse the apimachinery.


/sig node
/sig scalability
/sig apimachinery
/sig auth
/sig instrumentation

/priority important-longterm
/help

title: Memory/Timer leak in the work queue

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

body:
Hi,

We are experiencing a memory leak in our operator and it seems to be caused by some Timers:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/976373/66737404-27049080-ee6c-11e9-998e-91f75a5dd730.png)
_See here the original issue: https://github.com/elastic/cloud-on-k8s/issues/1984_

After some investigations I found out that the [waitingLoop](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/172b42569ccacc5c33a885060fc0b7eab863d81e/util/workqueue/delaying_queue.go#L175)  can create a lot of timers (at least [1 every 10 seconds](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/172b42569ccacc5c33a885060fc0b7eab863d81e/util/workqueue/delaying_queue.go#L172)) if the queue is not empty : 

https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/172b42569ccacc5c33a885060fc0b7eab863d81e/util/workqueue/delaying_queue.go#L207-L210

The problem here is that if the event in the queue is to expire in a "far" future the previous `nextReadyAt` timers will pile up and the memory will be reclaimed too late.

Could someone confirm this scenario ?

A fix would be to create some `Timer` with `time.NewTimer(...)` and close them when they are not needed (e.g. `ShutDown()` is called) or superseded by a most recent one.

Happy to discuss the issue and contribute if needed.

title: Fine grained Kubelet API authorization

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: sig/auth
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Auth.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
**Summary**
The node API authorization is too coarse. We need finer grained authorization of different request types, and maybe resources acted on.

**Background**

The Kubelet API on the authenticated (10250) port currently uses a very coarse-grained scheme for authorizing requests. For example, reading `/healthz` and calling `/exec/...` (i.e. execute arbitrary code) require the same `proxy` subresource. The SubjectAccessReviews are currently populated with:

- Requisting user (generally from a TokenReviewRequest or client certificate authentication)
- Request verb
- A resource request with:
    - `APIGroup: ""`
    - `APIVersion: "v1"`
    -  `Resource: "nodes"`
    - `Name: nodeName` (the name of the node the request was against)
    - `Subresource:` one of: proxy, log, metrics, spec, stats

The full mapping of request paths to subresources can be found here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/14344b57e56258e87cbe80c8cd80399855eca424/pkg/kubelet/server/auth_test.go#L110-L143

Fixing this issue is a prerequisite to removing the Kubelet's unauthenticated API: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/12968

Although this issue is specific to the Kubelet API, other components that use delegated authorization for a subdivided API will face the same problems.

**Desired State**

In an ideal world, authorization would happen against the following criteria:

1. Requester has permission to use the node API for this Kubelet.
2. If it's a resource request with a Kubernetes API analog, the requester is authorized to make the request through the regular API
    - E.g. `/exec/podNamespace/podID/containerName` maps to:
      ```
      apiGroup: "core"
      apiVersion: "v1"
      resource: "pods"
      namespace: podNamespace
      name: podName
      subresource: "exec"
      ```
    - E.g. `/pods/` maps to:
      ```
      apiGroup: "core"
      apiVersion: "v1"
      resource: "pods"
      verb: "list"
      ```
3. If it's a non-resource request (e.g. `/healthz`, `/logs`), then it's a regular non-resource request authorization check (still requiring [1]), with the requested path being the requested path.
   - _optional:_ We could prefix the request path to indicate a request via the kubelet API, so the authorization can't be used against other non-kubelet targets.

These changes need to maintain backwards compatibility with the current coarse grained permissions.

/sig auth
/sig node
/kind feature
/area kubelet-api
/priority important-longterm

See also:
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/12968
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/28138
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/2098

body:
**What would you like to be added**:
Add a label or metric with the Common Name of the certificate and the IP-address where the request is made to the kubernetes api-server. 

**Why is this needed**:
Kubernetes api-server has the metrics apiserver_client_certificate_expiration_seconds_bucket: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/authentication/request/x509/x509.go#L34-L66.

Which tells you that there are clients in the kubernetes cluster that are accessing the api-server with a certificate. Based on this metric, there are a few alerts on the Internet:
https://github.com/coreos/prometheus-operator/issues/1843.
https://medium.com/@DazWilkin/kubernetes-metrics-ba69d439fac4

However, it is impossible to understand from this metric who accesses the api-server with the certificate, which will soon end. And the only way to find such clients is to wait for the certificate to expire and to find clients who receive 403 response code by api-server logos with high verbose.

Is there any way to find these clients before their certificate expires? Usually these are kubectl or kubelet configs and sometimes you have to guess where you forgot to update your client certificate. Is there a metric for that?

**Cluster information**:
Kubernetes version: 1.16.6
Cloud being used: bare-metal
Installation method: kubeadm
Host OS: ubuntu 18.04
CNI and version: Flannel 0.11.0
CRI and version: docker://18.9.7

body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:
Unless disabled, the `test/e2e_node` tests will prepull all images when running. They do so using the [PrePullAllImages function](https://sourcegraph.com/github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes@master/-/blob/test/e2e_node/image_list.go#L138).

I think there's the opportunity to improve the runtime of the test suite by prepulling the images in parallel.

**Why is this needed**:
Its always nicer to have faster tests :) Specifically for users running `make test-e2e-node` locally, it's nice to have the image prepull occur as quick as possible.

That being said, we should also be cognizant of any tradeoffs associated with prepulling the images in parallel. If the code is substantially more complex, we would need a large improvement in test speed to justify it. I'm hopeful this discussion could be had once we have a proof of concept diff (which I think should be fairly minimal effort to create).

title: Kubelet Out-of-Pid eviction should rank based on pids used

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: help wanted
labels.description: Denotes an issue that needs help from a contributor. Must meet "help wanted" guidelines.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

body:
**What would you like to be added**:
Enhance the kubelet's eviction algorithm when handling out-of-pid scenarios to evict the pod using the most pids.

**Why is this needed**:
Currently, the kubelet ranks pods for out-of-pid eviction only by PodPriority.  When there are many pods of the same priority, it ranks them randomly, which is not ideal.  In the case of a fork bomb, the kubelet prevents the node from running out of pids, but may evict many innocent pods before choosing the fork bomb.

**How to implement this**

cAdvisor already collects process stats:  https://github.com/google/cadvisor/blob/master/info/v1/container.go#L814

The kubelet already enables process stats: 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/server/server.go#L343

These metrics just need to be used to make eviction decisions here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/eviction/helpers.go#L642
Notice that pid metrics are only ranked by priority, whereas disk and memory are ranked by (1) whether usage > requests, (2) priority, (3) usage - requests.

The eviction manager's decisions are made based on the Summary API:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/apis/stats/v1alpha1/types.go

We need to add ProcessMetrics to the PodStats struct.  We can start with number of processes.  Something like:

```golang
type ProcessStats struct {
	// Number of processes
	// +optional
	ProcessCount *uint64 `json:"process_count,omitempty"`
}

// PodStats holds pod-level unprocessed sample stats.
type PodStats struct {
        ...
	// Stats pertaining to processes.
	// +optional
	ProcessStats *ProcessStats `json:"process_stats,omitempty"`
}
```

The summary API is constructed from the cadvisorInfo, and the https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/stats/helper.go#L143 has methods for extracting particular metrics from the cAdvisorInfo structs.

This needs to be set when constructing the summary API in both the [cri_stats_provider](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/stats/cri_stats_provider.go) and the cadvisor_stats_provider)[https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/stats/cadvisor_stats_provider.go]

The eviction manager just needs to be able to take a [PodStats](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/apis/stats/v1alpha1/types.go#L95), and get the usage, like [memoryUsage(...](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/eviction/helpers.go#L323), then to implement a compare function for pids, like [memory(...](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/eviction/helpers.go#L546)

There is no need to implement an "exceedsRequests" function for pids, as there are no per-pod pid requests.  There is also no need to add container-level metrics to the summary API.  Pod-level metrics should be sufficient for our purposes.

**Testing**

To test the ranking, update the [PriorityPidEvictionOrdering](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e_node/eviction_test.go#L398) node e2e test.  Right now, it only has two pods, one that is malicious and low-priority, and one that is innocent and high-priority.  It relies on the priority ranking to ensure the malicious pod is evicted first.  We want to add a third pod, which is a high-priority malicious pod, with the same priority as the innocent pod.  This will test that the pod with higher PID usage is evicted first.

/sig node
/kind feature
/priority important-longterm
/help

body:
Fully described in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/87865#discussion_r384736714, `VisitPodSecretNames` and `VisitPodConfigmapNames` will visit these fields for all containers, regardless of whether they're hidden behind a feature gate (e.g. `EphemeralContainers`).

This is usually correct, these methods are often used to drop fields and in this case should visit all containers that are persisted regardless of whether they're disabled, but the callers of these methods should signal that explicitly rather than relying on the implicit behavior.

/priority important-longterm
/kind bug
/sig node

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
StatefulSet does not reflect image change to the Pod.

**What you expected to happen**:
StatefulSet to reflect image change to the Pod.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. Apply a StatefulSet with a wrong image - `.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image`.
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  serviceName: "nginx"
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: k8s.gcr.io/nginx-slim:foo
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
          name: web
```

2. Ensure that the Pod fails to pull the image
```
$ k get po
NAME                             READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
web-0                            0/1     ImagePullBackOff   0          1m
```

3. Update the StatefulSet `.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image` to a valid image - `k8s.gcr.io/nginx-slim:0.8`

4. Ensure that the StatefulSet does not update the Pod and the Pod still tries to pull the old image
```
$ k get po
NAME                             READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
web-0                            0/1     ImagePullBackOff   0          19m

$ k get po web-0 -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].image}'
k8s.gcr.io/nginx-slim:foo

$ k get sts web -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'
k8s.gcr.io/nginx-slim:0.8
```

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

There are flag descriptions where is stated that the unspecified address behaves differently depending on the IP family:

```
(set to 0.0.0.0 for all IPv4 interfaces and :: for all IPv6 interfaces)
```

However, that's not the behavior implemented in `net.Listen`  and `net.ListenPacket`, clarified in the golang documentation https://github.com/golang/go/commit/424b0654f8e6c72f69e096f69009096de16e30fa

> // For TCP networks, if the host in the address parameter is empty or
> // a literal unspecified IP address, Listen listens on all available
> // unicast and anycast IP addresses of the local system.
> // To only use IPv4, use network "tcp4".

**What you expected to happen**:

Fix the comment to state the reality,  i.e
```
 (set 0.0.0.0 or :: for all interfaces")
```

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

From the root of the kubernetes repo
```sh
grep -r "for all IPv4 interfaces"
```

title: Unexpected scheduling of replacement Pod upon Pod deletion

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: sig/apps
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Apps.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

body:
## Background

As you may have known, internally, the Kubernetes scheduler handles "unassignedPod" (nil `.spec.nodeName`) and "assignedPod" (non-nil `.spec.nodeName`) simultaneously.

- one to be handled in the internal cache:
    https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/15c3f1b119ff4b4073c86df05c819a9672b80d68/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L348-L349

- while the other to be dealt with in internal queue(s):
    https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/15c3f1b119ff4b4073c86df05c819a9672b80d68/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L373-L374

It works most of the time except for the case that **the scheduling decision of added Pod strictly depends on a previously deleted Pod**. For example, if you delete a Pod from a Deployment, (1) the Pod will be deleted, and then (2) a backfilling Pod will be created. Looking at the timeline, (1) happens prior to (2), however, in scheduler, (2) may be processed when (1) is still happening. In that case, the decision for the backing Pod is based on the presence of the terminating Pod, which is not the desired result.

Using pod topology spread constraints or pod anti-affinity can easily reproduce this scenario. #86037 is one DP.

## Is it an Issue?

Before jumping to possible solutions, we should brainstorm to conclude whether it's an issue or not.

- We should firstly verify, in the client-go/API's perspective, whether the informers will **_always_** get the new Pod event **after** the deleted Pod event. If it's uncertain, we don't need to continue the discussion.
- In the scheduler's point of view, can we simply say: it's not an issue as we handle Pod events individually, instead of handling one event to waiting for a preceding event to be finished. (no need to say, it's hard to figure out the implicit Pod dependency)
- From the user's perspective, it's an issue as the scheduling decision for the replacement Pod doesn't make sense.

## Workaround

As mentioned in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/86037#issuecomment-563095248, we can use `kubectl delete pod <pod name> --force=true --grace-period=0` to alleviate the issue.

## Possible Solutions

(This part will be updated now and then...)

- Hold the scheduling cycle (using proper lock) if a dependent terminated Pod is being processed in the caching goroutine.
- Using a workqueue to enqueue both assignedPod and unassignedPod, then process each item to in either caching or schedulingQ. But this may slow down the throughput.

/sig scheduling
/priority important-longterm
/assign

title: Invalid listTypes in FlowSchema cause errors in apiserver logs

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

body:
In the kind `flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1alpha1.FlowSchema`, the fields [`.spec.rules`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ec5321c6a9f23e5ad26cf88a41fda9dba0c5ce89/staging/src/k8s.io/api/flowcontrol/v1alpha1/types.go#L110), [`.spec.rules[].subjects`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ec5321c6a9f23e5ad26cf88a41fda9dba0c5ce89/staging/src/k8s.io/api/flowcontrol/v1alpha1/types.go#L155), [`.spec.rules[].resourceRules`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ec5321c6a9f23e5ad26cf88a41fda9dba0c5ce89/staging/src/k8s.io/api/flowcontrol/v1alpha1/types.go#L161), and [`.spec.rules[].nonResourceRules`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ec5321c6a9f23e5ad26cf88a41fda9dba0c5ce89/staging/src/k8s.io/api/flowcontrol/v1alpha1/types.go#L166) are all tagged with `+listType=set`, but their elements are non-scalar, which is not currently supported. This causes errors messages like:

```
[SHOULD NOT HAPPEN] failed to create typed new object: .spec.rules: element 0: associative list without keys has an element that's a map type
```

to appear in apiserver logs when the feature is enabled, and also prevents server side apply from working with this type. Changing these tags to `+listType=atomic` should fix the issue.

/cc @lavalamp @apelisse

body:
As a part of on-going migration of Kubelet flags to config by WG Component Standard group, below is a summary of flags that can be migrated, and flags with special cases,

**Kubelet flags to migrate:**

- [ ] --CertDirectory 
- [ ] --RegisterNode 
- [ ] --kubeconfig
- [ ] --bootstrap-kubeconfig
- [x] --runonce
- [x] --enable-server
- [x] --provider-id - Assigned to knabben
- [x] --cloud-provider - Assigned to knabben
- [x] --cloud-config - Assigned to @gavinfish 
- [ ] --root-dir - WIP @gavinfish 

**Platform-specific flags:**

In the past we've talked about not moving these until we decide on a standard way to include them in config. This can, however, be improved in future versions and we shouldn't stall the migration on it.

- [ ] --windows-service

**Experimental flags:**

Following flags might be experimental, but some are probably the stuff that was called "experimental" in the beginning and then became widely used and nobody updated the name. 

Below is the list of flags that needs to be evaluated and can be marked into categories like deprecated, removed. The remaining flags can be safely migrated to a stable config file format.

- [x] --experimental-mounter-path
- [x] --experimental-kernel-memcg-notification
- [x] --experimental-check-node-capabilities-before-mount
- [x] --experimental-allocatable-ignore-eviction
- [x] --node-status-max-images
- [ ] --lock-file
- [ ] --exit-on-lock-contention
- [x] --seccomp-profile-root
- [x] --bootstrap-checkpoint-path

**Testing flags:**

Test-specific config, should migrate may be worth grouping in a substructure, maybe call it KubeletTestConfiguration.

- [x] --chaos-chance
- [x] --really-crash-for-testing


**Global flags:**

This is probably the last thing we'd tackle, which is a list of flags that came from dependencies. We previously locked this down so that dependencies can't add arbitrary flags to our command line in the future, but still have all the flags from before that lock-down to contend with. We'll need to decide whether we can deprecate any of these, and whether it even makes sense to expose them in the config file. 

**Special cases:**

- [ ] --container-runtime-endpoint, 
- [ ]  --image-service-endpoint, and values in config.ContainerRuntimeOptions (these flag registrations are hiding over in pkg/kubelet/config/flags.go).
Many things marked alpha or experimental, but have been around for a long time with many users likely relying on them. Like "experimental" flags above, we should chase down which should be moved into config or deprecated and removed.

- [ ] --dynamic-config-dir
This is the directory used for storage by the dynamic kubelet config feature. Since omitting this option disables dynamic config, and since the feature is currently just exposing the entire config object, it would be too easy to accidentally set a dynamic config that disables dynamic config updates. So may be best to just leave as a flag for now.

- [x] --config
This has to remain a flag so there is a way to specify a path to the config file.

- [ ] --node-labels 

- [ ] --register-with-taints
There have been some security discussions in the past about replacing these or doing something better. We should check in and see if any progress has been made here.

- [ ] --NodeIP 

** Migrated flags: **
- [x] --VolumePluginDir


[Work In Progress] This issue is being actively worked on and will be updated regularly

Refer the email for details: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/kubernetes-wg-component-standard/W_5obNYw5DU

title: The presence of admission validating webhooks breaks Ephemeral Containers

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

body:
**What happened**:
Adding a validating webhook with resources section of `"pods/*"` or `"*/*"` breaks ability to add Ephemeral Containers as described in https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/debug-application-cluster/debug-running-pod/#ephemeral-container

**What you expected to happen**:
```
kubectl alpha debug -it rabbit --image=busybox --target=rabbitmq
```
Debug command should attach to the running pod and allow user to interact with the ephemeral container image. This works when no validating webhook is configured.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Using a K8 cluster with Ephemeral Containers feature gate enabled and v1.18.3
1. Create a validating webhook (contents don't matter except that resources is "pods/*")
<details>
  <summary>whconfig.yaml</summary>

  ```
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  name: test-repro
webhooks:
- name: test-repro.test.k8s.io
  clientConfig:
    url: https://localhost:8675/hook
  rules:
  - apiGroups: ["*"]
    apiVersions: ["*"]
    operations: ["*"]
    resources: ["pods/*"]
```
</details>

```
kubectl apply -f whconfig.yaml
```

2. Create a test pod
<details>
  <summary>test_pod.yaml</summary>

  ```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: rabbit
  labels:
    role: myrole
spec:
  shareProcessNamespace: true
  containers:
    - name: rabbitmq
      image: rabbitmq
      ports:
        - name: rabbit
          containerPort: 5672
          protocol: TCP
```
</details>

```
kubectl apply -f test_pod.yaml
```

3. Try to add an Ephemeral Container using alpha debug command
```
kubectl alpha debug -it rabbit --image=busybox --target=rabbitmq
```
Error:
```
$ kubectl alpha debug -it rabbit --image=busybox --target=rabbitmq
Defaulting debug container name to debugger-jvc8h.
error: error updating ephemeral containers: Internal error occurred: converting (core.Pod) to (v1.EphemeralContainers): EphemeralContainers not present in src
```

**Anything else we need to know?**:
When using `v=10`, can see that the api server appears to be throwing the error when trying to convert the object for the webhook invocation.
API returning the 500 error: `http://localhost:8080/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods/rabbit/ephemeralcontainers`

title: Node authorizer fails to authorize requests right after kube-apiserver restart

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/scalability
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scalability.

labels.name: sig/auth
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Auth.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

labels.name: lifecycle/rotten
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

body:
**What happened**:

In kubernetes clusters with O(100k) pods, the initialization of watch cache and shared informer inside of kube-apiserver takes 30-50 seconds. Before this happens, node authorizer is not able to accept any request.
When this happens, kubelets are retrying the requests leading to a retry loop and generating a significant load on the master which in effect can significantly slow down a kube-apiserver initialization, ultimately leading to 429 errors and kube-apiserver crashloop.

The information about state of node authorizer (if it's initialized or not) is not available externally and cannot be used by e.g. load balancer to direct traffic instances that are already initialized.


**What you expected to happen**:

We should have a way to determine if the kube-apiserver is ready to serve requests. Currently /healthz, /livez or /readyz endpoints don't export any information that can be used to determine state of node authorizer. 

In multimaster environment, when one of the kube-apiserver replicas is not yet initialized, we should redirect traffic to other replicas, but currently there is no signal we can use to determine if the replica is initialized or not.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Run scalability load test in 3000 node scale. Right before "Scaling objects" step, restart all masters. They will fail to reboot in ~minute window, so will be killed by livenessProbe.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

While in our repro we suffer from node authorizer not being initialized, this likely also affects other controllers working inside of kube-apiserver.

I suggest adding a poststarthook blocking /healthz that will expose the status of all informers in the system. This way we can use that information in load balancer to direct traffic only to already initialized instances. I will send PR for this.

- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): tested in 1.17 and 1.18

title: Remove the apiserver insecure port

labels.name: kind/cleanup
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to cleaning up code, process, or technical debt.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: sig/auth
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Auth.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

body:
The API server's "insecure-port" has been [deprecated since 1.10](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/2f175bc43279a1a4552610a42af0a006f4c6fba2), but never had a deadline for removal. Previous efforts to remove the port have been blocked by requirements for http healthz checks (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/43784).

I propose publishing a deadline to remove the feature in v1.20. This means that in v1.19 we:
1. Update the deprecation notice to indicate that removal will happen in v1.20 (rather than a "future release")
2. Add an [action required] release note to highlight the removal
3. Figure out a path forward to meeting healthz or other requriments

For item 3, there are already out-of-tree solutions available today, such as a healthz-only proxy which can serve the same API on the same port, and authenticates as a user that only has access to healthz.

/cc @justinsb @micahhausler @deads2k @liggitt 
/sig auth api-machinery
/milestone v1.20
/kind cleanup
/priority important-longterm

title: Reduce the number of calls to GCE API (for clusters on GCE) coming from cloud node-controller

labels.name: sig/scalability
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scalability.

labels.name: help wanted
labels.description: Denotes an issue that needs help from a contributor. Must meet "help wanted" guidelines.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

labels.name: sig/cloud-provider
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Cloud Provider.

body:
For external cloud provider - Kubelet setting the TaintExternalCloudProvider taint: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_node_status.go#L266

The results in calling `initializeNode` function in cloud node-controller:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c276a451d64d161b21d70042d93f4c4b8e3201d/pkg/controller/cloud/node_controller.go#L323

This (in a healthy case) sends 4 GCE API calls to:
1. get node addresses: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c276a451d64d161b21d70042d93f4c4b8e3201d/pkg/controller/cloud/node_controller.go#L439 (as part of getNodeModifier call)
2. get instance type:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c276a451d64d161b21d70042d93f4c4b8e3201d/pkg/controller/cloud/node_controller.go#L452 (as part of getNodeModifiers call)
3. get instance:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c276a451d64d161b21d70042d93f4c4b8e3201d/pkg/controller/cloud/node_controller.go#L233 (as part of updateNodeAddresses call)
4. get node addresses (again):
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c276a451d64d161b21d70042d93f4c4b8e3201d/pkg/controller/cloud/node_controller.go#L242 (as part of updateNodeAddresses call)

All those requests are read requests and could be replaced by a single call.
We could do that by introducing a simple struct like:
```
type InstanceMetadata struct {
  ProviderID ...
  Type ...
  NodeAddresses ...
}
```
and adding a method (or rather replacing the existing InstanceTypeByProviderID which is used only for this purpose) to Instances cloud-provider interface;
```
func InstanceMetadataByProviderID(...) (*InstanceMetadata, error)
```

With that change, we would be able to replace all that 4 calls with just a single API call.

This would be useful especially for creating large clusters (like 5k nodes), which may saturate the quota for API calls for quite some time.

This is quite significant size of refactoring, though it should be relatively mechanical task to do.

/sig cloud-provider
/sig scalability
/priority important-longterm

/help-wanted

@mborsz @mm4tt - FYI

title: Unnecessary scheduling attempt

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

body:
When there is not any node fits for an incoming Pod, scheduler firstly tries to [put it to internal unschedulableQ or backoffQ](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/429aefa2e6e1d41cab892703733cf6fdd9919561/pkg/scheduler/factory.go#L504). And right after that, scheduler [updates the Pod's status as unschedulable](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/429aefa2e6e1d41cab892703733cf6fdd9919561/pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go#L391-L396) via API server:

But unfortunately, the preceding step is running as a [goroutine](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/429aefa2e6e1d41cab892703733cf6fdd9919561/pkg/scheduler/factory.go#L487), which in practice can happen after the latter step. Or even worse, the preceding step may occur after the PodUpdate event comes in. In this case, the logic that scheduler intentionally bypasses the updated Pod doesn't work (L439~L446 below won't be reached):

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/429aefa2e6e1d41cab892703733cf6fdd9919561/pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L436-L452

Then the Pod gets added to activeQ (L452 above) and will soon be retried - which in most cases is a waste as it was just tried earlier.

**Reproduce steps:**

See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/90616#issuecomment-621520874.

**Solutions:**

- Aggressive option. Change the [goroutine](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/429aefa2e6e1d41cab892703733cf6fdd9919561/pkg/scheduler/factory.go#L487) to be synchronous call.
- Safe option.  Update `PriorityQueue#Update()` to guard the case: even if a Pod is not in unschedulingQ, it may also be unnecessary to be added into activeQ.

/sig scheduling
/priority important-longterm

title: Adjust watch bookmark policy to match watch-cache size policy

labels.name: sig/scalability
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scalability.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

body:
Currently, (best-effort) watch bookmarks are sent just right before the given watch is supposed to timeout:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3b00d7dce51b3833815e2459e3a92ed917402170/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L1243

In https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/90091 we're adjusting how the size of watch cache is determined and make it dynamic and more duration-oriented (rather than based on some magic constants) - we're targeting to always keep 5 minutes of history in watch cache.

With that change, we should get back to our bookmark policy:
- change it to (additionally to right before timeout) also send bookmarks every N seconds (setting N to slightly less than expected watch cache history period, so slightly less than X minutes we will use there)
- scale-test this change (to see if it doesn't introduce non-negligible overhead)
- if so permanently introduce this change

/sig scalability api-machinery

title: Make watch-cache size dynamic and get rid of magic constants

labels.name: sig/scalability
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scalability.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: help wanted
labels.description: Denotes an issue that needs help from a contributor. Must meet "help wanted" guidelines.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

body:
Currently, capacity for watchcache is a parameter at creation time and cannot be changed later:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L81
To make it scalable, we have a number of magic constants:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/registry/cachesize/cachesize.go#L25
and we already had a bunch issues with it (people don't know it should be updated for some new resources, we can't clearly say how to set it, ...)

We should try to get rid of of all those magic constants completely.

`At the high-level,  instead of providing magic constants, we want to change it so that last X minutes of history will be kept (e.g. X=5)`

How can we do that:
1. the first step is to allow modifying size of watchcache in a running apiserver:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/watch_cache.go#L127
- fortunately it's not that hard - it's enough to simply (under lock) create a new array, copy contents and adjust startIndex and endIndex appropriately
2. the second step is decide when the size should be adjusted
- objects don't have information about their last update time, but fortunately we don't need it - we don't have to be super accurate; we can simply assume that the last update time of the object is the time when we learned about it (received it from etcd); we know that the object was modified earlier that that, so if we ensure that we have at least X minutes of history based on those timestamps, we also will have at least X minutes of history based on real timestamps;
- how the above translates to concreate changes? we need to extend watchCacheEvent to also keep the timestamp, and on adding new item to cache, if the item we would have to overwrite is to fresh, trigger resizing of cache (increase by 2x)
3. the remaining part is to decide when we need to reduce the size of cache; we can probably start without that at all, but ideally, we should decrease the size by 2x when the X minutes history would fit into half of it (so 1/4th of the original size) - this should allow us to avoid flapping

@kubernetes/sig-scalability-feature-requests @mm4tt - FYI

For first solution we would need to protect against missing labels by adding static analysis. We would enforce that verifies that directories that import "k8s.io/component-base/metrics" have a sig/instrumentation label in OWNERS file.

(+) We can parse only small subset of files that changed
(-) Requires building custom mechanism

Third idea is to add presubmit that can commet on a PR with /cc $some_metrics_reviewer.
(-) Require setting up a github account

body:
This is a placeholder issue to remove support for the version skew handling as well as the deprecated seccomp annotations.

The [KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-node/20190717-seccomp-ga.md) states:

> Since we support up to 2 minor releases of version skew between the master and node, annotations must continue to be supported and backfilled for at least 2 versions passed the initial implementation. However, we can decide to extend support farther to reduce breakage. If this feature is implemented in v1.19, I propose v1.23 as a target for removal of the old behavior.
…
> To raise awareness of annotation usage (in case of old automation), a warning mechanism will be used to highlight that support will be dropped in v1.23. The mechanisms being considerated are audit annotations, annotations on the object, events, or a warning as described in KEP #1693.

Beside that, the kubelet `--seccomp-profile-root` has to be removed in v1.23, too:

> The existing kubelet (alpha) flag --seccomp-profile-root allows for seccomp root path configuration. This flag will be deprecated as of v1.19, and will be removed on v1.23. The seccomp root path will then be derived from the kubelet root path, which is defined by --root-dir. The current default value is <root-dir>/seccomp. This KEP will make the default behavior the only behavior.


/milestone v1.23
/sig node

cc @tallclair @pjbgf

title: UserInfo.UID is not passed by client-go

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

body:
It looks UserInfo.UID is newer than other fields and while #49677 added it SubjectAccessReviewSpec for webhook authorization, it's still not being sent by client-go in headers. Also there is no flag in APIServer to process those headers. As a result all authorizers needing that, may not work correctly for SubjectAccessReviews made by kube-aggregator extensions.

**What happened**:

Our webhook authorizer, authorizes users using UserInfo.UID. It's missing in SubjectAccessReviews created by kube-aggregator extensions (our case was state metrics), resulting authorizer to not work.

**What you expected to happen**:

I except All fields that is filled by authenticator be present for authorizer and I think it's valid to have an authorizer to use UID.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Make authentication webhook that fills SubjectAccessReviewSpec.UID. You will see there UID is missing from SubjectAccessReviewSpecs made by a kube-aggregator extension.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

UserInfo.UID is not passed to client-go round-tripper [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/transport/round_trippers.go#L118) and [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/transport/round_trippers.go#L101) and impersonate config do nothing for it. There is also no api-server flag to get it from headers.

title: Volume Binding PV/PVC Assume Cache should be updated before moving pods to active queue

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

labels.name: lifecycle/rotten
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR that has aged beyond stale and will be auto-closed.

body:
## Motivation 

There is no guarantee in which order different event handlers will be
called. If we use different event handlers, it's possible that PV/PVC
assume cache is updated after pods are moved to active queue and
the volume binding plugin may use stale cache.

Example race case:

1. pod go through volume scheduling, fail because of PVCs not bound, the pod will be marked unscheduable
2. PVC/PV are bound
3. scheduler factory informer handler is run, the pod will be moved to active queue
4. scheduler main thread runs this pod immediately and will use stale PV/PVC cache
  - this pod will be marked unscheduable again
  - if no new events to move it to active queue, this pod will be stuck forever
5. volume binder informer handler is run, PVC/PV cache is updated

3) and 5) are run in different event handlers and there is no guarantee in which order they are run, if 3) happens before 5) pods scheduled between them will use stale cache.

/sig storage
/sig scheduling 

This will not cause any problems in production, as we will move stuck pods every minute (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/72558).  However, it does not feel good in design and may cause flaky tests. I'd like to solve it fundamentally. 

## solution

In the framework, the scheduler can provide some methods which plugins can use to receive events. After calling all plugins' event handlers, if one of them thinks pods may be schedulable again, then move pods to active queue.

Alternatively, `PodQueue` can be exposed via FrameworkHandle, plugins register their separate informer handlers and move pods to active queue when they think it is necessary. The drawback is plugins may move pods to active queue multiple times if there is no coordination.

ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/73305

## alternative solution

VolumeBinding tolerates that the PV/PVC Assume Cache may be stale and check the informer cache hold by the scheduler when the PV/PVC object is not found.

(The update events may be missed, however, we holds pointers to objects in informer cache, so the content is always up to date)

**What happened**:

This issue was originally reported via the Kubernetes HackerOne bug bounty by HackerOne user [lazydog](https://hackerone.com/lazydog) but we have decided that due to the high privileges required, it can be addressed publicly.

A user able to create CRDs could create a malicious CRD such that listing CRs will cause enormous amounts of CPU usage on the API server.

**What you expected to happen**:

The `jsonpath` function should not expand strings with more than two consecutive periods. Either it should collapse additional repeated periods or it should return an error.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
```
$ kubectl create -f - <<EOF
---
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: foos.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: foos
    singular: foo
    kind: Foo
  version: v1
  additionalPrinterColumns:
  - name: FOO
    type: string
    JSONPath: ........................................................................................................................................................................................................
EOF

$ kubectl create -f - <<EOF
---
apiVersion: example.com/v1
kind: Foo
metadata:
  name: foo-cr
spec:
  foo:
    bar:
      baz:
        qux: data
EOF

$ kubectl get foo
# ( and the API server CPU usage jumps way up )
```

/committee product-security
/priority important-longterm

title: Provide ServiceAccountTokenProjection migration example

labels.name: kind/documentation
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to documentation.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: sig/auth
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Auth.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:

When switching from old `automountServiceAccountToken` to the new `ServiceAccountTokenProjection`, it would be helpful to have an example of equivalent configuration.

The old automount creates 3 files:

```
/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt
/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token
/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/namespace
```

If [the docs for service account token projection](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/#service-account-token-volume-projection) showed how to create the same 3 files, then migration should be quite simple.

**Why is this needed**:

All 3 of these files all seem important for using a service account inside a pod.

For example, the official Python Kubernetes client [requires both the token and the root CA certificate at those exact locations](https://github.com/kubernetes-client/python-base/blob/2da2b981ca806b25487ad92d01a2164815c18517/config/incluster_config.py#L72-L85) in order to load in-cluster config.

Also, the official `kubectl` CLI client does not support configuration via token file path, and will automatically look for those 3 files (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubectl/issues/927#issuecomment-693483957).

The [docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/#service-account-token-volume-projection) currently only give a vault-oriented example, adding audience to the token and skipping the root CA certificate and namespace files:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: nginx
spec:
  containers:
  - image: nginx
    name: nginx
    volumeMounts:
    - mountPath: /var/run/secrets/tokens
      name: vault-token
  serviceAccountName: build-robot
  volumes:
  - name: vault-token
    projected:
      sources:
      - serviceAccountToken:
          path: vault-token
          expirationSeconds: 7200
          audience: vault
```

Instead maybe change the sample to something like this, which would allow for easier migration:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: nginx
spec:
  containers:
    - image: nginx
      name: nginx
      volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount
          name: service-account
  serviceAccountName: build-robot
  volumes:
    - name: service-account
      projected:
        sources:
          - serviceAccountToken:
              path: token
              expirationSeconds: 7200
          - configMap:
              name: xyz # TODO
              items:
                - key: ca.crt
                  path: ca.crt
          - downwardAPI:
              items:
                - path: namespace
                  fieldRef:
                    fieldPath: metadata.namespace
```

The [original service account token projection proposal](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/design-proposals/storage/svcacct-token-volume-source.md#token-volume-projection) uses this approach, adding `ca.crt` and `namespace` together with `token` in the same projected volume.

The problem here is that I can't figure out a simple way to add the root CA certificate in my GKE cluster.

- The [fix](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/68812) for #68811 adds a `root-ca-cert-publisher`, but its documentation PR was not merged (https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/12963) and it's blocked (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubeadm/issues/1286) by the `BoundServiceAccountTokenVolume` (or [`RootCAConfigMap`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/service-accounts-admin/#bound-service-account-token-volume)?) alpha feature gate, so I'm not sure if this is the best recommendation?
- `kubeadm init` is [documented to create a `cluster-info` config map](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/setup-tools/kubeadm/implementation-details/#create-the-public-cluster-info-configmap) which according to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubeadm/issues/1286#issuecomment-576458208 includes the root CA, but I don't see this config map in GKE
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/61572#issuecomment-448487090 suggests `kubectl config view --raw --minify --flatten -o jsonpath='{.clusters[].cluster.certificate-authority-data}'`, but that doesn't seem right to run inside a pod

If the `ca.crt` issue could be solved, would it make sense to document migrating from `automountServiceAccountToken` to  `ServiceAccountTokenProjection`?

body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:
KubeProxy should remove the check to see if the source VIP ip exists in HNS as a prerequisite. It should also validate that the source vip passed in is valid (both a valid ip address and in the range of the network's subnet for both Ipv4 and ipv6).

**Why is this needed**:
When deploying Kubernetes with a CNI that uses HNS as the IPAM, it's not necessary to preallocate the source vip. Removing this check would make deployment easier for such CNIs.

body:
When we introduced this field in alpha we documented this as:

"	// Valid values are "OnRootMismatch" and "Always". If not specified defaults to "Always"."

But we aren't doing this strictly speaking. But if we did set the default to "Always", then it has implications for controllers who are hashing pod spec, because a k8s upgrade will cause all of these controllers to rollout a pod update now, which is not very desirable.

The discussion from slack:

> thockin @liggitt wrt defaulting fields under Pod - are we hard-banning this?  The whole API defaulting-per-version mechanism will kind of come apart if we do
12:10 PM
liggitt there are two problematic consumers of pod specs: 1) the kubelet mechanism for determining if a container needs to be restarted, 2) controller mechanisms for determining if a new rollout is required
12:10 PM
if those were resolved, we could allow it again
12:11 PM
defaulting-per-version doesn't impact pods until we have pods v2, right?
12:11 PM
thockin Well, we have PRs that are adding policy fields that transitively end up under pod
12:11 PM
so would trigger  the above
12:13 PM
The question here is really - are we on crack thinking that we can allow new fields  with default values which formalize the previously unstated behavior?  Or do we need to say that all such changes must have "not-specified" mean "whatever used to be implied".
12:13 PM
so versioned->internal would convert nil -> "ExplicitValue" and the same in reverse
12:14 PM
for v1
12:17 PM
msau42 is this problem specific to pods, or for any resource that is templated, for example, statefulset pvc templates?
12:17 PM
thockin It's particular to pods only because there are things that hash pod
12:18 PM
but it's not actually particular
12:19 PM
in general, how can anyone know that 2 reads of the same object are the same when a new field shows up?  Short of open-coding JUST the fields you care about (which will end up badly, too) you can't
12:19 PM
gnufied joined #api-reviews.
12:20 PM
thockin So maybe the right answer is to leave it nil in existing versions, make it explicit on conversion to internal, and nil on the way back to versioned.  Adding a v2 AFTER a field has been introduced can add an explicit default
12:21 PM
This would be a big change in guidance overall, but seems the only way to ensure the property that 2 reads of the same resource always produce the same non-status value
12:24 PM
msau42 what is the purpose of making it explicit in internal if the versioned read is nil?
12:25 PM
thockin Because 2 different aPI versions could have different defaults.
12:27 PM
msau42 so if v1 default was X and v2 default was Y, then if a consumer reads a v1 object that was created with v1, they get back nil. But if they read v1 of an object that was created with v2, they get back Y?
12:29 PM
thockin Yes.
12:29 PM
in v1, not-specified means X, but Y means Y.
12:30 PM
we already have a rule that if you add a field, it must have the same default in all EXISTING versions
12:30 PM
so if v2 default is Y, that implies v2 was added AFTER the field, meaning X and Y would be explicit.
12:32 PM
as I said - this is significantly different that existing guidance, so I will give @liggitt time to think and circle back to this.  I dislike forcing clients to encode implicit defaults, but that's the tradeoff.
12:32 PM

title: Explore `go buildmode` to simplfy building custom scheduler binary

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

labels.name: sig/architecture
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Architecture.

labels.name: lifecycle/stale
labels.description: Denotes an issue or PR has remained open with no activity and has become stale.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

body:
## Background

Kube scheduler, along with other Kubernetes core components, provides extensions to build custom scheduling logic to fit different business needs. As of today, the scheduler provides 3 ways to achieve that:

1. scheduler framework (the most recommended)
2. scheduler extender
3. multiple schedulers

The 2nd and 3rd options don't apply to the subject of this issue, but let me mention a bit here how they basically work and their shortages: the extender communicates the interim scheduling results with an external extender webhook, which in turn imposes extra HTTP communication and marshall/unmarshall overhead, and hence cannot apply to large-scale cluster; while for secondary schedulers, they may compete with each other on the limited node resources and if there is a conflict, the latter scheduled Pod will fail by kubelet - which cause unpleasant UX, and even worse, the failed Pod's `.spec.nodeName` won't be auto cleared, and hence will stay on that particular node until resources get released.

With that said, the most recommended way to customize scheduling logic is to build scheduler plugins via the scheduler framework. It keeps 100% functionalities of the vanilla scheduler - both core capabilities and so-called in-tree plugins, and also empower you to build compatible scheduling plugins.

## Challenge of scheduler plugins

The scheduler plugins function well as it builds (`go build`) the custom plugins based on the vanilla scheduler. And to avoid the shortages mentioned in multiple schedulers above, we usually recommend users to replace the vanilla scheduler with the custom scheduler as the single and universal scheduler image.

However, these 2 operational tasks are non-trivial indeed, and hence may prevent developers from exercising the scheduler framework.

## Maybe `go buildmode`?

Recently I came across `go buildmode`:

```
$ go help buildmode
...
	-buildmode=plugin
		Build the listed main packages, plus all packages that they
		import, into a Go plugin. Packages not named main are ignored.
```

Probably we can leverage this to simplify the process to plumb custom plugins into the vanilla scheduler image. The most desirable results would be:

- the vanilla scheduler image can be used as-is
- custom scheduling plugins can be glued by a scheduler config argument - to specify the plugins path

In this way, a cluster-admin/devops would mount the plugins in and tweak ComponentConfig args in the scheduler deployment manifest. And the out-of-tree plugins then have a smaller/neat scope and can be managed with much less efforts.

/sig scheduling
/priority important-longterm

body:
#### What would you like to be added:

To deploy cluster addon that communicates with Kubelet (for example Metrics Server), cluster administrator needs to figure out Kubelet endpoints, certificates and authorization configuration and pass it to Metrics Server. This can lead to errors and user frustration  as most applications deployed on Kubernetes just work out of the box. 

Some problems:
* Nodes publish multiple addresses, but it's not clear which one to use. 
* Kubelet can use self-signed certificate, which requires disabling verification on MS side.
* If Kubelet has not configured authorization, then MS cannot use secure port and should require action on user side.

Solving this problem would require Kubelet to publish additional some configuration available locally on node to cluster. Information:
* Preferred address to use
* Self signed certificate
* Authorization configuration

#### Why is this needed:

This work is part of simplifying Metrics Server configuration to remove number of support tickets due to misconfiguration.
https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/metrics-server/issues/688. I expect that this work should also benefit any other addon communicating with Kubelets.

#### Notes

I know that kubelet has Dynamic Configuration that publishes some of information mentioned above, but I would want to start discussion how we can make sure it can solve this problem.

title: Custom resource create might succeed after CRD deletion, leaving data in etcd

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: help wanted
labels.description: Denotes an issue that needs help from a contributor. Must meet "help wanted" guidelines.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->

Either `/priority important-longterm` or `/priority backlog`

#### What happened:

The chance for the race condition is low. There is a narrow window where CRs can be created after the CRD gets deleted:

1. CR create request hit API server; API server noted the request [isn't terminating yet](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2a05c786008f9d0592c0ea51dfb49124bc622100/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/customresource_handler.go#L316), went ahead to prepare the handler
2. CRD delete request hit API server; CRD got [marked as terminating](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2a05c786008f9d0592c0ea51dfb49124bc622100/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/registry/customresourcedefinition/etcd.go#L148-L149)
3. CRD finalizer controller deleted existing CRs, removed [CRD cleanup finalizer](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2a05c786008f9d0592c0ea51dfb49124bc622100/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/controller/finalizer/crd_finalizer.go#L125-L174); CRD got deleted from etcd
4. API server [served the CR create request](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2a05c786008f9d0592c0ea51dfb49124bc622100/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/customresource_handler.go#L380), wrote data to etcd
5. destruction of the CR etcd client happened after `#3`, and might [last a long time](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2a05c786008f9d0592c0ea51dfb49124bc622100/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/customresource_handler.go#L583-L584) to allow `#4` to happen-- as long as `#4` [registered itself to the in-flight requests](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2a05c786008f9d0592c0ea51dfb49124bc622100/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/customresource_handler.go#L379)

The window is narrow. It is more likely either
- `#4` happened before `#3`-- the created CR got cleaned up by CRD finalizer
- `#4` happened after `#5`-- the create request would get a 503 Service Unavailable "apiserver is shutting down"

#### What you expected to happen:

No CR data persists in etcd after CRD deletion. 

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

- Add `time.Sleep` to make triggering the race easier: https://github.com/roycaihw/kubernetes/commit/7f4d6cbf7ac015edd5dc799c97ab5bc49f814f1c
- `kubectl apply -f crd.yaml` (example yaml: https://github.com/roycaihw/kubernetes/commit/0d3732cab99e79118eeafca0534e1c28dc8c67d9)
- `kubectl apply -f cr.yaml`; immediately `kubectl delete -f crd.yaml` in parallel
- See the CRD was deleted immediately, the CR got 201 CREATED 10s later
- Moreover, re-create the CRD and see the old CR still exists `kubectl apply -f crd.yaml && kubectl get crontabs`

#### Anything else we need to know?:

The narrow window becomes a concern if we increase the latency between `#1` and `#4`, which is what https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/96403 is doing. A mitigation is to read the latest CRD from cache after the increased latency and right before `#4`, to make sure the window is still small: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/96403/commits/6ddc1eb1fb3c85a241a87ccf66c142be578ff4e3. The race still exist, but it isn't getting worse. 

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): HEAD

/sig api-machinery

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/

#### What happened:

We noticed on our clusters on bare-metal that nodes do not become `NotReady` after a read only remount by the kernel e.g. due to a filesystem corruption. This causes pods to get scheduled on the node but fail to start as the kubelet cannot create directories for the pod.

#### What you expected to happen:

Kubelet should notice that it cannot write to the filesystem and prevent further pods from being scheduled on the node.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

1. install minikube and virtualbox
2. minikube start --driver=virtualbox -n 2
```
$ kubectl get nodes
NAME           STATUS   ROLES                  AGE    VERSION
minikube       Ready    control-plane,master   3m6s   v1.20.2
minikube-m02   Ready    <none>                 119s   v1.20.2
```
3. start a pod on a machine
```
kubectk get pod                              
NAME                       READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
hello-1-657cb9b9f5-brbf4   1/1     Running   0          16s
```
4. ssh into the worker node and trigger an emergency readonly remount (simulate a filesystem failure) then wait a few minutes
```
minikube ssh --node minikube-m02
echo u | sudo tee /proc/sysrq-trigger
```
5. node stays ready and attracts new pods
```
kubectl get node
NAME           STATUS   ROLES                  AGE     VERSION
minikube       Ready    control-plane,master   10m     v1.20.2
minikube-m02   Ready    <none>                 9m12s   v1.20.2

kubectl get pod
NAME                       READY   STATUS              RESTARTS   AGE
hello-1-657cb9b9f5-brbf4   1/1     Running             0          8m41s
hello-2-7ddff58f66-6mgbm   0/1     ContainerCreating   0          16s

kubectl describe pod hello-2-7ddff58f66-6mgbm
...
Events:
  Type     Reason       Age               From               Message
  ----     ------       ----              ----               -------
  Normal   Scheduled    33s               default-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/hello-2-7ddff58f66-6mgbm to minikube-m02
  Warning  Failed       9s (x3 over 33s)  kubelet            error making pod data directories: mkdir /var/lib/kubelet/pods/b7d540b3-c949-4fad-becc-76743a654467: read-only file system
  Warning  FailedMount  1s (x7 over 33s)  kubelet            MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "default-token-5fjs5" : mkdir /var/lib/kubelet/pods/b7d540b3-c949-4fad-becc-76743a654467: read-only file system
```

#### Anything else we need to know?:

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.20.2 (also reproducible in latest 1.18.x and 1.19.x)
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: bare metal
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): Flatcar Container Linux by Kinvolk 2605.12.0 (Oklo)

body:
#### What would you like to be added:

The detection and recovery of kubelet processes that hang or enter hot loops as implemented in PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/94210

Systemd supports the detection and recovery of hung processes as well as terminated ones, but requires co-operation of the daemon under its control.

Currently kubelet only facilitates systemd to detect and recover from abnormal termination.

#### Why is this needed:

kubelet is the sole mechanism for starting, stopping, and monitoring the state of Pods on a node.
Without a functioning kubelet, the cluster cannot know the state of its Pods or react to failures and config changes.

This is especially relevant for resources with at-most-one semantics such as RWO volumes and StatefulSets which must not start duplicate copies while they are still thought to be running on the node with a failed kubelet.

The bar for kubelet's availability is therefore necessarily high, which is why kubelet.service already uses Type=notify to automatically respawn failed daemons.

There are however, additional failure modes that do not result in the kubelet process being terminated.
In the event of a hung process, hot loop, or resource starvation, the kubelet daemon is alive but non-functional from the cluster's perspective.

In a perfect world none of these scenarios would ever occur, but with minimal effort, Systemd is capable of detecting and recovering the kubelet process from these scenarios automatically even when they do.

body:
**What happened**:
Using this StorageClass:
```
kind: StorageClass
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: azurediskdedicated
provisioner: kubernetes.io/azure-disk
parameters:
  kind: dedicated
  storageaccounttype: Standard_LRS
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: Immediate
```

Volume provisioning fails with:
```
I0120 17:59:27.455266       1 pv_controller.go:1610] failed to save volume "pvc-984f8276-52dc-41a3-9a77-a2ea24139d5d" for claim "default/testclaim": persistentvolumes "pvc-984f8276-52dc-41a3-9a77-a2ea24139d5d" is forbidden: error querying AzureDisk volume jsafrane-1-lkb56-dynamic-pvc-984f8276-52dc-41a3-9a77-a2ea24139d5d: invalid disk URI: https://clusterp1uo5.blob.core.windows.net/vhds/jsafrane-1-lkb56-dynamic-pvc-984f8276-52dc-41a3-9a77-a2ea24139d5d.vhd
```

The error comes from admission plugin that adds / sets labels to PersistentVolume object. It expects that `https://clusterp1uo5....` has a very specific format, which "dedicated" disks don't have:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/106bc7e50d6dfdacbaa4be93f35c1af7a946a10d/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/azure/azure_managedDiskController.go#L324-L330

- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.19.1

cc @andyzhangx
