labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
The first call to `UpdatePod` for a failed (rejected) pod sets `terminatingAt` but doesn't set `termitatedAt` because we need to run `SyncTerminatingPod` to clean up:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/22e92c6a95c92329578154736a1e688f5ec35c87/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L803-L812

However, the first time we enter the pod worker loop, I'm pretty sure we end up saying the pod can never start, and exit the worker loop:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/22e92c6a95c92329578154736a1e688f5ec35c87/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L1234

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/22e92c6a95c92329578154736a1e688f5ec35c87/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L1180

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/22e92c6a95c92329578154736a1e688f5ec35c87/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L1047-L1049

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/22e92c6a95c92329578154736a1e688f5ec35c87/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L1240-L1243

Unless I'm missing something, this looks like a bug with how we handle clean up in this case. But, if that cleanup isn't actually necessary, then maybe we can just set the `terminatedAt` timestamp immediately for the failed pod, which would cause it to be considered inactive.

Note: There is a test case that is suppose to cover this, but since the test uses a fake cache implementation that doesn't match the defaulting logic of the real cache, it skips over the code that generates the terminating sync status.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/22e92c6a95c92329578154736a1e688f5ec35c87/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers_test.go#L750-L771

Copied from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136508#issuecomment-4411520959

### What happened?

title: apiserver: return 4xx instead of 500 when pod runtimeClassName is empty

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
### What happened?

The Kubernetes API Server returns HTTP 500 Internal Server Error when creating a Pod whose `spec.runtimeClassName` is set to an empty string.

The following request sets `spec.runtimeClassName` to `""`:

```bash
curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{"spec":{"runtimeClassName":""}}'
```
Actual response:
```bash
{
  "kind": "Status",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "metadata": {},
  "status": "Failure",
  "message": "resource name may not be empty",
  "code": 500
}
```
The request is invalid or incomplete, but the API Server returns an internal server error.

### What did you expect to happen?

The API Server should return a client-side error, such as HTTP 400 Bad Request or HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity, instead of HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.

Since `spec.runtimeClassName` is invalid when it is an empty string, the error should be reported as a validation error rather than an internal server error.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Start a Kubernetes cluster with an affected version.
2. Start a local API proxy:

```bash
kubectl proxy --port=8001
```
3. Send the following request:
```bash
curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{"spec":{"runtimeClassName":""}}'
```
4. Observe that the API Server returns HTTP 500:
```bash
{
  "kind": "Status",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "metadata": {},
  "status": "Failure",
  "message": "resource name may not be empty",
  "code": 500
}
```

### Anything else we need to know?

This issue was found during RESTful API fuzzing of the Kubernetes API Server.

The request is invalid because `runtimeClassName` is empty and the Pod body is incomplete. However, this should not be surfaced as HTTP 500. It appears that an empty `runtimeClassName` is propagated to runtime class lookup logic and reported as an internal error.

This behavior is reproducible in my tests on Kubernetes v1.33.1 and v1.36.0.

title: Job controller manageJob() returns active=0 during backoff, causing "cannot set more ready pods than active" status update rejection

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/apps
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Apps.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

When the Job controller's `manageJob()` function determines that replacement pods are needed but a backoff timer is active (due to recent pod failures), it returns `active=0` to the caller. The caller uses this value to set `job.Status.Active=0` in a status update, while `job.Status.Ready` retains the real informer-computed count. The apiserver validation `RejectMoreReadyThanActivePods` (GA in 1.33 via `JobManagedBy`) correctly rejects this inconsistent update with 422.

Because the status update fails, the controller cannot:
- Flush `uncountedTerminatedPods`
- Remove `batch.kubernetes.io/job-tracking` finalizers from terminated pods

This causes pods to appear stuck in Terminating state and job status to become stale.

**Root cause:** Two locations in `manageJob()` return a hardcoded `0` instead of the real `active` count when backoff is active:

```go
// Location 1: global backoff
if remainingTime > 0 {
    jm.enqueueSyncJobWithDelay(logger, job, remainingTime)
    return 0, metrics.JobSyncActionPodsCreated, nil  // BUG: should be `active`
}

// Location 2: per-index backoff
if remainingTime > 0 {
    jm.enqueueSyncJobWithDelay(logger, job, remainingTime)
    return 0, metrics.JobSyncActionPodsCreated, nil  // BUG: should be `active`
}
```

The caller sets `job.Status.Active = active` (the returned 0), while `job.Status.Ready` stays at the informer count (e.g., 5). Result: `5 > 0` → 422.

The `0` was likely a "don't care" value from before `RejectMoreReadyThanActivePods` validation existed. Every other return path in `manageJob` returns the real active count.

### What did you expect to happen?

The backoff early-return in `manageJob()` should return the real active pod count (unchanged, since no pods were created or deleted), not 0.

Proposed fix:
```diff
     if remainingTime > 0 {
         jm.enqueueSyncJobWithDelay(logger, job, remainingTime)
-        return 0, metrics.JobSyncActionPodsCreated, nil
+        return active, metrics.JobSyncActionPodsCreated, nil
     }
```

Returning `active` (initialized at top of `manageJob` as `int32(len(jobCtx.activePods))`) means "I didn't create or delete any pods" — the correct semantics for a backoff deferral.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```bash
# 1. Create a Job
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: repro-ready-active
  namespace: default
spec:
  parallelism: 30
  completions: 30
  backoffLimit: 500
  completionMode: Indexed
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: worker
        image: registry.k8s.io/pause:3.9
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "10m"
            memory: "16Mi"
EOF

# 2. Wait for all pods to be Running+Ready
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pods -l job-name=repro-ready-active --timeout=120s

# 3. Force-delete 25 pods simultaneously
kubectl get pods -l job-name=repro-ready-active -o name | head -25 | \
  xargs -P25 kubectl delete --force --grace-period=0

# 4. Observe: job status is frozen, KCM logs show error
kubectl get job repro-ready-active -o jsonpath='active={.status.active} ready={.status.ready} failed={.status.failed}'
# Output: active=30 ready=30 failed=   (stale — doesn't reflect reality)

# KCM logs show:
# "Unhandled Error" err="syncing job: tracking status: adding uncounted pods to status:
#   Job.batch \"repro-ready-active\" is invalid: status.ready: Invalid value: 5:
#   cannot set more ready pods than active"

# 5. Bug self-resolves after ~10 min when backoff expires (if no new failures arrive)
```

### Anything else we need to know?

- The bug fires on any multi-pod Job that experiences a pod failure while other pods are still Ready. For single failures (10s backoff), it produces a few 422 errors that self-resolve. For mass failures (spot reclamation, node failure → backoff capped at 10 min), it causes visible stuck pods and stale status for the full backoff duration.
- No data loss occurs. The job eventually completes. The impact is operational: stuck Terminating pods, stale status, KCM error log spam.
- The `metrics.JobSyncActionPodsCreated` label on the return is also incorrect (no pods were created), but that's cosmetic.


### Kubernetes version

<details>

Bug present from 1.31 (when `RejectMoreReadyThanActivePods` was introduced, beta default-on) through latest master. Unconditional from 1.33 (`JobManagedBy` GA).

Tested and reproduced on 1.35.


</details>

<details>
AWS (EKS), but not cloud-specific. Reproducible on any cluster.
</details>

title: CPU manager AddContainer does not write cgroup cpuset, reconciler never corrects mismatches

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
#### What happened?

CPU manager's `AddContainer` sets `lastUpdateState` to the desired cpuset without calling `updateContainerCPUSet` to write the cgroup. The reconciler compares `desired` vs `lastUpdateState` — since they always match, it never detects or corrects cpuset mismatches caused by the container runtime.

Additionally, the cpuset is not applied before the container starts. The container inherits the pod-level cgroup cpuset and only gets the correct dedicated cpuset when the reconciler runs (up to 10 seconds later, if the bug above didn't prevent it entirely).

#### What did you expect to happen?

The container should have its dedicated cpuset written to the cgroup before it starts, and the reconciler should detect and correct any subsequent mismatches.

#### How to reproduce it?

1. Create a Guaranteed QoS pod with `cpuManagerPolicy: static` and integer CPU requests
2. Check the container's cgroup `cpuset.cpus.effective` immediately after the container starts
3. Compare with `cpu_manager_state` — they may not match
4. Wait 10+ seconds — the reconciler still does not correct the mismatch because `lastUpdateState` was set without writing

Observed on Dell R760xa with KubeVirt VMs using `dedicatedCpuPlacement` + `guestMappingPassthrough`. The compute container's cgroup showed all odd CPUs (NUMA 1) while `cpu_manager_state` showed CPUs 4,6,68,70 (NUMA 0). The mismatch persisted indefinitely.

KubeVirt's virt-launcher reads `cpuset.cpus.effective` once at startup to build guest NUMA topology. With the wrong cpuset, it generated QEMU memory bindings for NUMA 1, but `cpuset.mems` only allowed NUMA 0, causing `set_mempolicy: Invalid argument`.

#### Anything else we need to know?

The bug is in `pkg/kubelet/cm/cpumanager/cpu_manager.go` in the `AddContainer` function.

/kind bug
/sig node
/area kubelet

title: Kubelet regression in 1.32, 1.31 and possibly 1.33 and 1.34 where pods get stuck in RunContainerError on OS with cgroupv1

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What happened?

We observed a Kubelet regression in 1.32 and 1.31 (and similar symptoms in 1.33 and 1.34) where pods get stuck in `RunContainerError` on Rocky Linux 8.6 OS which uses cgroup v1. While upgrading Kubernetes from 1.30 to 1.31 and 1.32, we observe the issue once we put the node out of maintenance mode.

The issue is observed with Containerd 1.7 and 1.6 as well.

We initially opened this issue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/138388 however at the time we didn't know what caused the regression and what versions were affected. We performed a git bisect (using GKE internal builds) and identified the regression was introduced in PR [#131018](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/131018). This commit was merged into 1.34 and backported all the way to 1.31. Kubelet works perfectly in the commits immediately preceding this PR.

Following this commit, we observe a massive spike in masked paths. Given our 96-core machines, the `thermal_throttle` paths alone add 96 new entries to the maskedPaths array for every container:

```
crictl inspect 4a44698096076 | jq '.info.config.linux.security_context.masked_paths'
[
  "/proc/asound",
  "/proc/acpi",
  "/proc/interrupts",
  "/proc/kcore",
  "/proc/keys",
  "/proc/latency_stats",
  "/proc/timer_list",
  "/proc/timer_stats",
  "/proc/sched_debug",
  "/proc/scsi",
  "/sys/firmware",
  "/sys/devices/virtual/powercap",
  "/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/thermal_throttle",
  "/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu1/thermal_throttle",
  "/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu2/thermal_throttle",
  "/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu3/thermal_throttle",
[...]
  "/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu94/thermal_throttle",
  "/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu95/thermal_throttle"
]
```

We suspect that this high volume of masked paths is causing kernel-level starvation or resource exhaustion on our cgroup v1 / Rocky 8.6 nodes when scheduling a large number of multi-container pods.

So far we compiled,  we compiled a custom Kubelet that breaks the loop after adding the first `thermal_throttle` path. Under load testing, the system remained completely stable with this patch:

```
v1.32.13-gke.100) ~/gke-internal/kubernetes $ git diff
diff --git a/pkg/securitycontext/util.go b/pkg/securitycontext/util.go
index 5e000f93333..f1889a8cff8 100644
--- a/pkg/securitycontext/util.go
+++ b/pkg/securitycontext/util.go
@@ -213,6 +213,7 @@ var (
                        path := fmt.Sprintf("/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu%d/thermal_throttle", cpu)
                        if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
                                maskedPaths = append(maskedPaths, path)
+                               break
                        }
                }
 
(v1.32.13-gke.100) ~/gke-internal/kubernetes $ 
``` 

The following kernel settings currently resolve the issue so it is not tracking kernel memory:
  * Set the `cgroup.memory=nokmem` config during the OS upgrade.
  * Reboot the node as part of the OS upgrade process.
  * Upgrade K8s to 1.31

Not tracking kernel memory to mitigate this issue is a big NO for us.

Questions & Asks for the Community: 

The PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/131018 that introduced this regression states that it "Mitigates potential Thermal Side-Channel Vulnerability Exploit," linking to a Moby security advisory ([GHSA-6fw5-f8r9-fgfm](https://github.com/moby/moby/security/advisories/GHSA-6fw5-f8r9-fgfm)). However, this link currently returns a 404 error, making it difficult for us to evaluate the exact threat model.

- Could you provide more context on the specific vulnerability (#131018 mitigates) since the advisory link is dead?

- What are the practical security consequences of bypassing or reverting this specific thermal_throttle masking change?

- Is there an appetite to introduce a feature gate or Kubelet flag to bypass this specific path masking for environments where it causes kernel starvation?

Any suggestions, alternative fixes, or guidance from the OSS community would be greatly appreciated.

### What did you expect to happen?

in 1.31, 1.32, 1.33 and 1.34, cgroupv1 is not yet deprecated https://kubernetes.io/blog/2024/08/13/kubernetes-v1-31-release/#cgroup-v1-enters-the-maintenance-mode  (although it was put in maintenance mode), Kubelet should not yet be unhappy with cgroupv1 until it is fully deprecated. The expectation is that this regression should not happen in Kubelet 1.32, 1.31, 1.33 and 1.34.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Rocky Linux 8.6 OS with cgroup v1

K8s version 1.32.13

Run the following deployment 

```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: multi-container-workload
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 300

    matchLabels:

      labels:
        app: multi-container-workload
    spec:

body:
### What happened?

When TopologyManager runs in `best-effort` mode, it may select a cross-NUMA preferred hint (e.g. `{0,1}`) based on CPU/GPU alignment. The static Memory Manager then rejects this hint at allocation time because one of those NUMA nodes already holds a single-node allocation from an earlier container in the same pod.
This surfaces as `UnexpectedAdmissionError` with the message:
```
[memorymanager] preferred hint violates NUMA node allocation
```
even though sufficient memory resources exist on the node.

## Root cause

The static Memory Manager enforces a strict invariant: a NUMA node cannot participate in both single-node and cross-node allocations simultaneously ([upstream docs](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2021/08/11/kubernetes-1-22-feature-memory-manager-moves-to-beta/#single-vs-cross-numa-node-allocation)). TopologyManager's best-effort policy is unaware of this constraint when scoring hints, so it can choose a cross-NUMA affinity that the Memory Manager will reject as a hard error during `Allocate()`.
The mismatch exists on both allocation paths:
- **Pod-level:** `policy_static.go` → `allocatePod()`
- **Container-level:** `policy_static.go` → `Allocate()`


### What did you expect to happen?

When TopologyManager is running in `best-effort` mode, a pod with sufficient resources on the node should be admitted successfully. If the preferred cross-NUMA hint conflicts with the Memory Manager's single-vs-cross allocation invariant, the system should either:

1. Avoid selecting that hint in the first place (by incorporating the Memory Manager's constraints into hint preference scoring), or
2. Fall back to a compatible NUMA affinity instead of hard-failing

The pod should not be rejected with `UnexpectedAdmissionError` when allocatable resources exist.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

## Reproduction scenario
On a multi-NUMA system (e.g. Grace-family GB200):
1. Configure kubelet with `--topology-manager-policy=best-effort` and `--memory-manager-policy=Static`
2. Submit a Guaranteed pod with multiple containers
3. First container gets a single-NUMA memory allocation on node `{0}`
4. Second container's best-effort preferred hint is `{0,1}` (driven by CPU/device alignment)
5. Memory Manager rejects `{0,1}` because node 0 already has a single-node allocation
6. Pod fails admission with `UnexpectedAdmissionError`

Switching `--topology-manager-scope` from `pod` to `container` does not eliminate the problem , container ordering can still trigger the same conflict.


### Anything else we need to know?

## Possible directions
- **Memory Manager participates in hint preference scoring:** mark cross-NUMA hints as non-preferred when the target NUMA nodes already have single-node allocations, so TopologyManager avoids them during merging
- **TopologyManager re-evaluates on allocation failure:** if `Allocate()` fails, TopologyManager tries the next-best hint instead of hard-failing
- **Memory Manager falls back gracefully:** instead of returning an error, attempt to find a compatible affinity that satisfies the single-vs-cross invariant
- 
## References
- PR: [#137280 ] (see PR description and review discussion on best-effort-vs-strict admission mismatch)
- TODO breadcrumbs added at both error sites in `pkg/kubelet/cm/memorymanager/policy_static.go`
- Upstream blog on single-vs-cross NUMA rule: https://kubernetes.io/blog/2021/08/11/kubernetes-1-22-feature-memory-manager-moves-to-beta/#single-vs-cross-numa-node-allocation

body:
### What happened?

This seems to be a corner case in the "Ensure secret pulled images" [feature](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2535).

1. pre-load an image from repo X behind kubelet's back
2. deploy pod A, which references the image from repo X, **without** specifying a pull secret and with `imagePullPolicy: Never`; delete pod A
3. deploy pod B, referencing the same (in terms of identical content digest)  image but from a different repo Y, **using** a pull secret and default `imagePullPolicy`; delete pod B
4. deploy the same pod A again -> get `Container image "X..." is not present with pull policy of Never`

### What did you expect to happen?

Step (4) should continue working if step (1) did.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Note: @SergeyKanzhelev suggested using agnhost/fakeregistryserver, but I was unable to make the container runtime reach a pod running on the same cluster 🤷🏻 So here is a recipe using my private toy repo on quay. But any non-public repo will do.

# Preparation

1. Prepare an image. You can use any image (does not even need to run properly) that you can get both:
- preloaded on the cluster behind kubelet's back from repository X, and
- present on a private OCI repository Y.

Here is how I did it, after giving up on trying to get the multi-arch `registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10.1` mirrored (`error from registry: manifest invalid` 🙈).

```
$ echo foo >> README.md
$ cat > Dockerfile.foo <<EOF
FROM scratch
COPY ./README.md .
EOF
$ docker build -f Dockerfile.foo . --tag quay.io/mowsiany/qa-multi-arch-priv:foo
$ docker tag quay.io/mowsiany/qa-multi-arch-priv:foo quay.io/mowsiany/qa-multi-arch:foo
$ docker push quay.io/mowsiany/qa-multi-arch:foo # X
$ docker push quay.io/mowsiany/qa-multi-arch-priv:foo # Y
```

2. Get the image preloaded on a node. I used [image-prefetcher](https://github.com/stackrox/image-prefetcher):

```
$ go run github.com/stackrox/image-prefetcher/deploy@v0.4.3 --version v0.4.3 --namespace t foo > foo-prefetch.yaml
$ echo quay.io/mowsiany/qa-multi-arch:foo > image-list.txt
$ kubectl create ns t
$ kubectl create -n t configmap foo --from-file=images.txt=image-list.txt
$ kubectl apply -f foo-prefetch.yaml
```

# Run pod A

```
$ cat > pod-a-never.yaml << EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: testpod-a-never
  namespace: t
spec:
  nodeName: gke-mowsiany-test1-default-pool-1e8c798d-q93d # just to make things deterministic
  restartPolicy: Never
  containers:
  - name: test
    args:
    - foo
    imagePullPolicy: Never
    image: quay.io/mowsiany/qa-multi-arch:foo
EOF
$ kubectl apply -f pod-a-never.yaml 
pod/testpod-a-never created
$ kubectl describe -f pod-a-never.yaml
[...]
Events:
  Type     Reason   Age   From     Message
  ----     ------   ----  ----     -------
  Normal   Pulled   6s    kubelet  spec.containers{test}: Container image "quay.io/mowsiany/qa-multi-arch:foo" already present on machine and can be accessed by the pod
  Normal   Created  6s    kubelet  spec.containers{test}: Container created
[...]
$ kubectl delete -f pod-a-never.yaml 
pod "testpod-a-never" deleted from t namespace
```

# Run pod B

```
$ cat > pod-b-pull.yaml <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: testpod-b-pull
  namespace: t
spec:
  nodeName: gke-mowsiany-test1-default-pool-1e8c798d-q93d
  restartPolicy: Never
  containers:
  - name: test
    args:
    - foo
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    image: quay.io/mowsiany/qa-multi-arch-priv:foo
  imagePullSecrets:
  - name: mowsiany-robot1-pull-secret
EOF
$ kubectl -n t create -f ~/Downloads/mowsiany-robot1-secret.yml # Attached below
$ kubectl apply -f pod-b-pull.yaml 
pod/testpod-b-pull created
$ kubectl describe -f pod-b-pull.yaml 
[...]
Events:
  Type     Reason   Age   From     Message
  ----     ------   ----  ----     -------
  Normal   Pulling  7s    kubelet  spec.containers{test}: Pulling image "quay.io/mowsiany/qa-multi-arch-priv:foo"
  Normal   Pulled   7s    kubelet  spec.containers{test}: Successfully pulled image "quay.io/mowsiany/qa-multi-arch-priv:foo" in 285ms (285ms including waiting). Image size: 4601 bytes.
[...]
$ kubectl delete -f pod-b-pull.yaml 
pod "testpod-b-pull" deleted from t namespace
```

# Run pod A again

```
$ kubectl apply -f pod-a-never.yaml 
pod/testpod-a-never created
$ kubectl describe -f pod-a-never.yaml 
[...]
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age              From     Message
  ----     ------             ----             ----     -------
  Warning  ErrImageNeverPull  3s (x3 over 4s)  kubelet  spec.containers{test}: Container image "quay.io/mowsiany/qa-multi-arch:foo" is not present with pull policy of Never
  Warning  Failed             3s (x3 over 4s)  kubelet  spec.containers{test}: Error: ErrImageNeverPull

body:
### Which jobs are flaking?

pull-kubernetes-kind-dra-all, an optional presubmit. The periodic ci-kind-dra-all has not shown this in two weeks.

Triage: https://storage.googleapis.com/k8s-triage/index.html?pr=1&job=pull-kubernetes-kind-dra-all%24&text=TLS%20handshake%20timeout%7Chttp2%3A%20client%20connection%20lost

### Which tests are flaking?

In [run 2103785290568044544](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/pr-logs/pull/142411/pull-kubernetes-kind-dra-all/2103785290568044544) 149 specs passed, 2 specs failed, and the ReportAfterSuite Log Check also failed. They were `verifies cgroup inflation and container OOM adjustment with overhead mappings` and `does not delete generated claims when pod is restarting`. Both failed in `DeferCleanup` steps that could not reach the apiserver, one deleting a ServiceAccount and one in the driver builder:

```
[FAILED] deleting ServiceAccount.v1 dra-node-allocatable-resources-6568/dra-kubelet-plugin-dra-9dee3718f9e05859-service-account: Delete "https://127.0.0.1:40963/api/v1/namespaces/dra-node-allocatable-resources-6568/serviceaccounts/dra-kubelet-plugin-dra-9dee3718f9e05859-service-account": http2: client connection lost
In [DeferCleanup (Each)] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/dra/utils/deploy.go:933 @ 09/26/26 10:24:54.647
```

Expected: the cleanup deletes its objects and the suite ends green. Actual: the client gets `http2: client connection lost` or `TLS handshake timeout`. The Log Check fails too, because its pod listing timed out twice and because the kubelet on kind-worker2 reported a data race, filed as [#142439](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/142439).

In the two weeks to 2026-09-26, 19 of 143 completed runs hit one of those errors, 15 after [#142127](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142127) merged.

### Since when has it been flaking?

At least since 2026-09-14 in the triage data.

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-presubmits#pull-kubernetes-kind-dra-all

### Reason for failure (if possible)

The whole job stalls for up to a minute, and the API errors are what the test client sees during the stall. My best guess for the stall itself is CPU starvation under the pod's 2 CPU quota, and the evidence for that guess follows.

From 10:24:13Z to 10:25:12Z, kubelet log lines on all four kind nodes reach the journal up to 42 seconds late. containerd on kind-worker2 fails a task delete with `context deadline exceeded`, etcd logs a read-only apply that took 16.9 s, and kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler both lose their lease and restart. Apiserver and etcd did not restart, nothing was OOM killed, and etcd logs no slow disk sync.

Runs [2102022370477740032](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/pr-logs/pull/142277/pull-kubernetes-kind-dra-all/2102022370477740032) and [2101978783241211904](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/pr-logs/pull/141917/pull-kubernetes-kind-dra-all/2101978783241211904) from 2026-09-21 look the same, only worse: etcd applies of 45 to 52 s and repeated controller-manager restarts. A green run of the same PR shows none of this.

The podlogs fixes from [#141962](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141962) and [#142127](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142127) are in the base of that run, and [#142026](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142026) was closed as not needed yet.

The pod runs four race-enabled kind nodes and eight race-enabled ginkgo workers under a 2 CPU / 12Gi limit, and the kind node processes still size themselves to the node's CPU count ([kubernetes/test-infra#37733](https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/37733) fixed the runner leaf only).

A local replay with the same image, script and limits had 93% of its CFS periods throttled during the test phase and used 1.93 of its 2 cores. Control-plane log lines fell up to 18.7 s behind, the apiserver logged handler timeouts, and the run also ended with two failed specs plus a Log Check race, though the two failures were timeouts, not transport errors. It did not reproduce the lease losses, the transport errors or the cAdvisor race.

A control run with the quota raised to 8 CPUs had no throttled periods, used 2.75 cores and passed all 151 specs with a clean Log Check.

CI ran its specs in 1018 s under the same quota while the local replay needed 2349 s, so the workstation is slower than the Prow node for this job and the local percentages do not transfer one to one.

### Anything else we need to know?

As far as I can tell the same stalls take cAdvisor's `statfs` wrapper into its timeout path, which exposes the kubelet race in [#142439](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/142439).

This issue was written in part with the assistance of generative AI. The analysis and the local replay ran on my workstation and I reviewed the results.

### Relevant SIG(s)

/sig node
/sig testing
/wg device-management
/cc @pohly @troychiu

title: kubelet: cAdvisor GetVfsStats data race in a race-enabled DRA presubmit

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
### What happened?

The race-enabled `pull-kubernetes-kind-dra-all` presubmit reported a data race in the cAdvisor filesystem statistics code that the kubelet uses, and the suite's `[ReportAfterSuite] [sig-testing] Log Check` failed on it.

Observed run: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/pr-logs/pull/142411/pull-kubernetes-kind-dra-all/2103785290568044544 (149 specs passed, 2 specs failed, and the ReportAfterSuite Log Check also failed).

The report is a write/write race inside `GetVfsStats`, between the timeout return and the goroutine that runs `statfs`:

```
#### kubelet/kind-worker2

- DATA RACE:

      Write at 0x00c003a40010 by goroutine 569:
        github.com/google/cadvisor/lib/fs/vfs.GetVfsStats()
            github.com/google/cadvisor/lib@v0.60.6/fs/vfs/stats.go:59 +0x6ad
        github.com/google/cadvisor/lib/fs/tmpfs.(*tmpfsPlugin).GetStats()
            github.com/google/cadvisor/lib@v0.60.6/fs/tmpfs/plugin.go:51 +0x4f
        github.com/google/cadvisor/lib/fs.(*RealFsInfo).GetFsInfoForPath()
            github.com/google/cadvisor/lib@v0.60.6/fs/fs.go:401 +0x80b
        ...
      Previous write at 0x00c003a40010 by goroutine 26416:
        github.com/google/cadvisor/lib/fs/vfs.GetVfsStats.func1()
            github.com/google/cadvisor/lib@v0.60.6/fs/vfs/stats.go:49 +0x204
```

The kubelet reported it six times in that run, once per named result. `GetVfsStats` starts a goroutine that assigns the function's named results and returns `ctx.Err()` through the same variables after two seconds. They collide whenever the timeout path is taken before the goroutine has finished.

The code is the same on cAdvisor master.

### What did you expect to happen?

No data race in the kubelet when cAdvisor's `statfs` timeout fires.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Standalone: a test in `lib/fs/vfs` that replaces `statfs` with a stub returning after the timeout reproduces the race with `go test -race` on every run of the current code. It is part of [google/cadvisor#3938](https://github.com/google/cadvisor/pull/3938).

In CI it needs the timeout path to fire, which so far has happened on stalled nodes. That was the case in 8 runs of this job between 2026-09-21 and 2026-09-26 (7 in the triage data plus this one), on different PRs, on all four kind nodes and through both the `tmpfs` and the `overlay` plugin. The periodic ci-kind-dra-all has not reported it.

### Anything else we need to know?

Upstream: [google/cadvisor#3937](https://github.com/google/cadvisor/issues/3937), with the fix and its regression test in [google/cadvisor#3938](https://github.com/google/cadvisor/pull/3938).

This issue tracks picking up the fixed `github.com/google/cadvisor/lib` release in the kubelet and checking that the Log Check stops reporting the race.

The same run also had API transport errors during DRA cleanup and log collection. Those are tracked in [#142440](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/142440). The race reports sit inside those stalls, which as far as I can tell is what made `statfs` exceed the timeout. Nothing in this issue depends on how the stalls get resolved.

The triage window starts on 2026-09-12 and the first occurrence inside it is 2026-09-21. Earlier runs were not checked.

This issue was written in part with the assistance of generative AI. The race reproduction and the artifact checks were run on my workstation and I reviewed the results.

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ cat artifacts/kind/kind-control-plane/kubernetes-version.txt
v1.38.0-alpha.0.1172+4153926968cfc6
```

Built by the presubmit with `KUBE_RACE=-race`.

</details>

### Cloud provider

<details>

A kind cluster inside the Prow Docker-in-Docker job.

</details>

### OS version

<details>

The kind node image runs Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie) on the Prow node's Linux 6.12.103, linux/amd64 (`docker-info.txt` in the artifacts).

</details>

### Install tools

<details>

kind `v0.34.0-alpha+dd00511b043a27`, with a node image built from the presubmit checkout.

</details>

### Container runtime (CRI) and version (if applicable)

<details>

containerd v2.3.4 inside the kind nodes.

</details>

### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

<details>

None involved. The race is in cAdvisor's filesystem statistics path.

</details>

body:
﻿## What happened
While removing duplicated `[Slow]` spec execution between `ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-serial` and `ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-slow` (kubernetes/test-infra#37903), we looked into why the `[Slow]`-tagged ImageGC/GarbageCollect/MirrorPod specs in `test/e2e_node` cost ~30 minutes per host.

It's not image size or pull time — these use the standard few-MB e2e-test-images (pause, busybox, nginx-slim/agnhost). The time comes from wait/poll budgets hardcoded in the tests themselves, bound to production defaults:

- `image_gc_test.go`: two `[Slow]` specs poll for up to `checkGCUntil = 6 * time.Minute`, gated by kubelet's `ImageGCPeriod` (hardcoded to 5 minutes).
- `garbage_collector_test.go`: `setupDuration = 10 * time.Minute`, `garbageCollectDuration = 3 * time.Minute`.
- `mirror_pod_test.go`: several `2 * time.Minute` `Eventually` polls, plus a couple `5 * time.Minute` waits.

Polling more frequently doesn't help — these tests aren't slow because they check infrequently, they're waiting on a real kubelet-side event gated by a fixed period.

## What we'd like
Make `ImageGCPeriod` (and whatever governs the GC/mirror-pod wait windows above) configurable for e2e_node tests, so these specs aren't bound to the 5-minute production default and can run with a much shorter period in test.

## Context
- kubernetes/test-infra#37903 (merged) — removed duplicate execution of these specs as a stopgap
- kubernetes/kubernetes#142147 — the investigation that led here
- Requested by @kannon92 during the review of https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/37903

### Which jobs are failing?

### Which tests are failing?

Job-level failure — no individual test row has alerted in TestGrid. The alerting rows are only the harness rows:

- `ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-serial.Overall` (fail_count 3)
- `kubetest.Node Tests` (fail_count 3)

Per-build junit shows the underlying spec failure **rotates** — a different test fails each run, so no single spec hits the 3-consecutive alert threshold:

- Build `2100188711563038720` (2026-09-16): ubuntu host failed `[It] [sig-node] Summary API when querying /stats/summary under pressure [FeatureGate:KubeletPSI] should report Memory pressure in PSI metrics` — suite timeout (`[TIMEDOUT] A suite timeout occurred ... at summary_test.go:406`). cos host: 0 failures.
- Build `2100158262149124096`: cos host failed `[It] [sig-node] GarbageCollect Garbage Collection Test: Many Restarting Containers Should eventually garbage collect containers when we exceed the number of dead containers per container`. ubuntu host: 0 failures.
- Build `2100128061046394880`: ubuntu host failed `[It] [sig-node] StaticPod when the static pod has init container should be ready after init container is removed and kubelet restarts`. cos host: 0 failures.

### Since when has it been failing?

Observed failing today (2026-09-16) during the weekly TestGrid review — tab was FAILING at review time with 3 consecutive failures.

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-containerd#ci-node-e2e-serial

### Reason for failure (if possible)

Truncated `failure_message` from the TestGrid summary:

```
error during go run /home/prow/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e_node/...o/test-infra/jobs/e2e_node/containerd/image-config.yaml: exit status 1
```

This is the generic kubetest wrapper error — the real failure is the ginkgo spec failure above (different spec each run). Example tail from build `2100188711563038720/build-log.txt`:

```
command [... ginkgo --nodes=8 --skip="" --label-filter="!Flaky && Serial && NodeConformance" ...] failed with error: exit status 1
...
Step 'go run .../run_remote.go ... --image-config-file=/home/prow/go/src/k8s.io/test-infra/jobs/e2e_node/containerd/image-config.yaml' finished in 1h19m10s
...
Something went wrong: encountered 1 errors: [error during go run .../image-config.yaml: exit status 1]
```

Rotating single-spec failures across both ubuntu and cos hosts with a suite timeout in one run suggests job-level flakiness / timeout pressure rather than one broken test. Sibling job `ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-slow` shares the same wrapper signature but fails on different specs (ImageGC, MirrorPod) and started 15 days earlier (2026-09-01), so it is **not** clustered here — see #141806 discussion.

### Which jobs are flaking?

`ci-node-crio-eviction` (prow job history: https://prow.k8s.io/job-history/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-eviction)

Failed runs in the last two weeks (2026-08-30 to 2026-09-14, 79 runs total):

- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-eviction/2098887875868233728 (2026-09-12 21:34 UTC)
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-eviction/2098751980372496384 (2026-09-12 12:34 UTC)

- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-eviction/2097255139881521152 (2026-09-08 09:26 UTC)
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-eviction/2097187190898429952 (2026-09-08 04:56 UTC)
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-eviction/2095963365972119552 (2026-09-04 19:53 UTC)
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-eviction/2095827467854942208 (2026-09-04 10:53 UTC)

Triage: https://storage.googleapis.com/k8s-triage/index.html?test=ImageGCNoEviction&job=ci-node-crio-eviction

### Which tests are flaking?

`E2eNode Suite.[It] [sig-node] ImageGCNoEviction [Feature:Eviction] when we run containers that should cause DiskPressure should eventually evict all of the correct pods [Disruptive] [Serial] [Slow]`

### Since when has it been flaking?

At least since 2026-09-04. 7 of the last 79 runs (~9%) failed on this test. It is the only test in the job with a repeating failure; the other eviction tests in the job each failed at most once or twice in the same window.

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-cri-o#ci-node-crio-eviction

### Reason for failure (if possible)

The test never observes the `DiskPressure` node condition and times out after 10 minutes:

```
[FAILED] Timed out after 600.000s.
Expected
    <*errors.errorString | 0xc20192b67b0>: 
    NodeCondition: DiskPressure not encountered
    {
        s: "NodeCondition: DiskPressure not encountered",
    }
to be nil
In [It] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e_node/eviction_test.go:816 @ 09/12/26 22:52:42.738
```

Test timeline from the 2026-09-12 21:34 run:

```
STEP: setting up pods to be used by tests @ 09/12/26 22:42:38.701
STEP: Waiting for the expected pods to complete: [] @ 09/12/26 22:42:38.702
STEP: Waiting for node to have NodeCondition: DiskPressure @ 09/12/26 22:42:42.736
[FAILED] in [It] - k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e_node/eviction_test.go:816 @ 09/12/26 22:52:42.738
```

Environment from the failing run:

- OS image: Fedora CoreOS 44.20260817.3.2 (kernel 7.1.8-200.fc44.x86_64)
- Container runtime: cri-o://1.36.0
- Kubelet: v1.38.0-alpha.0.750+d5cbb79be9160f

The same signature appears in every one of the 7 failures. Passing runs do reach `DiskPressure`, so the pre-fill step that is supposed to push image storage over the eviction threshold is not reliably doing so on this image/runtime combination. Root cause not yet identified.

### Anything else we need to know?

- The job is currently `FLAKY` on TestGrid, not `FAILING`; the failure never hit 3 in a row.
- The closest prior issue is #130663 (ImageGCNoEviction on containerd, closed 2025-09-05). The failure mode there was different and this report is CRI-O only.
- Job config: https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/blob/master/config/jobs/kubernetes/sig-node/crio.yaml

title: kubelet: cut PLEG relist memory with CRI field projection + delta listing

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

body:
### What would you like to be added?

Two additive, opt-in changes to the CRI container/pod list calls so the kubelet's PLEG can stop decoding data it doesn't use:

1. **Field projection** Let the client request only the fields it needs (container id, state, and the `io.kubernetes.*` identity labels). The runtime omits everything else; older runtimes ignore the request field and behave as today.
2. **Delta listing** Let the client receive only the containers that changed since the last relist, instead of the full set every cycle.

### Why is this needed?
This came out of a hallway conversation at gRPCConf after my talk on CRI list streaming: a few gRPC maintainers and I got into why server-streaming a big response doesn't actually cut memory and the receiver still decodes the whole object graph. That pointed back at the kubelet's own CRI list path, so I went and measured it.

PLEG relists every container on the node about once a second and the kubelet decodes the entire
result each time. On dense or high-churn nodes this is large, mostly-redundant memory and CPU:

- Measured on master: ~18k containers with realistic annotations ≈ **1.57M allocations / ~79 MB
  held per relist**, re-paid every second.
- A full "fat" response can cross the 16 MiB CRI client cap (`maxMsgSize`), so `ListContainers`
  fails → PLEG stalls → node NotReady → and container GC can't run because it needs the same list
  (the "PLEG is not healthy" failure on high-churn nodes).
- The list is dominated by accumulated terminated containers that never change, re-decoded every
  second for nothing.

Existing work doesn't cover this axis: KEP-5825 (CRIListStreaming) fixes the per-message size cap but, in its own words, "does not reduce kubelet memory usage"; KEP-3386 / PLEGOnDemandRelist change relist *frequency*, not per-object payload.

I have a small benchmark harness (happy to push it) that measures decode + hold cost for full vs projected vs changed-only responses on representative payloads:

- **Projection** (measured): −45% memory, −65% wire, −34% allocations.
- **Changed-only** reduces it much further, since the list is mostly static terminated containers, the mechanism is measured and linear, and the exact factor depends on per-relist churn, which isn't instrumented upstream today (I model it at ≤1% for the accumulated-dead-container case, giving ≥99%; grounding that number would be step one of an alpha).
- **Correctness:** projection is client-declared per call, so it can't remove a field a consumer is reading and safe by construction. For the PLEG path specifically, the needed set is small and verified in code (event generation uses only id + state; container→pod mapping uses only `pod.uid`; the restart hash comes from `ContainerStatus`, not the list).

I'd like to bring this to sig-node as a KEP; opening this to track the problem and gather input.

/sig node
/kind feature

body:
### What happened?

On current Kubernetes master, the DRA kubelet plugin helper can generate an unusable automatic service socket endpoint when rolling updates are enabled with a valid long driver name.

With normal defaults:

```text
plugin directory:
/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/<driver name>

rolling service socket:
dra-<Pod UID>.sock
```

With a normal 36-byte Pod UID:

```text
full endpoint length = 71 + len(driverName)
```

A valid 37-byte driver name:

```text
abcdef.dra-example-driver.sigs.k8s.io
```

produces exactly a 108-byte endpoint under the affected implementation. Kubernetes requires AF_UNIX pathname-based endpoints to remain shorter than 108 bytes. A valid 63-byte driver name produces a 134-byte old-style endpoint.

### What did you expect to happen?

Valid DRA drivers using `RollingUpdate` with the normal automatic/default directory and socket naming should receive an AF_UNIX-compatible endpoint. Rolling instances must remain distinguishable.

This expectation does not extend to arbitrary custom `PluginDataDirectoryPath` values.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Use:

```go
DriverName("abcdef.dra-example-driver.sigs.k8s.io")
RollingUpdate("11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555")
// no PluginDataDirectoryPath override
// no PluginSocket override
```

An injected `PluginListener` can observe the real automatically generated endpoint without relying on the local macOS Unix-socket behavior.

The affected implementation produces:

```text
/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/abcdef.dra-example-driver.sigs.k8s.io/dra-11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555.sock
```

and its length is exactly 108 bytes. The valid 36-byte control driver produces 107 bytes.

### Anything else we need to know?

### Root cause

Rolling-update service socket naming includes the complete Pod UID. The default containing directory independently contains the complete driver name. The service socket did not check the combined full-path budget or fall back to a shorter basename.

### Relationship to existing work

- #139166 / #139623 addressed the rolling **registration socket** under `plugins_registry`.
- #139623 explicitly left `dra-<uid>.sock` service sockets unchanged.
- #141815 corrected the registration fallback's exact-108 boundary.
- #140837 added kubelet-side endpoint and driver validation but does not prevent this helper from generating an invalid automatic service endpoint.

### Affected scope

Reproduced on Kubernetes master at `3af569e862d19a046cdfd63cda837f9bb29da6fa`. Older releases were not verified.

No production incident was observed.

title: DRA: AllocationMode All errors for incomplete or invalid pools are not per-node failures

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: priority/important-longterm
labels.description: Important over the long term, but may not be staffed and/or may need multiple releases to complete.

labels.name: triage/accepted

labels.name: wg/device-management
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to WG Device Management.

body:
### What happened?

An `AllocationMode: All` request returns a plain error when a pool gathered for the candidate node is incomplete or invalid. In `validateDeviceRequest`, same code in the stable, incubating and experimental variants:

```go
if pool.IsIncomplete {
	return requestData, fmt.Errorf("claim %s, request %s: asks for all devices, but resource pool %s is currently being updated", klog.KObj(claim), request.name(), pool.PoolID)
}
if pool.IsInvalid {
	return requestData, fmt.Errorf("claim %s, request %s: asks for all devices, but resource pool %s is currently invalid", klog.KObj(claim), request.name(), pool.PoolID)
}
```

Neither wraps `internal.ErrFailedAllocationOnNode`. `DynamicResources.Filter` maps only that sentinel to an `Unschedulable` result for the node; anything else becomes a framework `Error`, and `checkNode` in `findNodesThatPassFilters` cancels the remaining node checks when one shows up.

The other failing cases in the same suite do wrap it. Probe on master `a818af18fe2`, logging `errors.Is(err, ErrFailedAllocationOnNode)` for every case that errors:

```
all-devices-of-the-incomplete-pool                                                false | claim claim-0, request req-0: asks for all devices, but resource pool driver-a/pool-1 is currently being updated
invalid-pool-is-error-if-no-other-device-can-be-allocated                          true  | invalid resource pools were encountered
duplicate-slice                                                                   true  | invalid resource pools were encountered
partitionable-devices-validation-error-on-non-targeting-slice                     true  | invalid resource pools were encountered
partitionable-devices-device-counter-consumption-references-unknown-counter-set    true  | invalid resource pools were encountered
partitionable-devices-same-counter-set-name-in-different-resource-slices           true  | invalid resource pools were encountered
```

Same in all three variants.

`IsIncomplete` does not need a malformed object. `GatherPools` sets it when the generation resolved for the node holds fewer slices than its declared `resourceSliceCount`, which is what a pool looks like while a driver is publishing a new generation.

### What did you expect to happen?

The check itself looks right and I would leave it alone: a slice that has not arrived may hold another device matching the request, so the allocator cannot know the full set yet.

The classification is the part that looks wrong. Wrapping the sentinel keeps the visible message, since it has no text of its own, and keeps the failure on one node:

```go
return requestData, fmt.Errorf("claim %s, request %s: asks for all devices, but resource pool %s is currently being updated%w",
	klog.KObj(claim), request.name(), pool.PoolID, internal.ErrFailedAllocationOnNode)
```

Other nodes then keep being evaluated, and if all of them fail the Pod is `Unschedulable`. `EventsToRegister` already lists `ResourceSlice` `Add` and `Update`, so the slice update that finishes the rollout requeues it. The invalid branch wants the same treatment.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

`all-devices-of-the-incomplete-pool` in `allocatortesting/allocator_testing.go` already reaches the incomplete branch. Adding this next to the existing `expectError` assertion produces the output above:

```go
if err != nil {
	t.Logf("PROBE %s errors.Is=%v", name, errors.Is(err, internal.ErrFailedAllocationOnNode))
}
```

No case covers the invalid branch today.

### Anything else we need to know?

Same classification shape as #141214 and #141338, different trigger. Those need a malformed stored per-device `nodeSelector`; this one fires during an ordinary generation rollout. Filing separately so the accepted scope of #141214 stays as it is.

title: DeviceTaintRule with deviceSelector omitted blocks device allocation cluster-wide, including adminAccess claims, contradicting documented behavior

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/scheduling

labels.name: sig/node

labels.name: wg/device-management
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to WG Device Management.

body:
### What happened?

A `DeviceTaintRule` with the `deviceSelector` field entirely omitted (not an empty `{}` object
-- the field itself absent) makes every device on every node, across every driver and pool,
untolerated and therefore unschedulable -- not just whatever devices the taint was meant to
target.

Live-verified on a freshly-created kind cluster running v1.37.0 GA with **no non-default
feature gates set at all** (`DynamicResourceAllocation`/`DRADeviceTaints`/`DRADeviceTaintRules`
are all GA and enabled by default at this release):

1. An ordinary `ResourceClaim` targeting one device (`gpu-0`) allocates and its Pod runs, with
   zero `DeviceTaintRule`s present.
2. Apply a `DeviceTaintRule` with `taint.effect: NoSchedule` and `deviceSelector` omitted:
   ```yaml
   apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
   kind: DeviceTaintRule
   metadata:
     name: taint-no-selector
   spec:
     taint:
       key: example.com/no-selector-test
       value: "true"
       effect: NoSchedule
   ```
3. The exact same claim/Pod from step 1, recreated, now fails to schedule (`FailedScheduling`,
   `cannot allocate all claims`).
4. Also confirmed on a 4-device pool: every device becomes unschedulable, not just one --
   including a claim declaring `adminAccess: true`, which is otherwise documented to bypass
   ordinary device exclusivity but is not exempted from `DeviceTaintRule` enforcement.
5. Deleting only the `DeviceTaintRule` (no other change) immediately restores every
   previously-blocked claim to allocate successfully.



### What did you expect to happen?

According to the field's own documentation (`kubectl explain devicetaintrule.spec.deviceSelector`):

> The empty selector matches all devices. Without a selector, no devices are matches [sic].

A `DeviceTaintRule` with `deviceSelector` omitted should match **zero** devices and have no
scheduling effect -- the opposite of what actually happens.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?



1. Create a cluster running v1.37.0 (no special feature gates required).
2. Install any DRA driver advertising at least one device (repro used
   `kubernetes-sigs/dra-example-driver` v0.4.0).
3. Create an ordinary `ResourceClaim` + Pod referencing one device; confirm it runs.
4. Apply a `DeviceTaintRule` with any `taint` and `deviceSelector` omitted entirely.
5. Observe: any *new* claim against *any* device in the cluster -- including unrelated
   drivers/pools, and `adminAccess: true` claims -- fails to schedule.
6. Delete the `DeviceTaintRule`; confirm previously-blocked claims immediately allocate.



### Anything else we need to know?

- This appears specific to the `NoSchedule` enforcement path. Tested `NoExecute` separately: a
  `NoExecute` `DeviceTaintRule` with `deviceSelector` omitted does **not** evict an already-running
  pod on an unrelated device (its `EvictionInProgress` condition stays `reason: NotStarted`
  indefinitely) -- confirmed the eviction mechanism itself works correctly in the same environment
  via a positive control (a `NoExecute` taint with a matching selector evicted the target pod
  within 5 seconds). So the nil-selector matching bug looks confined to whatever code path
  `NoSchedule` uses to block new allocation, not the separate eviction controller.
- Distinct from #141422 / the pending fix in #141425: that issue concerns a selector that is
  *present but empty* (`deviceSelector: {}`). This report is about the field being *absent*
  entirely -- confirmed by reading #141425's diff that its new validation only rejects the
  empty-but-present case and returns immediately with no error when the selector is nil, so it
  does not cover this scenario.
- Creating a `DeviceTaintRule` is a cluster-scoped permission not granted by any built-in
  `view`/`edit`/`admin` ClusterRole -- but this bug means anyone holding that permission can
  silently take down DRA scheduling cluster-wide with one missing field, when the documented
  default behavior should be a no-op.

body:
> **Status 2026-09-14.** The comments below carry `[UPDATED]` notes and strike-through where they were wrong.
>
> - The failures are memory pressure at the 6Gi limit, not the CPU quota. Prow reports `Job pod was OOM killed by the cluster.` for both builds listed below (test container `OOMKilled`, exit 127 in the first) and for 22 of the 40 `ci-kind-dra-1-34` runs from 08-03 to 09-11, 21 of them after running into the 90 minute timeout. The kind node journals cannot see that kill, so I missed it at first.
> - The runner CPU quota problem was real but separate. kubernetes/test-infra#37733 (merged 08-21, in the job image since 09-07) copies the pod's `cpu.max` into the runner's `init` leaf. The release-1.34 binaries have `containermaxprocs=0` (`godebug default=go1.24`) and ignore it; with `GOMAXPROCS=2` in the runner env (kubernetes/test-infra#37731) my replica of the job still ran into the 6Gi limit (one run each way). Neither explains the OOM kills.
> - The apiserver leak claim is withdrawn. The memory comes from `ResourceSlice Controller creates slices`, which on release-1.34 and release-1.35 publishes 100 max-size ResourceSlices; master cut it to 10 in #136156 (1847d5b1a, "created too much load for an E2E test"). Same branch, count as the only change: about 2 GiB less non-reclaimable memory for the suite on both branches, 3.0 to 3.4 GiB in the 1.34 random seed runs that hit the scheduler log mode below.
> - Why 1.34 is worse than 1.35, and why the seed matters: the scheduler's experimental structured allocator logs the full ResourceSlice list at V(5) once per node it evaluates, per scheduling attempt (`structured/internal/experimental/allocator_experimental.go`, "Gathering pools"), about 74 MB per line while the 100 slices exist, and the jobs run kube-scheduler at `--v=5`. release-1.34 picks that allocator with the default gates (`DRAResourceClaimDeviceStatus`, beta); release-1.35 only when an alpha gate selects it (`DRADeviceBindingConditions` together with device status, or `DRAConsumableCapacity`), which the all-gates presubmit `pull-kubernetes-kind-dra-all` does. Master dropped the statement in #136588. In uncapped replays with random seeds the scheduler wrote 0.2 to 5.9 GB of log within about 30 s of that test; in job replicas at 2 CPUs, 0.2 to 4.3 GB, within about a minute at 12Gi and spread over 8 to 28 minutes in the 6Gi runs that thrashed; kube-scheduler at 1.0 to 1.7 GiB where it was sampled. With the statement deleted, the 100 slice presubmit replicas completed at 6Gi on both branches, still at 93 to 95% of the limit non-reclaimable.
> - Outcome (09-14): the remedy is the job memory, not branch code. #142082 (delete the log statement on release-1.35) and #142083 (the 100 to 10 change from #136156, release-1.35) were closed, they do not meet the cherry-pick guidelines; kubernetes/test-infra#37865 (6Gi to 12Gi for the 1.34 and 1.35 kind DRA jobs) merged on 09-14 06:25 UTC; the periodics run on a 24h interval and pick it up on their next runs, due around 14:20 UTC for `ci-kind-dra-1-34` and 20:17 UTC for `ci-kind-dra-1-35`. kubernetes/test-infra#37731 is closed. Whether the jobs stay green at 12Gi is what the next runs will show. First prow runs on the two PRs before they were closed (09-14): #142083 passed all three kind-dra presubmits; #142082 on its own passed the plain and `-all-slow` jobs; its `-all` job failed twice without an OOM kill (the first time with the apiserver stalling while the 100 slices were created and deleted, the second time on a different spec, a pod the kubelet rejected at device-plugin admission with the control plane quiet) and passed on the third run, so the log deletion alone leaves that job on the edge at 6Gi. The numbers are summarized in those PRs; I have the raw samples if anyone wants them.
>
> The original report follows, unchanged apart from the `[UPDATED]` notes, the strike-through and two heading remarks. The canary matrix and the three run rule were my own proposal at the time, superseded by the above.

### Which jobs are failing?

- https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-dynamic-resource-allocation#ci-kind-dra-1-34

I confirmed these failed runs:

- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kind-dra-1-34/2088993552422932480
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kind-dra-1-34/2082106833379528704

### Which tests are failing?

It is not only one test. The DRA suite starts but cannot finish.

One confirmed run says:

```text
Will run 66 of 7144 specs
Running in parallel across 8 processes

5 specs pass, then:

[FAILED] [847.336 seconds] [BeforeEach]
test/e2e/dra/utils/deploy.go:287

wait for service account "default" in namespace "dra-9418":
timed out waiting for the condition

Process did not finish before 1h30m0s timeout
```

There is no final `Ran N of M Specs` summary.

### Since when has it been failing?

I confirmed the two runs above.

I did not confirm the exact first bad run yet, so I do not want to give a wrong regression date. [UPDATED: the first run prow labeled as OOM-killed was on 07-14, the first run on the 07-13 kubekins image that moved dind under the pod cgroup (kubernetes/test-infra#37440).]

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-dynamic-resource-allocation#ci-kind-dra-1-34

### Reason for failure (if possible)

The primary failure is the Prow 1h30m timeout.

The job already started the tests, but namespace setup and control plane operation became very slow. One `BeforeEach` spent about 847 seconds and two namespaces could not get the default ServiceAccount in time.

The cleanup later also hit OOM or command failures around `kind export logs` and `kind delete cluster`. ~~I think this is secondary because the test process was already terminated by the Prow timeout.~~ [UPDATED: not secondary; prow reports the job pod itself as OOM-killed for this build, see the status at the top.]

Current job runs all these in one Prow container:

- Docker-in-Docker
- four kind nodes
- eight Ginkgo processes
- Kubernetes control plane
- 2 CPU
- 6Gi memory

Possible reasons (as listed at the time):

1. Eight Ginkgo processes and four kind nodes saturate the 2 CPU limit.
2. Memory reclaim makes apiserver, controller-manager or etcd very slow before OOM.
3. etcd or container storage has high I/O wait.
4. release-1.34 has a control plane or DRA regression.
5. The job downloads latest kind, and latest kind may interact badly with old release branch.
6. One DRA test or cleanup leaks cluster resources.
7. The floating latest 1.34 CI package introduced the regression.

I do not think increasing only the timeout is a good first fix.

Proposed canary matrix (superseded, see the status at the top):

| Ginkgo nodes | CPU | Memory |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | 2 | 6Gi |
| 4 | 2 | 6Gi |
| 8 | 4 | 6Gi |
| 4 | 4 | 6Gi |

~~Add 8Gi memory only when `memory.events`, `memory.peak` or container metrics show memory pressure before the timeout.~~

For each run, collect:

- `cpu.stat`
- `memory.current`
- `memory.peak`
- `memory.events`
- `docker stats`
- kube-apiserver logs
- kube-controller-manager logs
- etcd logs
- time from namespace creation to default ServiceAccount creation
- final Ginkgo summary
- cleanup exit status

~~A resource or parallelism change should have at least three successful runs before merge.~~

### Anything else we need to know?

This is different from #140701.

In #140701, the Ubuntu node jobs were OOM killed before tests and before guest VM creation. In this job, the kind cluster and tests already run, then the control plane becomes too slow.

Related test-infra history:

- kubernetes/test-infra#34343 moved etcd data to `/tmp` and reduced this job memory from 9Gi to 6Gi after a canary.
- kubernetes/test-infra#37491 changed DRA node-e2e jobs from 1Gi to 2Gi. That is another job type and another failure shape.

Cleanup error handling should be a separate PR. It should preserve the primary test exit code, always try both log export and cluster deletion, and not replace the first failure with a cleanup failure.

I searched open and closed issues in `kubernetes/kubernetes` and `kubernetes/test-infra` with `ci-kind-dra-1-34`, `kind-dra-1-34`, the ServiceAccount timeout and cleanup OOM messages. I did not find an exact issue for this failure. GitHub search index can have delay.

This issue is opened separately as requested in #140701.

body:
### What happened?

A pod using a Dynamic Resource Allocation claim got permanently stuck in `CreateContainerError` after its
node rebooted, with no automatic recovery.

Setup: a pod with a `ResourceClaimTemplate`-based claim, already `Running` with its device allocated and
prepared. I rebooted the node (a full reboot — kubelet and the container runtime both restart, along with
every workload container on that node, including the DRA driver's own pod).

After the node came back:
- The driver re-registered and kubelet re-prepared the same already-allocated claim (confirmed via the
  driver's own logs — it logged a fresh "prepare" call for the exact same claim UID and returned success).
- Despite that, the pod's container repeatedly failed to start:
  ```
  Warning  Failed  Error: failed to create containerd container: CDI device injection failed: unresolvable CDI devices k8s.gpu.example.com/gpu=<uid>-gpu-0
  ```
- This did not resolve on its own. I watched it for 5+ minutes: kubelet kept retrying the identical
  container creation with the identical (still-unresolvable) device reference, backing off further each
  time. It never attempted to re-prepare the claim again.
- The only way I found to recover was deleting and recreating the pod, which allocates a fresh claim and
  works immediately.


Note: a plain `systemctl restart kubelet` alone (container runtime left untouched, containers kept running)
does **not** reproduce this — I tried that first and saw no re-prepare attempt at all over several minutes.
The container runtime itself needs to also restart (i.e. an actual node reboot, or restarting kubelet and
the container runtime together) for this to trigger.


### What did you expect to happen?

Either the pod should recover cleanly after the node comes back, or if the replayed prepare produces a
result that doesn't actually work, there should be some way to detect that and retry — an Event, a condition,
or another re-prepare attempt — rather than an indefinite retry loop with a generic container-runtime error
that gives no indication anything DRA-related happened.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Set up a DRA driver and create a pod with a `ResourceClaimTemplate`-based claim (used
   [kubernetes-sigs/dra-example-driver](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-example-driver) v0.4.0 for
   this repro). Confirm it reaches `Running` with the claim allocated.
2. Fully reboot the node the pod is running on (in a `kind` cluster: `docker restart <node-container>`; on a
   real cluster: an actual node reboot, or restarting the container runtime and kubelet together).
3. Wait for the node to report `Ready` again and the driver's pod to come back up and re-register.
4. Observe: `kubectl describe pod` shows repeated `CreateContainerError` / `CDI device injection failed:
   unresolvable CDI devices ...` events, with a growing `BackOff`. This does not resolve on its own.
5. Delete and recreate the pod — it comes up fine immediately with a fresh claim.


### Anything else we need to know?

I reproduced this the same way on a second, real (non-kind) cluster — same sequence of events, same
`CDI device injection failed: unresolvable CDI devices` error, same lack of self-recovery. A comparison pod
on a node that wasn't rebooted kept running the whole time, so this is specifically tied to the reboot, not
something intermittent.

Two things worth separating here, since I've only tested with one driver:

- Kubelet does not appear to remember, across a restart, that a claim was already successfully prepared —
  every claim gets treated as unprepared again after a reboot, and gets a fresh `NodePrepareResources` call
  regardless of which driver is behind it. This part reproduced identically on both clusters.
- Once that replayed call happens, kubelet accepts whatever the driver responds with and never re-checks or
  retries even after the resulting container creation keeps failing — it just repeats the identical failing
  attempt indefinitely. This also isn't specific to any one driver's behavior; it's what kubelet does with
  the response once it gets it, and I did not see it change over the retries.
- What I can't say for certain is whether every DRA driver would produce an unusable result the way this one
  did on replay. I tested only [kubernetes-sigs/dra-example-driver](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-example-driver).
  A driver with more robust logic may not have any visible symptom. But it seems that kubelet
  gives a driver no way to tell "this is a replay of something you already told me was ready" versus a fresh
  request, and never verifies or retries regardless. So any driver whose restart-recovery isn't airtight may hit
 this type of problem. This happened on the very first attempt, with the reference driver
  meant to demonstrate best practices, using nothing more unusual than a node reboot.


### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
kind v0.32.0, node image kindest/node:v1.36.1
```

</details>



### Cloud provider

<details>

Local `kind` cluster, not cloud-hosted.

</details>


### OS version

<details>

N/A — reproduced on a local `kind` cluster.

</details>


### Install tools

<details>

([kubernetes-sigs/dra-example-driver](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-example-driver) v0.4.0).

</details>

title: [Bug] Device taint NoExecute eviction does not evict pods using DRA-backed extended-resource claims (pod.Status.ExtendedResourceClaimStatus)

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: sig/scheduling
